# Corollary of 086–087 for the block without physical truncation

Let E_j be the causal block of all strictly proper rational transforms with denominator ∏_l(s+v_{jl}), v_{jl}>0, counting multiplicities. Let μ_j be the minimum of W on its unit L² sphere. If u_j=min_l v_{jl}→∞ and Σ_l 1/v_{jl}→S, with 0<S<∞, then

    lim μ_j = λ_W(S),

where λ_W(S) is the full ground level of paper 46 on [−S,S]. The largest pole, the separation, the multiplicity and the numerator are not restricted. In particular for S≤553/200 the limit is positive by 193, endpoint included. The statement also identifies the limit in windows whose sign is unknown.

**Floor without estimating derivatives of the block.** Fix L>2S. For a unit f in the block, 085 gives ||exp(σy)f||₂≤∏(v+σ)/(v−σ). With σ=λu_j and λ>0 small enough, 2Σ1/v /(1−λ²)<L with uniform slack for large j. As in 194 it follows that r=f 1_{y>L} has ||exp(y)r||₂≤exp(−c u_j) for some c>0. With σ=1 fixed the same inequality gives ||exp(y)f||₂=O_S(1). For g=f−r, the difference between comb plus polar for f and g is o(1) uniformly. Indeed the moments are continuous in L²(exp(2y)dy) and each correlation of causal functions at distance t is bounded by exp(−t) times the product of their weighted norms; the series ΣΛ(q)q⁻³ᐟ² converges.

For the archimedean part, A(r)≥−6||r||₂²; each truncation belongs to the domain because it is piecewise smooth with finitely many jumps and exponential tail for each finite block. The cross term A(g,r) is O(||g||₂||r||₂) with an absolute constant. On the half-lines facing each other across L the kernel is −K(x+y)/2, x,y>0, with K from 077. One has K(t)≤C/t for all t>0; Schur with weight x⁻¹ᐟ² gives norm ≤Cπ/2 using ∫ y⁻¹ᐟ²/(x+y)dy=πx⁻¹ᐟ². The exterior identity of 077 extends to the boundary by this bound (or directly by the Lévy formula). Thus W(f)≥W(g)−o(1)≥λ_W(L/2)||g||²−o(1). The last norm tends to one uniformly. When taking L↓2S use the continuity of the full ground level established in 077. The result is liminf μ_j≥λ_W(S).

**Approximation from the block.** In the right half-plane set B_j(s)=∏(v−s)/(v+s). It has modulus one on the imaginary axis. For each real τ,
    
    B_j(iτ)=exp(−2i Σ arctan(τ/v)) → exp(−2iSτ),

since Σ v⁻³≤u_j⁻²Σ v⁻¹. Under Fourier–Laplace, the orthogonal complement of B_j H² inside the causal space is exactly E_j: division by each inner factor imposes the corresponding zero with its multiplicity, and the evaluation kernels and their derivatives generate the partial fractions of the block. Equivalently by the orthonormal basis of POWER_THREE_002. For causal f its projection onto the block is f_j=f−B_j P_+(conj(B_j)f) in Fourier representation, where P_+ multiplies in time by the indicator of the positive half-line.

Fix f smooth with compact support in (0,2S). For 0<s<1/2, P_+ is bounded in temporal H^s by 077. Multiplying in frequency by B_j or its conjugate converges strongly in that norm to the limit multiplier, by dominated convergence and modulus one. The limit conj(B_j) advances the signal by 2S, and P_+ annihilates it. Hence f_j→f in H^s, sufficient for convergence of the archimedean part of logarithmic growth. Moreover ||f_j||₂≤||f||₂, and 085 with σ=2 fixed gives ||exp(2y)f_j||₂=O_S(||f||₂). Cauchy–Schwarz between this norm and L² convergence gives f_j→f in L²(exp(2y)dy), which by the first paragraph controls comb and polar. We conclude W(f_j)→W(f). Smooth tests with interior support are a form core for the window problem (it also suffices to approximate minimizers of slightly smaller windows by convolution and use 077). After translating and normalizing, limsup μ_j≤λ_W(S).

**Audit of antecedents.** 086 and 087 were identified as direct antecedents: they already prove the effective window, even for each prescribed listing in 087, without maximum and with quantitative errors for the cutoffs. Carleman and the Hardy projection are precisely their mechanisms. The present statement only makes explicit the version without physical truncation, using weighted interpolation for the recovery sequence. The asymptotic floor of 194 already follows from the lower bound of 087 by sending the cutoff to infinity for each listing. No new sign route is claimed.

 014 identifies the dense regime of confluent poles, 085 supplies the Hardy reflection and 077 the boundary control. 194 only gave a floor for S strictly smaller than the certified window and required log(max v)=o(min v). The one-sided archimedean comparison makes it possible to discard that last hypothesis, and the projection onto the rational space provides the reverse inequality for the minimum. In particular v_{jl}=n/S for n poles realizes the limit of each finite window. The global sign is equivalent to all these limits being nonnegative (positive integer S suffices by inclusion). The identity of the limit does not establish its sign for arbitrary S.

**Persistent detection by subblocks of unequal rates.** Corollary of the preceding bridge. For each finite listing j suppose that, for each fixed R, the sum of 1/v over its rates v≥R tends to infinity as j grows. Additional slow rates in the domain of the form are allowed. If an admissible datum in some window S has Rayleigh quotient −δ<0, then, for all sufficiently large j, the full block contains a vector with quotient ≤−δ/2. One can even require that it use only rates tending uniformly to infinity, with sum of reciprocals tending to S. Therefore an infinite subsequence with floor ≥−o(1) in a family satisfying the hypothesis suffices to close the sign.

Indeed, choose a threshold R_j→∞ slowly enough that the rates ≥R_j have reciprocal mass larger than S in each eventual listing (diagonalize the integer thresholds). Add those rates in any order until S is exceeded for the first time. The selected mass lies between S and S+1/R_j. The theorem of 195 gives convergence of the minimum of that subblock to λ_W(S)≤−δ. The subblock is contained in the original block: multiply numerator and denominator by the omitted factors and the property of being strictly proper is preserved. The declared margin follows by inclusion. If rates of uniformly bounded total reciprocal mass are removed from each listing, the hypothesis on the tails still holds. The confluent reference is POWER_CONFLUENT_BRIDGE_014 and the case of finite mass with prescribed rates is 087/195. This corollary specifies which falsifier persists after selecting or discarding poles; it does not produce the subsequence with the required floor.

**Independent review of persistent detection: PROVED as a corollary of the bridge.** For each fixed integer threshold the available mass eventually exceeds S; diagonalizing those thresholds produces R_j→∞ without requiring a uniform rate of divergence. The first crossing of S adds at most 1/R_j, even with multiplicities, and the sublist satisfies exactly the two hypotheses of the previous limit. A negative admissible datum in the window gives λ_W(S)≤−δ, hence the minimum of the subblock is ≤−δ/2 for all sufficiently large indices. Inclusion in the full block preserves strictly proper rational functions on multiplying by the omitted factors, also when there are repeated poles.

Removing a total reciprocal mass bounded by C leaves, above each fixed threshold, at least the previous mass minus C; hence it does not alter the required divergence. An infinite subsequence of floors ≥−o(1) then contradicts the persistence of any negative test. This makes precise the quantifiers of the existing bridge 087/195 and of the confluent case 014; it is not a new positivity mechanism nor a construction of that subsequence.

**Two detectable directions for each distinct exterior quartet.** For the full hermitian form, if there exist k distinct quartets of exterior zeros, in some finite window there is a complex subspace of dimension 2k with strictly negative floor in the sense W(f)≤−δ||f||², δ>0. In each family of the previous corollary the same number of directions with negative margin eventually persists (with smaller margin). In particular a subsequence with SECOND eigenvalue, counted from smallest to largest, ≥−o(1) would suffice. The case k=1 uses that the nontrivial zeros are not real. Index V.2 already warns that abstractly counting pairs does not give this lower bound; here the tests are constructed and cut in the physical domain.

In the coordinate z=ρ−1/2 set E(z)=ξ(1/2+z), and for each chosen point w of multiplicity m_w take F_w(z)=E(z)/((z−w)^(m_w) c_w), with c_w=E^(m_w)(w)/m_w!. It is entire, equals one at w and zero at all the other points of the divisor. It is the bilateral transform of a smooth datum f_w which, with all its derivatives, decays faster than any fixed exponential: invert on the imaginary axis and shift to the lines Re z=±B for each B. The fast vertical decay in each fixed strip is obtained from the theta representation of ξ by integration by parts (also by Stirling and polynomial growth of ζ in fixed strips). The division has a removable singularity. Growing characters are not used as L² vectors.

Multiply these data by χ(y/L), with χ smooth compactly supported equal to one on [−1,1]. In |Re z|≤1/2 the transforms converge uniformly with error o(1)(1+|Im z|)^(−2), by convergence of the derivatives up to order two in L¹ with weight exp(|y|/2) and integration by parts. The unit zero count of 175 allows passing to the limit in the Weil formula of the compact data: up to the common positive normalization factor, the limit matrix is that of Σ_ρ F(z)overline{F(−conj z)} counting multiplicities. On the four cardinals of each quartet it consists of two disjoint swaps, of weight m_w>0. The differences of cardinals in each pair have negative definite matrix, also for the union of the k quartets. By finite dimension this persists at some common cutoff L with margin relative to the L² norm (the cardinals are independent by evaluation). Translating the compact space to the causal half-line preserves the quotient. In the selected subblock apply the recovery of 195 to each element of a basis and to its combinations by polarization; the norm and form matrices converge, preserving dimension and margin. No additional negative eigenvalue is claimed from the multiplicity of a single zero. The floor of the second eigenvalue by blocks remains to be proved.

**Amplification by opposite translations: semiboundedness of the second eigenvalue suffices.** If there are k distinct exterior quartets, the eigenvalue 2k counted from below of the full form in any family of blocks with the previous tail divergence tends to −∞. Consequently, to prove the sign it would suffice to have a subsequence whose second eigenvalue is bounded below by any fixed finite constant.

For each previous cardinal F_w take t_w=R sign(Re w) and G_w(z)=exp(t_w(z−w))F_w(z). Its values at all the zeros are exactly those of the original cardinal. On the imaginary axis its L² norm is multiplied by exp(−R|Re w|), since the modulation there only translates the physical datum. For the 2k paired differences, the limit matrix of the form remains diagonal with fixed negative entries. The squared norm of any combination of coefficients c is at most C exp(−2R b)||c||² with b=min_w |Re w|>0 by the triangle inequality and C fixed. For each R, cutting afterwards in a sufficiently large window preserves the form matrix up to a norm error smaller than half the fixed margin; the L² bound is preserved by taking |χ|≤1. Therefore in that window the whole subspace of dimension 2k satisfies W(f)≤−C' exp(2Rb)||f||², with C'>0 independent of R.

Given a target A>0 choose first R and then the compact window with quotient ≤−2A. The simultaneous recovery in the subblocks of 195 transfers it with quotient ≤−A to ALL sufficiently late listings, by min-max. The order of these limits does not require a uniform rate for the cutoff. R162_504 studied the second eigenvalue of the part without polar term at first contact and recorded the sign reformulation; here divergence in modulus is obtained for eigenvalues of the full form, from cardinals of arbitrarily small norm. The postulated subsequential lower bound is not known.

**Simultaneous physical rate for 2k directions.** Let λ_j(T) be the j-th eigenvalue of the full form on [−T,T], in increasing order. For k distinct quartets with minimal distance b>0 from the critical line one obtains

    liminf_{T→∞} log(1+max(0,−λ_{2k}(T)))/(2T) ≥ b.

In particular the liminf for the second eigenvalue is at least the supremum of the distances of the zeros from the line (zero if there are no exterior quartets). A subsequence of growing windows with λ₂(T)≥−exp(o(T)) would suffice. 119–121 already give a subexponential criterion for the first eigenvalue of specific matrices; the difference here is the multiplicity 2k and the use of the simultaneous cutoff in the full physical form.

Fix 0<η<1/2, set R=(1−η)T and translate and renormalize the cardinals as in the previous paragraph. Multiply in time by a smooth function equal to one on |y|≤T−1, zero on |y|≥T, with derivatives up to order two bounded independently of T. In the discarded zone one has |y−t_w|≥ηT−1 (for the opposite-translation convention change t_w to −t_w). Each derivative up to order two of the translated cardinal is dominated by C_B exp(−R|Re w|−B|y−t_w|), with B arbitrary fixed. Using exp(|y|/2)≤exp(R/2+|y−t_w|/2) and B>1/2+2/η, the weighted L¹ norms of the error and of those derivatives tend to zero exponentially. Thus the transform error at each zero is o(1)(1+|Im z|)^(−2) uniformly. Although the translated cardinals may grow in other parts of the strip, their exact values on the full divisor are still zeros or ones; hence the Weil sum of the cutoff has the same negative limit matrix. The L² norm of the space of differences is ≤C exp(−Rb) per unit norm of coefficients. Min-max gives λ_{2k}(T)≤−c exp(2(1−η)bT) for all sufficiently large T. Take first liminf and then η↓0. The qualitative bridge of 195 does not transmit this rate to listings of poles without a quantitative relation between index and radius.

**Exact rates and index if the exterior divisor is finite.** Suppose there are exactly k distinct exterior quartets. Order their distances b₁≥…≥b_k>0, with one entry per quartet even when distances repeat. In the full physical form, for 1≤j≤k and n=2j−1,2j,

    lim_{T→∞} log(1+max(0,−λ_n(T)))/(2T) = b_j.

Moreover λ_(2k+1)(T)≥0 for all T and the negative index equals exactly 2k in every sufficiently large window. The case k=0 gives nonnegativity directly by Weil.

Indeed, each pair of points swapped by z↦−conj z contributes, up to the common positive normalization and with multiplicity m, (m/2)(|F(z)+F(−conj z)|²−|F(z)−F(−conj z)|²). The zeros on the line contribute squared moduli. For quartet i there are two difference functionals. Each has norm in L²[−T,T] ≤2(exp(2b_iT)/(2b_i))^(1/2) by Cauchy–Schwarz applied to the exponentials. Imposing the vanishing of the two differences of the first j−1 quartets costs codimension at most 2(j−1). In the resulting subspace W(f)≥−C_j exp(2b_jT)||f||² by the remaining FINITE sum. The inequalities for smooth tests extend to the domain by form core and continuity of the evaluations in each window. Min-max gives λ_(2j−1)(T)≥−C_j exp(2b_jT), and likewise for λ_(2j). With all differences annihilated the floor is zero. The opposite inequalities in rate and the eventual index come from the preceding paragraph applied to the first j quartets, using λ_(2j−1)≤λ_(2j). The multiplicity of a zero modifies the constant, not the number of differences. The result also describes a limitation: a uniform floor for the third eigenvalue is compatible with the scenario of exactly one quartet, while the second would detect that scenario.

**Finite-rank model with bounded additive error.** Under the previous hypothesis of exactly k>0 quartets, let B_T be only the contribution of their zeros in the hermitian Weil formula, with the same normalization as W. For i=1,…,2k, if β_i(T) are its ordered negative eigenvalues, then for all sufficiently large T

    0 ≤ λ_i(T)−β_i(T) ≤ C,

with C depending on the quartets and uniform in T. B_T is computed only with the swap matrix and the explicit Gram of the 4k evaluation exponentials on [−T,T]. Knowledge of the positions of real quartets is not presupposed.

Proof. Use F(z)=∫f(y)exp(zy)dy, and write e_z(y)=exp(conj(z)y) in the window, z ranging over the 4k points. The evaluation map is surjective by independence of distinct exponentials and its Gram is positive definite. By congruence, B_T has exactly 2k negative eigenvalues and as many positive ones. Its nonzero eigenvectors lie in V_T=span{e_z}. The difference W−B_T is the positive sum over the zeros on the line.

For z=b+iγ with b≠0 use as basis of V_T the functions h_z=e_z exp(−|b|T+iγ sign(b)T). Measured inward from their dominant endpoint, they are decreasing exponentials of bounded norm. The Gram of those at the same endpoint converges to the positive definite Gram of distinct exponentials on [0,∞), by independence. Between opposite endpoints the integrated product is O(T exp(−2T min|b|)), with the minimum over the finite catalogue. Hence the Euclidean norm of the coefficients of a vector of V_T is ≤C||f||₂ uniformly for large T. At any real ordinate t the evaluation of h_z has modulus ≤2/|b+i(t−γ)| by explicit integration. The zero count of 175 makes its square uniformly summable over the zeros on the line, with multiplicities, for each fixed z. On V_T one gets 0≤(W−B_T)(f)≤C||f||². The truncated exponentials have only jumps at the endpoints, with transform O_T((1+|t|)⁻¹), and belong to the logarithmic domain. To justify Weil there, convolve their extension by zero with a smooth mollifier of decreasing support: the enlarged windows have a fixed bound for fixed T, the transform multipliers are uniformly bounded in the strip and converge to one; the zero series and the physical form converge by convergence in the logarithmic norm and continuity of comb and polar in that enlarged window. Finally apply min-max from below via W≥B_T and from above on the space of the first i eigenvectors of B_T. The bound only controls the positive contribution on V_T, sufficient for these 2k eigenvalues.

**Independent review of the cardinal directions: PROVED for the full hermitian form.** F_w equals one at its point even with multiplicity and zero at the other distinct points of the divisor. Its vertical decay in each fixed strip allows inverting and shifting to any fixed real line, giving a smooth datum of superexponential decay in both directions. The cutoff converges with its two derivatives in weighted L¹, so that the evaluation error is o(1)(1+|γ|)^(−2). The zero count makes the sums of products convergent and justifies the Weil limit.

The involution z↦−conj z pairs the two abscissae at each height. In each quartet there are two matrices m[[0,1],[1,0]], with m>0, and hence two negative and independent cardinal differences. The norm matrices are also nondegenerate by independence of the evaluations. The common cutoff and the linear recovery of 195 preserve the norm and form Grams in finite dimension; min-max transfers the 2k directions, and in particular the second eigenvalue. Multiplicity only changes m, it does not add independent cardinal points.

**Cross-check of antecedents.** [Phase 21, 01-parity-and-geometry, Theorem 21-A.1](../phase-21-negative-directions-geometry/01-parity-and-geometry.md) already states two directions per quartet. Its approximate localization does not by itself prove global independence nor membership in L²; warning V.2 of the index preserves exactly that limitation. Here that step is completed by means of cardinals of ξ and physical cutoff; the count is not claimed as a new principle. [R162_504](../phase-162-row-d-first-contact-closure/R162_504_SECOND_EIGENVALUE.md) treats the second eigenvalue of the form without polar term and first contact, so it is not the same assertion about the full form. 087/195 and the confluent bridge 014 supply the recovery used, without a new arithmetic sign bound.

**Independent review of the amplification: PROVED.** Multiplying by exp(t_w(z−w)) preserves all values on the divisor and multiplies the L² norm by exp(−R|Re w|). The differences have, for every coefficient, norm at most Cexp(−Rb) while their form Gram remains a fixed negative matrix. For each R the physical cutoff is taken afterwards, preserving that Gram and contracting the norm if |χ|≤1. Choosing first R for a target A, then the cutoff and finally the recovery index suffices to obtain λ_(2k)≤−A in all late blocks. Repeating this for each A proves the limit −∞; it requires no rate of recovery uniform in R, nor does it produce the proposed subsequential floor.

**Independent review of the physical rate: PROVED.** With R=(1−η)T, the cutoff error is at distance at least ηT−1 from the translated center. Its weighted L¹ norm, with two derivatives, is at most a constant times exp(R(1/2−|Re w|)−(B−1/2)(ηT−1)); the fixed B chosen in the text makes it exponentially small. Although the exact transforms may grow in other parts of the strip, on the divisor they only take the values zero or one: there the error terms are summed by the unit count, without multiplying them by a strip majorant growing with R. The norm of the differences is O(exp(−Rb)), preserving the exponent 2(1−η)bT in Rayleigh. Taking liminf before η↓0 gives the stated rate; this rate is not transferred to a block index without additional quantitative data.

**Independent review of the finite exterior catalogue: PROVED under that hypothesis.** The two evaluation differences per quartet are continuous functionals on L² of each window, with norm O(exp(b_iT)). Annihilating those of the first j−1 quartets costs codimension at most 2(j−1); the remainder has lower bound −C_jexp(2b_jT), since the critical part is positive. Passing to the domain uses the form core and the continuity of these finitely many evaluations, without having to annihilate the functionals exactly on each smooth approximant. Min-max gives the bound for λ_(2j−1) and λ_(2j); the opposite rate comes from the first j quartets. With all differences annihilated nonnegativity holds in codimension ≤2k, and the constructed directions give index exactly 2k for large windows. A finite number of quartets is not presupposed in the earlier detection statements.

**Independent review of the additive model: PROVED under the finite catalogue.** The map of the 4k evaluations is surjective by independence of the exponentials, and the swap matrix has inertia (2k,2k). In the basis h_z, each endpoint block converges to a positive definite Gram on the half-line; the opposite crossings are O(Texp(−2bT)). This makes the coefficient bound uniform. The critical evaluation satisfies exactly the majorant 2/|b+i(t−γ)| and its squares are summable with multiplicity; one obtains 0≤W−B_T≤C on V_T, without asserting that bound on the whole domain.

The truncated exponentials belong to the domain of logarithmic symbol because their Fourier transform is O_T(1/|t|). The mollification converges in that norm; in a fixed enlarged window for each T comb and polar also converge. The multipliers of the mollification are uniformly bounded in |Re z|≤1/2, which allows dominating the Weil series by the quadratic tail. Therefore the formula is valid on V_T. Min-max from below uses W≥B_T; from above only the first i eigenvectors of B_T contained in V_T. This gives 0≤λ_i−β_i≤C uniformly in large T, with dependence on the fixed catalogue. The conditional model is not turned into a procedure for locating unknown quartets.

**Negative product without oscillating phases, for a finite exterior catalogue.** Index the 2k right points by z_j=b_j+iγ_j (each quartet gives two points) and pair with −conj z_j. Let μ_j be the positive weight of each point in the Weil formula, including multiplicity and the common normalization factor. For exactly k>0 quartets, the product of the first 2k physical eigenvalues satisfies

    exp(−2T Σ_j b_j) ∏_{i=1}^{2k}|λ_i(T)| → det(C) ∏_j μ_j,
    C_ij = 1/(conj(z_i)+z_j).

The Gram determinant is strictly positive. For a single quartet of height γ and distance b the coefficient is μ² γ²/[4b²(b²+γ²)], and the normalization is exp(−4bT).

Indeed, in the synthesis of the normalized exponentials h_z of the previous model, their Gram G_T converges in norm to G₀=diag(C,conj C), up to conjugation or permutation of bases depending on convention. In particular (1−ε_T)G₀≤G_T≤(1+ε_T)G₀ with ε_T→0. The exterior operator is written H_T J_T H_T*, where H_T synthesizes that basis and J_T has zero diagonal blocks and diagonal cross block D_T with moduli μ_j exp(2b_jT); the phase factors have modulus one. Its nonzero eigenvalues are those of G_T^(1/2)J_T G_T^(1/2). By min-max applied to the quotients (x*J_T x)/(x*G_T^(−1)x), the moduli of the negative eigenvalues change by factors between 1−ε_T and 1+ε_T on replacing G₀ by G_T: for the i-th negative values one optimizes over negative spaces, where the comparison of denominators preserves these bounds. This is relative even when some b_j differ. With G₀ the negative magnitudes are the singular values of C^(1/2)D_T(conj C)^(1/2), whose product is det(C)|det(D_T)|. The smallest singular value grows at least like a fixed constant times exp(2T min b_j), so the uniform additive error of the previous model does not change the equivalent. The quartet formula follows from det(C)=(2b)^(−2)−|2b+2iγ|^(−2). This conditional invariant provides a testable scalar prediction for a model with prescribed zeros, without supplying an arithmetic bound for zeta.

**Criterion of the second eigenvalue in a primes-only matrix, without finite-catalogue hypothesis.** Fix 0<a<1. On [−T,T] take the first N=ceil(T³) Dirichlet modes of both parities jointly, orthonormal, and form K of 121 in this full basis with X=exp(2T) and X^a<p≤X. If κ₂(T) denotes its second LARGEST eigenvalue and Δ=sup_ρ |Reρ−1/2|, then

    lim log(1+max(0,κ₂(T)))/(2T) = Δ.

This tolerates an arbitrary positive eigenvalue of the centered comb. The comparison of 121 with W has the same norm error in this basis: it only requires ||F'||₂≤πN||F||₂/T and Dirichlet, and the polar identity via autocorrelation holds for both parities (use the real part for complex ones). The strip ceiling of 117/119 for the negative part does not require parity either. It remains to prove that the subspace of TWO directions of 195 can be approximated with the stated N.

Use the physical-rate proof with an additional fixed support margin: cut on [−T+1,T−1] and then convolve each cardinal with a fixed Gevrey 3/2 bump of radius <1/2, of integral one, chosen by dilation so that its bilateral transform does not vanish at the four points of the quartet. Divide each convolved cardinal by the value of that transform at its own point. The limit matrix of the form is thus preserved: in the zero strip the multiplier of the bump is bounded and at each own point the value tends to one. The error of the cutoff with this margin still tends to zero by the same budget ηT−2. Young preserves the norm bound O(exp(−bR)) per vector. By Cauchy–Schwarz the cut datum before convolving has L¹ norm ≪√T, uniformly. Thus the coefficients of each smoothed vector in the normalized modes are O(exp(−c(n/T)^(2/3))) by the Fourier estimate of the bump from 119 and the formula for sines and cosines. The error of the projection in H¹ is O(exp(−c' T^(4/3))) and by the physical bound O(exp T) of comb and polar the form matrix changes by o(1). The error is also o(exp(−bR)) in norm. This preserves the two directions with depth exp(2(1−η)bT) up to a constant factor.

For Δ>0, given η₀<Δ sufficiently close to Δ and larger than aΔ, choose the quartet and then η small so that (1−η)b>η₀. The comparison of 121 has norm O_ε(poly(T) exp(2a(Δ+ε)T)), smaller than exp(2η₀T) for small ε. Min-max thus transfers the TWO directions to the upper end of K. Take η₀↑Δ; the ceiling is obtained from the same comparison error and the ceiling of 119. For Δ=0, W≥0 and the comparison gives rate zero by taking ε↓0. The matrix is arithmetic and is constructed without knowing zeros. The criterion still requires an independent bound on κ₂(T) along an unbounded sequence; the norm bound of the comparison by itself does not provide it.

**Independent review of the negative product: PROVED under a finite exterior catalogue.** The relative equivalence (1−ε_T)G₀≤G_T≤(1+ε_T)G₀ compares the inverse denominators of the Rayleigh quotients. For negative values one may optimize only over negative subspaces; there the comparison preserves the factors 1±ε_T in their moduli, even if D_T has distinct rates. An additive perturbation of the pencil does not suffice and no such inference is used. With G₀, the operator has zero diagonal blocks and adjoint cross blocks, so its negative moduli are exactly the singular values of the indicated block. Their product is det(C)|det(D_T)| and does not depend on the phases.

The smallest singular value is bounded below by a fixed constant times exp(2T min b_j), using the smallest singular values of the two Gram roots. Hence the O(1) error of the physical form is relatively o(1) in each of the finitely many negative eigenvalues. For one quartet, det C=1/(4b²)−1/(4(b²+γ²))=γ²/[4b²(b²+γ²)], and the two weights are μ, whence μ² and exp(−4bT). The normalization of μ explicitly includes that of Weil; no multiplicity factor is omitted.

**Independent review of the second eigenvalue of the prime matrix: PROVED.** The comparison of [121](ROUND_121_A.md) only uses the real part of the autocorrelation, the extension by zero with Dirichlet trace and the derivative ceiling of the basis; it is preserved for complex functions and for the union of both parities. The polar identity does not require parity either. The strip argument of [117](ROUND_117_A.md) and the ceiling of [119](ROUND_119_A.md), with logarithmic budget O(log(2+N/T)), give the same upper bound in this full basis. The parity of those spaces was a choice of representation, not a hypothesis of those two estimates.

For the two-direction floor, dilating the Gevrey bump toward zero makes its transform tend to one at the four points simultaneously. Dividing each cardinal by its own value preserves the zero/one data on the divisor after convolution, and the previous cutoff error remains summable because the multiplier is bounded in the strip. The support margin ensures zero trace. In normalized modes, the factor T^(−1/2) compensates the L¹ bound O(√T) of the previous datum, and the Fourier transform of the bump gives exp(−c(n/T)^(2/3)) in both parities. The H¹ tail from N=ceil(T³) is exp(−c'T^(4/3)), even absorbing powers of T. This is smaller than the norm exp(−bR) and absorbs the physical cost O(exp T), so both the norm and the form matrices preserve the depth of the two directions.

Choosing η₀ between aΔ and Δ, then a quartet with b>η₀ and a small margin η, makes the comparison error have rate strictly smaller than the two negative depths. Min-max produces two positive eigenvalues in K and proves the liminf up to Δ, without requiring that the supremum be attained. The upper bound uses the same comparison; for Δ=0, W≥0 and ε↓0 suffice. The independent arithmetic estimate of the second eigenvalue along a growing sequence of windows remains open.

**Band by halves and minors of order two.** Fix 1/2<a<1. In each half take N=ceil(T³) normalized Dirichlet sines in the coordinate u measured from the outer endpoint, with ω_i=iπ/T. The matrix K of 121 in the union of these bases is [[0,C],[C,0]], with C real symmetric. Indeed, a shift t∈(2aT,2T] never joins points of the same half. Between the two halves it sets u+v=2T−t=:s<T. The entry is C_ij=(2/T)D[(sin(ω_i·)*sin(ω_j·))(s)] with causal convolution and D[h]=Σ_{X^a<p≤X}(log p)h(2T−log p)/√p−∫_{X^a}^X h(2T−log v)dv/√v. The factor 2 of the quadratic of 121 counts both crossings in the hermitian matrix. If F(x)=D[sin(√x s)/√x], then C_ij=(2/T)ω_iω_j(F(ω_i²)−F(ω_j²))/(ω_j²−ω_i²), by the convolution of sines; on the diagonal one uses −F'(ω_i²). Matrix monotonicity of F is not assumed.

The same rate Δ of the second upper eigenvalue is preserved in this basis. In the previous simultaneous construction, before convolving, additionally apply a smooth cutoff that is zero on |y|≤2 and one for |y|≥3. There the derivatives of the translated cardinal are O_B(exp(−B(R−3))) for each fixed B and the correction tends to zero in the weighted norm used on the divisor. After convolving with radius <1/2 a gap at the center is preserved. To apply the Gevrey decay separately in each half, separate the two parts of the cut datum BEFORE convolving; the gap prevents mixing. The sine tails in both halves cost the same O(exp(−cT^(4/3))) in H¹. The argument of 121 preserves the derivative and norm bounds on their union. Thus the rate log(1+s₂(C))/(2T) is Δ, where s₂ is the second singular value.

Let M=max|C_ij| and let L be the maximum modulus of all 2×2 minors divided by M, with L=0 if M=0. One has s₂(C)/N≤L≤N s₂(C). For the first inequality choose a pivot of modulus M and subtract the product of its column by its row divided by the pivot. The residue has entries of modulus ≤L and norm ≤NL. For the second, any minor is ≤s₁(C)s₂(C) by the exterior square and s₁(C)≤NM. Since N is polynomial, log(1+L)/(2T)→Δ. This leaves a scalar arithmetic criterion: control those determinants RELATIVE to the largest entry, allowing an unrestricted rank-one component. The divided-difference identity does not prove the control of the minors.

**Independent review of the halves and the minors: PROVED.** The normalized modes contribute 2/T to the correlation of a crossing. For t>T no half crosses itself, and s=2T−t<T makes the cross integral exactly the causal convolution without additional truncation. The quadratic K=2D[Re c] coincides with the two cross blocks of entry (2/T)D[convolution]; there is no other factor two in C. Commutativity of convolution makes C real symmetric. The partial fraction of ω_iω_j/[(z²+ω_i²)(z²+ω_j²)] gives the written divided quotient; the diagonal limit is −ω_i²F'(ω_i²), including the prefactor 2/T.

The central cutoff only removes tails of the translated cardinal at distance at least R−3. With a sufficiently large fixed B its weighted and L² error is smaller than the margins used in the construction. Separating the halves before convolving avoids the discontinuous edge: the central gap and the outer margin survive the bump. Each part admits the sine approximation with H¹ tail exp(−cT^(4/3)), so the two depths are preserved. The positive eigenvalues of [[0,C],[C,0]] are the singular values of C; in particular the second is s₂(C) for sufficiently large T. This verifies the rate, not merely an approximation of one direction.

For M>0, the approximant obtained with a maximal pivot has rank one and each residue is a minor divided by that pivot. Its norm is ≤NL, whence s₂(C)≤NL. In the opposite direction, each minor is bounded by the norm of ∧²C=s₁(C)s₂(C), and s₁(C)≤NM. The case M=0 is immediate. These bounds and polynomial N preserve the rate on passing to log(1+L). Known rank-one approximation and min-max are used; neither the arithmetic bound of the minors nor matrix monotonicity of the divided-difference function is deduced.

**Certificate linear in the number of modes for the relative minors.** Remove the diagonal factors and the sign of C to use the real matrix A_ij=(F(x_i)−F(x_j))/(x_i−x_j), A_ii=F'(x_i), x_i=(πi/T)². By the factorization of 195 and the polynomial bounds for ω_i and their inverses, s₂(A) has the same rate Δ as s₂(C). From the N values and N derivatives O(N) arithmetic operations suffice for a scalar E with that rate.

Let D=max|A_ii| and M=max(D,max_i |A_(i,i+1)|). This gives the maximum of the WHOLE matrix: every secant slope between nodes is a convex mean of the slopes of the consecutive intervals. If M=0 set E=0. If D<M/2 set E=M: compressing to the two nodes that give M, the determinant in modulus is ≥M²−D² and the norm ≤2M, hence s₂(A)≥3M/8, while s₂(A)≤NM.

Otherwise take a diagonal pivot h=A_kk of maximal modulus, u_i=A_ik and R=A−uuᵗ/h. With t_i=(x_i−x_k)u_i, v_i=h−u_i one has exactly h(x_i−x_j)R_ij=t_i v_j−v_i t_j for i≠j: substitute F_i−F_k=(x_i−x_k)u_i. Choose l with maximal |t_l| and use E=max(max_i|R_ii|,max_j|R_lj|). If all the t vanish the off-diagonal entries of R are zero. Otherwise the identity of determinants in dimension two expresses t_i v_j−v_i t_j as (t_i/t_l)(t_l v_j−v_l t_j)−(t_j/t_l)(t_l v_i−v_l t_i). Hence |R_ij|≤2(x_N−x_1)E/min_i(x_(i+1)−x_i)≤2N²E for i≠j. Thus s₂(A)≤||R||≤2N³E. Conversely each R_ij is a minor divided by h and therefore E≤s₁(A)s₂(A)/|h|≤2N s₂(A). The selection of k,l and the evaluation of the certificate only use adjacent slopes, column k, row l and the diagonal. The linear cost refers to combining the samples of F,F', without estimating the work of obtaining them from the primes. The sign requires a uniform bound for E; the identity by itself does not provide it.

**Independent review of the linear certificate: PROVED.** Every secant between nodes is expressed as a convex mean of the adjacent secants, with weights given by the interval lengths. Hence M is the maximum of all the entries. In the branch D<M/2 the pivot entry is adjacent and the compression has negative determinant of modulus ≥3M²/4 and norm ≤2M; its smallest singular value is ≥3M/8 and does not exceed s₂(A). This verifies both comparisons of that branch, including its sign.

In the diagonal branch, D≥M/2>0 makes division by h legitimate. From F_i−F_k=t_i one obtains exactly h(t_i−t_j)−(x_i−x_j)u_i u_j=t_i v_j−v_i t_j. Using the index l of maximal |t_l|, the two quotients of t have modulus ≤1; dividing by x_i−x_j gives the bound of range over minimal separation. For x_i=(πi/T)² that ratio is ≤N². If t is identically zero, F_i is constant on the nodes and the off-diagonal residue is zero; the diagonal maximum is still sufficient. Each residue is a minor of order two divided by h, and |h|≥M/2 gives E≤2Ns₂(A). The approximant uuᵗ/h has rank one, whence s₂(A)≤||R||≤2N³E. The cases M=0 or E=0 are compatible with the same conclusions.

The original matrix satisfies C=−(2/T)diag(ω_i)A diag(ω_i); the largest and smallest values of ω_i and their inverses are polynomial in T for N=ceil(T³), so the rate of s₂ is preserved. Reading adjacent slopes, two rows/columns and the diagonal requires O(N) operations on the already available values of F,F'. This neither reduces the cost of obtaining those samples nor proves the arithmetic bound of the certificate; it uses the known structure of divided differences.

**Cross block with positive prime weights and without centering integral.** In the same sine bases by halves, let B be the cross matrix formed with ALL primes 2≤p≤exp(2T), weight (log p)/√p, without subtracting the integral. The entry is the convolution of the two modes extended by zero outside [0,T], evaluated at 2T−log p. Let P be the orthogonal projection in the mode space of each half onto the hyperplane ∫₀ᵀexp(−u/2)f(u)du=0. Then log(1+s₂(PBP))/(2T)→Δ. The sampling weights are positive; the modes and the entries may change sign.

Indeed, the continuous reference matrix for the WHOLE band 1≤v≤exp(2T) is exactly exp(T)hhᵗ, with h_i=∫₀ᵀexp(−u/2)φ_i(u)du. Changing variable to s=2T−log v gives exp(T)exp(−s/2)ds and the integral of the convolution over [0,2T] factorizes by Fubini. Hence P annihilates it exactly. To pass from the centered high band C of 195 to the centered full band, the cross block of the centered low band costs O_ε(poly(T) exp(2a(Δ+ε)T)) in norm: apply the integration by parts of 121 to the cross correlation of two normalized combined modes, extended by zero, with bounds |c|≤1 and |c'|≤πN/T. Thus PBP differs from PCP by that same bound.

It remains to preserve the two directions under compression. In the halves argument, after the central cutoff, separation and compact smoothing, apply −∂²+1/4 to each piece. Both pieces are smooth, supported in the interior; two integrations by parts give moment exactly zero. On the divisor the operator multiplies by 1/4−z², nonzero at the four chosen points; renormalize each cardinal by that value. The cutoff estimates for the divisor can be done with four derivatives instead of two by the same decay, and in L² norm the cost of the operator on the smoothed datum is bounded by the L¹ norm of the derivatives of the bump times the norm of the initial datum. The Gevrey tails only add a power of frequency. After truncating in sines, correct any loss of the moment with the first normalized sine: its moment is √(2/T)(π/T)(1+exp(−T/2))/(1/4+(π/T)²), of order T^(−3/2). The cost of correcting is polynomial times the exponential projection error, negligible in form and norm. The two directions remain with depth exp(2η₀T) as before. By min-max the second singular value of PCP has rate Δ. Choosing aΔ<η₀<Δ and then ε small transfers the lower bound to PBP; the ceiling follows by comparison and compression, also if Δ=0. The subexponential arithmetic estimate of this second singular value is still pending.

**Independent review of the prime block without centering: PROVED.** The substitution v=exp(2T−s) turns dv/√v into exp(T)exp(−s/2)ds on [0,2T]. The integral of the normalized convolution then factorizes into h_i h_j, without an additional factor two. The compression P annihilates exactly that rank-one matrix. In the low band, the two pieces extended by zero are H¹₀; their cross correlation and its derivative have the same bilinear bounds used in 121. Integration by parts with θ(v)−v gives the declared error norm, also after compressing.

In each smooth piece of interior support, integrating −f''+f/4 against exp(−u/2) gives exactly zero; the same operator in the physical variable multiplies the transform by 1/4−z². This factor does not vanish at any of the four selected zeros. Applying it after smoothing allows controlling its norm by Young and the fixed derivatives of the bump; the cutoff uses four derivatives, available with the same decay. The cardinal normalization therefore preserves the two directions and not just one.

The moment of the first sine is positive and has the sign of 1+exp(−T/2), since cos π=−1. Its order is T^(−3/2); the moment error of the truncation is bounded by its L² error because the norm of exp(−u/2) is ≤1. Correcting with that sine adds only a polynomial factor to the Gevrey error, keeping each piece in the range of P. In that space, the high block is [[0,PCP],[PCP,0]], so two positive eigenvalues are equivalent to the second singular value of PCP. The low-band error has smaller rate when choosing aΔ<η₀<Δ, and transfers the floor to PBP; the compressions and the comparison give the ceiling, including Δ=0 by ε↓0. The arithmetic estimate of the singular value remains pending, and the positivity of the weights asserts no sign of the entries nor of the matrix.

**The smallest eigenvalue of the raw prime block, without projecting.** For the symmetric B of the previous section, log(1+max(0,−λ_min(B)))/(2T)→Δ. Thus the only obligation is a subexponential lower bound for the quadratic of the sampled causal convolution with positive weights. The projection is removed from the STATEMENT using its positivity in the density term and the parity of the witness.

For the lower bound in depth take a point w of an exterior quartet at distance b. With the bilateral convention, reflection of the datum takes z to −z. Let f be the difference of amplified cardinals for w and −conj w, with values +1,−1. Subtract its reflection: the other pair of the quartet is disjoint and contributes the same negative energy. The resulting datum is odd and its four values are (up to order) 1,−1,−1,1. Use the symmetric central and outer cutoffs, smoothing and moment correction of the previous section; equivalently, first prepare the difference of cardinals with both moments per half and then subtract its reflection. The approximate values of the cardinals on the divisor converge to the stated pattern, and the norm and error bounds are preserved by the reflection. In the projection onto sines use the same first corrector mode in both halves; the parity survives exactly. In coordinates measured from the outer endpoint the coefficients have the form (v,−v), v⊥h. The quotient of the high-band matrix [[0,C],[C,0]] at that vector is −⟨Cv,v⟩/||v||². The comparison with W therefore forces a NEGATIVE quotient for C of depth exp(2η₀T), for all aΔ<η₀<b after choosing the small translation margin. At that same vector the density term exp(T)hhᵗ vanishes. The centered low-band difference costs exp(2a(Δ+ε)T) times a polynomial, smaller in exponential order, and B has a negative quotient of that depth. Choose b arbitrarily close to Δ.

In the opposite direction, B=exp(T)hhᵗ+C+low-band error in norm as before. The first summand is positive; ||C|| is the LARGEST eigenvalue of [[0,C],[C,0]], with ceiling exp(2(Δ+ε)T) times a polynomial via 117/121 in the two halves. This bounds the negative part of B even in the unprojected space and gives rate zero if Δ=0. The prime measure is positive, but the quadratic evaluates the autoconvolution without temporal conjugation by reflection and has no immediate sign. For real modes it can be written sum_p (log p)/√p (v*v)(2T−log p), with v extended by zero. The one-sided bound for these sums is missing.

**Independent review of the raw smallest eigenvalue: PROVED.** The reflection takes F(z) to F(−z). Subtracting it from the cardinal difference of the pair at height γ produces, on the quartet, the values 1,−1,−1,1: the second pair gives the same negative contribution and does not cancel it. The norm only increases by a fixed factor. The symmetric cutoffs and the reflection preserve the bounds, and preparing the moments before antisymmetrizing keeps both halves in the same hyperplane. The projection by sines and the identical corrector in the two halves commute with the reflection, keeping coefficients exactly (v,−v), with v perpendicular to h.

At that vector the quadratic of [[0,C],[C,0]], divided by its norm 2||v||², is −⟨Cv,v⟩/||v||². Since the comparison is W+K=error and W is deeply negative, K is deeply positive; hence the quotient of C is NEGATIVE, with the declared depth. The continuous term exp(T)hhᵗ vanishes at v and the low-band error has smaller rate, giving the same negative witness for B. Choosing a quartet close to the supremum and then the translation margin proves the liminf up to Δ, without requiring that it be attained.

For the ceiling, B is the sum of the positive density, C and the error: the negative part is bounded by ||C|| plus the norm of the error. The largest eigenvalue of the cross block is ||C|| and satisfies the comparison already proved; for Δ=0 take ε↓0. There is no need to project the statement nor to assume a sign of B from the positivity of its weights. The one-sided arithmetic bound of this autoconvolution remains open.

**Small divisors in the raw prime block: uniform floor in all modes.** Passing from primes to Λ(n) changes the form by O(1+T)||v||² through the proper powers (121). Use Λ(n)=−Σ_{d|n}μ(d)log d, and cut this sum at d≤D. For 2≤D≤exp(2T) the contribution of those divisors to the matrix is

    e^T c_D hhᵗ + E_D,    c_D=−Σ_{d≤D} μ(d)log(d)/d,
    ||E_D|| ≪ (1+N/T)√D log(2D).

Here h is the moment of the preceding section. Indeed, for ||v||=1 set k(s)=(v*v)(s) real with extension by zero. One has |k|≤1 and |k'|≤πN/T by Cauchy–Schwarz and the H¹₀ extension. For each d the sum over the multiples n=dm is the sum over integers m≥1 of f_d(t)=k(2T−log(dt))/√(dt) (zero outside the support). Its difference from ∫₀^∞ f_d(t)dt is O((1+N/T)/√d): on (0,1) use ∫₀¹t^(−1/2)dt=2 and on [1,∞) compare each sample with the integral over [m,m+1], with total variation ≤C(1+N/T)d^(−1/2)∫₁^∞t^(−3/2)dt. There is no jump at the endpoints of the support. The integral equals e^T(hᵗv)²/d by the factorization of the convolution. Summing the errors with |μ(d)log d| gives the announced norm, uniformly on the real sphere of the symmetric matrix.

By the classical quantitative PNT used in 073, the series Σμ(d)log(d)/d converges ordinarily (partial summation) and its sum is −1: for s>1 the series with minus sign is (1/ζ(s))', and the Abel limit is 1. Thus c_D>0 eventually. For any D=T^A with A>0 fixed one obtains a floor −O_A((1+T²)T^(A/2)log(2T)) for ALL modes, without imposing the moment. Even D→∞ with log D=o(T) only costs exp(o(T)) in the floor. On the hyperplane h⊥ the estimate is two-sided. Consequently the difficulty cannot come from those divisors at subexponential level: what remains is the exact term d>D with its Möbius signs. Its uniform control remains open; no sign has been assumed for that tail.

**Independent review of the small divisors: PROVED.** The identity Λ=−(μ log)*1 has the written sign. For the cross block the correction of proper powers has norm O(1+T), by the sum of the weights (log p)p^(−j/2). The real autoconvolution of a unit vector satisfies |k|≤1 and |k'|≤πN/T by the H¹₀ extension. Its value is zero at the endpoints of the support, so f_d adds no jumps. The integral on (0,1) costs ≤2/√d; on [1,∞), the comparison with the integer cells costs its total variation ≤C(1+N/T)/√d. The continuous integral is exactly e^T(hᵗv)²/d. Summing |μ(d)log d|/√d gives O(√Dlog(2D)), uniformly on the sphere and hence in the norm of the symmetric matrix.

The quantitative bound for M makes Σμ(d)log(d)/d converge ordinarily: the boundary term disappears and the partial-summation integral is absolutely convergent. The Abel limit coincides with that sum, while (1/ζ)'(1)=1 by the simple pole of ζ; thus c_D→1 with positive orientation. For D→∞ and log D=o(T), the norm error is exp(o(T)) and the rank-one part is eventually positive; on h⊥ it disappears and a two-sided bound remains. In the full space, removing that positive part only preserves the sufficiency of a floor for the tail, not an automatic equivalence with the floor of the tail separately. The term d>D is not controlled nor is a sign deduced for its Möbius coefficients.

**Localization at the endpoints and divisors up to X^(1−ε).** For any fixed 0<ε<1 one obtains the following sufficient criterion. Set X=exp(2T), choose 0<θ<ε and an integer r≥2 with r(ε−θ)>(1−θ)/2. On smooth real functions of compact support in (0,θT) and moment ∫exp(−u/2)v(u)du=0, a floor −exp(o(T))||v||²_{H^r} would suffice for the sum of the tail d>X^(1−ε) of −μ(d)log d over dm≤X, with weight (v*v)(log(X/(dm)))/√(dm), along a sequence T→∞. Each cofactor m of this tail satisfies m<X^ε.

Indeed, k=v*v and its derivatives up to order r have sup norm ≤C_r||v||²_{H^r} by Cauchy–Schwarz. In the previous quadrature f_d is supported where dt≥Y=X^(1−θ). Its r-th derivative has absolute integral ≤C_r||v||²_{H^r}d^(r−1)Y^(1/2−r), by the chain rule and integration in n=dt. Poisson, integrating by parts r times at the nonzero integer frequencies and summing |j|^(−r), bounds the difference of sum and integral by that same order. There are no boundary terms since the datum is compact and smooth. Summing up to D=X^(1−ε) the error is O_r(||v||²_{H^r} log(2D) D^r Y^(1/2−r)), which decreases like a power of X by the choice of r. The main integrals are zero by the moment. The correction of proper powers costs O((1+T)||v||²).

To see that this narrower class still detects any exterior quartet at distance b>0, use the odd witness of 195 with centers ±R, R=(1−η)T. Cut smoothly to the two outer bands of width θ'T, where 0<θ'<min(θ,b,1/2) and η=θ'/2. The distance of each center to the edges of its band is ηT. The error on the divisor tends to zero with any fixed derivatives by the physical-rate proof (choose B large relative to 1/η). Each cardinal can be cut in its own band before subtracting the reflections. Apply −∂²+1/4 and renormalize the cardinals as before to annihilate the moments per piece. The Weil energy of the odd test stays ≤−c<0 and the H^r norm of each piece is O_r(exp(−bR)); this holds for any fixed r by translation, cutoff with bounded derivatives and smoothness of the cardinals. For complex tests decompose into real and imaginary parts, or extend the real inequality by hermitian polarization.

In the physical form of the test (v,−v), the polar term vanishes, the archimedean part costs O(||v||²_{H^1}) and the combs internal to each half only see log n≤θ'T. Their modulus is O((1+T)^2 exp(θ'T/2)||v||²) by the trivial sum of Λ(n)/√n. All these costs tend to zero relative to the absolute margin c. The comb between halves enters with positive sign by oddness and is twice the cross sum with Λ, with the physical normalization of 121. Therefore that sum must be negative with fixed absolute margin for all large T. A subexponential floor for the tail, together with the previous quadrature, would prevent this because ||v||²_{H^r} decreases exponentially. This proves sufficiency without requiring control of all vectors of the original matrix. The tail of short cofactors still contains the Möbius sums of large d; it has not been bounded.

**Independent review of the localization and of the fixed-order quadrature: PROVED as a sufficient criterion.** The smooth compact extension gives |k^(j)|≤C_r||v||²_(H^r) for j≤r. Writing f_d(t)=φ(dt), with φ(n)=n^(−1/2)k(log(X/n)), the chain rule gives |φ^(r)(n)|≤C_r||v||²_(H^r)n^(−r−1/2). Integrating from Y and changing variable contributes d^(r−1)Y^(1/2−r), with the written exponents. There are no boundary terms and Poisson is summable for r≥2. After summing d≤D, the exponent of X is (1−θ)/2−r(ε−θ), strictly negative. The main integral vanishes exactly by the moment and the correction of proper powers only costs O(1+T)||v||².

Each cardinal can be cut in its own outer band before combining it with the reflection. The centers are at distance θ'T/2 from their edges and the superexponential decay controls any fixed number of derivatives, also after applying the moment operator. Thus the odd test keeps W≤−c, while each piece has H^r norm O_r(exp(−bR)). The internal combs only see shifts ≤θ'T and are bounded by exp(θ'T/2) times a polynomial and the squared L² norm. Since θ'<min(b,1/2), that cost tends to zero, as do the archimedean and polar parts.

The correlation between the halves of the odd test is −k, so the comb, which enters W with minus sign, contributes +2 times the cross sum of Λ. Its negativity with fixed margin is therefore the correct consequence. The proposed floor must be uniform over the admitted real tests at each scale of the sequence; when applied to these pieces its error tends to zero by the exponentially small H^r norm. This contradicts the margin under an exterior quartet and proves only the declared sufficiency. The divisor identity and the quadrature neither estimate the tail nor assert that the condition suffices for each test without the norm budget.

**Polylogarithmic cofactor via theta and quadrature of growing order.** In the previous criterion it suffices to treat m<T^16, with X=exp(2T). A sufficient formulation: for each fixed sufficiently large L, on data with zero moment supported in (0,4log T) with finite norm G_L(v)=sup_{j≥0}||v^(j)||₂/(L^(j+1)(j!)²), prove a floor −exp(o_L(T))G_L(v)² for the tail d>X/T^16, along a single sequence T→∞. The constants 4 and 16 are chosen with slack.

First justify the logarithmic localization of the witness. The physical datum of ξ in the bilateral variable of 195 is a multiple of the even kernel Φ of POWER_WEIGHTED_COEFFICIENT_034. The theta series and its derivatives of each FIXED order are O(exp(−c exp(2|y|))) at both ends. Dividing the transform by z−w at a zero preserves that property: if the previous datum is f, the new one solves −g'−wg=f and is written g(y)=exp(−wy)∫_y^∞exp(wt)f(t)dt; in the left tail use minus the integral from −∞ to y by the vanishing at w. The integrals preserve the estimate with smaller c; the equation controls the fixed derivatives. Iterating m_w times uses the successive vanishings and gives the same decay to each cardinal. Translate to ±R, R=T−2log T, and cut each cardinal in its own band of width 4log T, leaving a fixed margin at the ends for smoothing. The tail begins at distance 2log T−O(1) from the center, so the error weighted by exp(|y|/2), including fixed derivatives, is O(exp(T/2−c' T⁴)) (absorbing constant or polynomial factors by reducing c'). The fixed negative energy is preserved as in 195.

Convolve each truncated cardinal with the compact Gevrey bump of 119 before applying −∂²+1/4. It can be chosen with ||ψ^(j)||₁≤L₀^(j+1)(j!)² for all j (the Fourier bound exp(−c|τ|^(2/3)) implies that estimate by inversion, gamma integration and fixed support). Choose the radius small to avoid zeros at the selected points. The two additional derivatives only increase the fixed L. Young gives G_L(v)≤C exp(−bR) for the final piece of the odd witness, with L fixed according to the quartet. The estimate of the internal combs now costs only a polynomial in T times ||v||².

For the quadrature take r=floor(T), Y=X/T^8, D=X/T^16. For k=v*v one has ||k^(j)||∞≤L^(j+2)(j!)² G_L(v)². The r-th derivative of f_d from the previous paragraph introduces the polynomial ∏_{i=0}^{r−1}(−∂_s−i−1/2) in k, besides t^(−r)(dt)^(−1/2). The sum of the moduli of its coefficients is ≤(r+2)^r. Therefore one can take as quadrature constant (C_L r³)^r G_L(v)², including the Poisson sum for r≥2. The total error over d≤D, relative to G_L(v)², is ≤C log(2D)√Y [(C_L r³)D/Y]^r. With D/Y=T^(−8), its logarithm is ≤T−5r log T+O_L(r+log T), which tends to minus infinity. The main integral is still exactly zero. This pays absolutely for the removed divisors in this class, and the same contradiction via an odd witness proves sufficiency. The remaining sum still includes d of order almost X, even for m=1; no cancellation in that variable is claimed.

**Independent review of the polylogarithmic cofactor: PROVED as a sufficient criterion.** The theta formula of [POWER_WEIGHTED_COEFFICIENT_034](../phase-211-sign-sandbox/POWER_WEIGHTED_COEFFICIENT_034.md) gives the decay exp(−c exp(2|y|)) of the even kernel and its fixed derivatives. The integral solution of −g'−wg=f has that decay on the right; on the left the opposite integral is used since F(w)=0. After each division by z−w the vanishing of remaining order is left, so one can iterate up to m_w. This justifies the double decay of the cardinals, without keeping an exponential homogeneous term in either tail.

The centers ±(T−2log T) lie in the middle of the outer bands of width 4log T. Leaving a fixed margin before convolving keeps the final support inside those bands; the removed part begins at distance 2log T−O(1), giving weighted error O(exp(T/2−c'T⁴)) with the fixed derivatives required by Weil and the operator. The Gevrey 3/2 bump admits the weaker Gevrey 2 bound written. Young allows moving ALL derivatives onto the bump, without requiring uniform control of derivatives of the cutoff of growing order. The two derivatives of the operator and the cardinal normalizations are absorbed by increasing a fixed L that may depend on the quartet. Therefore G_L(v)≤Cexp(−bR), while the internal combs only cost a polynomial in T times the squared L² norm.

For k, Cauchy–Schwarz using v^(j) and v gives L^(j+2)(j!)²G_L(v)². The absolute sum of the coefficients of the differential polynomial is ∏_(i=0)^(r−1)(i+3/2)≤(r+2)^r; together with (r!)² and Poisson this gives (C_Lr³)^r, without an uncontrolled growth constant in r. The support requires n≥X/T⁸=Y and the sum of d^(r−1)log d up to D costs ≤D^rlog(2D). With r=floor T and D/Y=T^(−8) the exponent T−5rlog T+O_L(r+log T) remains, strictly decreasing with slack.

The hypothetical floor must be uniform over all admitted data for each fixed L. Thus one can fix the L of the witness and apply the same sequence: its exponentially small G_L norm makes the floor error, the proper powers and the internal combs tend to zero, contradicting the fixed negativity of Weil. Sufficiency is proved, not that floor. The residual cofactor satisfies m<T^16, but the divisor d may still be almost X; no bound on its Möbius sums is obtained.

**A single one-sided Möbius form for all short cofactors.** Keep X=exp(2T), D=X/T^16 and define for real data

    Q_T(w)=−Σ_{D<d≤X} μ(d)(log d)/√d · (w*w)(log(X/d)).

A floor −exp(o_L(T))G_L(w)² along a common sequence T→∞ for each fixed sufficiently large L, for data with zero moment in (0,12log T), suffices. More precisely, only translations of a datum of width 4log T are used. For S_h v(u)=v(u−h), (S_h v*S_h v)(s)=(v*v)(s−2h). Thus the exact tail of 195 is

    Σ_{1≤m<T^16} m^(−1/2) Q_T(S_((log m)/2) v).

The terms with dm>X vanish by support. The moment is multiplied by m^(−1/4) and G_L is preserved by translation. The new support ends before 12log T. All the outer coefficients are positive and sum to O(T^8), so the loss in the floor remains subexponential. The enlargement of the support is for the criterion on Q_T; the quadrature of width 4log T is not reapplied there.

The difficulty of a direct absolute estimate is also identified. Under RH the classical Mertens bound |M(t)|≪_ε t^(1/2+ε) gives by partial summation |Q_T(w)|≪_{ε,L} X^ε (1+log X)^2 G_L(w)²: for k=w*w, |k|+|k'|≪_L G_L(w)² and the weight (log d)k(log(X/d))/√d has derivative ≪_L(1+log d)d^(−3/2)G_L(w)². The endpoints satisfy the same bound. By arbitrariness of ε one obtains the subexponential ceiling. Therefore the proposed one-sided bound is equivalent to the global sign; invoking Mertens with exponent 1/2+ε to prove it would be circular. 340 recorded a related obstacle for two copies of μ in a rectangle, with another form. Here exactly one copy and a single common cutoff D are kept. The identity does not prove cancellation in μ.

**Independent review of the single form and of the equivalence: PROVED.** Translation by h=(log m)/2 takes k(s) to k(s−log m), so that the tail identity reproduces exactly the weight 1/√(dm) and the argument log(X/(dm)). The terms dm>X are zero by support. The moment is multiplied by exp(−h/2)=m^(−1/4), while all L² norms of derivatives and G_L are invariant. Since h<8log T, the support stays strictly inside (0,12log T). The outer weights sum to O(T⁸); the floor condition must be uniform in the data in order to apply it to all those translations. The quadrature is not used again with the enlarged support.

For the converse under RH, let f(t)=(log t)t^(−1/2)k(log(X/t)). Partial summation on (D,X] contains M(X)f(X)−M(D)f(D)−∫_D^X M(t)f'(t)dt, with the global minus sign of Q_T. The lower boundary is NOT omitted: for a general datum of support up to 12log T it may be nonzero. Its modulus is O_(ε,L)(X^εlog X G_L(w)²), the same as the sufficient bound for the rest. Cauchy–Schwarz controls k and k' without a factor of the support length. This verifies the written ceiling uniformly over the admitted data, including the non-integer cutoff D via M(D).

For each fixed L the arbitrariness of ε makes the logarithm of the quadratic norm, divided by T, have limsup ≤0; thus one obtains a majorant exp(o_L(T)), not a choice of ε depending on the datum. Under RH it holds at all scales and, therefore, along the required common sequence. Together with the previous sufficiency it gives exactly the declared equivalence, without proving the new floor. [340](ROUND_340_A.md) is an antecedent of the Mertens obstacle for a block with two copies; it is not an earlier identity of this form with a single copy of μ.

**Effective arithmetic obstruction: semiprimes with a fixed factor have exponential negative contribution.** In the previous form Q_T fix a prime q and a single real Gevrey test w of fixed compact support in (0,∞) with M₀=0, M₁≠0, where M_j=∫u^j exp(−u/2)w(u)du. One can take w=φ'−φ/2 for a nonnegative nonzero Gevrey bump; integration by parts gives M₁=−∫exp(−u/2)φ(u)du. For X sufficiently large the lower cutoff D does not affect this test. In the subsum d=qp with p prime distinct from q one has

    Q_T^(q)(w) ∼ −(2 log q/q) M₁² √X/(log(X/q))³.

Indeed μ(qp)=1. The quantitative PNT applied by partial summation in p, over a fixed multiplicative interval around X/q, replaces the sum by the integral of dp/log p with error O_{q,w}(√X exp(−c√log X)); the polynomial factors in log X are absorbed by reducing c. This follows from π(t)−Li(t)=O(t exp(−c√log t)) and from the size O(log X/√X) and total variation of the same order of the smooth weight on that interval. With s=log(X/(qp)), k=w*w, U=log(X/q), the integral is exactly

    −(√X/q) ∫ exp(−s/2) k(s) [1+(log q)/(U−s)] ds.

The moments of orders zero and one of exp(−s/2)k(s) are M₀² and 2M₀M₁, both zero; the second equals 2M₁². Expanding (U−s)^(−1)=U^(−1)+sU^(−2)+s²U^(−3)+O_w(U^(−4)) proves the equivalent with strict sign. Hence even ONE family of true semiprimes violates any subexponential floor separately. The sought bound for Q_T requires compensation with other integers. This does not refute the bound for the full sum. 073 already exhibited obstructions through semiprime sectors in another contrast; here the first nonzero moment and its constant are determined for the one-sided Möbius form itself.

**Independent review of the fixed semiprime sector: PROVED.** For w=φ'−φ/2, integration by parts with the weight exp(−u/2) gives M₀=0 and M₁=−∫exp(−u/2)φ(u)du<0. Its fixed support forces d into a fixed multiplicative interval of X, eventually above D; p=q falls outside for large X. The sign is negative because μ(qp)=+1 and the definition of Q_T carries a minus.

The substitution p=(X/q)exp(−s) transforms dp/√(qp) into (√X/q)exp(−s/2)ds. The ratio log(qp)/log p is exactly 1+log q/(U−s); this verifies the factor 1/q, with no missing square root of q. The convolution has moments M₀², 2M₀M₁ and 2M₁²+2M₀M₂. The first two are zero and the third is 2M₁². The geometric expansion of 1/(U−s) introduces no factorial, giving exactly the main term −(2log q/q)M₁²√X/U³ and remainder O_(q,w)(√X/U⁴).

The weight of the sum in p has supremum and total variation O_(q,w)(log X/√X) on an interval of length O_q(X). The quantitative PNT, by partial summation, therefore produces O_(q,w)(√X(log X)^Cexp(−c√log X)), absorbable by reducing c and smaller than √X/U⁴. The constants depend on the fixed test and prime, without asserting uniformity for growing q. The contribution is exponentially negative relative to the fixed Gevrey norm; it only refutes a separate floor for the sector and forces compensation in the total. The semiprime antecedent of 073 refers to another contrast, not to this constant of Q_T.

**Effective compensation between two complementary sectors.** Fix the test w of the previous paragraph and 0<δ<1/2. In the support of Q_T take all d=hp with p prime and h≤X^δ, without restricting the number of factors of h. The joint contribution is equivalent to −2M₁²√X/(log X)³. The complement has the opposite equivalent. Both statements are unconditional for this fixed test.

Write V=log X, f(s)=exp(−s/2)(w*w)(s), J(U)=∫ f(s)/(U−s)ds. Since d lies between two fixed multiples of X, eventually p>h for the whole sector, and p is the unique largest prime. One has −μ(hp)=μ(h), even for h not squarefree. For each h, repeat the prime integral of the previous paragraph with sign μ(h). The error of the PNT approximation is O_w((√X/h)poly(V) exp(−c_δ√V)), uniform since p has size comparable to X/h and log(X/h)≥(1−δ)V. The sum of errors keeps decay exp(−c'_δ√V) relative to √X. The exact main term of the integrals (the constant term integrates to zero) is

    √X Σ_{h≤X^δ} μ(h)(log h)/h · J(V−log h).

On the whole interval of U considered, J(U)=2M₁²/U³+O_w(U^(−4)) and J'(U)=O_w(U^(−4)) by the two vanishings. The primitive A(t)=Σ_{h≤t} μ(h)log(h)/h tends to −1, as verified in 195. By partial summation, the previous sum without √X is −J(V)+o(V^(−3)): write A(t)=−1+o(1), separate first t≤K fixed, where the error integrated with |J'| dt/t costs O_K(V^(−4)), and then t>K, where the error costs O(sup_{t>K}|A(t)+1| V^(−3)), including the upper endpoint. The contribution of the constant −1 leaves −J(V) by the boundary formula. This gives the first equivalent.

For the total Q_T of the fixed test, partial summation in d and the quantitative PNT M(t)≪t exp(−c√log t) give O_w(√X exp(−c'√V)): the support is d≈_w X and the variation of the weight is O_w(V/√X). Subtracting the previous sector proves the second equivalent. In particular cancellation between those two sectors does occur, even beyond any fixed inverse power of log X relative to √X. This is very far from the floor exp(o(T)) and is not uniform in the tests of the criterion.

**Independent review of the complementary sectors: PROVED for fixed test and δ.** On its support d≈_w X and h≤X^δ, δ<1/2, one has p≈_w X/h>h for X sufficiently large uniformly in h. Thus p is the unique largest prime, there is no duplication of integers and p does not divide h; the identity −μ(hp)=μ(h) also holds if h is not squarefree. The size and variation of the weight of the prime sum are O_w(V/√X), while the error of π at p≈X/h is O((X/h)exp(−c_δ√V)). Summing their products and Σ_(h≤X^δ)1/h=O_δ(V) preserves the exponential error relative to √X.

With Y=X^δ, Abel writes the main sum as A(Y)J(V−log Y)+∫₁^Y A(t)J'(V−log t)dt/t. The constant part A=−1 gives exactly −J(V); the upper term is not omitted. For A+1, the interval up to fixed K costs O_K(V^(−4)), and the remainder, including the endpoint Y, costs O_δ(sup_(t>K)|A(t)+1|V^(−3)). First V→∞ and then K→∞ prove the equivalent. Since the second moment of f is 2M₁², the sign and constant are −2M₁².

Finally, in the total Q_T the cutoff D lies below the fixed support and partial summation with M controls all boundaries and the variation by O_w(√Xexp(−c'√V)). The complement is an exact difference of sectors, from which the opposite positive main term follows. The result is not uniform as w or δ vary toward the extreme, nor does it reach the scale exp(o(T)); it does not provide the sufficient estimate of the form in the full class.

**Common square compensator for variable functions.** Fix 0<δ<1/2 and V=log X=2T. On ALL real tests with zero moment supported in (0,8log T), the sector S of the d=hp with h≤X^δ and the complement simultaneously admit the forms

    Q_S(w)=−P_X(w)+O_δ(√X exp(−c√V)||w||²_H¹),
    Q_compl(w)=P_X(w)+O_δ(√X exp(−c√V)||w||²_H¹),

with P_X ONE AND THE SAME positive semidefinite quadratic and c>0. The width guarantees that the support of k=w*w does not cross the cutoff d>X/T^16. Neither M₁≠0 nor a fixed test is required.

Set A_V(t)=Σ_{h≤exp(δV)}μ(h)(log h)h^(−1+t). For some ε_δ>0 and large V, A_V(t)≤−1/2 uniformly in 0≤t≤ε_δ/√V. Indeed the primitive in the variable z=log h is A(z)=−1+O(exp(−c₀√z)) for z≥1 by the quantitative PNT and Abel, and bounded down to zero. The twisted sum is exp(tδV)A(δV)−t∫₀^{δV} exp(tz)A(z)dz. The constant −1 leaves −1. Choose ε_δ with tz≤c₀√z/2 on the whole interval; the rest costs O(exp(−c₀√(δV)/2)+t), also at t=0. Define P_X as the integral over [0,ε_δ/√V] of

    √X exp(−Vt) (−A_V(t)) [∫w(u)exp((t−1/2)u)du]² dt.

To justify both formulas, the physical support in d goes from X/T^16 to X. In the PNT estimate per h of the previous paragraph, extending the multiplicative interval to this width only adds fixed powers of T: |k|+|k'|≪||w||²_H¹, the logarithmic length is ≤16log T and d^(−1/2)≤T^8/√X. With p≥X^(1−δ)/T^16 the saving exp(−c_δ√V) stays uniform after summing 1/h. The constant integral is zero by the moment. In the remaining one insert 1/(V−log h−s)=∫₀^∞ exp(−(V−log h−s)t)dt; the convolution factorizes into the written square. For t≥ε_δ/√V use |A_V(t)|≪V²exp(δVt), and the square ≤8log T exp(16t log T)||w||²₂ by Cauchy–Schwarz. Integrating this tail costs the declared error. For the total Q_T, the same support, derivative bounds and PNT for M(d) give the same type of uniform error by partial summation. Subtracting S completes the proof. The error is still exponential in T, although it no longer depends on the choice of a test normalized in H¹.

**Independent review of the common compensator: PROVED with the stated support.** The quantitative estimate of A(z)+1 allows writing the twisted sum by Abel. Its constant part contributes exactly −1, boundaries included; the error is O(exp(−c₀√(δV)/2)+t) on choosing ε_δ with t√(δV)≤c₀/2. On the initial bounded interval of z it only adds O(t), and t=0 is covered by the boundary. Thus A_V(t)≤−1/2 uniformly, independently of w, and the integral defining P_X is positive semidefinite for real data.

The support of k is in (0,16log T), so the lower cutoff of Q_T removes no term of the smoothed sum. Uniformly for h≤X^δ, one has p≥X^(1−δ)/T^16>h, so the representation is still unique. Cauchy–Schwarz controls k and k' by ||w||²_(H¹) without a constant depending on its choice; the new range of d only adds fixed powers of T to the variation of the weight. The PNT error and its sum over h keep exp(−c_δ√V) after absorbing those powers.

The Laplace insertion is absolutely legitimate because V−log h−s≥(1−δ)V−16log T>0. The transform of the convolution is the real square of ∫w(u)exp((t−1/2)u)du. In the tail, |A_V(t)|≤CV²exp(δVt) and Cauchy–Schwarz give an integral dominated by √X·poly(V)exp(−c_δ√V)||w||²₂. The total Q_T is estimated with the same H¹ uniformity via the Mertens PNT. Subtracting the sector produces exactly the same P_X with opposite sign. The constants may depend on δ, not on the test nor on T. The support is not automatically extended to 12log T, where the lower cutoff could intervene, nor is the subexponential floor of the global criterion reached.

**Sign failure of the compensator when the cutoff splits the autoconvolution.** Keep the previous S,δ,V and set w_T(u)=w₀(u−8log T), with w₀ fixed smooth of compact real support and zero moment. If J₀=∫_{x<0}exp(−x/2)(w₀*w₀)(x)dx is nonzero, then

    Q_S(w_T) ∼ −J₀ √X T^(−8)/V.

Indeed s=16log T+x and the cutoff d>D selects exactly x<0. The prime density for each h produces the factor T^(−8) from exp(−s/2). Summing the constant parts yields J₀ Σ_{h≤X^δ}μ(h)/h, which is O(exp(−c√V)) by the quantitative PNT and the zero value of 1/ζ at 1. For the part with log h, set W=V−16log T, J(U)=∫_{x<0}exp(−x/2)(w₀*w₀)(x)/(U−x)dx. One has J(W)=J₀/W+O(W^(−2)) and J'(U)=O(U^(−2)) on U≥(1−δ)V−16log T. The same Abel summation with A(z)→−1 gives −J(W)+o(V^(−1)), separating bounded z from its tail. The single cutoff jump per h only adds its size to the variation of the PNT weight. All PNT errors are √X poly(V)exp(−c√V), smaller than the equivalent.

Take a Gevrey bump φ≥0 of integral one and radius <1/10 centered at zero. With w₀(u)=exp(u/2)(φ(u+1)−φ(u−1/2)), the moment is zero. The pieces of the weighted autoconvolution are centered at −2, −1/2 and 1 with masses 1,−2,1: the cutoff leaves J₀=−1. Changing the second center from 1/2 to 2 gives J₀=1. Thus the same sector S takes both signs at a scale exceeding √X exp(−c√V) by a factor tending to infinity. The tests fit in (0,12log T) and their H¹ norms are constant. They are even realized with the real discrete translations of the criterion: take m=floor(T^16 exp(−4)), v(u)=w₀(u−2); the shifted center differs from 8log T by O(T^(−16)), and the truncated mass converges to J₀ by continuity. This prevents extending the approximation Q_S≈−P_X with P_X≥0 and the previous error to all the required translations. It does not prevent compensation in the full Q_T.

**Independent review of the sign failure at the cutoff: PROVED.** Translating w by 8log T takes its convolution to 16log T+x and multiplies the weight exp(−s/2) by T^(−8). The cutoff d>D is exactly equivalent to x<0. The sum with μ(h)/h tends to zero with error exp(−c_δ√V), while the sum with μ(h)log h/h has primitive tending to −1. Abel, keeping the boundaries, gives −J(W)+o(V^(−1)); the expansion J(W)=J₀/W+O(W^(−2)) verifies the sign and factor of the equivalent. The jump of the weight at the cutoff only adds its size to the variation and keeps the PNT error uniform for this translated test.

Weighting w₀ by exp(−u/2) leaves two bumps of masses +1 and −1. Their convolutions have masses +1,−2,+1 with the written centers. The chosen radius separates those three supports from the zero cutoff. With centers −1 and 1/2 the first two masses lie to the left, giving J₀=−1; with centers −1 and 2 only the first remains, giving J₀=+1. The full moment is zero in both cases. The H¹ and Gevrey norms are constant under translation, and √XT^(−8)/V dominates the error √Xexp(−c√V).

Finally, (log floor(T^16exp(−4)))/2+2=8log T+O(T^(−16)). The fixed datum v=w₀(·−2) has positive support and fits in (0,4log T) for large T; the integer m satisfies m<T^16. The small variation of the cutoff and of the weighted factor preserves the equivalent and J₀ by continuity. Thus the counterexample is found among the translations actually used in the tail identity. It refutes the extension of the positive compensator with that error to the whole class of support 12logT, without contradicting the previous result of support 8logT nor the floor for the full Q_T.

**The boundary failure admits no fixed-rank correction.** For each integer n there are n simultaneous directions of each sign in the principal boundary form J₀, even with fixed support and zero moment. Consequently the translated sector S does not admit the previous approximation by a nonpositive form plus a fixed-rank correction, not even if that correction varies with T and its norm is arbitrary.

Real proof. Write w₀(x)=exp(x/2)f(x), ∫f=0, so that the polarized bilinear form is J(f,g)=∫ f(x) [∫_{−∞}^{−x} g(y)dy] dx. Simultaneous reflection of f,g changes the sign of J, since the total rectangle has integral zero. Hence J vanishes between two even functions or two odd ones. Choose n even Gevrey functions g_i, of mean zero and orthonormal in L², with support in (−1,1). For example use differences of symmetric bumps on disjoint annuli and normalize. Set h_i=g_i', odd with mean zero. Then J(g_i,h_j)=∫g_i(x)g_j(−x)dx=δ_ij. On the two lists g_i±h_i the form has matrices ±2I. Multiplying by exp(x/2) returns to the original tests. All can be realized with the same discrete translation m=floor(T^16 exp(−4)) of the previous paragraph.

In each fixed space of dimension n, the boundary equivalent at scale √X/(T^8 V) extends as convergence of matrices to −J by polarization (the expansion with error o(1) also holds for J₀=0). The H¹ norm matrices are fixed under translation. Therefore on one of those spaces Q_S≥c_n√X/(T^8 V)||w_T||²_H¹ for sufficiently large T. If the self-adjoint correction has rank r<n, its kernel meets that space; there the positive margin remains and any nonpositive approximant has error at least that size. The opposite argument holds for the other sign. It gives neither uniformity in growing n nor excludes a correction of growing rank, nor the compensation between S and its complement.

**Independent review of the two inertias and the fixed rank: PROVED.** The bilinear J is symmetric by Fubini over x+y<0. Reflecting both variables changes that half-plane into x+y>0; since both means are zero, the full rectangle contributes zero and the form changes sign. Hence its even-even and odd-odd restrictions vanish. For h_j=g_j', the antiderivative up to −x is g_j(−x), and J(g_i,h_j)=δ_ij with POSITIVE sign. Symmetry gives the same reverse crossing, so the lists g_i+h_i and g_i−h_i have matrices +2I and −2I. One can choose n even bumps of mean zero on disjoint annuli inside (−1,1); their derivatives and normalizations remain Gevrey for each fixed n.

Multiplying by exp(x/2) recovers the zero-moment data with fixed support. After first shifting by two, their supports lie in (1,3), so the same integer m=floor(T^16exp(−4)) realizes the admissible translation.
