The boundary expansion is a linear limit in the truncated quadratic, not just an equivalent for nonzero J₀. Polarizing over the finitely many combinations of a basis gives matrix convergence to −J; the H¹ norms are translation invariant and their Grams positive definite. Thus Q_S has spaces of both inertias with fixed margin relative to √X/(T⁸V).

For a correction of rank r<n, the kernel of its restriction to the positive space of dimension n is nontrivial, even if the correction and its norm depend on T. There the correcting form is zero and a nonpositive approximant does not compensate the positive margin of Q_S; the error in H¹ norm is at least c_n√X/(T⁸V), larger than the previous error √Xexp(−c√V). The opposite sign gives the analogous assertion for nonnegative approximants. Only fixed rank at the stated error is excluded, without uniformity in n nor obstruction to growing rank or compensation with the complement.

**Gathering the cofactors reverses the sign of the compensator.** Take the original tail d>D, ALL translations m<T^16 with their weights m^(−1/2), and classify by the same sector S of d=hp, h≤X^δ. For v with zero moment supported in (0,4log T), the gathered contribution of S is +P*_X(v)+O_{δ,L}(√X exp(−c√V)G_L(v)²), with P*_X≥0. The cutoff that prevented a representation by squares in each translation can be paid after gathering them. The gain here is in structure and main sign; the error is still too large.

Set k=v*v and K(s)=Σ_{m≥1}m^(−1/2)k(s−log m). For 0≤s≤S₀=16log T the sum coincides exactly with the truncated one, by support. For s>S₀ apply Poisson to the datum y^(−1/2)k(s−log y): its integral is zero by the moment. As in the growing-order quadrature, for r=floor(T) one obtains |K(s)|≤G_L(v)²(C_L r³)^r(exp(s)/T^8)^(1/2−r). Therefore, uniformly in 0≤t≤1/4, the tail of ∫exp((t−1/2)s)K(s)ds above S₀ is O_L(exp(−2T log T)G_L(v)²) eventually. Indeed at the endpoint the saving of (T^(−8))^r dominates (C_Lr³)^r and the remaining integral has exponential ratio r−t.

The FULL transform is ζ(1−t)[∫exp((t−1/2)u)v(u)du]²: for Re t<0 the sum is interchanged absolutely, and toward t=0 and 0<t≤1/4 it is continued by the Poisson tail; the pole at zero is removable by the moment. Its value at zero is zero. On 0<t<1, ζ(1−t)<0 by the alternating eta series.

The prime substitution and the Laplace integral of the compensator section are applied to the kernel K truncated to [0,S₀]. On that interval K and its first derivative are bounded by poly(T)G_L(v)² by direct summation. The jump at S₀ costs only another power of T in the variation bound. On the short interval 0<t≤ε_δ/√V replace the truncated transform by the full one with the previous error, using |A_V(t)|=O(1). The constant density term also falls within the error because of the zero value at t=0. For t≥ε_δ/√V it suffices to integrate the bound V²exp(δVt)poly(T)exp(tS₀) against exp(−Vt), obtaining the saving exp(−c√V). Thus P*_X is the integral over the short interval of √X exp(−Vt) A_V(t) ζ(1−t) times the indicated real square. Its two factors A_V(t) and ζ(1−t) are negative. The result refers to the sum with the exact weights of all m; it assigns no sign to the individual translations. The complement and the residue require control at subexponential scale to close the sign.

**The gathered complement requires compensation even after any fixed number of moments.** In the same tail with all cofactors, if v is a fixed nonzero Gevrey test with zero moment, let j≥1 be the order of the first nonzero moment M_j=∫u^j exp(−u/2)v(u)du. j exists by analyticity and uniqueness of the transform. With V=log X the gathered contribution of S and that of its complement are equivalent, respectively, to

    ±√X · (2j−1)! M_j² / ((j!)² V^(2j)).

Indeed, in the gathered compensator one has A_V(t)=−1+O(t+exp(−c√V)), ζ(1−t)=−1/t+O(1), and the transform of v starts with M_j t^j/j!. Integrating against exp(−Vt) up to ε_δ/√V and using the gamma integral gives the equivalent with positive sign. For the total first gather all divisors by n=dm: one obtains the sum with Λ(n), except for the removed contribution of d≤D, of norm o(1)G_L(v)² by quadrature. Since v has fixed compact support and zero moment, the continuous integral is zero. The sum with Λ(n) is O_v(√X exp(−c√V)) by ψ(x)=x+O(x exp(−c√log x)) and partial summation on the interval n≈_v X. Subtracting gives the negative sign of the complement.

Moreover, for each fixed r one obtains a fixed r-plane on which that complement is ≤−c_r √X V^(−2r)||v||²_H¹ for large T. Take v_j(u)=exp(u/2)φ^(j)(u), j=1,…,r, for a fixed Gevrey bump φ of integral one in (1,2). Their weighted transforms in the compensator are exactly (−t)^j Φ(t), with Φ(t)=∫exp(tu)φ(u)du. On 1≤Vt≤2, |Φ| is bounded below and A_V(t)ζ(1−t)≥c/t. By the positive definite Gram of the monomials y,…,y^r on [1,2] with weight exp(−y)/y, for any coefficient vector one obtains P*_X≥c_r√X Σ_j V^(−2j)|c_j|². The PNT and quadrature errors are uniform on the sphere of this fixed space by equivalence of norms. This rules out absorbing the complement through an isolated subexponential loss or through the exclusion of a fixed number of directions. The obstacle here appears already with fixed interior data and after gathering the cofactors, independently of the cutoff failure in isolated translations. No uniformity is given for growing r.

**Independent review of the gathered compensator: PROVED.** The Poisson datum y^(−1/2)k(s−log y) has integral exp(s/2)M₀²=0 and support y≥exp(s)/T⁸. Its r-th derivative norm is bounded by G_L(v)²(C_Lr³)^r(exp(s)/T⁸)^(1/2−r). Integrating from S₀=16log T against exp((t−1/2)s), with 0≤t≤1/4, leaves a majorant with logarithm −5Tlog T+O_L(T+log T), sufficient for the declared tail. For Re t<0, the absolute interchange gives ζ(1−t) times the square of the transform of v; the Poisson tail allows continuing to the positive range. The pole at zero is removable because the square has order at least two, and the value there is zero.

On the short range, ζ(1−t)<0 and A_V(t)<0, so the main term is POSITIVE. On [0,S₀], the direct sums of m^(−1/2) give polynomial bounds in T for K and K'; the cutoff only adds the jump at S₀ to the variation. This suffices for the uniform PNT with norm G_L². The truncated transform is replaced by the full one with the Poisson tail, including t=0. For the rest of the Laplace integral the truncated kernel is kept, bounded by poly(T)exp(tS₀)G_L², so the exponential denominator (1−δ)V−S₀ gives exp(−c_δ√V). Neither signs of individual translations nor an invalid absolute interchange at t>0 are used.

**Independent review of moments and of the r-plane: PROVED for each fixed order.** Analyticity of the transform of a nonzero compact test gives a finite first nonzero moment. As t→0, A_V(t)ζ(1−t)=1/t+O(1)+O(exp(−c√V)/t), and the square starts with M_j²t^(2j)/(j!)². The gamma integral gives (2j−1)!M_j²/((j!)²V^(2j)), with positive sign for S and no additional factor. The gathered total is exactly the sum of Λ minus the part of divisors already removed; the density equals √XM₀²=0 and the PNT for ψ gives O_v(√Xexp(−c√V)). Thus the complement has the opposite negative main term.

In the space spanned by the v_j, the transforms are (−t)^jΦ(t). Restricting to t∈[1/V,2/V] and setting y=Vt preserves the measure dt/t=dy/y. The Gram of the monomials controls ΣV^(−2j)|c_j|²; Φ(t) is bounded away from zero because Φ(0)=1. The H¹ and Gevrey norms are equivalent to the coefficient norm in this fixed space, and the exponential errors are o(√XV^(−2r)). This gives the stated uniform margin for the whole r-plane, not just its basis vectors. An exclusion of fixed codimension leaves some negative direction when taking r larger; neither uniformity for growing r nor a failure of the total sum, where the main terms do compensate, is asserted.

**Cost of making the compensator itself small: loss of sensitivity to nearby zeros.** Let v_T be real with support in (0,4log T), ||v_T||₂≤1 and zero moment. If P*_X(v_T)≤exp(o(T)), then, for each fixed complex z, its weighted transform M_T(z)=∫exp((z−1/2)u)v_T(u)du satisfies

    |M_T(z)| ≤ exp(−T/3+o_z(T)).

This concerns the strategy of paying P*_X individually; it does not presuppose a bound on the arithmetic residue. By homogeneity it holds when normalizing the family by any norm dominating L².

For the proof take I=[α/√V,2α/√V] with 0<2α<ε_δ fixed. On I the weight A_V(t)ζ(1−t)≥c√V and exp(−Vt)≥exp(−2α√V). Since √X=exp T, the mean quadratic norm (root of the average of |M_T|²) on I is ≤exp(−T/2+o(T)). Set L=4log T and n=floor(T/(3log T)). The Taylor approximation by the polynomial p_n of degree n at zero has error ≤√L exp(L|z|)(L|z|)^(n+1)/(n+1)! by Cauchy–Schwarz. For fixed z this error is exp(−T/3+o_z(T)), and on I it is ≤exp(−T/2+o(T)) by the additional factor V^(−(n+1)/2). Hence p_n has mean quadratic norm on I ≤exp(−T/2+o(T)).

After mapping I to [−1,1] affinely, the evaluation of a polynomial of degree n at fixed z costs at most poly(n)(C_z√V)^n times its mean quadratic norm on I. Indeed, expand in orthonormal Legendre polynomials: the three-term recurrence gives |P_j(y)|≤(3+2|y|)^j for the Legendre polynomials with P_j(1)=1, and the normalization adds √(2j+1). The transformed point has modulus O_z(√V). The cost is exp(T/6+o_z(T)), leaving exp(−T/3+o_z(T)) after multiplying by the norm of p_n. Adding the Taylor error proves the bound.

In particular, translating a piece of such a family to an endpoint ±T and reflecting it only multiplies its evaluations at a fixed bilateral coordinate w by factors of modulus ≤exp(|Re w|T); for the pieces M_T(1/2±w) appear. For |Re w|<1/3 even those amplified evaluations tend to zero. Therefore normalized witnesses required to have an evaluation of fixed size on that quartet cannot obtain it while paying P*_X separately at subexponential scale. This argument gives the number 1/3; its optimality for the isolated evaluation is established in the next paragraph. None of this excludes a bound for the sum of the two sectors preserving their cancellation.

**The exponent 1/3 is optimal for the isolated evaluation.** For fixed complex z≠0, there exist real tests with zero moment, support in a fixed compact subset of (0,∞) and L² norm one such that P*_X≤exp(o(T)) and log|M_T(z)|=−T/3+o(T). They also admit Gevrey normalization of order two with the same evaluation exponent. The binomial difference has antecedents in 241; here it is used to prove optimality for this concrete compensator.

Take n=floor(T/(3log T)), Δ_n=(δ_(1/n)−δ_0)/2 and a real Gevrey 3/2 bump φ≥0 with fixed support in (1,2) small enough that ∫exp(zu)φ(u)du≠0. Set φ_n(u)=φ(u)(1+cos(πnu)), f_n=Δ_n^{*n}*φ_n and v_n(u)=exp(u/2)f_n(u). The support lies in (1,3). The convolving measure has variation one. Its multiplier at frequency πn has modulus one and that of φ_n at that frequency converges to (∫φ)/2 by Riemann–Lebesgue. Thus ||v_n||₂ is bounded above and below by constants (use the fixed support and Cauchy–Schwarz for the lower bound). The modulation ensures that the normalization does not hide an exponential loss.

The transform M_n(t) is ((exp(t/n)−1)/2)^n ∫exp(tu)φ_n(u)du. In particular the first n moments, numbered from zero, vanish. At fixed z the last integral tends to that of φ and the factor has logarithm of modulus −n log n+O_z(n)=−T/3+o(T). For 0<t≤ε_δ/√V one has |M_n(t)|≤C(Ct/n)^n. Use |A_V(t)ζ(1−t)|≤C/t and exp(−Vt)≤1 in the representation of P*_X: its ceiling is C exp(T)(C/(n√V))^(2n)/(2n), with logarithm o(T) as an upper bound. Dividing by ||v_n||₂ preserves both assertions.

For the Gevrey version, differentiate the product with exp(iπnu). With L fixed sufficiently large, the Leibniz rule and the Gevrey bound of φ give G_L(v_n)≤C exp(C√n): after dividing by (j!)², the term with l derivatives of the modulation costs at most a constant times (C n)^l/(l!)² and is summed in l. The translations and multiplication by exp(u/2) on fixed support only change constants. The L² lower bound already obtained and √n=o(T) allow normalizing also by G_L without changing the rate. This excludes replacing 1/3 by a larger constant in the previous obstruction using only support, norm and smallness of the compensator. It is not asserted that these tests determine the sign of the full form.

**Localization by the cofactor of the product after quadrature.** Fix the test with M₁≠0 and δ of the previous paragraphs, H=X^δ, V=log X. To regroup S use its extension to all d=ph with h≤H and p>√X, summing all multiples m. For d>D it coincides with S, because p>D/H>√X eventually. What is added in d≤D has cost o(1) by the absolute per-divisor quadrature and the zero moment. This estimate holds for the whole added sum before dividing it again.

In this representation each n=dm≤X has at most one prime p>√X. Write n=pr and separate r≤H. Since p does not divide r, the exact coefficient of the packet of divisors is Σ_{h|r} μ(h)log(ph), equal to log p if r=1 and to −Λ(r) if r>1. For r>H only the h|r with h≤H are summed. For the interior packet r≤H, the joint contribution is

    −M₁² [(1−δ)^(−2)−1] √X/V² · (1+o(1)).

Indeed the term r=1 costs O_v(√X exp(−c√V)) by the zero moment and PNT for θ. For 2≤r≤H and pr in the fixed support n≈_v X the restriction p>√X is automatic. PNT for π, as in the uniform per-h estimate, gives the main term −√X Σ_{r≤H}Λ(r)J(V−log r)/r, with J(U)=2M₁²/U³+O_v(U^(−4)) and error relative to √X of order poly(V)exp(−c_δ√V). In this step the summation weight of the errors is Λ(r)/r, with sum O(V). By Σ_{r≤y}Λ(r)/r=log y+O(1) and Abel, the main term divided by −2M₁²√X is ∫₀^{δV}(V−u)^(−3)du+O(V^(−3)). This gives the declared coefficient.

The gathered total of S already has equivalent +M₁²√X/V², so the other packet, r>H in the extended representation, contributes +M₁²(1−δ)^(−2)√X/V² in equivalent. Thus, completing the sum over h|r in each interior product gives a NEGATIVE balance: the positive main term of the gathered sector depends on the products whose cofactor crosses the threshold. The equivalent of each packet is not transferred to the original cutoff d>D, since there the selection by r would alter the quadrature applied at the beginning.

**Independent review of the cost of smallness: PROVED with the stated evaluation scope.** On I, the factor A_Vζ is ≥c√V and its length is comparable to V^(−1/2); hence P*≤exp(o(T)) gives mean quadratic norm of M_T ≤exp(−T/2+o(T)). For n=floor(T/(3log T)), Stirling in the Taylor remainder gives −T/3+o_z(T) at a fixed point and −T/2+o(T) on I. The affine map to [−1,1] takes that point to modulus O_z(√V). The expansion in normalized Legendre polynomials controls the evaluation by poly(n)(C_z√V)^n, whose logarithm is T/6+o_z(T). Thus the rates T/2, T/6 and T/3 combine as asserted.

The pieces placed at the endpoints evaluate exp(±wT)M_T(1/2∓w). Therefore for |Re w|<1/3 those evaluations tend to zero. This only prevents building a normalized witness with fixed evaluation on that quartet while paying P* separately; it is not a general impossibility of detecting zeros or of preserving the compensation between sectors.

**Independent review of the optimality: PROVED for each fixed z≠0.** The difference measure has variation one and a multiplier of modulus one at πn. There the Fourier transform of φ_n tends to (∫φ)/2, and the fixed support turns that evaluation into an L² floor for f_n; multiplying by exp(u/2) preserves uniform upper and lower bounds. This justifies normalizing without losing an exponential. The factor ((exp(z/n)−1)/2)^n has logarithm −nlog n+O_z(n), and the remaining integral tends to the nonzero value chosen via the bump, giving −T/3+o(T). On the compensator range one obtains the majorant exp(T)(C/(n√V))^(2n)/(2n), whose logarithm is o(T).

For the Gevrey norm, Leibniz divided by (j!)² leaves for l derivatives of the modulation a majorant (Cn)^l/(l!)², after increasing a fixed L to absorb the derivatives of the bump. Its sum is ≤exp(C√n). Convolutions of variation one and multiplication by exp(u/2) on fixed support preserve this estimate. Since √n=o(T) and G_L has a positive floor by the L² norm, normalizing by G_L does not alter the rate either. Optimality of that isolated evaluation is proved, not a bound for the full form.

**Independent review of the packets by product: PROVED for the fixed test.** In d>D, p=d/h>D/H>√X uniformly. Extending to all d=ph with p>√X adds only a subfamily of d≤D, whose complete multiples have zero main term and absolute quadrature error o(1). Each d has only one such prime and no multiplicity is introduced in that estimate. After that extension, n=pr has a unique p>√X and p does not divide r. The complete coefficient for r≤H is Σ_(h|r)μ(h)log(ph), equal to log p at r=1 and −Λ(r) at r>1, with the written signs.

The first packet r=1 is controlled with θ and its density vanishes since M₀²=0. For 2≤r≤H, the PNT for π has uniform error summable with weights Λ(r)/r, and the sum of those weights is O(V). Abel on ΣΛ(r)/r=log r+O(1) gives the integral (1/2)[(1−δ)^(−2)−1]V^(−2), with error O(V^(−3)); multiplying by −2M₁² produces exactly the negative interior constant. The difference with the positive total gives the exterior constant M₁²(1−δ)^(−2). Only the added total was small before separating by r: it is not inferred that each added packet is. Hence the equivalents are kept for the extended representation and not for the packets of the original cutoff, without controlling the residue at the level of sign.

**Prime cutoff at √X: the comparable strip pays the interior deficit.** Consider now the sector of divisors containing some prime p>√X, with all cofactors m gathered. Fix v as before with M₁≠0 and B>0 fixed such that k=v*v has support in (0,B). After completing the quadrature over d, set R₀=√X exp(−B) and n=pr. In units M₁²√X/V² the balances of the packets r≤R₀ and r>R₀ tend respectively to −3 and +4. In particular the second main term is localized at factors r,p comparable to √X within constant ratios, without a fixed cutoff X^δ.

The per-divisor completion costs o(1) in the sectoral total as in the preceding paragraph. The condition p>√X makes the assignment unique. Now all h|r are summed and the coefficient of n is log p for r=1 and −Λ(r) for r>1. If r≤R₀, pr≥X exp(−B) automatically implies p>√X except for weightless endpoints. The previous proof with H=R₀ goes through with uniform PNT in p of size at least √X, and Σ_{r≤R₀}Λ(r)/r=log R₀+O(1). Replacing the upper limit of the integral by V/2−B gives the coefficient −3.

For r>R₀ necessarily r≤√X and √X<p<exp(B)√X. In the double sum replace π(p) by dp/log p and ψ(r) by dr. The error is O_{B,v}(√X exp(−c√V)): on that rectangle the weight k(log(X/(pr)))/√(pr) is O(X^(−1/2)) and its variation in each variable, with the other fixed, is O_{B,v}(X^(−1/2)); apply PNT by parts in each variable and sum the masses of the other, O_B(√X). The indicator p>√X imposes a fixed boundary. The change s=log(X/(pr)) in the integral gives exactly

    −√X ∫ exp(−s/2)k(s) log(1+2(B−s)/V) ds,

since the integral in r goes from R₀ to √X exp(−s), with integrand 1/[r(V−s−log r)]. The constant and linear terms in s integrate to zero. The quadratic term of the expansion of the logarithm, including the outer sign, contributes +4M₁²√X/V² and the Taylor error is O_{B,v}(√X/V³). In that packet the r that are proper prime powers contribute in modulus O_{B,v}(X^(1/4)poly(V)) by trivial counting of those powers in r≈√X and of the number of p, so the semiprimes with two distinct primes give the same main term. The identity is obtained for the sector with p>√X; it does not presuppose that the other sector of the global problem is small.

**Pointwise cancellation of the Laplace weights at the prime cutoff √X.** Take B=8log T, v real with zero moment supported in (0,B/2), f(s)=exp(−s/2)(v*v)(s), M(t)=∫exp((t−1/2)u)v(u)du, R=V/2−B. In the extended representation with p>√X the two previous packets are, up to O(√X exp(−c√V)||v||²_H¹), integrals against the SAME positive measure √X exp(−Vt)M(t)²dt on t>0. Their exact weights in the PNT approximations are

    interior: −Σ_{r≤exp R} Λ(r) r^(t−1),
    comparable strip: exp(Rt)/t.

For the interior it suffices to insert the Laplace integral of 1/(V−log r−s) in the previous prime substitution; the term r=1 has zero density by the moment. For the strip use the exact integral of the previous logarithm and the Frullani identity −log(A−s)+log A=∫₀^∞exp(−At)(exp(st)−1)dt/t with A=V/2+B. Since ∫f=0, only the square M(t)² and the factor exp(−At)/t remain. At t=0 it converges since M(0)=0. The double PNT remains uniform for B growing as chosen: the factors exp(O(B)) and the variation of the weights controlled by ||v||²_H¹ only cost fixed powers of T. The strip thus produces a positive semidefinite quadratic in its full density, without selecting the first nonzero moment.

The difference of the two weights has a cancellation before integrating in t. By the quantitative PNT and Abel, for z≥0 one has Σ_{r≤exp z}Λ(r)/r=z+C+E(z), |E(z)|≤C' exp(−c√z), enlarging the constant on compacts. By parts the net weight is exactly

    1/t − C − exp(Rt)E(R) + t∫₀^R exp(zt)E(z)dz.

For 0<t≤c₁/√V with c₁ sufficiently small, this is 1/t−C+O(exp(−c₂√V)+t) uniformly. The terms exp(Rt)/t of the packets have cancelled pointwise, even where separately they exceed 1/t exponentially. On the rest of the integral both original weights are bounded in modulus by exp(Rt)(O(V)+1/t); M(t)²≤(B/2)exp(Bt)||v||²₂, and V−R−B=V/2 allows absorbing the tail into the PNT error. The favorable sign of the net weight on the short range describes the sector p>√X. Compensation with the divisors without that prime and control of the error at subexponential scale are still needed; the theorem does not transport the two packets separately to the initial cutoff.

**Independent review of the prime cutoff and of the constants −3,+4: PROVED for fixed test and B.** The per-divisor extension is made before separating packets, adding a subfamily of the absolute quadrature with zero main term. The complete coefficient is −Λ(r) except at r=1. The interior integral up to V/2−B is (1/2)[(V/2+B)^(−2)−V^(−2)], and multiplying it by −2M₁² gives exactly −3 in the written normalization. In the comparable rectangle, the measure is dp/log p for p and dr for r; integration in r gives log(1+2(B−s)/V). Its quadratic term, with the outer sign, produces +4 because the second moment is 2M₁².

The double PNT is paid by the variation of each variable and the mass of the other, keeping O_(B,v)(√Xexp(−c√V)). The proper powers of r have weighted number O(X^(1/4)poly(V)); even with trivial counting of p and the weight X^(−1/2) they contribute only that same order. Therefore the distinct semiprimes give the comparable main term. These packets are those of the extended representation, not those of the original cutoff d>D, nor an estimate of the remaining global sector.

**Independent review of Frullani, Abel and growing uniformity: PROVED in the extended representation.** The strip has density −√X∫f(s)log(A−s)ds, with A=V/2+B; adding log A integrates to zero. Frullani then gives +√X∫exp(−At)M(t)²dt/t, absolutely convergent because s<B<A and M(0)=0. With respect to the common measure its weight is exactly exp(Rt)/t. The interior has negative weight ΣΛ(r)r^(t−1). If A_Λ(z)=z+C+E(z), partial summation gives ΣΛ(r)r^(t−1)=(exp(Rt)−1)/t+C+exp(Rt)E(R)−t∫₀^Rexp(zt)E(z)dz. Subtracting verifies all the boundaries and the sign of the net formula; at z=0 one has A_Λ(0)=0 and E(0)=−C.

Choosing c₁ with t√R sufficiently small, exp(Rt)E(R)=O(exp(−c₂√V)) and t∫exp(zt)E(z)dz=O(t), uniformly on the short range. For the tail, the identity V−R−B=V/2 leaves exp(−Vt/2) and absorbs the powers and the factor 1/t from t=c₁/√V. In the double PNT, exp(B)=T⁸ and the bounds of k,k' by ||v||²H¹ only add fixed powers of T to the variation and the masses on the rectangles; the saving exp(−c√V) survives with reduced c. The short main term is favorable, but the error is still outside the sufficient scale. It is not asserted that completing or separating divisors with that error is uniform in H¹ for the original cutoff.

**Exact closure of the partition by √X and positive contribution of the squares.** In the extended representation form the complement with all divisors whose prime factors are ≤√X. Write n_s for the part of n supported on those primes, with their full exponents. Its coefficient is exactly Σ_{d|n_s}−μ(d)log d=Λ(n_s), taking Λ(1)=0. Thus, for n=pr with p>√X and r>1, both sectors contribute −Λ(r) and +Λ(r) and cancel for EACH n, including all fluctuations of the prime sampling. At n=p only log p remains. When there is no large prime Λ(n) remains; in the support n≥X/T^8>√X this only occurs with nonzero weight for proper powers. It is thus proved that pursuing the exact pairing at this cutoff returns the whole sum with Λ; after subtracting the proper powers, identified below, the sum over the original primes is recovered. No estimate of the term log p at n=p results from cancelling the mixed products.

For v real supported in (0,4log T), k=v*v, one can moreover identify the operator of proper powers with absolute precision:

    Σ_{p^j≤X, j≥2} (log p)p^(−j/2) k(log(X/p^j))
      = (1/2)(∫v(u)du)² + O(exp(−c√V)||v||²_H¹).

At j=2 apply PNT for θ to p in [√X/T⁴,√X] with weight p^(−1)k(V−2log p). The endpoint and the variation integral, using |θ(p)−p|≪p exp(−c√V) on this range, cost O((1+log T)exp(−c√V)||v||²_H¹), absorbable by reducing c. The change s=V−2log p gives exactly (1/2)∫k(s)ds in the density. For j≥3 it suffices to count at most O(V X^(1/3)) pairs and apply (p^j)^(−1/2)≤T⁴/√X on the support. Their cost is O(poly(T)X^(−1/6)||v||²₂). The square surviving in the density uses the ordinary moment, distinct from the moment with weight exp(−u/2). Thus the whole part of proper powers admits a floor with decreasing error, without sign hypothesis or additional condition on the moment. The prime terms keep the global difficulty. The equivalence of this partition with the initial prime sum is recorded so as not to iterate the same separation as a closing mechanism.

**Independent review of the closure and of the powers: PROVED with the stated identity precision.** The sum of divisors without a large prime is exactly Λ(n_s). If n=pr, p>√X, then p has exponent one and does not divide r; for r>1 both coefficients are −Λ(r) and +Λ(r), so they cancel term by term. If there is no large prime, the coefficient is Λ(n). On the support n>X/T⁸>√X, its remaining nonzero terms are proper powers. Thus the sum of BOTH sectors reconstructs the sum with Λ; only after subtracting those powers does it reconstruct the prime block. That distinction was made precise in the statement so as not to identify both sums literally.

At j=2, the density of θ is dp and the weight is p^(−1)k(V−2log p). The substitution ds=−2dp/p gives the factor 1/2, and Fubini identifies ∫k=(∫v)². In the error, E_θ(p)=O(p exp(−c√V)) multiplies a derivative O(p^(−2)||v||²H¹); its integral costs only O(log T), without a factor √X. The boundaries satisfy the same bound, and the power of log T is absorbed by reducing c. This is uniform on the H¹ sphere, not only for a fixed test.

For j≥3 there are O(VX^(1/3)) pairs before weights and log p≤V; on the support the factor (p^j)^(−1/2) is ≤T⁴/√X. Therefore its absolute cost is O(poly(T)X^(−1/6)||v||²₂), smaller than the exponential error of logarithmic root. The final approximation has decreasing absolute error relative to ||v||²H¹ and positive ordinary main term. It does not require that ordinary moment to vanish, does not assert a sign term by term and does not estimate the residual prime sum.

**A fixed test with negative square bias on a proportional band.** There is a fixed real Gevrey test v, of compact support in (0,∞) and zero weighted moment, such that RH is equivalent to the raw prime sum B_X(v)=Σ_p(log p)p^(−1/2)(v*v)(log(X/p)) being eventually ≤−1/16. If RH fails this same test gives excursions of both signs above X^η along sequences for each 0<η<Δ. The direct antecedents are the one-sided test 104 and the spectral localization of 115; here the constant bias is obtained in the raw autoconvolution of fixed logarithmic width via the square term of 195.

Take φ real nonnegative, smooth Gevrey, supported in (1,2), of integral one. Let φ_A(u)=φ(u/A)/A and v=φ_A'−φ_A/2. With bilateral transform L_v(z)=∫exp(−zu)v(u)du one has L_v(z)=(z−1/2)L_φ(Az), L_v(1/2)=0 and ∫v=−1/2. On the critical divisor the sum of |(iγ−1/2)L_φ(Aiγ)|², including multiplicities, tends to zero as A→∞: integration by parts and the unit count of 175 give summable domination, and there is no zero ordinate. Moreover, the same estimate over ALL real ordinates γ of the zeros gives the choice of a threshold without assuming RH. Choose A large enough that this sum is <1/32. Exclude also the A with L_φ(Az)=0 for some z=ρ−1/2; they are at most countable since z≠0 and L_φ(0)=1.

In the smooth explicit formula for Λ with weight n^(−1/2)(v*v)(V−log n), V=log X, the pole at one has coefficient L_v(1/2)²=0. Each zero contributes −exp((ρ−1/2)V)L_v(ρ−1/2)². This is obtained by Laplace inversion of −ζ'/ζ, with the contour moved down at least to Re s=−1 in the usual variable s=z+1/2, and an error O_v(exp(−3V/2)) on that line by the functional equation and fast decay of the test in fixed strips. No trivial zero is crossed. The zero series converges absolutely for each V with summable coefficients by the unit count. On removing the proper powers there remains in addition −1/8+o(1) by the previous paragraph. Under RH the spectral series has modulus <1/32 and hence the announced ceiling holds eventually. If Δ>0 all coefficients at the distinct points are nonzero after grouping multiplicities. The lemma of 115 gives excursions of opposite signs with arbitrary exponent η<Δ (use an intermediate exponent to absorb the bounded term). This excludes the eventual ceiling. The test is existential; the generic choice of A does not certify a particular numerical value. A favorable sequence for this single test does not allow concluding RH. Nor has the arithmetic ceiling been proved without RH.

**Completely explicit eight-box test, without selection by the zeros.** Let U=1_[0,2]/2, φ=U^{*4}, v=φ'−φ/2 and k=v*v. In the inequality of the previous paragraph one can use directly

    k(s)=(∂²−∂+1/4) [ Σ_{j=0}^8 (−1)^j binom(8,j) (s−2j)_+^7 /(2^8·7!) ].

In particular RH is equivalent to the eventual ceiling Σ_{Xe^(−16)≤p≤X}(log p)k(log(X/p))/√p ≤ −1/16 with this single piecewise polynomial function and an explicit proportional band. Neither a generic parameter nor the computation of individual ordinates is involved in building the weight.

The truncated-power formula is the convolution of eight uniforms (by Laplace or finite differences); differentiation gives k because v is the derivative minus half of the convolution of four boxes. One has L_v(z)=(z−1/2)((1−exp(−2z))/(2z))⁴, with removable value at zero. No exterior zero of the centered ξ can annihilate this multiplier: the zeros of the box lie on the imaginary axis and z=1/2 is not a nontrivial zero. The critical zeros possibly annihilated are omitted from the series of 115 without altering the exterior supremum. The weight k is at least C⁴ and L_v(z)² decays like O((1+|Im z|)^(−6)) in fixed strips. This suffices for the previous contour shift: on horizontals of good height the logarithmic derivative grows at most polylogarithmically, and on the vertical s=−1 its growth is O(log(2+|Im s|)). The support touching zero adds no boundary mass, since k and its first derivatives vanish there.

Under RH, |L_v(iγ)|²≤(1+1/(4γ²))|γ|^(−6). Z1 gives |γ|>10; by symmetry and the unit count of 175 the sum over the zeros costs at most 202 Σ_{j≥10}log(4+j)/j⁶ ≤202 Σ_{j≥10}j^(−5)≤202/(4·9⁴)<1/32. The ordinary moment again gives −1/8 on removing the squares. Without RH use the same oscillatory detection of 115 on the nonzero coefficients. The finite regularity of the spline is used in the explicit formula and in the estimate of squares; it is not intended to be introduced into the Gevrey norm of the growing quadrature. The eventual ceiling is still an unproved arithmetic inequality.

**Unconditional interval for the explicit scalar test.** With Z1–Z3, the eight-box test satisfies B_X(v)<−1/16 on ALL of 200≤V=log X≤230. This is the scale of a single test; it is not the radius of the sign of the full form.

To see it let S_j=Σ_n Λ(n)n^(−j/2)k(V−j log n). The elementary inversion B_X=Σ_{j≥1}μ(j)S_j is exact by Σ_{j|l}μ(j). One has ||v||₁≤3/2, ||v||∞≤3/4 since φ'=((δ₀−δ₂)/2)*U^{*3}, hence ||k||₁≤9/4 and ||k||∞<2. For j≥3 there are fewer than 2V possible j, at most exp(V/3) integers per j and each weight costs ≤2V exp(8−V/2). The total tail ≤4V²exp(8−V/6)<1/1000 on the interval (it decreases for V≥200).

For j=1,2 the explicit formula gives the density exp((1/j−1/2)V)L_v(1/j−1/2)²/j, minus the contributions at the zeros ρ with the same factor replacing 1 by ρ (both in exponent and in argument). The trivial zeros −2l, l≥1, are included by the same shift: on lines of negative odd real part in the variable of ζ, the functional equation gives logarithmic growth and the support of the test contributes exp(−(V−16)|Re s|/j) to the integral in the limit. Their absolute sum for each j≤2 is ≤(9/4)Σ_{l≥1}exp(−(2l/j+1/2)(V−16))/j<10^(−10). The densities are 0 and 1/8, respectively.

For heights |γ|>G=3·10¹², let z=ρ/j−1/2. Since |Im z|≥|γ|/2, |Re z|≤1/2 and |1−exp(−2z)|<4, the box formula gives |L_v(z)|²≤65536|γ|^(−6) (use |z−1/2|≤2|z|). The sum of |γ|^(−6) over this tail is ≤400 log(2G)/(G−1)^5 by the unit count of 175, summing by decreasing integral in both signs. For j=1 multiply by exp(V/2)≤exp(115), and even with the constant 65536 the product is <1/1000. For j=2 the exponential is ≤1. For |γ|≤G all lie on the line: for j=1 the sum is <1/32 by the box certificate; for j=2 one gains exp(−V/4) and uses the same bound 65536|γ|^(−6) with Σ_{|γ|>10}|γ|^(−6)<1 by 175, leaving <1/1000. Hence B_X≤−1/8+1/32+4/1000<−1/16. This interval illustrates why obtaining the correct sign in finite computations, even for enormous X, does not verify the eventual ceiling.

**Moving test with unconditional sign at all large scales, and loss of detection.** Set m=ceil(V/8), φ_m=U^{*m}, v_m=φ_m'−φ_m/2 and k_m=v_m*v_m, with U=1_[0,2]/2. Without RH or verification of critical zeros at large height,

    Σ_p (log p)k_m(log(X/p))/√p = −1/8 + O(X^(−1/20)).

Here only |Imρ|>14 and the unit count are used. It does not extend the criterion of the fixed test: the response of the new filter to each possible exterior zero also tends to zero exponentially.

To verify it keep S_j and the inversion of powers of the previous paragraph. The norms ||v_m||₁≤3/2, ||v_m||∞≤3/4 remain uniform, the support of k_m ends at 4m≤V/2+4. The densities for j=1,2 are identical to the previous ones. In the right half-plane of z=ρ−1/2 the box factor |(1−exp(−2z))/(2z)|≤1/|γ|; in the left one it is ≤2/|γ| and exp(V Re z)≤1. Reserve four powers of the squared modulus (eight box factors) to make the factor |z−1/2|² summable with the unit count. The right sum over zeros is O(exp(V/2)14^(−2m+8)) and the left one O((2/14)^(2m−8)). Both are O(exp(−V/20)). At j=2 the argument is z=ρ/2−1/2, with exponential ≤1 and box factor ≤4/|γ|; the same reservation gives O((4/14)^(2m−8)). For the trivial zeros use ||k_m||₁≤9/4 and V−4m≥V/2−4 in the preceding estimate. The contour shift is done for each fixed m before applying the uniform bounds to the resulting series.

For j≥3 divide the support of n^j into dyadic intervals [R,2R] with R≥Y/2, Y=exp(V−4m). There are O(V) intervals and O(V) exponents. In each there are ≤(2R)^(1/3) integers n, and each summand has modulus ≤2V/√R. Thus the absolute total costs O(V³Y^(−1/6))=O(exp(−V/20)). The density of squares with the sign of μ(2) remains, giving the equivalent. The computation shows why increasing the smoothing order linearly solves the scalar inequality of that family even at unbounded scales: its own multiplier suppresses the exterior signal before it grows. The arithmetic obligation of the eight-box test, whose weight stays fixed, remains open.

**Growing smoothing that does preserve detection.** In each block 2^l≤V=log X<2^(l+1) fix the same order m_l≥4 of boxes per factor. If m_l→∞ and m_l=o(2^l), under RH the raw prime sum tends to −1/8 uniformly in each late block. If Δ>0, for each 0≤η<Δ in EACH sufficiently late block there are two scales with sums of opposite signs and modulus >exp(ηV). For example m_l=max(4,floor(2^(l/2))) allows a single prescribed moving test. The argument is not extended to an arbitrary order varying within the block.

For the proof use the spectral coefficients of S₁, grouped by centered zero z: a_{z,l}=−mult(z)(z−1/2)² U(z)^(2m_l), U(z)=(1−exp(−2z))/(2z). In the strip |Re z|≤1/2 one has |U(z)|≤2/|Im z|<1 on the divisor. The unit count gives Σ_z|a_{z,l}|≤C uniformly since m_l≥4. For each fixed exterior z, log|a_{z,l}|=O_z(1+m_l) in absolute value because U(z)≠0; thus |a_{z,l}|≥exp(−o(2^l)). Under RH the sum over the axis tends uniformly to zero by dominated convergence. Under both hypotheses S₂ has density 1/8 and uniformly bounded zero error (under RH it decreases like exp(−V/4)), using |U(ρ/2−1/2)|≤4/|γ|. The trivial zeros and the powers j≥3 are paid as in the linear moving test with V−4m_l=V−o(V). Therefore outside RH it suffices to detect the series of S₁ with O(1) perturbation.

Apply the Gaussian argument of 115 with frozen order l, mean H=3·2^l/2 and fixed relative radius δ<1/3 small enough to choose η(1+δ)<d<Δ. Its rates f_τ(z) depend on z,c,τ and not on l. The divisor with U(z)≠0 can be used as a fixed set. The unique maximum selected in 115 satisfies f_τ>max(d,max f₀) and is separated from the rest by a positive constant. Since d>0 and c<1, the maximizer is exterior in the right half-plane. Its term has modulus ≥exp(f_τ H−o(H)); the rest costs ≤C exp((f_τ−g)H) for some g>0 by the uniform sum of coefficients. Likewise the unmodulated average and the Gaussian tails have the ceilings of 115 with uniform constants. With the two nonnegative weights of 115 both signs result within the central interval of the block. In the integration outside the block only the series with the SAME frozen order is continued, whose tails are removed before inferring anything about the moving test. The margin d>η(1+δ) absorbs the O(1) error. This criterion rigorously separates a sublinear growth by blocks that preserves the excursions from the choice m=ceil(V/8) that suppresses them. It does not provide the one-sided bound in the detecting regime.


**Independent review of the fixed test with bias: PROVED as an equivalence, without proving the arithmetic ceiling.** Integration by parts gives L_v(z)=(z−1/2)L_φ(Az), with zero weighted moment and ordinary moment −1/2. The decrease of the sum over all ordinates as A grows does not require RH: the uniform Fourier decay for A≥1 and the unit count allow dominated convergence. Each entire function A↦L_φ(Az_ρ) is not identically zero, since at zero it equals one; excluding its countable set of real zeros preserves arbitrarily large choices of A. Thus no exterior coordinate is lost.

In the inversion of −ζ'/ζ(s), the factor is L_v(s−1/2)². The pole at one vanishes; moving down to Re s=−1 crosses no trivial zeros and leaves O_v(exp(−3V/2)). Removing the proper powers adds −(∫v)²/2=−1/8+o(1). Under RH the total spectral modulus is <1/32; outside RH the lemma of 115, with an exponent intermediate between η and Δ, absorbs the bounded term and gives both excursions. It is an application of the one-sided criterion of 104 and the oscillation of 115 with the explicit square bias, not a new proof of RH nor a criterion via a single favorable sequence.

**Independent review of the eight boxes: PROVED, with sufficient finite regularity.** The convolution U^{*8} has exactly the denominator 2⁸·7! and the nodes 2j of the formula. Applying (∂−1/2)² gives k, including the coefficient −1 of the first derivative. One has φ∈C², v∈C¹ and k∈C⁴; near both endpoints k vanishes to order at least five. No boundary term appears. The square of the transform decreases like |Im z|^(−6), sufficient for the contour and for the approximation of squares that only requires H¹. No Gevrey regularity is attributed to it for the growing-order quadratures.

The only zeros of the box factor are iπn, n≠0; the remaining factor only vanishes at z=1/2. No exterior zero is eliminated. The eliminated critical ones are omitted in 115, keeping all the exterior ones and their supremum. For the critical budget, the count of 175 costs 100log(3+j) per interval and multiplicities; reflecting gives 200 and the factor 1+1/(4γ²) is absorbed into 202. Then log(4+j)≤j and Σ_{j≥10}j^(−5)≤∫₉^∞t^(−5)dt. The final inequality is exact: 202·32<4·9⁴. The weight is built without selecting individual ordinates; the certificate uses Z1 and the unit count.

**Independent review of the interval 200≤V≤230: PROVED with joint margin.** The inversion by μ(j) is exact because each prime power has coefficient Σ_{j|l}μ(j). The densities of S₁,S₂ are respectively zero and 1/8, and μ(2)=−1. In both cases |Re(ρ/j−1/2)|≤1/2, |1−exp(−2z)|<4 and |z−1/2|≤2|z| for |γ|>10; hence |L_v(z)|²≤1024|z|^(−6)≤65536|γ|^(−6). The factor 1/j of the residue only improves that bound.

The high tail of S₁ at the endpoint V=230 is <0.000279, using the majorant 65536·400log(2G)exp(115)/(G−1)⁵; that of S₂ is smaller than that same budget without exp(115). The low contribution of S₂ is ≤65536exp(−50)<1.265·10^(−17), and the tail j≥3 is ≤4·200²exp(8−200/6)<1.593·10^(−6), decreasing from 200. The two trivial tails together are <2·10^(−10). Therefore ALL these errors jointly are <1/1000, even stronger than the margin 4/1000 used in the text. The low part of S₁ costs <1/32. The support and C⁴ allow moving the contour to negative odd lines and summing the trivial ones: the factor exp(−(V−16)|Re s|/j) dominates the polynomial factors. The whole interval is certified, without inferring an eventual ceiling from that finite verification.

**Independent review of the moving test: PROVED uniformly for large V.** For m≥2, the uniform convolutions have sup norm ≤1/2; the derivative identity gives ||v_m||₁≤3/2 and ||v_m||∞≤3/4, hence ||k_m||₁≤9/4 and ||k_m||∞<2 with constants independent of m. The contour is moved with m fixed, and then the uniform estimates are applied to its absolutely convergent series. Reserving eight box factors leaves a summable majorant independent of m for the rest of each coefficient, including the quadratic factor z−1/2.

The worst zero tail is O(exp((1/2−log(14)/4)V+O(1))), with 1/2−log(14)/4<−0.15. The other two cost O(exp(−log(7)V/4+O(1))) and O(exp(−log(3.5)V/4+O(1))). The support satisfies 4m≤V/2+4, so the sum of powers j≥3 is O(V³exp(−V/12+O(1))); the trivial zeros have a larger saving. All these terms are O(exp(−V/20)) with absolute constants, independently of the jumps of m=ceil(V/8). Exactly −1/8 survives from the squares. Each possible exterior zero is likewise exponentially suppressed: this moving result proves neither the eventual inequality of the fixed weight nor a statement of preserved spectral detection.


**Independent review of the sublinear smoothing by blocks: PROVED with the frozen order.** The active divisor can be fixed once: the zeros of the box factor only eliminate critical points, and each selected exterior point has coefficient ≥exp(−C_zm_l−C_z)=exp(−o(2^l)). The absolute sum of all coefficients is bounded by that of order four, via |U(z)|≤2/|γ|<1. These are exactly the two uniformities needed by the argument of 115: global ceiling independent of l and subexponential floor for the chosen maximizer.

First choose c and τ as in 115, without dependence on l. The penalized rate has a unique fixed maximizer and a fixed gap g>0 with respect to the rest; since c<1 and the winning rate is positive, that point has positive real part and survives the filter. Its amplitude exp(−o(H)) dominates the rest bounded by Cexp((f−g)H), while the unmodulated average has a strictly smaller rate. The Gaussian tails use only Σ|a_{z,l}|≤C and are therefore uniform as well. With H=3·2^l/2 and δ<1/3, the whole central interval lies inside the block; the series continued outside it keeps the SAME m_l and is removed before returning to the moving observable. No regularity of m in other blocks is assumed.

The strict inequality η(1+δ)<d<f absorbs both the floor exp(−o(H)) of the coefficient and the O(1) perturbation, including η=0. Under RH, dominated convergence on the axis gives uniform o(1); the powers and trivial zeros have terminal support 4m_l=o(V), so their errors are also uniformly o(1). This establishes both signs in each late block outside RH and the limit −1/8 under RH. It does not justify the same conclusion for arbitrary orders varying within the block nor prove a one-sided ceiling in the detecting regime.

**Exact slope threshold for the frozen order in short windows.** Write U(z)=(1−exp(−2z))/(2z). Define α*=0 if there are no centered zeros with b=Re z>0; otherwise set α*=max_{b>0} b/(−2log|U(z)|). The maximum exists since the positive quotients tend to zero in height. By Z1, α*≤1/(4log14)<1/8. For 0<α<1/4, on each interval H≤V≤H+2√H use m=ceil(αH) boxes per factor (one and the same m on the whole interval). If α>α*, the sum tends uniformly to −1/8; if 0<α≤α*, there are values tending to +∞ and to −∞ in EACH sufficiently late interval. Thus the eventual ceiling condition in these windows for all slopes 0<α<1/8 is equivalent to the global sign. This statement does not estimate α* from prime arithmetic.

For the proof assign to each zero with U(z)≠0 the rate f(z)=b+2αlog|U(z)|. The rates tend to −∞ in height; if the set is empty there is no series S₁. Otherwise its maximum F is attained on a finite set and there is a strict gap relative to the rest (if any). The sign of F is strictly negative above the threshold, positive below and zero at the positive threshold. For y=V−H=O(√H), the sum of the terms outside the maximal set is O(exp((F−g)H+O(√H))) with some g>0. Indeed reserve eight factors of U for the summability of |z−1/2|² and use H−4/α in the rate, with exp(4b/α) uniformly bounded and m≥αH. Above the threshold the same bound with F applies to the whole set. The other powers and the trivial zeros are o(1) uniformly: V−4m≥(1−4α)H−4 and the filter of S₂ is bounded by (4/14)^(2m−8) after reserving eight factors.

If F≥0, choose among its maximizers the largest b=B; it is positive, since |U|<1. Evaluate at y=√H+t with 0≤t≤L fixed. Dividing the series by exp(FH+B(√H+t)), the maximizers of smaller real part disappear uniformly. What remains is a real trigonometric polynomial in t with distinct nonzero frequencies, one for each zero with f=F and b=B. Each coefficient has modulus between two strictly positive constants independent of H: the rounding only introduces |U(z)|^{2(ceil(αH)−αH)}. The phases may depend on H. For L fixed sufficiently large the average of the polynomial has modulus O(1/L), while that of its square is ≥c>0: integrate each frequency, using the positive separation on that finite set and the conjugate pair. Since the sup norm is bounded, the mean of the modulus is ≥c' and the positive and negative parts both have mean ≥c'/4 after enlarging L. Both signs result with fixed margin, even with the uniform error o(1). Therefore there are excursions of order at least exp(FH+B√H) in both directions, also if F=0. The frozen order and the positive shift √H are essential for asserting the boundary result.


**Independent review of the exact slope threshold: PROVED, including the endpoint F=0.** For b>0, |U(z)|≤1/|γ|≤1/14; the threshold quotients tend to zero in height, so that, if there is any exterior zero, the positive supremum is attained and α*≤1/(4log14). The rates f tend to −∞ and the set of maximizers is finite with positive gap relative to the rest. If α>α*, every rate is negative, including the active critical ones and those of the left half-plane, so the maximum is strictly negative; at α=α*>0 it is exactly zero.

The reservation of factors is verified without a constant depending on the number of zeros: each modulus at V=H+y is the product of mult(z)|z−1/2|²|U(z)|⁸, exp((H−4/α)f(z)), exp(4b/α), |U(z)|^{2(ceil(αH)−αH)} and exp(by). The first factor is summable, the third is uniformly bounded for fixed α, the fourth is ≤1 and the last ≤exp(√H) for 0≤y≤2√H. Thus the gap gives the uniform bound of the rest, even with negative F. The other powers are O(poly(H)exp(−(1−4α)H/6+O(1))) and the trivial ones smaller; S₂ keeps the density 1/8 and its zero series decreases geometrically in m. All are o(1) for each fixed α<1/4.

When F≥0, its maximizers have b>0, since log|U|<0. Among them fix the maximal B. At y=√H+t, t in a fixed interval, the other b lose exp(−c√H); the non-maximizers lose exp(−gH+O(√H)). The points with b=B and f=F form conjugate pairs of distinct nonzero frequencies. Their coefficients, after normalizing, have moduli between positive constants; the rounding only runs over the compact factor |U|^{2θ}, 0≤θ<1. The averages over a fixed long interval are uniformly small for all phases, and the quadratic mean has a uniform floor by the Gram of that finite set. The uniform sup bound turns that floor into positive and negative mass bounded away from zero. This gives the two margins after the o(1) error, at points inside the window for large H. At F=0 the factor exp(B√H) still diverges: that is the precise reason for the positive shift and the frozen order. The equivalence uses all the prescribed slopes, not a single slope above the threshold.

**Fixed frequency per block and single slope 1/8.** Let τ be a fixed rational. Replace φ_m by exp(iτu)φ_m before applying ∂−1/2 and form the ordinary complex autoconvolution. Denote the same sum over primes by Bτ(V), with m=ceil(H/8) on H≤V≤H+2√H. The transform of the new kernel is (z−1/2)²U(z−iτ)^{2m}. The pole at z=1/2 remains exactly cancelled. The modulation itself has antecedents, among them the average of 115; here it changes the spectral rate of the arithmetic observable itself with fixed linear slope.

Under RH each Bτ stays uniformly bounded in these blocks for large H (constant depending on τ). Indeed in S₁ all box factors on the axis have modulus ≤1. Eight reserved factors give a finite absolute sum, even at exact coincidence of frequency, where U(0)=1. In S₂ write w=ρ/2−1/2, d=Re w≤0. The majorant |U(w−iτ)|≤exp(−2d) allows reserving eight factors and absorbing the rest into exp(d(V−4m+16))≤1, even without RH. The density of S₂ is U(−iτ)^{2m}/8. The L¹ and L∞ norms of the new v_m cost O(1+|τ|), by the product rule, which preserves the bound of the powers j≥3. For the trivial zeros w=−2n/j−1/2 with j=1,2 the same bound without reservation gives a polynomial in n times exp(Re w (V−4m)), summable and o(1).

If there exists a zero z=b+iγ with b>0, choose rational τ sufficiently close to γ. At τ=γ, Jensen gives U(b)≥exp(−b), hence the rate fτ=b+(1/4)log|U(z−iτ)| is ≥3b/4. Continuity preserves a positive rate. The rates tend to −∞ in height for fixed τ and for b≤0 are ≤b/2. The maximum F>0 has a finite set, a gap and largest real part B>0. The reservation of eight factors from the previous paragraph works with rounding bounded by exp(2) on the whole strip. At V=H+√H+t there remains, after dividing by exp(FH+B(√H+t)), a complex trigonometric polynomial with distinct frequencies and coefficients of modulus uniformly bounded away from zero, plus o(1). The mean of its squared modulus on [0,L] has positive diagonal and cross terms O(1/L), uniformly in the phases; fix L large. Therefore in each late block the supremum of the modulus of Bτ is ≥c exp(FH+B√H). Thus a single slope suffices if all fixed rational frequencies are checked. The sufficient arithmetic bound is limsup H^{-1}log(1+sup_V|Bτ(V)|)=0 for each τ. Obtaining it directly in primes is pending. This criterion does not enlarge the certified window.

In prime variables the precise cost is visible. Set h=φ_m*φ_m and D=∂−1/2. By commutation of derivative and convolution, the new kernel is exp(iτu)(D+iτ)²h(u). Therefore exp(−iτV)Bτ(V) is the sum of (log p)p^{−1/2−iτ}[(D²h)+2iτDh−τ²h](V−log p). Controlling each summand of the bracket separately loses even the cancellation of the continuous density: integrating against dp and changing to u=V−log p yields the factor exp((1/2−iτ)V) times the transform of the bracket at 1/2−iτ, exactly zero by its double factor. For τ≠0, the transform of the term −τ²h there is −τ²U(1/2−iτ)^{2m}≠0. Every estimate by parts needs to keep that cancellation, or first subtract the continuous density.

**Quantitative localization of the obstruction for fixed τ.** For δ=γ−τ, the modulus is computed without a zero series:
|U(b+iδ)|²=exp(−2b)(sinh²b+sin²δ)/(b²+δ²).
The individual rate is positive exactly when sinh²b+sin²δ>exp(−6b)(b²+δ²). Every right zero contributing with positive rate satisfies |δ|<exp(4b)≤exp(2), since |U(b+iδ)|≤1/|δ|. Conversely, if |δ|≤√b, rotating by exp(iδ) in the box integral gives |U|≥U(b)cos δ≥exp(−b−δ²): here log cos t≥−t² for |t|≤1/√2, since cos t≥1−t²/2 and log(1−s)≥−2s on [0,1/2]. Hence fτ≥b/2. More precisely the first positive boundary around δ=0 has δ²=18b+O(b²) as b↓0: use log U(w)=−w+w²/6+O(w⁴) and the resulting real-analytic function of (b,δ²), whose derivative in δ² at the origin is −1/24 for fτ. The implicit function theorem gives the branch and its local sign. 

Consequence for the arithmetic work: if all zeros in the band |γ−τ|≤exp(2) are known to lie on the line, there is an unconditional bound for that test at that frequency, even if there were exterior zeros outside the band. The critical points have |U|≤1; the left ones are absorbed as in S₂. The remaining right ones have strictly negative rates with a gap by the decay in height, so their sum decays by the reservation of eight factors. This inference only transfers known local information. Conversely, a prime bound with rate ≤ε for a mesh of step h excludes each right zero covered by a node at distance ≤h/2 with b≥h²/4 and b>2ε, by the lower bound of the rate and the maximum argument of the previous paragraph. No uniformity in the constants of a finite mesh is needed.

**Arithmetic cutoff above the square root for the modulated test.** In S₁ use Λ(n)=−Σ_{d|n}μ(d)log d. For fixed τ and m=ceil(H/8), the contribution of d≤exp(0.55H) is Oτ(H exp(−cH)), uniformly in the block, with absolute c>0. Unlike the subexponential cutoff of the raw block (§ «Small divisors»), this cutoff exceeds even exp(V/2) for sufficiently large H. The exponential profile of the boxes is used instead of suppressing it through the support length.

Indeed, let F_d(t)=(dt)^(−1/2)kτ(V−log(dt)) for t>0, extended by zero. Its integral is exactly zero by the polar factor in the transform. The integer quadrature error is bounded by C||F_d^{(4)}||₁ by Euler–Maclaurin of order four, with all boundaries zero for large m. Differentiating four times and changing to u=V−log(dt) one obtains the bound C d³ exp(−7V/2) Σ_{l=0}⁴ ∫exp(7u/2)|kτ^{(l)}(u)|du. Here kτ=(∂−1/2)²(exp(iτu)U^{*2m}(u)), with U the box density. Each derivative of order ≤6 of the convolution is distributed over distinct boxes; the derivative of a box is a finite difference of two atoms. The L¹ norm with weight exp(7u/2) is therefore bounded by Cτ U(−7/2)^{2m}, using the multiplicativity of the weight and absorbing up to six constant factors. Summing d³log d up to D=exp(0.55H) yields Oτ(H exp(−cH)), where c=7/2−2.2−(1/4)log((exp(7)−1)/7)>0 (log 7>1.8). The bound uses absolute values in d. The remaining problem is the weighted total of the larger divisors, where the cancellation of μ(d) matters again. No bound for that remainder is obtained by simply interchanging d with its cofactor, since μ(d) stays on the long variable.

**Upper end of the product and of the divisors.** In the expansion by d and cofactor l, the whole absolute mass corresponding to n=dl≥exp(0.98H) is Oτ(exp(−0.04H)) uniformly for large H. The same bound serves for any subfamily of those pairs, in particular for d≥exp(0.98H). To see it tilt the box by exp(−10u). Its mass is U(10)<1/20. In the previous expression of kτ at most two boxes are differentiated, whose tilted derivatives are finite measures. Reserving another box for the sup norm and using Young with the others in L¹ gives |kτ(u)|≤Cτ exp(10u)20^{−2m}. On the indicated range u≤0.02H+2√H. Moreover
Σ_{dl≤exp V} log(d)/√(dl) ≤2exp(V/2)Σ_{d≤exp V} log(d)/d = O((1+V)²exp(V/2)).
Thus the upper rate is ≤0.7−log(20)/4<−0.048, and the term O(√H+log H) leaves the asserted margin. Only |μ|≤1 was used.

In particular one can first remove the full contribution of d≤exp(0.55H) via quadrature and then remove n≥exp(0.98H) among the remaining d via this absolute bound. The only total requiring a subexponential estimate lies in exp(0.55H)<d≤n<exp(0.98H), with cofactor l<exp(0.43H). The first removal does require summing the full cofactor for each small d.


**Independent review of the cutoff d≤exp(0.55H): PROVED for each fixed τ.** The full integral of F_d is exp(V/2)L_{v_τ}(1/2)²/d=0. Although for the largest d the support may go below t=1, Euler–Maclaurin is used on the WHOLE line, with F_d extended by zero: the integer sum coincides with the sum over positive cofactors and the integral is still the full vanishing integral. That integral is not replaced by the one over [1,∞), which might not vanish. For large m the support stays away from zero and the endpoints have ample regularity for four integrations by parts; the periodic Bernoulli kernel of order four gives an absolute constant times ||F_d^(4)||₁.

Each derivative in t contributes t^(−1) and a fixed operator in u. The change dt=−tdu leaves exactly d³exp(−7V/2) times the combination of |k_τ^(l)| weighted with exp(7u/2), l≤4. Differentiating the kernel up to that order requires up to six derivatives of the spline U^{*2m}. They are distributed among different boxes, whose derivative is (δ₀−δ₂)/2; the weighted variation is (1+exp(7))/2. The remaining factors have weighted mass U(−7/2)=(exp(7)−1)/7. Replacing at most six factors only costs a constant, and the derivatives of the modulation cost C_τ, without factors growing in m.

Summing absolutely the coefficients −μ(d)log d costs Σ_{d≤D}d³log d≤CD⁴logD. Since 2m≤H/4+2 and V≥H, the logarithm of the majorant is −cH+O_τ(logH), with c=7/2−2.2−(1/4)log((exp(7)−1)/7)=0.0367056117…>0. Its positive sign also follows without decimal computation from log((exp(7)−1)/7)<7−log7 and log7>1.8. The window ceiling ensures 0.55H>V/2 for large H. The short range is thus certified even above the square root using absolute values; the long remainder is not controlled, nor can μ be moved automatically onto the small cofactor.

**Reduction to two long factors with explicit coefficients.** Use the classical Vaughan identity only as an equality of convolutions. The additional input here is the two vanishing moments of the kernel, which allow unconditionally removing BOTH type I terms with exponential error in the modulated sum. Let Y=exp(0.275H), a=μ restricted to [1,Y], b=Λ restricted to [1,Y]. With * Dirichlet convolution, one has exactly
Λ=a*log−a*b*1+b+(μ−a)*(Λ−b)*1.
It is verified by expanding, using 1*μ=δ₁ and 1*Λ=log. The term b lies outside the support because V−4m≥H/2−4.

In a*b*1 the divisor variable d is ≤Y² and its coefficient has modulus ≤Σ_{q|d}Λ(q)=log d. By the same quadrature argument already audited, the whole term costs Oτ(H exp(−cH)). In a*log the cofactor function is F_d(t)log t. Its integral also vanishes: after the change u=V−log(dt) it is proportional to the integral of exp(−u/2)kτ(u)(V−log d−u), zero by the double zero at 1/2. For d≤Y and within the support one has |log t|=O(H); differentiating log t up to four times only adds multiples of t^(−j). The same bound results for the integrated fourth derivative with a factor O(H), admissible even summing up to Y².

In the last term group the Möbius divisors with the free variable. What remains is the sum over r,q>Y with weight A_Y(r)Λ(q)(rq)^(−1/2)kτ(V−log(rq)), where A_Y(r)=Σ_{d|r,d>Y}μ(d). One can impose rq<exp(0.98H) with exponential error: for X=exp V the absolute weight without kernel is majorized by Σ_{dtq≤X}(dtq)^(−1/2)log q ≪√X(1+log X)³, summing first over t. The tilt by 10 of the preceding paragraph absorbs that polynomial. Therefore both variables lie between exp(0.275H) and exp(0.705H). On this trimmed rectangle it suffices to prove subexponential rate for the full bilinear sum. The sieve NO-GO recorded in the index (Selberg/Vaughan family) prevents attributing a sign to the identity by itself. Here there is a new estimate of the removed terms; the correlation of the two long coefficients remains open.

**Test of the asymmetric simplification and route decision.** One can take a=δ₁, b=Λ restricted to q≤D=exp(0.55H). Now ((μ−a)*1)(r)=δ₁(r)−1 is exactly −1 for r≥2. The piece b, which this time can touch the support, costs Oτ(poly(H)exp(−cH)): by Young with one box reserved in L∞ and up to two derivatives on distinct boxes, |kτ(u)|≤Cτ exp(−7u/2)U(−7/2)^{2m}. For n≤D one has u≥0.45H; summing (log n)/√n costs O(H√D). The rate is at most 0.275−3.5·0.45+(1/4)log U(−7/2)=−c, the same c>0 of the quadrature cutoff. The two type I terms admit the previous bounds (in b*1 the coefficient is Λ(d)≤log d). Thus S₁ differs exponentially little from the sum with minus sign over r≥2, q>D, rq<exp(0.98H), coefficient Λ(q) and the same normalized kernel. There is no longer an irregular coefficient in r.

But regathering r=1 with these r≥2 is exactly equivalent to convolving 1*(Λ−b), and 1*Λ=log. The test annihilates that sum with exponential precision by the two moments and the quadrature of b*1. This is the source of the apparent gain from replacing the prime sum by composites with a long factor. Trying to recover the term r=1 from this bound alone would repeat the renewal inversion d_125 of the index. The multiplier of the sum over all r is ζ(s) in Re s>1; applying its inverse requires precisely controlling its zeros when shifting the line. That inversion is discarded as a proof step. The symmetric version with A_Y(r) keeps a different correlation question. The lower boundary bound for n≤D is indeed absolute and independent of the inversion.


**Independent review of the upper end: PROVED, with absolute cutoff by product.** For h=U^{*2m}, the modulated kernel is exp(iτu)(∂+iτ−1/2)²h. In each term at most two boxes are differentiated. After tilting by exp(−10u), the derivatives are measures of uniform finite variation; one non-differentiated box is reserved in L∞ and all others are put in L¹. Since U(10)=(1−exp(−20))/20<1/20, losing up to three factors only modifies C_τ. This gives the declared pointwise bound without combinations growing with m.

In n≥exp(0.98H), 0≤u≤0.02H+2√H, while 2m≥H/4. The total weight of pairs is O(√X(1+V)²), by summing first over the cofactor; for any subfamily that absolute majorant is preserved. The exponent is (0.7−log20/4)H+O(√H+logH), with 0.7−log20/4=−0.048933…<−0.04. Hence the margin survives uniformly in the window for large H. The condition d≥exp(0.98H) implies the product condition, and does not change the orientation of the cutoff. Removing first the full small-divisor type is essential: truncating its cofactor beforehand would invalidate the vanishing quadrature integral.

**Independent review of the bilinear reduction: PROVED as a reduction, without a bound for the remaining block.** On expanding the Vaughan identity, a*log cancels a*Λ*1, μ*Λ*1=Λ and μ*b*1=b; thus the signs of the four terms are correct. In a*b*1, the coefficient per divisor is ≤Σ_{q|d}Λ(q)=log d and d≤Y²=exp(0.55H), so the already verified quadrature applies. The term b lies outside the support because Y<exp(V−4m) for large H.

The integral of F_d(t)log t is exp(V/2)/d times [(V−log d)L_k(1/2)+L_k'(1/2)], and both factors vanish by the double zero. The positive sign of the derivative comes from L_k'=-∫u exp(−u/2)k. On the support, |log t|=O(H), and Leibniz for four derivatives keeps t^(−9/2) times combinations of k and its first four derivatives, with a factor O(H). The polynomial loss is absorbable into the exponential bound, even using the ceiling Y². Again this concerns the full cofactor, not the already truncated product.

The remaining term is exactly Σ_{r,q>Y}A_Y(r)Λ(q)(rq)^(−1/2)k_τ(V−log(rq)), taking r=dt. To remove its upper end one uses |A_Y(r)|≤Σ_{d|r}1 and Λ(q)≤log q. Summing first over t, the absolute triple sum is ≤C√XΣ_{dq≤X}log q/(dq)≤C√X(1+V)³. The same tilted saving dominates it with margin −0.04H. After rq<exp(0.98H), each factor >exp(0.275H) forces the other <exp(0.705H), with the endpoints oriented as in the text. The reduction keeps the long signed correlation; neither the absolute cutoff nor the convolution identity by themselves provide the required subexponential bound.

**Size of the prime–prime sector in the moving symmetric remainder (τ=0).** The antecedents 066/067 and the prime cutoff of this note already prevent a proof by sectors without cancellation. The specific question here is whether the growing filter by itself removes that obstacle. In the current block, with L=0.275H, h=U^{*2m}, let P be the signed contribution of r,q both prime in the symmetric remainder, before the upper cutoff (removing it costs exponentially little). A_Y(r)=−1. Uniformly in V,
P ~ exp(V/2)U(1/2)^{2m}/[H²(1−0.275−ν/4)²],  ν=−U'(1/2)/U(1/2)=2−2/(e−1).
Its rate is 1/2+(1/4)log(1−1/e)>0. The full sum S₁ at frequency zero decays in these blocks by the previous spectral bound. Therefore the complement of this sector has the opposite main term.

Details. In the variables x=log r, y=log q, replace the two normalized prime measures by exp(x/2)dx/x and exp(y/2)dy. The quantitative PNT used in 073, by partial summation, gives errors of primitives O_A(exp(x/2)H^{-A}) on [L,V], for any A, and similarly in y with log q. To estimate the error after each substitution, use |k|+|k'|≤C exp(u/2)U(1/2)^{2m}: tilt by exp(−u/2), distribute up to three derivatives and reserve one box in L∞. Then each integration by parts, boundaries included, costs at most exp(V/2)U(1/2)^{2m}H^{-A+O(1)} after integrating the remaining variable (the sum of log q/q up to exp V is O(V²) even by integer comparison). Take A large. The double integral with the minus sign is equivalent to −exp(V/2)∫ exp(−u/2)k(u) g(V−u)du, with g(s)=1_{s>2L}log((s−L)/L).

Since exp(−u/2)k(u)=(exp(−u/2)h(u))'', g'' is −1_{s>2L}/(s−L)² plus δ_{2L}/L. The atom costs exponentially little by the majorant with tilt 7/2 of the asymmetric section applied to h, at s=2L. The positive part is exp(V/2)U(1/2)^{2m} times the expectation of 1_{V−u>2L}/(V−u−L)² under the law of 2m independent boxes tilted by exp(−u/2). The variance of u/H is O(1/H), its mean tends to ν/4 and V/H tends uniformly to 1. The integrand multiplied by H² is bounded by (H/L)² and converges in probability to the indicated constant. Hence the equivalence. This quantification is only for τ=0; at fixed nonzero frequency the phase may reduce the main term exponentially, and the absolute error of the previous PNT no longer suffices to attribute an equivalent to it.

**Centering of the long Λ factor, simultaneously in all sectors of r.** For fixed τ return to the symmetric sum before the product cutoff, with Y=exp(L), L=0.275H, W=V−L and hτ(u)=exp(iτu)U^{*2m}(u). In the factor q>Y one can replace exactly the measure ΣΛ(q)δ_q by its discrepancy relative to dq, with error Oτ(poly(H)exp(−cH)), c=7/2−2.2−log U(−7/2)/4>0. The PNT is not required for this removal. The full coefficient A_Y(r) is kept.

Indeed, with D=∂−1/2, kτ=D²hτ, a direct integration gives
∫_{Y}^∞ kτ(V−log(rq))dq/√q = √Y (Dhτ)(W−log r).
The sign of the boundary is positive on integrating (exp(−u/2)hτ)'' from −∞. The continuous contribution is therefore √Y Σ_r A_Y(r)r^(−1/2)(Dhτ)(W−log r). Extending to all r is exact, since A_Y=(μ−μ_{≤Y})*1 vanishes up to Y. Write this sequence as δ₁−μ_{≤Y}*1. For each d≤Y, the summand with full cofactor has integral zero by the remaining polar moment of Dhτ. The fourth-order quadrature gives Oτ(d³exp(−7W/2)U(−7/2)^{2m}) by the previous argument with at most five box derivatives. The isolated term r=1 equals zero since W>4m for large H. Finally √Y Y⁴exp(−7W/2)≤exp((0.1375+1.1−3.5·0.725)H); after including the boxes exactly the rate −c reappears. The upper cutoff in rq must be applied after this operation, or also estimated in the continuous portion by the same tilt by 10 and integral comparison.

Therefore what still requires control is the action of the prime discrepancy in q on the full signed sum in r. The continuous term that would be exponentially large in the prime–prime sector at τ=0 cancels on regathering the r, even at arbitrary fixed frequency. The discrepancy itself has not been bounded here.


**Independent review of the moving prime–prime sector: PROVED for τ=0, uniformly in the block.** For r,q primes larger than Y, A_Y(r)=−1. They are ordered pairs and only q carries log q: the two continuous measures in x=log r,y=log q are exp(x/2)dx/x and exp(y/2)dy. Hence integration at fixed sum x+y=s gives g(s)=log((s−L)/L), without a second denominator or a factor 1/2. The possible diagonal r=q is already included in the ordered sum and does not change the formula.

For x,y≥0.275H, the classical PNT gives errors of normalized primitives ≤C_Aexp(x/2)H^(−A) for each A, with uniform constants up to V. Tilting by exp(−u/2), differentiating at most three distinct boxes and reserving one in L∞ gives |k|+|k'|≤Cexp(u/2)U(1/2)^{2m}, with C independent of m. Each partial summation therefore keeps the exponential factor U(1/2)^{2m}, paying only powers of H at boundaries and in the other variable. Choosing A sufficiently large leaves error o(exp(V/2)U(1/2)^{2m}H^(−2)); this is the needed relative precision, stronger than a merely absolute bound by exp(V/2)H^(−A).

The identity exp(−u/2)k(u)=(exp(−u/2)h(u))'' allows two integrations by parts without additional boundaries, using g extended by zero. Its second derivative is −1_{s>2L}/(s−L)²+δ_{2L}/L. The negative outer sign makes the continuous term POSITIVE and the atom NEGATIVE. For the latter, exp(−u/2)h(u)≤Cexp(−4u)U(−7/2)^{2m}; at u=V−2L this results, even after exp(V/2), in rate ≤−0.0367056117…H+O(1). Therefore it is absolutely exponentially small and does not affect the growing equivalent.

Under the law of tilted boxes, E[u]=2mν, Var(u)=O(m), where ν=2−2/(e−1). Thus u/H→ν/4 in probability, uniformly for the windows, and V/H→1 uniformly. The integrand multiplied by H² is ≤1/(0.275)² because the indicator forces V−u−L>L; it converges in probability to (1−0.275−ν/4)^(−2). Dominated convergence proves the expectation and the equivalent, constant included. Its positive rate is 1/2+(1/4)log(1−1/e). Removing the upper cutoff only modifies an exponential error already controlled absolutely. Since unmodulated S₁ decays, the complement has the opposite main term. The restriction τ=0 is kept: the same absolute precision of the PNT does not automatically provide an equivalent after introducing a nonzero phase.

**Response to a continuous power in the discrepancy.** Replace the measure in q>Y of the symmetric remainder by q^{s−1}dq for a fixed s with 0<Re s≤1, s≠1. Let J_s be the resulting sum over all r with full A_Y, without upper product cutoff. Write M_Y(w)=Σ_{d≤Y}μ(d)d^{−w} and K(z)=(z−1/2)²U(z−iτ)^{2m}. Then uniformly in the block
J_s=exp((s−1/2)V)K(s−1/2)[1−ζ(s)M_Y(s)]+O_{s,τ}(exp(−cH)),
with the same positive c of the quadrature. If s is a zero of ζ, the bracketed factor equals exactly 1 for each Y. Therefore the cancellation of the constant density does not extend as attenuation to the powers of the explicit formula associated with zeros. This evaluates an individual power and avoids interchanging this estimate with an infinite sum over zeros.

Proof: on Re w=2, Laplace inversion against the product rq gives the integrand exp((w−1/2)V)K(w−1/2)[1−ζ(w)M_Y(w)]Y^{s−w}/(w−s), with measure dw/(2πi). The series of A_Y and the integral in q converge absolutely there. Move to Re w=−3. The pole at 1 is eliminated by the double zero of K; the only residue is the announced one. On the new line |M_Y(w)|≤CY⁴ and |Y^{s−w}|≤Y⁴. By the functional equation and Stirling, ζ(−3+it)=O((1+|t|)^{7/2}); reserving eight boxes for (1+|t|)^{-8}, the others cost U(−7/2)^{2m−8}. This gives an absolute integral O_{s,τ}(exp(−7V/2)Y⁸ U(−7/2)^{2m}). The horizontal sides disappear by the decay of the boxes for each fixed H and the polynomial growth of ζ in the strip. Since 8logY=2.2H, the stated exponent is obtained. At s=1 the poles merge and the product of both is cancelled by K, in agreement with the separate arithmetic computation.

Decision: varying only the coefficients of the polynomial M_Y, keeping the outer identity 1−ζM_Y, keeps value 1 at every zero. That variation by itself cannot supply the sought attenuation. The result does not prevent estimating the full discrepancy arithmetically by another mechanism.


**Independent review of the centering of the long factor: PROVED without PNT, with full A_Y.** The derivative of exp(−u/2)Dh_τ is exp(−u/2)D²h_τ. Integrating from −∞ to W−log r gives the POSITIVE boundary √Y·Dh_τ(W−log r), with the outer factor r^(−1/2) of the original sum. The exact identity A_Y=δ₁−μ_{≤Y}*1 allows summing all cofactors. The term δ₁ vanishes since W>4m, and each per-divisor integral vanishes because the transform of Dh_τ has a zero at 1/2.

Four quadrature derivatives require only five differentiated boxes and cost d³exp(−7W/2)U(−7/2)^{2m}. On summing d≤Y and multiplying by √Y, the factors are √Y·Y⁴exp(−7(V−logY)/2)=exp(−7V/2)Y⁸. One recovers exactly c=7/2−2.2−logU(−7/2)/4>0, with uniform constants for fixed τ. The product cutoff is applied afterwards; its continuous part has the same tilted absolute majorant as the discrete cutoff. Thus dq is subtracted with exponential error but its discrepancy relative to Λ is not estimated.

**Independent review of the Mellin response J_s: PROVED for fixed s, 0<Re s≤1.** On Re w=2, ΣA_Y(r)r^(−w)=1−ζ(w)M_Y(w), and ∫_Y^∞q^{s−1−w}dq=Y^{s−w}/(w−s); absolute convergence justifies the interchange. K(w−1/2) has a double zero at w=1: it eliminates the only pole of ζ and also the denominator if s=1. For s≠1 the only residue of the shift to Re w=−3 is w=s, with positive sign and the announced value.

On the new line, M_Y costs ≤CY⁴ and Y^{Re s+3}≤Y⁴. Reserving eight boxes leaves K(w−1/2)=O_τ((1+|Im w|)^(−6)U(−7/2)^{2m−8}); combined with ζ=O((1+|Im w|)^(7/2)) and the denominator O_s((1+|Im w|)^(−1)) an integrable majorant of order |Im w|^(−7/2) remains. Hence the error is O_{s,τ}(exp(−7V/2)Y⁸U(−7/2)^{2m}), without polynomial loss in H, and gives the same positive c. The horizontals are removed for each fixed m before making the vertical bound uniform. At s=1 there is no residue, in agreement with the previous centering.

If ζ(s)=0, the multiplier 1−ζ(s)M_Y(s) is exactly one, independently of multiplicity and of the finite coefficients of M_Y. This is a response to an individual power and an obstacle to attenuating it by means of that polynomial alone. The constants depend on s and no uniform estimate allowing the error to be summed over all zeros has been proved; nor is arithmetic cancellation in the full discrepancy by another mechanism excluded.

**Sieve up to κ(log X)² for the fixed Gevrey detector.** Use the fixed Gevrey v of the paragraph «A fixed test with negative square bias», k=v*v, V=log X. There exists a fixed κ>0 such that with z=κV² the sum
S_z=Σ_{n squarefree, P⁻(n)>z}(log n)n^{−1/2}k(V−log n)
is O(exp(−cV/log V)) unconditionally for large V. z is frozen when forming each sum. The primes of the support are >z for large V, so if C_z is the same sum restricted to composites one has C_z=−B_X(v)+O(exp(−cV/log V)). Under RH the bias and the spectral reserve of the test give C_z≥3/32−o(1); outside RH there are unbounded negative excursions. Therefore the eventual floor C_z≥1/16 is equivalent to the global sign. It remains to prove that floor from the arithmetic of the composites with all factors >κV².

Proof: A_z(s)=ζ(s)ζ(2s)^{-1}∏_{p≤z}(1+p^{-s})^{-1} on Re s>1. Invert −A'_z(s)K(s−1/2)exp((s−1/2)V), where K=L_v²; the only potential pole at 1 is cancelled by the double zero of K. In the fixed inversion strip |K(σ+it)|≤C exp(−c₀|t|^b) for some b>0 by integration by parts optimized with the Gevrey bounds. Choose H=V^A with Ab>1 and move from Re s=2 to 1/2−h, h=d/log V. For d sufficiently small (depending on A), the classical zero-free region of de la Vallée Poussin includes 2s in a slightly enlarged rectangle of margin h around the new vertical and up to height 2H+2. There 1/ζ(2s) and its derivative are O(H^C): the polynomial bound is obtained by integrating the local expansion of ζ'/ζ over the distance O(1/log H) from 1+1/log H, with O(log H) nearby zeros and distance ≫1/log H (at small heights use continuity of the reciprocal). Cauchy gives the derivative bound in the substrip. ζ(s) has polynomial growth outside a fixed disc around 1. The finite product on Re s≥1/2−2h has logarithm of modulus at most O(Σ_{p≤z}p^{-1/2+2h})≤C₁√κ V/log V by Chebyshev; p^{2h} is bounded and C₁ can be fixed before choosing κ small. For its derivative Cauchy is used on discs of radius ≍h. On the new vertical the factor exp(−hV) dominates the polynomial prefactors and the cost of the product by choosing C₁√κ<d/2. The horizontal sides and the tail of the initial vertical are absorbed by exp(−c₀H^b) against exp(3V/2+O(V/log V)). The integrand has no other poles inside the rectangle. This proves the bound.

To interpret the size of the removal with a fixed nonnegative nonzero Gevrey profile on the same band, replace k by that profile: now the residue at 1 is kept. In −A'_z the main term is β_z/(s−1)² without a simple pole, with β_z=ζ(2)^{-1}∏_{p≤z}(1+p^{-1})^{-1}; the weighted residue is β_z exp(V/2)[V K(1/2)+K'(1/2)] using K for the new transform. The primes cost O(exp(V/2)) by Chebyshev. Relative to the previous sieve up to p_{⌊V/log4⌋}, the ratio of gross composite weights is asymptotic to β_z/β_previous→1/2 by Mertens. This half compares positive weights in the smooth version; it is not a fraction of the signed discrepancy nor an enlargement of the positivity window.

**Explicit choice compatible with the shift.** In the explicit eight-box test of this note replace φ=U^{*4} by φ*g where g is the law of the sum of uniform boxes on [0,j^{-2}], j≥1. Its support is compact and its transform G(z)=∏ (1−exp(−z/j²))/(z/j²) converges locally uniformly, with removable factors at zero; G(0)=1 and it has no zeros off the imaginary axis since the sum of the distances of the factors from 1 converges locally. In fixed strips, for j≤c√|Im z| each factor has modulus ≤1/2 choosing c small; the rest is bounded by exp(CΣj^{-2}). Thus G decays like exp(−c'√|Im z|), sufficient with H=V³. On the axis |G|≤1 and the limit 1/32 for the critical zeros of the eight boxes is preserved. The multiplier L_v(z)=(z−1/2)L_φ(z)G(z) preserves the ordinary moment and all nonzero exterior coefficients. The explicit formula and the detector of 115 are applied as in the eight-box test. The previous composite floor therefore also refers to this single fixed explicit profile.

**Unconditional compensation between two and at least three distinct factors in the smooth sieve.** Fix the previous profile, K(s)=∫e^{−su}k(u)du and z=κV². Write C₂ for the terms of C_z with n=pq, z<p<q, and C_{≥3} for the rest. Then
C₂∼−K''(1/2)√X/(2V²),   C_{≥3}∼+K''(1/2)√X/(2V²).
