Here K''(1/2)=2(L'_v(1/2))²>0 for the explicit profile by the positivity of the transform of its base density at 1/2. The second equivalence is also unconditional. Unlike the symmetric Vaughan sector, here UNORDERED pairs are counted with the weight log(pq) of the full sieve.

Details. Set r=V−u and a=log p. First replace the count of q>p by dq/log q: q in the support is ≥exp((V−O(1))/2). By quantitative PNT and by parts, including the boundary q=p, the error for fixed p is O(√X exp(−c√V)poly(V)/p); summing 1/p introduces only a polynomial factor. In the new integral one obtains √X∫e^{−u/2}k(u)f(V−u)du with f(r)=Σ_{z<p≤exp(r/2)}r/[p(r−log p)]. For p>exp(V/3), partial summation with PNT at the moving endpoints replaces this sum by its integral dp/log p with uniform error O(poly(V)exp(−c√V)). For z<p≤exp(V/3), the second derivative in r of the difference sum minus integral is O(V^{-3}): compare Σ (log p)/p with its integral using the O(1) error of Mertens and the weight 2/(r−a)^3 whose maximum and variation are O(V^{-3}). The support in u is fixed, and its moments of order 0 and 1 with weight e^{-u/2}k are zero. By Taylor the error under the integral costs O(√X/V³), even though the initial error in f does not have that pointwise precision. The full continuous density is ∫_{log z}^{r/2}r da/[a(r−a)]=log((r−log z)/log z). Its second derivative is −1/(r−log z)² and the third O(V^{-3}); this gives C₂=−√X K''(1/2)/(2(V−log z)²)+O(√X/V³).

For the compensation apply PNT directly to B_X(v). The continuous prime density with weight log p produces √X K(1/2)=0. On the fixed proportional band one integration by parts gives B_X(v)=O(√X exp(−c√V)poly(V)). The identity audited or proved above C_z=−B_X(v)+O(exp(−c'V/log V)) makes C_z negligible relative to √X/V² and gives the second equivalence. This resolution of the main terms does not determine the constant floor of C_z. In fact the PNT only bounds its modulus at a scale growing without limit.

**Unconditional sign for a collective weight on composites in the same detector.** Reduce κ if necessary, keeping z=κV². With the same k= v*v, let W be the sum C_z with each term multiplied by 2^{ω(n)−1}−1. This factor is the number of UNORDERED partitions of the primes of n into two nonempty groups. Then
W=(K''(1/2)/2) b_z √X + O(exp(−cV/log V)),  b_z=∏_{p≤z}(1−1/p)² ∏_{p>z}(1+2/p)(1−1/p)².
In particular W>0 eventually, and b_z∼exp(−2γ_E)/(log z)². It is an effective inequality in the asymptotic sense for the whole signed sum with that weight; the numerical threshold is not certified.

Proof: for l=1,2 use F_l(s)=∏_{p>z}(1+l p^{-s}) and the integrand −F_l'(s)K(s−1/2)exp((s−1/2)V)/l. Subtracting the l=1 integral from the l=2 one removes every prime exactly. The first was already exponentially small. For the second write F_2=ζ(s)²ζ(2s)^{-3}G_z(s). If x=p^{-s}, the factors of G_z are (1−x)²/(1−x²)³ at p≤z and (1+2x)(1−x)²/(1−x²)³ at p>z. In the tail the expansion begins with 1+O(|x|³), which converges normally in Re s>1/3. In Re s≥1/2−2h of the previous proof the small factors cost exp(O(√κ V/log V)), with absolute constants for l=2; the tail stays uniformly bounded. The same zero-free region of ζ(2s), the Cauchy derivative bounds and the same Gevrey decay pay for the sides of the contour, choosing κ common to both orders. At s=1 the order-two term of F_2 is b_z/(s−1)². Its derivative with a minus sign and divided by two has leading term b_z/(s−1)³; the double zero of K leaves only the residue written. The product for b_z is obtained directly by removing ζ(s)² at 1, and the product over p>z tends to one by absolute convergence. Mertens gives the equivalent.

The sum over semiprimes carries multiplier one here, and over products of three primes, three. The result shows a collective compensation with proved sign in the same sign-changing kernel that defines the problem. To obtain the floor 1/16 for the unit weight one would need to compare the contributions of the two regions k>0 and k<0 when the multipliers are removed. The pointwise inequality 2^{ω−1}−1≥1 for composites does not allow that deduction.


**Independent review of the smooth sieve κV² and of the half mass: PROVED for a fixed Gevrey profile.** The series of squarefree numbers without factors ≤z is A_z=ζ(s)/ζ(2s)∏_{p≤z}(1+p^(−s))^(−1). Its only possible poles in the shifting rectangle come from ζ at 1 and from zeros of ζ(2s); the latter are excluded by the classical region by choosing first A and then d small. The point 2s=1 is a zero of the reciprocal and not a pole. The finite factors do not vanish for Re s>0. The derivative −A'_z has at 1 only the double pole β_z/(s−1)²; K of order two there removes the whole principal part.

The local expansion of ζ'/ζ and the distance ≥c/logH to its zeros allow passing from 1+1/logH to the substrip of 2s with polynomial growth H^C of the reciprocal; Cauchy on discs of radius comparable to h gives its derivative. For the finite product and its derivative the enlarged strip Re s≥1/2−2h is used: the logarithm of its modulus is ≤C₁√κV/logV, with C₁ fixed before κ. The new vertical pays exp(−dV/logV), while all prefactors are polynomial in H=V^A. Choosing C₁√κ<d/2 leaves the declared saving; the horizontals and the initial tail are suppressed by the Gevrey decay with Ab>1. The threshold κ is fixed and existential, dependent on the profile and on these constants; no universal numerical value is obtained here.

Thus S_z is exponentially small in V/logV without RH. All visible primes exceed z and C_z=S_z−B_X(v), with the correct negative sign. The critical budget of the fixed test gives under RH C_z≥3/32−o(1); outside RH the positive excursions of B_X produce negative excursions of C_z. The eventual floor 1/16 is an equivalence, not a proved arithmetic bound. With a positive profile, the residue is β_zexp(V/2)[VK(1/2)+K'(1/2)], because −A'_z has no simple pole. The prime contribution is O(exp(V/2)) against the principal term β_zVexp(V/2). Mertens gives β_z/β_previous→1/2; the half refers to smooth positive weights and not to the signed discrepancy or to a sharp cutoff.

**Independent review of the explicit profile: PROVED as a compatible Gevrey detector.** The radii j^(−2) are summable, so the law g has compact support. Each factor of G has removable value 1 at 0 and only imaginary zeros; the deviations from 1 are locally summable, so the product creates no zeros off the axis. For j≤c√|t| the numerator is uniformly bounded and the denominator is ≥|t|/j², giving modulus ≤1/2 when c is chosen small in the fixed strip. The rest of the product is bounded by exp(CΣj^(−2)); one obtains exp(−c'√|t|). This also implies Gevrey bounds of order two by Fourier inversion, and H=V³ removes the long sides of the contour.

Since g is a probability, G(0)=1 and |G(iγ)|≤1. The ordinary moment −1/2, the polar moment zero and the critical budget <1/32 are preserved; no exterior zero vanishes. The support grows only by a fixed constant and produces no new edges. The same explicit profile is therefore valid in the composite criterion, without claiming an unconditional prime ceiling.

**Independent review of the two/≥three factor compensation: PROVED for the fixed profile with K''(1/2)>0.** C₂ counts UNORDERED pairs p<q and the weight is log(pq); there is no additional factor 2. When q is replaced by dq/logq, the continuous weight in a=logp is exactly r/[p(r−a)]. The minimum q≥exp((V−O(1))/2) makes the PNT error uniform, including the edges q=p; summing 1/p only adds a polynomial loss absorbed by exp(−c√V).

For p>exp(V/3), the second substitution is uniform with exponential error. In the low range z is kept frozen when differentiating with respect to r. The second derivative of the discrete/continuous difference is the action of the O(1) error of Σlogp/p−logx on 2/(r−a)³. Edges and variation cost O(V^(−3)). The two vanishing weighted moments of k remove the constant and linear part of that error, so no pointwise estimate of the original error in f is needed. The continuous integral is log((r−logz)/logz); Taylor and ∫u²exp(−u/2)k(u)du=K''(1/2) give −K''(1/2)√X/[2(V−logz)²]+O(√X/V³). Freezing z is necessary for that derivative computation.

In the explicit profile, L'_v(1/2) is the positive transform of the base density at 1/2; hence K''(1/2)=2(L'_v(1/2))²>0. Direct PNT for B_X(v) cancels the density by K(1/2)=0 and leaves O(√Xexp(−c√V)poly(V)), which is o(√X/V²) but not o(1). Together with C_z=S_z−B_X, this forces the opposite positive principal term for C_{≥3}, unconditionally. The factors are distinct because the sieve is squarefree. The two large principal terms and their compensation are computed; the constant floor of the criterion is not resolved, nor is its difficulty reduced by controlling those principal terms separately.

**Two-sided test of sensitivity to the unit weight on composites.** Let a=exp(−V^{1/3}) and d=ω(n)≥2. Use in C_z the weights w_±(n)=1±a^{d−1}. Both are positive and satisfy sup|w_±−1|≤a→0. However the two balances C_± have opposite signs eventually, with
C_−∼+a K''(1/2)√X/(2V²),    C_+∼−a K''(1/2)√X/(2V²).
Indeed C_±=C_z±a C₂+O(a² V√X): in d≥3 it suffices to sum absolutely over ALL integers of the proportional support with |k| bounded. The error is o(a√X/V²) since aV³→0. Quantitative PNT and the polar zero already gave |C_z|≪√X exp(−c√V)poly(V)+o(1), also o(a√X/V²). Substituting the audited equivalent of C₂ concludes. This constructs positive sums with weights uniformly close to one and equally close negative sums for the same kernel and the same composites.

If only the weight of semiprimes is altered by adding t(V) to it, the exact variation of the balance is t(V)C₂(V). Hence a perturbation t=αV²/√X, with α constant, already shifts the balance by −αK''(1/2)/2+o(1). To transfer a floor at scale 1/16 with error o(1) through this isolated modification, |t|=o(V²/√X) is required and sufficient. This measures the transfer error, not the sign of the original balance. The two-sided test shows why uniform convergence to one of a family of weights, even faster than any inverse power of V, does not decide that sign.

**Arbitrary attenuation in logarithmic powers without losing detection.** For each fixed integer m≥1 there is an explicit detector v_m with the same square bias and target composite floor 1/16, whose semiprime sector C_{2,m} satisfies
C_{2,m}∼−[K_m^{(2m)}(1/2)/(2m)]√X/V^{2m},  K_m=L_{v_m}²,  K_m^{(2m)}(1/2)>0.
The asymptotic threshold may depend on m. Start from the smooth explicit profile v of the section on infinite boxes. With h=2log(100m), add to L_v the multiplicative factor [(exp(−hz)−exp(−h/2))/(1−exp(−h/2))]^{m−1}, realizable by convolutions of two-atom differences. The factor equals 1 at zero; its only zeros lie on Re z=1/2, where no centered nontrivial zeros are found. On the axis its squared modulus is ≤[(1+1/(100m))/(1−1/(100m))]^{2m}<1.05. The budget <1/32 is preserved because the previous explicit bound, before rounding, was 202/(4·9⁴). The weighted moment of v_m vanishes up to order m−1 and the order is exactly m; by self-convolution K_m has order 2m at 1/2 and first nonzero coefficient positive. The support and the Gevrey constant remain fixed for each m. The previous detector criterion and smooth sieve apply, with constants depending on the profile.

For the equivalent repeat the semiprime proof at the same cutoff z=κV². In the part p≤exp(V/3), differentiate 2m times in r the difference between the sum and its integral. The differentiated kernel is (2m)! (log p)/[p(r−log p)^{2m+1}]. By the same O(1) Mertens error and the variation of the remaining power, the difference of derivatives is O_m(V^{-2m−1}). Taylor over the support of the profile removes the earlier derivatives through the 2m vanishing moments. PNT in the two large ranges keeps an error smaller than any fixed inverse power of V after normalizing by √X. The derivative of order 2m of log((r−log z)/log z) is −(2m−1)!/(r−log z)^{2m}. The remainder after integrating has order O_m(√X/V^{2m+1}) if V−log z is kept in the principal term. The announced formula is obtained. Thus increasing a fixed number of moments allows reducing the logarithmic power of the obstruction, but C_{2,m} still diverges in modulus for every fixed m. The argument does not allow choosing m=m(V); that would change the support, the derivative budget and uniform detection.

**Continuous semiprime model at variable order: exact identity and rate.** Let k₀ be the explicit smooth kernel of initial polar order one, K₀ its transform and [0,S] a fixed support. In the previous detector put N=2(m−1), q=exp(−h/2), V₀=V−Nh, a=log z with z=κV². The continuous model M_m is √X∫exp(−u/2)k_m(u)log((V−u−a)/a)du, where here k_m=v_m*v_m. Assume V₀>S+2a so that the semiprime density has that expression on the whole support. Then, for m≥2,
M_m=−exp(V₀/2)(1−q)^{−N}∫₀^∞ exp(−(V₀−a)t)(1−exp(−ht))^N K₀(1/2−t)dt/t.
Indeed in the tilted measure exp(−u/2)k_m(u)du each shifted difference becomes q(δ_h−δ₀)/(1−q). Apply the integral representation of log and sum the N differences: the constant term disappears and (exp(ht)−1)^N remains. Near 0 the integral converges by the double zero of K₀; at infinity by V₀−a>S. The interchange is also obtained by first truncating the Frullani integral at both ends. Since K₀ is the square of a real transform on the real line, the integrand is nonnegative and not identically zero. The model is strictly negative for every admissible order.

Moreover, if m→∞ and V₀≥εV with ε>0 fixed, log|M_m|=V₀/2+o(V). On [1/h,2/h], K₀(1/2−t)≥c/h² by its exactly double zero; the rest of the integral costs at least exp(−2V/h)(1−e^(−1))^N log 2. Here N≤V/h and h→∞. For the ceiling the variation norm of the tilted measure suffices: the differences cost (2q/(1−q))^N, the logarithmic density O(log V) and the base measure has fixed norm. Since N=O(V/h)=o(V), these two extremes give the rate. Thus, as long as the effective scale V₀ remains a positive fraction of V, raising the order does not even bring the continuous density of this sector to constant scale. This is not a lower bound for the discrete sum with variable m: the PNT estimates used at fixed order do not control the relative error here, nor has detection been proved for these moving profiles.

**Relative comparison with real semiprimes for growing order.** Keep the explicit profile and z=κV². Write n=2m, N=n−2, and restrict to 4≤n≤V^{1/4}. Uniformly in that range the DISCRETE semiprime sector satisfies C_{2,m}/M_m=1+o(1) as V tends to infinity. In particular it is strictly negative. The symbol n in this section denotes the order of the derivative, not the product of primes.

Key detail to avoid uncontrolled constants: write k₀=(∂−1/2)²H₀, where H₀ is the self-convolution of the base box density, nonnegative and of mass one. Then exp(−u/2)k₀=(exp(−u/2)H₀)''. On a function of r=V−u, the two integrations by parts and the N tilted differences (N even) amount to averaging the n-th derivative at r=V−u−t₁−…−t_N, against the positive measure exp(−u/2)H₀(u)du dt₁…dt_N on [0,S]×[0,h]^N, multiplied by √X(q/(1−q))^N. All those r are V−O(n log(2n)).

In the discrete two-prime proof, now split at log p=b=V/n. PNT for the second prime and for the first prime in log p>b costs O(√X poly(V)exp(−c√b)) before differences for each shifted copy of the fixed profile, with uniform constants: in the first substitution the second prime is ≥exp((V−Nh−S)/2); in the second the first prime is ≥exp b. By parts, the weights r/[p(r−log p)] and their derivatives in p in the range b≤log p≤r/2 cost O(poly(V)/p) and O(poly(V)/p²). In the first substitution one proceeds with the base profile at argument V−jh, 0≤j≤N; its bound has √exp(V−jh)≤√X. Combining copies costs at most ((1+q)/(1−q))^N=O(1) in their untilted coefficients. The same bound covers moving endpoints.

In log z<log p≤b, let E(r) be the difference sum minus integral of r/[p(r−log p)]. By Mertens with remainder O(1) for Σ(log p)/p−log x and by Abel, |E^{(n)}(r)|≤C n!/(r−b)^{n+1}, with C absolute: the power used is monotone and its variation does not exceed its maximum. The derivative of the total density is −(n−1)!/(r−log z)^n. The ratio of the moduli is bounded by C n/(r−b) multiplied by ((r−log z)/(r−b))^n=O(1), since b=V/n and r/V→1 uniformly. By the positive representation the error of this part is O(n/V)|M_m|, with no loss from moment cancellation.

Finally that same representation implies |M_m|≥c√X (qh/(1−q))^N (n−1)!/V^n, with c=∫exp(−u/2)H₀(u)du>0. In particular |M_m|≥√X exp(−C n log V). The PNT error is relatively o(1) because √(V/n)≥V^{3/8} while n log V≤V^{1/4}log V. This closes the real sign of THIS sector with growing orders. It does not imply the floor for the set of all composites nor does it prove that the moving-order test still detects every zero.

**The same test of growing polar order preserves the global criterion by blocks.** In H=2^l≤V<2H choose m=m_l→∞ with 2m_l≤H^{1/4} for large l and keep it fixed in that block. The datum and the sieve are those of the last discrete computation. Under RH the composite balance C_{z,m}≥3/32−o(1) uniformly. Outside RH there are excursions of both signs of modulus >exp(ηV) in every sufficiently late block for all 0≤η<Δ. Therefore C_{z,m}≥1/16 eventually is equivalent to the global sign for this same family in which C_{2,m}<0 uniformly.

To justify it, expand the difference factor in the full kernel. One obtains a combination of copies of the base kernel evaluated at V_j=V−jh, 0≤j≤N, with real coefficients summing to one and absolute norm ((1+q)/(1−q))^N<1.05. All V_j≥V−O(H^{1/4}log H) tend to infinity uniformly. The sieve in each copy is frozen at the SAME z=κV²; since z≤2κV_j² for late blocks, the shift of F_z in the Gevrey proof keeps its uniform saving by choosing κ smaller than half the admissible constant. Therefore C_{z,m}=−B_m+o(1) and the square term in B_m is −1/8+o(1), by linearity and the uniform error of the base profile. Under RH the cost of the critical divisor stays below 1/32 by the previous explicit bound multiplied by 1.05.

To detect outside RH apply the already audited argument of 115 in the section on boxes by blocks, now only to the series of centered zeros with b=Re w>0. The zeros with b≤0 give O(1) in the real block by the absolute sum for the base kernel at each V_j and the coefficient norm. For b>0, the base coefficient is multiplied by [(exp(−hw)−q)/(1−q)]^N, of modulus ≤1.05 uniformly. For each FIXED right zero one has 0<b<1/2, so |exp(−hw)−q|≥exp(−hb)(1−exp(−h(1/2−b)))≥exp(−hb)/2 for large l. The original coefficient is nonzero and the new logarithmic cost is O_w(Nh+N)=o(H). Thus exactly the uniform upper summability and the subexponential lower bound at the Gaussian maximum required by 115 hold. Outside the block only the right series is extended with the same m, with uniformly summable coefficients; the O(1) errors are incorporated inside the block after extracting both excursions. The limit −1/8 under RH is not claimed, since the difference filter does not make the coefficients on the axis tend to zero. The negative semiprime contribution comes from the discrete comparator already constructed. The balance between that term and the composites with a larger number of factors still has no unconditional lower bound.


**Independent review of fixed polar order: PROVED for each fixed m, without automatic extrapolation.** The added factor is the transform of (δ_h−qδ₀)/(1−q), q=exp(−h/2)=1/(100m). It equals 1 at 0 and has a simple zero at each point 1/2+2πij/h, none of which corresponds to a centered nontrivial zero. Hence L_{v_m} keeps the ordinary moment −1/2 and exterior detection and acquires exactly order m at 1/2. The square K_m has order 2m and a positive first nonzero derivative of order 2m. The ceiling of the critical factor is ≤((1+q)/(1−q))^{2m}<1.05, which fits comfortably in the numerical reserve 202/(4·9⁴)<1/32. The support and the Gevrey constants may depend on m, as the fixed scope requires.

The derivative of order 2m of r/[p(r−logp)] is (2m)!(logp)/[p(r−logp)^{2m+1}]. Abel with Mertens O(1) costs O_m(V^{−2m−1}); the earlier moments vanish exactly. The derivative of order 2m of the logarithmic density is −(2m−1)!/(r−logz)^{2m}, giving the coefficient −K_m^{(2m)}(1/2)/(2m), with no factorial lost. It is preferable to keep V−logz in the principal term for the remainder O_m(√X/V^{2m+1}); replacing it by V only gives the equivalent. Each fixed m still leaves a term divergent in modulus and does not provide uniform detection with moving m.

**Independent review of the variable continuous model: PROVED with V₀>S+2logz.** The exact physical identity is k_m=(δ_h−qδ₀)^{*N}*k₀/(1−q)^N, N=2(m−1). On tilting by exp(−u/2), each difference becomes q(δ_h−δ₀)/(1−q). Frullani gives the negative factor −(exp(ht)−1)^N; combining it with q^N and with exp(−(V−logz)t) produces precisely exp(V₀/2)exp(−(V₀−logz)t)(1−exp(−ht))^N/(1−q)^N. This verifies the complete normalization of the shift, including the factor exp(V₀/2), not exp(V/2).

The integral converges at zero by the double zero of K₀ and at infinity by the support margin. K₀ at real argument is a nonnegative square, not identically zero, so the model is strictly negative. If m→∞ and V₀≥εV, on [1/h,2/h] one has K₀(1/2−t)≥c/h², the exponential loss is O(V/h) and that of (1−exp(−ht))^N is O(N). Both are o(V). The ceiling by tilted total variation costs exp(V₀/2)(2/(1−q))^N times a fixed base norm and O(logV), also exp(V₀/2+o(V)). It follows that log|M_m|=V₀/2+o(V). This continuous computation is not by itself a lower bound for the prime sampling.

**Independent review of the uniform discrete step 4≤n=2m≤V^{1/4}: PROVED for that range.** The positive comparator is H₀, the self-convolution of the base density, and not k₀, which changes sign. Two integrations by parts give (exp(−u/2)k₀)=(exp(−u/2)H₀)''; the N differences are represented as integrals over [0,h]^N. Since N is even, there is no additional sign when substituting the n-th derivative of the function of r. The remaining measure is positive, with factor √X(q/(1−q))^N and without normalizing dt₁…dt_N: its volume is h^N. This justifies comparing errors and principal term pointwise without losing moment cancellations.

The arguments r lie in V−O(nlog(2n)), uniformly. At the cut b=V/n, Mertens and the variation of the monotone power give |E^{(n)}(r)|≤Cn!/(r−b)^{n+1}, with C independent of n. On dividing by (n−1)!/(r−logz)^n, the ratio power is ≤exp(nb/(r−b))=O(1), since r/V→1 and n≥4. The error under the positive average is therefore O(n/V)|M_m|.

In the PNT substitutions the fixed base kernel shifted to V−jh, 0≤j≤N, is used first. Its physical coefficients, before tilting, have absolute sum ((1+q)/(1−q))^N=O(1), since Nq=O(1). Hence no 2^N loss appears, nor a hidden growing derivative constant. The first prime in the high range exceeds exp(V/n), the second exceeds exp((V−Nh−S)/2); the moving edges are controlled by the same fixed variations. An absolute error √Xpoly(V)exp(−c√(V/n)) remains.

The positive average gives the floor c√X(qh/(1−q))^N(n−1)!/V^n≥√Xexp(−CnlogV), where c=∫exp(−u/2)H₀(u)du>0. Uniformly up to n=V^{1/4}, √(V/n)≥V^{3/8} dominates nlogV≤V^{1/4}logV. Thus the relative PNT error tends to zero, and also n/V→0. C_{2,m}/M_m→1 and discrete negativity are proved over that whole range, including small orders. This does not control the total of composites nor deduce uniform spectral detection for the moving profiles; any additional claim needs its own proof of constants and support.


**Independent review of detection for the same growing order: PROVED by frozen blocks.** The physical expansion has coefficients c_j=binom(N,j)(−q)^{N−j}/(1−q)^N, 0≤j≤N. They sum to 1 and their absolute norm is ((1+q)/(1−q))^N<1.05. Each base copy is evaluated at V_j=V−jh, with V_j≥H−O(H^(1/4)logH), uniformly positive and tending to infinity. The cutoff z is kept exactly the same in all copies. The Gevrey bound of the base sieve is uniform when z/V_j² lies in a positive compact interval below the admissible constant; halving κ ensures that condition. By linearity and bounded norm, S_{z,m}=o(1) uniformly, C_{z,m}=−B_m+o(1), and the square term of B_m keeps −1/8 because Σc_j=1. The power errors of the copies are uniformly o(1).

Under RH, on the axis the norm of the additional spectral factor is ≤1.05 and the base budget, smaller than 1/32 even after that multiplication, remains valid. Thus C_{z,m}≥3/32−o(1). It does not follow that the critical sum tends to zero: unlike the growing smoothing of boxes, the present difference factor does not have that uniform property.

Outside RH, the part b≤0 must be treated in physical variables: its coefficients after the filter are not necessarily uniformly bounded, but at each positive V_j its base series has modulus ≤Σ|a_w|. The combination of norm <1.05 gives O(1) for that whole part in the block. For b>0, on the other hand, |exp(−hw)|≤1 and the additional factor has modulus ≤1.05, so the absolute sum of coefficients is uniformly bounded. For each fixed right w, b<1/2 and q/|exp(−hw)|=exp(−h(1/2−b))→0. The floor exp(−hb)/2 of the difference gives a selected coefficient ≥exp(−O_w(Nh+N))=exp(−o(H)). No new zeros appear in the right divisor.

Applying 115 to this real right series, freezing the order, allows choosing c, frequency and rate gap independent of the block. The subexponential floor of the winning term dominates the rest with fixed gap; the Gaussian tails use the uniform sum. A central mean 3H/2 and relative radius <1/3 leaves both excursions inside the block. Choosing an exponent intermediate between η and Δ absorbs the o(H) cost and the O(1) perturbation. The left part is reinserted only after removing the tails of the extension with the SAME order. This proves the eventual composite floor criterion for this family, compatible with the audited discrete semiprime negativity. The unconditional floor of the joint balance remains open; neither the detection principles nor the sectoral principal terms provide it.

**Three factors also hurt the sign: first favourable balance from four.** For the previous fixed Gevrey detector (initial polar order one), let C₃ be the restriction of C_z to n=pqr with z<p<q<r and h=log z. One has
C₃=(K''(1/2)/2)(√X/V²)[1−log(V/h)+o(1)].
Therefore the sector of three distinct primes is negative and in modulus exceeds that of semiprimes by an asymptotic factor log(V/h). The aggregate balance of four or more primes is +(K''(1/2)/2)(√X/V²)[log(V/h)+o(1)] by the previous bounds for C_z and C₂ (the constant term of C₃ cancels that of C₂). No sign follows for exactly four primes.

Details. To count ordered triples with repetition put dν(a)=Σ_p p^{-1}δ_{log p}(da), R=a₁+a₂+a₃, and use g_V(R)=R exp(−(V−R)/2)k(V−R), after dividing by √X. Split each variable into low h<a≤b and high a>b, b=V/5. On the support R=V+O(1) there is at least one high. For a high one, the accumulated discrepancy between ν and da/a on (b,t] is O(exp(−c√b)) by PNT and Abel, uniformly in t≥b; the variation and the supremum of g_V are O(V). The other two masses truncated to V+O(1) are O(log V) each. Replacing all the high ones costs O(V log²V exp(−c√b)).

When there are two low a,d and one continuous high, the conditional density in R is H₂=R/(R−a−d). With one low a and two continuous high ones it is H₁=2R log((R−a−b)/b)/(R−a). At the indicated scales all second derivatives in R are O(V^{-2}) and their derivatives in a low variable are O(V^{-3}), by rescaling and denominators bounded away from zero. Before substituting a low variable, integrate against exp(−u/2)k(u), u=V−R: the two vanishing moments remove the first two Taylor terms in R. The remainder has supremum and variation in the low variable O(V^{-2}), by the derivative bounds and length ≤b. By PNT and Abel the accumulated discrepancy on (h,t] is O(exp(−c√h)); any other low variable has mass O(log(V/h)). Thus the joint error in units √X is o(V^{-2}), since h≍log V. This also covers the permutations of the low positions.

In the repetitions p²q with p≤exp b, Chebyshev for q of size comparable to X/p² gives error O(√X Σ_{p>z}p^{-2})=O(√X/(z log z)). For p>exp b, counting q by integers costs O(√X V exp(−b)). Both bounds are o(√X/V²); they cover the case p=q. Now divide by six. Writing R/(adc)=1/(ad)+1/(ac)+1/(dc) under the restriction a+d+c=R, the resulting density is f₃(R)=½∫_{a,d≥h,a+d≤R−h} da dd/(ad). Differentiating gives f₃'(R)=log((R−2h)/h)/(R−h), and f₃''(R)=1/[(R−2h)(R−h)]−log((R−2h)/h)/(R−h)². On the support the latter is [1−log(V/h)+o(1)]/V² uniformly. Integral Taylor and the second moment K''(1/2) give the formula. The argument keeps the profile fixed; it does not transfer automatically to moving orders.

**Pattern for every fixed multiplicity of the composite.** Let C_d be the part of C_z with exactly d distinct prime factors, with the fixed detector and h=log z, z=κV². For each fixed integer d≥2,
C_d ∼ −[K''(1/2)/2] (√X/V²) [log(V/h)]^{d−2}/(d−2)! .
Thus for each fixed cut D≥2 all sectors 2,…,D are eventually negative and their sum is equivalent to C_D. The complement with more than D factors has opposite principal term because C_z=o(√X/V²). These equivalents are not summed over growing d.

Continuous density: with b_h(t)=1_{t≥h}/t, the ordered density divided by d! is f_d(r)=r b_h^{*d}(r)/d!. By symmetry of the simplex one of the denominators can be cancelled and one gets f_d(r)=(d−1)!^{-1}∫_{t_i≥h,Σ_{i<d}t_i≤r−h}∏_{i<d}dt_i/t_i. In particular f_d'(r)=f_{d−1}(r−h)/(r−h) for r>dh, with f₁(r)=1 for r>h. The box inclusions up to (r−h)/(d−1) and up to r give f_j(r)∼log(r/h)^{j−1}/(j−1)! for fixed j, r/h→∞. Differentiating the recurrence once more, the term −f_{d−1}(r−h)/(r−h)² dominates the one containing f'_{d−1}, smaller by a factor O_d(1/log(r/h)) for d≥3. For d=2 the second term is zero. The equivalence for f_d'' is uniform in r=V+O(1). Integral Taylor with the two vanishing moments and K''(1/2) gives the principal term.

Discrete justification for fixed d: in the d ordered variables, initially with repetition, split log p into low ones up to b=V/(3d) and high ones above b. Replacing each high one by its integral costs O_d(poly(V)exp(−c_d√V)) in units √X by the variation argument for g_V of the triple section. There is always at least one high. With l high ones already continuous and sum A of the low ones, the conditional density is r b_b^{*l}(r−A). Its second derivatives in r and its additional derivative in each low variable are O_d(V^{-2}) and O_d(V^{-3}): after rescaling by V, a simplex of dimension l−1 remains with slack (r−A−lb)/V≥1/2 for large V. Parametrize the excesses over b by that slack multiplied by coordinates of a fixed simplex; all rescaled denominators are bounded away from zero. This includes l=1 without integration. The two moments allow applying Abel to each low one after Taylor, with total cost O_d(V^{-2}(1+log V)^d exp(−c√h))=o_d(V^{-2}). 

For d≥3 the tuples with repetition are majorized, with a constant depending on d, by writing the product as p²m, with m an ordered product of d−2 primes. In m≤y there are O_d(y) tuples by unique factorization and their total weight log m is O_d(y(1+log log(3y))^{d−3}) for y≥1: distinguish a factor marked by its logarithm, sum it by Chebyshev and the remaining ones by their reciprocals. Hence the repetition costs in units √X at most O_d(Σ_{p>z} [log p+(1+log V)^{d−3}]/p²)=O_d(1/z+(1+log V)^{d−3}/(z log z)), negligible against V^{-2}log(V/h)^{d−2}. For d=2 the earlier semiprime computation is used. Dividing by d! after removing repetitions completes the argument. The result explains why computing an additional fixed order never produces a favourable sector in this detector; it does not decide the balance of the zone where the number of factors grows.

**Uniform extension of the computation.** Put U=log V, L=log(V/h), D=⌊U^{1/3}⌋. The preceding equivalence has relative error o(1) uniform for 2≤d≤D. Indeed, the two boxes give relative error O(d log(2d)/L) in the density for r=V+O(h), and the second contribution to the curvature is O(d/L) of the first. Taylor integrated against w preserves the relative error because the second moment is fixed and positive.

In the discrete replacement, each mass of one variable is O(1+U). There are at most d 2^d replacements when summing the partitions. The discrepancy of a high one costs O(V exp(−c√b)) before integrating the remaining ones. For the low ones, in the rescaled simplex each inverse denominator is ≤3d and the slack belongs to [1/2,2]. Differentiating up to three times the product of the inverses and the power of the slack costs at most (Cd)^(Cd), including the sum of Leibniz terms. The total cost in units √X is therefore ≤ exp(O(d log(2d)+d log(2+U))) [V exp(−c√b)+V^(−2) exp(−c√h)], which is o(V^(−2)) since h∼2U.

For the diagonal with j=d−2≥1, marking an equal pair leaves a factor 1/(2j!) after dividing by d!. There are at most j! y ordered tuples with product m≤y. For their weight log m, marking the prime carrying the logarithm and applying Chebyshev gives C j y (U+C)^(j−1). Thus the error in units √X is O(1/z+j(U+C)^(j−1)/(j! z log z)). Dividing by V^(−2)L^j/j! gives o(1) uniformly: j!/L^j≤1/L, and ((U+C)/L)^j=1+o(1) since U−L=log h. The case d=2 uses the semiprime diagonal already treated. The extension identifies a growing interval of adverse sectors. The global balance still depends on larger multiplicities.

**Upper localization of the compensation at logarithmic multiplicity.** For the fixed profile, put M=⌈6 log V/log 4⌉. Unconditionally Σ_{d>M}|C_d|≪√X/V². Indeed, the support forces n between two fixed multiples of X and the individual absolute weight is O(V/√X). Each squarefree integer has 4^{ω(n)} ordered factorizations into four positive integers, allowing ones. Up to Y there are at most Y(1+log Y)^3 such quadruples: fix the first three factors, count the fourth by division and extend the three harmonic sums up to Y. In the tail 4^{ω(n)}>4^M≥V^6. Multiplying these three bounds proves the claim even for the sum of absolute values at the level of integers.

For any fixed D ≥3, the balance of D<d≤M is therefore equivalent to −C_D>0: both the tail and the total are o(|C_D|). In particular the largest index of a strictly positive sector up to M tends to infinity. This conclusion uses only the already reviewed theorem for fixed multiplicity. With the preceding uniform extension one also obtains the same with D=⌊(log V)^{1/3}⌋: the last term dominates the initial sum by the ratio ≤D/L of successive principal terms in descending order and the uniform relative error. No alternating Möbius weight intervenes in C_d. The absolute tail bound still diverges at the scale of the global floor 1/16.


**Independent review of the triple sector: PROVED for the fixed profile, including the constant.** The reciprocal measure of primes replaced by da/a and the weight R lead, after dividing by 3!, to f₃=½∫da dd/(ad) over the simplex. They are unordered triples of distinct primes; the factor 1/6 is applied only after removing the repetitions. The two conditional densities are exactly R/(R−a−d) and 2Rlog((R−a−b)/b)/(R−a). In the low range a,d≤V/5, their denominators are bounded away from zero by a fixed fraction of V; the second and additional mixed derivatives have the announced sizes V^(−2),V^(−3).

The substitution of each low one is done AFTER integrating against the kernel with two vanishing moments, so its error and variation are O(V^(−2)), not the sizes before that cancellation. The discrepancy of the reciprocal measure from h costs exp(−c√h), which beats the fixed powers of logV. For p²q, the part p≤exp(V/5) is controlled by Chebyshev in q and costs √X/(zlogz); in p>exp(V/5), the integer count costs √XVexp(−V/5). Both are o(√X/V²), including p=q. The explicit derivatives of f₃ give [1−log(V/h)+o(1)]/V². Thus the constant term 1 is preserved, and on adding C₂ it cancels exactly in the principal term of the aggregate ≥4. The favourable aggregate does not imply that the sector of exactly four factors is favourable.

**Independent review of every fixed d: PROVED with constants depending on d.** Symmetry cancels one denominator with factor d/d!, and gives the simplex formula with (d−1)! in the denominator. Differentiating its boundary proves f_d'(r)=f_{d−1}(r−h)/(r−h), with f₁=1. The lower and upper boxes give f_j∼log(r/h)^{j−1}/(j−1)!. In f_d'', the positive term f'_{d−1}/(r−h) has one logarithmic power less than the negative −f_{d−1}/(r−h)². The correct sign and factorial (d−2)! result; for d=2 the positive term is zero.

After replacing the high ones, the conditional density r b_b^{*l}(r−A) has slack ≥V/2 and each denominator ≥V/(3d). Parametrizing it on a fixed simplex justifies the uniform derivatives in r and in the low variables, including l=1. The two vanishing moments allow applying Abel to the low ones without requiring a short-interval PNT. For the repetitions, the count of remaining tuples is O_d(y) and their logarithmic weight O_d(y(1+loglog(3y))^{d−3}). The error 1/z is not necessarily o(V^(−2)) by itself, but it is o(V^(−2)log(V/h)^{d−2}) for d≥3, which is the scale of the general equivalent. This validates all signs at fixed cardinality and the compensation by larger cardinalities, without yet summing equivalents with arbitrarily growing d.

**Independent review of the uniform range 2≤d≤⌊(logV)^{1/3}⌋: PROVED with the fixed profile.** Write U=logV, L=log(V/h). The box inclusions give relative error O(dlog(2d)/L) uniformly in r=V+O(h). The recurrence and the comparison of factorials leave the positive term of f_d'' with ratio O(d/L). These errors tend to zero over the whole range. For integrated Taylor it is not necessary that w=exp(−u/2)k(u) be positive: the fixed support, ∫w=∫uw=0 and ∫u²w=K''(1/2)>0 suffice. The uniform equivalence of the curvature controls the error by the fixed norm of u²w.

The simplex derivatives up to order 3 can be bounded by (Cd)^{Cd}: dimension ≤d, rescaled denominators ≥1/(3d), slack between 1/2 and 2 and only a number of differentiations polynomial in d for each term. Including partitions and reciprocal masses, the cost is exp(O(dlog(2d)+dlog(2+U))). For d≤U^{1/3} it is exp(O(U^{1/3}logU)), smaller than exp(c√h) since h∼2U. Thus the error of the low ones is o(V^(−2)); that of the high ones, with b=V/(3d), is even smaller. The computation hides no exponential constants in V here.

On the diagonal, marking one of the equal pairs and dividing by d! leaves 1/[2(d−2)!]. With j=d−2≥1, the ordered count is ≤j!y; for its weight logm, marking a position and applying Chebyshev gives Cjy(U+C)^{j−1}, with no other factorial. After summing over p>z, the error is the written 1/z+j(U+C)^{j−1}/(j!zlogz), with absolute constants depending only on the profile and κ. Dividing by V^(−2)L^j/j! leaves O(j!/L^j+j((U+C)/L)^j/((U+C)logz)). The first ratio is ≤1/L for 1≤j≤D and the power in the second is 1+o(1), because j(U−L+C)/L=O(U^(−2/3)logU). The remainder also tends uniformly to zero. The case d=2 is used separately and does not require a formula with j=0.

The equivalent is obtained with relative error o(1) over that whole growing range, and therefore simultaneous negative sectors there. Uniformity outside the range, a law for the complete typical multiplicity, or the joint floor at constant scale are not proved. The global balance still depends on larger cardinalities and on their compensation.

**Removal to constant precision near the maximal multiplicity.** The antecedent 374 gives exponent precision in a Gaussian sieve. Here the compact support and the distance of each prime from the edge z allow paying in absolute value o(1) for all d≥V/(h+δ), with δ>0 fixed and sufficiently small (depending on κ). The width in d removed relative to V/h grows like δV/h². Concretely the absolute tail is O(exp(−cV/h)).

Fix s>1. By PNT and partial integration H=Σ_{p>z}(p/z)^(−s)∼z/((s−1)h). In n≤BX for B fixed by the support, the products of d primes have Σ1≤(BX/z^d)^s H^d/d!, by multiplication and ordering. Each individual weight costs O(V exp(−V/2)). Write t=V/d−h, with −O(1/d)≤t≤δ for the nonempty layers of the range. Using d!≥(d/e)^d, the logarithm of the cost per layer divided by d is at most
(s−1/2)t + 1 + (log κ)/2 − log(s−1) + o(1).
Indeed log(z/(dh))=log V+log κ+log(1+t/h) and h=2 log V+log κ. The o(1) is uniform because s is frozen and d∼V/h. Choose first s with log(s−1)>2+(log κ)/2 and then δ>0 with (s−1/2)δ<1/2. Summing O(V) layers preserves the decay. The eventual floor 1/16 now admits a reformulation with the tail removed and a margin: under RH the subtotal exceeds 1/16 eventually by the reserve 3/32; outside RH it keeps unbounded negative excursions. The cancellation at intermediate multiplicities remains open.

**Removal threshold by sum of moduli at the fine scale.** For fixed a>0 let E_a(V) be the sum of the individual absolute values of the detector in d≥V/(h+a). Let F(a)=2+½ log κ+log a+a/2. If F(a)<0, E_a(V) decreases like O(exp(−cV/h)); if F(a)>0, E_a(V)≥exp(cV/h) along a sequence. The endpoint F(a)=0 remains open. The first statement optimizes the previous section by putting s=1+1/a. For the second one needs to adapt the packing of 374 to a tilted distribution of primes reaching the same frontier.

Choose 0<t<a with F(t)>0 and s=1+1/t. For growing integer d solve V₀/d=log(κV₀²)+t on the branch V₀>2d (existence by continuity and monotonicity), and put Z=κV₀². Use primes in [(1+ε)Z,RZ] with probability proportional to (p/Z)^(−s). By PNT the normalization mass H is equivalent to ZI/log Z with I=∫_{1+ε}^R y^(−s)dy. The mean of log(p/Z) tends to m=∫y^(−s)log y dy/I within those limits. Taking ε small and R large, I→t and m→t. Freeze them with m<a and 1+½logκ+log I+(s−½)m>0, possible by F(t)>0.

In d independent draws, the sum of log(p/Z) is dm+o(d) with probability 1−o(1) (Chebyshev with deviation d^(2/3) from the exact mean). Collisions have probability O(d²/H)=O(1/log Z). Each tuple in that concentration event without collisions has probability ≤H^(−d)exp(−sdm+o(d)). Dividing its lower count by d! and distributing the products into O(d) cells of fixed width leaves one cell with at least H^d exp(sdm−o(d))/d! distinct products. Choose the width smaller than an interval where |k| has a positive floor and shift the centre of the cell so that V−log n falls in that interval. Then V/d=log Z+m+o(1), V/V₀→1, h−log Z=o(1), the chosen primes exceed κV² and V/d−h<a. By Stirling, on multiplying by the minimal weight ≫V exp(−V/2), the logarithm of that mass divided by d has lower limit ≥1+½logκ+log I+(s−½)m>0. This proves the subsequential floor. The frontier depends on the method of taking moduli at the individual level; it does not decide the signed tail. Antecedent 374 uses a uniform box for another regime; the continuous tilting obtains the coinciding threshold here.


**Independent review of the extreme removal to constant precision: PROVED for the fixed detector.** With H_s=Σ_{p>z}(p/z)^(−s), s>1 fixed, PNT and parts give H_s=z/((s−1)h)(1+o(1)), h=logz. Counting products of d distinct primes through ordering costs H_s^d/d!; no product is counted twice because factorization is unique and one divides by the d! permutations. The restriction n≤BX allows Rankin with (BX/z^d)^s. On the fixed proportional support, the absolute weight (logn)n^(−1/2)|k(V−logn)| is ≤CVexp(−V/2).

For a nonempty layer with d≥V/(h+δ), t=V/d−h satisfies −logB/d≤t≤δ and d∼V/h. The logarithm of the majorant divided by d is
(s−1/2)t+1+(logκ)/2−log(s−1)+log(1+t/h)+o(1).
The term log(1+t/h) is o(1) uniformly and the factor CV and B^s also contribute only o(1) at this scale. This verifies the announced formula, its signs and the absence of a residual factorial. Fixing s with log(s−1)>2+(logκ)/2 and then δ>0 with (s−1/2)δ<1/2 leaves a uniform negative ceiling. Each layer costs exp(−cd), and summing the O(V) nonempty layers keeps O(exp(−c'V/h))=o(1). Integer roundings only alter O(1) layers or the exponent by O(1).

The threshold V/h is the elementary ceiling given by the minimal prime size, not a claim of attainability of the exact maximal multiplicity. The width δV/h²(1+o(1)) diverges and the conclusion removes that whole tail in absolute value. The EVENTUAL criterion with margin is preserved: under RH the subtotal keeps ≥3/32−o(1)>1/16 and outside RH the negative excursions survive. It is not claimed that a pointwise inequality at the exact threshold 1/16 transfers without margin for each X. The argument here is formulated for the fixed compact profile; a moving profile would require budgeting separately its norm and the lower edge of the support.

**Comparison with 374.** Both use ordering, factorial and a Rankin bound for layers of large cardinality. 374 studies a Gaussian weight and exponent precision, allowing removal of x^(1/2+o(1)) in the budget of its criterion; it contains no o(1) elimination of the present normalized sum. Here one uses that each prime exceeds z=κV², the tilted reciprocal mass with large fixed s and the proportional support of the detector to obtain a negative exponent at scale V/logz AFTER normalizing by √n. It is a specific refinement of that absolute cost and not a new cancellation mechanism. It does not control the band of intermediate multiplicities nor does it resolve the joint floor.

**Cancellation to constant precision for divisibility patterns by blocks.** The cutoff can be chosen adaptively among the primes ≤κV². Moreover, split ALL those primes into r arbitrary blocks, even dependent on V. For a squarefree composite record the exact set J of blocks in which it has some prime divisor. Denote by W_J the signed sum of the fixed detector on that class. There exist κ,c,η>0 such that for r≤ηV/log V one has uniformly Σ_{J≠∅}|W_J|≤exp(−cV/log V). Here the modulus is taken after summing each class: cancellation within each pattern is preserved, without cancellation between patterns. W_∅ is the floor problem that remains open.

Proof. In the audited proof of the shift of A_z, removing any subset of the finite product only reduces the majorant of its logarithm, since that was obtained by summing individual positive majorants. For T a set of blocks, let A(T) be the sum over all squarefree integers that can only use small blocks in T (the large primes remain free). Thus |A(T)|≤E=O(exp(−c₀V/log V)) with common constants. For J≠∅, exact inversion on the set of blocks gives W_J=Σ_{T⊆J}(−1)^{|J|−|T|}A(T): the visible primes only occupy the empty pattern. Hence Σ_{J≠∅}|W_J|≤(3^r−1)E. It suffices to choose η log 3<c₀. The argument allows choosing any collection of patterns after observing the weights, at the same cost. The global equivalence of the empty pattern prevents assigning it a floor through this inversion.


**Independent review of the fine threshold and of the tilted packing: PROVED for F(a)≠0.** In the Rankin ceiling, s=1+1/a minimizes (s−1/2)a+1+(logκ)/2−log(s−1); its value is exactly F(a). The remainder log(1+t/h)=o(1) is uniform over the nonempty layers. Thus F(a)<0 gives the saving exp(−cV/h). The function F is strictly increasing in a>0, since F'(a)=1/a+1/2, and has a unique zero; the behaviour at that zero has not been evaluated.

If F(a)>0, one can fix 0<t<a with F(t)>0 and then s=1+1/t. The equation V₀/d=log(κV₀²)+t has a unique solution V₀>2d for large d, because its left side minus the logarithm is strictly increasing there, starts negative and tends to infinity. On truncating the tilted law to [1+ε,R], its normalizer I and its mean m converge to t as ε↓0 and R→∞. One can therefore freeze ε,R keeping m<a and 1+(logκ)/2+logI+(s−1/2)m>0.

The prime normalization H∼ZI/logZ holds for those fixed limits. The draws have uniformly bounded variance; Chebyshev is applied to the EXACT MEAN and afterwards this converges to m, giving S=dm+o(d) with probability 1−o(1), without requiring a rate for that PNT. Each point weight is O(1/H), and d²/H=O(1/logZ) by V₀=d(logZ+t), so collisions also have probability o(1). On the joint event each tuple has probability ≤H^(−d)exp(−sdm+o(d)), providing the lower count. Division by d! is exact for tuples without collisions, by unique factorization; the O(d) cells of fixed width lose only exp(o(d)).

Choosing a concentrated cell and placing it in a fixed interval with |k|≥c produces V/d=logZ+m+o(1). Then V/V₀→1 and log(κV²)−logZ=o(1). The chosen primes are ≥(1+ε)Z, so they still exceed the FINAL cutoff κV²; the margin ε is necessary for that verification. Moreover V/d−log(κV²)→m<a, so the layer d belongs to the tail of the statement even after rounding the threshold. The individual weights have floor cVexp(−V/2).

Stirling gives for the logarithm of the contribution divided by d the lower bound 1+(logκ)/2+logI+(s−1/2)m+o(1)>0: one uses (1/2)logZ−log(dlogZ)=(logκ)/2+o(1). This verifies the same frontier F(a) from both sides and the subsequential lower bound exp(cV/h). It is a tilted packing of the mechanism of 374, now adjusted to the normalized absolute mass and to the moving final cutoff. The same lower bound does not follow at all scales, at the equality F(a)=0, for the signed tail or for the sign of the global balance.

**Simultaneous quadratic cancellation within the remaining composites, by prescribed large divisor.** Fix 0<ε<1. Choose κ>0 sufficiently small depending on ε, always within the authorized range of the sieve. For 1<q≤X^(1−ε) let B_q be the balance of C_z over multiples of q. Then
Σ_q |B_q|² ≪_ε exp(−c_ε V/log V).
This statement does concern the previous empty pattern: q can have only factors >z for the sum to be nonzero.

For squarefree q with all primes >z the series of such multiples, still without logarithm, is q^(−s) A_z(s) Π_{p|q}(1+p^(−s))^(−1). The primes of the support cannot be multiples of q: for prime q the only possibility would be n=q, below the support. The negative derivative provides the total logarithm. Repeat the already proved inversion with shift λ=b/log V, b fixed small. The additional product and its derivative cost O(poly(V)) in the enlarged strip: there are at most V/log z factors and each p^(−1/2+2λ)≤z^(−1/2+2λ)=O_κ(1/V). For the derivative Cauchy is used only on the product, differentiating q^(−s) explicitly. The double pole is still cancelled by K. The new vertical pays q^(−1/2) exp(−λ(V−log q)); choose κ so small that the cost of the product of small primes, exp(C√κ V/log V), absorbs at most half the saving ελV. The horizontals and the initial tail remain uniform after extracting q^(−1/2), because exp((σ−1/2)(V−log q))≤exp(3V/2) on the whole rectangle. One gets |B_q|≪q^(−1/2)exp(−cV/log V). The sum of 1/q is O(V), absorbable in the exponent. The q with a square or with a small factor contribute zero.

Consequence: any combination of the indicators q|n in this range whose coefficient vector has Euclidean norm exp(o(V/log V)) produces a balance o(1) by Cauchy–Schwarz. A combination reproducing the unit weight on these composites would therefore have to exceed that budget at any scale with C_z≥1/16. The bound controls divisibility combinations; a representation or one-sided estimate of the unit weight is still pending.

**Balanced semiprimes force a quantitative loss for reconstruction by divisors.** Let f(n)=Σ_{1<q≤X^(1−ε),q|n}b_q, with ε fixed in (0,1). For each of the two signs of k there is a band of semiprimes in which, if ||b||₂=o(X^(1/4)/√V), the weighted absolute error in approximating 1 by f is ≫√X/V. It is an unconditional obstruction to paying the reconstruction error in modulus, even in each sign region separately.

Indeed, k is continuous, real and nonzero and has vanishing exponential moment, so for each sign there is an open interval with that sign and |k|≥c>0. Choose fixed 0<A<B such that [−2log B,−2log A] lies in that interval. Between A√X and B√X there are N≍√X/V primes, all larger than z. In each product of two distinct ones from the interval only the two primes can enter as divisors in f: the product exceeds X^(1−ε). Complete the missing coefficients with zero. The mean of f over unordered pairs is (2/N)Σ_p b_p; its modulus is ≤2||b||₂/√N. By the triangle inequality the mean of |1−f| is at least 1−2||b||₂/√N. Each absolute weight of the detector is ≫V/√X, and there are N(N−1)/2 pairs, giving the claim. In particular every exact reconstruction forces ||b||₂≥√N/2, even at scales where the sign of C_z is unknown. In fact the equations of three distinct pairs force b_p=1/2 on the whole interval if there is exactness. The computation also does not exclude approximations designed so that their errors compensate with the sign of k; that compensation would be an additional mathematical obligation.

**Positive rings of imbalance between the two primes.** For the same fixed detector, freeze 0≤α<β<1 and restrict C₂ to αV<log(q/p)≤βV, p<q. The balance is
(K''(1/2)/2)(√X/V²)[G(β)−G(α)+O_{α,β}(1/V)], with G(t)=4t/(1−t²)².
Thus each fixed interior ring has favourable sign for large V, even though the whole semiprime layer has adverse sign. The constant of the remainder depends on the endpoint β.

Proof. First impose only log(q/p)≤b with b=tV fixed when integrating and 0<t<1. On the support r=log(pq)=V+O(1) both logarithms are ≥(1−t)V/2−O(1); z stays inactive. The same PNT replacement of the C₂ computation holds with error O(√X poly(V) exp(−c_t√V)): in q an additional interval is cut by q≤p exp(b), whose edge costs the same variation; in the remaining integral, for fixed r the additional cut in p is p≥exp((r−b)/2), still exponential in V. In a=log p the density of unordered pairs becomes ∫_{(r−b)/2}^{r/2}r da/[a(r−a)]=log((r+b)/(r−b)). Its second derivative in r is 4br/(r²−b²)² and the third is O_t(V^(−3)) on the band. Taylor against the two vanishing moments gives the equivalent; for t=0 the sum is empty. Subtracting the two cuts and using that G is strictly increasing concludes. On the other hand if one cuts log(q/p)≤t log(pq), the same continuous integral equals the constant log((1+t)/(1−t)); it disappears by the first vanishing moment (the one of order zero). The two edges differ only by a logarithmic O(1), but that movement explains the whole principal term.

By subtraction from the total C₂, the pairs with log(q/p)>βV have coefficient −1−G(β) in the same units. Removal at fixed β does not control β→1 uniformly. The interior sign is a signed result in the original sieve; the sum over all multiplicities remains open.


**Independent review of the block patterns: PROVED uniformly over the indicated partitions.** Allowing only the blocks of T amounts to excluding the complementary subset of primes ≤κV² in the product of A_z. The contour majorants are sums of positive terms per prime; omitting factors only reduces that ceiling, including the Cauchy derivatives. Thus A(T) has the same error E uniformly over all subsets and over the partition chosen after the weights. Since A(T)=B_X+Σ_{J⊆T}W_J and the visible primes are larger than the cutoff, subset inversion for J≠∅ removes B_X exactly. The sum of absolute coefficients is Σ_{J≠∅}2^{|J|}=3^r−1. Choosing ηlog3<c₀ leaves a uniform saving. The empty pattern is not estimated by this inversion; it is the piece that keeps the global difficulty.

**Independent review of the prescribed multiples B_q: PROVED for fixed ε and κ sufficiently small depending on ε.** If q is squarefree and all its primes exceed z, the exact series is q^(−s)A_z(s)∏_{p|q}(1+p^(−s))^(−1). Otherwise the sector is empty. For prime q, the only prime multiple would be q itself, outside the support because q≤X^(1−ε)<exp(V−S); hence the full series of multiples can be used for composite B_q. The negative derivative of the FULL PRODUCT has only a double pole at 1: when differentiating its Laurent expansion the simple pole does not appear. K of order two cancels it.

In the enlarged strip, each additional factor satisfies p^(−1/2+2λ)≤z^(−1/2+2λ)=O_κ(1/V), and there are ≤V/logz factors. Their product is uniformly bounded, and Cauchy only adds polynomial losses for its derivative. q^(−s) is differentiated explicitly, with logq≤V. Extracting q^(−1/2) leaves exp((σ−1/2)(V−logq)) in the exponential. The new vertical pays ≥ελV; the small products cost exp(C√κV/logV) and are absorbed by reducing κ. The horizontals keep the same extraction and the ceiling exp(3V/2), dominated by the Gevrey decay. One obtains q^(−1/2)exp(−cV/logV) uniformly. On squaring, Σ1/q=O(V) is absorbable. Cauchy–Schwarz controls combinations of coefficients of norm exp(o(V/logV)), not the unit weight without a representation of that cost.

**Independent review of the obstruction by balanced semiprimes: PROVED for absolute reconstruction error.** The vanishing weighted moment and k real, continuous and nonzero guarantee intervals of both signs. Choosing an interval of primes [A√X,B√X] with all its products inside one of those regions gives N≍√X/V primes, larger than z. Each product of two distinct ones exceeds X^(1−ε); its only proper nontrivial divisors are both primes. Those not entering the q budget are completed with coefficient zero, which also covers ε≥1/2.

The mean of f over all unordered pairs is exactly 2Σb_p/N, of modulus ≤2||b||₂/√N. The mean of |1−f| is therefore ≥1−2||b||₂/√N, even for complex coefficients. Each absolute weight has floor cV/√X and there are N(N−1)/2 distinct products, giving the error ≥c√X/V when ||b||₂=o(X^(1/4)/√V). In exact reconstruction, the equations of three pairs force b_p=1/2 on the whole band; if some missing coefficient was set to zero, exactness is impossible. The norm lower bound √N/2 is correct and holds in each sign region. It does not exclude an approximate reconstruction whose error is compensated using the sign of the kernel; that would be an additional signed step. The sign of C_z is not attributed to the sum of absolute errors.

**Interior positivity for any fixed multiplicity by translation of all the logarithms.** Fix d≥2. Write r=log n and order the primes of n. Let P be a fixed convex polytope of positive volume (in the first d−1 coordinates) in Σy_i=0, y₁≤⋯≤y_d, with min_P(1/d+y₁)>0. Select the n for which y_i=(log p_i−r/d)/V belong jointly to P. Their contribution to C_d is
√X K''(1/2) H_P''(1)/(2V²)+O_P(√X/V³), with H_P''(1)>0.
Here H_P(x)=∫_P Σ_i Π_{j≠i}(x/d+y_j)^(−1) dy₁⋯dy_{d−1}. The conclusion includes regions far from the perfectly balanced point: a fixed separation from the edge where a relative logarithm vanishes suffices. The scaling of the displacement is frozen at V.

Proof. On the band r=V+O(1) all logarithms t_i are ≥c_P V. Use the prime measure Σ_p p^(−1)δ_{log p} in each variable and the test √X r w(V−r), w(u)=exp(−u/2)k(u). Each section with the other variables fixed is an interval by convexity, ordering and linearity of the cuts; ties are excluded by strict inequalities. The test has variation O(V), even with the jumps of the interval. On [c_P V,2V] PNT by parts gives accumulated discrepancy O(poly(V) exp(−c'√V)) with respect to dt/t, uniform over intervals and their endpoints. Telescope d replacements; the individual masses on that band are O_P(1). Thus the continuous error is O_P(√X poly(V)exp(−c'√V)). Ordering counts each product once and removes the diagonals without additional correction.

Passing from (t_i) to (r,y₁,…,y_{d−1}) has absolute Jacobian V^(d−1), since t_i=r/d+Vy_i and Σ y_i=0. The elementary identity r/Πt_j=Σ_i Π_{j≠i}1/t_j cancels exactly that power of V. The density at fixed r becomes H_P(r/V). Each summand in H_P has strictly positive second derivative: when differentiating twice the reciprocals of positive factors, both the double and the cross terms are positive. The separation from the edge bounds the first three derivatives near 1. Taylor against w, with vanishing moments of orders zero and one, concludes. For each fixed d the total balance C_d is eventually negative: the part outside the polytope absorbs the favourable principal term of the interior. The limit V→∞ is not interchanged with an exhaustion of the simplex nor with d→∞. The identity assigns no discrete sign to arbitrarily small polytopes depending on V.


**Independent review of the positive semiprime rings: PROVED for fixed 0≤α<β<1.** With b=tV frozen, p<q and log(q/p)≤b impose exp((r−b)/2)≤p≤exp(r/2). The continuous measure has density ∫r/[a(r−a)]da on that interval, exactly log((r+b)/(r−b)), without duplication of pairs or additional factor 2. Its second derivative is 4br/(r²−b²)²; at r=V+O(1) it equals G(t)/V²+O_t(V^(−3)), with G(t)=4t/(1−t²)². The two vanishing moments and K''(1/2)>0 give the announced positive coefficient. G'(t)=4(1+3t²)/(1−t²)³>0, so subtracting the cuts keeps a positive margin for each fixed ring.

The primes at both edges are ≥exp((1−β)V/2−O(1)), far above z. PNT and variation pay uniformly for the limits q=p, q=pexp(b) and the corresponding moving endpoint in p, with error √Xpoly(V)exp(−c_β√V), smaller than the remainder √X/V³. The cut t=0 is empty and is treated exactly, not through a nonuniform limit. If instead b=tr depends on the product, the density log((1+t)/(1−t)) is constant and the vanishing weighted moment removes that principal term. The edges differ by O(1) but their movement is precisely of the order needed to change the curvature; the two partitions are not confused.

Subtracting from the semiprime total leaves the coefficient −1−G(β) for the outer edge, in the same units K''√X/(2V²). Uniformity β→1 is not claimed, nor a sign for the total over multiplicities. It is an interior signed positivity for this frozen partition, compatible with the negativity of the full semiprime sector and without automatic transfer to the constant floor.

**The semiprime edge loss changes sign when the smaller prime is fixed.** Let h=log z. Choose C>1+sup{|u|:k(u)≠0}, fixed, and g=h+C. Within C₂ compare two layers of the smaller factor p: the fixed one  h<log p≤g  and the moving one  h<log p<g+(r−V)/2, r=log(pq). Both have bounded logarithmic thickness and lie entirely in p≍z. For the fixed one the balance is ∼K''(1/2) C √X/V³, POSITIVE. For the moving one it is ∼−K''(1/2)√X/(8g²), NEGATIVE. The mere bounded change of the upper endpoint alters even the order of magnitude.

For the fixed layer, first replace q by PNT as in C₂. The exact remaining density is Σ_{z<p≤exp(g)}p^(−1)r/(r−log p). Its second derivative is Σ 2 log p/[p(r−log p)³]∼2C/V³, uniformly in r=V+O(1), since PNT by parts gives Σ log p/p=C+o(1) on that band of fixed ratio. Integral Taylor concludes.

For the moving layer first take its complement in C₂. It is the cut log(q/p)≤b with b=V−2g; for r=V+O(1) its lower edge ℓ=(r−b)/2 is >h. After replacing q, the remaining prime sum over ℓ≤log p≤r/2 has multiplier r/(r−log p) with respect to the measure Σ1/p; its supremum and variation are ≤2. By quantitative PNT and parts the accumulated discrepancy of that measure with respect to da/a on any subinterval of [ℓ,∞) is O(poly(ℓ)exp(−c√ℓ)), uniform in the right endpoint. Here ℓ=g+O(1) and the error is o(g^(−2)). The first replacement, in q≥exp((V−O(1))/2), costs only poly(V)exp(−c√V) in units √X, uniformly in b by variation over intervals. In the continuous density log(r+b)−log(r−b), the second derivative in V equals 1/(4g²)−1/(2V−2g)² and the third is O(g^(−3)). The moments give the complement the principal term +K''(1/2)√X/(8g²). Subtracting from C₂=O(√X/V²) proves the sign of the moving layer. The difference between the two layers, with the orientations of their endpoints, explains the full principal term. Hence an attribution of the deficit to primes p≍z based solely on moving cuts is not preserved under the fixed arithmetic cut.


**Independent review of interior positivity for fixed d: PROVED with a fixed polytope separated from the edge.** In the chosen coordinates, the matrix of (t₁,…,t_d) with respect to (r,y₁,…,y_{d−1}) has first column 1/d and remaining columns V(e_j−e_d). Its determinant has modulus V^{d−1}, without an additional factor d. The identity r/∏t_i=Σ_i∏_{j≠i}t_j^(−1) cancels that power exactly. The strict order counts each product of distinct primes once, so one does not divide by d! either. This verifies the normalization of H_P.

The polytope is convex and the coordinates y are affine functions of each t_i when the others are fixed. Together with the support of k and the strict order, the integration section in each variable is a single interval, possibly empty, with open or closed endpoints. Since min_P(1/d+y₁)>0 and the profile has fixed support, all t_i lie in [c_PV,2V] for large V. The test r w(V−r) has supremum and variation O(V), including the two jumps of the section. PNT for the reciprocal measure gives a uniform error over all those intervals and endpoints, while the other discrete or continuous masses are O_P(1). Telescoping the d replacements leaves O_P(√Xpoly(V)exp(−c_P√V)). Ties are excluded from the initial discrete sum; the continuous boundaries have measure zero and the endpoint errors are within that estimate. No separate hypothesis on diagonals is required.

In a fixed neighbourhood of x=1, each factor x/d+y_j is positive and bounded away from zero. Each second derivative of a product of their reciprocals is strictly positive: both repeated and cross terms have positive sign. Its integral over P of positive volume gives H_P''(1)>0; the first three derivatives are bounded with constants depending on P,d. Taylor in r/V=1−u/V and the two vanishing moments give exactly √XK''(1/2)H_P''(1)/(2V²), with remainder O_P(√X/V³).

Freezing the scale V is essential: normalizing the deviations by r instead of V would make the continuous density constant at the level of the product and would remove this principal term by the zero moment. The result extends the phenomenon of semiprime rings to interior polytopes; it does not imply a favourable sign of the full sector. The negative equivalents for each fixed d force its complement to absorb the contribution. It is not interchanged with an exhaustion towards the edge, with polytopes depending on V or with growing d.

**All multiplicities simultaneously: localization of the possible deficit when ordering by the largest prime.** Let [A,B] be the minimal closed interval containing the fixed support of k. Decompose each visible composite uniquely as n=mq with q its largest prime, P=P⁺(m)<q and m>1 squarefree without primes ≤z. Put a=log m, l=V−a, τ=l−log P. In every fibre with τ≥B the discrete balance is, uniformly in m,
(√X/m) K''(1/2) a/l³ (1+o(1)) >0.
There is no fixed limit on ω(m), nor the condition m≤X^δ of the small-cofactor antecedent. The fibres with τ≤A are empty except for possible zero-weight terms at the endpoints. Therefore any deficit in this partition can only come from A<τ<B. Each product of those fibres has 1<q/P≤exp(B−A), that is, the two largest primes are comparable. The positivity claim corresponds to complete fibres, not to truncations of a fibre by q/P.

Proof. In a complete fibre, write w(u)=exp(−u/2)k(u). Its balance in units √X/m is Σ_q (a+log q) w(l−log q)/q. The strict order removes no term of nonzero weight if τ≥B. The support forces log q=l+O(1), with l≥log z+O(1)→∞. By quantitative PNT for the measure Σ_q q^(−1)δ_{log q} on that band and parts, replacing it by dt/t costs O(V poly(l)exp(−c√l)), with constants independent of m. The resulting integral is ∫w(u)[1+a/(l−u)]du. The uniform geometric expansion, the two vanishing moments and ∫u²w=K''(1/2)>0 give K''(1/2)a/l³+O(a/l⁴). The relative PNT error is o(1) uniformly even if l≪V: V/a=1+l/a≤1+l for a≥1 and l tends to infinity uniformly. Errors with uncertain signs are not summed in order to claim positivity of each fibre. In a cut fibre the restriction q>P amounts to u<τ; if it contributes then log(q/P)=τ−u≤B−A. On summing, it suffices to control the balance of the cut fibres together with the positive reserve of the complete ones. The previous relative estimate does not give that comparison to constant precision.

**Balance after joining the two largest primes, uniform in the remaining multiplicity.** Fix the kernel and write n=mpq, with p<q the two largest distinct primes. m can be 1; otherwise it is squarefree with P⁻(m)>z. Let a=log m, L=V−a, H=log max(z,P⁺(m)), with P⁺(1)=1. If H/L belongs to any compact subset of (0,1/2), the full balance of this m, in units √X/m, equals
(K''(1/2)/(2L²)) [−b²+(a/L)(2log((L−H)/H)−2b−b²)] + O((1+a/L)/L³), b=L/(L−H).
The constant depends only on the compact set and the detector; ω(m) is arbitrary. The complete and truncated groups of the previous step are already summed here.

Proof. For r=log(pq)=L−u, H<log p<r/2. PNT allows replacing both prime measures Σ1/p by dt/t with error O(V poly(L)exp(−c√L)): the sections in each variable are intervals, the test (a+r)w(L−r) has variation O(V), and log p, log q lie between cL and 2L. L→∞ uniformly because H≥log z. The resulting density is F(r)=(1+a/r)log((r−H)/H), by integration in log p. Two derivatives give L²F''(L) equal to the announced bracket; the third is O((1+a/L)/L³) near L. Taylor gives the formula, absorbing the PNT error since V=L+a. There is no additional discrete contribution from p=q when strict order is imposed from the start.

Uniform favourable example: if 1/20≤H/L≤1/10 and a≥2L, the bracket is ≥c(1+a/L) with c>0: b≤10/9 and 2log9−20/9−100/81>0.93. Therefore the reserve of complete groups exceeds here the loss of the truncated ones. Adverse example: if 1/3≤H/L≤2/5, b≥3/2 and log((L−H)/H)≤log 2, so the bracket is ≤−c(1+a/L) for any a≥0. This prevents declaring every grouping by the two largest primes favourable. The sum over m and the regimes outside these compact sets still lack a sufficient one-sided bound.


**Independent review of the fixed and moving bands at the sieve edge: PROVED with the indicated signs and scales.** In the fixed band h<logp≤h+C, the second derivative of the discrete density is Σ2logp/[p(r−logp)³]. PNT at that fixed multiplicative ratio gives Σlogp/p=C+o(1), and r=V+O(1), logp=O(logV), so the curvature is 2C/V³(1+o(1)). The two weighted moments leave the positive principal term K''C√X/V³. The error of the first PNT replacement is smaller than that scale, and there is no need to approximate the sum over p with pointwise precision before differentiating.

For the complement of the moving band b=V−2g is frozen. The edge ℓ=(r−b)/2=g+(r−V)/2 stays strictly above h by the choice of C. The first replacement keeps q≥exp((V−O(1))/2) and the variation over an interval, regardless of b/V→1. In the second, the reciprocal prime measure has uniform discrepancy O(poly(ℓ)exp(−c√ℓ)) and the multiplier r/(r−logp) has supremum ≤2 and variation ≤1. The error is o(g^(−2)). The curvature of log(r+b)−log(r−b) in V is 1/(4g²)−1/(2V−2g)², with third derivative O(g^(−3)); hence the positive complement K''√X/(8g²). Subtracting the semiprime total O(√X/V²) gives the NEGATIVE principal term of the moving band. Signs are not transferred between the two cuts, although both restrict p to constant ratios of z. The comparison shows the effect of moving the edge with the product, not a universal negative contribution of small primes.

**Independent review of complete fibres by largest prime: PROVED uniformly, without a multiplicity limit.** Each squarefree composite n is written uniquely as n=mq with q the largest prime and P⁺(m)<q. The sum over a fibre divided by √X/m is exactly Σ_q(a+logq)w(l−logq)/q, where a=logm, l=V−a. The normalizing factor is NOT √(X/m): the identity uses q=e^{l−u} and the factor exp(−u/2) included in w. This verifies the announced scale.

If τ=l−logP≥B, the order q>P removes no term of nonzero weight: on the support logq≥l−B≥logP; equality only touches the endpoint u=B, where k(B)=0 by continuity and compact support. Moreover l≥logz+O(1)→∞ uniformly and a≥1 for large V. PNT for the reciprocal measure of primes on the band logq=l+O(1), integrated against (a+logq)w, costs O(Vpoly(l)exp(−c√l)), with constants of the fixed profile and not of m.

The continuous integral is exactly ∫w(u)[1+a/(l−u)]du. Expanding geometrically on the fixed support and using its moments of orders 0,1 leaves K''(1/2)a/l³+O(a/l⁴). The PNT error divided by the principal term is ≤(V/a)poly(l)l³exp(−c√l). Since V/a=1+l/a≤1+l, this majorant tends to zero uniformly for all l≥logz+O(1), even if l is much smaller than V. Uniform positivity and equivalence are obtained, without summing errors of uncertain sign over fibres.

If τ≤A there are no nonzero terms because q>P requires u<τ. For A<τ<B, any visible product has log(q/P)=τ−u in (0,B−A], hence 1<q/P≤exp(B−A). Only these partially cut fibres can originate a loss in the partition. The conclusion is about COMPLETE fibres, not about all products with two comparable primes nor about internal truncations of a fibre. The set of fibres is finite for each X by the support; there is no need to impose beforehand a limit on ω(m). The earlier results with small cofactor are restricted cases of the same change of variable and PNT; uniformity through V/a≤1+l allows reaching here down to l≈logz. It still remains to compare the cut fibres with the positive reserve of the complete ones at constant scale; the global floor has not been proved.

**Positive contribution at the opening threshold of the two largest primes.** With the previous notation fix the explicit detector v=(∂−1/2)φ for the nonnegative Gevrey box density. Write J(u)=exp(−u/2)(φ*φ)(u), so that w=J'' and J≥0. For every cofactor with θ=L−2H in a fixed bounded band, its full balance in units √X/m equals, uniformly,
[(1+a/(2H))/H] J(θ) + O((1+a/H)/H²).
In particular it is positive for large V whenever θ belongs to a compact set where J has positive minimum, with no restriction on ω(m). In this band H→∞. Compared with the interior curvature formula, the opening of the support contributes an additional power of H to the principal term.

Indeed, the exact continuous density is F(r)=0 if r≤2H, and F(r)=(1+a/r)log((r−H)/H) if r>2H. The discrete replacement costs O(V poly(H)exp(−c√H)) in units √X/m, by the same sections into intervals, even when crossing the empty threshold. This error is o((1+a/H)/H²), since V=a+2H+O(1). At the threshold, F is continuous and its derivative jumps from zero to (1+a/(2H))/H. By two integrations by parts, ∫w(u)F(L−u)du consists exactly of that jump multiplied by J(θ) and of ∫_{u<θ}J(u)F''(L−u)du, where F'' is here the ordinary derivative of the open branch. On the band r=2H+O(1) that derivative is bounded by O((1+a/H)/H²). This proves the formula. For m>1 the place of opening corresponds exactly to V=log(mP⁺(m)²)+θ; it is the contact of the two free primes with the largest prime already present in the cofactor. The previous analysis of bands H/L separated from 1/2 omitted this term. It remains pending to sum the reserve of these contacts against the loss of the open region with smaller H/L.

**Aggregate size of a family of contacts of three largest primes.** Fix 0<δ<1/4 and a closed interval I of positive length with min_I J>0. Take all cofactors m=tP with t≤X^δ squarefree without primes ≤z (including 1), P prime, V−log t−3log P∈I. The balance R_X of the corresponding COMPLETE fibres, summed only once, satisfies unconditionally
R_X ≍ √X/(V log z).
The constants depend on δ,I and the profile. The other composites have balance −R_X(1+o(1)), since PNT for the total detector already gave C_z=o(√X/(V log z)). The equivalence of the complement resolves its principal scale, not the constant remainder.

Indeed P≍(X/t)^(1/3)>t for large V, uniformly by δ<1/4, so P is the largest prime of m and the representation is unique. H=log P≍V, a=log(tP)=O(V). By the computation at the contact, each fibre gives between two fixed positive multiples of √X/(tPV). At fixed t, P runs over a band of fixed multiplicative ratio >1, where PNT gives Σ1/P≍1/V uniformly. It remains to estimate the harmonic mass of the admissible t. By Mertens the product Π_{z<p≤X^δ}(1+1/p)≍V/log z is a ceiling. For the floor take only primes ≤X^η with η=δ/4, choosing them independently with probability 1/(p+1). The law of the product of the chosen ones is the mass 1/t normalized by Π(1+1/p). The expectation of log t is Σ log p/(p+1)≤ηV+O(1) by Mertens, so by Markov at least half of the mass stays with t≤X^δ. The normalizing product is again ≍V/log z. Multiplying the three estimates proves the statement. The sector includes variable multiplicities without counting the same composite in two fibres.


**Independent review of the balance by the two largest primes: PROVED uniformly in ω(m) and on the declared compact sets.** After writing n=mpq, p<q and both larger than max(z,P⁺(m)), the normalization is again √X/m. Integrating the reciprocal measure of the two primes gives (a+r)∫_H^{r/2}dt/[t(r−t)]=(1+a/r)log((r−H)/H). One does not divide by two after imposing p<q. Differentiating this density twice gives exactly L^(−2) times −b²+(a/L)[2log((L−H)/H)−2b−b²], b=L/(L−H). The third derivative is O((1+a/L)/L³) when H/L stays in a compact subset of (0,1/2).

In that regime each prime logarithm lies between cL and 2L and the sections are intervals; endpoints and ties are handled through strict order from the start. PNT leaves O(Vpoly(L)exp(−c√L)) in units √X/m. Since V=L+a, that error is absorbed uniformly in O((1+a/L)/L³); L→∞ uniformly because H≥logz. The constant does not need to know how many primes m has. Taylor with the fixed moments gives the formula, without a small relative error when its bracket vanishes.

For 1/20≤H/L≤1/10, one has b²≤100/81 and 2log((L−H)/H)−2b−b²≥2log9−20/9−100/81>0.93. With a/L≥2, subtracting b² still leaves a floor c(1+a/L). For 1/3≤H/L≤2/5, b≥3/2 and the expression in parentheses is ≤2log2−3−9/4<0; the term −b² also has a negative floor. Both examples are uniform and of opposite signs. Not every grouping by two primes is declared favourable, nor are these estimates summed over m to obtain a joint floor.

**Independent review of the jump at the opening r=2H: PROVED for the detector with nonnegative base density.** The density F is continuous at 2H and equals zero there; its first derivative jumps from 0 to (1+a/(2H))/H. Therefore its distributional second derivative contains exactly that positive atom and the ordinary derivative in the open region, without an additional δ' term. For J=exp(−u/2)(φ*φ)≥0, w=J'' and two integrations by parts produce the atom times J(L−2H), with positive sign and without a scale factor: δ(L−u−2H)=δ(u−θ).

At bounded θ=L−2H, r=2H+O(1) in the integrated region and the ordinary F'' is O((1+a/H)/H²). The ordinary part only integrates u<θ; J has fixed support and norm. The PNT error has ceiling Vpoly(H)exp(−c√H); using V=a+2H+O(1) and H≥logz→∞, it is o((1+a/H)/H²) uniformly. This verifies the formula with absolute remainder and gives positivity only on compact sets where J(θ) has a positive floor. No sign is assigned when J(θ)=0.

For m>1 squarefree without factors ≤z, P⁺(m)>z and H=logP⁺(m); hence V=log(mP⁺(m)²)+θ identifies the contact exactly. The opening contributes a term of order (1+a/H)/H, larger by a power of H than the regular curvature. It remains to compare the contacts with the open region when summing over all m. The jump corrects the regime omitted by the compact sets H/L separated from 1/2; it is not a proof of the global floor.

**Local compensation between contacts and adverse groups of equal scale.** For t≤X^(1/5) squarefree without primes ≤z, including 1, put a=log t, L=V−a and H=8L/25. Collect all n=t p₁p₂p₃ with H<log p₁<log p₂<log p₃. They are the three largest primes, since H≥(32/125)V>log t. The balance per t lies between two uniform positive multiples of √X/(tV²); the aggregate balance is ≍√X/(V log z). This region contains groups of two largest primes with negative balance whose aggregate loss is ALSO ≍√X/(V log z).

To sum the three first, fix r=log(p₁p₂p₃), y=r−3H. The continuous density in units √X/t is
F(r)=(a+r)y²/6 ∫_Δ Π_{i=1}³(H+y v_i)^(−1) dv₁dv₂,
