where Δ is the simplex v_i≥0, Σv_i=1. The factor 1/6 uses the symmetry in the three continuous variables. Before the replacement strict order is imposed; the sections are still intervals and PNT gives error O(V poly(V)exp(−c√V)) uniformly. At r=L+O(1) one has y/H=1/8+O(1/V). If D=Π(H+yv_i)^(−1) and S=Σv_i/(H+yv_i)≤1/H, then (y²D)'=yD(2−yS)>0 and (y²D)''≥D(2−4yS)≥D for large V. By direct differentiation there is also a ceiling O(D) for this second derivative. Thus F''(r)≍V/H³≍V^(−2) uniformly. Integrating against J≥0, of positive mass, after the two integrations by parts gives the bounds per t. The harmonic mass of the t was proved in the section on contacts (δ=1/5).

To verify the included loss, restrict 0.321L≤log p₁≤0.325L. At fixed t and p₁ the formula of the two largest applies with cofactor m=t p₁ and ratio log p₁/(L−log p₁) in [0.472,0.482]. The bracket is strictly negative and bounded away from zero, because b>1.8 and log((L−2log p₁)/log p₁)<log 2. Therefore the balance per m is negative of modulus ≍√X/(t p₁ V²). The sum of 1/p₁ over that band of logarithms is ≍1 by Mertens, and summing 1/t gives the declared aggregate loss. The region also contains all contacts of t≤X^(1/5) in a fixed band of θ near the opening, since log p₁=L/3+O(1)>H. This comparison covers a concrete region of the detector; the rest up to the global floor remains without a one-sided estimate.

**Sign change of the complete subtotal when the third possibility opens.** Fix x sufficiently close to 3, on either side, with x≠3. For each previous admissible t, t≤X^(1/5), take H=L/x, L=V−log t. Include ALL composites n=t s of the support with s a squarefree product of primes >exp H, without fixing how many there are. Then the aggregate balance is positive of order √X/(V log z) for x>3 sufficiently close, and negative of the same order for x<3 sufficiently close. In both cases the sign already holds for each individual t. The families for different t are disjoint: every prime of t is ≤X^(1/5) and every prime of s exceeds that threshold, by L≥4V/5 and x close to 3. For t=1 prime s is omitted.

Computation of the curvature at the transition point. Use R=r/H, α=log(t)/H. On the band r=log s=L+O(1), the aggregate continuous density of one and two primes is f(R)=(1+α/R)(1+log(R−1)). If t=1, omitting the constant term 1 does not change the curvature. Above R=3 add also the triple density of the previous simplex. Its right expansion at the opening is (α+R)(R−3)²/12+O((1+α)(R−3)³), with derivatives obtained from the smooth integrand. Four primes do not fit. The lateral curvatures at R=3 are
f''(3−)=−1/4+α[2(1+log 2)/27−1/9−1/12],
f''(3+)=1/4+α[2(1+log 2)/27−1/9−1/12+1/6],
where in the second line f includes the triple sector. The coefficients of α are respectively negative and positive (use 1/2<log 2<1). The branches are smooth up to their lateral limits and affine in α; by continuity there are fixed neighbourhoods with f'' bounded away from zero with the declared sign, uniformly for α in the current bounded range. For fixed x in those neighbourhoods, the whole band R=x+O(1/H) eventually falls on the same side. Two integrations against J then give modulus ≍1/H² in units √X/t and the same sign, including the three possible numbers of factors. The PNT substitution costs V poly(V)exp(−c√V) in those units since even the smallest free prime has logarithm ≍V, with at most three replacements. Finally apply the harmonic mass ≍V/log z. It is a comparison with the loss of the full two-prime sector; the composites outside this partial partition remain.

**Cross-check with 392 and coexistence of signs for every cofactor weight.** The oscillation of Buchstab's ω′ on every tail is already proved in 213-392-A. Repeating its interpolation is not proposed. For the present composite detector a different condition appears: giving the same sign to (Rω(R))″ and to ω″(R), since the full curvature contains both with weight α=log(t)/H≥0. There are open intervals with both strictly positive and others with both strictly negative arbitrarily far out. Therefore the gain observed after x=3 does not propagate to all subsequent cuts, even summing all allowed numbers of free factors and letting nontrivial cofactors in.

Indeed, put g=ω′. By 392 g takes both signs on every tail. In a component of {g>0} after a negative point, between its left endpoint of value zero and any positive point, the mean value theorem gives a point with g′>0 and g>0. In negative components one obtains g′<0 and g<0. Work on R>5 where the delay equation implies ω twice continuously differentiable. By continuity choose non-integer points and short interior compact intervals. Then (Rω)″=2g+Rg′ has the same strict sign as ω″=g′. The modulus of [(R+α)ω(R)]″ has floor c(1+α) on each of those intervals, simultaneously for all α≥0.

Discrete application: for x fixed in the interior of one of those intervals define H=log(X/t)/x and take t≤X^δ with 0<δ<1/(1+x) fixed; t is the product of all the small factors, unique. At r=log s=L+O(1) the PNT replacements hold for up to ⌊x⌋ primes, with constants depending on x. The unweighted density, in R=r/H, is ω(R)=Σ_{j≥1} b^{*j}(R)/j!, b(R)=1_{R≥1}/R. To verify the identification, multiply by R and distinguish one of the j factors: Rω(R)=1+∫₁^{R−1}ω(v)dv for R>2, and Rω(R)=1 on (1,2). With the weight log n the density in dr is (R+α)ω(R), α=log t/H. The diagonals are excluded in the telescoping by strict order as before; if t=1, the omitted prime sector has constant weighted density. Therefore the simultaneous sign transfers to each fibre and the sum has modulus ≍_x √X/(V log z). This use of 392 identifies an obstruction to extrapolating the cut, not a new mechanism for the global floor. There is no uniform estimate when x is made to vary with X.

**Removing the zone with zero or one prime above a second cut without losing a relevant negative contribution.** Let b>1 be fixed with 2e√κ(√b−1)<1, Y=bz, h=log z. Within C_z, the subtotal with at most one prime factor >Y is positive for large V; more precisely it is equivalent to K''(1/2)log(b)√X/V³. The part with zero factors >Y and the incomplete groups with one have sum of absolute values O(exp(−cV/h)). This is a cut by size of the primes covering any multiplicity, different from the previous cut by extreme number of factors.

Indeed, put σ=1/2−1/h. For n≍X the individual absolute cost is ≤CV exp(−V/h)n^(−σ). The finite product over z<p≤bz satisfies log Π(1+p^(−σ))≤Σp^(−σ)=(2e√κ(√b−1)+o(1))V/h by PNT and p^(1/h)=e(1+o(1)) uniformly. The saving persists if a single exceptional factor in (Y,Y exp(B−A)] is also allowed, since the multiplicative cost is at most polynomial in V. This removes the products of the pure band and also the cut fibres q>Y in the representation n=mq, since in them no visible q exceeds Y exp(B−A).

In the other fibres with one q>Y and m>1 a product of primes of (z,Y], the support is complete, or empty. The complete ones have the previous uniform equivalent (√X/m)K'' log m/(V−log m)³. For log m≤√V all are complete and the denominator is uniformly equivalent to V³. The sum of log m/m over all those products without truncation equals Π(1+1/p) Σ log p/(p+1)→log b by PNT. The tail log m>√V has harmonic mass ≪exp(−√V/h)Π(1+p^(−1+1/h))≪exp(−√V/h), and the same computation with log m costs at most a polynomial factor in V (log m≤Σ_{p≤Y}log p=O(V²)). This allows truncating the equivalent and also bounding the remaining complete fibres, where V−log m≥log Y+O(1). Summing gives the claimed principal term. What remains to be compared with that credit is the set with at least two primes >Y; discarding it entirely would change the sign sought.


**Independent review of the aggregate of contacts: PROVED with unique residual cofactor.** For t≤X^δ, δ<1/4, and V−logt−3logP in I, one has P≍(X/t)^(1/3)>t uniformly. Hence P is the largest prime of the cofactor m=tP, does not divide t and the representation of m is unique. Moreover H=logP≍V, a=log(tP)=O(V). The opening remainder is uniformly smaller than its principal term on I with minJ>0; each complete fibre contributes between positive constants times √X/(tPV). The reciprocal sum of P over the band of logarithms of width |I|/3 is ≍1/V uniformly in t.

The harmonic mass of admissible t has ceiling ∏_{z<p≤X^δ}(1+1/p)≍V/logz. For the floor only primes z<p≤X^{δ/4} are chosen; with inclusion probability 1/(p+1), the law of the product is exactly (1/t)/∏(1+1/p). Its logarithmic expectation is ≤δV/4+O(1), so Markov leaves at least half of the mass in t≤X^δ for large V. The normalizer is again ≍V/logz. Multiplying gives R_X≍√X/(Vlogz), with variable multiplicities included and without duplicating products, since the cofactor of the two largest primes is unique. PNT for the total gives C_z=o(R_X), and therefore the complement is −R_X(1+o(1)). Principal scales are evaluated, without a constant remainder or a global floor.

**Independent review of the local three-prime compensation: PROVED with the fixed region.** The cut H=8L/25 exceeds logt when t≤X^(1/5), because H≥32V/125>V/5. Thus the three free primes are exactly the three largest and the residual cofactor t is unique. Changing their logarithms to H+yv_i with y=r−3H gives Jacobian y² over the simplex of area 1/2; the factor 1/6 corresponds to the symmetry of the three orderings and is correct. At r=L+O(1), y/H=1/8+O(1/V).

With D=∏(H+yv_i)^(−1), S=Σv_i/(H+yv_i) and T=Σv_i²/(H+yv_i)², one has D'=-DS and D''=D(S²+T). Hence (y²D)''=D[2−4yS+y²(S²+T)]≥D and (y²D)'>0 on that band, with absolute ceilings of the same order. Differentiating also the factor a+r keeps F''≍VD≍V/H³≍V^(−2), uniform in t. The prime replacement has at least logp≈V; the sections are intervals and strict order allows the same uniform PNT. Integrating against J≥0 gives the positive floors per fibre and the harmonic mass sums them to ≍√X/(Vlogz).

The subband 0.321L≤logp₁≤0.325L lies within the region and leaves H_m/L_m between 0.472 and 0.482 for the group of the two largest primes. The curvature of that group has a negative ceiling bounded away from zero, and a_m/L_m is uniformly bounded. Each m=t p₁ contributes modulus ≍√X/(t p₁V²). Here Σ1/p₁≍1, because the band has logarithmic endpoints proportional to L; it does not cost 1/V. The aggregate loss is also ≍√X/(Vlogz). It includes the contacts with p₁=L/3+O(1)>H. A genuine local compensation between regions of equal scale is shown, without evaluating the global remainder.

**Independent review of the two-sided transition at x=3: PROVED for fixed x close to and different from 3.** The density of one and two primes is (1+α/R)(1+log(R−1)). Its left curvature at 3 is −1/4+α[2(1+log2)/27−1/9−1/12]. When the third opens, the simplex adds (α+R)(R−3)²/12+O((1+α)(R−3)³), and therefore a curvature jump (α+3)/6. Exactly +1/4 and the additional coefficient α/6 of the right branch are obtained. The coefficient of α on the left is negative and on the right positive. One-sided continuity allows fixed neighbourhoods with a floor of the sign, uniform for α in its bounded range. The exact case x=3 is not evaluated here.

For t≤X^(1/5) and x close to 3, every free prime exceeds X^(1/5), while the factors of t do not. Each product therefore belongs to a unique residual fibre t. Four free primes do not fit because R<4; for t=1 the single prime is removed, whose weighted density is the constant 1 and does not alter the curvature. PNT and the two integrations against J transfer both signs to each fibre; summing the harmonic mass gives ≍√X/(Vlogz). Concrete partitions of composites are compared, without exhausting all of them.

**Independent review of the cross-check with 392 and of the cofactor weights: PROVED as a corollary, without new Buchstab oscillation.** 392 already proves that g=ω' takes both signs on every tail. After a negative point, a positive component has a finite left endpoint with g=0; the mean value in its interior provides g>0 and g'>0 at some point. Exchanging signs gives the negative case. On R>5 there is sufficient regularity and continuity allows non-integer compact intervals where both signs have a floor. On them (Rω)''=2g+Rg' shares the sign of ω''=g'; thus [(R+α)ω]'' has modulus ≥c(1+α) simultaneously for all α≥0.

The locally finite sum ω=Σb^{*j}/j! is identified with Buchstab by distinguishing one factor and obtaining Rω=1+∫₁^{R−1}ω. The density in r is ω(r/H)/H; multiplying by logn=a+r gives (R+α)ω(R), without a lost factor H. For fixed non-integer x there are only up to ⌊x⌋ free primes and the PNT replacement keeps constants depending on x. Choosing δ<1/(1+x) ensures H>(δV), separating each factor of t from the free ones and guaranteeing uniqueness. The sign transfers to each cofactor and then to its sum with harmonic mass ≍V/logz. Simultaneity in α is not a uniform bound in x nor over arbitrary signed coefficients of the cofactor. The argument derives a new reading of the previous profile, not a global-floor mechanism nor a valid extrapolation of the sign after x=3 to all cuts.

**Cancellation to constant precision by EXACT small part, without a limit on blocks.** There is κ₀>0 such that for Y≤κ₀V², Y≥2, letting U_m be the balance of the detector (primes included) over the squarefree integers whose product of prime factors ≤Y is exactly m, one has Σ_m |U_m|≪exp(−cV/log V), uniformly in Y. For m>1 they are automatically composites in the support. The previous result for r blocks lost 3^r in the inversion; here even all primes up to Y are admitted as individual blocks and groupings chosen after knowing the balances.

Indeed the series of each exact class is m^(−s)A_Y(s), m a divisor of the primorial up to Y, and the logarithm is obtained by differentiating the whole product. Apply the same audited shift of the Gevrey sieve to each class before summing the moduli. On the whole enlarged strip σ≥1/2−2λ, λ=d/log V, one has Σ_m m^(−σ)=Π_{p≤Y}(1+p^(−σ))≤exp(C√κ₀ V/log V) by the same Chebyshev sum evaluated at the maximum Y=κ₀V². Moreover log m≤Σ_{p≤Y}log p≪Y. Hence the TOTAL cost of the factors m^(−s) and their derivatives in each integral is exp(C√κ₀ V/log V) times a polynomial in V. That cost is added to that of the inverse product in A_Y, also exp(C'√κ₀ V/log V). Choose (C+C')√κ₀<d/2 before shifting. The potential pole at 1 is removed by the double zero of K for each m separately; horizontals and tails are absorbed as before by the Gevrey decay. Thus even the sum of absolute errors over ALL exact classes is paid, although an individual m may be close to X. For m=1 the visible prime is included, whose removal to form C_Y keeps the global problem.

Application to the second cut: reduce κ so that bz≤κ₀V² and keep the condition of the previous section. For m>1 with factors in (z,Y], decompose U_m into zero, one and at least two factors >Y. If E_m is the balance with exactly one and D_m that with at least two, then Σ_{m>1}|D_m+E_m|≪exp(−c'V/log V) over those m, by the exact result and the previous absolute bound for the pure band. In this way the gain of the sector with one large prime is consumed, to precision o(1), even within each small part and without compensating errors between different parts. The balance that decides the floor is transmitted to the group m=1. This identity prevents counting the previous gain as credit available for that group.

**Barrier to iterating the exact cut: classes with a single term.** If Y=κV² with κ>1/(4e²), along a sequence V→∞ the exact classes with a single visible integer contribute Σ_m |U_m|≥exp(cV/log V). Either of the two signs of k can be required for the constructed terms, along possibly different sequences. Therefore the sum-of-moduli bound of the last section cannot be propagated to arbitrary coefficients κ. The limit 1/(4e²) separates, except for equality, the behaviour of the absolute mass of the entirely Y-smooth products in the band. It is not proved that the bound for all exact classes persists up to that value from below.

Upper proof for entirely smooth products. Write h=log Y, σ=1/2−1/h. As before it suffices to multiply CVexp(−V/h) by Π_{p≤Y}(1+p^(−σ)). By PNT and parts, Σ_{p≤Y}p^(−σ)∼2e√κ V/h: on [εY,Y] one uses p^(1/h)→e uniformly and on the rest the Chebyshev majorant is O(√ε V/h) for each fixed ε in the upper limit. Thus there is a saving exp(−cV/h) if 2e√κ<1.

For the floor fix V₀→∞, Y₀=κV₀², h₀=log Y₀. Choose 0<ε<θ<1 with B₀=2√κ(√θ−√ε)>1/e and η=−log B₀<1. On the primes [εY₀,θY₀] take independent subsets with probability ratios e^η/√p between including and excluding. The probability of the product m is e^{ηω(m)}m^(−1/2)/Z. By PNT log Z∼V₀/h₀ and Eω(m)∼V₀/h₀ since Σ1/√p∼B₀V₀/h₀ and Σ1/p=O(1). Moreover Elog m∼V₀ because log p=h₀+O(1). The variances of both quantities are O(V₀/h₀) and O(V₀h₀), respectively. Chebyshev gives with probability 1−o(1) simultaneously ω(m)=(1+o(1))V₀/h₀ and log m=(1+o(1))V₀ (for example take relative tolerances (V₀/h₀)^(−1/4) with respect to the exact means). Split the log m into O(V₀) cells of fixed width smaller than that of an interval where ±k≥c₀>0. One cell gets probability ≫1/V₀; there the sum of m^(−1/2) is ≥exp((1−η+o(1))V₀/h₀) on the indicated event. Shift V so that the cell lies inside that zone of k(V−log m). Since V/V₀→1 and θ<1, all chosen primes are eventually ≤κV². Each m is in the support, is composite, and any other integer of its class is m multiplied by an integer with some prime >κV², already outside the fixed proportional support. This proves the floor. Internal antecedents: packing of 374 and of the multiplicity threshold in this note; here the Bernoulli measure on the primorial detects a barrier of the cut Y itself and the classes become unitary.


**Independent review of the second cut Y=bz: PROVED under 2e√κ(√b−1)<1.** For σ=1/2−1/h, h=logz, the individual weight on the proportional support satisfies ≤CVexp(−V/h)n^(−σ). PNT gives Σ_{z<p≤bz}p^(−σ)=(2e√κ(√b−1)+o(1))V/h, because p^(1/h)=e(1+o(1)) uniformly on that fixed band. The finite Euler product thus leaves a strict saving exp(−cV/h). Allowing an exceptional factor q in (Y,Yexp(B−A)] only adds a sum polynomial in V. This pays in absolute value for the pure band and all fibres incomplete with respect to the cut q>Y, not only with respect to P⁺(m).

For the complete fibres with m>1 formed by primes of (z,Y], the q integral is the same as in the proof by largest prime, because the support does not touch the new lower cut. If logm≤√V, they are complete and (V−logm)^(−3)=V^(−3)(1+o(1)) uniformly. The exact identity Σlogm/m=∏(1+1/p)·Σlogp/(p+1), with primes in that band, tends to logb. The term m=1 has logm=0 and is excluded because it would give the prime edge.

The tail logm>√V has reciprocal mass ≤exp(−√V/h)∏(1+p^(−1+1/h))=O(exp(−√V/h)); the weighting logm only adds O(V²). For remaining complete fibres, V−logm≥logY+O(1) and the previous uniform ceiling costs at most √Xpoly(V)exp(−√V/h). This error is not absolutely o(1), but it is o(√X/V³), which is the precision needed for the equivalent. The incomplete ones were indeed paid absolutely by Rankin. Thus the subtotal zero/one exceptional has positive principal term K''logb√X/V³. That credit is not converted into a floor of the unit balance without accounting for the classes with two or more exceptional factors.

**Independent review of the ℓ¹ cancellation by exact small part: PROVED for Y≤κ₀V² with κ₀ sufficiently small.** The exact class m, a divisor of the primorial up to Y, has series m^(−s)A_Y(s): all small factors are fixed once and the rest is squarefree with primes >Y. The logarithm of the integer is obtained from the full negative derivative. Its Laurent expansion at 1 has only a double pole after differentiating, without a simple pole; K of order two removes it class by class.

On the enlarged strip one can sum the moduli BEFORE integrating, because Σm^(−σ)=∏_{p≤Y}(1+p^(−σ)) is finite and has ceiling exp(C√κ₀V/logV), uniform from Y=2 up to κ₀V². The derivatives of m^(−s) cost logm≤θ(Y)=O(Y), a factor polynomial in V. The cost of the inverses in A_Y is added, of the same exponential order, and choosing (C+C')√κ₀<d/2 leaves the saving on the new vertical. Horizontals and the initial tail are paid with the same total ceiling and the Gevrey decay. It is not needed that each m be small compared with X; its mass on the contour is already included in the Euler sum. Tonelli for these finite majorants justifies summing all classes, not only a budgeted number of blocks.

For m>1 in (z,Y], write exactly U_m=P_m+E_m+D_m, where P_m is the term with zero primes >Y. The previous Rankin bound pays Σ|P_m|=o(1), and the ℓ¹ bound for U gives Σ|D_m+E_m|=o(1), with exponential saving. It is cancellation within each small part and absolute control after that sum, not an individual sign of D_m or of E_m. The gain of the sector with one large prime is consumed there and cannot be credited again to the pattern m=1. The latter contains the visible prime sum; removing it to form composites keeps the global difficulty. The result improves the 3^r budget of the block inversion through the exact weight m^(−s), but does not prove the floor of the empty pattern.

**Critical case of the smooth barrier.** For κ=1/(4e²), Y=κV², h=log Y, let M(V) be the absolute mass of the detector on entirely Y-smooth squarefree integers. Then limsup (h³/V) log(1+M(V))=2. In particular at the endpoint the o(1) control of all exact classes also fails. The lower limsup holds separately when requiring either sign of the kernel.

Detail of the second-order term. For the ceiling use y=κV²; for the floor, when preparing a nominal scale V, use y=κV²(1−(log(κV²))^(−4)). In the following formulas put H=log y, λ=1/H+b/H², T=1/2+λ and Z=Π_{p≤y}(1+p^(−1/2+λ)). Uniformly for b in a compact set,
log Z−λV=(V/H³)(4−2b+b²/2+O(1/H)).
Indeed replacing log(1+s) by s costs O(Σ_{p≤y}1/p)=O(log H) since p^(2λ)=O(1). Quantitative PNT and parts allow replacing the sum by ∫₂ʸ t^(T−1)dt/log t with error o(V/H⁴) (split t≤√y and use the exponential error in √H on the rest). Three integrations by parts give y^T/(TH)[1+1/(TH)+2/(TH)²+O(H^(−3))]. Use 2e√y/V=1+O(H^(−4)) and expand: the bracketed factor combined with 1/(2T) is 1+(4−2b)/H²+O(H^(−3)); there remains also exp(b/H). Take b=2 for the Rankin ceiling M(V)≤O(V)Z exp(−λV) by the fixed support.

For the floor use the product truncated at the slightly smaller y and the independent law with ratios p^(−1/2+λ). The mean of log m is y^T/T+o(V/H²), by the same PNT with a factor log p; the correction of the probabilities against their ratios costs O(H²). In particular mean/V is 1+(b−2)/H+O(H^(−2)). It grows continuously in b; by the intermediate value there is b=2+O(1/H) in [1,3] with mean exactly V. The variance of log m is O(VH) since log p≤H. With probability 1−o(1) one has |log m−V|≤V^(2/3). Split that interval into O(V) cells of fixed width and take one of probability ≫1/V. In it Σ m^(−1/2)≥Z exp(−λV−O(λ V^(2/3)))/O(V). The logarithm of the right side is (2+o(1))V/H³. Shift to V′=V+O(V^(2/3)) so that the kernel has the required sign and modulus bounded below. The relative slack H^(−4) ensures y<κ(V′)². Each selected product forms a visible unitary class at V′ and the factor log m only modifies the logarithm of the mass by O(log V). This matches the ceiling at the fine scale without presupposing a sign between different classes.

**Collective sign of the unitary classes through a smooth local limit.** Fix κ>0, 0≤α<1, Y=κV², h=log Y. Let S be the balance of the detector over squarefree products with ALL their primes in (αY,Y]. It includes the smooth version α=0 and the version with positive lower cut of the composite detector. At every sufficiently large scale,
S ∼ V Z exp(−λV) K(0)/√(2πD) >0.
Here Z=Π(1+p^(−1/2+λ)) over the band, the tilt λ is chosen so that the logarithm of the random product has mean V, and D is its variance. K(0)=(∫v)²=1/4. Unlike the packing that selects a sign of k, ALL signed terms at the original scale are summed.

Proof. Use independent Bernoulli variables with probability π_p=p^(−1/2+λ)/(1+p^(−1/2+λ)), and write S₀=Σ Bern_p log p. For λ=η/h with η fixed, PNT by parts gives E S₀/V→2√κ(1−√α)exp η. The mean is continuous and strictly increasing, so there is a λ with E S₀=V and |λ|h bounded. Then D=Σ π_p(1−π_p)log²p≍Vh, by the ceiling hV and an upper proportional band of primes for the floor. The sum of centered absolute third moments is ≤hD. The exact identity is S=V Z exp(−λV) E G(V−S₀), G(u)=(1−u/V)exp(λu)k(u).

Justification of the local limit at the fixed scale of the detector. The centered characteristic function χ(ξ) has modulus ≤exp(−Σ π_p(1−π_p)(1−cos(ξ log p))). For |ξ|≤1/h this gives exp(−cDξ²). At ξ=t/√D, for fixed t, the expansion of the characteristic functions gives χ→exp(−t²/2), with remainder O_t(h/√D) by the third moments. For 1/h≤|ξ|≤h⁴ choose a band [bY,Y] with α<b<1. There π_p(1−π_p)≫1/√Y. By quantitative PNT and parts, the average of 1−cos(ξ log p) on that band, normalized by Y/h, differs from its integral against dp/log p with the same normalization by O(poly(h)exp(−c√h)), uniformly up to h⁴. This integral is ≥c_b min(1,ξ²): in s=log(p/Y) the normalized density has a positive floor on [log b,0], and the uniform average of 1−cos(ξs+φ) has minimum in φ equal to 1−|sin(ξ log b/2)/(ξ log b/2)|. Hence |χ|≤exp(−cV/h³) on that whole stretch. For |ξ|>h⁴ only |χ|≤1 is used together with the uniform decay of the Fourier transform of G as O(exp(−c√|ξ|)), by the already proved Gevrey property of boxes, also for the factor u by Cauchy on a fixed strip. The integral of this tail is o(1/√D). By Fourier inversion and dominated convergence at the central scale, E G(V−S₀)∼K(0)/√(2πD), since ∫G→∫k=K(0)>0. On the support there are no products of length zero or one for large V. For α=0 and κ=1/(4e²) the previous saddle expansion, now with exact mean and without shifting V, gives log S∼2V/h³ at ALL scales. The balance of the complement still has to be compared with S.

**Uniform positivity by exact large part up to almost the whole product.** Fix 0<α<1, Y=κV², h=log Y and make the lower cut of the sieve αY (with ακ admissible for the criterion). For each squarefree r whose primes exceed Y, including 1, group ALL terms n=rm with the primes of m in (αY,Y]. Let W=V−log r. If h^10≤W≤V, its balance is uniformly positive. Thus the only fibres capable of contributing a loss are those with r>X exp(−h^10). In them log m≤h^10+O(1) on the whole support. Each composite belongs to a unique fibre; for the positive fibres m necessarily has more than one prime.

Details for uniformity when W/V→0. In the product Z of the band choose E S₀=W and put β=1/2+λ. For 0≤β≤1, π_p≍Y^(β−1) uniformly because α is fixed, and E S₀≍Y^β by PNT on the proportional band. At the endpoints β=0,1 the mean is respectively below and above the required range; therefore β=(log W+O(1))/h, D≍Wh and π_p(1−π_p)≍W/Y. The exact balance is V r^(−1/2) Z exp(−λW) E G(W−S₀), with the same G(u)=(1−u/V)exp(λu)k(u). Its integral is K(−λ)+O(1/V), where K(−λ)=β² L_φ(−λ)²≍β², since the base density is positive and −λ lies in a compact set. When W decreases this double zero appears, so a local limit with mere o(1) error in the numerator would be insufficient.

In units 1/√(2πD) the absolute error of approximating the expectation by ∫G is O(h/√D)+o(h^(−2)), uniform. Indeed, for |t|≤√h, ξ=t/√D, the logarithm of the centered characteristic function is −t²/2+O(h|t|³/√D) by expansion of each Bernoulli (|ξ|h=o(1)); the remainder is o(1) on that whole interval. Integrating the difference costs O(h/√D) by the third Gaussian moment, and the Fourier transform of G varies by O(|t|/√D) from its value at zero. For √h<|t|≤√D/h the Gaussian bound leaves O(exp(−c h)); for 1/h≤|ξ|≤h⁴ the sinc proof of the previous band gives exp(−cW/h³), absorbable even after multiplying by h⁴√D since W≥h^10 and D≤Vh. The Gevrey tail is also uniform for bounded λ. Since h/√D≪h^(−9/2) and β≫(log h)/h, the error is o(β²). In particular the equivalent carries the positive factor K(−λ) and holds for all those r simultaneously. It is not concluded that the remaining fibres have a loss nor that it is smaller than the reserve; they include r with m=1, among them primes that must be excluded from the composite detector.


**Independent review of the barrier of unitary classes: PROVED away from the endpoint, with absolute-mass scope.** For κ<1/(4e²), the same Rankin at σ=1/2−1/h gives log∏(1+p^(−σ))≤(2e√κ+o(1))V/h. PNT by parts and a split p≤εY controlled by Chebyshev justify that coefficient, including the sum from the first prime. The factor CV of the detector does not alter the negative rate. It is a bound for entirely smooth products, not an automatic extension of the ℓ¹ theorem to all classes.

If κ>1/(4e²), one can fix 0<ε<θ<1 with B₀=2√κ(√θ−√ε)>1/e and η=−logB₀<1. The Bernoulli ratios e^η/√p produce exactly the law e^{ηω(m)}m^(−1/2)/Z. η need not be positive. With N=V₀/h₀, PNT gives logZ∼N, Eω∼N and Elogm∼V₀, while the variances are O(N),O(V₀h₀). Concentrating around the EXACT means and then using their equivalents gives an event of probability 1−o(1) with ω=N+o(N), logm=V₀+o(V₀).

Packing the logm into O(V₀) cells of fixed width loses only exp(o(N)). In one of them, Σm^(−1/2)=ZΣprob(m)exp(−ηω(m))≥exp((1−η+o(1))N); this also holds if η<0. Shifting V to place that cell in either of the two sign regions of k only changes V/V₀ by o(1). The fixed slack θ<1 ensures that each chosen prime is still ≤κV² after the shift. Since each m is visible and any additional integer of the same exact class contains a prime >κV², the separation of their logarithms eventually exceeds the whole fixed width of the support. The constructed classes are unitary, their products are composites and the contributions do not cancel within a class. Multiplying by logm and the floor of |k| proves the lower bound exp(cV/logV), separately for both signs along subsequences. It is not a conclusion about the signed sum or about all scales.

**Independent review of the critical case: PROVED with limsup 2.** For y=κV² or y=κV²(1−log(κV²)^(−4)), κ=1/(4e²), H=logy and λ=1/H+b/H², the sums of squares of the logarithmic product cost O(logH). PNT and three integrations by parts give, uniformly for bounded b,
logZ=V/H+bV/H²+(4−2b+b²/2)V/H³+O(V/H⁴).
The change of y by the relative slack H^(−4) only alters lower-order terms. Subtracting λV gives the formula; the quadratic minimum in b is 2 at b=2. The polynomial factors of the weight and the support have logarithm O(H), negligible against V/H³, giving the limsup ceiling.

In the tilted law of the floor, Elogm=y^T/T+o(V/H²), with the probability correction O(H²) absorbed. Its uniform expansion is V[1+(b−2)/H+O(H^(−2))]. It is strictly increasing in b because its derivative is the variance divided by H²; the intermediate value allows fixing the mean exactly V with b=2+O(1/H). The variance is ≤H·Elogm=VH. Chebyshev with window V^(2/3) leaves probability 1−o(1), and packing into cells loses only O(logV) in the logarithm. The conversion to reciprocal mass costs λV^(2/3)=o(V/H³). The lower bound (2+o(1))V/H³ is preserved.

The shift to V'=V+O(V^(2/3)) requires comparing with the FINAL cut κ(V')²: the relative slack H^(−4) is much larger than V^(−1/3), so y stays below the cut even under a backward shift. The change of normalization V/H³ to V'/log³(κ(V')²) is 1+o(1). The same unitary classes then give the floors of both signs, with the factor logm only polynomial. This verifies limsup 2 and excludes o(1) in the ℓ¹ mass of classes at the endpoint. This packing argument, by itself, does not determine a limit at all scales nor the signed balance, and does not locate the optimal constant of the ℓ¹ theorem below the critical value.

**Real negative fibres with W of order h² at every scale.** In the same partition by exact large part r, fix ℓ=log(1/α)>0 and j=⌊h/(4ℓ)⌋. For each sufficiently large V there are two distinct primes r, both >Y, whose complete fibres have opposite signs, with W=V−log r=jh+O(h). In particular the universal positivity of W≥h^10 cannot be extended to the whole zone of growing W. It is not claimed that h² is the optimal threshold.

Proof. For products m of exactly j distinct primes of the band, log m lies in [j(h−ℓ),jh]. Adding the support [A,B] of w one obtains an interval I_j of length O(h), separated from the intervals of all other multiplicities by ≫h: it suffices to compare endpoints with j±1 and use jℓ≤h/4. The mass M=Σ_m 1/m is positive, since there are more than j primes in the band. Let c be the mean of log m with these weights. As a real function of W define F(W)=Σ_m (V−u)w(u)/m, u=W−log m. Then ∫F=0 exactly, by the two vanishing moments. Moreover ∫(W−c)²F(W)dW=M(V K''(1/2)−∫u³w(u)du): the mixed term disappears by the choice of c, and the term quadratic in log m−c by ∫F of each translate being zero. The right side is ≫MV. On I_j one has |W−c|≪h, hence ∫|F|≫MV/h². The positive and negative masses are equal and each reaches ≫MV/h². By the length of the support there are points W_± with ±F(W_±)≫MV/h³. The norm of F′ is O(MV); therefore each sign persists on a neighbourhood of radius c₁/h³. That precision does not depend on the mass, which may be small.

Quantitative PNT gives in each corresponding interval of log r=V−W of width ≍h^(−3) a prime r, since V−W∼V and the exponential relative error in √V is o(h^(−3)). In the real fibre, outside multiplicity j all terms vanish by the previous gap, and the balance is exactly (√X/r) F(V−log r). Thus two fibres of opposite signs remain with j→∞ and large part a single prime. The construction does not use a normal approximation nor extrapolate the sign of a fixed multiplicity. It prevents discarding all intermediate fibres one by one; for the global floor their sum is still needed.

**Compensation of the counterexamples in their own band.** Keep I_j,j,h,ℓ,M,F of the preceding section. Let P_j be the sum of the fibres with PRIME large part r with W∈I_j and A_j the sum of their absolute values (modulus after summing within each fibre). Then
P_j ∼ K''(1/2)√X M jh/V³ >0,     A_j ≫ √X M/h².
In particular the positive balance is at most O(h⁴/V³) of the absolute mass. If moreover κ is sufficiently small for the theorem of exact small part up to Y, the fibres with COMPOSITE r in the same I_j have balance −P_j+O(exp(−cV/log V)). Thus the complete band has negligible balance to constant precision although both subtotals grow without bound.

Indeed, by isolation of the multiplicity, summing in the other order runs exactly over the m with j primes of the band and then all primes r of the support of rm. They are complete fibres with log m=jh+O(jℓ)∼jh and V−log m∼V. The uniform equivalent by largest prime gives the formula for P_j. For the modulus, A_j=√X Σ_{r prime}|F(V−log r)|/r. By PNT and parts this normalized sum differs from ∫_{I_j}|F(W)|dW/(V−W) by O(M poly(V)exp(−c√V)): the absolute value is Lipschitz and its variation on I_j is O(hMV). Use ∫|F|≫MV/h² and V−W∼V. The inequality of both subtotals grows at absolute scale: there are N≍Y/h primes in the band and M≥binom(N,j)Y^(−j)≥(N/(jY))^j≥exp(−O(h log h)), so P_j→∞.

Finally with admissible Y, for each m of that multiplicity apply the ℓ¹ estimate of U_m to all r with P⁻(r)>Y: log m=O(h²) excludes r=1 on the support, and W∈I_j is automatic. The classes by exact small part use only primes of (αY,Y], so the visible composites belong to the detector with cut αY. The union coincides with the whole band of W within the same detector. Subtracting P_j proves the balance for composite r. The positive contribution from prime r and its compensation by composite r are computed on the same set where individual fibres of both signs had appeared; no global reserve remains available in that band.

**Overlapping bands: edge formula with o(1) error, without isolating multiplicities.** Fix 0<α<1, Y=κV² with κ sufficiently small, and a fixed Gevrey transition χ, from 0 to 1 on [0,1], constant on both tails (for example the integral of a rescaled Gevrey box density). In the previous partition n=mr, with m formed by primes of (αY,Y] and P⁻(r)>Y, select with weight χ(W−s), W=V−log r. If s>B, visible primes never enter. Uniformly in s>B, the full balance of this cut is
β_Y √X Σ_m m^(−1) ∫ (V−u) w(u) χ(log m+u−s) du + O(exp(−cV/log V)),
with β_Y=ζ(2)^(−1)Π_{p≤Y}(1+1/p)^(−1).
In the principal sum only log m∈[s−B,s+1−A] are kept. This also gives the difference between two cuts to constant precision, even with overlapping numbers of factors. The weight of the cut is smooth; the formula does not replace that weight at no cost by a discontinuous indicator.

Proof. In the exact class m the new kernel is k_m(u)=k(u)χ(log m+u−s). Its support remains in [A,B] and its Gevrey bounds are uniform by Leibniz and invariance of the bounds of χ under translation. Repeat the contour of the class m with this kernel. Now the transform need not cancel the double pole at 1. The series m^(−v)A_Y(v) has residue β_Y/m; its negative derivative has polar part β_Y/[m(v−1)²], without a simple pole. Differentiating the other factor exp((v−1/2)V)∫exp(−(v−1/2)u)k_m(u)du at v=1 gives exactly the indicated integral multiplied by √X. The sum of moduli of ALL the remainders of the classes is still O(exp(−cV/log V)) by the audited argument of the exact small part: the only alteration is a transform with uniform support and decay. If χ is constant on log m+[A,B]−s, the moments of w cancel the integral. Finally a visible prime has m=1 and W=u≤B, so it does not contribute. The sum can be restricted to any subset of m with the same total absolute error.

Consequence for the global comparison: in a smooth cut chosen within W≥h^10 all fibres are positive by the uniform lemma; the formula locates their amount, to precision o(1), in the harmonic distribution of m near the transition. On summing complementary cuts their residues cancel exactly for each m, by the two moments. This explains why adding more bands of this type does not by itself generate a constant reserve in the sector m=1. The floor still depends on the prime detector of that sector.


**Independent review of the collective smooth local limit: PROVED at all scales for fixed parameters.** The Bernoulli tilt is chosen by the EXACT mean V. PNT gives E S₀/V→2√κ(1−√α)expη for λ=η/h, so the solution has |λ|h bounded; D≍Vh and the aggregate absolute third moment is ≤hD. The identity of the signed sum is exactly VZexp(−λV)E G(V−S₀), G(u)=(1−u/V)exp(λu)k(u). There is no additional factor √X: it is already incorporated in the tilted mass Z.

For |ξ|≤1/h, the Bernoulli inequality gives |χ(ξ)|≤exp(−cDξ²), and the centered expansion at ξ=t/√D converges to exp(−t²/2). For 1/h≤|ξ|≤h⁴, a proportional subband [bY,Y] has weight π_p(1−π_p)≥c/√Y. The PNT replacement of the phase average costs poly(h)exp(−c√h), smaller than h^(−2). The uniform average over a fixed logarithmic interval has minimum in the phase equal to 1−|sinc|≥c min(1,ξ²). This provides the bound exp(−cV/h³) uniformly up to h⁴, even near resonances of the terminal phase. Independence of prime phases is not presupposed; the independence is that of the Bernoulli variables of the finite product.

For |ξ|>h⁴, the Fourier transform of G has uniform ceiling Cexp(−c√|ξ|), by the fixed Gevrey-2 profile and bounded λ. The tail, even multiplied by √D≤C√(Vh), is o(1) because h≈2logV and exp(−ch²) dominates exp(h/4). Inversion and dominated convergence in the central zone give E G∼K(0)/√(2πD), with K(0)=1/4. All external factors are positive. For α=0 at κ=1/(4e²), the saddle expansion with exact mean gives logS∼2V/h³ at ALL scales; the normalization factors only add O(h). Together with the previous absolute ceiling, it even follows that the smooth absolute mass has normalized limit 2, improving the limsup obtained by packing. The signed complement is not controlled nor is a global floor obtained.

**Independent review of the fibres by large part with W≥h¹⁰: PROVED uniformly and with control of the moving zero.** On the band αY<p≤Y, 0<α<1 fixed, the mean W of S₀ requires β=1/2+λ=(logW+O(1))/h, D≍Wh and π_p(1−π_p)≍W/Y. The endpoints β=0,1 enclose h¹⁰≤W≤V uniformly. The fibre identity is V r^(−1/2)Zexp(−λW)E G(W−S₀), with the same factor 1−u/V, because log(rm)=V−u.

The integral of G is K(−λ)+K'(−λ)/V. For the detector with positive base density, K(−λ)=β²L_φ(−λ)²≍β² and β≥c logh/h. The 1/V correction is negligible against β². In the central zone |t|≤√h, the remainder of the logarithm of χ is O(h|t|³/√D), uniformly o(1); integrating against the Gaussian majorant costs O(h/√D). The variation of the Fourier transform of G contributes only O(1/√D). The central tail from √h costs exp(−ch). The zone 1/h≤|ξ|≤h⁴ has ceiling exp(−cW/h³), and W≥h¹⁰ beats even the length h⁴ and √D≤C√(Vh). The uniform Gevrey tail is also o(h^(−2)) after normalizing.

Thus the normalized error is O(h/√D)+o(h^(−2)), smaller than β²; in particular h/√D≤Ch^(−9/2). This proves positivity for ALL those fibres simultaneously, not just a local limit with o(1) error, insufficient when approaching the double zero. The visible small part m contains several primes because logm≥h¹⁰−O(1)>h. The exact separation between primes ≤Y and >Y guarantees uniqueness of the fibre. The result assigns no sign to the remaining fibres, especially to those containing the prime edge m=1.

**Independent review of the counterexample W≈h²: PROVED at each large scale.** For j=floor(h/(4log(1/α))), the possible logm with exactly j primes lie in [j(h−ℓ),jh]. After adding [A,B], the interval I_j has length O(h), and its distance to neighbouring multiplicities is ≥3h/4−O(1); this isolates it from ALL the others, not only from j±1. With M=Σ1/m and c its mean of logm, the exact computation gives ∫F=0 and ∫(W−c)²F=M(VK''−∫u³w). The mixed term −2K''Σ(logm−c)/m vanishes by the choice of c.

One has |W−c|≤Ch on I_j and ∥F'∥∞≤CMV. The second moment implies ∫|F|≥cMV/h²; the positive and negative masses are equal and both have that lower order. By length, each sign reaches cMV/h³ and persists on an interval of radius c/h³, independently of the size of M. Uniform PNT in log r=V−O(h²) produces a prime in each interval; they can be chosen disjoint by the sign. Since r≫Y and the multiplicity j is isolated, the REAL fibre is exactly (√X/r)F(V−logr) and receives no terms of other orders. Opposite signs are obtained with W=jh+O(h) at every scale, without a normal approximation or a fixed-order argument. The optimal threshold of universal positivity is not located.

**Independent review of the compensation in the band I_j: PROVED, with explicit difference of norms.** On summing first over m, all primes r of its support land automatically in W∈I_j and form a complete fibre by largest prime. The uniform equivalent gives P_j∼K''√X Mjh/V³, because logm=jh+O(jℓ)∼jh. In the other order, A_j=√XΣ_{r prime}|F(V−logr)|/r. The variation of |F| over I_j is ≤ChMV; PNT pays an error Mpoly(V)exp(−c√V), smaller than M/h². The continuous integral is ≥cM/h², whence A_j≥c√XM/h² and P_j/A_j=O(h⁴/V³).

There are N≍Y/h candidate primes and M≥binom(N,j)Y^(−j)≥exp(−O(hlogh)); thus P_j and A_j diverge at absolute scale. If Y is admissible for ℓ¹ by small part, summing the classes U_m of those m gives absolute error exp(−cV/logV). The isolation of I_j ensures that their union is that whole band of the detector with cut αY; r=1 is impossible because logm=O(h²)≪V. Subtracting the prime-r subtotal produces composite balance −P_j with that same absolute error. This leaves no global positive credit in the band, although each subtotal is large and individual fibres of both signs exist.


**Independent review of the edge formula for smooth cuts: PROVED uniformly in s>B.** In n=mr, W=V−logr=logm+u, so the exact kernel of the class m is k_m(u)=k(u)χ(logm+u−s). Its support remains fixed in [A,B]. The derivatives of χ are globally uniform under translation and Leibniz keeps a common Gevrey norm for the whole family m,s; its transform also has uniform decay on the contour strip. Thus the ℓ¹ proof for exact classes admits those kernels before summing the moduli of the remainders. Choosing m or a subset of classes after observing the balances does not increase that total error.

The Laurent expansion of m^(−v)A_Y(v) has residue β_Y/m; on differentiating negatively β_Y/[m(v−1)²] remains, WITHOUT a simple pole. The weighted residue is obtained by differentiating exp((v−1/2)V)K_m(v−1/2) and is exactly β_Y√X/m∫(V−u)w(u)χ(logm+u−s)du. Neither the factor 1/m nor the term −u is lost. The kernel now has no vanishing polar moment, which is why it is necessary to retain that residue before applying the same contour saving.

If logm≤s−B, the transition is zero on the whole support; if logm≥s+1−A, it is one and the integral is V∫w−∫uw=0. Only the indicated bounded band of logm remains, including its zero-weight endpoints. A visible prime has m=1 and W=u≤B<s, so the initial cut contains no primes. For differences of two cuts the two uniform remainders and the residues of their edges are summed; separating the multiplicities is not required, nor is χ replaced at no cost by an indicator.

For complementary cuts, χ+(1−χ)=1 and the residues sum to exactly zero FOR EACH m by the two moments. The complement does include the edge m=1 and the visible primes, so a formulation over composites must subtract the genuine prime sum. If the cut is chosen within W≥h¹⁰, its positivity comes from the uniform theorem by large part and from 0≤χ≤1, because the weight is constant within each fibre r. The formula locates its amount at an edge of the harmonic distribution of m, but does not create a free reserve for the pattern m=1. The prime difficulty and the global floor persist; there is no conclusion for sharp cuts or transitions without common Gevrey bounds.

**One-sided sampling of the prime detector with only polynomially many scales per logarithmic block.** For H=2^j it suffices to check B_exp(V)(v)≤−1/16 at all V∈[H,2H]∩H^(−3)ℤ, along an unbounded sequence of complete blocks, to deduce the global sign. Under RH it holds in all sufficiently late blocks. The fixed Gevrey detector with square bias and decay exp(−c√|γ|) is used; the continuous lemma of 115 by itself does not allow rounding an excursion point to this mesh. The new step is to discretize the positive average that proves the lemma. The arithmetic inequality has not been verified along an unbounded sequence.

Proof. For the real series J(V) of zeros of 195, the grouped coefficients a_z have Σ_{|γ|>R}|a_z|≪exp(−c'√R) by the decay of boxes and the unit count; |Re z|≤1/2. B_exp(V) differs from that series with its agreed sign by O(1) for large V. Use the Gaussian average of 115 centred at T=3H/2, variance cT, with fixed modulations τ. Replace the integral by the sum over the infinite mesh of step Δ=H^(−3), multiplied by Δ. For each |γ|≤π/(2Δ), Poisson applied to the exponential Gaussian gives in the error only the frequencies γ−τ+2πk/Δ, k≠0. Their summed moduli are ≪exp(T(1/2+c/8))exp(−c₁T/Δ²) for large H, uniformly in those γ. For |γ|>π/(2Δ), both the discrete and the continuous Gaussian average |exp(zV)| with cost O(exp(T(1/2+c/8))) by completing the square; the discrete mass of any shifted normalized Gaussian is uniformly bounded. By the coefficient tail, the total error is O(exp(−c₂H^(3/2))) for each fixed τ. This avoids an estimate through the pointwise derivative of J.

If there is a right zero, apply the strict rate gap of 115 with d>0 smaller than the spectral Δ and c small so that the tails outside [H,2H] cost O(exp(−T)); on the mesh the same bound is obtained by completing the square and summing Gaussian tails. The discrete averages with nonnegative weights 1±cos preserve both signs and exponential modulus. Their masses are bounded. Points of both signs, exponentially large, remain on the mesh of EACH late block, also for B after incorporating the O(1) error. There are O(H⁴) samples per block. It is a one-sided sampling criterion for the raw prime discrepancy, without unconditional arithmetic bound at the points and without claiming detection with fixed step.

**Duration of both excursions; samples at free position.** If RH fails, there exist c,d>0 such that in each late block H≤V≤2H the fixed prime detector B_exp(V) exceeds exp(dH) on a whole interval of length c/H² and falls below −exp(dH) on another interval of that length. Thus, along an unbounded sequence of blocks it would suffice to find a favourable point at free position in each cell of length H^(−2)/log H (with trimming at the endpoints). O(H³ log H) cells are used. The width is in V=log X. The argument by averages on a fixed mesh does not prove persistence between its nodes.

Proof. Put g(V)=J(V) multiplied by the normalized Gaussian density of 115, of mean T=3H/2 and variance c₀T, where J is the real series of the detector. By the spectral separation of 115 there exist fixed τ and a>0 such that ||g||₁≥|I_τ|≥exp(aH) and |∫g|=o(||g||₁). Outside the block the mass of |g| is O(exp(−cH)) by the choice of c₀. Hence both the positive and negative parts have mass (1/2+o(1))||g||₁ inside the block.

Moreover ||g′||₁≤C H²||g||₁. Detail: cut its Fourier transform smoothly by a multiplier equal to one on [−2R,2R] and zero outside [−3R,3R], R=C₁H². The derivative of the retained part costs O(R)||g||₁ by the L¹ norm of the rescaled differentiated kernel. In the series of g the ordinates |γ|>R cost exp(−2H) in W^(1,1) before and after the cut: the norm of each exponential Gaussian and of its derivative is bounded by poly(H)(1+|γ|)exp(O(H)) and the coefficient tail by exp(−c√R), taking C₁ large. For |γ|≤R, the Fourier transform of each term is a Gaussian of width O(H^(−1/2)) centred at γ, with amplitude ≤exp(O(H)). Outside [−2R,2R] the L² norm of the Fourier transform of the differentiated remainder and of its first frequency derivative is O(exp(−cHR²)) per term without coefficient, absorbing polynomial factors. This bounds its physical L¹ norm by Plancherel and Cauchy–Schwarz with weight (1+V²)^(−1); summing the coefficients absolutely concludes.

With 0<d<a/3, the mass inside the block of (±g−2exp(dH))_+ still exceeds ||g||₁/3. If all components of that superlevel set inside the block had length <l, its integral would be ≤l||g′||₁: in each component start from an endpoint where the level is attained, also for components touching an endpoint of the block. If the whole block were one component the length would already be proved. Therefore each sign has an interval of length ≥c/H²; by reducing c both endpoints can be included. The Gaussian density is smaller than one, and passing from J to B only adds a bounded term and a possible global sign. Thus |B|>exp(dH) persists on each corresponding interval. A complete cell of the indicated mesh fits inside for large H. The result does not supply the arithmetic favourable point in each cell.

**Threshold of the positive Gaussian average of the prime detector itself.** For fixed 0<c<1 let M_c(V) be the average of B_exp(t)(v) over t normal with mean V and variance cV. Define c_* as the supremum of 2b/(γ²−b²) over right zeros z=b+iγ of the centred variable, and zero for the empty set. Then for c>c_* one has M_c(V)→−1/8. For 0<c<c_* there are exponential excursions of both signs. Unconditionally c_*≤1/(G²−1/4) with G=3·10¹² by Z2. This proves a favourable arithmetic average, for example with c=2/G², at all large scales. The threshold is zero exactly under RH; the equality c=c_* is not used.

Justification. The explicit series of this detector, with bias −1/8+o(1) as t→∞, can be averaged term by term. On t≥V/2 the o(1) error is uniform; on 0≤t≤V/2 the difference between detector and series is bounded by local continuity and the asymptotic formula. On t<0 the detector is bounded (eventually empty), and the extended series is majorized by C exp(−t/2). The normal integral of this majorant over t<0 is o(1) by completing the square, since c<1. One gets M_c(V)=−1/8+Σ a_z exp((z+cz²/2)V)+o(1), with the spectral sign incorporated in a_z. The real part of each exponent is b+c(b²−γ²)/2. Since |γ| is bounded away from zero and exceeds |b| for all zeros, the non-right zeros decay, and the rates tend uniformly to −∞ as |γ| grows. For c>c_* the maximum of the rates is strictly negative. For c<c_* the maximum f is positive, attained by a finite set separated in rate from the rest. Its frequencies γ(1+cb) are nonzero and distinct after grouping equal zeros: equality of exponents would give (z−z′)(1+c(z+z′)/2)=0, and the second factor cannot vanish. Dividing by exp(fV) leaves a nonzero real trigonometric polynomial of mean zero plus o(1). Its positive mean square and finite sup norm force values of both signs bounded away from zero on every sufficiently long interval (the first and second means converge uniformly in the translation). This proves the excursions. The Gaussian suppression of 115 is the antecedent; here the exact frontier of variances is identified for the unmodulated arithmetic observable. The average has infinite support: its sign does not guarantee a favourable point in a cell of length H^(−2)/log H.


**Independent review of the one-sided sampling H^(−3): PROVED with fixed Gevrey detector.** Poisson applied to each exponential Gaussian introduces only the frequencies γ−τ+2πk/Δ, k≠0. For |γ|≤π/(2Δ), fixed τ and Δ=H^(−3), those frequencies are separated from the origin by c/Δ; their contributions have ceiling exp(T(1/2+c/8))exp(−c₁T/Δ²). The sum of coefficients is finite. For the other ordinates, completing the square gives the same ceiling exp(T(1/2+c/8)) both in the integral and in the discrete sum: the mass of a normalized Gaussian sampled with step Δ≪√T is uniformly bounded under any shift. The Gevrey tail from R≈H³ costs exp(−c√R), so the total error is O(exp(−c₂H^(3/2))). These majorants also justify all the absolute interchanges.

The tails outside [H,2H] of the frozen series are removed by the same Gaussian bound, in integral and in sum. The weights 1±cos remain nonnegative at the nodes and have bounded mass. The gap of 115 and the selected frequency are fixed, so the alias error does not alter the two exponential signs. The arithmetic O(1) terms are incorporated only after obtaining nodes inside the block. Outside RH each late block has a positive node incompatible with the ceiling −1/16; an unbounded sequence of completely favourable blocks therefore forces RH. Under RH the ceiling holds at all late points. The count is O(H⁴), including the endpoints of the mesh.

**Independent review of the duration and free samples: PROVED for the indicated widths.** With g equal to the real series times the Gaussian density, 115 gives ||g||₁≥|I_τ|≥exp(aH) and |∫g|/||g||₁→0. The exterior absolute mass is exponentially small, so each sign has mass (1/2+o(1))||g||₁ inside the block. For the derivative, a smooth Fourier cut at R=C₁H² has differentiated kernel of L¹ norm ≤CR; applied to g it costs CR||g||₁. The high spectral tail and its derivative cost exp(−2H) when choosing C₁ large, even after the cut. The low modes have Gaussian Fourier transform centred at γ, with width H^(−1/2); the remainder outside 2R costs exp(−cHR²) in L² and in its first frequency derivative. Plancherel and Cauchy–Schwarz with weight (1+V²)^(−1) convert it into an L¹ error, without losing an uncontrolled sup norm. One obtains ||g'||₁≤CH²||g||₁.

Subtracting the level 2exp(dH), d<a/3, loses at most 2Hexp(dH)=o(||g||₁). If all components of a superlevel set have length <l, its excess integral is ≤l||g'||₁: each interior component has an endpoint at the level, and those touching an edge have the other one; if it touches both, the length of the block already solves the problem. This forces a component of each sign of length ≥c/H². Trimming a margin keeps closed intervals and the smaller threshold exp(dH). The Gaussian density is positive and smaller than one for large H, and B differs from the series by O(1) and an agreed sign, so both excursions of the detector persist.

Each interval contains a complete cell of size H^(−2)/logH for large H. Requiring a favourable point at free position in EACH cell along an unbounded sequence of blocks thus suffices for RH, with O(H³logH) cells; one arbitrary point per block does not suffice. Detection at fixed step is not proved nor is an arithmetic estimate of those points provided.

**Cross-check of the sampling.** 115 is the exact antecedent of the continuous average and its positive weights; Gaussian Poisson and L¹ Bernstein are classical tools. 241/242 already control aliasing and discrete samples of another observable, through differences and filters; 073/076 use meshes of powers in the physical variable, much finer in logarithm. R167_102 Prop1 records a width floor by Bernstein for a different positive spectral weight. In the targeted cross-check no literal duplicate of this fixed prime detector, polynomial sampling by blocks and simultaneous duration of both excursions was found. A reduction of the set to be controlled is recorded, not a new sign mechanism nor an arithmetic bound of the sampling.

**Precision of the arithmetic second moment at the Gaussian threshold.** Let s²=cV, t=V+s²/2, g_s the centred normal density of variance s², J(u)=exp(−u/2)(φ*φ)(u)≥0. Form the positive measure on (p,u) with weights (log p)/p · J(u)g_s(t−log p−u)du; call Z its mass and E its normalized expectation. Then, with Q=log p+u,
s²−E[(Q−t)²]=−s⁴ exp(−V/2−s²/8) M_c(V)/Z.
It is a second moment with respect to the prescribed centre t, not a variance with respect to the empirical mean. In particular for c>c_* one obtains the positive equivalent s⁴ exp(−V/2−s²/8)/(8∫J), and for 0<c<c_* the defect changes sign along unbounded sequences. Thus requiring only the ceiling E[(Q−t)²]≤s² for all sufficiently large V, along a sequence of fixed c decreasing to zero, would suffice for the global sign.

Derivation. In the integral defining M_c replace k(u) by exp(u/2)J''(u), and use p^(−1/2)=p^(−1)exp(log p/2). Completing the square in log p+u turns the exponential factor and the initial Gaussian into exp(V/2+s²/8)g_s(t−log p−u). Two integrations by parts change J'' into J and give the exact identity via g_s''(v)=(v²/s⁴−1/s²)g_s(v). The absolute sums converge by the Gaussian against the trivial count. Moreover Z→∫J>0: the cumulative sum of Σ(log p)/p up to log p≤v is v+O(1) for v≥0 by Mertens. By parts the replacement by dv on the half-line costs O(∫|g_s′|)=O(1/s) uniformly in the translation by u; the integral of the Gaussian over the half-line tends to one since t/s→∞. The equivalent follows from the limit of the average audited or derived above. Even in the already resolved regime the deficit relative to the second moment s² is only of order s² exp(−V/2−s²/8). Convergence of the prime profile to a Gaussian with polynomial error does not determine this sign. The horizontal-covariance antecedent G1_B10_R3 ensures positivity of variances; here a ceiling with prescribed centre is required, and the identity does not by itself provide a mechanism to prove it.

**The variance ceiling with respect to the real mean has the same threshold.** With Z(t,s), Q and s²=cV of the previous section, also s²−Var(Q) is eventually positive and equivalent to s⁴exp(−V/2−s²/8)/(8∫J) when c>c_*. For 0<c<c_* it takes both signs along unbounded sequences. Therefore it suffices to prove log-concavity of the positive density t↦Z(t,s), with respect to t at fixed s, at t=V+s²/2 for all late V and a sequence c↓0. The exact position of the arithmetic mean is not required. The log-concave condition is an obligation on this particular density of primes; it is not inferred from the positivity of the Gaussian kernel.

Indeed E(Q−t)=s² Z_t/Z and Var(Q)−s²=s⁴(∂²_t log Z). The term distinguishing the two defects is (s² Z_t/Z)². To bound it with the necessary precision, use a second test k₁(u)=exp(u/2)J′(u). Its transform in the centred variable w is (w−1/2)L_{φ*φ}(w), so it cancels the pole and has the same Gevrey decay on strips. The Gaussian average M_{c,1} of its raw prime sum satisfies exactly M_{c,1}=exp((1/2+c/8)V) Z_t: one integration by parts in u produces g_s′(t−Q). The same explicit formula as in 195 applies to this smooth kernel: the polar residue is zero, the zeros contribute their coefficients with the same exponent z+cz²/2, the squares contribute O(1) by PNT on a proportional band and the higher powers o(1). The error in extending the series to average over negative t is controlled as in the threshold section. Hence |M_{c,1}|≪_c exp(fV), with f=max(0,max_z Re(z+cz²/2)). For fixed c>0 one has f<d₀=1/2+c/8, by |Re z|≤1/2 and the strictly negative term −cγ²/2 (the maximum is attained). Therefore, in units s⁴exp(−d₀V)/Z, the correction of the mean is O(exp((2f−d₀)V)), since Z→∫J>0. For c>c_* f=0 and the correction tends to zero in those units. For c<c_* f>0, and along the two sequences of excursions of the principal trigonometric polynomial |M_c|≥ε exp(fV); there the correction is relatively o(1). This proves both statements. The criterion only uses spatial derivatives at frozen variance; differentiating along the curve s²=cV would introduce different terms.

**The bias decides the equality at c_*; logarithmic resolution below.** For the explicit Gevrey box profile of this note, if c_*>0, the average of variance c_*V stays eventually <−1/16, although it does not converge to −1/8. On the other hand the average of variance c_*V−log V has unbounded excursions of both signs. Thus a fixed coefficient c gives the eventual ceiling ≤−1/16 exactly for c≥c_* within 0<c<1. In the case c_*=0, RH and the ceiling for the detector itself had already been proved equivalent.

At the positive threshold the maximum of the ratio defining c_* is attained because it tends to zero in height. The zeros of zero rate form a finite nonempty set, all right zeros with |γ|>G. The rest of the rates have strictly negative maximum. If z=b+iγ is a right zero, the box of length 2 has transform of modulus ≤1/|γ| and the transform of the probabilistic smoother supported on [0,∞) has modulus ≤1. Therefore the per-zero coefficient of the detector series, in modulus, is ≤2|γ|^(−6) for |γ|≥G. By the unit count of 175, summing both signs and multiplicities, its mass above G is ≤400 Σ_{j≥⌊G⌋−1}log(4+j)/j⁶<1/64 (for example log(4+j)≤j and integral comparison). The average is −1/8 plus a real trigonometric polynomial of modulus <1/64 and o(1). This polynomial is not constant by the already proved injectivity of the exponent and the non-vanishing of the coefficient of any right zero; its mean square is positive, which excludes convergence to −1/8.

With variance c_*V−log V the same Gaussians multiply each critical term by V^{(γ²−b²)/2}exp(−ibγ log V). The non-critical terms remain O(exp(−εV)) together for large V: at bounded height the fixed gap is preserved, and for large |γ| the rate for c=c_*−log V/V is uniformly dominated by −c_*γ²/8. In the critical set maximizing γ²−b² selects a unique conjugate pair after grouping multiplicities, because b=c_*(γ²−b²)/2 fixes b and then |γ|. The principal term is a nonzero amplitude times V^{(γ²−b²)/2} times a cosine of phase γ(1+c_*b)V−bγ log V+fixed phase. Its derivative tends to a nonzero constant, so there are sequences of maxima and minima; the other critical powers are strictly smaller. The bias and the o(1) error are preserved by the same extension of the average to t<0. This delimits how much the favourable sign exactly at the frontier tells; it provides no additional arithmetic bound on the value of c_*.

**Comparison without auxiliary kernel; the endpoint changes sign.** For fixed 0<c<1, s²=cV, let Q_c(V)=Σ_p(log p)/√p · g_s(V−log p) with g_s a normalized Gaussian. Let D_c(V)=Q_c(V)−exp(V/2+s²/8), subtracting exactly the integral over the line of exp(t/2)g_s(V−t). For c>c_* one has D_c→−1/2; for c<c_* there are exponential excursions of both signs. If c=c_*>0 then limsup D_c≥1/2 and liminf D_c≤−3/2. The eventual ceiling Q_c≤exp(V/2+cV/8) characterizes the strictly open interval c>c_* within (0,1). Here all prime weights are positive and neither derivatives nor the profile φ intervene. Unlike the detector with boxes, equality is excluded from the favourable side.

Indeed for all prime powers the inversion in w of −ζ′/ζ(1/2+w) multiplied by exp(Vw+s²w²/2) is exact on Re w=1 by the transform of the Gaussian and absolute convergence. Shift to Re w=−1. The pole of ζ gives exp(V/2+s²/8), the nontrivial zeros give −Σ_z exp((z+cz²/2)V) with multiplicities and no trivial zero is crossed. On the new vertical the logarithmic derivative has at most polynomial growth by the functional equation, so the error is O(exp(−V+s²/2)) for s≥1. The horizontals are removed at good heights before taking V large; the Gaussian factor ensures convergence. The contribution of squares is Σ_p (log p)/p g_s(V−2log p)=1/2+o(1) by Mertens and parts: the error is O(1/s), and ∫₀^∞g_s(V−2t)dt→1/2. The powers k≥3 cost O(1/s) by Σ_{p,k≥3}(log p)p^(−k/2)<∞.

The rates are the same as at the threshold, although the coefficients no longer decay in height. For fixed positive c the Gaussian dominates the tail by the unit count of zeros, uniformly for V≥1 once finitely many low frequencies are removed. The arguments of finite maximum and gap then apply. At equality, D_c=−1/2+P(V)+o(1), where P is a real trigonometric polynomial of mean zero and some coefficient has modulus ≥1 (an integer multiplicity, unattenuated). For any nonzero frequency present, the modulus of that coefficient is bounded by the mean of M−P for M=sup P, since M−P≥0. Thus M≥1; likewise inf P≤−1. The same upper and lower limits hold on every tail by the argument of means applied on that tail. The two announced inequalities are obtained. This comparison gives an explicit arithmetic target; proving the ceiling for arbitrarily small c with inputs independent of the exterior spectrum remains pending.


**Independent review of the arithmetic Gaussian threshold: PROVED for each fixed 0<c<1.** The error between the detector and its series with bias is bounded on the whole positive half-line and tends to zero at infinity. Its average converges to zero by separating t≥V/2 from the rest. On t<0, the majorant Cexp(−t/2) integrated against N(V,cV) is exponentially small on completing the square. The absolute sum of coefficients and E|exp(zt)|≤exp(V/2+cV/8) justify the interchange first; the Gaussian formula then preserves the decay in height. The positive maximum of the ratio defining c_* is attained if there is some right zero; Z2 gives c_*≤1/(G²−1/4). Above the threshold all rates are strictly negative, with maximum attained and negative. Below, the maximal set is finite, nonempty and separated in rate. On it the injectivity of z↦z+cz²/2 is verified because Re(1+c(z+z′)/2)≥1−c/2>0; the frequencies are nonzero. The Gram matrix on sufficiently long intervals and the zero mean of the real polynomial give both signs with margin uniform in the translation. The favourable average at c=2/G² is therefore unconditional, but it does not locate a favourable point in a short cell. The rate map is exactly the parabolic one of 364/365, plus the average of 115; the specialization to the fixed detector and to the bias −1/8 is not a new spectral mechanism.

**Independent review of the positive second moment and of the real mean: PROVED with exponential precision.** Completing the square produces exactly exp(V/2+s²/8)g_s(t−Q), t=V+s²/2. Two integrations by parts give M_c=exp(V/2+s²/8)Z(E[(Q−t)²]/s⁴−1/s²), with the sign and all the indicated powers of s. Mertens for Σ(log p)/p and variation of the Gaussian give Z=∫J+O(1/s)+o(1). Thus the defect with respect to the prescribed centre has the announced equivalent; its size relative to s² is s²exp(−V/2−s²/8)/(8∫J), not a polynomial error of the normal limit.

For the empirical mean, the single integration by parts gives M_{c,1}=exp(d₀V)Z_t, d₀=1/2+c/8; the transform of k₁ has the simple polar factor w−1/2. The explicit formula keeps the same exponents and bounded square bias. If f=max(0,max Re(z+cz²/2)), then f<d₀ and |M_{c,1}|≤C_c exp(fV). The correction (E(Q−t))², divided by s⁴exp(−d₀V)/Z, is O(exp((2f−d₀)V)). Above the threshold f=0 and it is o(1); along the sequences of excursions below the threshold, the principal term has size exp(fV) and the relative correction is O(exp((f−d₀)V))=o(1). Both signs are preserved. The equivalence with log-concavity uses exclusively derivatives in t with s frozen; it does not allow differentiating along the curve s²=cV nor deducing log-concavity from the mere positivity of the measure.

**Independent review of the endpoint and of the logarithmic variance reduction: PROVED for the indicated explicit profile.** The four box factors of each φ and the quadratic factor of the detector give per right zero |a_z|≤2|γ|^(−6); the probabilistic smoother has transform of modulus ≤1 on Re z≥0. The unit count with multiplicities of 175 implies the total bound 400Σ_{j≥⌊G⌋−1}log(4+j)/j⁶<1/64. At c=c_*>0 there remains therefore −1/8 plus a real polynomial of norm <1/64 and o(1), which even gives a strict margin with respect to −1/16. The polynomial has mean zero and positive mean square, so it does not converge to zero. For variance c_*V−logV, each critical term receives V^{(γ²−b²)/2}exp(−ibγlogV). Maximizing γ²−b² fixes b by the critical relation and then |γ|: a unique conjugate pair remains, including its grouped multiplicities. The phase has derivative γ(1+c_*b)−bγ/V, eventually nonzero, and the other powers are smaller. The non-critical terms keep a uniform exponential gap: beyond a fixed height the negative quadratic coefficient remains ≤−c_*γ²/8. The same estimate of the tail t<0 and of the arithmetic error holds for this eventually positive variance. This proves both unbounded signs, without changing c_* or providing its arithmetic bound for c↓0.

**Independent review of the Gaussian comparison without boxes: PROVED, including the exclusion of the favourable endpoint.** In the inversion of −ζ′/ζ(1/2+w), the shift from Re w=1 to −1 crosses the pole and all nontrivial zeros, with their multiplicities, but no trivial zero. The functional equation bounds the new vertical and the remainder is O(exp(−V+s²/2)); the horizontals at good heights disappear by the Gaussian factor. Mertens gives exactly 1/2+o(1) for the squares; the powers of order ≥3 are O(1/s). One obtains D_c=−1/2−Σ_z mult(z)exp((z+cz²/2)V)+o(1). The lack of decay of the coefficients does not matter for fixed c>0, because the factor exp(−cγ²V/2) dominates the zero count uniformly for V≥1.

At the positive endpoint, the critical polynomial P has a Fourier coefficient of integer modulus ≥1, without collision of exponents. If M=sup P, the function M−P is nonnegative and its non-constant coefficient has modulus ≤ its mean M; therefore M≥1. Applying the same argument to −P gives inf P≤−1. The Bohr means computed on any tail keep those coefficients, so these are limsup and liminf at infinity. Thus limsup D_c≥1/2 and liminf D_c≤−3/2. The eventual ceiling of the positive comparison characterizes strictly c>c_*; it contrasts correctly with the closed endpoint of the attenuated detector. Obtaining that ceiling for a sequence c↓0 through independent arithmetic inputs remains pending.

**Exact cost of replacing large primes by integers without small divisor in the raw comparison.** Fix 0<c<1/8, y=exp(θV) and θ>(1+c/2)/2. In Q_c keep exactly the primes ≤y and replace the larger ones by ALL integers n>y without prime ≤y, with the same positive weight (log n)/√n · g_s(V−log n). The excess E over Q_c has equivalent
E ∼ exp(VF)/(θ V sqrt(2πcV) a²),   F=θ−(2θ−1)²/(2c),   a=(2θ−1)/c−1/2>0.
In particular at the cut itself θ₀=(1+c/2+sqrt(c+c²/4))/2 the excess is already o(1), of order V^(−3/2). Just below (still a>0) it grows exponentially. The squares of primes among the misclassified composites are negligible here. Therefore at θ₀ the eventual ceiling of the raw comparison, including the failure at c=c_*>0, is preserved for this entirely positive sieve. Its evaluation only needs primes ≤y, through divisibility, but it still requires bounding the balance against the integral to constant precision.

Proof. Put H=log y, r=log n=2H+v. On r≥2H,
exp(r/2)g_s(V−r)= exp(VF) exp(−av−v²/(2cV))/sqrt(2πcV).
Hence v>log²V costs o(exp(VF)V^(−3/2)) even when counting all integers: in unit cells of r there are O(exp r) candidates and the maximal weight gives O(poly(V+v)exp(VF−av)/√V) per cell, using the product exp(r/2)g_s and the bounded variation of exp(r/2) within the cell. In the remaining interval only two primes >y fit, since 2H+log²V<3H. Replace the measures Σ1/p by dt/t (t=log p) over H≤t≤H+log²V for the two ordered primes p<q. The uniform discrepancy is poly(V)exp(−c₁√V) by PNT, and the test r exp(r/2)g_s(V−r) has supremum and variation ≤poly(V)exp(VF); each section is an interval. Thus the absolute error is o(exp(VF)V^(−3/2)), even if F<0. The squares are paid separately by Σ_{p>y}1/p²≪exp(−H) multiplied by that same supremum. The continuous density in r after including the label r is log((r−H)/H)=log(1+v/H). Since H log(1+v/H)≤v and tends to v for fixed v, dominated convergence leaves ∫₀^∞v exp(−av)dv=1/a². This proves the formula. Compared with 368, here the absolute error of a sieve without parity is studied on the raw Gaussian average at variance cV; the fixed-width Möbius criterion is not used.


**Independent review of the cost of the positive sieve: PROVED for fixed c and θ in the indicated range.** Every composite without prime divisor ≤y has log n≥2H. Writing r=2H+v, the exponential identity is exact: the constant exponent is VF and the linear one −av, with F=θ−(2θ−1)²/(2c) and a=(2θ−1)/c−1/2>0. Counting all integers by unit cells gives for v>log²V a ceiling exp(VF)poly(V+v)exp(−av)/√V, with sum o(exp(VF)V^(−3/2)). This bound is relative to the equivalent even when F<0; it is not intended to be converted first into an absolute error independent of F.

In 0≤v≤log²V there are exactly two prime factors, counted with multiplicity. For distinct ones, p<q removes duplication and the product of the measures dt/t has, after incorporating log n=r, density ∫_H^{r/2}r/[t(r−t)]dt=log((r−H)/H)=log(1+v/H). No other factor 2 appears. PNT in the two variables has relative error poly(V)exp(−c₁√V), because all its endpoints are ≥exp(H); the sections of the truncated domain are intervals and their variation is polynomial after extracting exp(VF). The squares weigh at most exp(VF)poly(V)Σ_{p>y}p^(−2), negligible against the principal term. Thus E=exp(VF)/√(2πcV)·(1+o(1))/(H a²), using Hlog(1+v/H)≤v and dominated convergence against exp(−av). The exact constant is verified.

The upper root of F is θ₀=(1+c/2+√(c+c²/4))/2, with a₀=√(c+c²/4)/c>0. There E∼[θ₀√(2πc)a₀²]^(−1)V^(−3/2), and below, keeping a>0, F>0. The substitution adds a positive excess o(1) at θ₀: it keeps the margin −1/2 of the regime c>c_*, the excursions of the regime c<c_* and the positive failure at the endpoint c=c_*>0. An approximation relative to the principal term exp(V/2+cV/8) is not enough: the comparison still needs constant absolute precision. The construction allows computing the sieve with primes ≤y, but does not by itself prove its arithmetic ceiling. The contrast of scope with 368 is correct: here there are no Möbius signs nor a fixed-width detector.

**What exactly the Selberg principal term loses for the Gaussian comparison.** The index already discards reopening the Selberg/Vaughan class as a mechanism by itself. For the new cut θ₀ one can decide quantitatively whether optimizing the usual square and paying the distribution error by its modulus suffices. Let D=y=exp(θ₀V). Majorize the indicator of integers without primes ≤y by (Σ_{d|n,d≤D}λ_d)² with real coefficients on squarefree divisors and λ₁=1. On replacing the divisibility densities by 1/[d,e], the BEST possible principal term for n>y, divided by the target integral exp(V/2+cV/8), tends to (1+c/2)/θ₀>1. The loss is already a fixed fraction of the target, before adding the primes ≤y or the absolute value of any error. The use of a remainder with signed cancellation is not excluded.

Indeed, the minimum of Σλ_dλ_e/[d,e] is 1/G(D), G(D)=Σ_{r≤D}μ²(r)/φ(r). To see it, write b_r=Σ_{r|d}λ_d/d. The square equals Σφ(r)b_r² by the gcd identity, and Σμ(r)b_r=λ₁. Cauchy gives the floor, attainable by b_r proportional to μ(r)/φ(r) by triangular inversion on the finite divisor-closed set. Moreover G(D)=log D+O(1): the series of μ²(r)/φ(r) is that of 1/n convolved with a multiplicative factor whose non-constant local coefficients are 1/[p(p−1)] at p and −1/[p(p−1)] at p². Its mass is one and it has finite absolute logarithmic moment by Euler product. Summation against Σ_{n≤x}1/n proves the estimate. Since D=y every prime of an allowed d is ≤y.

Finally the integral of (log n)/√n · g_s(V−log n) with respect to dn for n>y, divided by exp(V/2+cV/8), is E[R 1_{R>θ₀V}], with R normal of mean (1+c/2)V and variance cV. For 0<c<1/8, θ₀<1+c/2 with fixed separation, so that expectation is (1+c/2)V+o(1). The announced ratio follows on dividing by G(D). If other D are allowed with the same sieved primes, G(D) without additional restrictions only increases the possibilities and is still a ceiling for the optimal denominator. To aim at paying errors in modulus one needs at least log D≥(1+c/2)V−O(1). In particular, as c decreases to zero the ratio of the optimal principal term at level D=y approaches two. The constant margin of squares does not compensate that excess of the principal term.


**Independent review of the optimal Selberg principal term: PROVED, with discard restricted to the absolute treatment of the remainder.** For real squarefree coefficients d≤D, the identity 1/[d,e]=gcd(d,e)/(de) and gcd(d,e)=Σ_{r|d,e}φ(r) diagonalize the principal term exactly into Σφ(r)b_r². The condition λ₁=1 is equivalent to Σμ(r)b_r=1. The triangular transformation is invertible on the finite set of squarefree indices ≤D; hence Cauchy–Schwarz gives not only the floor 1/G(D), but an admissible minimizer b_r=μ(r)/(φ(r)G(D)). No inadvertent additional restriction on those b_r has been imposed.

The convolution with 1/n has per prime the two non-constant coefficients +1/[p(p−1)] and −1/[p(p−1)], at p and p² respectively. Its total signed mass is 1 and its absolute sum weighted by log n is finite. The formula for the harmonic numbers gives G(D)=logD+O(1), including the terms truncated by that logarithmic sum. On changing r=log n and completing the square, the principal integral over n>y, divided by exp(V/2+cV/8), is exactly E[R1_{R>θ₀V}], R normal with mean (1+c/2)V and variance cV. Since θ₀<1+c/2 with fixed separation, it equals (1+c/2)V+o(1). The optimal ratio is therefore (1+c/2)/θ₀>1, and tends to 2 as c↓0.

If D>y but only divisors with primes ≤y are kept, the exact minimum uses the restricted sum G_y(D)≤G(D); using G(D) only weakens the floor. Thus reaching the target by a principal term without compensation requires at least logD≥(1+c/2)V−O(1). At level D=y, neither adding the positive contributions of primes ≤y nor paying the errors by their modulus can remedy the fixed excess already present. This computation does not exclude a signed remainder cancelling the principal term, other observables or a signed reorganization. It is a quantification of the preexisting Selberg/Vaughan NO-GO for this average, not a universal obstruction to every positive sieve.

**Saturation even at unlimited level: real magnitude of the signed remainder.** Let P_y be the primorial and θ₀ the cut that pays the false positives to precision o(1). Allowing ALL divisors of P_y gives as exact minimum of the principal term the density φ(P_y)/P_y.
