Even among arbitrary periodic majorants of the coprimality indicator, their average cannot go below that value, attained by the indicator itself. Therefore when
R(c)=exp(−γ_E)(1+c/2)/θ₀>1

Indeed the sum of μ²(r)/φ(r) over r|P_y is exactly Π_{p≤y}(1−1/p)^(−1). Alternatively the mean of 1_{gcd(n,P_y)=1} is φ(P_y)/P_y by direct count. Mertens gives the latter as exp(−γ_E)(1+o(1))/log y. Multiplying by the truncated integral of the previous entry gives R(c) times I=exp(V/2+cV/8), with error o(I). It is essential to keep the exact product, not to replace it by its asymptotic equivalent, if constant precision is sought.

For the exact indicator one can decide unconditionally which part of the principal term its remainder already cancels. Let S_y be the sum over n>y coprime to P_y with the Gaussian weight log n/√n, and L_y the product of that exact density by the truncated integral. Then (S_y−L_y)/I→1−R(c). Indeed the raw contrast of 195 gives Q_c/I→1 even outside RH, since max_z Re(z+cz²/2)<1/2+c/8 and the Gaussian tail is summable. The primes ≤y cost o(I): group log p into unit cells, use Chebyshev and the Gaussian tail after completing the square, with distance (1+c/2−θ₀)V to the tilted centre. The error of the composites >y is O(V^(−3/2)). Subtracting L_y concludes. This proves the negative sign of the remainder in the regime R(c)>1 and its initial magnitude, but an o(I) error still exceeds the budget of order one. This fractional saving is not to be counted as closure of the sign.


**Independent review of the saturation by complete primorial: PROVED for fixed c in the previous range.** When all divisors of P_y are allowed, the diagonal sum G is exactly ∏_{p≤y}(1−1/p)^(−1), so its inverse is φ(P_y)/P_y. The minimizer can be realized directly with λ_d=μ(d): its square is the coprimality indicator itself at each integer. This statement compares mean densities; it does not claim an inequality between their sums against any non-constant weight.

Mertens and the already checked truncated integral give L_y/I→exp(−γ_E)(1+c/2)/θ₀=R(c), with I=exp((1/2+c/8)V). For the real sum S_y, the spectral maximum of the raw comparison is strictly smaller than d₀=1/2+c/8, since |Re z|≤1/2 and |Im z| is bounded away from zero; the tail in height is Gaussian. Thus Q_c/I→1 unconditionally. The fixed positive distance between θ₀V and the tilted mean (1+c/2)V allows removing the primes ≤y by Chebyshev and the Gaussian tail, at cost o(I). It is an already proved fractional cancellation, but not its precision at constant scale; it does not close the sign of the contrast nor discard a finer use of the location of the residues.

**Calibrated cut with exponential absolute error: comparison of the zero residue with the exact mean of translations.** The excess 2exp(−γ_E) was obtained by freezing the smallest cut that pays for the composites. The calibration removes an obstacle of the majorant, but leaves unproved the sign of the discrepancy for c↓0.

**The calibrated discrepancy resides in large joint denominators.** In the exact Fourier expansion over translations modulo P of the previous paragraph, the sum of moduli of ALL non-constant coefficients of reduced denominator q≤X^(9/10) is O_c(exp(−V/3)) for 0<c≤1/1000 fixed. ||f^(k)||₁ ≤ poly_c(V) exp([1/2−k+c(k−1/2)²/2]V).

P^(−1) Σ_a |S(a)−mean(S)|² ≫_c √V.
An explicit family of denominators formed by two large primes and an additional divisor suffices. This prevents justifying the comparison of the zero class with the mean via an o(1) bound in quadratic norm over all classes.

Write F(ξ)=Σ_n f(n)e(nξ), N=⌊X^1.07⌋. The ℓ¹ tail beyond N is O(exp(−V)) by the previous integral and variation, with exponent .535−.07²/(2c)≤−1.915. Σ_{p₁<p₂, 1<d≤X^.01, d squarefree} |T_{dp₁p₂}|=O_c(exp(−V/3)).

If 0<κ<κ₀ there is a real saddle of positive curvature u=λ−t/H with t→t₋, where t₋∈(0,1) is the smaller root of t exp(−t)=κ/(cb²). If κ>κ₀ there is no saddle in 0<u<λ for large V. 1−t∼sqrt(2 log log V/log V),   B/(cV)∼1−t.
In the cases with a positive saddle the equivalent of the previous entry remains valid with its current values of u,B; B/V is not required to be bounded away from zero at the endpoint. This threshold refers to the real integration mechanism; it does not determine the sign beyond it.

Proof. Write L=log V. For bounded t, u=λ−t/H, PNT with partial summation gives l′(u)=z^(1−u)/(1−u)(1+O(1/H)), and −l″(u)=H z^(1−u)/(1−u)(1+O(1/H)). In the first sum the prime term is Σ log p/p^u and in the second it carries another log p; replacing 1/(1−p^(−u)) or its square by one introduces a relative error polynomially small in z, uniformly on that compact set of t. The saddle equation is then equivalent to
t exp(−t)=[κ/(cb²)](1−log L/L+O(1/L)),
by H=(L−log L+log κ)/b. For unbounded t and 0<u<λ, restricting l′ to z/2<p≤z gives Hl′/(cV)≥C exp(t), making t=Hl′/(cV) impossible for large t. For u≥λ the phase derivative is positive. This proves supercritical non-existence and, by sign change near the smaller root, subcritical existence. At the endpoint, the sign of t−Hl′/(cV) is negative at t=0 and positive at t=1 because of the term log L/L. The smaller root in (0,1) tends to one, and the expansion e·t exp(−t)=1−(1−t)²/2+O((1−t)³) gives the equivalent. At any bounded root B/(cV)=1−t+O(1/H) by the quotient of the two PNT estimates. There is at most one root of positive curvature, since l‴>0 on the positive line by the local series.

For the integral at the endpoint the global modulus bound exp(−Bτ²/2) is kept. The cubic error on the scale 1/√B is O(VH/B^(3/2))=o(1) by the equivalent of B. The logarithmic amplitude l′/log a is still O(1/H); u remains in a compact subset of (0,1). The same dominated convergence proves the equivalent. In particular for fixed λ the calibrated cut y=exp(Θ(V)) falls far beyond the vanishing scale: by monotonicity of l′ in the set of primes, it does not recover a real saddle by adding further factors either. An extension up to y needs another source of cancellation.

**The threshold is recovered by counting only signs at integer scales.** Fix C=1/1000. For each integer n≥1 count the length of the c∈(0,C) such that Q_c(n)>exp(n/2+cn/8). Then
lim_{N→∞} (1/N) Σ_{N<n≤2N} length{c∈(0,C): Q_c(n)>exp(n/2+cn/8)} = c_*/2.

Proof. For fixed c in (0,c_*), the boxless expansion has dominant rate f>0. The rates b−c(γ²−b²)/2 are affine functions of c. Two identical lines have equal b and |γ|, hence correspond to the same conjugate pair (grouping multiplicities). The coincidences between distinct lines are confined to a countable set of c. Outside it there is a unique dominant pair with b>0 and ordinate γ>0, separated in rate by the quadratic decay in height. At integer scales, exp(−fn)D_c(n)=−2m cos(nγ(1+cb))+o(1), with multiplicity m≥1. For each right zero the frequency divided by 2π is irrational except on a countable set of c, since its slope bγ does not vanish. Outside the exceptional union, equidistribution of the irrational rotation makes the discrepancy positive on a fraction tending to 1/2 in N<n≤2N: first exclude an arbitrarily small neighbourhood of the zeros of the cosine and then let its width tend to zero. For c>c_* the discrepancy tends to −1/2 and the fraction tends to zero. The single endpoint and the countable sets do not affect the integral. The dependence of Q on c>0 is continuous by local uniform convergence. The sample fractions lie in [0,1], so integration and passage to the limit require only dominated convergence, without uniformity of the spectral gap in c. Finally c_*<C by Z2. The same identity holds with the sign of S(0)−mean(S) of the calibrated cut at each (c,n): the error tends to zero for fixed c and in the growing case does not modify the density of signs. The step cut in c is measurable. The result does not assert density 1/2 for each exceptional variance.

Only isolated intersections remain for each pair of distinct rates; their union is countable. Outside it and for 0<c<c_*, the positive maximum has a unique conjugate pair, with a gap to the rest from the quadratic decay in height. Its b is necessarily positive. For each right pair, the condition γ(1+cb)/(2π) rational excludes only a countable set of c, because the slope bγ is not zero. The union of both exceptional sets is still countable.

For each n, Q_c(n) is continuous in c>0 by local uniform convergence of the positive sum; the indicators and their averages are measurable and lie between 0 and 1. For the calibrated cut, y(c,n) is a measurable step function by the first-finite-product criterion; at fixed c its exponential error does not alter the supercritical sign nor the density of signs in the generic subcritical case. The same integration applies. Therefore a liminf of zero forces c_*=0 and RH, but the identity provides no independent arithmetic bound to prove it nor asserts frequency 1/2 at the exceptional variances.

**One scale at a time: density in width and number of crossings.** Fix C=.001 and D(c,V)=Q_c(V)−exp(V/2+cV/8). Without averaging in V, for real V→∞ one has length{0<c<C:D(c,V)>0}→c_*/2. Moreover there is a counting dichotomy. Under RH, on each [ε,C], 0<ε<C fixed, there are no crossings for V sufficiently large. Outside RH there is a fixed ε for which at EACH large scale there are ≫V sign changes in [ε,C]. Unconditionally the number of zeros in any [ε,C] is O_ε(V), counting multiplicities. An arithmetic bound o(V) along a sequence of scales on each [ε,C] would therefore suffice, without needing to locate the zeros or decide the sign at specific parameters.

To prove it, on [ε,C] only finitely many lines of rate b−c(γ²−b²)/2 can attain the maximum: compare with any fixed zero, and the high ordinates fall quadratically in a uniform way. On each interior compact subset of a subcritical piece with a fixed winner, there is a uniform gap and rate f(c)>0 bounded away from zero. The raw explicit formula, with squares 1/2+O_ε(V^(−1/2)) and uniform Gaussian tail, gives D(c,V)exp(−Vf(c))=−2m cos(Vγ(1+cb))+o(1) uniformly. Now vary c at fixed V: the phase is linear with non-zero slope Vγb. By complete periods, the positive set occupies half the length of the piece in the limit, temporarily removing the zones |cos|<δ and then δ↓0. At successive maxima and minima the signs are opposite, giving ≫V crossings by continuity in any subcritical subinterval of positive length with a fixed winner. On the supercritical compact sets D→−1/2 uniformly. Intervals of arbitrarily small length around the finitely many intersections, the endpoint c_* and the origin are discarded (first fix ε, then ε↓0). Thus the stated limit length is obtained without an irrationality condition on any ordinate.

For the counting ceiling, use the complex disc centred at C with radius R=C−ε/4, where Re(1/c)≥k_ε>0 and the square root has a holomorphic branch. The prime series converges normally and |D(c,V)|≤exp(O_ε(V)) there: majorize by all integers, group log n in unit intervals and complete the square in exp(r/2−k_ε(r−V)²/(2V)), allowing polynomial factors and the unit shift. At the centre D(C,V)→−1/2 unconditionally by Z2. Jensen at the inner radius C−ε/2 gives O_ε(V) zeros and covers [ε,C]. The linear order would therefore actually be attained in some band if RH fails. This formulation leaves as a target a strict improvement of a sign-complexity ceiling for the arithmetic sum in width; the Jensen ceiling alone does not supply it.


**Independent check of the density at individual scale and of the linear zero ceiling: PROVED.** On a compact set [ε,C], a fixed zero provides a uniform floor for the maximum of the rates; the decay −εγ²/2 excludes all sufficiently high ordinates. Only finitely many lines can win and, after grouping conjugates and multiplicities, their intersections are finite. On every interior compact subset of a subcritical piece with fixed winner, the gap and the positive rate have uniform floors. The raw Gaussian series, the squares and the higher powers admit there the uniform expansion of the note. The phase Vγ(1+cb) has slope Vγb≠0. By complete periods in c, the proportion of each sign tends to 1/2; successive values with cosine ±1 give ≳V changes in any fixed subinterval of that piece. This continuous argument does not require irrationality of the frequency.

On the supercritical compact sets the expansion is uniformly −1/2+o(1). Removing neighbourhoods of arbitrarily small length of the intersections and of the endpoint c_* allows integrating in c at fixed V. The piece 0<c<ε always weighs at most ε; letting ε↓0 gives positive length →c_*/2. Under RH all the compact sets [ε,C] are supercritical and remain without zeros. If RH fails, there is a fixed subinterval inside (0,c_*) without intersections; it contains ≳V changes for EACH sufficiently large V. The strength of the quantifiers of the sublinear criterion along subsequences is thus verified.

For Jensen, the disc of centre C and radius C−ε/4 is contained in Re c≥ε/4; there √c has a holomorphic branch and Re(1/c) has a positive floor. The prime sum converges normally in the disc, and counting all integers by logarithmic cells gives |Q_c(V)|≤exp(O_ε(V)): completing the square absorbs both the factor log n and the variations within each cell. The integral term has the same ceiling. At the real centre C>c_* by Z2, |D(C,V)|≥1/4 for V large. Jensen between that radius and C−ε/2 bounds the number of zeros by O_ε(V), counting multiplicities; [ε,C] lies strictly inside the smaller radius. This ceiling includes the real changes but does not make them sublinear. The formulation identifies a possible arithmetic sign-complexity obligation, without proving it or enlarging the certified window.

**Proof of insufficiency of a crossing argument based only on PNT, positivity and fixed progressions.** There exist subsets of the ordinary integers with unit atoms, coinciding with the primes up to any prescribed finite limit, which satisfy the PNT in all reduced progressions of fixed modulus, and whose raw Gaussian comparison has ≫V sign changes in a fixed band of widths at each large scale. That band can be placed below 2/G² while keeping the bias −1/2 above the artificial threshold. It is a counterexample to those partial hypotheses, not to an argument using the prime factorization of the integers.

Construction. Fix 0<b<1/2, γ>G and, for large x, the counting density
dM(x)=[1−(1/2)x^(−1/2)+x^(b−1/2)cos(γ log x)]dx/log x.
It is positive. In each block [2^j,2^(j+1)) choose m_j=lcm(1,…,⌊log j⌋). Only the residues coprime to m_j are needed. In each of them, running through its consecutive candidates, select one each time the integer part of (M(x)−M(2^j))/φ(m_j) increases, comparing at the candidates themselves (start the counter at zero). The jump is ≤1 for large j: by Chebyshev log m_j=O(log j), and by Mertens m_j/φ(m_j)=O(log log j); the density of M is O(1/j). The final piece without a candidate also introduces O(1) per class. Thus for any prefix of the block the error relative to M/φ(m_j), with origin at the start of the block, is O(1) per residue. For each fixed modulus q, eventually q|m_j and each reduced residue modulo q contains φ(m_j)/φ(q) of the chosen residues. The cumulative count in that progression is M(x)/φ(q)+O_q((log x)^K) for some fixed K, by summing O(m_j) per block and a finite initial adjustment. In particular the usual PNT holds in those progressions with an error relative to li(x)/φ(q) of O_q(x^(1/2+b)). No fixed prime divides the sufficiently late elements. The whole initial part can be fixed arbitrarily.

By partial summation, replacing this set by dM in Q_c costs o(1) uniformly on compact intervals of c⊂(0,.001]: against the polylogarithmic counting error it suffices to integrate (1+log x)^K |f′(x)|. On changing to r=log x and completing the square the cost is poly(V)exp((−1/2+c/8)V); the initial piece is negligible. The three Gaussians of the integral give exactly, up to o(1), the discrepancy
−1/2 + exp([b−c(γ²−b²)/2]V) cos(γ(1+cb)V).
Therefore each compact interval of positive length inside (0,2b/(γ²−b²)) exhibits ≫V sign changes. Above that threshold the limit is −1/2. The Beurling antecedent in the index alters the multiplicative system; this construction specifically proves the limit of counting in width for a subset of integers equidistributed in all fixed progressions. It preserves neither the von Mangoldt convolution identity nor the fundamental theorem of arithmetic for those atoms. To attempt o(V) one must use additional information, and improving the rounding of a continuous density with those same properties is not enough.


**Independent check of the counterexample of equidistributed integer atoms: PROVED with the indicated non-multiplicative scope.** The density of M is positive for large x because b<1/2. In a block of index j, two consecutive candidates of a reduced class are m_j apart. The increment of the target (M(x)−M(2^j))/φ(m_j) between them is ≤C m_j/(jφ(m_j))=O(loglogj/j)<1. This includes the first partial interval from the start of the block and the last one without a candidate. Selecting when the integer part rises produces distinct unit atoms and error O(1) per class on EVERY prefix of the block. Chebyshev gives m_j≤j^K for a fixed constant; summing class and block errors produces a power of logx.

For fixed q, eventually q|m_j. The reduction of the unit group modulo m_j to that modulo q is surjective, with fibres of cardinality φ(m_j)/φ(q). Summing the O(1) errors of the classes projecting onto a reduced residue gives the approximation M(x)/φ(q)+O_q((logx)^K′), after absorbing the finite prefix and the previous blocks. The difference M−li is O(x^(1/2+b)), so the PNT holds in all those progressions. The construction can start after any prescribed finite limit; it imposes no changes on the prefix of primes. No fixed prime divides the sufficiently late atoms, since it eventually becomes part of m_j.

The polylogarithmic counting error is integrated against f′ by parts. After r=logx, its polynomial moments and the factor exp(−r/2) leave O_c(poly(V)exp((−1/2+c/8)V)), uniform on positive compact sets of c; the fixed prefix and the lower tail of the Gaussians are o(1) with the same uniformity. In the integral of the density, logx cancels: the three terms become respectively exp(r/2)g_s(V−r), −g_s(V−r)/2 and exp(br)cos(γr)g_s(V−r). Their integrals over the line are I, −1/2 and exp([b−c(γ²−b²)/2]V)cos(γ(1+cb)V). This reproduces the formula with error o(1), sufficient for alternating signs at ≳V points of any fixed subcritical band; above it the bias −1/2 remains.

Since γ>G and 2b<1, the artificial threshold 2b/(γ²−b²) is less than 2/G². The example satisfies positivity, integer support, unit multiplicities, any prefix and PNT in all FIXED progressions, but those atoms are not a generating system with unique factorization of the integers nor do they satisfy the convolution identities of the true primes. It refutes inferring a sublinear count solely from those partial hypotheses. It is not a counterexample to an argument using additional arithmetic information nor to the crossing claim for the actual prime observable.

**What the divisor identity detects of the artificial perturbation, without inverting ζ.** For the integer set E just constructed put Λ_E(n)=Σ_{q∈E,k≥1:q^k=n} log q (summing even if two representations coincide), ρ=1/2+b+iγ. The Dirichlet series of the defect (1*Λ_E)(n)−log n is H(s)=ζ(s)L_E(s)+ζ′(s). In a strip crossing Re s=1/2, its only possible poles are a simple one at 1 and a pair at ρ,ρ̄ with residues ζ(ρ)/2 and its conjugate. Thus, if a frequency outside the divisor of ζ is chosen, the smoothed identity distinguishes the perturbation. If RH fails, one can choose precisely a right zero as ρ: then the centred Gaussian average of the defect becomes exponentially small even at the widths where the artificial prime detector exhibits ≫V crossings. This alternative is conditional on the existence of the zero; it does not assert that the artificial set satisfies the pointwise identity.

Details. The first-power part P_E(s)=Σ_{q∈E}(log q)q^(−s) continues to Re s>0 with polar parts 1/(s−1)−(1/2)/(s−1/2)+(1/2)/(s−ρ)+(1/2)/(s−ρ̄). Indeed integrating log x against dM gives those powers, and the polylogarithmic error of the rounding, after partial summation, is holomorphic of polynomial growth in closed interior half-planes. Starting the density at a fixed threshold only adds entire terms with the same bounds in strips. In L_E=P_E(s)+P_E(2s)+Σ_{k≥3}P_E(ks) the tail converges absolutely for Re s>1/3, and the pole of P_E(2s) at 1/2 cancels exactly the real pole of P_E(s) there. Choose σ₀ between max(1/3,Re ρ/2) and 1/2. On Re s≥σ₀ only the three simple poles of L_E remain. On multiplying by ζ and adding ζ′ the double poles at 1 cancel, proving the description of H.

To measure the defect, apply to its series the inverse with multiplier (s−1) exp((s−1/2)V+cV(s−1/2)²/2). It is the first derivative with respect to the centre at frozen variance minus half a unit of the Gaussian window. On the line σ₀ the cost is O_c(poly(V)exp((−η+cη²/2)V)), η=1/2−σ₀>0; the Gaussian allows the shift with the previous polynomial bounds. The factor s−1 separately removes any linear bias in the cumulative defect. Only the pair with coefficient (ρ−1)ζ(ρ)/2 remains. If ζ(ρ)=0, exponential decay is obtained for each 0<c≤.001 even though the Gaussian sum of the atoms E keeps violating the ceiling at the subcritical widths. Do not repeat the multiplier inversion already discarded in the paragraph 1*(Λ−b): here the defect of the example with integer atoms and their powers, squares included, has been concretely measured. The exact identity for each integer retains more information than this single type of smoothed check.


**Independent check of the divisor-identity defect with powers: PROVED, including the conditional alternative.** For Re s>1, counting all representations q^k=n gives L_E(s)=Σ_{k≥1}P_E(ks) exactly, even if two representations coincide. The convolution with 1 and the series Σ(logn)n^(−s)=−ζ′(s) produce H(s)=ζ(s)L_E(s)+ζ′(s), with the indicated sign. Integrating logx against the constructed density gives residues 1 at 1, −1/2 at 1/2 and 1/2 at ρ,ρ̄ for P_E. The polylogarithmic rounding error continues holomorphically to Re s>0 with polynomial growth by partial summation; modifying the initial threshold only adds entire terms of polynomial growth in fixed strips.

The term P_E(2s) has residue +1/2 at s=1/2, cancelling EXACTLY that of the first powers; its other poles have real part ≤max(1/4,Reρ/2). The tail k≥3 converges absolutely for Re s>1/3. Thus choosing σ₀ between max(1/3,Reρ/2) and 1/2 leaves in L_E only the poles 1,ρ,ρ̄ to its right. At 1, ζL_E has double principal part +1/(s−1)² and ζ′ cancels it with −1/(s−1)²; a simple pole may remain whose residue depends on the regularization and the prefix. At ρ the residue is ζ(ρ)/2, and the conjugate analogously; if ζ(ρ)=0 the pole is removable, whatever the multiplicity of the zero.

Multiplying by (s−1) removes the possible real simple pole without introducing singularities. The Gaussian shift to σ₀ is justified by the previous polynomial bounds, also for ζ and ζ′; the vertical tail costs poly_c(V)exp((−η+cη²/2)V), η=1/2−σ₀>0. This exponent is negative in the range c≤.001. The only remaining residues have coefficient (ρ−1)ζ(ρ)/2 and the conjugate. In the case of a genuine right zero that same ρ can be chosen in the construction —its height exceeds G by verification— and the smoothed check of the defect decays exponentially, while the detector of the atoms keeps the subcritical crossings. Squares and other powers have been included; no exact divisor identity for the atoms has been assumed nor an unconditional counterexample to the pointwise information obtained. The example makes concrete the loss of the multiplier ζ without resorting to its inversion.

**Local classification of the divisor defect to all orders.** Antecedents: phase-200/D_CONSTRUCTION_001 §on Λ_k and the audit of the von Mangoldt hierarchy in the index. That classical hierarchy is used to subject the previous counterexample of integer atoms to a stronger test. Let ρ be a hypothetical right zero of multiplicity m. Replace the coefficient of the cosine in the density by 2r, r real fixed. The relative term tends to zero since b<1/2, so it suffices to delay the start of the rounding. In L_E the residue at ρ becomes r, without altering the cancellation of squares. For r different from zero the previous Gaussian oscillation acquires a factor 2r and keeps the crossings.

Define A₀=1, A_{k+1}=L_E A_k−A_k′ and D_k=ζ A_k−(−1)^k ζ^{(k)}. In coefficients, each step convolves with Λ_E and adds log(n) times the previous coefficient. For the true primes, L=−ζ′/ζ gives D_k=0 by induction. For the constructed set one has the exact classification: all the D_k are holomorphic at ρ if and only if r belongs to {0,−1,...,−m}. Outside that set, the first pole appears for k=m+1 and is simple, with residue (ζ^{(m)}(ρ)/m!) times the product r(r+1)⋯(r+m). Indeed, A_k has a pole of order at most k with coefficient of degree −k equal to that product up to r+k−1, by the differentiation rule. For sufficiency put r=−l with 0≤l≤m. Locally there is Z=(s−ρ)^l h, with h holomorphic without zeros, obtained by integrating the regular part so that −Z′/Z=L_E. Then ζ A_k=(−1)^k (ζ/Z) Z^{(k)} is holomorphic for all k. The same argument holds at the conjugate.

In particular ONE single set with r=−m hides the pair at all fixed orders simultaneously. For each k multiply D_k by (s−1)^{k+1}, which removes the only possible remaining pole in Re s≥σ₀. The bounds on the shifted line are obtained for the derivatives by Cauchy using a slightly wider strip. The same Gaussian contour gives O_{k,c}(poly(V) exp((−η+cη²/2)V)). The constant may depend on k; the result does not cover orders growing with V, nor does it impose the pointwise identities. With the original coefficient r=1/2 the pair would be detected at order m+1. This distinction rules out increasing a fixed order as a universal remedy for the loss of the pair in these averages.

The cancellation also has a convergent two-variable version near the zero. For |s−ρ| and |w| sufficiently small, the series Σ_{k≥0} D_k(s) w^k/k! represents exactly (ζ(s)/Z(s)) Z(s−w)−ζ(s−w), by Taylor, when r=−l and l≤m. It is jointly holomorphic even at s=ρ. The convergence is uniform on interior compact polydiscs by Cauchy. Thus forming a small analytic translation of the hierarchy does not reveal a hidden local pole either. This local fact does not provide uniform estimates of the Gaussian integrals over the shifted line.

**What the square of the defect recovers before averaging.** For E⊂{2,3,…}, write d(n)=Σ_{q∈E,k≥1:q^k|n} log q−log n. Suppose each prime divides only finitely many elements of E, a property shown above for the rounding by classes. Then liminf X⁻¹Σ_{n≤X}|d(n)|²=0 if and only if E is the set of primes.

Indeed, if a prime p is missing, form B from p and the prime factors other than p of the finitely many elements of E divisible by p (product without repetitions). For (n,B)=1, the terms that could be added in passing from n to pn come from atoms divisible by p. Those with another factor do not divide pn, and the pure powers of p present in E have exponent at least two. Thus d(pn)−d(n)=−log p on that whole coprimality class. The pairs (n,pn), for n≤X/p coprime to B, are disjoint, with contribution to the square at least (log p)²/2 per pair. The lower limit is at least φ(B)(log p)²/(2pB)>0. If E contains all primes and also a composite q, the ordinary factorization gives d(n)≥log q for q|n and d(n)≥0 at every integer. The lower limit is at least (log q)²/q. For the ordinary primes d=0 pointwise.

Application without presupposing that the selection by rounding accidentally differs from the primes. After any prescribed prefix choose a prime p larger than the prefix and delete from E all its multiples, which are finitely many. The modification of L_E is a finite sum of terms −log(q)/(q^s−1), holomorphic in Re s>0. Hence it preserves the residue r=−m, the regularity of all the D_k and their Gaussian bounds at fixed order, as well as the crossings of the original count (each deleted atom contributes o(1)). Now B=p and the explicit lower bound is (1−1/p)(log p)²/(2p). The same example that hides the pair in each signed average is separated by a quadratic test of positive density. There is in this lemma no inequality transferring the zero energy of the primes to the bound of the Gaussian detector.

**Uniform instability of the transfer from a small energy.** Given ε>0 and a finite prefix, there is ONE set E containing the ordinary primes, coinciding with them on the prefix, satisfying the PNT in all fixed progressions and with sup_N (N⁻¹Σ_{n≤N}d(n)²)^{1/2}≤ε. For each fixed c>0 there are scales V→∞ at which Q_{E,c}(V) exceeds I=exp((1/2+c/8)V) by at least a positive constant depending on c times I/V^{5/2}. It does not require a hypothetical zero. The contrast with the immediately preceding characterization distinguishes zero energy from uniform quantitative stability.

Construction. By blocks j choose a new prime l, then Y so large that l is fixed for this choice and Y exceeds four times the end of the previous block. Add M=⌊Y/(log Y)³⌋ composites q=lp, with p distinct primes in [Y/l,2Y/l], avoiding l and all factors already used. The PNT provides more than M candidates as Y increases. Each prime divides only finitely many atoms. Up to x, O(x/log³x) atoms are added: the blocks with Y≤√x contribute O(√x) by geometric separation, and the remaining ones have log Y≥(log x)/2 and ΣY=O(x). The PNT in each fixed progression is preserved by absolute comparison.

The defect added by each block is d_j(n)=Σ_q log(q) Σ_{k≥1}1_{q^k|n}. The frequency up to any N of two divisibilities is ≤1/lcm(q^k,r^h). On the diagonal the sum over k,h≥1 equals Σ_{t≥1}(2t−1)/q^t=O(1/Y). For q=lp, r=lp′ distinct, the lcm equals l^{max(k,h)}p^k p′^h, and the reciprocal sum is ≤1/[l(p−1)(p′−1)]=O(l/Y²). Thus the mean square per block is O(log²Y(M/Y+lM²/Y²)), with absolute constants if Y/l≥2. Choose Y so that its square root is ≤ε2^(−j), j≥1. The triangle inequality on each prefix gives the uniform bound.

Take V=(log Y)/(1+c/2), s²=cV. In the block, log q=V+cV/2+O(1). Each term (log q)q^(−1/2)g_s(V−log q) is ≳_c √V Y^(−1/2)exp(−cV/8). Multiplying by M gives ≳_c I/V^{5/2}. The other added atoms sum positively. For the ordinary primes Q_{P,c}=I+O_{A,c}(I/V^A) for each fixed A: apply Abel to θ(x)=x+O_A(x/(1+log x)^A) with the weight x^(−1/2)g_s(V−log x). After t=log x the cost of the error is bounded by the integral of exp(t/2)g_s(V−t)(1/2+|V−t|/(cV))(1+t)^(−A) over t≥log 2 plus the initial boundary. Completing the square centres the Gaussian at (1+c/2)V and gives the bound by concentration; extending the main term to the line costs a relative exponential tail. A=3 suffices. The construction is independent of c; each c uses its own sequence of centres. This obstruction rules out uniform continuity at the level of the additive ceiling. It leaves open an implication exploiting exclusively the exact identity or additional information about the primes.

**Optimal constant for the one-sided transfer at fixed scale.** For fixed c,ε>0 take the supremum S(V) of Q_{E,c}(V)−Q_{P,c}(V) over E containing all primes and whose energy sup_N N⁻¹Σ_{n≤N}d(n)² is ≤ε². With A=1+c/2, I=exp((1/2+c/8)V), one has
S(V) ∼ ε² I/[A√(2πc) V^{3/2}].
The same equivalence holds imposing any initial prefix of primes and PNT in fixed progressions. The supremum allows E to change with V.

Upper bound proof. All the terms of d are positive or zero. For any finite part F of the added atoms, d(n)²≥Σ_{q∈F}(log q)² 1_{q|n}. Averaging and taking N→∞, then exhausting the atoms, gives Σ_{q added}(log q)²/q≤ε². The quotient between the contribution of q to the detector and this cost is, with t=log q,
I exp(−(t−AV)²/(2cV))/(t√(2πcV)).
Its maximum over t≥log 4 is asymptotic to I/(AV√(2πcV)): on |t−AV|≤V^{2/3} the denominator is (1+o(1))AV, and outside the Gaussian beats the factor O(V) of the comparison. For each fixed E of finite energy, the difference is even o(I/V^{3/2}) by dominated convergence with respect to the previous summable measure: at each fixed atom the normalized quotient tends to zero.

Lower bound proof. Fix 0<δ<1/2 and Y=exp(AV). Among q=2p in [Y,(1+δ)Y] select successively until reaching from below the budget (1−δ)ε² for Σ(log q)²/q. For V large there is available budget of order ≫_δ log Y by PNT, and each increment is O(log²Y/Y)=o(1). The number M chosen is O(ε²Y/log²Y). For every N the diagonal of the mean of d² is at most Σ(log q)²[1/q+O(1/q²)], by the sum over powers of the previous section. The terms between distinct q cost O(M²log²Y/Y²)=O(ε⁴/log²Y), since the only shared prime divisor is 2. The total cost fits under ε² for V large. For these atoms t=AV+O(1) and the upper quotient coincides uniformly with its maximum up to a factor 1+o(1). Therefore the normalized lower limit is ≥1−δ; let δ↓0. Each lower competitor only adds finitely many composites.

This fixes the scale loss for perturbations by addition relative to the count of the actual primes. It estimates neither Q_{P,c}−I nor the case with simultaneous deletions and additions.

At the additive scale of the sign there is a quantitative corollary. If ε=ε(V) and ε(V)²=κ V^{3/2}/I with κ>0 fixed, the same supremum tends to κ/[A√(2πc)]. Indeed, the maximal budget jump O(log²Y/Y) is o(ε(V)²), since Y/I=exp((1/2+3c/8)V). The energy errors O(ε(V)²/Y+ε(V)^4/log²Y) are also o(ε(V)²). Thus the argument with fixed δ survives intact and then δ↓0 is taken. For ε(V)²=o(V^{3/2}/I) the upper bound gives o(1). The critical scale refers to the displacement of Q_P by additions; to decide the sign one must also determine where Q_P lies relative to I.

**One arithmetic width per integer, without integrating in the width.** Let C=1/1000. For N=2^j and N≤n<2N, put c_n=C(n−N+1)/N and check a single inequality Q_{c_n}(n)>exp(n/2+c_n n/8). The fraction of successes among those N integers tends exactly to c_*/(2C). The recipe does not depend on the zeros. Unlike counting along a continuous row of widths at each integer, the observations form a single deterministic sequence. The convergence in area of the indicator proved earlier would not suffice by itself to sample it along this diagonal.

Proof. Cut out of (0,C) neighbourhoods of arbitrarily small total length of the origin, the threshold and the ties between winners (finitely many after cutting the origin). A finite union of removed bands affects at most its length times N/C plus O(1) integers. On a supercritical compact interval J the previous uniform formula gives negative discrepancy for every n of the piece when N is large. On a subcritical J with fixed winner (b,γ) the sign is given by −cos φ_N(n) with error o(1) after normalizing, where φ_N(n)=γn(1+bC(n−N+1)/N). The error is uniform because n≥N and c_n∈J. The indices of that piece form an interval of length N|J|/C+O(1).

For each fixed integer h≠0, averaging exp(ihφ_N(n)) over the piece gives o(1). Indeed, on differencing with an integer shift u≥1 the phase h[φ_N(n+u)−φ_N(n)] has slope 2hγbCu/N. For fixed u and N sufficiently large, the corresponding geometric sum, divided by N, has modulus O_{h,b,γ,C}(1/u). The shifted-averages inequality (Cauchy–Schwarz applied to the average of H translates of the sum, extending the sequence by zero) gives for the square of the modulus of the original sum divided by N an upper limit O((1+log H)/H). First N→∞, then H→∞. This proves equidistribution modulo 2π on the piece and allows removing arbitrarily small zones around the zeros of the cosine to absorb the o(1). The local positive fraction tends to 1/2 without any irrationality hypothesis. Summing the intervals and restoring the discarded zones gives c_*/(2C).

Therefore it would suffice to prove o(N) excesses along a subsequence of these dyadic blocks, querying one rational width per integer. For now an arithmetic estimate of that count is missing; the formula does not by itself provide such a subsequence.

**Localization at consecutive centres.** In fact one may take any sequence of integer starts N→∞ and integer lengths M→∞, even M=⌈log log N⌉. Only n=N+j, 0≤j<M, are queried, with c_j=C(j+1)/M. The same limit fraction holds with no growth relation between M and N. In the previous proof M|J|/C+O(1) indices are counted and the phase at j is γ(N+j)(1+bC(j+1)/M). Its quadratic coefficient is γbC/M, independent of N. The geometric differences normalized by M therefore have the identical bound O(1/u), whatever the linear coefficient; the error of the explicit formula is uniform from n≥N. This allows searching for short blocks with low frequency of excesses: if the fraction tends to zero for even one choice of N→∞, M→∞ with this sweep, then c_*=0.

**What happens when keeping a single centre and choosing it after the mesh.** For any non-empty finite list of prescribed widths 0<c_i≤C, there exist integers N with bounded gaps (bound depending on the list) for which simultaneously Q_{c_i}(N)−exp(N/2+c_i N/8)<−1/4. It is unconditional, even when a width falls exactly at the threshold or at a tie. Hence, checking finite meshes that become dense, choosing each time a single favourable centre after fixing the mesh, can always give zero excesses. In the immediately preceding result the variation of the centres is essential for the conclusion to hold for every start and every growing length.

For each c_i keep in the raw explicit formula ALL pairs of zeros with rate f=b−c_i(γ²−b²)/2≥0. They are finitely many by the quadratic decay, and the other rates have a strictly negative maximum. Their joint contribution is o(1) by summability of the Gaussian tail. The discrepancy then equals −1/2−Σ 2m exp(Nf) cos(Nγ(1+c_i b))+o(1), where the absolute error tends to zero simultaneously for the finite list. Let α be the vector of all retained frequencies over all lists, taken modulo 2π. The closure K of the integer orbit of α is a compact group. The returns of Nα to the neighbourhood U of zero where each cosine exceeds 1/2 have bounded gaps: the translates U−kα with k≥0 cover K by density of the semi-orbit, and a finite subcover suffices. Therefore from any integer there is a return within a bounded number of steps. At each sufficiently late return all retained contributions have favourable sign, including the zero-rate ties; the remaining bias is −1/2+o(1). If there are no retained phases all large integers suffice.

In particular for each m one can fix the mesh Cj/m, 1≤j≤m, and then choose N_m arbitrarily large with zero excesses on the whole mesh. This is compatible with a positive continuous proportion of excesses at that same centre if c_*>0. There is no uniform control of the return gap in m, nor any claim about a mesh imposed in advance as a function of N. Antecedents on recurrence: ES-12/NGR and phase-104_56/67. The application here distinguishes two concrete protocols of the same arithmetic detector; no attempt is made to use recurrence to close the sign.

For the equispaced mesh there is even a lower density bound that does not presuppose independence of frequencies. Every retained ordinate has γ²≤1/4+m/C. Let D be the number of distinct right pairs with γ up to that height bound (that is, γ≤√(1/4+m/C)). Instead of using m coordinates per pair two suffice, Nγ and NγbC/m. If their distances to zero modulo 2π are less than 1/5 and 1/(5m), respectively, the phase of each entry j is at distance <2/5 from zero. In the compact group of these 2D phases the integer returns are equidistributed with respect to Haar: for each non-trivial character on the closure, the mean is a geometric sum tending to zero. The indicated open set has mass ≥(K m)^{−D} with K absolute. Indeed, split each circle of the first type into O(1) intervals of width <1/5 and each circle of the second type into O(m) intervals of width <1/(5m). Two independent Haar points fall in the same box with probability Σp_i²≥1/(Km)^D; their difference has Haar law and then belongs to the open set. The lower density of favourable centres is therefore ≥(Km)^{−D}. The ordinary zero count gives D=O_C(√m log(2m)), whence the floor exp(−O_C(√m log²(2m))). This is asymptotic density, with no bound for the first centre nor for the size of the maximal gap.

**Exact exponential mean of the prime ceiling and limit of its moments.** Write I(V)=exp(λ₀V), λ₀=1/2+c/8, P(s)=Σ_p(log p)p^(−s), L(s)=−ζ′(s)/ζ(s). For 0<c≤.001 and real λ>λ₀, put u=√(1+2cλ), s=1/2+2λ/(1+u), B=1+cs/2. One has exactly
F(λ)=∫₀^∞ exp(−λV)[I(V)−Q_c(V)]dV=c/(2uB)+[1/(s−1)−P(s)]/u>0.
Indeed, integrating the kernel with t=log p gives exp[(1−u)t/c]/u by the Gaussian integral of V^(−1/2)exp(−aV−b/V). Tonelli gives P(s)/u for the prime sum. One has λ−λ₀=(s−1)B and u−B=c(s−1)/2. To verify the sign, (s−1)ζ(s) is the expectation of t/(1−exp(−t)) under the gamma law of shape s−1 and rate 1 (integrate the geometric series). Its derivative is the covariance of that function with log t, strictly positive by the two-copy formula and strict monotonicity. Therefore P(s)≤L(s)<1/(s−1).

Even the means of growing order pass a test that probes centres tending to infinity. If V has gamma distribution of shape k+1 and rate 3/5, then
E[I(V)−Q_c(V)]=1/2+O_c((15/16)^k).
To check it, on the disc |λ−.6|≤.65 the principal root is analytic and |s−(.5+λ)|=|2cλ²/(1+u)²|<.004. Thus Re s>.44 and |Im s|<.66. There P(s)=L(s)−L(2s)+H(s) by continuation, with H analytic, since H=Σ_{k≥2}P(2ks)−Σ_{k≥3}P(ks) converges absolutely. The only relevant poles of the two logarithmic derivatives come from the pole of ζ at 1, using the low-height zero-free strip already verified in the corpus. In F=1/(λ−λ₀)−P(s)/u the pole of s=1 cancels, since dλ/ds=u. The pole of P at s=1/2 has residue −1/2 and leaves in F a pole of residue +1/2 at λ=0. By Cauchy on the circle of radius .64, the derivatives of F−1/(2λ) at .6 have modulus ≤O_c(k!/.64^k). Differentiating the original integral at .6 and multiplying by (−1)^k .6^(k+1)/k! gives the limit with the declared error. The mean centre is (k+1)/.6, with standard deviation √(k+1)/.6. Even if there were exponential positive excursions of Q_c−I, these means of the deficit would converge to +1/2. The averaged positivity here is unconditional and does not control the frequency of excesses in the sweep.

**Sign of the intermediate moments of the Gaussian deficit.** In the previous notation, for every rate λ with 1<s(λ)≤2 and every integer k≥0 one has
∫₀^∞ V^k exp(−λV)[I(V)−Q_c(V)]dV>0.
In particular there is no exceptional order in the family of rate .6. The object of 253–255 was KP with another arithmetic weight; here the point requiring proof is the contribution of the subtracted pole of ζ to the Gaussian deficit.

Let G(s)=1/(s−1)+ζ′(s)/ζ(s). G>0 by the previous gamma argument. For k≥1 the Hadamard factorization of ξ and the digamma series, after cancelling the pole of the gamma at zero with −1/s, give
(−1)^k G^{(k)}(s)/k! = Σ_{j≥1}(s+2j)^(−k−1) + Σ_ρ(s−ρ)^(−k−1).
The two sums converge absolutely counting zeros with multiplicity. To check the margin the height of the first zero (>14) and the classical sum Σ Re(1/ρ)=1+γ_E/2−log(4π)/2<.024 (logarithmic derivative of ξ at 1 and symmetry) suffice. By the symmetry β↔1−β one has Σ1/γ²=2Σβ/γ²≤2(1+1/196)Σ Re(1/ρ)<.049. On 1<s≤2 the contribution in modulus of all non-trivial zeros is therefore <.049·14^(1−k); the first trivial zero alone already contributes ≥4^(−k−1), strictly larger for all k≥1. A strict sign is obtained at all orders of G on the interval.

In F=c/(2uB)+[G(s)+L(s)−P(s)]/u, L−P is a sum of prime powers of exponent ≥2 with positive coefficients, and therefore also has non-negative alternating derivatives. To verify the composition without a global hypothesis on G, fix λ in the range and write s(λ−h)=s(λ)−w(h). The local series of w has positive linear term and all its coefficients non-negative by the binomial for the square root. The series of G(s−w) has all its coefficients positive by the previous bounds; similarly for L−P. The series of 1/u(λ−h) and 1/B(λ−h) are positive by the binomial and the geometric series respectively. Consequently every coefficient of F(λ−h) is positive. Differentiation under the integral is valid because λ>λ₀. In terms of rates, the certified interval is λ₀<λ≤3/2+9c/8. It does not provide arbitrarily narrow concentration at a fixed centre and does not change the pointwise sign.

**Explicit falsifier when extending the band of rates.** For each 0<c≤.001, the moment of order k=400 of the deficit is strictly NEGATIVE at one and the same rate λ=400/log 2. The term of the prime 2 suffices. Put t=log 2 and W(V)=V^k exp(−kV/t). On the interval |V−t|≤.75√(ct) one has |V/t−1|<.03. Taylor for log(1+x)−x gives W(V)/W(t)≥exp(−400·.03²/(2·.97²))>.82. On the same interval, the integral of g_{√(cV)}(V−t) is bounded below by 1.5 exp(−.75²/(2·.97))/√(2π·1.03)>.43. Thus ∫W Q_c /W(t)≥(.82)(.43)log(2)/√2>.17. On the other hand
∫W I/W(t)=t exp(k)k!/k^(k+1) · (1−λ₀t/k)^(−k−1)<.13:
use k!≤√(2πk)(k/e)^k exp(1/(12k)), t<.694, λ₀<.501 and −log(1−x)≤x/(1−x). The certified margin is greater than .04 W(t) in the adverse direction. Therefore requiring all moments positive at ALL rates for this raw deficit is false already at finite order. The eventuality in V at fixed c remains essential.

**Minimal scale of the excesses due to individual atoms.** Centring at V=log p, the isolated term of p exceeds I exactly when V exp(−(2+c/4)V)>2πc, by direct comparison and squaring. For c→0, the upper root R_c of the equality satisfies R_c=[L+log L−log(4π)]/2+o(1), L=log(1/c): first R_c∼L/2 by logarithms and then substitute log R_c=log L−log 2+o(1), cR_c=o(1). By PNT the largest prime strictly less than exp(R_c) has logarithm R_c−o(1). At that centre the individual term already violates the ceiling. Consequently, any eventual threshold V₀(c) valid for all larger real centres must be ≥R_c−o(1), if it exists. This quantifies an unavoidable cost of letting the width go down. It is neither an upper bound for the last excess of the complete count nor a result about the integer centres of the sweep.

In particular, even at the certified rate .6, the full Hankel matrix of those moments has some indefinite finite section. Let ν=e^(−.6V)(I−Q_c)dV. The test in the previous paragraph is equivalent to integrating against ν the square of h(V)=V^200 exp(−(400/log 2−.6)V/2), with negative result. Polynomials are dense in L²(|ν|): |ν| has a positive exponential moment by the absolute integrals of I and Q_c at rate .55; if f is orthogonal to the polynomials, the transform of f d|ν| is holomorphic near the imaginary axis by Cauchy–Schwarz and all its derivatives at zero vanish. Fourier uniqueness gives f=0. Approximating h in that norm eventually preserves the strict sign of its integrated square, by Cauchy–Schwarz. The entry of order zero is positive, hence the section containing the test polynomial is indefinite. An explicit degree at rate .6 is not obtained here. This matrix belongs to the moments of the raw prime deficit and is distinct from the bridge family of paper 46.

**Degree proportional to the shift of the weight: a test that does distinguish the tail.** Fix r=.6, D(V)=I(V)−Q_c(V), and test the form ∫V^k exp(−rV)D(V)P(V)^2 dV on real polynomials. Here the degree grows together with the shift order k. Three statements hold.

1. Unconditionally, for every fixed c in the range and every degree ≤k/150, the form divided by ∫V^k exp(−rV)P² converges to 1/2 uniformly in non-zero P.
2. Whenever D(V)→1/2, the same holds for degrees ≤Bk with ANY fixed B. In particular it holds under RH at each fixed c.
3. If c lies in a subcritical piece with a unique dominant pair of rate f>0 and frequency ω=γ(1+cb), for each B>ω²/(r−f)² there is a negative direction of degree ≤Bk for all sufficiently large k. Consequently eventual positivity at each fixed slope B, for each fixed c, is equivalent to the global sign by the threshold of 195. It does not require positivity in all degrees at fixed k, a condition already falsified by the prime 2.

Proof of 1. In x=rV use the gamma law of shape k+1 and rate 1, with L² norm denoted ||·||. The moment formula at rate .6 gives |E[(D−1/2)x^i]|≤C_c(15/16)^k (k+i)!/k!, simultaneously for i≥0 (D is evaluated at x/r). For P² this bounds the error by C_c(15/16)^k ||P_abs||², where the moduli of the monomial coefficients of P are taken. The orthonormal basis is L_j^k(x)/√binom(k+j,j). By the finite Laguerre formula, the absolute value of the coefficient i in that basis is √binom(k+j,j) binom(j,i)/[(k+1)⋯(k+i)]. Since ||x^i||≤(k+2j)^i for i≤j, the norm of the polynomial of moduli is ≤√binom(k+j,j)(1+(k+2j)/(k+1))^j. Summing by Cauchy–Schwarz in the basis up to d≤k/150 gives ||P_abs||²/||P||²≤(d+1)binom(k+d,d)9^d. Use binom(k+d,d)≤[e(k+d)/d]^d and monotonicity in d of the exponent to bound by (k+1)exp(k log(9e·151)/150). The exponent <.055 is less than log(16/15). This proves uniform convergence.

Proof of 2. For x≤R fixed and j≤Bk, the same coefficient formula bounds each basis element by √binom(k+j,j) exp(jR/(k+1)). The sum of squares of the basis on that interval is exp(O_{R,B}(k)). Its integral under the gamma up to R is ≤exp(O_{R,B}(k))R^{k+1}/(k+1)!, tending to zero. Thus every normalized P has negligible quadratic mass on any fixed compact set, uniformly in the allowed degree. The deficit is bounded on compact sets down to zero (the kernel over log p≥log2 decays as V goes down to zero), and converges to 1/2 in the tail by hypothesis. Splitting into a compact set and its complement proves the statement.

Proof of 3. Now a=r−f>0 and H(V)=exp(−fV)D(V)=2m cos(ωV)+o(1) in the tail, with m the multiplicity. H is globally bounded. The form has the same sign as E_a[H P²] under the gamma law of shape k+1 and rate a. For h(V)=1−cos(ωV), E_a[Hh²]→−2m: the law escapes from compact sets and each non-constant harmonic has expectation (1−iℓω/a)^(−k−1)→0. The average of the product cos(t)(1−cos(t))² over a period is −1.

For this purpose h can be approximated by polynomials of degree ⌊Bk⌋. In the previous Laguerre basis with x=aV, integrating the generating formula (1−z)^(−k−1) exp(−xz/(1−z)) against exp(iωV) gives (1−iω/a+iωz/a)^(−k−1). After normalization the squared moduli of the coefficients are binom(k+j,j)p^(k+1)(1−p)^j, p=a²/(a²+ω²). They sum to 1, the squared norm of the exponential. The mean of this distribution is (k+1)ω²/a² and its variance is (k+1)(1−p)/p². For B>ω²/a², Chebyshev makes the mass above ⌊Bk⌋ tend to zero. Taking the real part of the projection and subtracting it from 1 produces P with ||P−h||₂→0. By boundedness of H, the quadratic integral converges to the same negative number. If RH fails, there is an interval of widths with such a unique winner in its interior by 195. The sufficient constant B depends on the winner and is not claimed to be optimal. There is no unconditional proof of point 2 for all widths.

**Admissible degree using the frequency, without discarding its phase before integrating.** For each fixed c, 0<c≤.001, the unconditional conclusion of uniform convergence to the quotient 1/2 extends from degree k/150 to degree 10¹² k. The Z2 verification up to G=3·10¹² is used. The novelty relative to 253–255 and to the previous estimate is the control of all cross terms of the polynomial coefficients for this shifted weight.

In D=I−Q separate the bias 1/2, the finitely many modes exp(zV) of rate f=Re z≥0 (ties included), and a bounded o(1) remainder, as in the proof of the meshes. Each mode comes from a right zero and has |Im z|=|γ|(1+cb)>G. The remainder contributes o(1) to the normalized form by the escape of mass from compact sets already proved, valid for any fixed slope. For the modes we keep their phase in the monomial moments. Let r=.6, x=rV under Γ(k+1,1), q=r/|r−z|≤2·10⁻¹³ and ||P||₂=1 in x. The modulus of E[exp(zV)x^i] is exactly q^(k+1+i)(k+i)!/k!. Consequently the modulus of the form of the mode is bounded by q^(k+1) E[P_abs(qx)^2]. For j≤d≤Bk the Laguerre formula of the previous paragraph bounds the polynomial of absolute coefficients of each basis vector, at qx, by √binom(k+j,j)exp(jqx/(k+1)). Cauchy–Schwarz in the basis and the gamma integral give
|E[exp(zV)P²]| ≤ (d+1)binom(k+d,k)[q/(1−2Bq)]^(k+1)
if 2Bq<1. Using binom(k+d,k)≤[e(1+B)]^k, for B=10¹² the exponential base e(1+B)q/(1−2Bq) is <.907. Each of the finitely many modes dies out uniformly in P, with no uniformity required in c. This proves the statement; it does not provide a numerical initial k.

**A slope sufficient to detect a mode grows linearly with its frequency.** In statement 3 above, with a=r−f and ω>0, B>(√(1+(ω/a)²)−1)/2 suffices. Introduce t≥0 and use as test the imaginary part of g(V)=exp((−t+iω/2)V), divided by ||g|| under Γ(k+1,a). For H=exp(−fV)D(V) one has E_a[H(Im g)²]/||g||²→−m/2: the normalized factor exp(−2tV) changes the rate a to a+2t, and the average of cos(θ)sin²(θ/2) is −1/4. The non-constant harmonics decay and the new law escapes from every fixed compact set.

On projecting g onto Laguerre, the squared moduli of the coefficients divided by ||g||² form another negative binomial law with parameter p=a(a+2t)/[(a+t)²+ω²/4]. This is verified by the same generating function, now with iω replaced by −t+iω/2. Its mean divided by k+1 is (t²+ω²/4)/(a(a+2t)). For any larger slope, the tail from ⌊Bk⌋+1 on tends to zero in relative norm by Chebyshev. Taking the imaginary part of the projection and using the boundedness of H keeps the negative sign, with the previous normalized test. The minimum over t≥0 is attained at t=(√(a²+ω²)−a)/2, and the reduced mean there is t/a. The bound is sufficient, with no claim of optimality among all polynomials. The verified height only covers a finite band of slopes; the hypothetical zeros may have arbitrarily high frequencies.

**Negative inertia of linear order in the presence of a subcritical winner.** Let M_k be the real matrix of ∫V^k exp(−rV)D(V)|P|² on the monomials of degree ≤⌊Bk⌋. With the unique winner (f,ω,m), a=r−f and B>(√(1+(ω/a)²)−1)/2, there is η>0 such that M_k has at least ηk strictly negative eigenvalues for all large k. In particular, to close it would suffice to have a bound o(k) along a subsequence of k for each fixed B and c. It is not necessary for the whole matrix to be positive along that subsequence. The index already treats inertia in other families (F26 and R183); here it is counted for the shifted moments of the prime deficit, constructing a complete subspace of polynomials.

Work under Γ(K,a), K=k+1, with the bounded multiplier H=e^(−fV)D(V)=2m cos(ωV)+o(1). Let t_* be the minimum of the previous paragraph. By the strict inequality in B there is a compact rectangle of positive area around (t_*,0), with t>0, width in v less than ω/4, and such that (t²+(v±ω/2)²)/(a(a+2t))≤B−δ for some δ>0 throughout. For each point (t,v) of a square mesh of step L/√k in that rectangle take the packet
u_{t,v}(V)=exp((−t+iv)V)sin(ωV/2)/||exp(−tV)||₂.
For fixed L the number of packets is ≍k. Their Hermitian forms are evaluated exactly using the gamma transform. For two exponentials with dampings t,s, normalized by their norms and separated in frequency by ξ, the modulus of the integrated product is
[1+((t−s)²+ξ²)/((a+2t)(a+2s))]^(−K/2).

The matrix of 2m cos(ωV) on the packets is a finite combination of those integrals with ξ=v−w+ℓω, |ℓ|≤2, since both sines have the same phase. For ℓ≠0 the cost per entry is exponentially small, uniformly by the width of the rectangle. For ℓ=0 the coefficient is −m/2 and the diagonal of the normalized integral is 1. In any row the sum of the off-diagonal moduli for this term is bounded by Σ_{n∈ℤ², n≠0}exp(−C L²|n|²), with C>0 independent of k,L: on the compact rectangle log(1+y)≥const·y for the y of the formula. Choose L fixed so large that the sum is less than 1/4. The main matrix is then negative with uniform margin in the Euclidean norm of the coefficients, by row sums. For the Gram matrix without multiplier, expanding sin² in the same way gives a uniformly bounded norm.

The o(1) in H produces an o(1) error in operator norm. On V>R it is bounded by sup_{V>R}|H−2m cos| times the Gram norm. On V≤R fixed it suffices to sum the diagonal masses of the packets: there are O(k), their squared inverse normalizers are exp(O(k)), and the gamma has mass ≤(aR)^K/K!. Take k→∞ and then R→∞.

Finally project each packet onto the polynomials of degree ⌊Bk⌋. For each of its two normalized exponentials the squared error is a negative binomial tail with K successes and mean/K≤B−δ. On the rectangle the error is O(exp(−κk)) uniformly: the probability generating function is [p/(1−(1−p)exp(h))]^K for the exponential moment and, for fixed small h>0, its logarithm divided by K is ≤(B−δ)h+O(h²) uniformly. Markov gives the strict exponent. On summing O(k) squared errors the difference between the operators forming combinations of packets and of their projections tends to zero in norm. Since H is bounded, the negative margin survives. This implies linear independence of the projections and a negative subspace of dimension ≫k. Although the packets are complex, the complexification of a real symmetric matrix preserves its number of negative eigenvalues. The constant η may depend on B,c and the winner and is not estimated uniformly here.

Under RH the previous statement on escape from compact sets gives zero negative eigenvalues eventually for each fixed pair B,c. If RH fails there is c with a unique subcritical winner and a slope B for which the preceding linear floor holds. These two implications prove the criterion by zero density of negative eigenvalues; they do not yet supply the arithmetic bound o(k).

**Cancellation of the trace versus linear inertia.** For k≥1, d≥0, let Π_d be the orthogonal projection onto degrees ≤d under the gamma of shape k+1 and rate a>0. For every frequency ω≠0 one has the explicit finite upper bound
|tr(Π_d exp(iωV) Π_d)| ≤ 2a√((d+1)(d+k+1))/(|ω|k).
In particular the total trace of a fixed harmonic remains O(1) as d=⌊Bk⌋ grows, even though ≍k diagonals are being summed. The estimate uses no information about zeros.

Proof. Put x=aV and absorb the square root of the gamma density into the normalized polynomials to obtain real orthonormal functions φ_j(x) in dx. The operator A=x∂_x+1/2 is antisymmetric by integration by parts; Aφ_j lies in the first j+2 vectors since acting on the square root of the weight introduces the factor (k+1−x)/2. By antisymmetry it is tridiagonal, with modulus of the coefficient of φ_{j+1} equal to α_j=√((j+1)(k+j+1))/2 by comparison of leading terms. Moreover ∫φ_j²/x=1/k: integrate the derivative of the product of x^k exp(−x) and the squared normalized polynomial, using orthogonality to its derivative and k>0.

With τ=ω/a, put m(x)=−∫_x^∞ exp(iτy)dy/y. An integration by parts gives |m(x)|≤2/(|τ|x). The commutator [A,m]=xm′ is multiplication by exp(iτx). In the sum of the first d+1 diagonal entries all internal links of A cancel by antisymmetry, and only the link d,d+1 remains with modulus at most 2α_d∫|m φ_d φ_{d+1}|. The boundary terms of the integration by parts vanish (at zero m=O(1+|log x|)). Cauchy–Schwarz with weight 1/x and the previous identity give the declared bound.

Application to the unique winner of the previous paragraph. With the normalization a=r−f and H=e^(−fV)(I−Q_c), the traces divided by d+1 of the compressions of H, |H|, max(H,0) and max(−H,0) tend respectively to 0, 4m₀/π, 2m₀/π and 2m₀/π, where m₀ is the multiplicity of the winner. Indeed H differs from 2m₀ cos(ωV) by a bounded o(1). This error and its images under 1-Lipschitz functions are removed on average by the uniform escape of mass from compact sets. For every continuous periodic function of the angle, uniform approximation by trigonometric polynomials and the bound for each harmonic give the mean over a period (d=⌊Bk⌋, B>0 fixed). Thus even when the negative inertia is ≫k, the signed mean trace tends to zero and the two masses of opposite sign have equal positive limits. The positive and negative parts here are those of the multiplier BEFORE compressing; we do not identify the sums of the positive or negative eigenvalues of the compression. The normalization a depends on the hypothetical rate; this cancellation is not deduced for the trace of the original monomial matrix.

**Exact threshold for detecting a proportion of negative eigenvalues with fixed margin.** Work in the winning normalization a=r−f, x=aV, τ=ω/a, with d=⌊Bk⌋. If H=exp(−fV)D(V)=2m cos(τx)+o(1), the compression of H to degrees ≤d has o(k) eigenvalues of modulus ≥ε for each ε>0 when B≤B₀=(√(1+τ²)−1)/2. For B>B₀ it has ≥ηk eigenvalues ≤−ε for certain ε,η>0 by the packets of the previous paragraph. Thus B₀ is exact for this detection with margin and density, even at the lower endpoint. Inertia without a modulus threshold may count eigenvalues tending to zero, to which the first statement does not apply.

The second-order piece is a formula for the overlap of the harmonic U=exp(iτx) with the space of polynomials. For each B>0, τ≠0,
lim k⁻¹ ||Π_d U Π_d||²_HS = ∫₀ᴮ Pr{A(y)+2D₀(y)cos θ≤B}dy,
where θ is uniform on [0,2π], A(y)=y+τ²(2y+1) and D₀(y)=|τ|√(1+τ²)√(y(1+y)). The squared norm sums the squared moduli of all entries in an orthonormal basis. In particular it measures the compression directly and keeps the cross terms lost in the previous trace.

Proof. In L² of the gamma of rate 1 and shape k+1, the number operator N is diagonal with value j on the orthonormal Laguerre polynomial of degree j. Its differential expression is −x∂²−(k+1−x)∂. Conjugating by U gives
N′=U*NU=N+τ²x−iτ(2x∂+k+1−x).
The identity holds on each polynomial: integration by parts against each Laguerre gives the coefficients of the differential operator applied to U times the polynomial, which is square integrable, and by Parseval this verifies the domain of the diagonal operator. Successive applications of N′ again produce polynomials. In the Laguerre basis, x has diagonal 2j+k+1 and real links of modulus √((j+1)(j+k+1)) by its recurrence. The operator 2x∂+k+1−x has zero diagonal and antisymmetric links of the same modulus by the dilation generator of the previous paragraph. Thus N′ is Hermitian tridiagonal. Its diagonal at j is j+τ²(2j+k+1) and the modulus of the upper link is |τ|√(1+τ²)√((j+1)(j+k+1)). The links can be made positive by diagonal phases.

For j/k→y>0, each fixed moment of the spectral measure of N′/k at the vector j is a finite sum of closed paths with steps 0,±1. In a neighbourhood of fixed radius of j, the coefficients divided by k tend to A(y),D₀(y). The limit moments are therefore those of the constant operator on the integers, that is those of A(y)+2D₀(y)cos θ by Fourier series. The limit law is compact and determined by moments; the higher even moments bound tails and justify weak convergence. It has no atom at B for y>0. The mass up to d/k is consequently convergent, even if B is an endpoint of the support. That mass is exactly ||Π_d U e_j||², by spectral conjugation. Integrating the step functions j=⌊ky⌋ using dominated convergence (values between zero and one) gives the formula.

The lower endpoint of the local support is (√((1+τ²)y)−|τ|√(1+y))². It decreases to zero at y=τ² and then grows. If B<τ² the minimum on [0,B] is at B, and there it is strictly less than B exactly when τ²<4B(B+1). If B≥τ² there is already a piece of positive measure with lower endpoint <B. At equality it only touches at the endpoint of the interval, so the limiting overlap is positive exactly for B>B₀. For B≤B₀ the HS norm of the compressed cosine is o(√k) by U and U*. The bounded o(1) remainder has compressed operator norm o(1) by escape from compact sets and therefore HS norm o(√k). The sum of squares of the eigenvalues of the normalized form is o(k), proving the counting bound. For B>B₀ the packet construction had negative margin in the coefficients and a synthesis operator of bounded norm, also after projecting. The min-max principle then gives the stated fixed spectral margin. The verification of the threshold does not by itself estimate the arithmetic entries at arbitrary slope.

**The square of the deficit over the ordinary primes: exact diagonal to o(1) and suppression of short additive distances.** Let w_p=(log p)p^(−1/2)g_s(V−log p), s²=cV, with c>0 fixed in the previous range. For 1≤H≤√V, the sum over distinct ordered pairs with |p−q|≤H is O_c(H/√V); the diagonal equals √V/(2√(πc))+o(1). Both estimates are unconditional, without choosing a spectral frequency.

For the diagonal apply Abel with θ(x)=x+O_A(x/(1+log x)^A) to the weight (log x)g_s(V−log x)^2/x. With t=log x, the main term is ∫t g_s(V−t)^2 dt=V/(2√π s) extending to the whole line with exponential error. On V/2≤t≤2V, the integral of the error is bounded by O_A(V^(−A)) times the integral of (1+t+t|V−t|/s²)g_s²; outside, the Gaussian tails dominate. A=2 suffices for error o(1).

In the central range split p into [X,2X], X dyadic. For even h≤H the upper sieve for two linear forms gives # {p∈[X,2X]: p+h prime} ≪ X S(h)/log²X, S(h)=∏_{ℓ|h,ℓ>2}(1+1/(ℓ−2)). Indeed the sieve avoids two classes per prime except for divisors of h, where it avoids one; sieving up to a small fixed power of X gives the indicated product by Mertens. The sieve constant is uniform in h (here h≤√V≪log X). Odd h contribute no central pairs. Expanding the squarefree product gives Σ_{h≤H} S(h) ≤ H∏_{ℓ>2}(1+1/[ℓ(ℓ−2)])=O(H). [Upper sieve, Tao–Teräväinen](https://doi.org/10.1112/jlms.12663)

In that block w_pw_{p+h}≪_c log²X/(XV) exp(−(V−log X)²/(2cV)); the bounded shifts in log are absorbed by widening the Gaussian. Summing over blocks leaves O_c(H/√V). For the tails use all integers: in the cell m≤log p<m+1 the sum of 1/p is O(1), the second Gaussian factor is ≤1/√(2πcV), and log(p+h)≤m+1+log(1+H). The first Gaussian already provides exponential decay when summing m outside the central range. The factor two from the order of the pair does not change the bound.

Thus, fixing for example H=⌊V^(1/3)⌋, the purely arithmetic expression
R_c(V)=Σ_{|p−q|>H} w_pw_q−2I Q_c+I²+√V/(2√(πc))
satisfies R_c(V)=(I−Q_c)^2+o(1) in absolute error, despite the size of its summands. To close it would suffice that at each rational width 0<c≤.001 there were a subsequence V→∞ with ∫_V^{V+1}R_c(u)du bounded above, evaluating H,I,w at u. Under RH those integrals tend to 1/4. If RH fails there is a subcritical open interval with a unique winner and it contains a rational: there e^(−fu)(I−Q_c)=2m cos(ωu)+o(1). The integral of the squared cosine over any length one has minimum 1/2−|sin ω|/(2|ω|)>0, so the unit average of the square grows at least like a constant times exp(2fV). A subsequence of pointwise values of the square is not enough. The signed balance of distant pairs and main terms remains unbounded; no uniformity as c goes down is attributed to the o(1).

**Floor of the centred local balance at the scale of the mean spacing of the primes.** Put s²=cV, h(x)=x^(−1/2)g_s(V−log x) for x>0 and zero elsewhere, μ=Σ_p(log p)h(p)δ_p−h(x)dx. Its total mass is Q_c−I. For H=λV, λ>0 fixed, let
E_H=∬(1−|x−y|/H)_+ dμ(x)dμ(y)=H⁻¹∫_ℝ μ((u,u+H])²du.
The second equality results from the intersection length of two intervals of length H; the measure has finite variation for each V. This cut includes the three contributions of the square with their sign, not only pairs of primes. If θ is the fractional part of λ, for non-integer λ one has
liminf E_H/√V ≥ θ(1−θ)/(2λ√(πc)).
If λ is a positive integer the floor liminf E_H≥1/(2π) holds. Both are unconditional for fixed c. Poisson statistics for the primes are not presupposed.

Restrict the non-negative integral to the band J: |t−V|≤V^{2/3}, t=log u. Write W(u)=[t h(u)]², N(u)=π(u+H)−π(u), ν(u)=H/t. Freezing the weights on each interval gives μ((u,u+H])=√W(u)[N(u)−ν(u)+O(poly(V)exp(−V+V^{2/3}))]. Indeed the logarithmic derivatives with respect to t of h and th are bounded in the band and the variation of t is O(H/u); N≤H+1 suffices. The error after squaring and integrating with 1/H is o(1), since ∫_J W du=∫_J t²g_s²dt=O_c(V^{3/2}).

For each integer n, (n−ν)²≥α(n−ν)+{ν}(1−{ν}), α=1−2{ν}, by (n−⌊ν⌋)(n−⌊ν⌋−1)≥0. The weighted linear term satisfies
H⁻¹∫_J W α (N−ν)du=o(1).
In detail, put b=Wα in the band and zero outside. For V large there is at most one interior jump of α, at t=V if λ is an integer. By Fubini the first term after dividing by H is Σ_p H⁻¹∫_{p−H}^p b(u)du. Replacing the average by b(p) costs o(1): away from the jumps |b′(u)|≤poly(V)/u², and the O(H+1) samples next to each jump cost O(poly(V)exp(−V+V^{2/3})). Summing the derivative error even over all integers from exp(V−V^{2/3}) gives o(1). Now the PNT with remainder O_A(x/log^A x) for π−li gives Σ_p b(p)=∫ b(u)du/log u+o(1). By partial summation on each piece, x|b′(x)|dx and the jumps multiplied by x have integrals or sums of polynomial size in V, so it suffices to take A fixed sufficiently large. The last integral coincides with that of Wαν/H. It is important that the PNT is only used here AFTER integrating in u, never on an individual window of length H.

There remains the floor H⁻¹∫_{|t−V|≤V^{2/3}} t²g_s(V−t)²{H/t}(1−{H/t})dt + o(1). For non-integer λ the fractional part tends uniformly to θ and ∫g_s²=1/(2√π s). For integer λ, the fractional factor is λ|t−V|/V+O_λ((t−V)²/V²). On multiplying by t²/H the main term is |t−V| and the integrated error is O_c,λ(V^(−1/2)). The identity ∫|t−V|g_s²dt=1/(2π) and the Gaussian tail give the second floor.

In particular for an already proved supercritical width, (Q_c−I)²→1/4. If λ is not an integer, the complementary contribution with kernel 1−(1−|x−y|/H)_+ must then be negative of order at least √V in modulus. That complement includes part of the short pairs through the ramp of the kernel. At integer λ the floor 1/(2π)<1/4 does not force that sign. The local argument does not compute the complementary term at arbitrary widths.

**Isolated jumps of the count: exact order also when λ is an integer.** For the same centred triangular kernel and H=λV one has E_H ≍_{λ,c} √V for EACH fixed λ>0. The floor 1/(2π) at the integers only measured the variation of the local mean; the jumps at the primes force a contribution of larger order. An exact asymptotic coefficient is not obtained.

To see this, fix 0<δ<min(.01,λ/10), which will be reduced once. In each dyadic block [X,2X) contained in |log x−V|≤s, call p good if there is no other prime p+h with 0<|h|≤2δV nor a prime p+h with |h−H|≤2δV. This also counts companions from outside the block. For the non-zero shifts treated, the upper sieve of the previous paragraph costs per h at most C X S(|h|)/log²X (for negative h the block can be translated by O(V); the same order is kept). On each interval of shifts of length O(δV) in |h|≤(λ+1)V, the sum of S is O(δV)+O_λ((log(2V))^C). Indeed expand S(n)=Σ_{d|n}g(d) over odd squarefree divisors, with g(d)=∏_{ℓ|d}1/(ℓ−2). The length/d part is summed by the convergent product Σg(d)/d; the error per divisor is paid by ∏_{2<ℓ≤(λ+1)V}(1+1/(ℓ−2)), of polylogarithmic size by Mertens. The implied constant of the linear term is absolute. By PNT there are (1+o(1))X/log X primes in the block. Since log X/V→1 uniformly there, choosing δ sufficiently small guarantees ≫X/log X good primes per block for all large V.

The intervals (p−δV,p+δV) of the good primes are disjoint by construction. On the two halves of each one, N(u)=π(u+H)−π(u) takes two consecutive values: the only jump is the exit of p at the centre. Indeed there is no other nearby exit nor nearby entry q−H. Freezing at p the two weights and H/log p as before costs o(1) in the normalized count, uniformly even using N≤H+1 and the exponentially small variation in p. The sum of the squares of the distances of two consecutive integers to any real number is ≥1/2, and with o(1) perturbations in both distances it is still ≥1/2−o(1) by the difference between them. Thus the integral of μ((u,u+H])² over the interval of p is ≥(1/2−o(1))δV W(p). There W(p)≫_c V/X because g_s²≫1/(cV) and log p∼V. The good primes of each block contribute ≫_c 1 to Σ W(p), and there are ≍_c √V complete blocks. Dividing by H gives the stated floor.

For the ceiling separate the two positive measures: (A−B)²≤A²+B² in each window. The triangular prime-prime mass is ≤ the diagonal plus the distinct pairs at distance ≤λV. The dyadic proof of the previous sieve bound still gives O_c(H/√V) up to H=λV, because in the central bands H=O_λ(log X) and the tails only cost a polynomial in V. The diagonal is O_c(√V). For the continuous measure, Cauchy–Schwarz in each window and Fubini give at most H∫ h(x)²dx=H/(2√π s). Hence E_H=O_{c,λ}(√V).

At every fixed supercritical width, the contribution of the complementary kernel is (Q_c−I)²−E_H=−Θ_{λ,c}(√V), also when one, two or any fixed integer number of mean spacings is chosen. At arbitrary widths, the same identity and the local ceiling show that if the square grows exponentially along a sequence, that growth lies in the complement. The sign of the complement at those widths remains open.

**Localization of the excess in a covariance of contiguous intervals of exponential length.** For the centre v and the previous signed measure μ_v, let A_H(u;v)=μ_v((u,u+H]) and J_H(v)=H⁻¹∫A_H(u;v)A_H(u+H;v)du. A failure of RH forces, at each subcritical width with a unique winner (rate f>0), the following: for EACH large V there is a dyadic integer length H, fixed over the whole range of centres [V,V+1], such that
∫_V^{V+1}J_H(v)dv ≫_c exp(2fV)/V,
and 2fV−O_c(log V) ≤ log H ≤ (2+5c/4−2f)V+O_c(log V).
The required sign is positive. These are two contiguous additive intervals in the variable of the primes; it differs from the coercivity of contiguous windows in the support parameters of P38/C6.

Indeed, A_{2H}(u)=A_H(u)+A_H(u+H). By expansion and translation invariance, J_H=E_{2H}−E_H, |J_H|≤E_H. Any interval of length H contains at most H+1 integers. Cauchy–Schwarz and Fubini on the prime contribution, and the continuous estimate of the previous paragraph, give E_H≤(H+1)Σ w_p²+H∫h²≪_c(H+1)√v for H≥1. On the other hand |1−(1−|x−y|/H)_+|≤(x+y)/H on the positive support, so |E_H−(Q_c−I)²|≤2||μ_v||_{TV}∫x d|μ_v|/H. Each of the absolute moments of order l=0,1 is ≤poly_c(v) exp(((l+1/2)+(c/2)(l+1/2)²)v). To see this, majorize the primes by all integers and group log n in unit cells: the sum is bounded by the masses of exp((l+1/2)t)g_s(v−t) with a polynomial factor and shifts of at most one unit, which only change the bound by a constant factor after completing the square. The continuous integral is computed with the same Gaussian. Thus the error is ≤poly_c(v)exp((2+5c/4)v)/H; |J_H| also has that bound up to a constant by comparing E_H and E_{2H} with the same square.

Take L=⌈3V/log 2⌉. For 0<c≤.001, E_{2^L}(v) differs exponentially little from the total square uniformly on [V,V+1]. At a width with a unique winner the unit integral of that square is ≫_c exp(2fV) by the minimum of the integral of the squared cosine. By contrast E_1≪_c√V. Telescoping the integrals of J_{2^j}, 0≤j<L, and dividing by L=O(V) gives the stated length. The two previous absolute bounds force simultaneously the lower and upper limits on log H.

To close it would therefore suffice to bound by exp(o(V)) the positive part of the maximum of those O(V) integrals along some subsequence of V for each fixed rational c in the range. It is a sufficient condition: it has not been shown that each covariance is subexponential under RH, nor that large covariances of opposite signs must be small separately. The identity localizes a mandatory signal; its arithmetic bound remains pending.

**Converse of the contiguous covariance criterion.** Under RH one has sup_{H≥1} E_H(v)≪_c(1+v)^A for some absolute A, at each fixed c and v≥1. Thus |J_H(v)| also has a simultaneous polynomial bound at every length H. The sufficient criterion of the previous paragraph (subexponential positive maximum over the O(V) scales, along a subsequence for each rational c) is equivalent to the global sign. This direction uses a classical conditional result; it does not produce an unconditional bound on the correlations.

Detail of the transfer of Selberg's theorem. Under RH one has ∫_X^{2X}|ψ(u+θu)−ψ(u)−θu|²du≪X²θ log²(2/θ) for 1/X≤θ≤1. For a fixed length t, 0<t≤X/16 and u in a block comparable with X, one gets ∫|ψ(u+t)−ψ(u)−t|²du≪tX log²(2X). Indeed for bounded t it suffices to count O(1) integers per interval and integrate each indicator over length t. For t larger than a constant, average the identity Δ_t(u)=Δ_{t+h}(u)−Δ_h(u+t) over t≤h≤2t after applying |a−b|²≤2|a|²+2|b|². In each double integral change the length to θ by the left endpoint: the Jacobian is O(X) and θ runs over a band of size O(t/X) at height ≍t/X. Enlarging the positive region to dyadic blocks and applying the relative bound gives, after dividing by t, O(tX log²(2X)). Only left endpoints between X−X/16 and 2X are needed for a piece supported in [X,2X]; the constants of the blocks do not affect the argument. [Zaccagnini, §3.2, formula (8)](https://www.rivmat.unipr.it/fulltext/2016-7-1/pdf/6_Zaccagnini.pdf)

The same bound with log⁴(2X) holds for the function θ_pr of first-power primes. In [X/2,3X] there are O(√X log(2X)) integer powers with exponents ≥2 counting representations; in an interval of length t there are O(log(2X)(1+t/√X)), since for each exponent those powers are separated by ≫√X. Integrating the sum of their indicators costs t per power; majorize the square by the local maximum times that sum, with two factors log(2X) for the weights. The cost is O(tX log⁴(2X)) for t≤X.

Apply a smooth partition of unity with pieces at geometric scales X, support [X,2X] and derivative O(1/X), plus a bounded initial piece. For b=h_v times the piece, put M_X=sup(|b|+X|b′|). Let Δ_t(u) be the centred increment of θ_pr. When H≤X/16, integrating by parts on (u,u+H] gives b(u+H)Δ_H(u)−∫₀ᴴ b′(u+t)Δ_t(u)dt. The relevant interval of u lies in [X−H,2X]. By Minkowski and the additive lemma, its L²(du) norm divided by √H is ≪M_X√X log²(2X)(1+H/X). If H>X/16, any subinterval of the support has weighted integral against dθ_pr−dx of modulus ≪M_X√X log²(2X) by partial integration and the pointwise bound under RH for θ_pr−x. The length of the support in u is O(X+H)=O(H), which gives the same normalized bound. The initial piece contributes to the normalized norm at most its total variation, by Minkowski applied to each mass.

Finally M_X√X is bounded by the supremum on the logarithmic cell of g_s(v−t)(1+|v−t|/(cv)) times a constant. On summing over the cells with the factor log²(2X) one gets O_c((1+v)²) for large v by the Gaussian moments (the suprema can be majorized by widening the Gaussian by a fixed factor). Therefore even E_H(v)≪_c(1+v)^4 uniformly in H≥1. Knowing the rate or the height of a possible zero is not required to define the arithmetic maximum.

**Exact rate of a boundary part at a single length and fixed width.** Fix a single c∈(0,.001], even c=.001. At X=2^n, v=log X and H=X, define F_X(y)=∫_{(0,y]} h_v(x)(dθ_pr(x)−dx) and B_X=X⁻¹∫_{X/4}^X |F_X(y)|²dy. It is a positive part of E_X(v): in the sliding-interval formula only the starts u=y−X≤0 are taken. If Θ=sup_ρ Re ρ, then
limsup_{n→∞} log(1+B_{2^n})/log(2^n) = 2Θ−1.
Thus subpower control of this single observable on ALL sufficiently large dyadic blocks is equivalent to the global sign. The quantifier differs from the previous covariance condition along subsequences. The Gaussian count itself without the moving endpoint may converge to its bias at this same width whatever Θ is; the prefixes retain additional information.

Ceiling.
