Removing the higher powers costs pointwise O(√x) by Chebyshev for squares and trivial counting for exponents ≥3. Hence ∫_[X/2,3X] F(x)² dx≪X². To pass to prime entries divide [X,2X] into cells of length comparable to √X/log²X. The mass of entries in each cell is O(length) by Brun–Titchmarsh with modulus one, and the oscillation of F is O(√X/log X) by counting integers. Compare each sampled value with the quadratic mean of its cell, as in the previous paragraph in the reverse direction. One gets P(X)≪1. Consequently, a subsequence with P(X) bounded by a constant is already equivalent to the sign.

Excluding r=p from F(p/2) changes the root of the average by O(log X/√X) by Chebyshev. For the remaining sum, its diagonal r=s contributes (3/2+o(1))log X unconditionally: uniformly in 2X≤p≤4X, by PNT and partial summation Σ_{p/2<r<p}(log r)² cos²(4πr/p)=(1/4+o(1))p log X, since the integral over [1/2,1] is 1/4. Another application of PNT gives Σ p log p∼6X² in the band. Under RH the ordered contribution r≠s of THREE distinct primes is therefore the negative of the exact diagonal plus O(1). A one-sided upper bound with that precision along a subsequence would suffice by the P criterion. The isolated asymptotic coefficient does not replace the exact diagonal to obtain a bounded remainder.

**It suffices to decide the sign of the triples, without estimating their compensation.** Denote by U(X) the ordered sum of the distinct triples of the previous paragraph with the same weights and normalisation, and by D(X) the diagonal. The identity P_excl=D+U and the exponent criterion give the following dichotomy. Under RH, U(X)/log X→−3/2. If β>1/2, U(X)=X^(2β−1+o(1))>0 for EVERY X sufficiently large: the cost O(log X/√X) of passing from √P to √P_excl is negligible and D=O(log X). Hence U(X)≤0 in arbitrarily high bands suffices. In particular the precision O(1) in compensating the diagonal is a consequence under RH but is not the precision required for the arithmetic proof.

**Exact control of the modular antecedent.** At each exterior prime p replace 2 in cos(2π·2r/p) by k uniform nonzero mod p. For distinct p/2<r,s<p, both r−s and r+s are nonzero mod p. By product-to-sum and orthogonality, the mean of the two multiplied cosines equals −1/(p−1). The mean of U with that substitution per prime is therefore strictly negative when there are pairs. Its limit is −3/2 (without a log X factor): by PNT the internal mass is (1+o(1))p/2 and the quadratic mass O(p log p), so the interior average equals −(1+o(1))p/4 and Σp log p∼6X². The direction-averaging mechanism is already in 233; this computation makes its limitation here precise: it attains the required sign on average, but the identity does not control the fixed frequency k=2 at all primes. Do not use the existence of favourable p-dependent choices as a proof.

**Limit of a modular average preserving frequency 2.** For each exterior prime p choose any distribution ν_p on k mod p and put K_p(r,s)=E_ν cos(2πkr/p)cos(2πks/p). If it is proved that the aggregate contribution of triples with that kernel is ≤0 along a subsequence, and ν_p(2)≥X^(−o(1)) uniformly in its band, the average of squares without endpoint at frequency 2 is ≤X^o(1): the averaged diagonal is O(log X) by Chebyshev, and all squares of the frequencies are nonnegative. AGGREGATE compensation with an average biased towards 2 thus suffices.

However no such choice can make the kernel nonpositive pair by pair, even if only pairs of true PRIMES are required. In A_p={r prime: 11p/12<r<p} one has cos(4πr/p)≥1/2. If K_p(r,s)≤0 for all distinct ones in A_p, then ν_p(2)|A_p|²/4 ≤ E_ν(Σ_{r∈A_p}cos(2πkr/p))² ≤ Σ_{r∈A_p} K_p(r,r) ≤ |A_p|. By PNT this forces ν_p(2)≪log p/p. More generally the ordered sum of the off-diagonal positive parts in that sector is ≥ν_p(2)|A_p|²/4−|A_p|. This rules out proving the aggregate sign through a modular kernel with pointwise sign while keeping subpolynomial mass at the target frequency. It differs from the uniform average of 233 in that the obstacle holds for every distribution, even one depending on the primes of the window.

**Arbitrarily large negative reserve on excluding rational frequencies.** For each constant A>0 a bounded number (depending on A) of frequencies per exterior prime can be eliminated, keeping frequency 2, so that the remaining uniform average of the normalised sum of triples is ≤−A in every sufficiently high band. For each fixed prime d≥13 up to a fixed cut-off D take k the integer nearest to ap/d, 1≤a<d, only when |δ|=|k−ap/d|≤1/6. There are 2 floor(d/6) values per d, since p permutes the nonzero residues. The reduced fractions are distinct and, for p large depending on D, so are the k, and they stay away from 2. By the prime number theorem in progressions of fixed modulus d and partial summation, uniformly over these choices, the interior weighted cosine sum divided by p is
    −(d−1)⁻¹ ∫_[1/2,1] cos(2πδu)du + o_D(1).
Indeed the mean of the additive character e(ar/d) over the units is −1/(d−1); δ takes only finitely many values. The integral is at least 1/4. Each eliminated k contributes to the square at least p²/(25(d−1)²) eventually; its diagonal is O(p log p). Hence the sum of the eliminated triples divided by p−1 is ≥ c p Σ_{13≤d≤D prime}1/d for an absolute constant c and p sufficiently large depending on D. The original mean of all interior triples was already negative. Renormalising among the kept frequencies only intensifies the negative ceiling. Summing the exterior ones as before and using the divergence of the prime reciprocals yields the claim. Compared with antecedent 234, here the losses of many different frequencies are summed for the same triple form. The remaining weight at k=2 stays of order 1/p. Even a normalised reserve O(log X), the maximum possible by positivity of the square and size of the diagonal, would not by itself justify raising that weight to X^(−o(1)) if the contribution of k=2 had power growth.

**Consecutive blocks with favourable sign at the true frequency.** Unconditionally, in arbitrarily high bands [2X,4X] there is a block of ≫√X/log X consecutive exterior primes for each of which the ordered interior sum of distinct triples (k=2) equals −(1/4+o(1))p log p. Use Y(x)=F(x)/√x. Between events its derivative is (F'(x)−F(x)/(2x))/√x<0 eventually, by the cosine drift and F=o(x) by PNT. The exits give negative jumps and the entries positive ones of size log(2x)/√x. By 237 there are arbitrarily high upward passages from negative values up to 1/10. Let b be the first arrival at 1/10 after a negative excursion, and a the last entry crossing zero upwards before that arrival (touching zero included). On [a,b] the values lie between 0 and 1/10+o(1), with Y(a)=O(log a/√a). If b≤2a, the net rise requires ≫√a/log a entries by the maximal jump size, all consecutive within [a,b]. Take X=a. If b>2a, all the entries in [a,2a] serve and number ≫a/log a by PNT. Possible exact contacts with zero do not alter the argument, taking the last step from strictly negative to nonnegative values. On entering p=2x, excluding p changes F by log p, so that the remaining square is O(p) over the whole block. The interior diagonal is (1/4+o(1))p log p uniformly by PNT, as above; subtracting it gives the announced sign. The block is not localised in advance. Its guaranteed cardinality is insufficient for the complete sum over the band.

**When the large entries occupy a positive proportion at extreme scale.** Let β=sup Reρ>1/2. If it is attained, there are c,η>0 such that in EVERY sufficiently high band at least a fraction η of the primes p in [2X,4X] satisfies |F(p/2)|≥c X^β. If it is not attained, for each c>0 that fraction tends to zero. The threshold is of exact order X^β.

Proof in the continuous variable. In a band of fixed ratio, write x=X exp v and normalise by X^β. The part |γ|>G of the explicit formula for F_ψ has L²(dv) norm uniformly small as G grows: in the block argument already used under RH, each coefficient now carries X^(Reρ−β)≤1 and a factor exp(v Reρ). The smooth cut-off in the product of two terms still has two uniformly bounded derivatives for 0≤Reρ+Reρ'≤2. The quadratic bound of the tail is therefore O(Σ_{n≥G−2} log²(2+n)/(1+n)²), uniform in X. The higher powers cost o(1) in this normalisation. If β is not attained, the remaining finite sum tends to zero, giving L² convergence to zero. If it is attained, on the interior band [1.2X,1.5X] the filter of 230 with FIXED support and norms applied as in 236 to an extreme zero gives a fixed lower L² norm l>0 by H(ρ₀)≠0 and Cauchy–Schwarz. To verify that there is positive measure above a fixed threshold, truncate with a tail of norm <l/4; the finite part is uniformly bounded by M_G. On the set where |F|/X^β≥c, the norm of F/X^β is ≥3l/4 on choosing c small, hence the finite part there has norm ≥l/2 for X large (absorbing the remainders). The measure of the set is ≥(l/(2M_G))². The measures dv and dx/X are comparable.

Passage to primes. In the attained case partition the interior band as for P(X) into cells of length comparable to X^a with (1+β)/3<a<β. The cells touching the good set occupy length ≫X, the oscillation of F is o(X^β) by counting integers and each cell contributes entry mass comparable to its length. In the non-attained case use on [X,2X] cells of length comparable to √X/log²X; Brun–Titchmarsh bounds their entry mass by O(length) and the oscillation is still o(X^β). The cells with a large entry occupy only o(X) by the continuous L² ceiling. Convert log p weights to cardinalities by PNT. In particular, in the attained case a positive proportion of primes has positive triple contribution of order at least X^(2β), since the diagonal only costs O(X log X). In the other case the result does not give the sign at the much smaller threshold √(X log X).

**Quantitative tail of the sign per exterior prime under RH.** In [2X,4X], for all V≥1 and X sufficiently large, the fraction of entries with |F(p/2)|>V√X is O(exp(−c√V)) under RH, with uniform constants. In particular, except for a fraction O(exp(−c'(log X)^(1/4))), the interior contribution of distinct triples is ≤−p log p/10.

In the formula for F(X exp v)/√X of the previous paragraph, under RH the part with |γ|≤G is O(log²(2G)) uniformly in 0≤v≤log 2 by absolute summation. The non-spectral remainder, including prime powers, is O(1). The integrated quadratic norm of the spectral tail is O(log²(2G)/G) by the blocks of the same paragraph. Choose G=exp(d√V) with fixed d small enough that the head and the non-spectral remainder cost ≤V/4 for V large. Chebyshev gives relative measure O(log²(2G)/(G V²)) for |F(x)|>V√X/2 on [X,2X]. To sample it is not necessary to differentiate the zero polynomial: on cells of length comparable to √X/log²X the oscillation of the complete F costs O(√X/log X). Hence any cell containing an entry above V√X is contained in the continuous set at half the threshold. Brun–Titchmarsh and PNT convert relative length into a fraction of primes as before. Larger constants cover bounded V. Take V=√(log X)/5. At the remaining entries the square after excluding the endpoint costs ≤(V√X+log(4X))², while the diagonal is (1/4+o(1))p log p with p≥2X. Subtracting gives the stated margin. This conditional distributional prediction proves no additional cancellation for primes without RH.

**Criterion by counting alone, discarding extreme values.** Fix any 0<η<1, for example η=1/100. Order the moduli |F(p/2)| of the band in decreasing order and take the one of rank ceil(X^(1−η)), called Q_η(X); the band has more primes than that rank eventually by PNT. One has
    log(1+Q_η(X)/√X)/log X → B.
Indeed the pointwise ceiling of 236 gives the limsup. If β=1/2+B>1/2, the paragraph on the discrete average gives for each 0<δ<B at least X^(1−o(1)) entries above X^(β−δ), more than the rank fixed in power for all large X. This gives the liminf on sending δ to zero. For B=0 nonnegativity suffices. The same formula holds when ordering the root of the positive part of the interior triple sum: excluding p costs log p and the diagonal is O(X log X), negligible at the threshold X^(β−δ).

In particular it suffices that along a subsequence there be at most X^0.99 primes with strictly positive interior triple sum (use for example rank X^0.995). Here it is not necessary to evaluate how large those terms are. The statement with the alternative logarithmic threshold is moreover biconditional: the global sign is equivalent to having, in arbitrarily high bands, at most X^0.99 primes with |F(p/2)|>√X log³X. Under RH none exceeds that ceiling eventually by the pointwise bound O(√X log²X) from partial summation in 235; if it fails there are more than the quota by the above. The conditional limit exp(−c(log X)^(1/4)) for the fraction at the sign threshold is weaker than a fixed power saving; it does not establish the necessity of the counting criterion at threshold zero. This is a consequence of the cardinality bound already recorded, not an arithmetic mechanism to prove it.

**Cubic weight on a half window: counting criterion at threshold zero in both directions.** Define w(u)=(u−1)(2−u)(u−3/2) on [1,2], zero outside, and F_w(x)=Σ_r(log r)w(r/x) over primes. At the endpoint x=p/2 the exterior prime has weight zero. The ordered sum U_p of triples with distinct internal elements is F_w(p/2)² minus its diagonal D_p. By PNT D_p∼p log p/1680: with v=u−1, ∫₀¹v²(1−v)²(v−1/2)²dv=1/840. Under RH U_p∼−p log p/1680 for ALL large primes. If RH fails there are p with U_p>0 numbering X^(1−o(1)) in EACH band [2X,4X]. Hence ≤X^0.99 exceptions to the sign in arbitrarily high bands is now necessary and sufficient.

Detection details. The mean of w is zero by antisymmetry. For H(s)=∫₁²u^(s−1)w(u)du, two integrations by parts give s(s+1)H(s)= (2^(s+1)−1)/2+∫₁²u^(s+1)w''(u)du, because w'(1)=w'(2)=−1/2. Another integration bounds the last term by 100/|s+2| in the critical strip (|w''|≤3, |w'''|=6). The main term has modulus ≥(2^1.5−1)/2 in the right half; Z2 covers all heights ≤400. Thus H annihilates no right zero and H(ρ)=O((1+|γ|)⁻²). Under RH the explicit formula converges absolutely, giving F_w(x)=O(√x) after removing prime powers as above. In general the same argument gives O(x^β), β=sup Reρ. For each target zero with real part β₀>1/2, apply exactly the FIXED filter of 230/236 to F_w on [1.2X,1.5X]: the nonzero coefficient H(ρ₀) survives, giving ∫|F_w|² dx≫X^(1+2β₀). To transfer that energy to primes use the cells of length X^a of the preceding discrete average, choosing β₀ arbitrarily close to β and above a. The oscillation on a cell costs O(X^a log X) by Lipschitz and counting, hence X⁻²Σ log p |F_w(p/2)|²=X^(2β−1+o(1)). At the entries with U_p≤0 the square is O(X log X), at the others O(X^(2β)); comparing contributions gives the announced count. The smoothing mechanism has an antecedent in 247; the improvement over the cosine count refers to the same sign threshold zero for half-window triples, with a uniform per-prime margin under RH. There is still no arithmetic proof of the count.

**Sparse sampling robust to the choice of representatives.** For the preceding cubic, fix 0<η<1/4 and divide [2X,4X] into N=ceil(X^η) equal cells. Choose ONE arbitrary exterior prime per cell (for example the first; they exist by 238, since the length exceeds X^(3/4)). Under RH all the sampled signs are negative eventually. If there is an exterior zero, for EVERY choice of representatives there are N^(1−o(1)) positive signs in each high band.

The specific step is an oscillation estimate that the cosine with jumps does not satisfy by the same argument. Between entry or exit points, xF'_w(x)=−Σ log r (r/x)w'(r/x). The continuous part of that sum is zero since ∫₁²uw'(u)du=[uw]₁²−∫w=0. The function uw' has bounded variation including the endpoints. By partial summation against θ(y)−y and the ceiling of 235, |F'_w(x)|≪_ε X^(β−1+ε) on the band. F_w is continuous at the events because w vanishes at both endpoints; integrating this bound across them is legitimate by piecewise regularity. Each cell then induces error O_ε(X^(β−η+ε)) on sampling F_w(p/2). For β>1/2, the continuous mean of |F_w|² over [X,2X] is X^(2β+o(1)) by the fixed filter applied to each β₀ approaching β and the absolute ceiling of the previous paragraph. By the L² triangle inequality, the root of the discrete mean of the N squares differs from the root of the continuous one by O_ε(X^(β−η+ε)), negligible on choosing ε<η/2. Each square costs O(X^(2β)); those of nonpositive sign only O(X log X). Dividing the remaining energy by the individual maximum gives N X^(−o(1))=N^(1−o(1)) positive signs uniformly in the representatives. In particular it suffices to control the sign at the first primes of the cells in arbitrarily high bands, tolerating N^(1−δ) exceptions for any fixed δ>0. The same result is not deduced for subpolynomial N. This reduces the number of samples while keeping the dichotomy; it does not establish their signs.

**What fraction keeps the favourable sign if there are finitely many extreme zeros.** Suppose β>1/2 is attained at m distinct zeros (counting conjugates, not multiplicities), with m finite. Then the fraction of primes p∈[2X,4X] with U_p≤0 for the cubic weight tends to zero in EVERY band, even without a spectral gap. If moreover all other zeros have real part ≤σ with 1/2≤σ<β, their NUMBER is O_ε(X^(1−(β−σ)/(m−1)+ε)).

Indeed for x=X exp v, divide F_w(x) by x^β. The explicit formula gives a real exponential polynomial S_X(v)=−Σ_j d_j H(ρ_j)exp(iγ_j(log X+v)) plus a uniform error o(1): in the absolutely convergent series of the other zeros each normalised term tends to zero and is dominated by O((1+|γ|)⁻²). With a gap the error is O(X^(σ−β)) including prime powers. The sign U_p≤0 forces |S_X(log(p/(2X)))|≤t_X with t_X=o(1), or t_X≪_ε X^(σ−β+ε) with a gap, by the ceiling of the diagonal.

The sublevel sets |S_X|≤t in [0,log 2] are covered by a bounded number of intervals of total length O(t^(1/(m−1))), uniformly in X for small t. At each point some derivative of order between 0 and m−1 has modulus ≥c>0: invert the Vandermonde matrix of the iγ_j, using that |d_j H(ρ_j)| are positive constants. The derivatives up to m are bounded, so on each cell of a sufficiently fine fixed partition a derivative of order k keeps modulus ≥c/2. For k=0 the sublevel set is empty. For k≥1 Rolle gives at most k solutions to each equation S_X=±t and hence O(k) components; k equally spaced finite differences on each component of length l force (c/2)(l/k)^k≤2^k t. This proves the ceiling. The intervals in p have total length O(X t^(1/(m−1))). With a gap counting integers suffices. Without a gap enlarge the short intervals to length √X and apply Brun–Titchmarsh to each one: the fraction of primes costs O(t_X^(1/(m−1))+X^(−1/2)). For infinitely many extreme zeros the finite Vandermonde inversion fails. This conclusion distinguishes a majority in the band from the unconditional blocks previously proved for another weight.

**Majority without assuming a spectral maximum, on smoothing at logarithmic scale.** Replace the compact weight by k(y)=(1−y)exp(−y²/2)/√(2π) with y=log(r/x). Write S(x)=Σ_r log r k(log(r/x)), D(x)=Σ_r(log r)²k(log(r/x))², U(x)=S(x)²−D(x). Here ALL the internal primes intervene; U sums distinct pairs (one can also exclude the exterior prime p at x=p/2, at cost O(log p) in S). The bilateral transform is K(s)=(1−s)exp(s²/2), which kills the pole and kills no zeros. By PNT D(x)∼c x log x with c=∫k(y)²e^y dy>0 (truncate the tails by Chebyshev on dyadic bands). Under RH U(p/2)<0 eventually for every p. If β>1/2, attained or not, in EACH band [2X,4X] the fraction of primes with U(p/2)≤0 tends to zero.

Justification of the quantitative analyticity. For complex v in any fixed disc |v|≤R, Mellin on Re s=2 for the Λ weights has integrand (−ζ'/ζ)(s)K(s)(Xe^v)^s. Move to Re s=−1/2 through good heights as in 247; the Gaussian dominates exp(R|Im s|) and all polynomial factors, the remaining line costs O_R(X^(−1/2)). What remains is −Σρ K(ρ)X^ρ exp(ρv) counting multiplicities. Removing higher powers costs O_R(√X) uniformly: |k(log(n/X)−v)|≪_R exp(−log²(n/X)/4), and up to Y the mass of powers of order ≥2 is O(√Y) by Chebyshev and counting for orders ≥3. Hence sup_{|v|≤R}|S(X exp v)|≪_R X^β. On any fixed interior interval of v, the filter of 230 of mass one, multiplied by exp(−ρ₀v), isolates each right target of real part β₀ and kills the others with real part ≥σ chosen between 1/2 and β₀. The error of the smaller zeros costs O(X^σ) by absolute convergence. Thus sup_{0≤v≤log 2}|S(X exp v)|≥c_(ρ₀)X^β₀ for all large X.

If a fixed fraction η of the primes is favourable along a subsequence, there |S(p/2)|≪√(X log X). For n=floor(a log X), a>0 fixed, one can choose n of those nodes v=log(p/(2X)) separated by at least d_η/n: each exclusion of radius d_η/n removes O(d_η X/(n log X)) primes by Brun–Titchmarsh; take d_η small and select greedily. The sum of moduli of the basic interpolation polynomials over [0,log 2] is ≤(n/d_η)^(n−1)2^(n−1)/(n−1)!≤C_η^n by the factorials of the ordered gaps. The interpolation error on the disc |v|≤4 costs O(X^β 2^(−n)) by the Cauchy formula with nodal product (on the circle each denominator exceeds 3 and each real numerator is less than 1). Hence the real maximum costs O(C_η^n √(X log X)+X^β 2^(−n)). If β>1/2, choosing a small leaves BOTH exponents strictly below β, contradicting the floor when a zero sufficiently close to the supremum is chosen. Thus a positive fraction of favourable signs along a subsequence suffices for this weight. The interpolation has an explicit antecedent in 242; the contribution here is the majority criterion over primes for the sign of pairs, even without attained abscissa. It does not transfer this majority to the compactly supported cubic.

**An inverse fraction of any fixed power of log X already suffices for the Gaussian weight.** For fixed A>0, it would suffice that along a sequence of bands there were ≥X/(log X)^(A+1) exterior primes with U(p/2)≤0. Equivalently, if an exterior zero exists, the number of those primes is o(X/(log X)^M) for each fixed M. The quantitative hypothesis refers to the same Gaussian S of the previous entry and allows the good nodes to be concentrated.

Put t=log X, R=t^(1/4). The majorant on the growing disc is X^β exp(O(R²+R+1)): in the explicit formula each spectral term costs O(X^β(1+|γ|)exp(R+R|γ|−γ²/2)) and the sum pays exp(O(R²)) by Z3 and completing the square. On the line −1/2 the same Gaussian computation costs X^(−1/2)exp(O(R²+R)); for the prime powers, |k(y−v)|≪exp(O(R²+1))exp(−y²/4) for |v|≤R, by the quadratic inequality, and the preceding dyadic count applies. All the extra growth is exp(o(t)).

Choose n=floor(a t/log t) with fixed a>0. By Brun–Titchmarsh one chooses n good nodes separated in log by d/(n t^A), with absolute d sufficiently small: the physical length of each exclusion is O(X d/(n t^A)), with logarithm asymptotic to t, and n exclusions cost less than the assumed quota. The factorial interpolation of 242 costs at most (C t^A)^n=exp((aA+o(1))t) on values of size O(√(X log X)). The Cauchy remainder on the circle of radius R costs X^β exp(o(t))(R−1)^(−n)=X^(β−a/4+o(1)). If β>1/2, choosing aA<β−1/2 makes both exponents strictly less than β. The spectral floor of the previous paragraph contradicts this ceiling along the subsequence. For the little-o conclusion, apply the criterion with a slightly larger logarithmic exponent. The argument does not offer a fixed power saving in X for the number of favourable signs with a non-attained supremum.

**Power saving for the Gaussian count if an extreme zero exists.** If β>1/2 is attained, there exists κ>0 such that in every sufficiently high band there are O(X^(1−κ)) favourable exterior primes U(p/2)≤0. Infinitely many zeros on Re s=β are allowed and no gap below is required. The constant κ is existential.

Let f_X(v)=X^(−β)S(X exp v). On |v|≤4 it is uniformly bounded by the preceding explicit formula, and its supremum over [0,log 2] is ≥c>0 by the FIXED filter isolating a zero of real part exactly β. There are an integer L≥1 and b>0 such that for all large X and all v of that segment, max_{0≤j≤L}|f_X^(j)(v)|≥b. If this failed, there would be X_n→∞ and v_n→v_* after extraction, with all derivatives up to order n less than 1/n. By normal compactness on the interior disc, a subsequence converges together with each derivative on compacts. The limit would have all derivatives zero at v_* and would be identically zero, incompatible with the uniform floor of the supremum. The Cauchy bounds up to L+1 allow a fixed partition where on each cell some real derivative keeps modulus ≥b/2. Applying there the elementary Rolle and difference argument of 2218 (sublevel paragraph for the cubic), the set |f_X|≤t is covered by O(1) intervals of total length O(t^(1/L)). The favourable sign requires t≪X^(1/2−β)√log X. Returning to p, counting even all integers in the intervals gives O(1+X^(1−(β−1/2)/L)(log X)^(1/(2L))). For example κ=(β−1/2)/(2L) works. The argument acts on the exact function and avoids paying for the speed at which the interior zeros attenuate. A favourable count X^(1−o(1)) along a subsequence would thus exclude every exterior maximum, but by itself would not exclude a non-attained supremum.

**Lower bound for favourable Gaussian signs for almost every fixed dilation.** For λ∈[1,2] evaluate U(p/λ) at the exterior primes. The preceding band criteria remain valid for each fixed λ, by change of scale. If β>1/2, for almost every λ there are arbitrarily high bands with a block of ≫X^(3/2−β)/√log X consecutive favourable primes (X the scale, constants allowed). Under RH all are favourable eventually. Indeed S(x) changes sign arbitrarily far out if there is a right zero. Its bilateral Mellin transform in x is K(s)Σ_p(log p)p^(−s) for Re s>1; restricting to x≥1 changes it by an entire function, by Gaussian decay towards zero and Chebyshev. The product has a pole at every right zero and none on the real half-line s>1/2, so Landau excludes both eventual signs as in 236. By continuity there are crossings z→∞ with S(z)=0. Thus on [z,z+H], H=d z^(3/2−β)√log z, d>0 small enough, one has S²≤D/2 by the uniform asymptotics of D; in particular all those arguments are favourable.

For any fixed interval J interior to [1,2], average over λ∈J the number N_z(λ) of primes in [λz,λ(z+H)]. Each prime whose ratio p/z lies in the central half of J contributes length pH/(z(z+H))≍H/z, and PNT counts ≫|J|z/log z of those primes eventually. Hence ∫_J N_z≥c|J|H/log z with absolute c independent of J. Brun–Titchmarsh gives N_z≤C H/log z since H≥√z. Consequently an absolute fraction of J has N_z≥cH/(2 log z). The same holds in measure for the limsup along the crossings, by continuity of measure for unions of tails. Taking rational intervals and applying the Lebesgue density theorem to the complement, that limsup has full measure. All the primes counted are consecutive in a favourable interval for the same λ. The gain is a genuine lower count for the dilated Gaussian detector without attributing to it the crossings of the cosine; for each β>1/2 the exponent obtained is strictly less than one.

**Recurrent crossings in every sufficiently wide band of fixed ratio.** If β>1/2 there exist C>1 and z₀ such that S takes both signs in EACH [X,CX] for X≥z₀, even without a spectral maximum. For 1/2<σ<b₀≤β with a target zero of real part b₀, both extremes, positive and negative, reach modulus ≫X^b₀ in that band (C depends on σ). This gain over the use of Landau comes from combining the positive filter of the separation track with the local floor of 230.

For each ordinate γ>0 of a zero b+iγ with b≥σ use the probability on 0,l=π/γ whose weights are proportional to 1,exp(−bl). Its moment at b±iγ is zero. Ingham's count from 230 implies Σ l=L<∞ over the targets, by dyadic integration with exponent 3(1−σ)/(2−σ)<1. The sum of independent variables with these laws converges absolutely and its law μ is a probability on [0,L] annihilating all targets. Convolving it with the uniform on [0,L+2] gives a positive or zero density h, identically 1/(L+2) on [L,L+2] except at endpoints and supported on [0,2L+2]. The Gaussian explicit formula implies ∫ h(v)S(X exp v)dv=O(X^σ), by absolute convergence of the remaining moments and the O(√X) cost of the powers. On the other hand the fixed filter of 230 applied on [L,L+1] to the target, with fixed sup norm and K(ρ₀)≠0, gives ∫_[L,L+1]|S(X exp v)|dv≫X^b₀. Thus ∫h|S|≫X^b₀. The two identities for positive and negative parts force ∫h S_±≫X^b₀ separately, uniformly in X. Take C=exp(2L+2) and use continuity.

Consequence for the original dilation: if 1/2<β<11/12, the favourable block of the previous paragraph exists in EACH [X,C'X] for λ=2, with ≫X^(3/2−β)/√log X consecutive primes. Indeed around the crossing a length H=d z^(3/2−β)√log z is available to its right; the short PNT cited in 238 applies uniformly because 3/2−β>7/12 with a fixed margin. The same argument holds for each λ∈[1,2]. In the remaining scenarios this step from counting to a prescribed dilation remains pending. Neither the recurrence nor the width of the block gives the sought inverse-logarithmic density.

**The linear Gaussian sum, sampled at the original endpoints.** Under RH, S(x)<−√x/5 eventually for EVERY x. By PNT the term of the removed squares is (K(1/2)/2+o(1))√x=(exp(1/8)/4+o(1))√x (change p=√x u and Gaussian truncation by Chebyshev); orders ≥3 cost o(√x) by the same dyadic cut and the count O(Y^(1/3)log²(2Y)). The contribution of the zeros to S/√x has modulus ≤Σ|K(ρ)|<0.05: for |γ|≥14 one has |ρ|³ exp(1/8−γ²/2)<1, then use the Hadamard identity Σ|ρ|⁻²=2+γ_E−log(4π) of 247 under RH. The square-bias and Hadamard-domination mechanisms are explicit antecedents from 247.

If β>1/2, there exists a fixed C and in EVERY band [2X,2CX] there are X^(1−o(1)) primes p of EACH sign of S(p/2), even when β=1 or it is not attained. Fix σ between 1/2 and β in the preceding recurrence; C depends only on σ and can be kept as the target b₀→β varies. For each sign, ∫ S_±(x)dx/X over [X,CX] is ≫_(b₀) X^b₀ by that proof (the filter density is bounded). Split into cells of length comparable to X^(3/4), with entry mass log p comparable to the length by the short PNT of 238. The oscillation per cell is O(X^(β−1/4)) by Cauchy; the positive part and the negative part are both Lipschitz as functions of the value of S. Thus X⁻¹Σ(log p)S_±(p/2)≫_(b₀) X^b₀ if b₀>β−1/4. Dividing by the individual ceiling O(X^β log X) and letting b₀→β gives the announced cardinality. It therefore suffices to find bands [Y_n,Z_n] with Y_n→∞ and Z_n/Y_n→∞ in which S(p/2)≤0 for ALL primes of the band; neither eventual sign nor magnitude is required. Arithmetically S(p/2)≤0 says that the mean of log(2r/p), with positive weights (log r)exp(−log²(2r/p)/2), is ≥1. The pending step is to establish the comparison in such bands. Large samples of both signs do not ensure samples close to the crossing at scale √X.

**The recurrence of the linear sum contains consecutive blocks of both signs.** If β>1/2, in each [2X,2CX] of the previous result there is a block of X^(1−o(1)) consecutive primes with S(p/2)>0 and another of X^(1−o(1)) with S(p/2)<0. Continuity alone does not give this step from cardinality to consecutiveness.

Indeed let t=log X and f(v)=S(X exp v). On [0,log C] there is a v_X with |f(v_X)|≥X^(β−o(1)): the uniform floor holds for each fixed target b₀<β arbitrarily close to the supremum (or for the endpoint if it is attained). In the disc centred there of radius R=t^(1/4), log sup|f|≤βt+O_C(√t+1) by the previous complex Gaussian bound. Jensen bounds the number of zeros in |v−v_X|≤1+log C, counting multiplicities, by [log sup|f|−log|f(v_X)|]/log(R/(1+log C))=o(t/log t). One may take a slightly smaller radius if a zero falls on the outer circle. If β is attained, the floor is c X^β and using two FIXED radii with ratio 2 gives O(1) zeros directly. Splitting the interval at those real zeros leaves at most 1+o(t/log t) open components. The prime count of each sign is X^(1−o(1)) by the previous entry. The pigeonhole principle preserves the exponent in a single component of each sign, where all the primes are consecutive. In particular, proving only the existence of favourable blocks of X^(1−o(1)) for the LINEAR SIGN would be compatible with an exterior zero; the previous criterion required whole bands of growing ratio. This does not assert equal length for the quadratic sign U.

**Exact arithmetic cancellation when centring the weight at the exterior prime.** Choose x=p/e in the same S (a constant translation of the scale, valid for the linear criterion). With g(y)=exp(−y²/2)/√(2π), a_p=(log p)/p and y=log(r/p), one has exactly
    (log p)/p² · (log r) k(log(er/p)) = −exp(−1/2) a_p a_r y g(y).
It is antisymmetric under exchange of the primes. In particular, UNCONDITIONALLY, for every Y≥2,
    Σ_{p≤Y}(log p)/p² S(p/e) = −J(Y)<0,
    J(Y)=exp(−1/2) Σ_{p≤Y<r} a_p a_r log(r/p)g(log(r/p)).
Every internal pair cancels with its inverse, the diagonal is zero and the tails converge absolutely for the fixed cut. On a band (Y,Z] the sum equals exactly J(Y)−J(Z). At a jump at p, S(p/e)<0 is equivalent to J increasing. This gives an unconditional sign for all prefixes, although the problem requires local information about the jumps.

Moreover J(Y)→exp(−1/2)/2. In coordinates u=log(Y/p)≥0, v=log(r/Y)>0, the two measures with mass a_p converge on each compact set to du and dv by PNT and partial summation. Each strip of length one has mass O(1) uniformly by Chebyshev, also near the first prime. Hence the tails of the product against (u+v)g(u+v) are uniformly negligible by summing over unit squares. The limit integral is ∫₀^∞ s²g(s)ds=1/2. The convergence of J to this constant does not determine the sign of its increments. Despite the change of scale from 2 to e, each multiplicative band is only translated and the spectral sign dichotomy still holds. Do not deduce monotonicity from the representation by positive pairs: when passing a prime, pairs enter and leave the cut.

**Exact separation of the cut error into one and two discrepancy factors.** With the measures on the two sides of the cut from the previous paragraph, write μ_−(du), μ_+(dv) and ν_±=μ_±−Lebesgue on [0,∞); the atom at the cut belongs only to the left side. Put A(Y)=Σ_r (log r)/r · g(log(r/Y)). Then
    exp(1/2)J(Y)−1/2 = A(Y)−1 + R(Y),
    R(Y)=∬ (u+v)g(u+v) dν_−(u)dν_+(v).
Indeed the integral against the continuous measure of the other side is exactly g(u) by −g'(s)=s g(s). Adding the two linear pieces recovers A−1, with no losses at the edges.

If β=sup Reρ<1, then for every ε>0 one has R(Y)≪_ε Y^(2β−2+ε). In particular, for β<3/4 the full two-discrepancy term is o(Y^(−1/2)). To verify this, truncate both coordinates at T=4√log Y; the total masses on unit intervals are O(1) and the Gaussian decay gives error O(Y^(−6)). For 0≤u,v≤T, the cumulative sums of each ν from zero cost O_δ(Y^(β−1+δ)) for every δ>0: partial summation of θ(x)−x=O_δ(x^(β+δ/2)) against 1/x between Y and Y exp(±T); the factor exp(O(T))(1+T) is absorbed into Y^(δ/2). Open or closed endpoints change only O(log Y/(Y exp(−T))). Two Stieltjes integrations by parts bound the rectangle by the product of both suprema times an absolute constant: one adds the value of the kernel at the upper corner, the integrals of its first derivatives along both upper edges and the absolute integral of the mixed derivative; all are uniformly bounded by the Gaussian. Take δ<ε/2. This identifies the linear observable governing any deviation of order Y^(β−1−o(1)) if β<1. It gives neither a sign for A−1 nor a power gain when β=1.

**The oscillation of the cut also detects β=1 in each dyadic band.** Define V(X)=sup_{X≤u,v≤2X}|J(u)−J(v)|. Then log V(X)/log X→β−1, including β=1 and β=1/2. There is no need to estimate R or to know the limit constant of J.

Indeed the exact jumps are ΔJ(p)=−(log p)/p² S(p/e). The uniform ceiling |S|≪X^β and Chebyshev bound the total variation on the band by O(X^(β−1)). For β>1/2, on a fixed interior subinterval of [X/e,2X/e] the filter of 230 gives ∫|S(x)|dx≫_(b₀) X^(1+b₀) for each target real part b₀ sufficiently close to β. No positive filter is needed because the modulus is used. The oscillation estimate O(X^(β−1/4)) on cells of length comparable to X^(3/4), followed by the short PNT as in the entry on both signs, gives Σ_{X<p≤2X}(log p)|S(p/e)|≫_(b₀) X^(1+b₀) for b₀>β−1/4. Thus the total variation is X^(β−1+o(1)). By Jensen as above, S(p/e) changes sign at most O(log X) times on the band, using the same local floor for the maximum and two fixed discs. Within each stretch of constant sign the total variation of J is its net variation and is bounded by V(X), also at the endpoints via one-sided limits. Hence V(X)≥total variation/O(log X). Under RH all jumps are eventually positive and |S(p/e)| is comparable to √X by the bias already proved; PNT gives V(X) comparable to X^(−1/2). For β=1 the formula expresses V(X)=X^(−o(1)) in the logarithmic sense although V→0 by convergence of J.

In particular it suffices to find a sequence with V(X)≤X^(−1/2+o(1)). No control of the individual jumps nor approximation to the absolute value of the limit is required: it suffices to confine J to some vertical interval of that width on a dyadic band. This arithmetic estimate remains open.

**The quadratic error has relatively negligible oscillation even if β=1.** Write osc_X for the range on [X,2X] and Ω=(log X/log log X)^(1/3). There is c>0 such that, for X large,
    osc_X R ≪ exp(−cΩ) osc_X J.
The profile is controlled up to an additive constant, without asserting the same ceiling for |R(X)|. In particular osc_X A=(exp(1/2)+o(1))osc_X J.

Indeed, differentiating the absolutely convergent sum for A(y) gives B(y):=exp(−1/2)A'(y)=−S(y/e)/y². The increments of J are exactly the integral of B against dθ. The Gaussian ceilings on a fixed disc and Cauchy give |B|≪X^(β−2), |B'|≪X^(β−3) uniformly on the band. Split it into cells of length comparable to H=X^(3/4). On each whole cell I, 238 gives |Δθ−|I||≪exp(−c₀Ω)|I|; replacing B by its value at the centre costs O(H X^(β−3)) per unit mass in both measures. Therefore, summing the absolute errors over whole cells, one obtains O(exp(−c₀Ω) ∫|B|dy + X^(β−5/4)). The same computation for |B| (Lipschitz with the same constant) allows that integral to be replaced by O(var_X J + X^(β−5/4)), where var_X J=∫_(X,2X]|B|dθ. In any subinterval at most two partial cells remain; by positivity their prime mass is O(H), so they cost O(X^(β−5/4)). The identity dR=exp(1/2) B(dθ−dy) gives the uniform ceiling for increments. If β>1/2, the previous Jensen argument ensures var_X J≪log X ·osc_X J and osc_X J=X^(β−1+o(1)). Under RH J is eventually monotone and its range is comparable to X^(−1/2). In both cases absorb log X into the exponential by reducing c, and the term with a saving of 1/4 using the floor of the range. This relative comparison of increments removes the loss at the endpoint β=1 in the local comparison; only the linear oscillation of A remains to be estimated at root scale.

**A comparison of positive masses at ratio two and its orientation.** Let D₂(y)=A(2y)−A(y). Under RH there exist c,C>0 such that c y^(−1/2)≤D₂(y)≤C y^(−1/2) for all large y: integrate A'(u)=−exp(1/2)S(u/e)/u² and use the ceilings of both signs already proved for −S. If β>1/2, on each band [X,C'X] of sufficiently wide fixed ratio there are excursions of both signs for D₂ of size X^(β−1+o(1)) in the exponent sense. This also holds with y=p/√2 a rescaled prime. It vanishes at NO right zero, since Reρ<1, even if the supremum is one. The constant main term disappears and the prime powers weigh O(y^(−1/2)). Apply to the detector y D₂(y) the same fixed filter and positive average as before (their exponents are ρ); all coefficients remain absolutely summable. To sample at primes, the Cauchy bound for the derivative of y D₂(y) is O(X^(β−1)) and the transfer by cells of length X^(3/4) works. No uniform lower bound for the multiplier is required as the target zero varies.

There is moreover an exact arithmetic check of the orientation for the DISCRETE comparison. Put h=log 2, y=p/√2, z=log(r/p). Then D₂(y)=Σ_r a_r [g(z−h/2)−g(z+h/2)]. The bracket is odd and strictly positive for z>0. Hence Σ_{p≤Y} a_p D₂(p/√2)>0 for every Y≥2, without hypotheses, by cancellation of the interior pairs. The limit of this prefix is h/2: repeat the cut proof with the integral ∫₀^∞ z[g(z−h/2)−g(z+h/2)]dz=h/2 by parity and the first moment of the shifted Gaussian. The comparison A(√2p)≥A(p/√2) pits only two positive sums against each other; the positive prefix proves that comparison neither prime by prime nor on growing bands. It is a difference version of the same antisymmetric mechanism, not an independent route.

**Global adversarial control for prefixes and progressions.** Fix 0<α<1/2 and m(x)=1+x^(−α)cos(log x). There is ONE sequence of integers E weighted by log n, valid on all bands, with the same sign and limit of the antisymmetric prefixes, and with local sign changes of D₂ on all bands of sufficiently wide fixed ratio. It moreover satisfies, for each fixed modulus q and each reduced class a, Σ_{n≤x,n∈E,n≡a mod q} log n=φ(q)⁻¹∫₂ˣ m(v)dv+O_q(log³(2x)); in non-reduced classes there are only finitely many terms. Unlike the rounded local profile of 195, a single sequence satisfies all these constraints.

Construction. On [2^j,2^(j+1)) choose Q=lcm(1,…,k) with k maximal such that Q≤√j (for j large); Q eventually contains any fixed modulus. In each reduced class mod Q start a counter at zero, with target φ(Q)⁻¹∫_{2^j}^x m. At each candidate integer add log n if the new total does not exceed the target. Between consecutive candidates the target grows by at most 2Q<log(2^j), also on the initial and final stretches. By induction the deficit after each candidate is less than log n (if it is added, the increment since the previous candidate is less than the new weight); between candidates it costs O(j). Aggregation over classes and bands up to j costs O(Σ_{i≤j} i√i)=O(j^(5/2)). For q|Q, each reduced class mod q has exactly φ(Q)/φ(q) reduced lifts. This gives the formula, and the initial bands only change the constant. 

With A_E defined with the same weights as A, integration by parts against this error for q=1 gives
    A_E(Y)=1+Re[Y^z exp(z²/2)]+O(Y⁻¹log³(2Y)),   z=−α+i.
Indeed the derivative of g(log(x/Y))/x is (g'−g)/x² and the change x=Y exp u leaves a finite Gaussian moment with weight exp(−u); extending the continuum below 2 costs less than any inverse power. Thus D₂,E has main term Re[(2^z−1)exp(z²/2)Y^z], with nonzero coefficient. Both phases of strict sign occupy intervals of fixed logarithmic length per period, with elements of E by the mass law. The internal cancellation of the prefixes also holds exactly for E and its limit is (log 2)/2 by the same local convergence of measures. This rules out deducing the local inequality solely from the exact sign of all prefixes, their limit, the eventual exclusion of each fixed divisor and the asymptotic PNT in each fixed progression. The constructed sequence does not reproduce the convolution identities of the true primes.

**Divisor identity: only one Möbius band can affect the comparison at root scale.** Write l=log Y, P(t)=Σ_{k≥1}k⁻¹g(log(k/t)), W(t)=P(2t)−P(t). For each fixed a>1, on the true primes one has
    D₂(Y)= [exp(1/8)/2](1−2^(−1/2))/√Y − Σ_{|log(d/Y)|≤a√l} μ(d)(log d)/d · W(Y/d) + o(Y^(−1/2)).
The plus sign of the bias is important. This separation is done WITHOUT RH and without using cancellation of μ in what is discarded.

Indeed Λ=(−μ log)*1 by differentiation of the Dirichlet product, and the difference of the two masses with Λ is exactly the sum with minus sign extended to all d. The squares removed from the mass with Λ at scale Y contribute (exp(1/8)/2+o(1))/√Y by PNT and the change p=√Y u (integral ∫u⁻²g(2 log u)du); powers of order ≥3 cost O(Y^(−2/3+o(1))) by dyadic counting. For small t the direct count on logarithmic strips gives |W(t)|≤exp(−log²t/2+O(|log t|+1)). For large t, the Mellin transform of P has integrand ζ(1+s) exp(s²/2)t^s; shift to Re s=−m with m an integer close to log t. Only the pole with residue 1 is crossed. On that line the functional equation gives |ζ(1−m+iv)|≤exp(O(m log(m+2))+O(|v|)) for m≥2, using |Γ(m−iv)|≤Γ(m), sine ≤exp(O(|v|+1)) and |ζ(m−iv)|≤ζ(2). The Gaussian factor makes the integral converge uniformly, and the horizontals disappear upon taking large height for each fixed m. Therefore P(t)−1 and W(t) cost exp(−log²t/2+O(log t log(2+log t))). Grouping d by unit strips of log(d/Y) gives mass Σ(log d)/d≪1+l+|log(d/Y)| per strip. The two discarded tails together are O(Y^(−a²/2+o(1))), strictly below the root scale. The remaining centre still contains Y^(1+o(1)) indices and requires signed cancellation; its logarithmic length O(√log Y) does not prove the local comparison.

**Exact centring and optimal absolute-value cost of the Möbius band.** In the previous formula log d may be replaced by log(d/Y). Indeed Σ μ(d)W(Y/d)/d = g(log(2Y))−g(log Y): after expanding P, the sum over d|n is zero except for n=1, and g is even. The series are absolutely convergent at fixed Y. The remainder multiplied by log Y is o(Y^(−N)) for every fixed N. Cutting the tails preserves the precision of the previous entry. The principle of subtracting a constant via a mass identity already appears in the quadrature of phase 213; here one determines moreover how much ANY choice of that constant can gain.

Let I_Y be the previous truncated band. Then
    inf_c Σ_{d∈I_Y} |μ(d)|/d · |log d−c| · |W(Y/d)|
       → (1/ζ(2)) min_b ∫_ℝ |u−b| |W(exp(−u))| du > 0.
To prove it, translate c=log Y+b. By the elementary count of squarefree numbers (expand μ²(n)=Σ_{k²|n}μ(k)), the measure Σ μ²(d)/d in u=log(d/Y) converges locally to du/ζ(2). The tails of the integrand, uniform for bounded b, are dominated by the Gaussian ceilings of W and the mass bound O(1) on each unit strip. Uniform convergence for b in a compact set follows from uniform Lipschitz continuity. The minimisers lie in a compact set because a fixed strip with positive limit mass gives a floor proportional to |b|−O(1), and b=0 has bounded cost. The minimum is the cost of a median of the continuous weight, strictly positive: W is not identically zero since P goes from zero to one, and by continuity the weight has positive mass on an interval. For the centring b=0 the signed sum tends to zero by the PNT for μ and the same truncation; the positive and negative contributions tend separately to half of the limiting absolute cost. The verified improvement removes a factor log Y, but the root inequality needs to control the difference between two quantities of order one.

**What a second scale ratio really adds to the Möbius centring.** Let f_h(u)=P(exp(h−u))−P(exp(−u)), h>0, and G(u)=u f_h(u) the centred weight. Each fixed translation of f_h summed against μ(d)/d, u=log(d/Y), gives a difference of two Gaussians in log Y via μ*1, negligible to every power. However NO finite linear combination of such translations, nor their L¹ closure, approximates G with arbitrarily small error at fixed ratio h. Using in addition h'=log 3 together with h=log 2, one does obtain arbitrary approximation in L¹. It is a qualitative statement, with no rate in Y.

With transform ∫f(u)exp(−iτu)du the multiplier is F_h(τ)=(exp(−iτh)−1)ζ(1−iτ)exp(−τ²/2). It follows by Mellin on the line of convergence and continuation to Re s=0 after cancelling the pole; at τ=0 the value is h. At τ₁=2π/h the zero is simple since ζ(1−iτ₁)≠0. Every translation vanishes there in Fourier, while |Ĝ(τ₁)|=|F'_h(τ₁)|=h|ζ(1−iτ₁)|exp(−τ₁²/2)>0. This quantity bounds from below the L¹ error of ANY combination. For h'/h irrational the two transforms have no common real zero. To see this constructively in the approximation, cut Ĝ by χ(τ/T), with χ smooth, compactly supported and equal to one near zero. Write the cut transform as Σ_j F_j · [χ Ĝ conjugate(F_j)/(Σ|F_i|²)]. The two brackets are smooth and compactly supported; their inverses are integrable. The resulting convolutions are approximated in L¹ by finite sums of translations (truncation and continuity under translation). Letting T go to infinity, the cut approximates G in L¹ by approximate identity. For the ratios 2,3 the irrationality follows from unique factorisation.

For each FIXED approximant, the discrete absolute cost of its residue tends to its L¹ norm divided by ζ(2) by the squarefree law and the Gaussian tails. With two ratios one thus removes the constant positive floor that persisted with a single centring. The coefficients, number and positions of translations may grow as the approximation is refined: interchanging this limit with Y→∞ without estimates does not justify the required error o(Y^(−1/2)).

**Quantitative limit via complex zeros: the cost falls on the translations towards smaller scales.** Let Q_R=Σ c_j f_{h_j}(u−a_j), h_j∈{log 2,log 3}, a_j≥−R, with no upper bound on a_j. If R→∞ and log(1+Σ|c_j|)=o(R²), then, for each nontrivial zero ρ=b+iγ of ζ,
    liminf R⁻¹ log ||u f_{log 2}−Q_R||₁ ≥ −(1−b).
In particular a known zero at b=1/2 suffices to prevent precision Y^(−1/2+o(1)) when R≤(1−δ)log Y and log(1+Σ|c_j|)=o((log Y)²), for any fixed δ>0 (use R=(1−δ)log Y). Large scales do not compensate for that restriction.

Proof. Let z=i(ρ−1) and m the multiplicity. All the F_h have a zero of order m at z: the dilation factor does not vanish since b<1. Since the transform of the target G=u f_h is i F'_h, the derivative of order m−1 of the transform of the residue at z is the SAME nonzero constant for every Q_R. It is an integral against (−iu)^(m−1) exp(−izu), of pointwise modulus |u|^(m−1)exp(−(1−b)u). For L=(1+ε)R, on u≥−L the weight costs O_ρ((1+L)^(m−1)exp((1−b)L)). On u<−L each translated kernel is uniformly bounded by C exp(−c(|u|−R)²) by the previous Gaussian ceilings and a_j≥−R; the target satisfies the same ceiling with a polynomial factor. The weighted integral of that tail is o(1), since |u|−R≥εR and the logarithm of the total coefficient cost is o(R²). The nonzero constant then forces ||G−Q_R||₁≳_ρ (1+L)^(1−m)exp(−(1−b)L). Take liminf and ε↓0.

The conclusion only limits the continuous certificate by absolute error. At radius essentially log Y one reaches scales Y exp(a_j) of subpower size or smaller, where the explicit remainders of μ*1 must be accounted for according to their coefficients. The argument does not rule out signed cancellation directly in the discrete sample.

**Explicit coefficients and profile at the end of the translation.** Put B(u)=P(exp(−u)), φ(u)=g(u−h)−g(u), f(u)=B(u−h)−B(u). There is an exact pointwise representation at ONE ratio:
    u f(u)=−f'(u)+h Σ_{j≥0} f(u+jh)−Σ_{n≥1} Λ(n)/n · f(u+log n).
Indeed f(u)=Σ_{k≥1}φ(u+log k)/k. Use tφ(t)=−φ'(t)+h g(t−h), split u=t−log k and expand log k=Σ_{n|k}Λ(n). The Gaussian term is hB(u−h), equal to the first series by telescoping. All the series converge absolutely for fixed u, locally uniformly; convergence in L¹ is not claimed.

For R=mh truncate both series at jh<R and log n<R, keeping −f'. In the endpoint coordinate u=−R+v, the error target minus approximant converges, uniformly for v compact, to
    E_h(v)=h Σ_{l≥0} f(v+lh)−∫₀^∞ f(v+s)ds.
The first tail is exact, and in the second the measures Σ_{n≥exp R}Λ(n)/n in s=log n−R converge locally to ds by PNT. Each unit strip has mass bounded by Chebyshev, and for v compact the tails are uniformly Gaussian. This discrepancy does not disappear: for large fixed v, φ and its translations are positive and strictly decreasing there (for large t, (t−h)g(t−h)>t g(t)); by the series for f the left rectangle sum is strictly larger than the integral. Thus there is a fixed interval of v with positive error bounded below. The cost of truncated coefficients is O(R) by Chebyshev and partial summation. The obstruction to using the pointwise identity as an integral approximation is displaced to u≈−R, although the error on each fixed compact set of u tends to zero. For R≈log Y this falls at d≈Y exp(−R), exactly where the integer sample must already be distinguished from the continuum. Under the Möbius sum, each f(u+log n) gives exactly φ(log(n/Y)) via μ*1: the coefficients Λ(n)/n reconstruct the original difference of masses with Λ. Hence applying the infinite expansion without another inequality is an algebraic return to the problem, not a closure by small coefficients.

**The endpoint profile does have a zero in the signed sample.** With the previous truncation R=mh, choose Y=exp(R−w) for fixed real w. The truncated error after applying Σ_d μ(d)/d in u=log(d/Y) converges to
    L_h(w)=h g(w−h)−∫_{w−h}^w g(t)dt.
In particular with Y=exp R the limit is strictly NEGATIVE although E_h(v)>0 for large v. For a unique w_h∈(h/2,h), the limit is exactly zero. This removes the constant edge obstruction on a geometric progression explicitly determined by the weight.

Indeed apply μ*1 to the two tails before passing to the limit. The first reduces exactly to hΣ_{l≥0}φ(w+lh)=h g(w−h). The second is Σ_{n≥exp R}Λ(n)φ(w+log n−R)/n. The interchanges are absolute for each fixed m by the Gaussian tails towards +∞; PNT and Chebyshev give for the last sum the limit ∫₀^∞φ(w+s)ds=∫_{w−h}^w g. Dividing the equation L_h=0 by g(w−h) one obtains ∫₀^h exp(−(w−h)s−s²/2)ds=h. The left-hand side decreases strictly from infinity to zero; at w=h/2 it exceeds h and at w=h it is smaller. At the phase w_h the FINITE signed error is exactly the negative of the integral of φ(w_h+s) against the discrepancy of Λ(n)/n relative to ds on s≥0, with s=log n−R. In particular PNT gives only o(1); it does not authorise o(Y^(−1/2)). Nor does a single geometric progression replace the criterion over bands. It is a genuine sign effect in the term that escaped to the endpoint, not a proof of the comparison D₂.

**Two independent cuts: the signed edge can be paid for by a single atom at EVERY scale.** Fix h=log 2 and φ(s)=g(s−h)−g(s). Truncate the geometric series at j<m and the Λ series at n<N. After applying μ*1 the exact remainder is
    E(Y;m,N)=h g(w−h)−Σ_{n≥N} Λ(n)φ(log(n/Y))/n,    w=mh−log Y.
For every large Y one can explicitly choose m and, using a finite search over prime powers, N comparable to Y, such that |E|≪log Y/Y=o(Y^(−1/2)).

Indeed H(b)=∫_b^∞φ(s)ds=∫_{b−h}^b g(s)ds decreases strictly for b>h/2. Choose B fixed and sufficiently large with h g(B−h)<H(h/2), and m=ceil((log Y+B)/h), so that w∈[B,B+h]. The target h g(w−h) lies in an interior compact subset of (0,H(h/2)). Choose b₁>h/2 and b₂>b₁ fixed with H(b₁) larger than the whole compact set and H(b₂) smaller. By PNT, the tails of Λ at the cuts ceil(Y exp b_i) tend to H(b_i). Between the two cuts the tail decreases with N because φ is positive. Each jump is O(log Y/Y), even at prime powers. The first crossing of the target approximates the remainder with that precision. The search may omit n>Y exp(3√log Y) with error O(Y^(−2)): group by unit strips of log(n/Y), use Chebyshev for the mass Λ(n)/n and the Gaussian decay. The first crossing computed with that finite tail still gives the stated bound.

This resolves the edge at root scale without restricting Y to a progression. The cut N depends on the actual mass of Λ in a tail. The expression that remains contains the prefix Σ_{n<N}Λ(n)φ(log(n/Y))/n; this still has terms of both signs. The choice of the cut controls the remaining positive sum and by itself gives no inequality between the parts of the prefix. Do not confuse the resolution of the truncation error with the estimate of the sign of D₂.

**Exact cost of splitting by sign the prefix completed with its tail.** For the comparison with Λ at ratio 2 put h=log 2, a=h/2 and b(t)=g(t−a)−g(t+a) at t=log(n/Y)−a. It is odd, positive for t>0 and b'(0)=2a g(a)>0. Let K_+(z)=∫₀^∞ b(t)exp(zt)dt and K_−(z)=∫_{−∞}⁰ b(t)exp(zt)dt be the responses of the two halves with their signs. For z=ρ−1, the common scale response is (Y exp a)^z, and the individual responses satisfy uniformly for −1/2≤Re z≤0:
    K_+(z)=b'(0)/z²+O(|z|⁻³),    K_−(z)=−b'(0)/z²+O(|z|⁻³).
These are three integrations by parts; b(0)=b''(0)=0 and the integrals of |b'''(t)|exp(|t|/2) are finite. But exactly K_++K_−=2sinh(az)exp(z²/2). Thus the ratio between the total response in modulus and that of each half is O_h((1+γ²)exp(−γ²/2)) at large heights |γ|. The formula also holds for the critical line. In arithmetic terms the continuous means of the two sectors already cancel by oddness; the loss described affects EACH high-frequency oscillation even after removing those means. Estimating only the moduli of the two errors does not preserve the Gaussian attenuation. This does not rule out one-sided bounds that exploit correlation or that only need the root threshold.

As a check of the cut alternative, if the edge is moved to a fixed t₀ with b(t₀)≠0, the leading term of the upper half is −exp(zt₀)b(t₀)/z, and that of the lower half is its opposite. Hence among finite real cuts the only one that removes the first-order loss is the sign cut t₀=0; even there the second-order loss remains. The previous quantile adjustment of N still pays a small discrete remainder, but analysing the new prefix as an isolated function with fixed cut would introduce these edge terms.

**Positive splitting before the last smoothing, with optimal cost at reserved variance.** Write g_v for the normal density of variance v, a=(log 2)/2 and b=g₁(·−a)−g₁(·+a). For 0<v<1 put b₀=g_{1−v}(·−a)−g_{1−v}(·+a) and P_v=g_v*(b₀)_+, M_v=g_v*(b₀)_− (positive and negative parts in magnitude). One has b=P_v−M_v pointwise, with both weights nonnegative and reflections of each other. Each has mass exactly
    m(v)=2Φ(a/√(1−v))−1,
where Φ is the standard normal distribution. Indeed b₀ is positive for t>0 and the integrals over that half-line differ by m(v). Normal convolution preserves mass. For z=s+iγ, −1/2≤s≤0, each response, taken separately, has modulus ≤C_a exp(−vγ²/2): the factor of the last smoothing is exp(vz²/2), and the remaining absolute moment is dominated uniformly by the two shifted Gaussians, even as v∈(0,1) varies.

The mass is minimal among ALL decompositions b=g_v*μ₊−g_v*μ₋ with finite nonnegative measures. By injectivity of Gaussian convolution (its Fourier transform is nonzero), μ₊−μ₋=b₀ dt. The Jordan decomposition forces each measure to dominate the corresponding part, and our construction attains equality. Compared with the hard cut, which has mass m(0) per half, reserving small v costs only O_a(v) of additional mass. Even choosing v=1/G for a height G≥2 costs O_a(1/G) and gives a factor ≤exp(−G/2) for |γ|≥G in EACH part. The scale Y remains free: for a fixed exterior frequency the arithmetic amplitude may grow relative to the root although its coefficient is tiny. This splitting resolves the specific spectral loss of the hard cut and does not prove the relative order of the two sums over primes.

**Exact average of the interior quadratic term when moving the cut.** For a compact logarithmic band I, take ν=(Σ_p (log p)/p δ_{log p}−dt)|_I, and R_I(t)=∫_{x≤t<y}(y−x)g(y−x)dν(x)dν(y). This is exactly the contribution to R(exp t) with BOTH coordinates in I. Let B_I=g_{1/2}*ν, with variance 1/2. Then
    2∫_I R_I(t)dt = ||B_I||²₂ − ||B_I'||²₂.
Indeed an interior pair x<y crosses the cut over a length y−x. Fubini and symmetry give the kernel (y−x)²g(y−x), even in the presence of atoms since the diagonal is zero. The identity z²g=g+g'' and the factorisation g=g_{1/2}*g_{1/2} give the formula by integration by parts over the whole line, with no boundary term. In angular Fourier the multiplier is (1−τ²)exp(−τ²/2). Therefore the contribution of ALL frequencies |τ|≥1 to the interior quadratic average is nonpositive for the true primes and for any band. The positive energy of |τ|<1 remains; the restriction to I mixes the frequencies, and the first ordinate of ζ cannot be invoked as if the restricted discrepancy had a spectral gap.

Nor does the formula authorise discarding external pairs. For t∈I=[L,U], the omitted part of the average of R is exactly the integral over x<y with at least one coordinate outside I, with kernel (y−x)g(y−x)·length([x,y]∩I). This retains, in particular, the pairs crossing both edges. The identity treats an average of the quadratic error; the linear oscillation bound for A remains the decisive step of the criterion.

**Averaging over variances reduces the interior positive contribution to a single mass.** In the interior cut identity, replace g by g_v of variance v and write R_{I,v}. For every finite real measure ν supported on I, of mass M, and every v₀>0 one has exactly
    ∫_{v₀}^∞ v^(−3/2) [2∫_I R_{I,v}(t)dt]dv
       = √(2/π) M² − 2√v₀ ||g_{v₀/2}*ν||²₂.
To prove it, the kernel of each interior average is z²g_v(z). Its integral against v^(−3/2) is √(2/π)(1−exp(−z²/(2v₀))) by differentiation in v; it also holds at z=0. Fubini holds even for a signed measure by the uniform bound of that integrated kernel against |ν|⊗|ν|. The exponential part factorises by convolution of two Gaussians of variance v₀/2. In particular for the ORIGINAL prime discrepancy the only explicit positive term is √(2/π)(Σ_{log p∈I}log p/p−|I|)². If one uses the continuum with density equal to the prime mass divided by |I|, the identity gives a strictly negative sign unless the centred measure is zero, by injectivity of convolution. That centring changes the original observable when M≠0.

The upper integral may be truncated at V>v₀: the absolute error is ≤√(2/π) diam(I)² ||ν||_TV²/(2V), applying 1−exp(−u)≤u to the residual kernel. This resolves all interior frequencies at once for the centred variance average. The average is cumulative: knowing its sign for every v₀ does not fix the sign of its derivative in v₀, which would recover the particular variance, nor does it include the external pairs of the original cut.

**Single-variance falsifier for the deduction by moments.** On any interval I with nonempty interior, for any v>0 and integer m≥0, there exist two positive densities on I with exactly the same moments 0,…,m as Lebesgue, for which the interior average A_v=2∫_I R_{I,v}(t)dt of the discrepancy has opposite signs. In both cases the cumulative average over variances ≥v is negative by the previous identity.

Proof. The multiplier of z²g_v(z) is L_v(τ)=v(1−vτ²)exp(−vτ²/2). The transforms of ν=D^(m+1)φ dx with φ smooth and compactly supported in the interior of I are dense in L²(|L_v|dτ) when complex φ is allowed. Indeed, if H is orthogonal to all of them, the inverse transform of H|L_v| is entire by Cauchy–Schwarz and the Gaussian tail, decays to zero on the real axis by Riemann–Lebesgue, and its (m+1)-th derivative vanishes distributionally in the interior of I. By continuation it is a polynomial on the whole line, hence zero. Fourier uniqueness gives H=0. For targets with Hermitian symmetry, taking the real part of φ keeps the approximation by symmetrisation. Approximate in this way two nonzero even real functions supported respectively in |τ|<1/√v and |τ|>1/√v. Continuity of ∫ L_v |ν̂|² in that norm ensures both strict signs already with finite approximants. The moments of ν up to m are zero by integration by parts. Scaling each ν by a small positive number turns 1+εν(x) into a strictly positive density while preserving the quadratic sign and the equality of moments. In particular neither a narrow band, nor matching any finite number of moments, nor knowing the sign of the average for ALL lower limits v₀ allows one to infer the sign at fixed variance for general positive measures. The counterexample is to the logical step, not to the prime discrepancy; 226 already treats moment failures for another functional.

**Incomplete sieving near √n introduces a signed bias of opposite sign.** Fix c>1. In A(Y) replace the primes by ALL integers n≥2 whose least prime factor exceeds √n/c, keeping the weight (log n)/n. Denote the new mass by A_c. As Y→∞ one has unconditionally
    [A_c(2Y)−A_c(Y)]−[A(2Y)−A(Y)] = −4(log c)(log 2)/(log Y)² + O_c((log Y)⁻³).
In particular the sieved comparison is eventually NEGATIVE: the quantitative PNT gives A(Y)=1+O((log Y)⁻³). This complements the semiprime obstacle of 195, line 785, which treats the absolute reconstruction error.

Indeed only finitely many integers with three or more prime factors pass the cut, since n>(√n/c)^3 would force n<c⁶ (equivalently use n≥P⁻(n)^3). For semiprimes n=pq, p≤q, the cut is equivalent to q<c²p. The squares contribute O(Y⁻¹/²) by Chebyshev. For the pairs with p<q change to t=log(pq), u=log(q/p), 0<u<2log c. Replacing each dπ by dx/log x the weighted density in (t,u) is 2t/(t²−u²) dt du, including the Jacobian 1/2. The replacement costs O_c((log Y)⁻⁴): truncate |t−log Y|≤log Y/4 with Gaussian cost via integer counting, and perform two successive partial summations in q and p using π(z)−Li(z)=O_K(z/log^K z) for arbitrary K. In that zone p,q are comparable and their logarithms comparable to log Y; in each dyadic box of p,q the weight and its variation in each variable are O_c(log Y/(pq)), even with the endpoints q=p,c²p or the cut in t. After replacing the first variable one can invert the order and impose the same endpoints in the second; O_c(log²Y) boxes suffice and K=10 is enough. The continuous model integrated against g(t−log Y) gives 4log c/log Y+O_c((log Y)⁻³) by expanding 2t/(t²−u²) and the zero mean of the linear moment of g. Subtracting the two scales proves the coefficient. Therefore approaching the exact primality threshold up to a constant factor does not suffice even to preserve the orientation of this comparison: the contribution of balanced semiprimes must be removed or compensated.

**A growing additive strip next to √n is discardable, except for the squares.** For large n replace primality by P⁻(n)>√n−√(log log n), and explicitly exclude the squares. The Gaussian mass so obtained differs from A(Y) by O(Y^(−1/2)/√(log log Y)), unconditionally and already in ABSOLUTE VALUE. Consequently the error in D₂ is o(Y^(−1/2)). With squares included, the correction to D₂ is instead −exp(1/8)(1−1/√2)/√Y+o(Y^(−1/2)), since in this sieve they weigh log(p²)=2log p. The conventions for the first integers are irrelevant.

Proof of the count. A large composite that passes has two prime factors p≤q; three factors would give n≥(√n−√loglog n)^3>n. For p∈[P,2P] one deduces 0≤q−p≤C√loglog P via (√n−p)(√n+p)/p, since p∼√n. Let H=ceil(C√loglog P). For distinct p,q count pairs (p,p+k), 1≤k≤H. Take Q the product of the primes 3≤ℓ≤z=c log P with c small, so that Q≤√P by Chebyshev. In the valid reduced classes for p mod Q one must avoid −k mod ℓ when ℓ∤k. Brun–Titchmarsh in each class gives for each k a ceiling
    C P/(log P log z) · ∏_{ℓ|k,ℓ≥3}(1+1/(ℓ−2)).
Here ∏_{3≤ℓ≤z}(1−1/(ℓ−1))≪1/log z by the Mertens product. The sum of the last factor over k≤H costs O(H): expand over odd squarefree divisors d and use Σ_{k≤H,d|k}1≤H/d, with the product ∏_{ℓ≥3}(1+1/(ℓ(ℓ−2))) convergent. Hence there are O(P/(log P √loglog P)) pairs in the box. Each weight is O(log P/P²) by the maximum of g in the box log(n/Y). In the region Y^(1/4)≤P≤Y the dyadic boxes give the announced ceiling upon summing P⁻¹ against a Gaussian envelope in log(P²/Y); the factor exp(−log(P²/Y)/2) arising from extracting Y⁻¹/² is integrable against that envelope. Outside that region the Gaussian decay in log Y absorbs even the integer count. The asymptotic for the squares is that of the previous separation of powers, multiplied by two. The criterion with squares excluded keeps the strict margin under RH and the excursions of larger exponent if it fails. This does not estimate the comparison for the sieve itself at additive distance.

**Logarithmic threshold of the additive sieve (squares excluded).** Any nonnegative distance H(n)=o(log n) preserves the error o(Y^(−1/2)) in mass and in D₂. By contrast for H(n)=log n the contamination E(Y) of the mass A is ≍Y^(−1/2) at every large scale and E(2Y)−E(Y)≤−cY^(−1/2) at arbitrarily high scales for some c>0. The result for differences is one-sided along a subsequence, not an asymptotic.

For the ceiling apply Selberg's upper sieve to p,p+k in [P,2P], k even ≤O(log P). Detail of the uniformity: with z=P^(1/20), for odd primes ℓ≤z one excludes ω(ℓ)=2 classes except for ℓ|k where ω=1. The standard form of Selberg's quadratic bound gives P/G(z)+O(Σ_{d,e≤z}ω([d,e])) with d,e squarefree and G(z)=Σ_{d≤z}∏_{ℓ|d}ω(ℓ)/(ℓ−ω(ℓ)) over products of those primes (the optimal weights have modulus ≤1). The error is O(z⁴) since ω([d,e])≤[d,e]≤z². Restrict the factors to ℓ≤z^δ for small absolute δ: in the complete product the expectation of log d is Σω(ℓ)log ℓ/ℓ≤2δ log z+O(1), so at least half the weight has d≤z. Mertens then gives G(z)≫log²P / ∏_{ℓ|k,ℓ≥3}(1+1/(ℓ−2)). Odd k produce no large pairs. Summing over k≤K as in the previous entry one obtains O((K+1)P/log²P) for K=O(log P). In each box K may be taken to be a multiple of 1+sup H(n) for n comparable to P². The same Gaussian sum over boxes proves the announced ceiling by dominated convergence; with H=log n it gives O(Y^(−1/2)).

For the floor take P=√Y and count consecutive gaps between primes of [P,2P]. There are (1+o(1))P/log P of them and they sum to ≤P, so ≫P/log P of them measure ≤2log P. For such p<q, √(pq)−p≤(q−p)/2≤log P<log(pq), so pq passes and is not a square. Products are distinct by unique factorisation. Since 1≤pq/Y≤4 each contributes ≫log P/P², and E(Y)≥c₀/√Y. By the ceiling E(Y)→0. If all drops E(Z)−E(2Z) were eventually less than c/√Z, telescoping from Y would give E(Y)≤c/(1−2^(−1/2))/√Y, absurd for c<c₀(1−2^(−1/2)). The threshold identifies up to which order that sector can be discarded without knowing its correlations; it does not fix the sign of D₂ for the primes.

**The margin distinguishes small and large constants in H(n)=c log n.** Write D_c^*(Y) for the difference of masses with this additive cut and squares excluded, and E_c(Y) for the spurious mass. There are absolute constants 0<c₀<c₁<∞ with these properties. For every fixed 0<c≤c₀, the criterion D_c^*≥0 on bands of growing ratio remains equivalent to the global sign. For every fixed c≥c₁, even UNDER RH there are arbitrarily high scales with D_c^*<0. This last statement concerns the eventual sign and does not by itself exclude favourable bands of growing ratio.

For the first part the pair sieve of the previous paragraph gives limsup √Y E_c(Y)≤C c with C absolute: in each box p comparable to P the admissible gaps are ≤C'c log P for P sufficiently large depending on c; the +1 factor of the ceiling disappears when passing to the limsup, and the sum over Gaussian boxes has an absolute constant. This holds for each fixed c, and for c≤1 one can moreover use the ceiling at c=1 as dominant. Under RH integrate −S(u/e) exp(1/2)/u² from Y to 2Y with −S(x)≥√x/5: D₂(Y)≥[2(1−1/√2)/5]/√Y. Take c₀ with C c₀ less than half that margin. Then D_c^*=D₂+E_c(2Y)−E_c(Y)>0 eventually. If RH fails, the negative excursions of D₂ at scales p/√2 exceed Y^(−1/2+δ) in modulus for some δ>0 on every sufficiently wide band; an error O_c(Y⁻¹/²) cannot remove them.

For large c there is moreover liminf √Y E_c(Y)≥k c with k absolute positive. Split [P,2P], P=√Y, into ceil(P/(2c log P)) equal boxes. Each pair of primes in a box passes the cut since q−p≤2c log P and √(pq)−p≤(q−p)/2. If N is the total number of primes and B the number of boxes, the number of distinct pairs is ≥(N²/B−N)/2. By PNT this is ≥k' cP/log P for fixed c≥2 and P sufficiently large. Each pair costs ≫log P/P² with an absolute constant. Since E_c→0, telescoping over doubled scales forces drops ≥k c(1−2^(−1/2))/(2√Y) at arbitrarily high scales. Under RH D₂≤C₁/√Y with C₁ absolute by the same previous Gaussian bound; choosing c₁ large enough concludes. Neither a critical constant nor a mechanism to prove the sieved inequality for small c without RH has been determined.

**Using the bias of composites as margin: one-sided comparison with the continuous density.** Let H(n)/log n→∞ and H(n)=n^o(1), for example exp(√log n). Form B_H(Y) with ALL integers passing P⁻(n)>√n−H(n), with the same positive weight (log n)g(log(n/Y))/n. Even the squares may be included. Then the global sign is equivalent to B_H(Y)≥1 on bands of arbitrarily high growing ratio. Under RH, √Y(B_H(Y)−1)→+∞; if RH fails, there is a fixed C and in each sufficiently high [X,CX] some Y with B_H(Y)<1.

Indeed E=B_H−A≥0, and √Y E(Y)→∞: for each large fixed c the cut eventually contains all pairs of the cut c log n, which contribute liminf √Y E≥kc with k absolute by the previous boxes. The first integers weigh less than any inverse power. On the other hand E(Y)≤Y^(−1/2+o(1)) unconditionally. Each large admitted composite has two factors, and for p∈[P,2P] there are at most P^o(1) possible q per p, even counting integers; the individual weight costs O(log P/P²) before the Gaussian. Summing the Gaussian boxes gives the ceiling (for every fixed ε use H(n)≪_ε n^ε and then ε↓0). The included squares respect that ceiling.

For the pure mass A, the Gaussian explicit formula of the previous entries has main term 1 and zero terms −Y^(ρ−1)exp((ρ−1)²/2), counting multiplicities; the higher powers cost O(Y^(−1/2)). Thus under RH |A−1|≪Y^(−1/2), strictly dominated by E. If there is a zero with real part b₀>1/2, apply the recurrence of 2242 to the observable Y(A(Y)−1), with nonzero multiplier exp((ρ−1)²/2) and remainder O(√Y). It produces on every band of sufficiently wide fixed ratio a point with A(Y)−1≤−c'Y^(b₀−1). The contamination has strictly smaller exponent. The lower bound B_H≥1 remains open, but root precision is no longer required when removing semiprimes, nor is a difference of two scales needed. The margin under RH is obtained from pairs of true primes by elementary counting.

**Calibration of the width by the exterior abscissa, endpoint included.** For each 0<δ<1/2 take H_δ(n)=n^δ(log n)² and admit squares. Then B_{H_δ}(Y)≥1 eventually if and only if β=sup Reρ≤1/2+δ. Even the inequality on bands of arbitrarily high growing ratio suffices. The endpoint β=1/2+δ lies on the positive side with no hypothesis that the supremum is attained.

Indeed, for E_δ=B_{H_δ}−A one has uniformly for large Y
    Y^(δ−1/2) log Y ≪_δ E_δ(Y) ≪_{δ,ε} Y^(δ−1/2+ε).
For the ceiling only large semiprimes exist: H_δ=o(√n), p∼√n, q−p≪P^(2δ)(log P)² in the box p∈[P,2P]. Count integers q and sum the boxes with the Gaussian as before. For the floor take P=√Y and split [P,2P] into boxes of length comparable to L=P^(2δ)(log P)², at most L. In each box the pairs p<q pass the cut by √(pq)−p≤(q−p)/2. Cauchy with N∼P/log P primes and O(P/L) boxes gives ≫P L/(log P)² distinct products, since L/log P→∞. Each contributes ≫log P/P². Thus E_δ exceeds the scale Y^(δ−1/2) by at least a factor log Y.

The absolutely convergent explicit formula for A gives |A(Y)−1|≪Y^(β−1), even at the endpoint, with cost O(Y⁻¹/²) from the powers. Therefore if β≤1/2+δ the floor of E_δ gives B_{H_δ}>1 eventually. If β>1/2+δ choose a zero with real part b₀>1/2+δ and ε<b₀−1/2−δ. The negative excursions of A−1 from the previous entry dominate the ceiling of E_δ on each band [X,CX]. In particular, proving the comparison for a sequence of positive δ tending to zero would exclude ALL right zeros without needing uniformity in the thresholds of Y or in the bands for different δ. This family of comparisons has not been proved.

**A moving member of the sieved comparison does have an unconditional sign.** Put t=log Y, Q(t)=(log t)^(2/3)(log log t)^(1/3) for large t. There is a fixed d>0 such that with H(n)=√n exp(−d log n/Q(log n)) one has, eventually at ALL scales,
    B_H(Y)−1 ≫ exp(−d t/Q(t))/t > 0.
No fixed zero-free strip needs to be assumed. It is an application to this concrete mass of the Vinogradov–Korobov region already used by 371 and 400, not an improvement of that region.

Indeed, in the Gaussian formula for A split the zeros into |γ|≤2√t and the rest. In the head the cited free region gives Reρ≤1−c/Q(t) with c absolute (adjust the constant for the compact stretch). Σ exp(−γ²/2) is finite and |exp((ρ−1)²/2)|≤exp(1/2−γ²/2). The tail costs O(exp(−t)) by Z3 and Reρ≤1. Including the higher powers one obtains |A(Y)−1|≪exp(−c t/Q(t)), reducing c if necessary. Choose 0<d<c. For P=√Y divide [P,2P] into boxes of length comparable to L=P exp(−d t/Q(t)), at most L. One has L/log P→∞ and L/P→0. For n∈[Y,4Y], H(n)≥L for large Y: the derivative with respect to t of t/2−d t/Q(t) is eventually positive. Each pair of primes in a box passes the cut. The same count via Cauchy and PNT contributes to E=B_H−A at least a constant times L/(P log P). This floor dominates the ceiling of |A−1| since (c−d)t/Q(t)−log t→∞. Only distinct pairs are used; the conclusion also holds excluding squares. The effective power of H is 1/2−d/Q(log n) and TENDS TO 1/2; for any fixed δ<1/2 this width eventually exceeds n^δ(log n)². Hence no member of fixed exponent is covered, nor the sequence δ→0 required for the goal.

**Margin with leading constant in the short-interval regime.** For fixed 7/24<δ<1/2 and H(n)=c n^δ log n, c>0 fixed, put s=δ−1/2. The added mass satisfies unconditionally
    B_H(Y)−A(Y) ∼ 4c exp(s²/2) Y^s.
Indeed for p≤q the admissible length in q is (4c+o(1))p^(2δ)log p: one has q/p→1 and the inequality √(pq)−p<H(pq) is enclosed between two intervals with endpoints (4c±ε)p^(2δ)log p above p. The short PNT of 238 (threshold 7/12 with fixed margin) gives (4c+o(1))p^(2δ) primes q>p. On a compact set of log(p²/Y) the weight of each pair is (2+o(1))(log p)/p² times g(log(p²/Y)), uniformly. The sum in p is evaluated by PNT; the resulting integral is 8c∫ p^(2δ−2)g(log(p²/Y))dp=4cY^s exp(s²/2). To pass from the compact set to the axis, the same short-interval ceiling counts O_c(p^(2δ)) partners for every large p and Chebyshev controls p by dyadic boxes; the factor in the coordinate u=log(p²/Y) is O(exp(su)) via a Gaussian envelope shifted by a constant. The squares cost O(Y⁻¹/²). This justifies the equivalence without correlation hypotheses.

At the edge β=1/2+δ the constant has a precise spectral meaning. Let T(t)=Σ_{Reρ=β} exp((ρ−1)²/2) exp(i Imρ t), with multiplicities, real by symmetry. Absolute and dominated convergence in the explicit formula give
    (B_H(Y)−1)/Y^s = 4c exp(s²/2) − T(log Y) + o(1).
If β is not attained, T=0 and any c>0 works. If it is attained, T is uniformly almost periodic, not identically zero (uniqueness of coefficients), and of mean zero; it has positive supremum and its almost periods are relatively dense by uniform approximation by trigonometric polynomials. Therefore c larger than sup T/(4 exp(s²/2)) guarantees an eventual positive sign; smaller c gives failures on every sufficiently wide band. The critical equality remains undecided. The spectral constant depends on hypothetical zeros and does not constitute a new arithmetic bound on β.

**A single logarithm suffices for the calibration on ALL 0<δ<1/2.** For H=c n^δ log n one has without short PNT
    liminf (B_H(Y)−A(Y))/Y^(δ−1/2) ≥ 2c exp((δ−1/2)²/2).
This recovers at least half the previous continuous constant without presupposing the distribution of primes in short boxes. In particular for c=1, for ALL exponents δ>0 less than 1/2 the condition B_H≥1 on bands of growing ratio is equivalent to β≤1/2+δ, equality included.

Detail of the factor 2. First restrict to |log(p²/Y)|≤K fixed. Split that compact set into subbands [P,(1+η)P] (adjust the last endpoint), with η fixed and small. In each one divide into equal boxes of length ≤L=(4c−ε)P^(2δ)log P and asymptotic to L. For all pairs p<q in a box, √(pq)−p≤(q−p)/2≤L/2<H(pq).
