If the length of the subband is D, PNT gives N∼D/log P primes, and Cauchy gives at least (1−o(1))DL/(2log²P) distinct pairs, since L/log P→∞. In each subband use the minimum of the weight (log(pq))/(pq) g(log(pq/Y)); as η→0 this reproduces the continuous integrand, uniformly at fixed K by positivity and continuity on the compact set. In the lower limit one obtains (4c−ε)∫p^(2δ−2)g(log(p²/Y))dp over the compact set, in units Y^(δ−1/2). Sending ε→0 and K→∞ gives the stated constant via the change p²=Y exp u. The squares only increase the mass.

To check sufficiency at the edge, let β=1/2+δ. After dividing A−1 by Y^(β−1), only the contributions with Reρ=β survive up to o(1), by dominated convergence as before. Their absolute amplitude is ≤exp((β−1)²/2)Σ_{Reρ=β}exp(−γ²/2). The last sum is <1: for |γ|≥14 one has exp(−γ²/2)<1/|ρ|² and on the front β>1/2 one has Σ|ρ|⁻²≤2Σ_ρ Re(1/ρ)=2+γ_E−log(4π)<0.05 by Hadamard and symmetry, without RH. The minimal mass already exceeds that margin for c=1. For smaller β the pointwise ceiling of A applies, and for larger β the integer-count ceiling E≪_ε Y^(δ−1/2+ε) together with the negative excursion suffices. This improvement does not extend below 7/24 the asymptotic equivalence with constant 4c: there what is proved is the lower bound.

**Obstruction to compensating a critical ordinate by choosing squares prime by prime.** Extend the scalar adjustment of 102–103 and allow any fixed mask 0≤w_p≤1 on the squares. Let B_w=A+Σ_p 2w_p(log p)/p² g(log(p²/Y)). Even under RH, none of these masks makes B_w(Y)−1=o(Y⁻¹/²). More precisely, for each critical ordinate γ>0 of multiplicity m, the liminf of the modulus of the mean coefficient (1/T)∫₀ᵀ exp(−iγt)exp(t/2)(B_w(exp t)−1)dt is ≥(m−1/π)|exp((−1/2+iγ)²/2)|. This concerns two-sided approximation; it does not obstruct a positive one-sided margin from squares.

Indeed under RH the explicit formula for the mass with Λ, after normalising, gives an absolutely convergent series whose coefficient at γ is −m exp((−1/2+iγ)²/2). The powers ≥3 cost o(1) after normalising; hence the square corrections with weights 2w_p−1 follow. Averaging first in t, each square contributes the indicated common Gaussian factor, multiplied by (2w_p−1)(log p)/p exp(−2iγ log p). Restricting to p≤exp(T/2) and extending the individual Gaussian integral to the whole line, the TOTAL error before dividing by T is O(1): group 2log p into unit strips next to each endpoint and use Chebyshev and the tails of g(v)exp(−v/2). For any angular direction, the projection of the remaining sum is bounded by Σ_(p≤exp(T/2)) (log p)/p |cos(2γ log p+θ)|. Divided by T it tends to 1/π uniformly in θ: PNT and partial summation give logarithmic mean zero for each exponential of fixed nonzero frequency, and uniform trigonometric approximation of |cos| preserves uniformity in the phase. The reverse triangle inequality proves the floor. The ceiling 1/π of the mask is attained in projection by taking 2w_p−1=sign cos(2γ log p+θ). The spectral constant of the floor is very small but fixed as Y tends to infinity. Choosing different weights for each Y is not covered by the statement.

**A binary selection of squares strictly improves the constant-weight threshold.** Under RH let K_γ=exp((−1/2+iγ)²/2), T(t)=Σ_γ K_γ exp(iγt) with multiplicities and M=sup T>0. The infimal threshold of the constant mask is λ*=1/2+M exp(−1/8): the normalised formula equals exp(1/8)(λ−1/2)−T(t)+o(1), and the almost recurrences realise values arbitrarily close to the supremum. The previous Hadamard bound gives λ*<0.55. There is a FIXED subset of primes of relative density λ<λ* whose squares, added with full weight, give B_w(Y)>1 eventually with margin ≫Y⁻¹/² under RH.

Choose G fixed with ||T−T_G||∞<M/2 by truncating by height, and λ=λ*−α M exp(−1/8)/4. Provisionally take w_p=λ+αΣ_{|γ|≤G}exp(2iγ log p), including both signs and multiplicities. Choose α>0 sufficiently small so that 0<w_p<1 uniformly. By PNT and smoothness, the normalised contribution of each mode to the squares is α K_γ exp(iγ log Y)+o(1): change p=√Y exp(u/2) in the continuous integral, controlling the Gaussian tails, and apply PNT on compact sets to the rescaled measure. The lower margin is then ≥exp(1/8)(λ−1/2)−(1−α)M−α||T−T_G||∞+o(1)≥α M/4+o(1) (take α<1). Thus a LOGARITHMIC mean smaller than the constant threshold is tolerated. To make the density precise, the initial claim of relative density is understood with respect to the measure (log p)/p: the mean of each nonzero mode up to P divided by log P tends to zero by PNT. Ordinary natural density is not claimed.

Make the mask binary by ordering the primes and rounding down the cumulative sum of their weights; use the increments, which are 0 or 1. The unweighted cumulative error stays bounded by one. By partial summation the change in the square mass is O(log Y/Y), since the smooth weight 2(log x)/x² g(log(x²/Y)) is unimodal for x>1 (its logarithm is strictly concave in log x) and its maximum is O(log Y/Y). Logarithmic density is also preserved by partial summation. The ordinates used and λ depend on the spectrum: this construction is a structural improvement of the one-sided criterion under RH, not an unconditional certification of B_w≥1. If there is an exterior zero, any bounded mask still contributes only O(Y⁻¹/²) and does not avoid the negative excursions of A−1.

**The density improvement for squares requires oscillation in the ordinary count.** If w_p∈[0,1] has ordinary relative density λ, that is Σ_{p≤x}w_p/π(x)→λ, then without RH
    B_w(Y)−B_constant λ(Y)=o(Y^(−1/2)).
Indeed, by PNT and partial summation Σ_{p≤x}(w_p−λ)log p=o(x). On each compact set 0<a≤p/√Y≤b the measures (1/√Y)Σ(w_p−λ)log p δ_{p/√Y} tend weakly to zero. Integrate 2u^(−2)g(2log u); the tails are uniformly small in the root normalisation by Chebyshev on dyadic boxes. Thus under RH ordinary density λ<λ* prevents B_w≥1 eventually, even if the distribution of the weights is irregular. For λ>λ* every mask with that density gives an eventual positive margin; at contact λ=λ* the little-o does not decide. A fluctuation of order √Y in the weighted count of squares is necessary to improve the constant threshold in the mass normalisation (equivalently, the term of order Y⁻¹/² in B_w must be changed).

For the binary mask constructed above the fluctuation can be seen directly. The ordinary proportion up to x is
    λ+α Σ_{0<|γ|≤G} x^(2iγ)/(1+2iγ)+o(1),
with the previous multiplicities. PNT via partial summation gives that coefficient for each fixed frequency and the rounding costs ≤1/π(x). The real polynomial in log x is not constant, has mean zero after removing λ, and recurs near its positive maximum and its negative minimum. Therefore the upper and lower ordinary densities are strictly different although the logarithmic density exists. Do not replace this mask by one of smaller natural density hoping to keep the gain.

**The threshold 7/24 drops to 1/12 for the exact constant by sampling typical intervals.** In the formula with H(n)=c n^δ log n one has B_H(Y)−A(Y)∼4c exp((δ−1/2)²/2)Y^(δ−1/2) for ALL 1/12<δ<1/2. The input is the PNT in almost all intervals of length ≥P^(1/6+ε) already used in 268; its application at endpoints that are primes must be justified.

On a stretch [P,(1+η)P], fix L comparable to P^(2δ)log P with fixed constants. Except for a set of measure o(P) in [P,2P], θ(x+L)−θ(x)=L+o(L) in the sense of convergence in relative measure. It also follows if the input is formulated for ψ: the integral of the contribution of higher powers over those starting points costs O(L√P log²P)=o(LP). Fix a tolerance ε₀>0. Divide the stretch into cells of length h comparable to dL, with d>0 fixed and sufficiently small depending on ε₀,δ. Brun–Titchmarsh at the endpoints gives variation O_δ(h) of the increment of θ when moving the start within a cell: the two extreme intervals are majorised by complete intervals of length h. A cell containing a prime with error >ε₀L contains only starting points with error >ε₀L/2, so all of them add up to length o(P). Each cell carries O_δ(h/log P) primes, again by Brun–Titchmarsh, so the exceptional primes are o(P/log P). For each there are O_δ(L/log P) partners by the same bound. Their contribution to the pair count is o(P L/log²P); for the others the partner count is (1+O(ε₀)+o(1))L/log P. Let ε₀↓0.

For the actual length depending on p, enclose the intervals between fixed lengths (4c±O_c(η)+o(1))P^(2δ)log P in the subband; use both endpoints with an additional fixed tolerance and then send it to zero. On a compact set of log(p²/Y) finitely many subbands are summed and η↓0; outside the compact set the Brun–Titchmarsh bound O_δ(p^(2δ)) for the partners holds for ALL large p and gives exactly the integrable Gaussian envelope of the previous proof. Thus the constant 4c is preserved, as is its interpretation at the edge β=1/2+δ. No independence of the two primality events is used. For δ≤1/12 this argument does not give the asymptotic; the previous box floor remains.

**The semiprime constant at the edge is determined for ALL fixed δ.** For 0<δ<1/2 the WEAKER spectral condition β<1/2+3δ (with β<1 when the following density argument is used) suffices to obtain the same asymptotic 4c exp((δ−1/2)²/2)Y^(δ−1/2). In particular β=1/2+δ always suffices, even if δ≤1/12 and the supremum is not attained. If β=1 and the strict inequality β<1/2+3δ holds, then δ>1/6 and the previous unconditional entry already covers the case.

Detail of the short average. For x∈[P,2P] use a multiplicative interval of ratio 1+h with h comparable to P^(2δ−1)log P. In the explicit formula for (ψ((1+h)x)−ψ(x))/(hx) the contribution of each zero ρ is −x^(ρ−1)((1+h)^ρ−1)/(hρ), with the last factor ≪min(1,1/(h(1+|γ|))). The main term is one and the trivial-zero term is O(P⁻²) or smaller by differentiation in log x. In the variable v=log(x/P), the integrated square of the sum over zeros is bounded by
    C Σ_ρ log(2+|γ|) P^(2Reρ−2) min(1,(h(1+|γ|))⁻²).
Indeed, multiply by a smooth majorising cutoff of the interval in v and group by floors of γ as in the L² argument of 195: two integrations by parts give (1+|n−m|)⁻² between blocks, and Cauchy in each block costs O(log(2+|n|)) by Z3. The computation is uniform in the real parts, justifies L² convergence of the tails and identifies the limit via the distributional explicit formula.

For Reρ≤1/2 the ceiling costs O(P⁻¹h⁻¹ log³P)=o(1). For the rest count by layers in σ∈[1/2,β] and by dyadic height blocks. With q(σ)=3(1−σ)/(2−σ), Ingham gives a sum of the height weights ≪h^(−q(σ))log^8P uniformly: above 1/h sum geometrically with factor T^(q−2), below use the cumulative count. Up to polylogarithmic factors, the integrand costs P raised to
    (1−σ)[−2+3(1−2δ)/(2−σ)].
There is a uniform power saving from β<1 and β<1/2+3δ. PNT in relative measure follows for these increments. The proper powers are removed by their first moment as in 268. Brun–Titchmarsh on cells of length d hP transfers the statement to prime endpoints; moving the start changes the length, but both endpoints move by O(d hP). For the partner count in a relative subband of width η enclose its endpoint between (1+h_±)p with h_± comparable to P^(2δ−1)log P and relative error O_c(η)+o(1) in the length. The remaining steps and the domination of tails are those of the constant 4c. Consequently the critical coefficient described for the edge by the sum over extreme zeros also holds for δ≤1/12; β<1/2+3δ has not been established unconditionally in that range, nor is the equality of the critical coefficient decided.

**Second-order precision when compensating a tie.** Fix 0<δ<1/2, s=δ−1/2, β=1/2+δ and H(n)=c n^δ(log n+b) with b real fixed and c>0. At this edge the pair computation gives, with t=log Y,
    (B_H−A)/Y^s = 4c exp(s²/2)(1+b/t+O(t⁻²)).
To justify the precision, the STRICT power saving in the mean square of the previous entry costs O(P^(−κ)) for some κ>0, uniformly in h comparable to P^(2δ−1)log P. It allows the use of tolerance (log P)^−4 and cells of length hP/(log P)^6 for the transfer: the endpoints change by O_δ(hP/(log P)^6) by Brun–Titchmarsh. By Chebyshev the number of exceptional primes is still O(P^(1−κ') ) for some κ'>0, even summing over a fixed power of log P of choices of h. Removing higher powers in the average with that tolerance still costs a proportion O(P^(−1/2)polylog P). Subdividing each dyadic box into relative bands of width ≍(log P)^−4 allows approximating the variable length by two fixed multiplicative lengths with relative error O((log P)^−4): q−p=2c p^(2δ)(2log p+b)(1+O(p^(2δ−1)log p)) at the threshold, by Taylor. The long PNT on these subbands has relative error smaller than every inverse power of log P by β<1 and 235. On |log(p²/Y)|≤log t, the Gaussian weight varies relatively by O((1+log t)t^-4) within a subband, and outside this strip the BT envelope gives error o(t^-K) in units of Y^s for every fixed K. This leaves the integral of 4c exp(su)g(u)(1+b/(t+u)) in u=log(p²/Y) over the central strip, with error O(t⁻²). Expanding the denominator there and integrating proves the formula. The squares are of order Y⁻¹/² and are absorbed.

If the extreme line is attained and all zeros off it have real part ≤β−η with η>0, fix c=sup T/(4 exp(s²/2)) as in the computation of the critical coefficient. Then FOR EACH b>0, B_H>1 eventually, with margin ≫Y^s/log Y. Indeed the term of A after normalising is −T(log Y)+O(Y^(−min(η,δ))) by the absolute Gaussian sum; the second positive term of the pairs uniformly dominates that error even when T attains its maximum. This admits infinitely many zeros on the extreme line. It does not decide b=0; for b<0 a sufficient recurrence speed to the supremum of T has not been proved. Without a gap the interior spectral error may exceed 1/log Y and the second conclusion does not follow.

**Quantitative recurrence for a finite front of rational rank at most two.** Under the hypotheses of the previous paragraph, the Gaussian multiplier gives exactly T(t)=exp(s²/2) Σ exp(−γ²/2) cos(γ(t+s)), counting both ordinates and multiplicities on the extreme line. The absolute sum is maximised at t=−s and returns arbitrarily close at large times by simultaneous approximation of any truncation and absolute control of the tail. Therefore the critical c is a quarter of the sum of exp(−γ²/2). For a finite front of rational rank two, write the ordinates as integer combinations of ω₁,ω₂ after clearing denominators, with ω₁>0. Take t+s=2πq/ω₁ at denominators of convergents of ω₂/ω₁. All phases lie within O(1/q) of multiples of 2π, with fixed constants, hence sup T−T(t)=O(t⁻²). In rank one there are exact returns. In both cases, with a spectral gap and critical c, any b<0 implies B_H<1 along a sequence by the preceding expansion. The rank, the existence of the front and the gap are hypotheses; b=0 remains open.

**Critical contact in local measure.** For β=1/2+δ attained, c=critical c and any fixed b, even without a gap, the set E of t=log Y with B_H(Y)≤1 has measure o(1) in EACH interval [u,u+P] as u→∞, for each fixed P>0. Indeed the normalised balance is Σ wγ(1−cos γ(t+s))+r(t), with wγ=exp((s²−γ²)/2)>0 and r(t)→0 in the ordinary sense. For the interior zeros this follows by dominated convergence via the summable Gaussian envelope, since each factor exp((Reρ−β)t) tends to zero. Choose an extreme ordinate γ≠0 (zeta has no real zeros in (0,1)). On E the distance from γ(t+s) to 2πZ is at most arccos(1−sup_{v≥u}|r(v)|/wγ) for large u. In a period 2π/|γ| the covered fraction is that angle divided by π; a fixed number of periods covers any interval of length P. This also proves zero upper Banach density on the logarithmic half-line. The result admits pointwise exceptions and uses the hypothesis on β.

**Unconditional improvement of the arithmetic floor via slightly longer boxes.** In the pair estimate for H=c n^δ log n, the previous liminf is at least 2c(1+δ²/32) exp((δ−1/2)²/2) for each δ in (0,1/2). Take up exactly the subbands of length D and the safe threshold L=(4c−ε)P^(2δ)log P from the proof of the factor 2. Fix e=δ²/16 and divide into ceil(D/((1+e)L)) equal boxes. Their length W is asymptotic to (1+e)L and never larger. Cauchy and the ordinary PNT give at least (1+e−o(1))DL/(2log²P) internal pairs p<q. If q−p>L, p and q lie in opposite strips of length ≤eL of their box. Brun–Titchmarsh in each strip gives at most 2eL/(δ log P) primes for large P, since log(eL)∼2δ log P. There are at most D/L boxes for P sufficiently large. The number of pairs to be removed is ≤4e²DL/(δ²log²P). In units DL/(2log²P) the factor 1+e−8e²/δ²−o(1)=1+δ²/32−o(1) remains. Integrate via positive minima and take the limits of the previous proof. It uses only upper estimates in the strips. It improves the composite floor even for δ≤1/12; the error of the prime mass A−1 keeps an unknown sign.

**Common shift of the boxes: absolute gain over one half.** There is an absolute κ>0 such that for each fixed 0<δ<1/2 and c>0 the liminf of (B_H−A)/Y^(δ−1/2) is ≥2c(1+κ)exp((δ−1/2)²/2). The starting scales may depend on δ,c. In the previous subband of length D comparable to ηP, use a grid of step W=(1+e)L translated uniformly modulo W. There are ≤D/W+2 boxes meeting the band. For EACH translation Cauchy and the long PNT give ≥(1+e−o(1))DL/(2log²P) distinct internal pairs. For an integer separation L<k≤W the probability of being in the same box is 1−k/W≤e. It suffices to control these pairs BEFORE selecting the grid.

In the upper-sieve proof for p,p+k of this round replace the length P of the residue count by D and take z=D^(1/20). The error O(z⁴) is uniform in k and the class counts have error O(1) per class in any translated interval. Since log D∼log P for fixed η, the ceiling is CD F(k)/log²P with C absolute and F(k)=∏_{ℓ|k,ℓ>2}(1+1/(ℓ−2)); for odd k the count is zero. The average of F over (L,W] is absolutely bounded in the limit for each fixed e: expand F(k)=Σ_{d|k}a_d with a_d=∏_{ℓ|d}1/(ℓ−2) over odd squarefree d. Σ a_d/d converges by the product and Σ_{d≤W}a_d=o(W) by convergence and truncation. Counting multiples gives Σ_{L<k≤W}F(k)≤eLΣ a_d/d+o(L). Therefore the expected cost of the bad pairs is ≤(C' e²+o(1))DL/(2log²P), with C' absolute. Choose e>0 fixed smaller than min(1,1/(2C')); then κ=e/2. The number of admissible pairs in the band dominates the retained average. Integrate as in the proof of the factor 2. The conclusion concerns only the size of the composite margin; its order in Y remains the same.

**Criterion by exceptional length with deficit truncated at root scale.** With H(n)=exp(√log n), count only the logarithmic length of the set U={Y:B_H(Y)<1−Y^(−1/2)}. The global sign is equivalent to the existence of a fixed η>0, X_j→∞ and C_j→∞ such that ∫_[X_j,C_j X_j]1_U(Y)dY/Y≤X_j^(−η). Under RH the set is eventually empty by the semiprime margin. If β>1/2, fix σ between 1/2 and β and use the band [X,CX] of the proof of recurrent crossings (C depends only on σ). For every target zero of abscissa b>σ, the positive filter and the isolation on the central subinterval applied to M(Y)=Y(A(Y)−1) give ∫ M_- dY/Y ≫_b X^b, where M_-=max(−M,0). The Gaussian multiplier does not vanish and the power remainder is O(√X). Outside U, M_-≤Y(B_H−A)+√Y≤X^(1/2+o(1)). On the whole band M_-≪_C X^β by absolute Gaussian summability. Dividing the remaining moment by this ceiling gives ∫_[X,CX]1_U dY/Y ≫_b X^(b−β). One can choose b>β−η/2 without requiring a maximum. If the endpoint is attained, there is exceptional length bounded below by a positive constant on each band. Thus the criterion tolerates arbitrarily deep failures concentrated on small sets. The sampling antecedent for S(p/2) already uses the moment-to-measure argument; here it is applied to the sieved observable with shifted threshold. The arithmetic estimate of the exceptional length remains pending.

**Local concentration of the deficit: a logarithm is gained even without an attained front.** In the preceding criterion X^(−η) may be replaced by exp(−η log X/log log X) for any fixed η>0. Indeed if β>1/2, on the same fixed band I=[0,log C] in v=log(Y/X) the exceptional measure is ≥exp(−o(t/log t)), t=log X. The gain over the previous bound requires comparing the ceiling of the oscillation with its LOCAL mass, not with the absolute ceiling X^β.

Fix 1/2<σ<β, the filter h of 2242 and its central interval J of length one. Write F(v) for the Gaussian sum over zeros with the sign of M, so that M(X exp v)=F(v)+O_C(√X) on I. For each target of abscissa b>σ, m=∫_J|F|≫_b X^b, and |∫hF|≪X^σ. Since h is a positive constant on J and bounded on I, ∫_I F_-≫m. On the complex disc |v|≤R=t^(1/4), each term has modulus at most X^β exp(O(R+1)) exp(−γ²/2+R|γ|). Completing the square and using the unit count, the total ceiling is X^β exp(O(√t)). For fixed ε>0 and n=ceil(8(β−b+ε)t/log t), the Taylor polynomial P_n at zero has uniform error o(X^(b−ε/2)) on I by Cauchy and the geometric tail. This also holds for b=β.

For a polynomial of degree n, sup_I |P_n|≤K_I^(n+1)∫_J|P_n|. Indeed divide J into n+1 equal cells and choose in the central half of each a node with modulus ≤2(n+1)∫_J|P_n|. In the Lagrange denominators the distances between nodes i,j are ≥|i−j|/(2(n+1)); the sum of the inverse products is bounded by [2(n+1)]^n 2^n/n!. The numerators cost at most max(1,|I|)^n. Absorb the linear factor into K_I. Therefore sup_I |F|≤2K_I^(n+1)m for large X. Outside the exceptional set F_-≤X^(1/2+o(1)) as before; hence |U∩I| in logarithmic coordinates is ≫K_I^(−n−1). The interval, the filter and K_I depend on σ but not on b. First take the lower limit of (log |U∩I|) log t/t, then b→β and ε↓0. Under RH U is still eventually empty. The proof improves the tolerance of the criterion, without providing the arithmetic bound on exceptions.

**Concentration by number of effective zeros.** For the same U it suffices that its length on growing bands be ≤exp(−√(log X)/(log log X)^k) for some fixed k≥0. If there is a right zero, fix 1/2<σ<b with a zero of abscissa b. Keep only the abscissas >σ of absolute height ≤2√t, t=log X, in the sum F of the previous paragraph. The discard on I is O_I(X^σ): the Gaussian tail costs O_I(X exp(−2t)poly(t)) by the unit count, and the left part is summed absolutely. The remaining sum G has N≪t^(q/2)polylog(t) distinct nodes by Ingham, q=3(1−σ)/(2−σ)<1. In particular ∫_J |G| is comparable to m≫X^b and the discard error is o(m).

Elementary propagation lemma: sup_I |G|≤exp(O_I(N+1))∫_J|G| for J a unit interval in I and exponents with real parts in [0,1]. To evaluate at y∈I choose a subcell of J of length 1/4 at distance ≥1/4 from y (one of the two extreme quarters). Let d be the distance to its centre, and orient the steps from y towards that centre. Take M=ceil(100(1+|I|)N) and let h vary between (d−1/32)/M and (d+1/32)/M. The nodes with indices M to M+N−1 lie in the subcell. In the reverse direction, the values from the last node to y form an exponential sequence with roots r_j=exp(±hρ_j) of modulus ≤exp(O_I(1/N)). Its generating series has denominator Π(1−r_j z) and numerator of degree <N determined by the N initial values. The coefficient norm of the numerator is ≤N max_initial |G| Π(1+|r_j|); the coefficient of order l of the inverse of the denominator has modulus ≤binom(l+N−1,N−1)max(1,max|r_j|)^l. Up to l=M+N both factors cost exp(O_I(N)), even with collisions between roots. Averaging over h each initial node runs over an interval of length ≥1/16 inside J; replacing the maximum by the sum costs only N. This proves the lemma without frequency separation constants.

The floor of ∫_I F_- from the previous paragraph, after discounting the complement of U, is ≫m; the pointwise ceiling just obtained is exp(O_I(N))m. Thus |U∩I|≥exp(−O_I(1+t^(q/2)polylog(t))) in logarithmic coordinates. Since q<1 is fixed in each exterior scenario, this exceeds the proposed threshold for any fixed k. A single target is used, without approximating the supremum or assuming it is attained. The upper arithmetic estimate has not been obtained.

**A single positive weight with effective cut at height log log X.** Change the sieve weight to w(u)=f(u)^2/∫f², f the inverse Fourier transform of exp(−cosh ξ), with phase exp(iuξ). Fix H(n)=exp(√log n) as before. For this observable B_w it suffices to prove that {Y:B_w(Y)<1−Y^(−1/2)} has logarithmic length ≤(log X)^(−η), for some η>0, on growing bands at arbitrarily high scales. It is important to change the observable also in the pending arithmetic estimate.

Indeed f is real and even and f(0)>0. Shifting the contour in ξ to height ±d, 0<d<π/2, gives |w(u)|≪_d exp(−2d|u|). Its transform is, up to positive normalisation, ∫exp(−a cosh v)dv with a=2cosh(z/2), by the product formula at real z and continuation to |Im z|<π. There Re a>0. With r=cosh v−1 the integral is 2exp(−a)∫₀^∞exp(−ar)/√(r(r+2))dr. The last factor never vanishes: each inverse power of exponent 1/2 is the Laplace transform of a positive measure by the gamma integral, and their product is too, by convolution. Integrating first in r gives ∫(a+x)⁻¹dμ(x), with strictly positive real part; the absolute interchange is verified at Re a. Moreover on |Im z|≤2, Re a≫exp(|Re z|/2), so the transform decays like O(exp(−c exp(|Re z|/2))) by the initial integral (cosh v≥1+v²/2).

Apply Mellin inversion to the von Mangoldt mass with weight w as in the Gaussian case: multiplier in s given by ∫w(u)exp((s−1)u)du, main pole 1 and zero residues with nonzero multipliers. Shift from Re s=2 to −1/2 along the usual heights avoiding zeros; the double exponential dominates the ceilings of the logarithmic derivative and the remainder for Y times the mass is O(Y^(−1/2)). Removing powers costs O(√Y) in that normalisation by Chebyshev and dyadic summation with 2d>2. Contamination by composites is still Y^(−1/2+o(1)): the previous absolute box count is summed with this exponential envelope in the logarithmic variable. For the floor √Y(B_w−A_w)→∞ a fixed band around p²/Y=1 where w is bounded below suffices; the pair boxes with cut c log n for arbitrarily large fixed c give the same floor linear in c. This proves the direction under RH.

If there is a zero of abscissa b>σ>1/2, the positive filter of 2242 still annihilates the same exponents and the isolation of the target keeps its multiplier. The local floor m≫X^b and the bound O(X^σ) on the signed moment are maintained. Now cut the right sum at height 4log t with t=log X: the absolute tail is O(X exp(−c' t²)) on the fixed band. By Ingham there remain N≪(log t)^q (log log t)^O(1)=o(log t) with q<1. The recurrence of the preceding entry gives adverse length ≥exp(−O_I(N+1))=t^(−o(1)), larger than t^(−η) for each fixed η. Proving that upper bound via the integers is pending; this change does not transfer it to the original Gaussian weight.

**Limit of choosing a fixed weight for an absolute spectral tail.** Let K be the transform of a fixed nonzero weight with two-sided exponential moment, and suppose one wants to guarantee sup_{x≥H}|K(x+iy)|≤X^(−a) for fixed a>0 on a fixed interior line of the strip. Then H=o(log log X) is impossible even allowing zeros of K. Indeed, translate the line to Im z=0, and take above it a substrip of width d>0 with |K|≤M. Choose an interior point x₀+id/2 where K≠0. The map exp(π(z−x₀)/d) sends the strip to the upper half-plane and that point to i. Jensen's inequality on the conformally equivalent disc, followed by Fatou for the nonnegative function log(M/|K|), bounds its boundary integral against harmonic measure by log(M/|K(x₀+id/2)|). On the lower edge the density is (2d)⁻¹sech(π(x−x₀)/d). Thus the mass of [H,H+1] weighs ≫exp(−πH/d); the assumed tail gives (a log X+log M)exp(−πH/d)≪1. In particular H≥(d/π)log log X−O(1). Boundary zeros are admitted by Fatou.

If K does not vanish on |Im z|<d and is bounded there, on the middle line there is a factor two better: u=log(M/|K|)>0 is harmonic and Harnack on the disc via tanh(πz/(4d)) gives u(x)≤u(0)exp(π|x|/(2d)). For the exp(−cosh) weight of the preceding entry, taking any d<π and then d↑π shows liminf H/log log X≥2 on the real line. Conversely the integral with 2cosh(x/2) gives K(x)≪exp(−c exp(x/2)), so H=2log log X+O_a(1) suffices there. This optimal threshold refers to the continuous envelope of a fixed multiplier. The argument does not prevent using discrete locations of zeros or cancellation between terms, nor does it directly limit the measure of the arithmetic exceptional set.

**On bands [X,X²] it suffices to control o(1/log log X) of exceptional length.** For the exp(−cosh) weight w, if there is a right zero then on EACH sufficiently high such band the logarithmic length of U is ≫1/log log X. The allowed band width in the criterion is changed: a subsequence of these specific bands suffices. Selecting the maximum gives an alternative proof whose total length bound is surpassed by the following sum over fixed bands.

Write T=log X, t=log Y, fix a zero of abscissa b>σ>1/2 and form G(t) with the terms of zeros of abscissa >σ and absolute height ≤4log T of the balance Y(A_w−1), multiplied by exp(−σt). Its exponents are λ+iγ with 0<λ≤1 and the sum of moduli of the coefficients is absolutely bounded. On [T,2T] the error for the normalised balance is O(1) by the double exponential cut already proved (also for the semiprimes after this normalisation). Isolation on a unit interval at t=3T/2+O(1) gives sup |G|≫exp((b−σ)3T/2). Multiply G by D(t)=exp(−100(t−3T/2)²/T) and call A the global absolute maximum of DG. It is exponentially large and is attained at t₀ between 1.1T and 1.9T: outside there the ceiling D(t)exp(max(t,0)) is exponentially small.

One has ||(DG)'||∞≪A log T. Indeed the transform of a damped term has modulus, up to constant and coefficient, √T exp(3λT/2+λ²T/400)exp(−T(ξ−γ)²/400). Outside |ξ|≤4log T+100 the L¹ norm weighted by 1+|ξ| is O(exp(−T)) after summing coefficients. The cut inside the interval therefore has supremum ≤A+O(exp(−T)); its derivative is bounded by O(log T) times that supremum. For this, convolve with the inverse of a smooth function equal to 1 on the band and with double support, whose derivative has L¹ norm of the order of the width by rescaling. Thus |DG|≥A/2 at distance ≤c/log T from the maximum. In any neighbourhood of fixed radius of t₀ the ratio D(t)/D(t₀) lies between uniform positive constants.

Translate the filter of 2242 so that its unit plateau is centred at t₀. For G use the density h(v)exp(σv), positive and bounded, with a lower bound on the plateau: its integral against each term of G is exactly zero by the annihilation of the original exponent. Hence the negative integral of G on the support is ≫A/(D(t₀)log T). There |G|≪A/D(t₀), and outside U the negative part is O(1) by the normalised error. Dividing gives the announced length. Under RH U is eventually empty. The wider band offers room to choose the reference point; this rate is not claimed on every band of fixed ratio.

**Correction of scope by summing fixed bands.** For the exp(−cosh) weight, in logarithmic coordinates let E be the adverse set. If there is an exterior zero, there is a fixed d>0 such that for each ε>0 and every sufficiently large r, |E∩[r,r+d]|≥r^(−ε), by the paragraph on the cut at height 4log r. In [u,v] with u→∞ and v−u→∞ there fit floor((v−u)/d) complete disjoint intervals. Each contributes at least v^(−ε). The adverse fraction is therefore ≥v^(−ε)/(2d) for v−u≥2d. On [X,X²] the total logarithmic length is (log X)^(1−o(1)) if RH fails, stronger than the peak bound of the previous entry. To close it suffices, for example, to have total length O(√log X) on a subsequence of [X,X²], or in general fraction O(v^(−η)) on growing logarithmic bands for some fixed η>0. Under RH E is eventually empty. A fraction o(1) without a rate does not by itself decide this criterion.

**Size and arithmetic distribution of the margin for H=exp(√log n).** For the exp(−cosh) weight w one has unconditionally B_w(Y)−A_w(Y) ≍ H(Y)/(√Y log Y). Moreover the pairs whose index difference in the sequence of primes is ≤r contribute only O((1+r)/√Y), including squares. In particular for r=o(H(Y)/log Y) their relative contribution tends to zero.

On each subband [P,(1+η)P] with P=√Y and η small and fixed such that w is bounded below on the products, put L=H(Y) and divide into boxes of length ≤L asymptotic to L. All internal pairs are admitted. More precisely, if p is required to have at least k internal successors, in each box at most k primes fail (only the last k). By the long PNT the fraction of failing primes is ≤(1+o(1))k log P/L for k≥1. Taking k=floor(L/(4log P)), at least two thirds of the primes have k forward partners for large P, giving ≫PL/log²P pairs with weight ≫log P/P². This localises the floor on many distinct factors without short PNT.

For the ceiling, every large admitted composite is pq with p≤q∼p and q−p≪H(p²). For p∈[P,2P] the upper pair sieve of this round summed up to k≪H(P²) gives O(PH(P²)/log²P) distinct pairs: the ceiling per k is uniform and the sum of the singular factors is O(H(P²)) by divisor expansion. The squares contribute O(Y^(−1/2)). In each block the weight leaves O(H(P²)/(P log P) exp(−a|log(P²/Y)|)) for some a>1. The inequality H(P²)/H(Y)≤exp(√|log(P²/Y)|) allows summation: for P²≥√Y one has log P≫log Y, and in the rest the exponential decay absorbs that denominator. For the rank restriction it suffices to count at most r partners per prime and apply Chebyshev in each block, with total cost O((1+r)/√Y). Thus the composite margin can only compensate prime-mass deficits up to the indicated order, even summing all ranks. The frequency of those deficits has not been controlled.

**The signed average on [X,X²] always has favourable subsequences.** For the same B_w and J(t)=∫_[t,2t](B_w(exp v)−1)dv, RH implies J(t)>0 eventually by the previous margin. If there is a zero of abscissa b>1/2, for each 0<ε<b−1/2 there are arbitrarily large t with J(t)>exp((b−1−ε)t) and also with J(t)<−exp((b−1−ε)t). Therefore the signed average along a subsequence is an insufficient test even for the true primes; eventual nonnegativity of that average is equivalent to the goal.

Indeed let L(s) be the Laplace transform from zero of f(t)=B_w(exp t)−1. By the previous explicit formula it is meromorphic on Re s>−1/2. The zero terms are simple fractions with poles at λ=ρ−1, residues nonzero by the zero-free transform of the weight and multiplicity; the series converges normally away from the poles by the double exponential decay. The remainder is holomorphic there by the composite bound exp(−t/2+o(t)) and the power bound. No pole is real, including s=0. By Fubini for Re s>0 the transform of J is (L(s/2)−L(s))/s, regular at zero by Taylor. Start from λ with Re λ=b−1 and divide by two as long as the half is still a pole. The process terminates by discreteness and regularity at zero. At the last point λ' the second function L(s) has a pole and the first is regular, with Re λ'≥b−1. This covers even sup Reρ=1 without an extreme front.

If J were eventually ≤exp(at) with a=b−1−ε, the transform of exp(at)−J would have a nonreal pole with real part >a and would be regular on the whole real half-line (a,∞). This contradicts Landau's theorem for an eventually nonnegative function: its abscissa of convergence, at least Re λ', would have to be singular on the real axis. The same argument applies to exp(at)+J. The impossibility concerns replacing the exception count by ONE signed balance on selected bands; the estimate of the adverse fraction remains open.

**Comparison with 254: the semiprime margin delays the first negative order by an additional power.** Consider m_n(s)=∫₀^∞t^n exp(−st)(B_w(exp t)−1)dt/n!, s>0. It is the disc geometry of 254 with centre shifted by one unit: write λ=ρ−1 and r=s+1/2. If there is an exterior zero, let s_* be the first centre for which |s_*−λ|=s_*+1/2 for some exterior λ. It exists and is positive by the discrete minimum of 254. Let r_*=s_*+1/2 and k=max (Re λ+1/2)/r_*² over the contact points. For some fixed N₀ and d↓0 the least n≥N₀ with m_n(s_*+d)<0 satisfies n∼1/(r_* k²d²). The initial orders whose sign has not been certified for this observable are excluded. The geometric boundary was already in 254. The change relative to the transition of order 1/d for that observable comes from the unconditional size of the semiprime margin.

Indeed in the units r^(n+1)m_n the composite term is positive and its logarithm is √(n/r)+O(log(n+2)), uniformly for s in a compact neighbourhood of the contact and n large. By the previous arithmetic floor and ceiling it is equivalent, up to bounded factors, to the expectation of exp(√t)/t for large t under Gamma(n+1,r) (rate r). The window |t−(n+1)/r|≤2√(n+1)/r has probability ≥3/4 and there √t=√(n/r)+O(1). For the ceiling apply the tangent of √t at n/r and the generating function (1−u/r)^(-(n+1)) with u=1/(2√(n/r)); the Taylor remainder of the logarithm costs O(1). A fixed initial interval contributes a factorially small amount. The contribution of the prime powers removed from the von Mangoldt formula is O(1) in these units by its ceiling O(exp(−t/2)); the contour error is too. Each zero term contributes a fixed nonzero coefficient times (r/(s−λ))^(n+1). The non-tangent ones have total modulus O(θ^n) with θ<1 uniform for nearby s by discreteness and summability.

For a contact j, log(r/|s−λ_j|)=k_j d+O(d²) with k_j=(Re λ_j+1/2)/r_*². The maximum k belongs to a single conjugate pair of positions, since the abscissa and the distance to the centre fix |Im λ|. For any fixed ε in (0,1), up to n≤(1−ε)/(r_*k²d²) the margin exp(√(n/r)+O(log n)) dominates the sum of contacts for n sufficiently large; N₀ can be fixed independently of ε, by eventual strict positivity at d=0 and continuity for the finitely many intermediate orders. Near n=(1+ε)/(r_*k²d²) the maximal pair exponentially dominates both the margin and the other contacts. Its phase advances by arg(1/(s−λ)), not real. Within a bounded number of steps a cosine ≤−c appears with c>0 uniform for nearby s: for the limiting angle every initial rotation meets that arc (in the rational case the orbit has at least three equally spaced points); compactness and continuity give uniformity. A negative order appears in that block. Sending ε↓0 gives the equivalent. This quantifies the difficulty of detection by high moments; it does not prove a new free zone.

**Resolution of the transition that the arithmetic count permits.** Under the same hypotheses and with N₀ sufficiently large, let λ_* be the fast contact, a=log(r/|s−λ_*|)>0 and n_c=1/(r a²). For the first negative order above N₀ one has
    n_first = n_c − 2 log(n_c)/a + O(1/a).
In units of d, the term added to the main term 1/(r_*k²d²) is −4log(1/d)/(kd)+O(1/d). Indeed for the gamma variable of the previous computation, from half its mean μ onwards the factor 1/t≤2/μ is retained in the tangent ceiling. Between a fixed initial cut and μ/2 the ceiling is O(exp(√(μ/2))), which is absorbed into exp(√μ)/μ. The same central Chebyshev interval gives the floor with 1/t≫1/μ. Thus the logarithm of the normalised composite contribution is √(n/r)−log n+O(1), uniformly, without an exact pair asymptotic.

Put D(n)=na−√(n/r)+log n. Near n_c its slope is a/2+O(a²+a³|n−n_c|) and D(n_c)=log n_c. At n_*=n_c−2log(n_c)/a one has D(n_*)=o(1) by Taylor (error O(a log² n_c)). On [0.9n_c,1.1n_c] the slope is comparable to a. The slow contacts are exponentially smaller than the fast one in this band. Below a negative constant level of D all orders there give a positive sign; above a positive constant level there is a negative one in a block of length bounded by the phase rotation already proved. The orders from N₀ to 0.9n_c are covered by the previous argument. This encloses the first negative within distance O(1/a) of n_*.

The scale of that error does matter if one tries to deduce more solely from the comparable semiprime bounds. In the weighted observable A_w+M(B_w−A_w) with fixed M≥1, the logarithm of the margin adds exactly log M. The criterion D(n)<log M−C suffices for positivity in the transition band, with C independent of M by the fixed ceiling of the zero contributions and the initial composite floor. For the original weight M=1 a negative already exists before D(n)=C' with C' fixed (increase C' to include the phase block). Taking log M>C+C'+2 separates the two first negatives by ≫1/a using the upper bound on the slope; the previous positivity for M=1 is preserved when increasing the weight. Both composite counts satisfy the same arithmetic order. This limits the precision deducible from that order alone; for M=1 it does not exclude a finer term obtained by other means.

**Fixed subset of semiprimes with exact asymptotic margin at full scale.** For H(n)=exp(√log n) and the exp(−cosh) weight w, there is an explicit binary selection of distinct products among the original survivors whose mass E₀ satisfies
    E₀(Y) ∼ (1/2) [∫ exp(−u/2)w(u)du] H(Y)/(√Y log Y).
The selection is the same for all Y. On each band [P_m,P_{m+1}) with P_m=exp(√m), D=P_{m+1}−P_m and L=H(P_m²), divide into ceil(D/L) equal boxes. Enumerate lexicographically the primes p<q in the same box and keep the first floor(DL/(4log² P_m)) products, or all of them if that quota is not reached. Bands and boxes are half-open. The ordinary quantitative PNT with error o(P/log³ P) for π(P) against li(P) gives (1+o(1))D/log P primes, since D∼P/(2log P). By Cauchy there are ≥(1/2−o(1))DL/log²P internal pairs: the diagonal term is negligible since L/log P→∞. Every sufficiently high quota is thus filled. Each pair satisfies √(pq)−p≤(q−p)/2≤L/2<H(pq). Unique factorisation avoids duplicates.

For fixed |log(P²/Y)|≤K the variation of u=log(pq/Y) within each band is O(1/log Y). The error of replacing w by its value at u_m=log(P_m²/Y) is o(1) absolute uniform by continuity, even at the zeros of the weight. Rounding of the quota has uniform relative error o(1). On the compact set the sum therefore corresponds to the integral of H(p²) w(log(p²/Y))/(2p²log p) dp, with error o(H(Y)/(√Y log Y)). After the change p=√Y exp(u/2), the ratio H(p²)/H(Y) tends uniformly to 1, leaving the announced factor 1/2. For |u|>K the selection is a subset of the sieve and the exponential dyadic ceiling from the margin-size entry gives normalised tail o_K(1) as K→∞. The first incomplete bands are negligible.

Thus A_w+E₀ is an explicit arithmetic minorant with margin known to leading order and keeps the exceptional fraction criterion: under RH it dominates the deficit O(Y^(−1/2)); with an exterior zero the normalised error in the filter proof is O(1) because E₀≪Y^(−1/2+o(1)). The result gives a constant for this subset of full order, not for the mass of all pairs. The frequency of the prime deficit at that threshold remains pending.

**The true counts of the quota bands, even by classes, do not control the deficit.** Construct two fixed sets of integers with exactly as many elements as primes in EACH band [P_m,P_{m+1}) of the previous construction. For each fixed modulus q they moreover respect exactly the true count of each class in each sufficiently high band. Despite this their masses with weight (log n)w(log(n/Y))/n are 1+1/(4log Y)+o(1/log Y) and 1−1/(4log Y)+o(1/log Y), respectively, at EVERY large scale. The difference exceeds the margin available from semiprimes. The antecedent of the mesh of 2142 was local and that of 2288 imitated densities in progressions; here the true histograms of π on the prescribed bands are preserved with a computed bias.

Let P=P_m, D=P_{m+1}−P, l=log P and h=log(P_{m+1}/P)∼1/(2l). Choose Q=lcm(1,…,k) with k maximal such that Q≤√l for m large. In each class modulo Q select the first N_a available integers of the band for the left model, or the last N_a for the right one, N_a being the true number of primes of that class. There is capacity by construction. With N=ΣN_a∼D/l, the selected points lie at most Q(N+1)=O(D/√l) from the corresponding endpoint. Fixed moduli eventually divide Q. In the initial bands use the primes themselves.

Write t=log Y, u=l−t, F(x)=(log x)w(log(x/Y))/x. On each band compare N F(endpoint) with ∫_P^(P+D) F(x)dx/log x. PNT with error O(P/log^K P) for each fixed K replaces N by ∫dx/log x with summable error o(1/t) after weighting. The first-order expansion around P gives, in the right model, main difference F'(P)D²/(2l), with the opposite sign in the left one. Indeed the mean position under dx/log x is P+D/2+O(Dh) and F'(P)=[l(w'(u)−w(u))+w(u)]/P². Replacing the selected positions by the endpoint costs O(h/√l) relative to the local reference mass with an envelope for w,w'; the second-order remainder costs O(h²). For precision, w,w',w'' are bounded by O(exp(−a|u|)) with a>1 by the same contour shift of f, which tolerates polynomial frequency factors. On |u|≤10log t all l are t+O(log t); the previous errors sum to o(1/t) and the PNT errors there sum to O(t^(2−K)) up to logarithmic factors. Outside that range the count N≪D/l and the envelope give o(1/t) both in the sum and in the integral. The main sum is written Σ h²(w'(u)−w(u))/2+o(1/t); since h∼1/(2t) in the central zone, the Riemann sum gives (1/(4t))∫(w'−w)=−1/(4t). The reference integral tends to 1 with exponential error.

Even adding all products of two members with difference ≪H(p²) by smaller factor p, the additional mass is ≤Y^(−1/2+o(1)) by integer counting in dyadic blocks, even with multiplicities. Therefore one of these two models fails the adverse threshold at every large scale and the other satisfies it at all of them. This refutes a deduction from the histograms alone. The constructed sets do not satisfy the global primality condition.

**Critical resolution of a true prime histogram for the sieve margin.** Put S(x)=exp(√log x)/(√x log x). Fix α>0, partition the integers into consecutive bands with left endpoint P and length D=floor(αP S(P)) from P sufficiently large onwards. Keep the true number N of primes in each band. For each Y consider all possible masses using subsets of integers with exactly those same counts. Their diameter (supremum minus infimum) is
    (α J+o(1))S(Y),    J=∫ exp(−u/2)|w'(u)−w(u)|du>0.
The extreme configurations may depend on Y. This determines the cost of using only this histogram, at the same scale as the margin computed by quotas. PNT on bands of length D is not presupposed.

Indeed Brun–Titchmarsh implies N≪D/log P, since log D∼(log P)/2. For F(x)=(log x)w(log(x/Y))/x, the diameter per band is obtained by choosing the N largest or smallest values of F. Replacing F by its linearisation at P costs O(ND² sup|F''|) in the diameter. For a linear function the diameter is exactly |F'(P)|N(D−N) on the D integers of the band. Replacing D−N by D costs O(ND|F'(P)|/log P). The diameters add up by independence between bands and absolute convergence. For fixed |u|=|log(P/Y)|≤K one has D/P∼αS(Y)exp(−u/2) uniformly and F'(P)=P⁻²[(log P)(w'−w)(u)+w(u)]. Since D/P→0, the errors when summing over that compact set are o(S(Y)): the sums of N log P/P are bounded by Chebyshev. Each P may be replaced by the primes it represents in every continuous function on the compact set, with error o(1) in normalised units. The ordinary PNT gives convergence of Σ_p(log p)/p δ_{log(p/Y)} to du on compact sets. The integral J restricted to |u|≤K is obtained.

For the tails the ceiling ND sup|F'| suffices, summing N as true primes in dyadic blocks. For P≥√Y, S(P)/S(Y)≤2exp(−u/2+√|u|) and w,w' decay like exp(−a|u|) with a>1. For P<√Y the additional factor log Y/log P is absorbed into the exponential tail. The fixed initial bands are negligible. Taking K→∞ completes the proof. J is positive since w'=w on the whole line is incompatible with ∫w=1 and its decay.

Application to the quota minorant: if C₀=(1/2)∫exp(−u/2)w(u)du and αJ<C₀, even the lower extreme of the histogram plus E₀ keeps an eventual positive margin under RH. Conversely that extreme is ≤A_w, so its drops with E₀ include all those of the true minorant. The exceptional length criterion is preserved for this lower extreme computable from the counts alone (and E₀ can be replaced by C₀S by the same proof under RH and the subpower error in the presence of an exterior zero). There is no new arithmetic estimate on the frequency of those drops.

**Position of the true primes and threshold of the lower extreme.** For the previous histogram let A_min,A_max be its extremes. Unconditionally A_w−A_min∼A_max−A_w∼(αJ/2)S(Y). In particular, UNDER RH, (A_min+E₀−1)/S(Y)→C₀−αJ/2. If α<2C₀/J, the exception criterion for the worst arrangement remains equivalent to the goal. If α>2C₀/J, that arrangement falls below 1−1/√Y at every sufficiently high scale even under RH. Equality is not decided at leading order.

To see this, in each box the midpoint of the two extreme sums of the affine function is exactly N times its value at the centre of the D integer slots, since the N minimal and maximal slots are reflections. The quadratic errors sum to o(S) as before. It suffices to show that the centred linear moment Σ F'_Y(P)(p−P−(D−1)/2) is o(S). On a compact set of u it reduces, after dividing by S and splitting into a fixed number of dyadic blocks [Z,2Z], to integrating the bounded function (x−P−(D−1)/2)/D against Σ(log p)δ_p/Z with a smooth multiplier at scale Z: indeed Z D F'_Y(P)/(S log p) is uniformly approximable by α(Z/p)exp(−u/2)(w'−w)(u) there. The tails are dominated by the absolute ceiling of the previous diameter.

In each block smooth the prime measure by averaging over intervals of length l=Z^(1/3). The smoothed density converges to 1 in L¹(dx/Z) on the block by the PNT in almost all short intervals used in 268 and the uniform Brun–Titchmarsh ceiling O(1) for the density weighted by log p. The effect on the original integral is o(1): at distance >l from the box endpoints the centred sawtooth varies by at most l/min D=o(1), and the smooth multiplier varies by o(1). In the edge strips the weighted prime mass costs O(l) per endpoint by Brun–Titchmarsh, and there are O(1+Z/min D) endpoints; their total is o(Z). The two cuts of the block are treated alike. Against dx the sawtooth has mean O(1/D) on each complete box and the multiplier varies by o(1) on it. The boxes cut by the block have length o(Z). Therefore the weighted mean tends to zero and the moment is o(S). The term A_w−1 under RH is O(1/√Y)=o(S), whence the threshold. For subcritical α and failure of RH the adverse inclusion is preserved by A_min≤A_w.

**One additional arithmetic bit per box allows width P^(3/4).** In addition to the count N store a left/right decision in each box [P,P+D) with P an integer, D=floor(P^(3/4)). With these data one constructs a fixed set of integers whose mass A_bit satisfies |A_bit(Y)−A_w(Y)|≪Y^(−1/2) for ALL large Y, without RH. Since this is o(S(Y)), A_bit+C₀S keeps the exceptional length criterion. It is a compression of the position data: the bit does use prime information beyond the count. The cumulative rounding of 102–103 was already applied to selecting squares; here it controls the linear moment lost by histograms and pays a second derivative of the weight.

In each box the N leftmost and the N rightmost integers minimise and maximise the sum of the N positions. Let R be the cumulative balance of sums of prime positions minus reconstructed ones, starting at zero and copying a finite prefix. Choose between the two options the one leaving the smaller modulus of the new R, ties broken to the left. If the two options straddle zero, the new modulus is ≤ND; if not, one of them does not increase the previous modulus because the true sum lies between the extremes. By induction |R|≤historical max ND≪P^(3/2)/log P at high endpoints, by Brun–Titchmarsh. The same argument can be implemented with positions relative to the endpoint, because the counts coincide.

For F(x)=(log x)w(log(x/Y))/x, the constant Taylor part at P disappears exactly. The quadratic error is ≪Σ N D² sup_box|F''|. In a block [Z,2Z] there are O(1+Z^(1/4)) endpoints, N≪D/log Z and |F''|≪(log Z) Z^(−3)exp(−a|log(Z/Y)|) for a>1. This gives O(Z^(−1/2) exp(−a|log(Z/Y)|)) per block. The sum of linear parts is Σ F'(P)ΔR. By global Abel summation it costs at most the sum of |R| times the consecutive differences of F', estimated by D sup|F''|, with the same cost per block. The initial and final endpoints do not contribute (copied prefix and |R F'|→0). Summing dyadic blocks gives O(Y^(−1/2)). Under RH the margin C₀S dominates the true and reconstruction errors. With an exterior zero the change to the balance used in the filter after multiplying by Y^(1−σ), σ>1/2, is still o(1), even with the term C₀S. The adverse-length floor of the proof for fixed bands and their sum is therefore preserved. No favourable count of boxes or bits follows.

**Counts alone with a cut independent of the primes, at width P^(2/3).** Fix integer boxes [P,P+D) with D=floor(P^(2/3)). In each one independently choose a single cut U uniform on [P,P+D], before observing the primes. Store the two counts on either side. For the approximate mass assign those with p≤U to the endpoint P and the rest to P+D, with multiplicity. For almost every choice of the mesh, once fixed forever,
    |A_mesh(Y)−A_w(Y)| ≪_mesh Y^(−1/2)log(2Y) = o(S(Y))
uniformly as Y grows. The endpoints and their multiplicities represent a quadrature rule. In contrast with the previous arithmetic bit, the only prime data it consumes are counts on prescribed intervals. The result is almost sure for the fixed true primes, not uniform over all sets compatible with the observed counts.

In a box, let e be the sum of represented positions minus the true one. The probability of sending p to the upper endpoint is (p−P)/D. Therefore E[e]=0 without assuming independence between primes in the same box. The e are independent between boxes and |e|≤ND≪D²/log P by Brun–Titchmarsh. In a block of endpoints P∈[Z,2Z), Z=2^j, there are O(Z^(1/3)) boxes and the sum of variances is O(Z³/log²Z). By Kolmogorov's maximal inequality the probability that some partial sum of the block exceeds Z^(3/2) in modulus is O(1/log² Z). Summing over j and by Borel–Cantelli, almost surely ALL blocks have partial maximum O_mesh(Z^(3/2)), absorbing the finitely many initial ones. This event does not depend on Y.

With F(x)=(log x)w(log(x/Y))/x apply Taylor at P. The constant term is preserved and the quadratic error of the block is ≪Σ N D² sup|F''|≪Z^(−2/3)exp(−a|log(Z/Y)|), a>1. For the linear one, Abel on the block gives cost ≤partial maximum times (sup|F'|+ΣD sup|F''|), of order O_mesh(Z^(−1/2)log(2Z)exp(−a|log(Z/Y)|)). The dyadic sum gives the statement simultaneously in Y. Thus A_mesh+C₀S keeps the previous adverse length criterion: under RH it has an eventual margin; in the presence of an exterior zero the error is o(1) in the normalisation Y^(1−σ) of the filter. The number of counts in a dyadic block is O(Z^(1/3)); the arithmetic bound on their deficits remains unproved.

**Resolution limit for the random rule without correction.** For D=floor(P^θ), fixed 2/3<θ<1, and the true primes, under the law of the independent cuts one has, without RH,
    (A_mesh(Y)−A_w(Y))/Y^((3θ−3)/2) ⇒ Normal(0,Vθ),
    Vθ=(1/12)∫ exp((3θ−3)u)(w'(u)−w(u))² du >0.
Therefore for each fixed M the probability of precision ≤M S(Y) tends to zero. Under RH, after adding the margin C₀S the probability (over meshes, at a given scale Y) of a false drop below 1−Y^(−1/2) tends to 1/2. This explains why widening the mesh of the preceding entry to a fixed higher exponent spoils ITS estimator; it does not exclude other uses of the two counts.

For a cut U=P+Dv, the fraction of primes sent to P is their empirical distribution function G_P(v). By the short PNT of 238, N∼D/log P and G_P(v)→v uniformly: apply the theorem on a fixed subdivision, then refine it by monotonicity. θ>7/12 is available with margin. The linear error e in positions divided by ND is 1−G_P(v) minus its mean over v, by the exact unbiasedness already proved. It has variance 1/12+o(1), even though all primes in the box share v. For fixed |log(P/Y)|≤K, summing F'(P)² Var(e) amounts to integrating (1/12)p^(3θ−4)(w'(log(p/Y))−w(log(p/Y)))² dp, with error o(Y^(3θ−3)); the Riemann step is D. Each centred random summand is bounded by O_K(Y^(2θ−2)), which divided by Y^((3θ−3)/2) tends to zero. Lindeberg gives the normal on the compact set when its limiting variance is positive. The variance of each exterior dyadic block p∼Z is ≪Z^(3θ−3) exp(−2a|log(Z/Y)|) by BT and independence; the normalised tails become arbitrarily small as K grows. The total quadratic Taylor remainder is O(Y^(2θ−2)) by the same block sum as in the preceding entry. This proves convergence in distribution for the difference without additional centring. Vθ>0 because w'=w cannot hold identically. The probabilistic limit does not establish a density of drops for each fixed mesh.

**Overcoming the 2/3 limit by quadrature of the cumulative error of π.** Fix ANY 0<θ<1. On consecutive boxes [P,P+D), D=floor(P^θ), take a uniform independent point U in each. It suffices to know π(U), equivalently a count between consecutive points plus the initial one. Define R(x)=π(x)−∫₂ˣ dv/log v for x≥2 and F(x)=(log x)w(log(x/Y))/x. The estimator is
    A_corr(Y)=∫₂^∞ F(x)dx/log x − Σ D F'(U)R(U).
The corresponding exact identity has ∫₂^∞ F'(x)R(x)dx in place of the sum, by integration by parts including the atom at 2 (R(2−)=0). The rule integrates the continuous term exactly and estimates only the remainder. It is unbiased box by box and the tails converge absolutely. It also admits the variant with two local counts: centre R at P in each box and add F(P+D)(R(P+D)−R(P)) with the box convention (P,P+D], accounting for the prefix. The following proof directly uses the cumulative version.

Let β=sup Reρ. By the ceiling of 235 and partial summation, R(x)≪_ε x^(β+ε). For dyadic Z the variables Δ=D R(U)−∫_P^(P+D)R(x)dx are independent and centred and have total variance O(Z^(1+θ+2β+2ε)). Kolmogorov and Borel–Cantelli bound simultaneously all partial sums of each block by O_mesh,ε(Z^((1+θ)/2+β+ε)log Z). Freezing F' at P and summing by Abel costs this ceiling times O(Z^(−2)log Z exp(−a|log(Z/Y)|)), with a>2 available. The remainder from freezing costs per box ≤2D² sup|R|sup|F''|, so that the block costs O(Z^(β+θ−2+ε)log Z exp(−a|log(Z/Y)|)). Summing the dyadic tails and absorbing logarithms, for each ε>0 and almost every mesh
    A_corr(Y)−A_w(Y)=O_mesh,ε(Y^(β−1−(1−θ)/2+ε)).
A single event serves for all Y and all ε by countable intersection. In particular under RH the error is o(Y^(−1/2)); if β>1/2 choose σ strictly between max(1/2,β−(1−θ)/2) and β, and then a zero of abscissa b>σ and ε sufficiently small. The error is o(Y^(σ−1)), absorbed by the exceptional length filter. Thus A_corr+C₀S keeps the equivalence of the criterion, although the estimator is signed and although β is not a maximum. Computing the rule does not require knowing β. There are O(Z^(1−θ)) samples in [Z,2Z] for each fixed θ. The reduction is not uniform as θ→1; the balances of π at the samples remain to be estimated.

**Direct reading of the exterior abscissa with two sampling parameters.** Number the previous boxes by consecutive integers j and take U_j=P_j+D_j{ja+b}, with a single uniform pair (a,b) on the unit torus for the whole mesh. For each fixed θ in (0,1) and almost every (a,b),
    β=max(1/2, limsup_j log(1+|π(U_j)−∫₂^{U_j}dx/log x|)/log U_j).
Therefore in this rule a root bound with subpower loss for the sampled cumulative counts suffices. It is a condition on ALL sufficiently high samples for each loss ε, distinct from the exceptional length criterion on a subsequence of bands. No explicit numerical pair is designated, and the limsup is not identified without the truncation at 1/2 under RH.

For j≠k the coordinates {ja+b},{ka+b} are independent uniform, since the integer homomorphism of the torus with rows (j,1),(k,1) has nonzero determinant and its image is the whole torus, so it preserves Haar as image measure. The Δ of the proof by parts are centred and pairwise orthogonal. For n boxes in a block pad with zeros up to a power of two. Each prefix decomposes into at most 1+ceil(log₂ n) dyadic intervals, so by Cauchy the squared partial maximum is bounded by that factor times the sum of squares of ALL interval sums of the hierarchy. By orthogonality the expectation of that sum at each level is the sum of variances. The total cost is O(log²(2n)) in the second moment, absorbable together with the Borel–Cantelli factor into Z^ε. The uniform estimate for A_corr of the previous entry is preserved without requiring joint independence.

The ceiling of the limsup follows from the global ceiling for R. For the converse, if β>1/2 and the limsup were smaller, choose σ strictly between max(1/2,limsup,β−(1−θ)/2) and β. One has |R(U_j)|≪U_j^σ. By absolute summation in blocks the discrete part of A_corr is O(Y^(σ−1)log Y): for Z≤P<2Z widths O(Z) are summed and |F'|≪log Z·Z^(−2)exp(−a₀|log(Z/Y)|), a₀>2. The continuous integral equals 1+O(Y^(−a₀)). The reconstruction error stays below that exponent by taking ε small. But for any target of abscissa b₀>σ the isolation proof gives ∫_J |Y exp(v)(A_w(Y exp(v))−1)|dv≫Y^b₀ on a fixed band. Contradiction with O(Y^σ log Y). The argument also holds when the supremum is not attained. The same generic pair can be used for all θ in any prescribed countable list by intersecting full-measure events.

**Deterministic sampling of both signs, even at tenth powers.** For R(x)=π(x)−∫₂ˣdv/log v and any increasing unbounded sequence x_j with x_{j+1}−x_j≪x_j^θ, 0<θ<1 fixed, the maximum of 1/2 and the limsup exponent of EACH of the two parts R_± at the nodes is β. One uses log(1+R_±)/log x. In particular one can directly fix x_j=j^k for any fixed integer k≥2. There are no exceptional seeds. Antecedents: the two-parameter sampling entry obtained the absolute value almost surely by quadrature; the transfer to primes of 2158 used density for existence in intervals. Here a ceiling for the INCREMENT OF THE ERROR is required, smaller in exponent than the exterior error, even when θ>β.

If β>1/2 fix σ∈(1/2,β), q=3(1−σ)/(2−σ)<1. In [X,2X] for distance H≤C X^θ the difference of the error θ_pr(y)−y between two points is
    O((X^σ+X^(β−(1−θ)(1−q))) log^C₁ X).
Use the truncated explicit formula of 235 at height comparable to X common to both endpoints; half-integer endpoints can be taken at cost O(log X), and powers removed at O(√X log²X). The terms of abscissa ≤σ cost O(X^σ log²X) by absolute summation. Each remaining zero contributes to the difference at most O(X^β min(X^(θ−1),1/|ρ|)), by integration of the derivative of x^ρ/ρ and by the separate ceiling at the endpoints. By Ingham, up to V=X^(1−θ) there are O(V^q log^C₁ X) such zeros and the tail of 1/|ρ| from V costs O(V^(q−1)log^C₁ X). The two terms give the written exponent. It also holds for β=1. By integration by parts with 1/log x against the primitive of dθ_pr−dx centred at the first endpoint, the same bound holds for the differences of R. Thus there is a fixed η>0 with |R(y)−R(x)|≪X^(β−η) on each high gap of the mesh.

To make both global signs explicit, let M(s)=∫₂^∞R(x)x^(−s−1)dx. For Re s>1, −(sM(s))'=Σ_p(log p)p^(−s)−∫₂^∞x^(−s)dx. The right-hand side continues meromorphically to Re s>1/2 via −ζ'/ζ minus the higher powers, with cancellation of the pole at 1 and poles at all exterior zeros. The primitive extends locally along the whole real axis s>1/2; it reaches each exterior pole along paths avoiding the others and has a non-removable logarithmic singularity there. If for some a∈(1/2,β) one had R(x)≤x^a eventually, the Mellin transform of x^a−R would be regular on the real half-line s>a but with abscissa of convergence ≥Reρ for a zero of abscissa >a: convergence further to the left would give a derivative holomorphic at that pole by analytic identity. Contradiction by Landau. The same argument holds for −R. For a arbitrarily close to β, with a>β−η, moving each excursion to the previous node preserves its sign and at least half its size; the global ceiling of 235 closes the limsup. If β=1/2 the ceiling and the lower truncation of the statement suffice.

One-sign consequence: it suffices to prove, for example, π(j^10)≥∫₂^{j^10}dv/log v−O_ε(j^(5+ε)) for every ε>0 and all sufficiently large j. Under RH the bound holds. The argument proves its sufficiency, not the inequality for those integers.

**Adverse runs in the integer variable of the powers.** Fix k≥2 and a>1/2. For dyadic J, let L_a(J) be the length of the longest run of consecutive integers j in [J,2J) with R(j^k)<−j^(ka). If a<β then
    limsup_{J dyadic→∞} log(1+L_a(J))/log J = 1.
If a>β, L_a(J)=0 eventually. The same holds with the upper sign. Nothing is claimed at a=β nor on each individual band. This refers to the unsmoothed counting error; the previous result of 2250 for a Gaussian observable at prime endpoints does not directly provide runs of the ordinary count.

Indeed given 0<d<1 use the preceding uniform increment estimate with θ=1−d/(2k), obtaining a saving η>0. Choose a' strictly between max(a,β−η) and β. By Landau choose x arbitrarily high with R(x)<−x^a'. On ALL of [x,x+x^θ] the error is ≤−x^a'/2 by the saving in its variation, even if the supremum β is not attained. Taking k-th roots there appear ≫(x^(1/k))^(1−d/2) consecutive integers by the mean value theorem; for them the strict bound at level a persists. This sequence meets at most two dyadic bands of indices comparable to x^(1/k), and one contains at least half. This contradicts a uniform bound O(J^(1−d)) and, varying d, gives the limsup. The ceiling for a>β follows from 235.

In particular for k=10 it suffices that for each ε>0 there exist some d_ε>0 such that on EVERY high dyadic band the longest run with π(j^10)<li₂(j^10)−j^(5+ε) is O_ε(J^(1−d_ε)). Under RH it is even eventually empty, by the ceiling with loss smaller than ε. It is sufficient to bound the total number of bad indices by that power, but it suffices to prevent runs of that length, even if many isolated failures remain uncontrolled. The arithmetic leap is still to prove such a run bound for tenth powers.

**Both signs of the ordinary count recur in EACH power band.** Let R(x)=π(x)−li₂(x). If β>1/2, for each a between 1/2 and β and each fixed C>1 there are points of BOTH signs with ±R(x)>x^a in [X,X^C] for ALL sufficiently large X. This strengthens Landau's subsequence of bands; it is not claimed on [X,cX] of fixed ratio. The additional difficulty for π is the primitive in the partial summation from θ, which may bring in information from before the band.

Write r(t)=R(exp t), p(t)=θ_pr(exp t)−exp t. By Stieltjes p(t)=t r(t)−∫_[log 2,t]r(u)du+c. Fix a target of abscissa b<1 or b=β attained, with b>max(a,β/C), and a<σ<b. The positive filter h of 2242, supported on [0,L] and with an interior plateau, satisfies |∫h(v)p(t+v)dv|≪exp(σt)poly(t) and ∫h(v)|p(t+v)|dv≫_b exp(bt). In detail, by the truncated formula of 235 at height comparable to exp t the zeros of abscissa ≤σ and the powers cost O(exp(σt)(1+t)^2); the rest form the sum of −exp(ρ(t+v))/ρ extended to infinity with error O(exp(βt)exp((q−1)t)poly(t)) if truncated there. To prevent that last error from exceeding exp(σt), take height exp(Kt) with K>(β−σ)/(1−q) fixed in addition to K>1. At half-integer endpoints the classical truncation error is still O(poly(t)); moving to the real argument in the extended RIGHT sum does not require differentiating the whole series: alternatively apply the distributional truncated formula INTEGRATED against the smooth filters and sum all zeros directly. For this last argument convolve h with a smooth function of short support and mass one that keeps a subplateau. The isolation test of 230 in the interior can be smoothed without killing the target with sufficiently short support. The integrations by parts of the fixed tests give absolute convergence in the integrated explicit formula also to the left of σ. The target multiplier for p is −1/ρ, nonzero. Thus the two filter estimates are obtained without truncation error from the right tail.

Now suppose r(s)≥−exp(as) on [T,CT]. On [T,CT−L] put Q(t)=∫h(v)r(t+v)dv and W(t)=∫h(v)∫_[log 2,t+v]r(u)du dv, so that W'=Q almost everywhere. Since v≥0, the contribution ∫v h(v)r(t+v)dv is ≥−O(exp(at)). The identity for p therefore gives tQ(t)≤W(t)+O(exp(σ't)) with σ<σ'<b. Integrating (W/t)' one obtains W(t)≤poly(t)[exp((β+ε)T)+exp(σ't)] by the global ceiling at the initial endpoint. The same bound holds for ∫h|r(t+v)|dv≤Q(t)+O(exp(at)). For the integral of the absolute value of the primitive inside p, bound its initial portion up to T+v by O(exp((β+ε)T)) and integrate from T to t the previous bound for ∫h|r(s+v)|dv. Consequently ∫h|p(t+v)|dv has the same ceiling up to polynomial factors. At t=CT−L it contradicts the floor exp(bt) if ε>0 is taken with β+ε<bC. Applying the same to −r,−p gives the other excursion.

For any fixed k≥2 the excess of each sign also reappears among j^k with j in EACH [J,J^C]. Use a strictly interior power band (exponents 1<c₁<c₂<C) and a level a' above a and above the exponent of the mesh transfer error; the previous recurrence allows choosing that level, and the transfer of 235 preserves the inequality at the node. In particular, to close it suffices to have the one-sided root inequality with loss at ALL nodes of a subsequence of bands [J,J²] for each loss. The favourable arithmetic bounds on those bands have not been proved.

**Arithmetic gate for a factorial minorant at x=j^10.** The identity (Λ*1)(n)=log n is already recorded in the Chebyshev track (212-003-6); it is not proposed again as a closure. Here a quantitative restriction of the one-sided profile is proved. For real coefficients of finite support, balanced by Σ c_d/d=0, put g(t)=Σ c_d floor(t/d). If g(t)≤1 for all t≥1, then Σ c_d log(floor(x/d)!)=Σ_{n≤x}Λ(n)g(x/n)≤ψ(x) exactly. Its leading Stirling coefficient is I=−Σ c_d log d/d=∫₁^∞g(t)dt/t² by integration up to a common cut and balance (equivalently, Mellin ζ(s)Σ c_d/d^s divided by s as s→1). The remainder depends on the coefficients if they are changed with x.

Let D be the largest divisor used and m the number of nonzero coefficients. Even with arbitrarily large signed coefficients,
    1−I ≫ 1/(D log(2D)),       1−I ≫ 1/((m+1)log²(2m+2)).
Indeed if c₁≤1/2, [1,2) gives a loss ≥1/4. If c₁>1/2, at each prime p without coefficient c_p the jump of g at p is exactly c₁, because only 1 and p divide p. Thus on all of [p−1,p) one has 1−g≥1/2. These intervals are disjoint and their losses add up with weight 1/t². The primes of (D,2D] give the first inequality by PNT (adjust the constant for bounded D). For the second take the first 2m+2 primes: at least m+2 are missing and the largest is O((m+1)log(2m+2)). The argument remains valid counting as missing any p with c_p>−1/4, with local loss at least 1/4.

In particular, if the continuous main term alone is to approximate x with error O(x^(1/2+ε)), it needs D log(2D) and (m+1)log²(2m+2) both ≫ x^(1/2−ε). For precision x^(1/2+o(1)) at x=j^10 this forces D and m ≥j^(5−o(1)). The second requirement blocks the shortcut of a few factorials with huge denominators. It is a necessary condition on the pointwise profile and its main term; it does not exclude a signed Stirling remainder that compensates, profiles valid only on effective x/n, or the original inequality for π. No favourable band has been produced by this argument.

**Barrier at the true arithmetic nodes, without Stirling.** For large x allow real coefficients c_d of finite support, different for each x, without balance or magnitude bound. Impose g(x/n)≤1 only where Λ(n)>0, n≤x. Let m be the number of nonzero coefficients, K=B(m+1)log(2m+2) with B a large absolute constant, and fix ε>0 with K≤x^(5/17−ε). Then the exact certificate satisfies
    ψ(x)−Σ_d c_d log(floor(x/d)!) ≫_ε x/((m+1)log²(2m+2)).
The antecedent 213-040 treats a fixed divisor profile and an omitted interval; here the loss is summed uniformly for variable signed profiles and the minorant is required only at the nodes of Λ.

The difference on the left is exactly ΣΛ(n)(1−g(x/n)), a sum that is nonnegative term by term. If c₁≤1/2, the primes of (x/2,x] contribute ≫x by PNT. Otherwise, choose B so that there are ≥2(m+1) primes in (K,2K], by PNT adjusting the finite cases. Of these ≫K/log K have no coefficient, increasing B if necessary so that m is at most half the count. For each omitted prime p, the values of g on [p,p+1) and [p−1,p) differ exactly by c₁. In (x/(p+1),x/p] there is a prime n, so the value on the first cell is ≤1 by the sampled constraint. On the preceding cell 1−g≥c₁>1/2. The primes n of (x/p,x/(p−1)] contribute ≫x/K² of weight log n. On both intervals the endpoint is ≍x/K and the length ≍x/K², so the uniform short PNT used in 238 suffices: 1−2δ>(7/12)(1−δ) precisely for δ<5/17, with δ=log K/log x. The fixed slack absorbs the logarithms and allows choosing the ε of the short PNT. The loss intervals are disjoint. Summing gives ≫x/(K log K) and the formula in m.

At x=j^10 the proved range includes all m≤j^(50/17−η) for fixed η>0 and j sufficiently large. The loss is relative to ψ(x), not automatically relative to x. Under RH, ψ(x)=x+O(√x log²x), so even in that favourable scenario the certificate of that size stays below x by much more than the root scale. Being an exact identity, no better control of the Stirling remainder rescues this class in the indicated range. The argument leaves open certificates with compensation between nodes and larger supports; it provides no favourable band for π.

**The exact barrier reaches K=O(x^(5/11)), endpoint included, by counting bad cells.** In the previous statement the same floor x/((m+1)log²(2m+2)) holds for K=B(m+1)log(2m+2)≤C x^(5/11), C fixed. It is not enough to know that almost all intervals are good: the prime indices we need already have decreasing density.

Put Y=x/K and h=x/(40K²). For k between K−1 and 2K+1 the cells I_k=(x/(k+1),x/k] are disjoint and have length ≥3h for large K. In the indicated range h≥c_C Y^(1/6), since h/Y^(1/6)=x^(5/6)/(40K^(11/6)). On a bounded number of dyadic blocks covering their endpoints t≍Y, the main theorem of Zaccagnini applied with ε(Z)=A_C/log Z, to absorb the constant factor of the threshold, and Chebyshev give
    meas{t: π(t)−π(t−h)<h/(2log(2Y))} ≪_C Y (log log Y/log Y)².
The estimate used is for π and fixed length, not a pointwise asymptotic. [Zaccagnini, Acta Arithmetica 84 (1998), p. 225](https://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa84/aa8432.pdf).

If I_k contains fewer than h/(2log(2Y)) primes, all endpoints t of a subband of length ≥h inside I_k have (t−h,t]⊂I_k and are bad. The number of bad cells is therefore O_C(K(log log Y/log Y)²)=o(K/log K) in the regime K→∞; for bounded K use the long PNT. Removing the p∈(K,2K] with I_p or I_(p−1) bad costs at most twice that number, even without any independence between the position of the prime and the quality of its two cells. After also removing the support there remain ≫K/log K primes p. I_p contains a witness for the cap and in I_(p−1) the logarithmic prime mass is ≫h, since n≍Y there. The exact sum of losses still gives ≫x/(K log K). At x=j^10 it includes m of order j^(50/11)/log j with a fixed constant. The 5/11 indicates how far this proof reaches; it establishes neither optimality nor the global sign bound.

**Effective compensation of the odd jump in the signed factorial identity.** Write W_k=Σ_{n∈I_k}Λ(n), with I_k=(x/(k+1),x/k]. If K→∞ and K≤C x^(5/11), Y=x/K, then unconditionally
    Σ_{K<p≤2K} |W_p−W_(p−1)| = o(Y/log K),
with p prime. By contrast Σ_p(W_p+W_(p−1))≍Y/log K. Unlike the minorant argument, here BOTH sides of the jump are kept, with sign.

Take h=Y/(40K log Y) and the smoothed density d(t)=(θ_pr(t)−θ_pr(t−h))/h at t≍Y. On the necessary blocks Zaccagnini's theorem from the previous entry gives ∫|d−1|²dt≪_C Y(log log Y/log Y)². Indeed h≥c_C Y^(1/6)/log Y, so one can use ε(Z)=(log log Z+A_C)/log Z with A_C sufficiently large. Multiplying the counts by log t to obtain θ_pr costs in d an error O(h/(Y log Y)) by Brun–Titchmarsh and log(t/(t−h))=O(h/Y). The family of cells with k=p or p−1 is disjoint for odd primes and its union has length ≍Y/log K by PNT. By Cauchy, the integral of |d−1| over that union is O_C((Y/log K)√(log K)log log Y/log Y). When replacing the smoothed mass by the true one, each boundary only displaces prime mass O(h) by Brun–Titchmarsh (log h comparable to log Y). The summed cost is O(Y/(log K log Y)). Powers of order ≥2 add O(√Y log²Y) over the whole band. Therefore Σ_{k=p,p−1}|W_k−|I_k||=o(Y/log K). Finally |I_(p−1)|−|I_p|=2x/[p(p²−1)], with sum O(Y/(K log K)). This proves both statements.

For any coefficient support and each omitted prime, write b_p=(g(p)+g(p−1))/2. Its pair of cells contributes to the deficit exactly
    (1−b_p)(W_p+W_(p−1)) + (c₁/2)(W_(p−1)−W_p).
Summed over ANY subset of omitted primes of the band, the second term costs |c₁| o(Y/log K), regardless of how the subset was chosen. Consequently the loss of order Y/log K of the minorant is not forced by the antisymmetric jump in the signed problem; it is concentrated in the mean level b_p and in the other cells. The proved gain is relative to the mass of these pairs. Neither an absolute error O(√x) nor control of the mean level has been proved.

**The mean level over all pairs of primes is computed by reflection.** Fix a finite real balanced factorial profile Σ c_d/d=0, with integer period L a multiple of all the d. Put C_s=Σ c_d. In the range K→∞, K≤C x^(5/11), the EXACT deficit of the union of the cell pairs (p−1,p), K<p≤2K, divided by its total mass, tends to 1+C_s/2. Within a single reduced class a mod L the limit is 1−b(a), with b(a)=(g(a)+g(a−1))/2 and periodic extension. The profile and its period are fixed before taking the limit.

Indeed, for integers k one has floor((L−1−k)/d)=L/d−1−floor(k/d). By balance g(L−1−k)=−C_s−g(k). Thus b(a)+b(−a)=−C_s exactly. By the absolute error estimate of the previous entry both masses can be replaced by x/p² with total cost o(x/(K log K)), even restricting to a class. The coefficients of the profile are bounded since they are periodic. In each reduced class the weight Σ x/p² is asymptotic to the same fraction 1/φ(L) of the total by the PNT for fixed modulus and partial summation. Therefore the weighted average of the level b is −C_s/2, including the self-reflected classes. This settles the mean level in this sector for fixed profiles. The cancellation between classes does not hold for an arbitrary selection of primes.

**Example with exactly calibrated factorial main term.** On the indices d=(1,2,3,6) choose c=(1,0,−3,0)+λ(0,1,−2,1), λ=(1−log 3)/((log 3)/2−(2log 2)/3). The denominator is log(27/16)/6>0. Then Σc_d/d=0, C_s=−2, g(1)=1 and −Σ c_d(log d)/d=1. For the classes 1 and 5 modulo 6 the levels b are, respectively, 1/2 and 3/2 by g(0)=0 and reflection. The relative deficits of those classes tend to +1/2 and −1/2, while the joint deficit is o(x/(K log K)). The exact sum of factorials equals x+O(log x) by Stirling with four fixed coefficients. To deduce a lower bound for ψ(x) from this example one would need to control the signed balance of ALL the other cells and the rest of the prime sector at root scale. The calibration does not provide that control and the example is not a pointwise minorant.

**Absolute root bound for the WHOLE sector n≤x^(4/7) of the signed profile.** For the previous four-factorial profile, with g(t)=Σc_d floor(t/d), let
    E_N(x)=Σ_{n≤N}Λ(n)(1−g(x/n)).
