Unconditionally E_N(x)≪_{c,ε}x^ε [x^(6/13)+(x²N⁷)^(1/12)] for 1≤N≤x^(4/7). In particular at N=x^(4/7) the bound O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) is already reached, without selecting only the cells around omitted primes. If N=x^ν with fixed ν<4/7, the exponent can be taken strictly less than 1/2.

The specific step is that the balance and Σc_d=−2 exactly cancel the linear term and the constant term of the fractional parts. With B(t)={t}−1/2 (also at integers) one has 1−g(t)=Σc_d B(t/d). For each fixed d apply (4.3) of Proposition 4.1 of Liu, Wu and Yang, with δ=0, z=x/d, to each block D<n≤2D. It gives O_ε(z^ε(z²D⁷)^(1/12)) if z^(6/13)≤D≤z^(2/3). Split from N downwards into complete intervals by halving down to that lower bound; the remainder contains O(x^(6/13)) of mass by Chebyshev. The upper limit eventually holds for all four d and the factor D^(7/12) allows geometric summation. The exponent at the endpoint is (2+7·4/7)/12=1/2. The external input is a published estimate of von Mangoldt sums with fractional part; the application exploits the fixed signed profile, and does not claim originality of the analytic estimator. [Liu, Wu and Yang, Proposition 4.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.10844)

Since g=1 on [1,2), the stretch x/2<n≤x has exactly zero deficit. With Stirling for the four factorials one obtains, for all large x,
    ψ(x)−x = Σ_{x^(4/7)<n≤x/2}Λ(n)(1−g(x/n)) + O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)).
It is an exact reduction at the level of precision sought: the intermediate sector can still have either sign. Its negative part has not been estimated by this route, nor have the errors in going back from ψ to π been removed.

**Moving profile that simultaneously removes two power strips.** For large x take M=floor(x^(1/34)) and N=x^(9/17). There is an explicit profile g_M with support d≤8M for which
    ψ(x)−x = Σ_{N<n≤x/(M+1)} Λ(n)(1−g_M(x/n)) + O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)).
In particular all remaining arguments n are ≤x^(33/34). The price is a lower endpoint N smaller than the x^(4/7) of the fixed profile. The form of the construction is truncated Möbius plus three corrections; the additional step needed is to control the fractional-part estimate uniformly for the moving profile.

Fix c_d=μ(d) for d≤M and three unknowns c_(rM)=M u_r for r=2,4,8, with zero elsewhere. Require Σc_d=−2, Σc_d/d=0, −Σc_d log(d)/d=1. After dividing the first row by M and subtracting the multiple log M of the balance row in the third, the fixed matrix of u_r has rows 1,1/r,(log r)/r (up to sign). It is invertible: multiplying columns by r gives the three rows r,1,log r, independent at 2,4,8 by strict concavity of the logarithm. The constant terms are O(log²(2M)) by the absolute sums of 1/d and log d/d, hence c_(rM)=O(M log²(2M)). For each fixed α in [0,1) this gives Σ|c_d|d^(−α)≪_α M^(1−α)log²(2M). By elementary inversion Σ_{d≤t}μ(d)floor(t/d)=1 for t≥1: group each integer ≤t by divisors. Thus g_M(t)=1 exactly on [1,M+1), since the three corrections do not enter there.

By balance and calibration of the mean, 1−g_M(t)=Σc_d({t/d}−1/2). Proposition 4.1 (4.3) of Liu–Wu–Yang has a uniform constant in z=x/d for zero shift; N≤(x/(8M))^(2/3) for all sufficiently large x. The previous dyadic sum gives for each d the ceiling O_ε(x^ε[(x/d)^(6/13)+(x/d)^(1/6)N^(7/12)]). After summing coefficients, the two exponents in x are 6/13+7/(13·34)<1/2 and 1/6+(9/17)(7/12)+5/(6·34)=1/2. Reduce the internal ε to absorb logarithms. On the other hand, uniform Stirling for floored factorials gives error O(log(2x)) per unit of coefficient against (x/d)log(x/d)−x/d. The three conditions leave main term x and error O(M log²(2M)log(2x)), below root. This proves the identity. The remaining stretch is signed and the profile may grow with x: the reduction is not by itself an induction nor a bound on the negative mass.

**Test of the induction at root scale: amplification in the first free block.** For the moving profile, write h(t)=1−g_M(t) for t≥1 (zero for t<1). The jump a_k=h(k)−h(k−1) equals exactly μ(k) for M<k<2M: all proper divisors of k are ≤M and Σ_{d|k}μ(d)=0. By expanding the step function, the counting-error term that would correspond to a primitive E in the signed identity is Σ a_k E(x/k); for continuous E with interior support it coincides with ∫h(x/u)dE(u). The nodes of this first block lie fully inside the intermediate sector of the previous entry if restricted to 5M/4≤k≤7M/4.

Even under |E(u)|≤√u and monotonicity of u+E(u), that functional can be ≤−c√x√M. Prescribe at the previous interior nodes E(x/k)=−μ(k)√(x/M)/4, and zero at all other nodes; interpolate linearly between consecutive nodes and extend by zero. The support lies near x/M. The distance between nodes there is ≍x/M², so the slopes are O(M^(3/2)/√x)=o(1). Both constraints are verified, also on the transition intervals. The value of the functional is −(√(x/M)/4)Σ μ(k)² over the block. There are ≫M squarefree integers there: excluding the multiples of each r², 2≤r≤√(2M), costs at most the length of the block times Σ_{r≥2}1/r² plus O(√M), and that series is strictly less than 1. Changing the sign gives the other extreme. For M=floor(x^(1/34)) the magnitude is ≫x^(1/2+1/68), a genuine power loss against a budget x^(1/2+ε) for every ε.

Local robustness: keeping c_d=μ(d) up to M but adding coefficients in (M,2M), in the block the jump becomes μ(k)−c_k; only the correction at k itself modifies it. The same construction with signs in place of μ(k) realises a cost proportional to √(x/M)Σ|μ(k)−c_k|. Adding o(M) coefficients in that band therefore leaves the same obstruction, whatever their magnitudes or those of higher corrections. The conclusion limits an induction that uses only the pointwise ceiling and monotonicity. The example is a comparison primitive, not the true von Mangoldt discrepancy; for the latter the signed correlation of μ(k) with E(x/k) remains to be controlled.

**The true Möbius block does not individually annihilate an exterior ordinate.** Let ρ=b+iγ be a zero with 1/2<b<1, of multiplicity r, A=5/4, B=7/4, and P_ρ(M)=Σ_{AM<k≤BM}μ(k)k^(−ρ). For this subblock of the moving profile one has
    limsup_{M integer→∞} |P_ρ(M)|/(log M)^(r−1) ≥ r log(B/A)/|ζ^(r)(ρ)|.
The antecedent 285 treats maxima of Möbius increments. Here the subblock is fixed, twisted by the ordinate itself, and its response at that frequency is measured, with a residue constant.

Indeed integrate P_ρ(M)M^(−s)dM/M from zero to infinity. For Re(s)>1−b absolute convergence allows interchange: k/B≤M<k/A contributes k^(−s)(B^s−A^s)/s. The transform is (B^s−A^s)/(sζ(ρ+s)). Cutting to M≥1 subtracts an entire function since the integrand vanishes for M<1/B. Passing from real M to its integer part alters O(1) summands of size O(M^(−b)). If the limsup L is infinite we are done. If it is finite, the cut integral is holomorphic on Re(s)>0, coincides there meromorphically with the formula, and as s↓0 positive its modulus multiplied by s^r has limsup ≤(r−1)! L, integrating the envelope in the variable log M. The pole at zero gives the limit in modulus r! log(B/A)/|ζ^(r)(ρ)|. This does not presuppose that ρ lies on the extreme abscissa.

At x=j^10 one has M=floor(j^(5/17)), which takes all sufficiently large integers because the increments of the argument tend to zero. Therefore along a subsequence the COMPLEX SPECTRAL summand associated with the individual model −x^ρ P_ρ(M)/ρ has modulus ≫_ρ x^b (log M)^(r−1) (multiplicity only multiplies the term). A root estimate by absolute value of each zero and subblock separately cannot prove the closure if such a zero existed. It is not claimed that the real part, the conjugate pair or the total balance obey the same floor.

The identity also distinguishes what would change when signing across scales. Splitting (A,B] into two halves of equal logarithmic length at C=√(AB) and subtracting their responses replaces the Mellin numerator by ±(B^s−2C^s+A^s)/s=O(s). This removes one order of the pole at s=0; in particular it removes the local singularity for r=1. It does not prove that the contrast is small, nor that the original sum can be replaced at no cost by that contrast.

**The complete real subblock of μ against ψ retains exterior excursions.** Put Θ=sup Reρ and, with A=5/4, B=7/4 and M an integer, X=M^34, define
    C_M(y)=Σ_{AM<k≤BM} μ(k)(ψ(y/k)−y/k),   X≤y≤2X.
For Θ>1/2 one has limsup_M log(1+sup_{X≤y≤2X}|C_M(y)|)/log X ≥ Θ. In particular, not even after combining conjugates and ALL other frequencies is there a uniform root ceiling for this real block on the indicated bands if there is an exterior zero. The selection of k is frozen during the band, but it remains inside the first free block of the profile appropriate to y: floor(y^(1/34))≤2^(1/34)M<AM and BM<2floor(y^(1/34)). The floor is claimed neither for each M nor for a sign orientation.

Proof. Fix 1/2<σ<Θ and a zero ρ of abscissa b>σ+(Θ−σ)/34, possible by taking b sufficiently close to Θ. Use the smooth filter of 230 on [0,log 2], multiplied by exp(−ρv), so as to have ∫h(v)exp(ρv)dv=1 and annihilation at all other zeros of abscissa ≥σ, including the conjugate. In the distributional explicit formula of 230 for ψ(y/k)−y/k, integrating y=X exp v against h, the constant and trivial terms cost O(M) by absolute summation. The target term is −r X^ρ P_ρ(M)/ρ. For the remaining zeros z, of abscissa u<σ, the partial Möbius sum has the ceiling of 285, O_ε(M^(Θ+ε)), also with Θ=1. By Abel on [AM,BM] one obtains |P_z(M)|≪_ε(1+|z|)M^(Θ+ε−u), uniformly in 0≤u≤1. The factor (1+|z|) is absorbed by the rapid decay of ∫h(v)exp(zv)dv and the unit count of zeros. Thus the remaining total is O_ε(M^(Θ+ε)(X/M)^σ)=o(X^b) for fixed sufficiently small ε.

The floor of the previous entry gives |P_ρ(M)|≫_ρ1 along a sequence of integers M. By the integral inequality, sup|C_M|≥|∫hC_M|/||h||₁≫_ρ X^b along it. Although h is complex, C_M(y) is real and its absolute value has been bounded as a real function. Bringing b close to Θ proves the statement. The bound does not control its sign at the point of maximum, nor does it transfer that real scale to y=j^10. Nor does it exclude compensation with the other subblocks of the profile. In particular, the pending arithmetic step cannot be reduced to justifying unconditionally a root ceiling for each real subblock separately without having excluded exterior zeros.

**Both signs of the arithmetic subblock at tenth powers with subpower cut.** In the moving construction use M(y)=floor(exp(√log y)), and freeze the indices 5m/4<k≤7m/4 for y near Y=exp((log m)²), m an integer. For Θ>1/2 there is a fixed C>1 such that, in the limsup over m, each of the two maxima of (±C_m(j^10))_+ for Y≤j^10≤CY has exponent exactly Θ relative to Y. More precisely, for each b of a zero sufficiently close to Θ there are infinitely many m for which BOTH maxima are ≫_b Y^b on the same band. The cut is changed relative to M(y)=floor(y^(1/34)); this statement is not transferred to that profile. On every fixed band considered M(y)/m→1, so the frozen indices really are a subblock of the μ jumps of the moving profile at each node. The three factorial adjustments remain available and their costs are y^o(1).

Fix 1/2<σ<Θ. The positive filter of 2242 annihilates, by its exponential moments, ALL zeros of abscissa ≥σ. Smooth it with a fixed positive kernel of short support so as to keep an interior unit plateau. Move the support to [1,L+1], with L fixed depending on σ. For a target zero of abscissa b>σ and the m of the floor of P_ρ, apply the isolation of 230 on that plateau (fixed translation, nonzero target factor). Since m=Y^o(1), the trivial ceiling |P_z(m)|≪m^(1−Re z) for 0≤Re z≤1 gives remainder O(Y^(σ+o(1))) in the two filters by rapid decay and zero counting; the constant and trivial terms cost O(m). Hence ∫h|C_m(Y exp v)|dv≫_b Y^b and |∫h C_m(Y exp v)dv|≪Y^(σ+o(1)). With h≥0 the integrals of the two parts each have floor ≫_b Y^b. There are real points of both signs inside the support.

To round those points to tenth powers use the estimate of increments of θ_pr from the deterministic mesh entry with gap exponent 0.92; for ψ the saving is preserved by the ceiling O(√t log²t) of powers. It gives η>0 depending on Θ,σ with variation of the error ψ(t)−t of order O(t^(Θ−η)) for displacements ≤t^0.92 at large t. Rounding y to j^10 moves each t=y/k by O(Y^0.9/k)≤t^0.92. O(m)=Y^o(1) errors are summed and the variation is O(Y^(Θ−η/2)). Choose b>max(σ,Θ−η/2). The transfer preserves each sign and a margin ≫_bY^b. The interval [Y,CY] with C=exp(L+2) leaves room at the edges; it does not depend on b. Finally the pointwise ceiling of ψ(t)−t and m=Y^o(1) give O_ε(Y^(Θ+ε)) on the whole block. Letting b tend to Θ completes the claim. The two tenth powers obtained may be different; nothing is claimed about the sign of the remaining subblocks at either of them.

**Test of compensation at the SAME node with an isolated simple front (CONDITIONAL).** Suppose that the only zeros on Re s=b>1/2 are the simple pair ρ=b+iγ and its conjugate, and that every other zero has abscissa ≤σ₀<b. In the first free block of the subpower cut there is a fixed weighted portion in k/m which, along a sequence of tenth powers, has a deficit of order y^b SIMULTANEOUSLY with its complement in E(y)=ψ(y)−y. There are also nodes of simultaneous surplus. It is not an assumption about the actual location of the zeros, but a test of the proposed mechanism under that scenario.

Choose 0≤w≤1 nonzero, Gevrey of order two, unimodal, supported inside (log(5/4),log(7/4)) on an interval of length <π/(4|γ|). Define W(s)=∫w(v)exp(sv)dv and P(m)=Σμ(k)k^(−ρ) w(log(k/m)). One has
    P(m)=W(0)/ζ'(ρ)+m^(−2iγ)W(−2iγ)/ζ'(conj ρ)+O(m^(−η)).
Indeed apply Mellin inversion to m^s W(s)/ζ(ρ+s) and shift to Re s=−η with 0<η<b−σ₀ small. Only 0 and −2iγ are crossed. The shift is justified as in 285: the Gevrey decay beats exp(O(log²(2+|Im s|))) on cuts at good heights and on the vertical line, separated from the zeros. W(−2iγ)≠0 by positivity and by the width of the support. Since the phases m^(−2iγ) approach any point of the circle (round the real solution to an integer), there is a subsequence with P(m)→p not real.

Let C_w(y)=Σμ(k)w(log(k/m))E(y/k), with Y=exp((log m)²). The truncated explicit formula under the gap gives E(y)=−2Re(y^ρ/ρ)+O(y^σ) for any max(σ₀,1/2)<σ<b, absorbing logarithms. On bands Y≤y≤C Y, the total error after summing over k is O(Y^σ m^(1−σ))=o(Y^b). Hence the two balances C_w and E−C_w, normalised by y^b, are −2Re(y^(iγ)P(m)/ρ) and −2Re(y^(iγ)(1−P(m))/ρ) up to o(1). The numbers p and 1−p are not collinear, since Im p≠0 and they sum to 1. There is an open arc of phases where both real parts are strictly positive with fixed margin (use the bisector of their conjugate directions after dividing by ρ), and another opposite arc where both are negative. A band of logarithmic width larger than one period contains both phases in its interior. The tenth powers have logarithmic spacing o(1), so there is also one in each arc for the same large m of the subsequence. M(y)/m→1 keeps the support within the free block.

Variant without weights at the cost of choosing the interval at the node: by level decomposition of w, C_w is the integral over 0<t<1 of the balances of the consecutive intervals {k:w(log(k/m))>t}. At a negative node with E and C_w≤−c y^b there is an interval with balance ≤−c y^b/2. Running through it, the jump of each partial sum costs O(y^b m^(−b))=o(y^b) by the formula under the gap. One can stop at −c y^b/4+o(y^b), leaving E minus that balance also strictly negative to order y^b. The same for surplus. For the fixed weight the simultaneous signs were already obtained without subsequent choice of the interval. This rules out an automatic compensation by opposite sign between these parts under the assumed scenario. It neither proves that this scenario occurs nor resolves the case of a general front.

**Strengthening at the same node for any FINITE SIMPLE front with a gap (CONDITIONAL).** In the previous entry the single pair can be replaced by any nonempty finite set of simple zeros of abscissa b>1/2, with all the others to the left of b−η for some η>0. Rational independence between the ordinates is not required. There is a single fixed weight 0≤w≤1 of the free block and a set of m of positive lower logarithmic density such that on [Y,CY], Y=exp((log m)²), the two pieces C_w and E−C_w are simultaneously ≤−c y^b at one tenth power and ≥c y^b at another, with fixed c>0.

Define A(t)=Σ exp(iγt)/ρ and B(s)=Σ exp(iγs)/ζ'(ρ), summing the whole front with conjugates. They are real trigonometric polynomials, not identically zero, without constant term. For t=log y, u=log m, the explicit formula and the same Mellin shift applied to each pole of the front give uniformly on the fixed band
    E(y)/y^b=−A(t)+o(1),
    C_w(y)/y^b=−∫ w(v) A(t−u−v) B(u+v)dv+o(1).
Indeed for each term ρ_i of E, the residues of 1/ζ in the Möbius sum are W(i(γ_j−γ_i)) exp(i(γ_j−γ_i)u)/ζ'(ρ_j). Multiplying and summing reproduces the written integral. The gap error is uniform by finiteness and m=Y^o(1).

Work in G, the closure of the continuous flow of the phases, a compact connected torus, and write τ(s) for the phase of s. The functions A,B have Haar mean zero and the zero set of each nonzero trigonometric polynomial has measure zero (in torus coordinates, by Fubini and induction on dimension). S={A>0} has measure strictly between 0 and 1. Its stabiliser in L¹ is a proper closed subgroup, since invariance under all translations would make its indicator constant almost everywhere. It has empty interior by connectedness. Choose s in the open set {B<0} outside the stabiliser. Since S and s+S have equal measure but do not coincide modulo null sets, there are two points with strict crossings of opposite signs between A(t) and A(t−s), one in each direction.

Fix v₀ in the interior of (log(5/4),log(7/4)) and a positive Gevrey weight on a small neighbourhood of v₀, zero outside, with sufficiently small fixed mass. For τ(u) close to s−τ(v₀) and τ(t) in neighbourhoods of the crossing points, the integral has, with the minus sign, the same sign as −A(t), with modulus bounded below and strictly less than |A(t)|, by continuity and B(s)<0. This gives simultaneous margins for the complement. In the admissible open set of τ(u) choose a smaller ball with boundary of measure zero. Its preimage in integers m has logarithmic density equal to its positive Haar measure: for continuous functions the time average of the flow tends to Haar by integration of characters, and the weights 1/m reproduce that average with u=log m by Riemann sums; approximate the indicator by continuous functions. Minimality of the flow and compactness guarantee a uniformly bounded time to enter each of the two open phase sets of t (use smaller interior neighbourhoods). Thus C is fixed before m, and rounding y to the nearest tenth power within the band changes the phase by o(1). The result concerns profiles chosen for the assumed front. It establishes no law under multiple zeros, an infinite front or without a gap, nor does it produce an exterior zero.

**Compensation in density at prescribed nodes (conditional).** Suppose a finite right front of distinct zeros ρ_i=b+iγ_i, b>1/2, with a fixed gap to the rest as above, multiplicities r_i and maximum r≥2. Fix any Gevrey weight of order two as above, nonnegative with positive mass. For each integer m≥2 take u=log m and y the tenth power closest to exp(u²) (in case of a tie, the smaller). Then for each fixed H the logarithmic proportion of m with |C_w(y)|≤H y^b tends to zero. In the same density (E−C_w)/C_w tends to −1.

Proof. Use A(t)=Σ_i r_i exp(iγ_i t)/ρ_i and B_r(t)=Σ_{r_j=r} r exp(iγ_j t)/ζ^(r)(ρ_j). For t=log y=u²+o(1), E/y^b=−A(t)+o(1). The previous Mellin shift gives
    C_w/(y^b u^(r−1))=−∫ w(v) A(t−u−v) B_r(u+v)dv+o(1).
At a pole of order r, the top coefficient in u of the residue comes from exp(su) and equals r!/(r−1)! times W(i(γ_j−γ_i))/ζ^(r)(ρ_j). The other degrees are ≤r−2. The gap absorbs the contour error and that of the explicit formula as before.

On the previous torus G, the phases (τ(u²),τ(u)) are equidistributed according to product Haar with weights 1/m normalised by log M for m≤M. Each nontrivial character gives exp(i(cu²+du)) with (c,d) different from (0,0) by density of the flow. Its integral mean tends to zero by integration by parts outside a fixed neighbourhood of the stationary point, or by direct integration if c=0. The cumulative error of replacing the integral by the sum is O(Σ_m (1+log m)/m²). Rounding y changes the first phase by o(1).

The integral with minus sign defines a real trigonometric polynomial F on G². Its characters in the parameters of the two flows have frequencies (γ_i,γ_j−γ_i), which identify the pair of indices without ambiguity. For i=j of maximal order, W(0)>0 guarantees a nonzero coefficient. F has mean zero because γ_i≠0, and its null set has Haar measure zero by analyticity on the connected torus. By equidistribution the normalised variable converges in distribution to F. For any δ>0 the set |C_w|≤Hy^b lies, up to initial indices, inside |F|≤δ; letting δ go to zero proves the claim. E/y^b is bounded, which gives the announced ratio, omitting possible zero denominators of density zero. Both orientations of C_w have positive logarithmic density. The complement is defined by exact difference; proving by an independent arithmetic estimate that this compensation is impossible would be an additional obligation.

**Direct test of a comparison by alternating dilations (unconditional obstruction).** Extend E₀(x)=ψ(x)−x for x≥1 by zero for x<1. Freeze m and write T_m f(y)=Σ_k μ(k)w(log(k/m))f(y/k) with the previous support. For Rf(y)=Σ_{d≤y}(−1)^(d+1) f(y/d), both R T_m E₀ and R(I−T_m)E₀ are O_w(m log(2y)), uniformly for y≥1. For m close to exp(√log y) these two bounds are y^o(1), even without hypotheses on zeros.

Indeed Df(y)=Σ_{d≤y}f(y/d) gives D E₀(y)=log(n!)−yH_n, n=floor(y), because Σ_{d|h}Λ(d)=log h. Stirling and H_n=log n+γ+O(1/n) give −(1+γ)y+O(log(2y)), also between integers. Subtracting twice the value at y/2 cancels the linear term and gives R E₀. The range 1≤y<2 is bounded. With m frozen, R and T_m commute, by interchange of finite sums in dk≤y; one concludes by the absolute bound over the O(m) terms. The same m is kept in all dilated arguments.

This simultaneous control loses precisely the information needed to detect a spectral excursion. In the Mellin transform with measure y^(−s−1)dy the multiplier of R is (1−2^(1−s))ζ(s), initially on Re s>1 and by continuation near any nontrivial zero. At each zero of multiplicity r it has a zero of order at least r. In particular the pole of −ζ'/ζ in the prime error is cancelled, also after multiplying by the finite Dirichlet polynomial of the frozen block. The small alternating balance cannot be identified with a pointwise bound on the original pieces. This is an application of the classical eta factor to the concrete proposal of comparing the complements, with no claim of novelty for the factor.

**The alternating tail recovers the pointwise balance at polynomial cost (unconditional).** For integer x≥2, fix N=2x², H=x² and y continuous uniform on [Nx,Nx+H]. Let S_N f(y)=Σ_{N<d≤y}(−1)^(d+1)f(y/d), with the previous extension by zero. Then
    average_y S_N E₀(y) = E₀(x)/2 + O(1).
The constant is absolute. More generally, for integer 1≤k≤x one has average_y S_N[E₀(·/k)](y)=E₀(x/k)/2+O(1) uniformly. Therefore the same recovery for T_m E₀ and its complement costs O_w(m) if the indices of the block do not exceed x.

Proof. By finite interchange, the ψ part of the tail for k is Σ_{h≤x/k} Λ(h) 1_{floor(y/(kh)) odd}, since N is even and floor(y/N)=x on the whole band. A term with floor(y/(kh))=N contributes zero. The periodic indicator of period 2kh has average 1/2+O(kh/H) over the interval. The total error is O(x ψ(x/k)/H)=O(1) by the Chebyshev bound. For the linear part one sums (y/k)Σ_{N<d≤y/k}(−1)^(d+1)/d. The infinite tail from N+1 is 1/(2N)+O(N^(−2)), by its integral ∫₀¹t^N/(1+t)dt. Replacing it by the finite one costs O(1) after multiplying by y/k, by the alternating remainder (also if y/k<N, a situation excluded here). The main term is x/(2k)+O(1), uniformly. Linearity gives the statement for the block.

Thus a uniform one-sided bound on the average of this tail at root scale in x would give the same orientation for E₀(x), with factor two and absolute error. The recovery also holds at tenth powers x; the auxiliary average is continuous in y. Elementary control of the full alternating operator does not control the truncated tail separately.

**Which ingredient is missing in the recovery by parity.** A specific sensitivity test of the previous tail, with the exact support of prime powers and a positive Euler product in both models. Put ε_p=exp(−(log p)^(1/3)), α_p=1±ε_p (a fixed sign in each model), a(p^k)=α_p log p for all k≥1 and zero outside prime powers. The series of these weights is the negative logarithmic derivative of ∏_p(1−p^(−s))^(−α_p) on Re s>1, using the branch given by the series of logarithms. Its Dirichlet coefficients as a product are positive, by the binomial expansion with α_p>0.

If A(t)=Σ_{n≤t}a(n), the same parity proof gives average S_N[(A(t)−t)1_{t≥1}]=(A(x)−x)/2+O(1), since it only uses positivity and A(t)≤2ψ(t)≪t. However, in the two models respectively ±(A(x)−x)≫x exp(−(log x)^(1/3)) for all sufficiently large x, including tenth powers. Indeed the total perturbation has magnitude D(x)=Σ_{p^k≤x} ε_p log p ≥ ε_x(θ(x)−θ(x/2))≫x ε_x, with ε_x defined by the same formula. The classical unconditional error ψ(x)−x=O(x exp(−c√log x)) is o(x ε_x). At the same time D(x)≪√x log²x + x ε_{√x}: the primes ≤√x contribute O(√x log²x) counting their powers and the others have relative weight ≤ε_{√x}. Thus both models satisfy A(x)=x+O_B(x/(log x)^B) for each fixed B.

Parity, the support, positivity of the product and those precisions of the prime number theorem are compatible with root-scale failures of either sign. The exact identity Σ_{d|n}Λ(d)=log n does distinguish the models already at n=p. This test only rules out deducing the bound from the shared properties; the estimate of the full alternating operator in the previous entry used that additional identity.

**Necessary calibration of the exponent in the recovered tail.** Let B(x,k) be the tail average of the previous entry, so that 2B(x,k)=E₀(x/k)+O(1) uniformly. Littlewood's classical oscillation theorem gives E₀(t)=Ω_±(√t log log log t). Both orientations persist at squares. Indeed, if E₀(t)>0, choose j=ceil(√t): by monotonicity E₀(j²)≥E₀(t)−(j²−t). For the negative excursion take j=floor(√t), which gives E₀(j²)≤E₀(t)+(t−j²). Each loss is O(√t), absorbed by the divergent factor. In particular B(j^10,j^8)=Ω_±(j log log log j), since the recovered argument is exactly j².

Therefore a one-sided ceiling C√(x/k) uniform over all dilations k≤x would be false, even restricting the exterior parameter x to tenth powers and using the genuine prime weights. The same obstacle affects the bound C√x for k=1 over all integers. This monotonicity reasoning does not reach k=1 at x=j^10, nor the range of k of the moving block: the jump between tenth powers is of order x^(9/10). The sufficient gate already recorded for the mesh admits an arbitrary loss in the exponent. Reference for the oscillation theorem: Hardy and Littlewood, Contributions to the theory of the Riemann zeta-function and the theory of the distribution of primes, equation (5.77), https://personal.math.ubc.ca/~gerg/teaching/592-Fall2018/papers/1916.Hardy.pdf .

**Runs of proportional length in the ordinary count when β is attained.** If the supremum β>1/2 of the abscissas of zeros is attained, there exist C>1, c>0 and h>0 such that in EACH high [J,CJ] there are two intervals of consecutive integer indices, each of length ≥cJ, on one of which (log(j^10))R(j^10)≥h j^(10β) and on the other ≤−h j^(10β). It holds without a gap or finiteness on the extreme line. If β>1/2 is not attained, the absolute maximum in the same normalisation tends to zero. The almost-periodicity mechanism has antecedents in 2150 and in the smoothed observables of this phase; here it is used for the ordinary count in runs at the exact scale of the exponent.

Indeed, fix 1/2<σ<β. By Ingham as in the sampling entry, Σ_{Reρ>σ}1/|ρ| converges with multiplicities (sum over dyadic bands with q<1). In the truncated explicit formula of 235 for ψ, at height comparable to x, the abscissas less than or equal to σ cost O(x^σ log²x). Half-integer endpoints can be used and moved to x at cost O(log x) in ψ−x. For the terms to the right of σ, after normalising by x^β there is a summable majorant. Those of abscissa <β tend individually to zero, including the moving cuts; on the extreme line, rounding x changes each phase by o(1) and the tail converges uniformly. Thus (ψ(x)−x)/x^β=F(log x)+o(1), F(t)=−Σ_{Reρ=β} exp(i Imρ t)/ρ, with multiplicities. The contribution of higher powers is O(√x log²x). Partial summation for R=π−li₂ adds, after multiplying by log x/x^β, O(1/log x) by the bound θ(x)−x=O(x^β). The same F is obtained.

If the front is attained, F is real, uniformly almost periodic, of mean zero and nonzero by uniqueness of coefficients. It has both signs with margin (a nonnegative almost periodic function that is positive on an interval has positive mean by recurrence). By uniform continuity take two short intervals of fixed margin; their translates with reduced margin reappear with gaps bounded by the almost periods. The variable 10 log j runs over an interval of length 10 log C in each band. Choose C sufficiently large to contain a complete translate of each interval; their preimages have length ≫J. If the front is not attained F is the empty sum. In particular, to exclude every attained exterior front it would suffice to have a root minorant with arbitrary loss on a single mesh of indices with consecutive ratio tending to one (e.g. floor(exp(√n)), removing repetitions). Each proportional run would contain a node. This does not exclude an unattained exterior supremum.

**Deficits on the single mesh x_n=2^(10n²), with bounded gaps in n (attained front).** Under the hypothesis of the previous entry, there are h>0 and an integer L such that each block of L sufficiently high indices contains an n with (log x_n)R(x_n)≤−h x_n^β. The ratio x_(n+1)/x_n diverges. The base 2 is fixed before knowing the zeros. It suffices to detect the negative orientation, and for it a favourable point is known a priori: by conjugation F(0)=−Σ_{Reρ=β} β/|ρ|²<0 (multiplicities included).

Truncate the series of F symmetrically so that the uniform tail costs less than |F(0)|/8. On the torus of the retained phases, let g be the vector (exp(iγ 10 log 2)) and K the closure of the cyclic group generated by g. In a neighbourhood of the identity of K the truncated sum is below −|F(0)|/2. The component group of K is finite; for its exponent D, g^D and also g^(D²) densely generate the connected torus K₀ (the D-th power map of K has image K₀, by divisibility of K₀). For n=Dm, the phases are (g^(D²))^(m²). In K₀ they form an equidistributed sequence even on intervals of m of growing length with arbitrary start. Indeed each nontrivial character gives exp(2πiαm²) with α irrational by density and connectedness. A difference with fixed step l has mean O_l(1/M) over M terms, uniformly in the start, by the geometric sum with ratio exp(4πiαl). Van der Corput's inequality, first with a fixed number of steps and then a growing one, gives a uniform o(1) mean. Approximate a continuous nonnegative function supported in the identity neighbourhood and positive there by sums of characters. Its integral is positive, also in the case of the trivial torus. Therefore every sufficiently long interval visits the neighbourhood. Returning to the n, adding the uniform tail and the arithmetic o(1) proves the claim.

To exclude an attained exterior supremum it then suffices, for each ε>0, to prove R(x_n)≥−x_n^(1/2+ε) along blocks of consecutive indices of arbitrarily large length and arbitrarily high. One chooses ε<β−1/2 and a length larger than L. It is not required that the certified indices cover all scales. The arithmetic existence of those blocks and the scenario without a maximum remain pending.

**Optimum of the dyadic binomial minorants at the true nodes.** Put x=2^M and b_l(h)=floor(x/(2^l h)) mod 2, 0≤l<M. Even allowing real coefficients a_l depending on M and requiring only Σ_l a_l b_l(h)≤1 for h a prime power ≤x, the supremum of Σ_{h≤x}Λ(h)Σ_l a_l b_l(h) is
    x log 2 + O_A(x/(log x)^A) for each A>0.
This includes x=2^(10n²). The elementary construction a₀=1 and all others zero attains the leading coefficient. The loss against ψ(x) is therefore (1−log 2+o(1))x even with access to all levels and to the actual list of primes to impose feasibility. The restriction to dyadic dilations is essential.

Indeed, by Legendre, ΣΛ(h)b_l(h)=log binom(2^(M−l),2^(M−l−1))≤2^(M−l)log 2, and for l=0 it equals x log 2+O(log x) by Stirling. Fix K such that 2^K is comparable to (log x)^A. For each integer 1≤q<2^K there is a prime in (x/(q+1),x/q]: the length is x/(q(q+1)), and the prime number theorem for θ with remainder O_B(t/log^B t), B>A+2, gives positive mass uniformly. At that prime the b_l are exactly the binary digits of q. Choose the q with ones precisely at the indices l<K where a_l>0. If the set is empty the positive sum is zero; otherwise the constraint at the chosen prime gives Σ_{l<K}max(a_l,0)≤1. For h>x/2^K all higher bits vanish. The weighted mass there is at most the sum with those positive coefficients, hence ≤x log 2 by the binomial identity at each level. For h≤x/2^K the original constraint bounds the contribution by ψ(x/2^K)≪x/2^K even with unbounded coefficients. Summing gives the formula. The argument uses all constraints on one and the same coefficient vector; it does not treat nonlinear profiles, combinations with other dilations, or compensations between nodes.

**Degree threshold for recovering mass at root scale through binary interactions.** Let x=2^M. Allow a real multilinear polynomial P of degree d in the M bits of floor(x/h) from the previous entry, with P(0)=0 (without introducing ψ directly as a constant term) and P≤1 at the sampled prime powers. At h=1 the M bits may be zero but Λ(1)=0. Call loss the quantity Σ_{h≤x}Λ(h)(1−P). For d≤M/4 this loss is ≫x/4^d uniformly. For d=ceil(M/4) there is a P whose cost is O(√x). Thus the critical coefficient of M in the degree for loss x^(1/2+o(1)) is 1/4. This is about approximating ψ from below; the arithmetic value of the polynomial still has to be evaluated in order to use it as a certificate of the sign.

For the floor, restrict to the first d+1 bits, setting the rest to zero. The alternating difference of order d+1 of 1−P is zero because each monomial omits some variable. At the zero vertex the deficit is one. For q=1,...,2^(d+1)−1 the cell (x/(q+1),x/q] has prime mass ≫x/(q(q+1)) uniformly: this is the short PNT of 238 used above, since q≤2x^(1/4) and 1/4<5/17. Thus all those deficits are nonnegative. Their sum over the vertices with an odd number of ones equals the sum over the even ones and is therefore ≥1. Each cell of the first sum weighs ≫x/4^d. The remaining prime powers do not reduce the loss either.

For the ceiling choose P=1−∏_{l<d}(1−b_l), Q=2^d. Exactly the cells with quotient q=Qn, n≥1, remain. Take d=ceil(M/4), so that Q lies between x^(1/4) and 2x^(1/4). For n≤(log x)^2, the same short PNT and the total cost O(√x log²x) of higher powers would not together suffice for a ceiling without logarithm. All higher powers are separated from the start: their total mass is O(√x) by Chebyshev for prime squares and O(x^(1/3)log²x) for powers of exponent ≥3. The prime mass in the first cells is O(Σ_n x/(Qn)^2)=O(√x) by the uniform short PNT. For (log x)^2<n≤U=floor(√(x/Q)), count integers by length plus one and multiply by log x: the cost is O((x/(Q² log²x)+U)log x). For n>U there are only integers h≤x/(QU), of cost O(x log x/(QU)). Both remainders are o(√x). The construction holds in particular at the nodes 2^(10n²). The products of bits represent Λ-weighted sums over intersections of parity conditions; the identity of a single binomial does not give their evaluation.

**Compression of the OR into an lcm of explicit binomials, with error of exact root order.** For x=2^M, d=ceil(M/4), Q=2^d, put B_l=binom(x/2^l,x/2^(l+1)) and L=lcm(B₀,...,B_(d−1)). Then
    c√x ≤ ψ(x)−log L ≤ C√x
for absolute constants and M sufficiently large. Thus the recovered expression can be computed with binomials and greatest common divisor, without evaluating intersections of primes. Distinct antecedent: 264-A builds binomial atoms from the initial lcm; here the lcm is built from a prescribed number of central binomials that are small relative to that construction.

For each prime p, the valuation of L is max_l Σ_{a≥1} b_l(p^a), by Legendre. In the OR weight of the previous entry one uses Σ_{a≥1}max_l b_l(p^a). Their difference (OR minus valuation) is nonnegative, zero for p>√x and at most the number of exponents a≥2 with p^a≤x: if some row of bits is nonempty, the maximum of the sums is at least one. Hence the total weighted cost is O(√x) by Chebyshev. The defect of the OR was already O(√x). For the floor, all primes in (x/(Q+1),x/Q] have quotient Q and exceed √x for large x, so they divide no B_l. The cited short PNT gives mass ≫x/Q²≫√x. The same floor x/4^d for d≤M/4 is inherited from the OR: in that range the cell Q suffices, except for the trivial d=0.

Form of the remaining obligation: construct, at the nodes and blocks of the attained-front criterion, a minorant of log L by x−O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)). In terms of overlap, D=log((∏ B_l)/L)≥0 is computed exactly as the sum of log gcd(B_l,lcm(B_0,...,B_(l−1))) for l≥1. By Stirling, log ∏B_l=2(1−2^(−d))x log 2+O(M²). The desired inequality comes from a ceiling for D by [2(1−2^(−d))log 2−1]x+O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)); approximating 1−2^(−d) by one here would lose order x^(3/4). The identity by itself does not bound that overlap to the required precision.

**One-sided criterion by fixed levels of the lcm, without the attained-front hypothesis.** For fixed l≥1, Q=2^l, x a multiple of 2Q, use the binomials B_i=binom(x/2^i,x/2^(i+1)), 0≤i≤l. Measure only the part that the last one adds to the lcm:
    V_l(x)=log(B_l/gcd(B_l,lcm(B_0,...,B_(l−1)))).
Define H_Q(s)=Σ_{m odd≥1}[(Qm)^(−s)−(Qm+1)^(−s)]. It suffices to obtain, on an unbounded set of fixed levels l, for each ε>0 and all sufficiently high multiples of 2Q,
    V_l(x)≥H_Q(1)x−O_{ε,l}(x^(1/2+ε)).
The constants and the starting point may depend on l. Such an estimate would exclude every exterior zero, even if the abscissas do not attain their supremum. Here all multiples at each level are used, not only the tenth powers.

Proof. For p>√x, the valuation of the new factor is one precisely when floor(x/p) has bit l set and all earlier ones zero. For all primes, comparing with S_Q(x)=Σ_h Λ(h) 1_{floor(x/h)≡Q (mod 2Q)} costs O(√x): for p≤√x both local weights lie between zero and floor(log x/log p), and their total mass there is O(√x) by Chebyshev and the higher powers. For real x, S_Q(x) jumps only at integers n, with absolute jump ≤Σ_{h|n}Λ(h)=log n. The minorant extends from the fixed mesh to S_Q on the whole half-line with additional cost O_Q(log x).

For Re s>1, integrating S_Q(x)x^(−s−1) from 1 gives (−ζ'/ζ)(s) H_Q(s)/s by the quotient cells. H_Q is holomorphic in Re s>0 by differences that are absolutely convergent there. The pole at 1 cancels when H_Q(1)x is subtracted. For each fixed s with Re s>0, the first-order expansion, with absolute summation of the remainders, gives
    H_Q(s)=s Q^(−s−1)(1−2^(−s−1))ζ(s+1)+O_s(Q^(−Re s−2)).
The leading coefficient is nonzero by the Euler product in Re(s+1)>1. Hence for each exterior zero ρ one can choose a level of the family with H_Q(ρ) nonzero, however large its ordinate. At that level the centred Mellin transform has a pole at ρ and is regular on the real axis s>1/2. A minorant with a=1/2+ε<Reρ would make S_Q(x)−H_Q(1)x+C x^a eventually nonnegative. Its Mellin transform cannot converge to the left of Reρ because of the pole, but it is regular at each real point to the right of a, a contradiction by the Landau theorem used above. Modifications on an initial interval only add an entire function. The reasoning identifies the sufficient estimate; it does not prove it.

In the first overlap, log gcd(B₀,B₁) itself agrees to O(√x) with the cell floor(x/h)≡3 mod 4 weighted by Λ. The Mellin factor of that cell is [(1−2^(−s))/2−4^(−s)]ζ(s)−L(s,χ₄)/2 by separation of the odd residues. Thus a single level may miss a common zero; the above expansion of the new-mass factors removes the need for hypotheses about common zeros.

**Converse of the level criterion, with uniformity for the cells.** Under RH, for each ε>0 and 1≤Q=2^l≤x,
    S_Q(x)=H_Q(1)x+O_ε(x^ε √(x/Q)).
Therefore V_l(x)=H_Q(1)x+O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) at the multiples of 2Q, uniformly even as the level varies. Combined with the previous entry, the minorant on an unbounded set of fixed levels is equivalent to RH. GRH for characters of growing conductor is not assumed.

Details of the averaging that gives uniformity. Write H_Q(s)=Q^(−s)D_u(s), u=1/Q, where D_u is the difference of the series over 1,3,5,... and 1+u,3+u,5+u,... (the difference is taken term by term). For fixed σ=1/2+η<1 and T≥2, uniformly in 0<u≤1,
    ∫_[T,2T] |D_u(σ+it)|² dt ≪_η T^(1+2η).
Indeed truncate both sequences smoothly at N=T^(1+η), with the same weight in their real argument, one up to N and zero from 2N on. The difference of the step-two combs has mean zero and periodic primitives of any order bounded uniformly in u (choose mean zero at each integration; the first primitive is a step function). In the tail, r integrations by parts against the power through the smooth cutoff give O_{r,η}((1+T)^r N^(1−σ−r)), which is O(1) on choosing r large. The initial justification for Re s>1 extends through the integral of the derivatives to σ>0. Each truncated polynomial separately has frequencies log(m+u) successively separated by ≫1/N (also for u=0). On expanding the integrated square, use 2|a_i a_j|≤|a_i|²+|a_j|² and sum the inverse distances: bound (T+O(N log(2N)))Σ|a_i|². The quadratic norm of the coefficients is O_η(1). This proves the estimate.

To apply Mellin, smooth S_Q(x exp(v/x)) in v∈(0,1) with a fixed smooth density of mass one, x≥2. The cost of undoing it is O(log(2x)) by the divisor jumps; the main term varies by O(1) because H_Q(1) is bounded. The extra multiplier K(s)=∫w(v)exp(sv/x)dv costs O_r((1+|t|/x)^(−r)) on the lines used. Shift from Re s=2 to σ=1/2+η; under RH, −ζ'/ζ=O_η(log²(2+|t|)) in the strip at large heights, by the local formula for the logarithmic derivative and the unit count of zeros. Only the pole at 1 is crossed. The shift is valid by decay of K and polynomial growth of D_u (already from one integration by parts). By Cauchy–Schwarz, in each band T≤|t|≤2T the remaining integral, including 1/s, costs O_{r,η}((x/Q)^σ T^η log²(2T)(1+T/x)^(−r)). For |t|≤2 the defining difference converges uniformly. Summing the bands and choosing η sufficiently small relative to ε gives the formula. The loss O(√x) in passing from S_Q to V_l has an absolute constant by the same comparison of valuations. The proof makes it possible to locate the difficulty of the converse in the bound for ζ'/ζ; the average of the cell factors has been controlled unconditionally.

**One band per level and only the mean deficit (diagonal criterion).** Take Q=2^l, X=exp(Q), and A_l the arithmetic mean of (H_Q(1)x−V_l(x))_+ over the multiples of 2Q in [X,QX]. For RH it suffices that for each ε>0 there are arbitrarily high levels with A_l≤X^(1/2+ε). Under RH this holds eventually by the previous converse (use a smaller loss and Q=log X). There is no need to control a fixed level on a half-line, nor for the extreme abscissa to be attained.

Proof of the necessity of excursions. If there is a zero ρ of abscissa b>1/2, fix 1/2<σ<b. For E_Q(y)=S_Q(y)−H_Q(1)y and a fixed smooth test f of compact support in the coordinate v=log(y/X), the integrated formula has terms
    −mult(z) X^z H_Q(z) F(z)/z,   F(z)=∫f(v)exp(zv)dv.
Indeed shift the Mellin transform of the previous entry to Re s=−1/2; the pole at 1 was already subtracted. H_Q(s)= (2Q)^(−s)[ζ(s,1/2)−ζ(s,(1+1/Q)/2)] in Hurwitz terms, entire by cancellation at 1. Uniform Euler–Maclaurin for parameters in [1/2,1] gives polynomial growth in Q and in 1+|Im s| in the fixed strip, both for H_Q and for its value at zero. The possible residue of 1/s and the integral on the left line cost O_f(Q^C), with ζ'/ζ of logarithmic growth there by the functional equation. On the horizontal cuts use good heights as in 235. The rapid decay of F and the zero count justify absolute summation and a cost O_f(X^σ Q^C) for all terms of abscissa <σ. The exponent C can be fixed together with the tests.

Take the two tests of 2242 and 230 as in the proof of the moving subblock: a weight h≥0 that annihilates all zeros of abscissa ≥σ with a positive plateau, and a complex test g supported on that plateau that keeps only the target zero with G(ρ)≠0. They can be smoothed preserving the inner plateau and the nonzero moment. Their supports lie in a fixed [0,log C₀] by translation. The signed moment with h is O(X^σ Q^C); the modulus of the moment with g is ≫ X^b Q^(−b−1) by the expansion of H_Q(ρ) and Q=log X. Since |g|≤C' h, the integral of h|E_Q| reaches the same scale. Subtracting the signed moment gives ∫ h(E_Q)_− dv ≫ X^b Q^(−b−1), where t_−=max(−t,0).

On the fixed band [X,C₀X], the integral mean in y of the deficit therefore has that same floor up to a fixed constant. Rounding to the next multiple of 2Q costs O(Q log X) in E_Q by the divisor jumps and the slope of the main term. Replacing S_Q by V_l on the mesh costs O(√X) uniformly on that band. Each rounded node receives an interval of length ≤2Q. All fall in [X,QX] for high Q; their contribution to the total mean, after diluting by a factor O(Q), proves A_l≫ X^b Q^(−b−2) for ALL sufficiently high l. This is incompatible with the frequency minorant of favourable levels formulated above for ε<b−1/2. An already indexed isolation mechanism is adapted; the gain is the explicit arithmetic diagonal and the average over its nodes. The favourable estimate of A_l without RH remains pending.

**Removal of the primes up to X^(2/3) from the diagonal deficit.** In the previous band fix H=X^(2/3). For each x=2Qn put
    U(n)=Σ_{H<p≤QX} (log p) 1_{ {n/p}∈[1/2,1/2+1/(2Q)) }.
The brace denotes fractional part. Let B_l be the mean over the same band of (H_Q(1)x−H/(2Q)−U(n))_+. The diagonal criterion remains equivalent to RH with A_l replaced by B_l. An unconditional arithmetic step is that the contribution of all primes p≤H to the cell can be replaced by θ(H)/(2Q) with root mean-square error (RMS norm O(√X)). The subsequent replacement of θ(H) by H requires another argument.

Indeed the cell condition at a prime p is exactly equivalent to the fractional-part condition written above, also for p>x, where it is false. Expand each indicator in Fourier over Z/p. Its mean μ_p differs from 1/(2Q) by ≤1/p. By partial summation and Chebyshev, Σ_{p≤H}log(p)/p=O(log H). By Parseval, the sum of squares of its nonconstant coefficients is μ_p(1−μ_p)≤μ_p. For distinct primes the nonzero frequencies a/p are distinct, and the circular distance between any two is ≥1/H². Apply the dual form of the additive large sieve to the average over the N consecutive integers n of the band, N≍X. The square of the RMS norm of the centred sum is bounded by
    O((1+H²/N)(H log H/Q+log² H)).
Here Σ_{p≤H}(log p)²≪H log H and Σ(log p)²/p≪log² H were used. With Q=log X, H=X^(2/3), the result is O(X). This proves the unconditional statement about the fluctuations, including the error of rounding the means. For the complete balance all powers of exponent ≥2 can be removed at pointwise cost O(√(QX)), and V_l replaced by S_Q at the same cost. Since the positive part is 1-Lipschitz and L¹≤RMS,
    |A_l−B_l|≪√(QX)+|θ(H)−H|/Q.

Under RH the second summand is O(H^(1/2)log²H/Q) and the favourable criterion for B_l holds eventually for each loss. If β=sup Reρ>1/2, choose a zero of abscissa b>max(1/2,2β/3). The global ceiling θ(H)−H=O_η(H^(β+η)) used in this phase (for β=1 Chebyshev suffices) makes the previous error o(X^b/Q^(b+2)) on choosing η small. The diagonal floor of A_l passes to B_l for all high l. Thus proving B_l≤X^(1/2+ε) at arbitrarily high levels for each ε would suffice. The deficit of the primes p>H has not been bounded. The argument does not claim that θ(H)−H is unconditionally O(√X Q).

**Pointwise replacement of any power cutoff by continuous density.** Write K_Q(t)=1_{floor(t)≡Q mod 2Q}, and β=sup Reρ. For 2≤H≤x, 1≤Q≤x dyadic, one has
    |Σ_{h≤H}Λ(h)K_Q(x/h)−∫₁ᴴ K_Q(x/u)du| ≪_ε x^(1/2+ε) H^(β−1/2).
Unlike the previous large sieve, the exponent on the right-hand side depends on β. The integral is deterministic and keeps the effect of the boundary H on the cells.

Justification. For small η>0, the twisted balance Σ_{h≤y}Λ(h)h^(−it)−∫₁ʸu^(−it)du is O_η(y^(β+η) log^C(2+y+|t|)) uniformly in y≥2 and real t. If β+η≥1 Chebyshev suffices. Otherwise apply truncated Perron to −ζ'/ζ(s+it) with half-integer cutoff y and height T=(2+y+|t|)^4. The truncation error is O(log²(2y)) by the separation of the integers (start at 1+1/log y). Shift to β+η: the local formula for the logarithmic derivative gives O_η(log²(2+|t+Im s|)) there and on the horizontals, avoiding the pole at 1. The residue y^(1−it)/(1−it) coincides with the integral up to O(1); the horizontals cost O(y log²T/T). Rounding y affects sum and integral by O(log(2y)). By partial summation with the real weight u^(−σ), at σ=1/2+η the finite transform
    D_H(s)=Σ_{h≤H}Λ(h)h^(−s)−∫₁ᴴ u^(−s)du
is bounded by O_η(H^(β−1/2) log^(C+1)(2+H+|t|)), even at β=1/2 through the logarithm of the integral. For cases with β+η close to 1 the constant of the line may depend on its distance to the fixed pole.

The Mellin transform of the cell difference is D_H(s)H_Q(s)/s. After smoothing of additive width one, shift to σ=1/2+η without crossing poles, since D_H is entire. The uniform mean square for Q^s H_Q(s) and the band computation of the converse give the stated ceiling, choosing η small relative to ε. Undoing the smoothing costs O(log(2x)): the discrete jumps are divisor subsums, and in the integral each endpoint x/q, truncated to [1,H], changes at speed at most 1/q; it suffices to sum up to q≤2x+2. The proof remains valid for H or Q fixed as functions of the evaluation point, freezing them inside the smoothing.

In the diagonal band fix any 0<α<1 and H=X^α. In the previous deficit replace the mass of all h≤H by that integral, and keep only primes p>H in the sum. The resulting mean deficit satisfies the same equivalent criterion: under RH the cost per node is O_ε(X^(1/2+ε)), first reducing ε to absorb Q=log X and the cost of the higher powers. If β>1/2, the exponent 1/2+α(β−1/2) is strictly smaller than β. Choose a zero of abscissa larger than that exponent and a loss smaller than the slack; the replacement cost is o(X^b/Q^(b+2)). The floor of the mean deficit persists at all high levels. For example α=0.99 leaves as the only prime entries the p>X^0.99. The unconditional root bound centred at θ(H)/(2Q) of the previous entry was proved only up to X^(2/3); here the centre changes and the comparison is with the scale of the zero. The choice α=1 loses the exponent slack.

**A single cell and reduction to correlations at intermediate separations.** In the diagonal criterion it suffices to count primes in (x/(Q+1),x/Q], without the other odd quotients and without correction by a power cutoff. An equivalent arithmetic condition is given that contains only pairs of distinct integers. Let Q=2^l, X=exp(Q), n an integer with X≤2Qn≤QX, N the number of such n. Put a_m=1_{m prime}log m−1, I_m=[m/2,(1+1/Q)m/2) and W(m,r)=N^(−1) #{n of the band in I_m∩I_r}. For D=floor(exp(√log X)) it suffices to prove, for each ε>0 at arbitrarily high levels, the uniform one-sided ceiling
    Σ_{|m−r|>D} a_m a_r W(m,r) ≤ X^(1+ε).
The sum is over ordered pairs of positive integers. Those of positive weight satisfy m,r≤X and |m−r|≤X/Q. Here the arithmetic difficulty is concentrated in the collective sign of the correlations at intermediate separations. There are classical antecedents for the second moment of short intervals (Selberg's integral); the specialization is this discrete band and the explicit removal of the other quotients and of the small separations.

To justify the single cell, its Mellin factor is J_Q(s)=Q^(−s)−(Q+1)^(−s), and J_Q(1)x is the length of the interval. By its explicit formula, in fixed strips it has polynomial growth in Q,|s|, and for each exterior zero ρ of abscissa b one has J_Q(ρ)=ρ Q^(−ρ−1)(1+O_ρ(1/Q)). Replacing H_Q by J_Q in the two tests of the diagonal criterion keeps the floor of the mean deficit ≫X^b/Q^(b+2) at each high level. This compares the cell directly with its own length; it does not approximate the sum of all cells by the first. For the passage to primes alone the Chebyshev bound for higher powers O(√(QX)) suffices; rounding to the nodes costs O(Q log X) through the jumps of the endpoints. Under RH, the difference between θ and its argument at both endpoints is O(√X log²X) on the whole band. Hence the same root-scale criterion for a single cell, without a maximum assumption.

At a node the prime balance minus the length differs by ≤1 from Z_n=Σ_m a_m 1_{n∈I_m}. Indeed the interval for m is (2Qn/(Q+1),2n], and the integer count differs from its length by ≤1. Expanding, the mean of Z_n² is exactly Σ_{m,r}a_m a_r W(m,r). For the terms with |m−r|≤D, the weight is O(1/Q), since N≍X and |I_m|≤X/(2Q) for relevant m. Using 2|a_m a_r|≤a_m²+a_r² and Σ_{m≤X}a_m²≪X log X by Chebyshev, this whole contribution, in absolute value, is O((1+D)X log X/Q)=X^(1+o(1)). Consequently the postulated ceiling, taking a loss smaller than the final one, gives a mean deficit at root scale by Cauchy–Schwarz. An exterior zero contradicts it by the previous floor. Conversely, under RH the mean of Z_n² is O(X log⁴ X); removing the same strip of pairs one obtains the required ceiling for each ε at all sufficiently high levels. The one-sided ceiling of the remaining correlations has not been proved.

**Positive reference on pairs with at most three factors and exact separation of signs by parity.** Keep x=2Qn and the first cell of the preceding criterion. Split the integers into consecutive blocks of length B=floor(X^0.44). In each complete block J that touches some cell, distribute B uniformly among the m=2u of J with Ω(u)≤2 (Ω counts multiplicities). Call w_m the weight received, zero at the others. The integers of the block outside the cells are also counted when defining its normalization. In all relevant blocks there are ≫B/log X receivers, with a uniform constant.

Indeed those blocks lie between X/(2Q) and 2X for high X. Lemma 1 and the proof of the theorem of Li Hong-Ze, «Almost Primes in Short Intervals» (1994), give ≫y^0.4386/log y integers with at most two factors in (y−y^0.4386,y]. Inside the scaled half J/2, fit those intervals successively from the upper end until the next one no longer fits. They occupy length ≫B, since the remainder costs O(X^0.4386)=o(B). Summing the bounds gives the claim. Source: https://www.sciengine.com/doi/pdf/24f4c4ca33c64e14bb528deed60a9962 (Lemma 1 and §5).

Put b_m=1_{m prime}log m−w_m in the relevant blocks and zero outside. The complete interior blocks have reference mass exactly equal to their discrete length; the two boundary blocks cost at most 2B in total absolute discrepancy by positivity. Thus Σ_{m in cell}b_m differs from the prime error relative to the true length by O(B+1) uniformly, strictly below the root scale. Moreover w_m≪log X and Σw_m≪X, so that Σb_m²≪X log X. Replacing a by b in the equivalence of the previous entry is valid by the triangle inequality in quadratic norm and the same absolute bound for the small separations.

With D=floor(exp(√log X)), let E and O be the sums of |b_m b_r| W(m,r) at separations >D, even and odd respectively. In these bands the prime 2 is absent: the positive coefficients are at odd primes and all the negative ones at even integers of the form 2u with Ω(u)≤2. Hence the remaining signed sum is exactly E−O. The necessary and sufficient condition is E≤O+X^(1+ε) at arbitrarily high levels for each ε>0 (the smaller losses absorb constants). The step uses the unconditional abundance of almost primes to build the reference weights, not an estimate of the correlations. The two nonnegative masses remain to be compared; the argument provides no pairing between their pairs.

**Effective local pairing of almost all the mass with subroot error in each cell.** In the previous reference one can choose the integer origin of the blocks modulo B=floor(X^0.44) and cancel equal masses on the two supports within each block. Writing δ=log log X/log X, the total unpaired absolute mass is O(Xδ). The paired portion contributes O(B log X)=o(√X) in EACH first cell. These are two distinct controls: the second is pointwise and applies only to the paired portion.

Indeed, for e(t)=θ(t)−θ(t−B)−B, at the relevant integer endpoints and their block neighbours, one has Σ_t e(t)²≪XB²δ². Cover [X/(3Q),2X] with dyadic intervals [Y,2Y] of total length O(X). The main theorem of Zaccagnini (1998), ε(Y)=0, holds with B≥Y^(1/6), and log Y≍log X. For integer t, the count in (t−B,t] stays constant on [t,t+1); changing log t to the logarithm of the real endpoint costs O(B/Y) after multiplying the prediction by log t. Weighting individually by log p instead of log t costs O(B²/Y) by the trivial count. These errors are absorbed into Bδ. Summing the quadratic estimate over the bands gives the bound. Source: https://bibliotekanauki.pl/articles/1390756.pdf (theorem, p. 225).

Choose the class of endpoints modulo B that minimizes the sum over that finite range (smallest representative in case of a tie). Averaging divides by B, hence Σ_J e_J²≪XBδ² over the blocks touching cells, where e_J=Σ_{p∈J}log p−B. In each J order both supports and successively transfer the minimum of the two weights still available until one side is exhausted. Splitting weights is allowed. Every pair has separation at most B. The remaining absolute mass in J is exactly |e_J| and its sign is unique there. Cauchy–Schwarz with O(X/B) blocks gives Σ_J |e_J|≪Xδ. In a cell only the two endpoints cut pairs; even there the mass of each paired side is at most B per block, so even O(B) suffices for the pointwise discrepancy.

Let r_m be the signed residual coefficient. Replacing b_m by r_m in the quadratic criterion keeps the equivalence by the triangle inequality in RMS, and |r_m|≤|b_m| preserves the absolute control of nearby pairs. Moreover there is a sign-free bound for the second moment of the residual mass: each cell touches O(X/(QB)) blocks and each block enters O(X/Q) nodes, since its endpoints in n lie between inf(J)/2 and (1+1/Q)sup(J)/2. By Cauchy–Schwarz inside the cell and N≍X,
    mean_n (Σ_{m in cell}|r_m|)² ≪ [X/(QB)] [1/Q] Σ_J e_J² ≪ (Xδ/Q)².
The target remains O_ε(X^(1+ε)) for the signed second moment at arbitrarily high levels. The absolute bound obtained is larger; the balance between the surplus and deficit blocks remains pending.

**Second cancellation between blocks and limit of the available estimate.** In the selected partition group K consecutive blocks of length B into groups of length L=KB. Take K even with L≍√X/δ, δ=log log X/log X. The balance of a group is g=Σ_J e_J, that is the prime mass minus the length of the whole group. In each group leftovers of opposite signs can be paired again. One can also concentrate g in a single atom at its right endpoint. In both cases the additional change in the balance of the first cell costs O(√X) in RMS over n, without hypotheses on zeros. In the second formulation it suffices to study sums of the g of groups whose endpoints fall in the cell: this reduces to O(X/L) consecutive prime balances per band.

For the boundary groups of the domain extend with blocks in the same class of endpoints (already covered in [X/(3Q),2X]). For each group G let u_G=Σ_{J⊂G}|e_J|, the residual absolute mass of the first stage. The interior groups keep their sum exactly; in a cut group the difference from the atom or from the new pairing costs at most 2u_G. Each of the two cell endpoints, 2n and 2Qn/(Q+1), visits a group in O(L) indices, because both grow at speed ≥1 per index. Since N≍X and Σ_G u_G²≤K Σ_J e_J²≪XLδ², the mean of the squares of the changes is O(L²δ²). Add the pointwise error O(B) of the first stage. This allows the RMS equivalence with the balances g; it does not authorize removing the diagonal squares of the concentrated atoms.

The dependence Lδ in this operation is optimal if only the quadratic bound on e_J is used. As an auxiliary model, give the first K/2 blocks of each group weight +s_G Bδ and the others −s_G Bδ, with independent equiprobable signs s_G per group. Distribute each weight uniformly inside the block. All g are zero and Σe_J²≪XBδ². However the partial balance of a group at distance between L/4 and 3L/4 from its initial endpoint has modulus ≥Lδ/4 up to rounding O(δ). For a fixed proportion of the indices n of the band the endpoint 2n is there (it runs through the groups in steps of 2). On the whole band the cell length is ≫X/Q², larger than L for the indicated choice or, more generally, L=o(X/Q²). Its two endpoints are in different groups, and their cross terms have expectation zero. The expectation of the second moment of the balance is ≫L²δ²; some choice of the signs realizes it. The model does not prescribe the weights of the primes: it shows why pairing at significantly larger distances with cost O(√X) requires additional information about the actual e_J.

**Unconditional reach larger than √X by any power of log X.** For the same fine blocks B=floor(X^0.44) one can choose in the two previous stages
    δ*=exp(−c(log X/log log X)^(1/3)),    L≍√X/δ*
with fixed c>0 sufficiently small. With that choice the first stage leaves O(Xδ*) of absolute mass and the second has RMS cost O(√X). An explicit length that avoids knowing c is L≍√X exp((log X)^0.30), rounded to an even multiple of B. For this last length the RMS cost of the two stages together is even o(√X).

The additional input relative to the arbitrary-signs model is the second moment for θ with exponential saving of Saffari–Vaughan, in the form of Theorem 3.2 of Languasco–Zaccagnini, k=1 and C=12/5 by the unconditional density. For Y^(1/6+η)≤B≤Y (take η=1/10) it bounds ∫_[Y,2Y]|θ(t+B)−θ(t)−B|²dt by O(YB² exp(−c₀(log Y/log log Y)^(1/3))). Source: https://www.impan.pl/shop/publication/transaction/download/product/82818 . In the block range [X/(3Q),2X] the hypothesis holds uniformly, and log Y/log X tends to one. Since B is an integer, the integrand is constant on each half-open unit interval. Covering the integer starts by dyadic bands gives a sum O(XB²(δ*)²), reducing c to absorb the square root and the boundaries. Averaging the B origins as before gives Σ_J e_J²≪XB(δ*)². Li's reference is built in that selected partition. From here the two claims follow by the previous inequalities: total RMS cost O(B+Lδ*) and unpaired mass O(Xδ*). For the explicit formula, (log X)^0.30=o((log X/log log X)^(1/3)). The saturation example of the previous entry only satisfied the old bound and therefore does not prevent this improvement. The jump in L remains subpower and the balance between groups remains open.

**Spectral barrier for a compression at power scale averaged over the origin.** Fix 1/2<α<1, L=X^α and r=Q/(Q+1), with Q and X diagonal as before. Put E(y)=θ(y)−y. For a uniform in [0,L), let [y]_a be the largest point of a+L Z not exceeding y. Measure at the same n the cost of replacing the balance E(2n)−E(2rn) by E([2n]_a)−E([2rn]_a). This latter difference is the sum of the errors of complete groups between the two rounded endpoints. If its joint RMS error (in n and a) is O_ε(X^(1/2+ε)) at arbitrarily high levels for each ε, then β≤3/2−α. Thus with α=0.6 such a bound would already exclude all zeros of real part >0.9. The conclusion concerns averaged origins, or a ceiling uniform in them; it does not follow from a single favourably chosen origin.

Proof. At each endpoint the mean of the rounding error is D(y)=E(y)−L^(−1)∫₀ᴸE(y−h)dh; independence of the two endpoints is not needed. Let Y=X/Q. If β>3/2−α, choose a zero ρ of abscissa b so close to β that b>3/2−α and b>β+α−1. Fix 1/2<σ<b. Use the smooth isolation function f of 230, with nonzero moment ∫f(v)exp(ρv)dv and vanishing at all other zeros of abscissa ≥σ, translating its support to a fixed [1,K]. Consider the moment of D(Ye^v)−D(rYe^v) against e^v f(v)dv. For the first term, in y coordinates the test density is w(y)=f(log(y/Y))/Y. Moving the translation onto the test produces w(y)−w(y+h)=−hw'(y)+O(h²/Y³) on a support of length O(Y). The ceiling E=O_η(Y^(β+η)) gives, after averaging h, the total moment
    −(L/(2Y))∫ f'(v)[E(Ye^v)−r^(−1)E(rYe^v)]dv + O((L/Y)^2 Y^(β+η)).
For the second endpoint the same computation was applied with scale rY. The tests are fixed and r→1.

In the integrated explicit formula, the moment of f' at z is −z times that of f. The target contributes inside the integral a fixed nonzero multiple of Y^ρ(1−r^(ρ−1)). Its modulus is ≫_ρ Y^b/Q because ρ≠1. The other zeros and higher powers cost O_f(Y^σ polylog Y) by rapid decay and the previous vanishing. Take η sufficiently small using b>β+α−1: both errors are o(L Y^(b−1)/Q) after accounting for their prefactors. By Cauchy–Schwarz the continuous RMS norm of D(y)−D(ry) on [eY,e^K Y] is ≫ L Y^(b−1)/Q. Passing to y=2n costs O(log X) in that norm: θ varies by O(log X) under bounded shifts, also after translating and averaging. The local band contains ≍Y nodes within the N≍X global ones; the dilution costs O(√Q). By Jensen in a, the joint RMS dominates the RMS of the average in a. Consequently it is ≫_ρ L Y^(b−1)/Q^(3/2) at all sufficiently high levels, of exponent α+b−1>1/2. This contradicts the proposed bound for ε smaller than the slack. The obstruction is for the true arithmetic sequence under a hypothetical zero; the auxiliary sign model of the previous entry only treated the limits of an abstract inequality.

**Groups of length X^(3/4): one mass and its centre suffice for a smoothed test that keeps every exterior zero.** Keep Q,X,n of the diagonal, y=2n, r=Q/(Q+1). Fix h the convolution of four uniform densities on [0,1]. Average in v with that weight the prime count of the first cell (ry exp v,y exp v] minus its length. In any partition into groups of length L≤X^(3/4), replace the prime measure of each group by a single atom: mass M_J=Σ_{p∈J}log p at z_J=Σ_{p∈J}p log p/M_J, omitting empty groups. Take the complete groups touching the support (primes up to e^4X+L are needed). The change of the smoothed balance costs O(√X) POINTWISE at all nodes and for every origin of the partition. The condition that the mean deficit of the compressed balance be ≤X^(1/2+ε) at arbitrarily high levels for each ε is equivalent to RH.

Indeed the weight of a prime in the smoothed balance is W_y(z)=∫_[log(z/y),log(z/y)−log r] h(v)dv. Its support lies in [ry,e^4y], and ||W_y''||∞≪1/(Qy²): differentiate under the integral after translating the interval to [0,−log r], using bounded h' and h'' and z≍y. The extension by zero keeps this regularity. In each group the first variation at z_J vanishes exactly. The error is at most ||W_y''||∞ L² M_J/2 by Taylor. Since y≥X/Q and L=o(y), the relevant groups together weigh O(y) by Chebyshev. The error is therefore O(L²/(Qy))=O(√X). The mean length of the interval is kept as an exact deterministic term, (1−r)y∫h(v)e^v dv.

Under RH the smoothed count has error O(√X log² X) by the pointwise ceiling on θ. For the other direction, using the two fixed tests of the diagonal in the variable x=Qy, the cell factor J_Q(s)=Q^(−s)−(Q+1)^(−s) gets multiplied by ∫h(v)e^(sv)dv=((e^s−1)/s)^4 (value 1 at zero). The new factor is fixed, does not vanish in Re s>0 and is bounded in fixed vertical strips. The isolation moment at an exterior zero ρ and the moment of the positive test annihilating all zeros to the right of σ therefore keep the previous estimates; the higher-power terms cost O(√(QX)) or less. Passing to the next node costs O(Q log X) or less even after smoothing because v stays in [0,4]. Again the mean deficit has floor ≫_ρ X^b/Q^(b+2) for b=Reρ>1/2 at every high level. The uniform perturbation O(√X) does not remove that floor. This use of the first moment differs from the global barycentre of 247-A: the centres are local, used only as a second-order quadrature for a fixed test. It does not control at root scale the rounding of the sharp cell of the previous entry. The arithmetic estimate of the smoothed balance from the masses and the centres is missing.

**Masses only, prescribed groups of length X^(2/3)/(log X)^4.** In the smoothed four-uniform test one can store only M_J=Σ_{p∈J}log p per group and place it at the midpoint of its integers. Choose L a power of two comparable to X^(2/3)/(log X)^4. For any integer origin of the groups of L consecutive integers, the error is o(√X) uniformly in the nodes, unconditionally. Here the first moment of the primes is not consulted. It is a conclusion for the smoothed cell.

Proof. For an integer m of a group with midpoint c(m), s(m)=(c(m)−m)/L is periodic modulo L, with mean zero by the choice of the midpoint (it may be a half-integer). The expansion of W_y(c(p)) around p has linear term L s(p)W'_y(p). The remainder costs O(L²/(Qy)) as before, since L=o(y) and all contributing groups lie in an interval of size O(y). In the discrete transform of s, the successive difference is −1/L except for one jump per period. Thus, for k nonzero, the modulus of the coefficient is ≤1/(L|1−exp(2πik/L)|)≪1/min(k,L−k). A translation of the origin only changes phases.

Apply Vaughan's classical theorem for Σ_{m≤t}Λ(m)exp(2πi k m/L): with q=L/gcd(k,L), at t≍y the ceiling is O((y/√q+y^(4/5)+√(yq))log⁴(2y)). The restriction to primes costs O(√y) by Chebyshev. To sum the frequencies one uses Σ|ŝ(k)|≪log(2L) and Σ|ŝ(k)|/√q≪log(2L)/√L: group by the binary valuation j of k≤L/2, apply Σ_{2^j|k≤L/2}1/k≪2^(−j)log(2L) and sum 2^(−j/2); reflect the other half. By Abel, integrating with W'_y costs O(1/(Qy)), since ||W'_y||∞ and the integral of |W_y''| have that bound. Therefore the total error is
    O(L²/(Qy) + L log^5(2X)/(Qy) [y/√L + y^(4/5) + √(yL)]).
Since X/Q≤y≤X and Q=log X, the three linear terms are respectively O(√L log⁴X), O(L X^(−1/5)log^(21/5)X) and O(L^(3/2)X^(−1/2)log^(9/2)X). They are o(√X) with the chosen length, as is the remainder. For the exponential sum estimate see the classical statement via Vaughan's identity, for example J. Salmensuu, thesis, https://www.utupub.fi/bitstream/handle/10024/153603/AnnalesAI667Salmensuu.pdf .

The same diagonal criterion is kept by the Lipschitz property of the positive part. The number of masses needed on the whole band is reduced to O(X^(1/3)log⁴X), at prescribed positions. The improvement over the compression of pure totals by pairing uses the cancellation of a prime sum against the periodic rounding error and the smoothing of the test; it does not extend that precision to the sharp count.

**Unconditional amplitude barrier for certifying the smoothed test by factorials.** With r=Q/(Q+1) and h of four uniforms, put w(t)=W_1(1/t) for t>0. A global minorant g(t)=Σ_j c_j floor(t/d_j) with real dilations d_j>0, real coefficients, finite sum and balance Σ c_j/d_j=0, gives a lower count through ΣΛ(m)g(y/m)=Σ c_j log(floor(y/d_j)!). With Δ=∫₀^∞(w−g)dt/t² and B=||w−g||∞ one has
    B Δ ≫ 1/Q².
In particular, if y≍X and one seeks yΔ≤C√X in the continuous main term, it is necessary that B≫_C √X/Q², and also Σ_j|c_j|≫_C √X/Q² for high X. The barrier is independent of how many factorials are used and allows their dilations to be moved off the integers.

Proof. For Re s>1, the integral of g(t)t^(−s−1) is ζ(s)Σ c_j d_j^(−s)/s. The profile vanishes for sufficiently small t and is bounded by Σ|c_j| thanks to the balance; hence its continuation to Re s>0, with removable singularity at 1 in the formula. On the other hand, by the change of variable u=1/t and integration over the first cell,
    ∫w(t)t^(−s−1)dt = (1−r^s)/s · ((e^s−1)/s)^4.
Fix any known zero ρ of ζ on the critical line. The modulus of this expression is ≫_ρ 1/Q for large Q; that of g is zero. For the deficit D=w−g≥0 and b=Reρ, the triangle inequality and the cut at R>0 give
    c_ρ/Q ≤ ∫D(t)t^(−b−1)dt ≤ R^(1−b)Δ + (B/b)R^(−b).
Neither B nor Δ can be zero. Take R=B/Δ. For b=1/2 the unconditional barrier follows. Since ||w||∞=O(1/Q), the limit on the absolute sum of coefficients follows from ||g||∞≤Σ|c_j|. At any hypothetical zero of abscissa b>1/2 one gets the stronger condition B^(1−b)Δ^b≫_ρ 1/Q. The same proof holds for global majorants, changing the orientation of the deficit.

Compared with the jump count of the factorial minorant of this round, here the obstacle is the amplitude, even with real support of arbitrary size. The precision Δ refers to the continuous main term: it is not a lower bound for the loss sampled at the primes, nor does it rule out that the signed Stirling remainders compensate that loss. The ψ versus θ variant only affects higher powers in the count, not the statement about profiles.

**Correction of scope: the global optimum for the previous factorial minorant is zero.** The BΔ inequality of the previous entry is valid, but it does not describe the decisive obstacle. A finite balanced profile g that minorizes on the whole half-line a nonnegative function w(t) tending to zero at infinity is necessarily ≤0. Indeed, if g has a positive value, by right continuity there is a point t₀ interior to a positive step. There exist arbitrarily large T with all T/d_j at arbitrarily small distance from integers n_j (simultaneous returns of the phase flow on a compact torus). Without crossing any edge in the phases of t₀, g(t₀+T)=g(t₀)+Σ c_j n_j, and the last summand tends to zero by balance. This contradicts the ceiling w(t₀+T)→0. The optimum is attained with g=0 and, for the previous compact weight, Δ_min=(1−r)∫h(v)e^v dv. Increasing amplitudes offers no escape under global minorization. It does not apply to an inequality required only on the physical range t≤y or only at prime samples.

**A positive filter that removes the critical line, but not the recurrence obstruction.** To distinguish the two obstacles, construct a level-independent filter that removes all critical zeros and annihilates no point off that line. For each positive ordinate γ of a nontrivial zero (also those of exterior zeros, with multiplicity) put a_γ=π/(2γ). By the zero count Σ a_γ²<∞. With independent fair signs, U=Σ ±a_γ converges in L² and almost surely. Its two-sided transform is ∏ cosh(a_γ s): the bound cosh(t)≤exp(t²/2) on the real line guarantees exponential uniform integrability of the partial sums. Tilt the law of U by exp(−U/2) and normalize, and add an independent standard Gaussian. The resulting positive law ν has entire transform
    K(s)=exp(s²/2) ∏_γ cosh(a_γ(s−1/2))/cosh(a_γ/2).
The product converges on compacts because the deviations from one are O_compact(a_γ²). It cannot vanish without a factor vanishing. Hence all its zeros lie on Re s=1/2, and among them are all the points 1/2±iγ. There are additional critical harmonics. The construction uses the ordinates of the zeros; it does not presuppose that they have real part 1/2. Unlike the cosh products of the HYP index, no attempt is made to represent the theta kernel by the product.

For fixed r=1/2 average ψ(y exp v)−ψ(ry exp v) against ν(dv) and subtract (1−r)K(1)y. Under RH the balance is O(1/y) for y≥1. By inversion the integrand before subtracting the main term is y^s(−ζ'/ζ)(s)K(s)(1−r^s)/s. In each fixed strip K decays like a Gaussian in height (the tilted law without the Gaussian has all exponential moments). Shift to Re s=−1: the pole at 1 gives the main term and the singularities at the nontrivial zeros are removed under RH even at multiple zeros, since the logarithmic derivative has a simple pole. The quotient at s=0 is regular and no trivial zero is crossed yet. Cuts at good heights and the functional equation on the left line justify the shift.

Conversely, an eventual minorant of the balance by −1 would exclude any exterior zero: there the factors K and (1−r^s)/s do not vanish. Apply Landau to the Mellin transform over [1,∞) of the balance plus 1, regular on the real half-line s>0 after subtracting the main term and with a pole at each exterior zero. The (0,1) portion of the observable BEFORE centring has entire Mellin transform: ψ(t)≪t and the test has exponential moments of all orders, so the uncentred expectation is O_A(y^A) for each A>1 at that end. The smallest adjustment on a finite interval does not affect the argument.

This diagnosis does not produce a factorial certificate. The profile at t=y/p of the new test is the probability that v falls in an interval of fixed length that moves towards −∞ as t→∞. It also tends to zero, so the recurrence correction applies unchanged. The critical zeros can be removed from the test; the impossibility of the global factorial minorant persists for an elementary reason independent of them. There is no arithmetic estimate of the balance by −1.

**Arithmetic finite-selection test of the filter, without ordinates in the definition of the test.** For each integer X≥3 and fixed integer budget A, enumerate lists of at most ceil(log X) numbers a=k/X²≥0, k an integer, with Σa²≤A. For each list use independent signs tilted as before and an independent Gaussian N(−1/2,1). Its transform is
    K_a(s)=exp((s²−s)/2) ∏ cosh(a(s−1/2))/cosh(a/2).
Both K_a(0) and K_a(1) equal one. For r=1/2 define F_a(y)=E_ν[ψ(y exp v)−ψ(ry exp v)]−(1−r)y. Let V_A(X) be the minimum over the finite list of X^(−1)∫_X^(2X)|F_a(y)|dy. The test uses only arithmetic counts, Gaussian weights and a rational mesh. RH is equivalent to having, for some fixed A, V_A(X)≤1 at arbitrarily high integers X. Under RH for some A the minimum is O(X^(−1)) at all large X. With a zero of abscissa b>1/2 it is ≫_{ρ,A} X^b for every fixed A and all sufficiently large X. This reduces the dependence on ordinates of the previous entry to an existence argument under RH. No efficiency of enumeration is claimed.

Key uniformity. For a fixed exterior target ρ, |cosh(a(ρ−1/2))|/cosh(a/2) does not vanish for 0≤a≤√A. The logarithm of that modulus divided by a² extends continuously at zero. Hence the product is ≥exp(−C_{ρ,A}Σa²) and |K_a(ρ)| stays uniformly away from zero. In a bounded real strip, by |cosh(u+iv)|≤cosh u and log cosh u≤u²/2, all K_a(s) are bounded by C_A exp(−(Im s)²/2), with a constant depending on the strip. The integrated explicit formula or the shift to −1 used above thus hold with remainder O_A(1/y), uniformly in the list. The contribution of each zero is −mult(z)y^z(1−r^z)K_a(z)/z.

If there is a target zero ρ, choose 1/2<σ<b. Use the complex isolation test of 230 inside [0,log 2], with nonzero moment at ρ, zero at the other distinct zeros of abscissa ≥σ. The list is frozen for the whole band. After integrating F_a(X exp v) against that test, the zeros of abscissa <σ cost O_A(X^σ) by the Gaussian bound.
