The explicit formula for L and Stirling give l(u)=½log(u/(2π))+O(1/u), l'(u)=1/(2u)+O(1/u²); for the terms of ζ and their derivatives use their absolutely convergent series. Thus ε(U)=sup_{u≥U}|u l'(u)/l(u)|→0. For distance x=|log(u_i/u_j)| the difference with respect to C is bounded by 2exp(−x/2)(cosh(εx/2)−1). For ε≤1/2 the majorant on x≥rh is dominated by 2exp(−rh/4); for fixed r its supremum tends to zero (separate a compact part and an exponential tail). By dominated convergence the two-sided sum of these suprema tends to zero with ε. Choose U so that the perturbation has row sums <b_h/2. The floor b_h/2 remains for all coefficients in unit-diagonal coordinates, without controlling the roots of the numerator.

There is also a finite q_0 for which any u_1>1/2 can be taken if q≥q_0. Indeed l(u) is comparable to log(2+u) uniformly in u≥1/2 by Stirling and by strictly positive continuity at the endpoint (theta representation at u=1/2). For two rates with ratio exp(x) both ratios l_i/l_j and l_j/l_i are ≤C(1+x), using log(2+e^x u)≤log(2+u)+x. The normalized kernel has modulus ≤C' exp(−x/2)√(1+x). The off-diagonal rows have sum tending to zero as h→∞, uniformly in the initial rate. This proves the second claim by diagonal dominance. The thresholds are existential. For fixed q the sum Σ1/u_j converges, so these separated families do not realize the causal density condition by divergence of the Blaschke sum from the beginning of this memo. Passing to q descending to 1 requires controlling the floor and the initial rate simultaneously.

### Full spaces with ratio between rates tending to one

Let x_i=log u_i. There is an absolute X such that, if x_1≥X and x_{i+1}−x_i≥200/x_i, the full POWER block is positive definite at all orders, for any coefficients. A single sequence with u_{i+1}/u_i→1 is admissible. Antecedent: the real-positive comparator no-go of phase 212 treats global closure; here only comparison with a weighted floor on nodes whose Blaschke sum converges is used.

In the coordinates obtained by diagonal congruence with √(2u_i), the matrix is C_ij(l_i+l_j), where C is the previous normalized Gram matrix. Take A=2πe² and g(u)=1+½log(1+u/A). By Stirling r=l−g=O(1/u). The comparator block is ≥2C: indeed log(1+u/A)=∫_0^1 u/(A+tu)dt, and the Pick kernel of u/(A+tu) is [A+2tuv/(u+v)]/[(A+tu)(A+tv)], positive by Cauchy Gram and congruence. This avoids the error of inverse logarithmic size from comparing directly with a constant.

Let S_i=Σ_j C_ij. The explicit inverse of C gives C≥diag(1/(p_i² S_i)): in the formula for C^−1 bound in absolute value by Σ_ij C_ij p_i|v_i|p_j|v_j|≤Σ S_i p_i²|v_i|² and invert the order. All subsequent bounds are uniform for finite subsets. A unit interval [t,t+1] with t≥0 contains O(1+t) nodes by the separation rule. Hence S_i=O(1+x_i) by exponential summation. Among nodes with x_j≤2x_i the minimal consecutive distance is ≥100/x_i. By monotonicity of f(s)=log coth(s/2) and sum-integral comparison, their contribution to log p_i is ≤2(x_i/100)∫_0^∞f(s)ds<0.06 x_i: the integral is 2Σ_{n odd}1/n²=π²/4. For x_j>2x_i the contribution is O((1+x_i)e^(−x_i)) by the unit density and f(s)=O(e^(−s)). The row floor is therefore ≳exp(−0.12 x_i)/(1+x_i).

The difference E_ij=C_ij(r_i+r_j) has absolute row sum O((1+x_i)^2 exp(−x_i/4)): if |x_j−x_i|≤x_i/2 both remainders are O(exp(−x_i/2)) and S_i suffices. Outside that interval the remainders are uniformly bounded and C_ij≤2exp(−|x_i−x_j|/2); sum over unit intervals. By 2|v_i v_j|≤|v_i|²+|v_j|², this error is absorbed simultaneously by the floor of C for x_1≥X. Strict positivity follows.

The recurrence x_{i+1}=x_i+200/x_i gives x_i∼20√i by summing x_{i+1}²−x_i²=400+40000/x_i². Although the ratio of rates tends to one, the absolute jump grows and Σ1/u_i converges. Hence this result does not supply the density bridge in the norm of the form. The reduction of the error to order 1/u and the weighted floor explain why the fixed multiplicative separation can indeed be abandoned.

### Scope correction and optimal logarithmic floor at small reciprocal mass

ROUND_085_A already contains positivity for all numerators with Σ1/u≤1/512, even after physical truncation. Taking the truncation to infinity (or repeating its estimate without truncation) includes the mere-sign conclusions of the two recent separation entries: the mass of their tails tends uniformly to zero by the unit density O(1+x) in x=log u. For large q with a low initial pole, the direct diagonal argument keeps its additional scope. The floors on the Pick diagonal are not formulated in 085. Do not present the mere sign of the tails of those sequences as a new extension with respect to the corpus.

Quantitative improvement. Let S=Σ1/u≤1/4, L>0 (infinity included), g=f·1_[0,L] for any f in the rational block. With an absolute constant C, simultaneously in rates, multiplicities, numerator and cutoff,
    W(g) ≥ [log(1/min(S,L))−C] ||g||².
To prove it normalize ||f||₂=1 and take σ=1/(4S). The Hardy reflection of 085 gives ||exp(σt)f||₂²≤exp(16/15)<3. If L≥10S, ||g||₂²≥1−3 exp(−5)>1/2 and ||g||₁²≤3/(2σ)=6S. If L<10S, Cauchy gives directly ||g||₁²≤L||g||₂². Thus in both cases ||g||₁²/||g||₂²≤12 min(S,L). The comb and the polar term cost O(||g||₂²) uniformly: in the first case ||exp(t)g||₂≤√3 since σ≥1; in the second L≤2.5 gives ||exp(t)g||₂≤exp(2.5)||g||₂. Apply the weighted comparison of the first lines of this memo.

In Plancherel the normalized density |ĝ(τ)|²/(2π||g||₂²) is ≤12s/(2π) with s=min(S,L). By the digamma bound the archimedean symbol is ≥log(1+|τ|)−C. The loss relative to log(1/s) has integral at most (12s/π)∫_0^(1/s)log(1/(st))dt=12/π, using the positive part. Adding the terms gives the floor. The coefficient of log(1/S) is optimal in a universal floor without truncation: a single pole u=1/S gives quotient 2l(u)=log(1/S)−log(2π)+o(1). For any fixed sequence with finite Σ1/u, the bound on each tail grows without limit in the physical L² norm and the total algebraic negative index is finite (codimension at most the number of removed poles, counted with multiplicity). The argument indicates why continuing to choose sequences with convergent mass and discarding their first terms does not prove global positivity.

### From one positive window to an exponential comparator on a whole shifted half-plane

Assume λ_W(S)>0 for the window of paper 46 (for example S=2.765 by the bridge at the beginning). Write l(z)=ξ'(1/2+z)/ξ(1/2+z) and h=(l−1)/(l+1). There is a Schur function H_S of the right half-plane, with real symmetry, such that for all Re z>1/2
    |H_S(z)−h(z)| ≤ 2 exp(−2S(Re z−1/2)).
Consequently g_S=(1+H_S)/(1−H_S) has positive real part on Re z>0 and g_S(v)−l(v)=O_S((1+log v)² exp(−2Sv)) on the real ray v→∞. The comparator comes from the window certificate and does not need l to have positive real part on the whole half-plane. In particular it is not claimed that the kernel of the difference is positive, a condition relevant to obstruction 212-001-L.

Proof: take n distinct poles u_j=n/S+j/n² for j=1,…,n, with sum of reciprocals tending to S and minimum tending to infinity. The bridge of 195 implies positivity of the full POWER matrix on those nodes for all n sufficiently large. Its congruence by the Cayley factors is the Pick matrix of h(u_j) in the right half-plane. Finite Nevanlinna–Pick interpolation and averaging with the conjugate reflection give a real-symmetric Schur H_n interpolating those values. Independently, on Re z>1/2 one has Re l(z)>0 by the centred Hadamard product of ξ: grouping zeros w and −w, the summands of Re 1/(z−w) are positive and absolutely summable in real part (Re w bounded and count O(T log T)); the parity of the centred ξ eliminates the linear term of the paired product. Hence |h|≤1 there. On that half-plane (H_n−h)/2 is Schur and vanishes at all nodes. Iterated Schwarz gives the majorant ∏|(u_j−z)/(u_j+z−1)|. For each fixed z the logarithm of each factor is −(2Re z−1)/u_j+O_z(1/u_j²). The sum of errors tends to zero. Extract a normal subsequence on Re z>0. Its limit H_S satisfies the bound on the whole indicated half-plane. It is not a unimodular constant: along the ray h(v)→1, but 1−h(v)=2/(1+l(v)) is of order 1/log v, incompatible with H_S≡1. By the maximum principle |H_S|<1. Undoing Cayley on the ray gives the bound for g_S using 1−H_S(v) comparable to 1−h(v) there.

Checkable obstruction consequence: for any finite list of points z_i with Re z_i>1/2, strict window positivity requires that the discs with centres h(z_i) and radii 2exp(−2S(Re z_i−1/2)) admit a choice of values w_i with matrix [(1−w_i conj(w_j))/(z_i+conj(z_j))] positive semidefinite. It is a necessary condition, without certification here of impossibility for ζ. If H_S of this class were constructed for unbounded S, by Montel their limit would coincide with h on the shifted half-plane and would supply a Schur extension to Re z>0. That would exclude poles of l there by maximum principle and meromorphic uniqueness. For finite S an error remains and there is no closure. The local positive extension has antecedents in KEP of paper 46; here the uniform Cayley bound from interpolation at receding real nodes is made explicit.

Extension to the semidefinite endpoint (independent check). λ_W(S)≥0 suffices. If μ_n is the minimum in physical norm, add δ_n||f||², δ_n=max(0,−μ_n)→0. The physical Gram matrix has entries 1/(u_i+u_j), so this correction is exactly equivalent to l_n=l+δ_n/2. Interpolate the Cayley transform of l_n at the nodes and compare it with that same Cayley transform, Schur on Re z>1/2. The Schwarz argument is identical and the Cayley transform of l_n tends to h at each point of the shifted half-plane. Thus the same bound and the disc obstruction survive even without a strict floor.

### Converse at fixed window and complete test at the integers

For S>0 the following are equivalent: (i) λ_W(S)≥0; (ii) there is a Schur H on Re z>0 whose values at each integer n≥2 differ from h(n) by ≤2exp(−2S(n−1/2)); (iii) for each N≥2 there are real numbers w_n in those closed intervals, 2≤n≤N, such that [(1−w_n w_m)/(n+m)] is PSD. (i)⇒(ii) is already proved. In (ii) H can be symmetrized by conjugation. (ii)⇒(iii) is Pick; for the converse interpolate each list and take a normal subsequence, since the constraints are closed and nested. The whole family of finite tests is necessary and sufficient; a single compatible list does not certify a window.

For (ii)⇒(i), D(z)=(H(z)−h(z))/(z+1)² is in the Hardy space H² of the half-plane Re z>1. It is the Laplace transform of a causal d with e^(−t)d(t) in L² by Paley–Wiener. Transport the finite measure e^(−2t)d(t)dt by x=e^(−t) to [0,1]. Its j-th moment is D(j+2), of modulus O_S(exp(−2Sj)). Hence the Laurent series of its Cauchy transform Σ D(j+2)/ζ^(j+1) converges on |ζ|>exp(−2S), and coincides by continuation with the integral on both sides of the cut. The real measure vanishes on (exp(−2S),1] by Stieltjes inversion (also as a distributional jump); there cannot be an atom at 1. Thus d=0 on t<2S. Multiplying by (z+1)² does not advance the support. This deduces the exact delay exclusively from the integer samples.

H is strictly Schur by the real behaviour at the integers, as in the previous entry. For g=(1+H)/(1−H), the identity g−l=(H−h)(1+g)(1+l)/2 preserves the delay: both additional factors have causal inverse Laplace transforms of exponential growth. Indeed g is real-positive, and Schwarz–Pick on the half-plane gives |g(z)|≤C(1+|z|)² for Re z≥1; l satisfies a polynomial bound there by its explicit formula. Dividing by a sufficient power of z+1, using Hardy and then differentiating justifies the causal inverses and the multiplication by convolution. 

For f smooth with compact support inside (0,2S), write k_m for the causal inverse of m. One has W(f)=2Re∫ (k_l*f)(t)conj(f(t))dt in the POWER normalization. Indeed, in the centred Hadamard product, each term 1/(z−w) has causal kernel exp(wt). Summing the zeros with −conj(w), the two halves t>s and t<s of the integral give the full spectral product. The sum is taken in pairs w,−w: on Re z=1 their truncations are uniformly O((1+|z|)^3), separating |w|>2|z| (tail ≤C|z|Σ|w|^(−2)) and the rest (each resolvent ≤2 and there are O((1+|z|)log(2+|z|)) terms). This allows the limit against smooth tests. The delay makes that pairing identical for g. For σ>0, integrating (k_g*f)conj(f) with weight exp(−2σt) has nonnegative real part by Plancherel and Re g(σ+iτ)≥0. Letting σ go down to zero the pairing converges by compact support of f and smoothness of the convolution. Translating and passing to the form kernel of paper 46 proves (i), even at the semidefinite endpoint.

Condition (iii) is a finite convex feasibility: with C_nm=1/(n+m) and V=diag(w_n), it suffices to use [[C,V C],[C V,C]], whose Schur complement is C−V C V. The advantage over KEP and the previous direction is that a single explicit real mesh with given tolerances suffices; the arithmetic content persists in compatibility for all N.

### Elimination of the free values: two explicit matrices per sublist

With S>0 fixed, the integer mesh can be started at any sufficiently large n₀: omitting a prefix only replaces the weight e^(−2t) of the moment proof by e^(−n₀t). Take n₀ such that the intervals of h(n) lie strictly in (−1,1), possible by the real asymptotics. Transport both endpoints w by (1+w)/(n(1−w)), obtaining [a_n,b_n] for g(n)/n. For any nonempty finite sublist n_1<…<n_m put x_i=n_i², D(t)=∏(t+x_i). For e=0,1 with e<m, choose B_i=b_{n_i} if (−1)^(i−1+e)=+1 and a_{n_i} otherwise. Then λ_W(S)≥0 is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness of ALL the explicit matrices
    M_rs=Σ_i B_i (−x_i)^(e+r+s)/D'(−x_i),   0≤r,s≤⌊(m−1−e)/2⌋.
The sublists are arbitrary; the sequence of prefixes does not suffice in this proof. It is not required that a single alternating choice of endpoints interpolate the list.

Proof. By Herglotz with real symmetry, the allowed values of g(n)/n have the form c+∫ dμ(t)/(t+x_i), c≥0, μ positive on [0,∞), ∫dμ/(1+t)<∞ (pair the opposite frequencies and put t=τ²). Conversely each representation produces a comparator with nonnegative real part. In finite dimension the cone is closed: use the generators (1+t)/(t+x_i) compactified by the vector of ones at infinity, whose first coordinate is bounded below. By separation with the compact box, feasibility is equivalent to sup_box Σ c_i v_i≥0 for every vector of the dual cone. Its coordinates are exactly c_i=P(−x_i)/D'(−x_i), where deg P<m and P≥0 on [0,∞): use partial fractions, and the term at infinity is nonnegative by the limit of (1+t)P/D.

If P=t^e q², the supremum is exactly the indicated quadratic form, since the signs of c_i alternate except at zeros of q; the degree bound gives the sizes. To prove sufficiency, decompose any nonzero dual P, preserving the signs of its residues in each summand. Its leading coefficient is positive; the positive roots are double or of even multiplicity. An irreducible factor (t−a)²+b² splits into a square plus a constant; at all negative nodes both summands are nonnegative and the box supremum distributes exactly. Keep those squares inside q. For each linear factor coming from a negative root r, if r coincides with a node −x_i, cancel in the denominator; the residue at i is zero and a sublist remains. Otherwise interpolate t−r linearly between the two extreme factors of the cell of r in the mesh {−x_m,…,−x_1,0}; if r<−x_m use t+x_m plus the constant −r−x_m. At each node of the sublist the two extreme factors have compatible signs (or one is zero). Hence, after multiplying by the rest of the numerator and dividing by D, compatible signs are preserved coordinatewise. Each term of the decomposition remains dual; cancelling an endpoint shortens the list and using zero or the constant removes that negative factor. Repeat on the pending linear factors. The remaining power of t is reduced by parity, incorporating its even part into q. The final terms are of the declared matrix class, with degree strictly less than the size of their list. The proof covers multiple roots and zero residues. Feasibility of each prefix is recovered by separation and then the previous integer test is used.

The elimination gives purely scalar failure certificates: a sublist, a parity and a real polynomial q of the indicated degree with negative sum would suffice. The criterion still requires all sizes to prove the sign. No general novelty is attributed to the classical Stieltjes cone.

### Resolution in the radius of finite integer certificates

If λ_W(S)≥0 there is c(S)>0, computable from S and l at one real point close to 1/2 only, such that ALL constraints for 2≤n≤N remain feasible with the larger radius S+c(S)/(2N²). It is a bound on what truncation can distinguish, not an extension of the sign. To prove it take a global comparator H_S from the window construction and put G(z)=exp(2S(z−1/2))(H_S(z)−h(z))/2. It is Schur on Re z>1/2. Choose a between 1/2 and 1 so close to the boundary that η=exp(2S(a−1/2))(1+|h(a)|)/2<1; this is possible by continuity and 0<l(1/2)<∞. Thus |G(a)|≤η independently of the comparator. Schwarz–Pick for n≥2, with r=(n−a)/(n+a−1), gives |G(n)|≤(η+r)/(1+ηr). In particular
    1−|G(n)| ≥ (1−η)(2a−1)/[(1+η)(n+a−1)] ≥ c(S)/n,
    c(S)=(1−η)(2a−1)/(1+η).
By 1−c/n≤exp(−c/n) and 2·[c/(2N²)]·(n−1/2)≤c/n, the same values H_S(n) satisfy the narrower error radii. An admissible a is found by bisection towards the boundary or by trying successive 1/2+2^(−j).

In particular, if S_* is the finite global boundary of radii with λ_W≥0 (it includes S_* by continuity), define S_N as the supremum, possibly infinite, of the feasible radii using the integers 2,…,N. Then S_N descends to S_* by the previous equivalence and nesting, but S_N≥S_*+c(S_*)/(2N²). A failure certificate at distance ε from the boundary needs some node larger than √(c(S_*)/(2ε)). This restricts the largest index needed, not the cardinality of a sublist with gaps. For ζ it has not been established that a finite boundary exists. A set of matrices passing for a radius somewhat larger than the last proved one may reflect this intrinsic slack.

### Height of the first negative prefix on the mesh of multiples

For d≥1 consider rates u_j=dj and the first N=M(d) whose exact kernel [(l(di)+l(dj))/(di+dj)] has a negative direction; use infinity if no such N exists. If the critical radius of the full form S_* is finite, then
    lim_{d→∞} log M(d)/d = S_*.
If there is global positivity, all M(d) are infinite. The law for a finite boundary is a corollary of the existing bridge, not another estimate of S_*.

Indeed N=⌊exp(sd)⌋ gives Σ_{j≤N}1/(dj)→s and the smallest pole is d. By the first lines of this memo the minimum in physical norm converges to λ_W(s). For s<S_* the floor is strictly positive; for s>S_* it is strictly negative. The strict monotonicity also needed for the full domain without primitive restrictions is seen by the translation argument of 212 BUILD_083 (136)–(137): the form on a finite window has compact resolvent (archimedean symbol growing to infinity, bounded remainder on the window), and if two bottoms were equal, all small translations of one minimizer of the smaller window would be minimizers in the larger one. They are linearly independent for any finite number of distinct shifts by their left support endpoints, a contradiction. Continuity by 077. The nesting by sublists shows that M(d) lies between the prefixes at s=S_*−ε and s=S_*+ε eventually, for all small ε>0. No rate of convergence is claimed nor is a finite boundary for ζ assumed to exist. The same comparison works for the first smallest physical eigenvalue below any level crossed by λ_W.

The mesh moreover introduces an explicit conditioning cost in the physical norm. The Gram matrix of the normalized exponentials is C_ij=2√(ij)/(i+j), independent of d. Its inverse has last diagonal entry p_N², p_N=∏_{j<N}(N+j)/(N−j)=binom(2N−1,N). Hence κ₂(C)≥binom(2N−1,N)², since λ_max(C)≥1. At fixed window scale s, log κ₂(C)≥(log 16−o(1))exp(sd). This concerns the passage between power coordinates and the physical norm; it is not a universal lower bound for algorithms using another basis. The exact mesh, unlike the relaxed boxes of the previous entry, serves to characterize the first failure, but sweeping prefixes of manageable size at large step does not distinguish a high critical radius from global positivity.

### Hypothetical first contact: a single exponential tail detects the negative sign

Direct antecedent 196: it already constructs the window space plus a tail and identifies its bottom, with a Schur criterion if the window has a positive floor. Here the singular case is studied. Assume the critical radius S_* of the full bottom is finite and put L=2S_*. There is a single real minimizer φ≠0 on [0,L] such that for every rate v>1/2 except a discrete set, the form on the plane spanned by φ and h_v(t)=1_{t>L}exp(−v(t−L)) is indefinite. The existence of a finite contact is not claimed.

Indeed the bottom is zero by continuity and is attained by compactness. The real form, invariant under reflection, allows choosing φ with fixed parity with respect to L/2. Let b(v)=W(φ,h_v), real polarization. It is analytic in v>1/2: the complexified tail depends holomorphically in H^s, 0<s<1/2, by its explicit Fourier transform exp(−iτL)/(v+iτ), and in L² with weight exp(2ηt) locally for 1/2<η<Re v. These norms control the form with one fixed input (for comb and polar, as in 196). Hence it suffices to prove that b is not identically zero.

If it vanished identically, the crossing with φ would vanish for every restriction of a compactly supported smooth test to [L,∞), including the possible jump at L. In the coordinate y=t−L≥0, write that restriction as exp(−2y)p(exp(−y)), with p of class C¹ on [0,1] and zero near 0 before approximating. Approximate p in C¹ by polynomials (approximate its derivative and integrate). One gets convergence in weighted L² with η=1 and in H^s after extension by zero: the error on the half-line tends to zero in H¹ and the jump is controlled by the boundedness of the cutoff in H^s. Each approximant is a sum of the permitted tails. By reflection the crossing with the left piece of any test also vanishes. The interior piece of the test, even with jumps, belongs to the window domain (approximation in H^s with interior support, s<1/2); by semidefiniteness and W(φ)=0 its crossing is zero. Thus W(φ,f)=0 for every compactly supported smooth test on the line.

By translation invariance, in one strictly larger window infinitely many distinct small translations of φ belong to the weak kernel of the operator, by density of the tests in the domain. They are linearly independent by their essential left endpoints, against the finite dimension of the kernel by compact resolvent. The contradiction holds even if the larger window already has negative directions. For b(v)≠0 the matrix of the plane has first diagonal entry zero and determinant −|b(v)|²<0. By 196, for each v so chosen negativity is also detected eventually with a fixed rate and fast blocks whose reciprocal mass tends precisely to S_*. A window of strictly larger mass is not needed for that hybrid listing. The threshold in dimension and the possible exceptional rates are not located.

### Comparator determined by a minimizer at contact: quotient formula

Assuming the previous finite first contact, let φ be a real minimizer of norm one supported on [0,L], L=2S_*. Among the real-symmetric comparators g of the delay criterion there is exactly one. Its meromorphic continuation is odd. It is obtained explicitly as
    g(z)=Lap(K)(z)/Φ(z),    Φ(z)=∫_0^L exp(−zt)φ(t)dt.
The compact distribution K is determined by gluing k_l*φ on t<L with −k_l^* *φ on t>0; here superscript * denotes reflection and conjugation of the causal kernel and the asterisk between factors is convolution. In particular every root of Φ off the imaginary axis cancels in the quotient, with its multiplicity. At an imaginary root of multiplicity m the numerator has order ≥m−1 and, if a pole remains, its residue is real strictly positive. The number of possible poles with |Im z|≤R is O_φ,L(1+R), counting the candidates with multiplicity.

Proof. The comparator exists by 3667 and the exact delay by the integers entry. Let T_g=k_g+k_g^*. For every compactly supported smooth test ψ, ⟨T_g*φ,ψ⟩=0: approximate φ in the form kernel of its window by smooth φ_j with interior support. Their g-energy coincides with W(φ_j)→0; Cauchy–Schwarz for the positive global form of g kills the limit of the crossing with ψ. By L² convergence with common compact support one also converges in distributional pairing towards T_g*φ. Hence K=k_g*φ=−k_g^* *φ. The two sides are supported respectively on [0,∞) and (−∞,L], so K is supported on [0,L]. By the delay of k_g−k_l and of its reflection, the two expressions in terms of l hold precisely on the indicated open sets, whose union includes the endpoints. This proves uniqueness without choosing values at the gluing points.

The bilateral transform of K coincides on the right with g(z)Φ(z) and on the left with −g(−z)Φ(z), using real symmetry. The quotient of entire functions gives the continuation and oddness by uniqueness. There are no poles in the open half-planes by analyticity and oddness. On the boundary, nonnegativity of the real part in the right half-disc forces every pole to be simple with positive residue: a principal term of order ≥2 takes real parts of both signs as the argument varies over an interval of length π; at order one the condition forces argument zero of the residue. Finally |Φ(z)|≤√L exp(L|z|); Jensen on discs with fixed centre where Φ does not vanish bounds the count of its zeros by O(1+R). The KEP theory of paper 46 already treats determination of extensions; the formula here uses the null datum and both arithmetic convolutions to recover the unique comparator and express the necessary cancellations. It has not been proved that these cancellations are impossible for a minimizer.

Size consequence: at arbitrarily large heights the residues of the critical comparator must grow at least like a constant times the logarithm of the height. Indeed the positive Herglotz measure is atomic at the poles: on the remaining intervals g is analytic and purely imaginary on the axis by oddness and real symmetry (Poisson inversion). On the ray v>0 write g(v)=∫ v/(v²+t²)dμ(t) with μ on [0,∞), grouping symmetric masses; the slope is zero by g(v)~½log v. Each positive mass is twice the residue except at zero. Since the kernel is ≥1/(2v) for t≤v, μ([0,v])≤C v log(2+v). For fixed large A, the part t<v/A contributes ≤C log(2+v)/A, and the part t>Av contributes O((log(2+v)+log A)/A) by dyadic summation. Choose A sufficiently large and then v large: ≫log v remains on [v/A,Av]. There the kernel is ≤1/v, so there is mass ≫v log v, distributed over O_{A,φ,L}(v) poles. Some one has residue ≫_{A,φ,L}log v. These are residues of the comparator, not multiplicities of zeros of ζ.

### At contact, typical density, residues and separation of the comparator

Under the hypotheses of 3732, enumerate the positive poles of the comparator by heights τ_j and call r_j their residues. One obtains
    #{j: τ_j≤R} ~ LR/(2π),
    Lr_j/log τ_j → 1 in natural density of indices,
    τ_{j+1}−τ_j → 2π/L in natural density of indices.
Here convergence in density allows a proportion tending to zero of exceptions of any size. They are auxiliary poles, not zeros of ζ.

For f smooth with support interior to the window, modulate by exp(iRt). The positive representation of 3732 gives exactly Σ_τ r_τ |fhat(τ−R)|², over both orientations and the possible zero. The normalization is 2Re g in the Plancherel integral dτ/(2π), with Re g→πΣ r_τ δ_τ. This sum equals ||f||² log R+O_f(1) for R≥2: the archimedean symbol is log(1+|τ|)+O(1), the spectrum of f decays rapidly and comb and polar are bounded on the window. Take an f with nonzero transform near zero and cover a unit interval by a fixed number of translations: the mass on [t,t+1] is O(log(2+|t|)). Integrate the identity in R from 0 to T. Replacing the convolution of 1_[0,T] with |fhat|² by 2π||f||² 1_[0,T] costs O_f(log(2+T)) when integrating against the atoms: the pointwise error is O_f((1+|τ|)^−3+(1+|τ−T|)^−3) by the Schwartz tails. One gets Σ_{0<τ≤T} r_τ ~ T log T/(2π).

At R=τ_j keep only that atom. Approximating the indicator of [0,L] in L² by smooth interior functions (also in L¹), one obtains limsup r_j/log τ_j≤1/L, since |fhat(0)|²/||f||²→L. The total mass forces n_+(R)≥(L/(2π)−o(1))R. On the other hand, in the complex frequency coordinate the transform of the centred minimizer satisfies |Φ_c(w)|≤√L exp((L/2)|Im w|). If it has a zero at the origin divide by its monomial. Jensen gives for the count n_Φ of all zeros with multiplicity ∫_1^R n_Φ(t)dt/t ≤ LR/π+O(log(2+R)). The symmetry and the poles give n_Φ(t)≥2n_+(t)−O(1)≥(L/π−o(1))t. Consequently n_Φ(R)=(L/π+o(1))R: if it exceeded (L/π+ε)R along a subsequence, monotonicity would keep an excess ≥εR/2 above the line on [R,(1+c_ε)R], contradicting the integral bound and its previous floor. The first formula is proved, and up to o(R) all candidate zeros of the minimizer up to R are simple poles in the counting sense (the excess multiplicities also sum to o(R)).

With the asymptotic mass and the uniform ceiling, a positive proportion of residues ≤(1−ε)log τ_j/L would contradict the total mass (first discard τ_j<δR and take δ small). Thus the second formula is obtained. To see the third, consider consecutive pairs whose normalized residues converge to 1 and whose separation has a finite limit b. In the modulated identity at R=τ_j keep the two poles and pass to the limit: |fhat(0)|²+|fhat(b)|²≤L||f||². Approximate the indicator again. One deduces ∫_0^L exp(−ibt)dt=0; hence b is a nonzero multiple of 2π/L. By compactness and the convergence in density of the residues, for each ε>0 only o(J) of the first J gaps can be <2π/L−ε. Their average tends to 2π/L by the first formula and telescoping. The positive gaps below the mean have mean deficit tending to zero; hence the mean excess also tends to zero. This proves even absolute mean convergence of the separations to the indicated value. Neither uniform convergence of the gaps nor a fixed phase for τ_j−2πj/L is obtained.

### Signal of each prime power in the deviations of the critical comparator

Under the same contact hypothesis, for each fixed h with 0<h<L,
    (1/T) Σ_{T<τ_j≤2T} r_j exp(ihτ_j) → −Λ(n)/(2π√n) if h=log n, and to zero otherwise.
Here n≥2 is an integer and Λ is nonzero only at prime powers. It is a Landau-type identity for the auxiliary atoms deduced from the local data; it does not presuppose that they coincide with the ordinates of ζ.

Take f real smooth with interior support in (0,L) with C_f(h)=∫ f(t+h)f(t)dt>0, possible since h<L. In the previous modulated proof now integrate against exp(ihR) over T<R<2T. The atomic side is 2π C_f(h)Σ_{T<τ≤2T}r_τ exp(ihτ)+O_f(log(2+T)), by Fourier of |fhat|² and the same Schwartz boundary error against unit masses O(log(2+|t|)). The archimedean one is ||f||² log(R/(2π))+o(1) by Stirling and rapid decay, so its oscillating integral is o(T) by parts. The polar one is o(1) before integrating, by Riemann–Lebesgue. The comb is exactly the finite sum of −2Λ(m)C_f(log m) cos(R log m)/√m over log m<L. After dividing by T only the resonant term survives. This also fixes the sign and the constant.

In particular, put α=2π/L, h=log n<L with Λ(n)>0 and w_j=log τ_j/L. On each band I=(T,2T] the following first-order requirement complements the relative saturation of the previous entry:
    liminf_{T→∞} ( Σ_{τ_j∈I}|r_j−w_j| + [h log(2T)/(L |1−exp(ihα)|)] Σ_{τ_j,τ_{j+1}∈I}|τ_{j+1}−τ_j−α| )/T ≥ Λ(n)/(2π√n).
Indeed |1−exp(ihα)|>0 because 0<h<L. To bound Σw_j exp(ihτ_j), multiply by 1−exp(ihα) and subtract the sum shifted by one index. The endpoints and the total variation of the monotone weight cost O_L(log T), and each difference of interior phases has modulus ≤h|τ_{j+1}−τ_j−α|. Add the difference of real weights r_j−w_j and use the resonant limit. In particular mean absolute residue error o(1) and mean absolute gap error o(1/log T) cannot hold simultaneously on high bands. The previous theorems only give o(log T) and o(1), respectively, so there is no contradiction. This condition distinguishes the prime-power comb from the main archimedean term.

### Complementary frequencies: the residues alone cannot produce the comb

Under the same contact, α=2π/L. There are constants c_L,C_L>0 such that for every I=(A,B]⊂[T,2T], T sufficiently large,
    Σ_{τ_j,τ_{j+1}∈I} min(2,L|τ_{j+1}−τ_j−α|) ≥ c_L (B−A)/log T − C_L.
In particular the truncated mean deviation of the gaps over the whole band is ≳_L1/log T, regardless of the fluctuations of the residues. The previous conclusion allowed the residues to pay the whole cost.

Uniformity detail. For fixed h in (0,L), denote by a_h the coefficient of the previous entry. Uniformly in both endpoints of I,
    Σ_{τ∈I} r_τ exp(ihτ)=a_h (B−A)+O_{f,h,L}(log T).
In the modulation proof, the cost of the two spectral endpoints is O(log T) even on short intervals. The archimedean term of the modulated proof is ||f||² log(R/(2π))+O_f(1/R): on |τ−R|≤R/2 use Stirling and the first derivative of log, and outside the Schwartz tails. The main term integrated against exp(ihR) costs O_h(log T) by parts; the integrated remainder costs O_f(1). The polar term decays rapidly by smoothness and the comb has only a fixed number of distinct frequencies, with the nonresonant ones having bounded integral. This proves the required uniformity.

Take h=log 2 and k=L−h. Then |a_h|>|a_k|, even if k also resonates: L≥2·2.7695 gives exp(k)>120, and log(x)/√x decreases on x≥120 with log(120)/√120<log(2)/√2. On I subtract from the discrete measure of masses r_j exp(−ikτ_j) the constant density conj(a_k)dt. Its primitive from A is bounded by O_L(log T) on all of I by the previous paragraph. Multiply by a step function U of modulus one which at each atom equals exp(iLτ_j), constant between successive atoms and extended by constants to the endpoints. Each jump can be placed at the atom-free midpoint. The total variation is ≤Σ min(2,L|τ_{j+1}−τ_j−α|), since exp(iLα)=1. If there are no atoms any unit constant works. The integral of U against the residual is O_L(log T)(1+Var U) by parts. Against the diffuse part it costs at most |a_k|(B−A). Against the discrete measure it gives exactly the signal at frequency h, of modulus ≥|a_h|(B−A)−O_L(log T). Subtracting both bounds and using the strict difference of moduli proves the result. In particular there cannot be a stretch of exact lattice bounded by poles and contained in [T,2T] of length greater than C'_L log T. It remains compatible with mean convergence of the gaps to α.

### Sufficiency falsifier for Landau signals at any fixed logarithmic order

Fix L and any fixed integer m≥1. There are artificial positions and positive masses, with x_j=2πj/L, τ_j=x_j+O(1/log x_j), r_j=(log x_j+O(1))/L, which simultaneously satisfy for each fixed h in (0,L) the prime coefficients a_h of 3758. On any I=(A,B]⊂[T,2T] their error with respect to a_h(B−A) is O_{h,L,m}(log T+(B−A)/(log T)^m). Their positions, reflected to negative heights, are moreover zeros of the transform of a nonzero real L² datum with support of length L. Neither the uniform O(log T) error of the exact law nor that the datum has zero energy for W is claimed.

Construction. Let b=1/log x_j. Put τ_j=x_j+Σ_{s=1}^m b^s U_{s,j}, Lr_j=b^(−1)+Σ_{s=1}^m b^(s−1)V_{s,j}, with U_s,V_s finite real trigonometric polynomials in the index j. Frequencies are considered modulo L on this mesh. Denote by [P]_h the coefficient of exp(−ihx_j), that is the mean of P_j exp(ihx_j). At first order one must choose [V_1]_h+ih[U_1]_h=A_h=2π a_h. The conjugate equation for k=L−h uses the same coefficients with −ik. Hence
    [U_1]_h=(A_h−conj(A_k))/(iL),   [V_1]_h=(k A_h+h conj(A_k))/L.
Complete by conjugation. At h=L/2 this recipe gives the two unique real coefficients; the zero class can be set to zero because h=0,L is not required. There are only finitely many prescribed nonzero frequencies and their complementary ones.

By induction, in the expansion of Lr_j exp(ih(τ_j−x_j)), the coefficient of b^(s−1) is V_{s,j}+ihU_{s,j}+P_{s,j}(h), where P_s depends only on the previous orders. Its frequency support is contained in a finite list independent of h by finite products. For s≥2 use the same recipe with A_h=−[P_s(h)]_h and the corresponding datum at k. Thus the resonant frequency is cancelled at each additional order. For fixed h, the mean-free terms of each order have bounded partial sums before weighting by b^(s−1), by the geometric series and finiteness of frequencies. Abel also controls the initial term log x_j exp(ihx_j) by O_h(log T). The Taylor remainder is O_{h,L,m}(b^m) per node. The number of lattice points in I is (B−A)L/(2π)+O(1); the change at the endpoints from shifting the nodes costs O(log T). This proves the claimed error. The model depends on m and there is no control of the constants as m grows.

For the support statement, keep only the perturbations from a sufficiently large index on, put the earlier nodes on the lattice, extend by symmetry and keep τ_0=0 as an auxiliary node. The initial masses can be taken positive. On the centred interval of length L, synthesis by perturbed exponentials differs from the normalized Fourier basis in operator norm by at most exp(L sup|τ_j−x_j|/2)−1: expand exp(it(τ_j−x_j)) and apply Parseval to each power before multiplying by t^s. Choosing the cutoff large the norm is <1 and the synthesis is invertible. The family omitting j=0 has nonzero orthogonal complement; by symmetry a real datum can be chosen. Its transform vanishes at all required nodes. This construction prevents deducing a contradiction from the averaged prime terms, even adding error rates of any fixed logarithmic order and the mere condition of zeros of a compact transform. The exact local energy pairing of the comparator remains unreproduced.

### Exact divisor and kernel dimension at first contact

Let V be the complex space of transforms of the null vectors in the critical window [0,L], and D its dimension (finite and positive). Let Λ be the set of POLES of the comparator in the Laplace variable, including the origin if it is a pole. There is Φ₀, unique up to a scalar, with roots exactly Λ, all simple, and
    V = { Φ₀(z) P(z) : P complex polynomial of degree ≤D−1 }.
In particular the exceptions to the simple divisor of poles are at most D−1 in the WHOLE plane for each null vector, counting multiplicities. This strengthens the previous o(R) and allows choosing a minimizer without exceptions.

Proof. By the atomic representation of the comparator (without slope by its real asymptotics), every vector of the domain in [0,L] has energy equal to the weighted sum of the squares of its evaluations on Λ. To extend from smooth tests, approximate in physical form norm: their evaluations are Cauchy in ℓ² of the residues by the local equality and converge pointwise by L² on fixed support. Thus on this domain nullity is equivalent to vanishing of all evaluations.

If Φ(a)=0, Φ(z)/(z−a) is the transform of the causal solution of (∂_t−a)ψ=φ, that is ψ(t)=∫₀ᵗ exp(a(t−s))φ(s)ds for t≥0. It is zero after L by Φ(a)=0, and ψ∈H¹ with support in the same window, by the equation and continuity at the endpoints. If the zero is surplus (at least one is kept at every point of Λ), the division gives another null vector. For each point a and each order j up to its surplus multiplicity, Φ/(z−a)^j and Φ itself are linearly independent when all those functions are considered together: divide by Φ and use uniqueness of partial fractions. This holds for any finite selection, so the total number of surplus orders is ≤D−1. Dividing successively by all of them produces Φ₀ with the indicated divisor.

To avoid assumptions on the growth of a quotient of entire functions, fix w outside Λ and define TΨ=(Ψ−Ψ(w)Φ₀/Φ₀(w))/(z−w). It is an endomorphism of V by the previous division. With ε_z evaluation at z, one has ε_z[I−(z−w)T]=Φ₀(z) ε_w/Φ₀(w). The bracketed matrix is invertible at w and its inverse is rational in z; hence Ψ/Φ₀ is rational for all Ψ in V. All its poles would be removable because Φ₀ has only the simple zeros required of Ψ. It is thus a polynomial, of degree at most D−1 by the count of surplus orders. The dimensions of both spaces are D and the inclusion gives equality. In particular another generator with minimal divisor differs by a constant. The property admits models of spaces of entire functions; no contradiction for the arithmetic divisor follows without controlling the exact energy identity.

### Multiplicity of the contact and simultaneous detection with one-sided tails

If the first full contact has a kernel of dimension D, any strict enlargement of the window has at least D negative directions, and every sufficiently small enlargement has exactly D. Moreover, keeping the original critical window, D exponential tails added only on the right suffice to produce D negative directions. The rates can be chosen in any open interval contained in (1/2,∞); the valid D-tuples form an open dense subset of that interval raised to D.

First part: for any fixed k the ordered eigenvalues of the full window operator decrease strictly with its length. Let E be the space of the first k eigenvectors in the smaller window and λ its largest eigenvalue. If the k-th eigenvalue in the larger one were the same, there would be fewer than k strictly lower eigenvalues. For every admissible small translation of E one can choose a nonzero vector orthogonal to the strictly lower modes; its quotient is both ≥λ and ≤λ, so it belongs to the eigenspace of λ in the larger window. This is impossible: in any finite space of compactly supported functions the essential left support endpoints of its nonzero elements form a finite set (distinct values give linearly independent functions). Choose a translation avoiding the finitely many differences between those endpoints for E and the larger eigenspace. Apply to k=D at contact. For local exactness, the (D+1)-th positive eigenvalue of the contact is right-continuous: if on decreasing windows there were D+1 orthonormal vectors with nonpositive energy on their whole span, their shifted archimedean norms would be uniformly bounded by boundedness of the remainder on a fixed window. Control of the Fourier tail by the growing symbol and the common compact support give strongly convergent subsequences in L²; the limit support lies in the critical window. By semicontinuity of the archimedean term and L² continuity of the remainder, the limits would give D+1 orthonormal null vectors, absurd. This compactness argument directly proves the required sign statement; continuity of an arbitrary level is obtained likewise with a fixed ceiling on its quotient.

For the second part, the map φ↦(v↦W(φ,h_v)) is injective even without choosing parity. If all crossings of φ vanish, the exponential density proved in 3722 implies that T_l*φ vanishes on the open set (L,∞), where T_l=k_l+k_l^*. There k_l^* *φ is already zero by support, hence k_l*φ has compact support in [0,L]. Its entire transform coincides with l(z)Φ(z) on Re z>1/2. By meromorphic uniqueness, Φ must vanish at all poles of l, including ≫R log R distinct points up to height R by the simple zeros on the line of Conrey and the Riemann–von Mangoldt count (Conrey, J. reine angew. Math. 399, 1989, pp. 1–26, https://aimath.org/~kaur/publications/24.pdf). Jensen for a nonzero compact transform allows only O_φ(R) zeros. Hence φ=0.

The D real-analytic crossing functions for a real basis of the kernel are linearly independent on any open interval of rates. The evaluations therefore span the dual of dimension D, and their determinant for D rates is analytic and not identically zero. For any nonsingular tuple the matrix restricted to the kernel plus those tails has blocks [[0,B],[B*,C]] with B invertible. By congruence it has inertia (D,D), independently of C. Fewer than D tails cannot produce D negatives in a space starting from a semidefinite window, by codimension. No real contact for ζ is deduced and D is not determined.

### Crossing identity: classification of each rate and detection with one confluent rate

Let E=l−g for a real-positive comparator with delay L in k_E. For real data f on [0,L] with transform F and right tails h_v of 3722 one has
    (W_l−W_g)(f,h_v)=exp(vL)E(v)F(v),
    (W_l−W_g)(h_v,h_w)=[E(v)+E(w)]/(v+w).
The complex crossings follow by sesquilinearity. For the first identity it suffices to start with smooth f with interior support. The distribution k_E*f starts at L+inf supp(f)>L and the reflected k_E^* *f ends at sup supp(f)−L<0. Pairing with a tail smoothed near L preserves exactly the pairing of the first with exp(−v(t−L)) over its whole support, and kills the second. The result is its Laplace transform at v times exp(vL). One can cut at infinity because the causal kernels have controlled distributional growth on each line Re z>1/2 and v>1/2. Pass to the jump of the tail by approximation: in W_l, H^s, s<1/2, and weight exp(ηt), η<v with η>1/2, suffice; in W_g its spectral representation is used, pointwise convergence of the transforms and the uniform bound C/(1+|τ|) by uniform total variation of the smooth cutoffs. This bound is square integrable for the Herglotz measure. For general f approximate in the window form kernel; the pairing with the tail in W_l is continuous (196), and in W_g by Cauchy–Schwarz and equality of energies on the window. The second identity is the Pick identity of exponentials by translation (for g also by integration against its measure). It is applied here to the comparator of 3732, whose slope is zero.

At the contact S_*, g is unique. The form on the full window PLUS h_v is positive semidefinite IF AND ONLY IF E(v)=0. Indeed for E(v)=0 the form on the whole hybrid coincides with that of g; if E(v)≠0 the crossing with the minimal generator of 3794 is nonzero, since Φ₀(v)≠0. In general for a finite set of distinct rates, the hybrid is PSD exactly when ALL of them are zeros of E. In the basis Φ₀(z)z^k, 0≤k<D, the crossings with h_{v_i} are v_i^k exp(v_i L)E(v_i)Φ₀(v_i). Exceptional rates give zero columns; any r≤D distinct nonexceptional rates give rank r by Vandermonde. In the hybrid with exactly r nonexceptional rates (plus any set of exceptional ones), the negative index is exactly r if r≤D: the upper bound follows from semidefiniteness of the space with only exceptional rates and the lower one from the crossed submatrix of rank r.

Now fix ONE rate v with E(v)≠0. Adding the D functions (t−L)^j h_v(t), j=0,…,D−1, produces D negative directions. Their crossing columns are the derivatives (−∂_v)^j of the previous evaluation. Multiplying a polynomial of degree <D by the nonzero germ exp(vL)E(v)Φ₀(v) gives an isomorphism on jets of order D−1; the confluent jets thus have rank D. Differentiation is valid in the tail norms of 3722 and, for g, in its atomic representation. At an exceptional rate of vanishing order b it suffices to add the tails with j=b,…,b+D−1 to obtain the same rank, by the Leibniz rule. E is not identically zero under finite contact (by 3806). Hence there is no rate v>1/2 blind to all confluent orders. The set of real zeros of E for a hypothetical contact is not known.

### Prime rates suffice: window test on every submesh of divergent harmonic mass

Let J⊂{2,3,…} with Σ_{n∈J}1/n=∞. In the criteria of 3667–3691, both Pick feasibility with boxes and the two matrices of alternating endpoints per sublist, it suffices to use ONLY the nodes of J. In particular one can use only the primes, for any fixed S, with the same tolerances 2exp(−2S(n−1/2)). The key is that a bounded holomorphic error cannot exhibit at those nodes an exponential delay larger than the true one. Uniqueness by exact Blaschke zeros already appears in 212-001-L; here small nonzero values are involved.

Lemma. For f Schur and not identically zero on Re z>0, there is a≥0 with |f(z)|≤exp(−a Re z), and, for x_n=n−1/2, for all ε>0,
    Σ_{n: |f(x_n)|≤exp(−(a+ε)x_n)} 1/n < ∞.
Extract the Blaschke product B of the zeros b and write f=Bq, q Schur without zeros. By the representation of the positive harmonic function −log|q| (including the constant case), −log|q(x)|/x→a: the term additional to the mass at infinity is an integral of (x²+t²)^−1 against a measure with integrable weight (1+t²)^−1 and tends to zero by domination. The representation also gives −log|q(z)|≥a Re z.

For B, divide by x the sum of (1/2)log(1+4x Re b/|x−b|²). In the distant terms |x−b|≥x/2 one has |b|≤3|x−b| and x≥1, so each summand divided by x is dominated by C Re b/(1+|b|²), summable. For fixed b it tends to zero. Discard the nodes at distance <1/4 from some zero: their sum of 1/n is finite by the same condition, since each zero counts at most one node and weighs ≍1/n there. At the remaining nodes close to b, |x−b|<x/2 implies x≍Re b=:R and |Im b|≲R. For each b the sum of its contributions NOT divided by x at these nodes is O(R): the term is ≤log(CR/max(1/4,|x−R|)), and in each distance strip of length one there are O(1) nodes; sum the logarithm by an integral. Here R is bounded below on the relevant strips. After weighting by 1/n², the cost is O(1/R)=O(Re b/(1+|b|²)). By Tonelli and Markov's inequality, the n for which the near contribution exceeds εx have finite sum of reciprocals. This proves the lemma. The exclusion scale is necessary for an abstract lemma: a Blaschke product with zeros on a list of finite mass can vanish there without positive delay (the previous argument gives a=0 for a pure product).

Now, by finite Pick and Montel, the boxes on J produce a global Schur H. Apply the lemma to f(z)=[H(z+1/2)−h(z+1/2)]/2. If f≡0 the full bound already holds. Otherwise, the boxes on J force a≥2S; otherwise J would lie in an exceptional set of finite mass. Thus the bound is recovered on the WHOLE shifted half-plane and the fixed-window converse concludes. Truncating J from below does not affect the result.

In particular, at the first finite contact, for its unique comparator the constant a is exactly L=2S_*: if a>L the same H would certify a strictly larger window. E=l−g and the Cayley difference differ on the ray by a factor of order (log n)². Consequently for each ε>0 the list of n≥2 with |E(n)|≤exp(−(L+ε)n) has finite sum of reciprocals, including exact zeros. This statement also controls almost exceptional tails, not the size of the smallest physical eigenvalue of the hybrid.

### Physical margin and detection before contact with a single fast tail

If there is a finite first contact L=2S_*, for EACH ε>0, outside a set of integer rates n of finite reciprocal sum, and for n sufficiently large, the window of length L−exp(−εn) plus a single tail of rate n at its new edge has a unit vector of energy ≤−exp(−εn). The window alone has strictly positive floor by monotonicity. This advance in length is conditional, depends on n and does not give the value of L. The statement does not allow fixing a macroscopic advance when n tends to infinity.

First, for the unit minimal generator, log|Φ₀(v)|=o(v) on the real ray v→∞. Indeed Φ₀ can be taken real on the ray (uniqueness and conjugation) and its time datum has fixed parity around the centre (uniqueness and reflection). The centred entire function exp(Lz/2)Φ₀(z) has order ≤1 and its only zeros are the simple poles ±iτ, with the possible simple zero at the origin. By paired Hadamard and parity it is C z^m ∏_{τ>0}(1+z²/τ²), m∈{0,1}; parity eliminates the residual linear exponential. The sum of logarithms of the product at v, divided by v, converges to L/2. By parts it is equivalent to integrating 2v n_+(t)/[t(t²+v²)]dt; use n_+(t)/t→L/(2π), its global boundedness (there is no accumulation at zero) and t=vy. The linear term cancels on decentring.

Now use u_n=√(2n)h_n, unit and orthogonal in physical norm to φ₀. Its crossing B_n with φ₀ equals √(2n)exp(Ln)E(n)Φ₀(n). For each η>0, |B_n|≥exp(−ηn) except on a set with finite Σ1/n, by 3827 applied with a smaller exponent, and the estimate of Φ₀. The physical matrix of the plane has diagonal entries 0 and 2l(n)=O(log n). For each η'>0, the modulus of its negative eigenvalue is ≥exp(−η'n) with the same class of exceptions (choose η sufficiently small): one uses monotonicity in |B_n| of [√(4l(n)²+4|B_n|²)−2l(n)]/2, rationalizing at the lower threshold.

For the passage to length L−δ cut φ₀ on the right and translate u_n to that edge. The extension by zero of φ₀ has bounded H^(1/4) by 077. The lost piece has L²=O(δ^(1/4)) by Sobolev in L⁴ and H^(1/4) bounded by uniform continuity of the cutoffs in that space. By interpolation its H^(1/8) is O(δ^(1/8)); its L² norm with weight exp(t) also satisfies the required error floor by fixed support. For the tail, ||u_n||_{H^(1/4)}=O(n^(1/4)) by explicit Fourier. Its change in H^(1/8) is O(n^(1/4)δ^(1/8)) by the translation multiplier. In L² with weight exp(t) the same translation costs O_L(√(nδ)+δ) for nδ≤1, by separating the small jump interval and the common tail. The full bilinear form is continuous in the sum of the H^(1/8) norms and the weighted L² on the half-line, by the logarithmic symbol and the weighted bounds for comb and polar. Consequently each entry changes by O_L(poly(n)δ^(1/8)); renormalizing the cut of φ₀ introduces the same type of error, and the new basis remains orthogonal. Take δ=exp(−εn) and for example η'=ε/16. For n large the perturbation is o(exp(−η'n)), even giving the margin stated. It is a result on the hybrid with uncut tail; it is not negativity of the shorter window.

### Bottom comparator on every window and linear term of its mass

For EVERY S>0, without presupposing contact with zero, put b=λ_W(S), L=2S and centre the form Q=W−b||·||². The centred form has its first contact exactly at S by strict monotonicity, compactness and attainment of the minimum. Its determined comparator g_b is atomic (in its Herglotz measure) with the residues and divisor described before. In particular on each window with an already certified floor the whole prime signal at frequencies 0<h<L of the critical model is realized EXACTLY. What changes in the modulation with respect to W is a constant at frequency zero.

Justification of the transfer: in the Pick coordinates l_b=l−b/2, since the physical Gram matrix is 1/(u+v). To construct the comparator choose σ_b>1/2 sufficiently large: Re l(z)>b/2 uniformly on Re z≥σ_b by uniform Stirling in the right half-plane and by control of the series of ζ'/ζ there (Re l(z)=½log(|z|/(2π))+O(1) in that range). In the moving-block bridge the minima shift exactly by b. Interpolate as in 3667 with a scalar correction tending to zero and apply Schwarz on Re z>σ_b: the majorant converges to 2exp(−L(Re z−σ_b)). This change of prefactor does not affect the delay. The local equality for Q, the null vector and the two convolutions of 3732 give existence, uniqueness and atomicity, now without condition on the sign of b. The modulations at nonzero frequency eliminate the constant shift when taking their mean.

For the positive poles of this comparator and their residues in the individual orientation one has
    Σ_{0<τ≤T} r_τ = T/(2π)·[log(T/(2π))−1−b] + O_S(log(2+T)).
Fix a real smooth test of norm one inside the window. Its modulation at R has archimedean term log(R/(2π))+O_f(1/R), rapidly decaying polar term and a finite number of terms cos(R log n) without zero frequency. In Q there is additionally −b. Integrate from 2 to T: the comb contributes O_{S,f}(1), the archimedean error O_f(log T) and the dimensional term is −bT+O(1). The same smoothing argument of 3744 and the local bound O(log(2+|τ|)) for the mass allow replacing the atomic integral by 2πΣ_{0<τ≤T}r_τ+O_{S,f}(log(2+T)), endpoints included. Thus the sign is equivalent, for each S, to the limit of [2πΣr_τ−T(log(T/(2π))−1)]/T being ≤0. The identity alone does not estimate that limit because g_b was constructed by centring with b itself.

Identification obstruction: replacing W by W+c||·||², its bottom becomes b+c and its centred form, comparator, poles and residues remain exactly the same. Knowing only the pole pattern of the centred comparator and the signals at h≠0 without fixing the archimedean constant cannot decide the absolute sign. For W of paper 46 that constant is fixed by digamma: the quantitative question is a mass comparison at order T, not at order T log T. This does not modify any datum of the paper.

### Lower certificates by periodic lattices, with quadratic loss

Let L=2S and P>3L. Define β_P as the supremum of the levels b such that the energy W−b||·||² on all smooth interior tests of [0,L] admits a formula Σ_{k∈Z} a_k |fhat(2πk/P)|² with a_k≥0. This specification of the problem uses only the known form and the prescribed lattice. Then
    λ_W(S)−C_L/P² ≤ β_P ≤ λ_W(S),
with C_L depending only on the known LOCAL kernel. The supremum is attained. If P/L is not an integer the second inequality is strict. For windows with positive floor there are therefore exact positive extensions of W on every sufficiently fine lattice (to pass from positive b to zero add the Parseval quadrature on the period). The mere existence proved by comparison does not provide their concrete weights.

Proof. Fix ψ real smooth, supported in (−1/6,1/6), ||ψ||₂=1. Let η be its autocorrelation, supported in (−1/3,1/3), η(0)=1, and 0≤1−η(s)=||ψ−ψ(·+s)||²/2≤s²||ψ'||²/2. Write T for the hermitized kernel of W in the difference variable with the normalization where I has kernel δ₀. On 0<|t|<L, t²T is a finite measure: the archimedean term away from zero has density O_L(1/|t|), the comb consists of finitely many atoms and the polar term has smooth density. The local archimedean term is interpreted by subtracting the test function at zero in the Lévy formula (077); multiplying by 1−η(t/P) leaves no additional singular distribution. Thus C_L=(||ψ'||²/2)∫_{0<|t|<L} t² d|T|(t) works, with the variation computed away from zero.

Take the positive extension at level λ of 3851. Multiply its kernel by η(t/P) and periodize with period P. The Fourier coefficients are nonnegative: they amount, with a positive normalization factor, to sampling the convolution of the positive spectral measure with P|ψhat(P·)|². On |t|<L there are no translated copies and the resulting kernel is η(t/P)(T−λδ₀). Also periodize the finite measure (1−η(t/P))T restricted to |t|<L; it corrects exactly the local datum and each of its coefficients is ≥−C_L/P³ by the series convention with 1/P. Adding the periodic delta of weight C_L/P² restores positivity in all coefficients at once. The resulting level is λ−C_L/P². The converse β_P≤λ is immediate by positivity and the form kernel.

To attain the supremum use a sequence of admissible levels tending to β_P. Each weight is bounded by O_{L,P}(log(2+|k|)) uniformly along the sequence, by modulating one fixed test f with fhat(0)≠0 up to 2πk/P and keeping only that atom; the levels remain bounded. Extract a diagonal limit and pass by domination against smooth tests. If β_P=λ, the minimizer kills all nodes of positive weight (extension of the identity by approximation in form norm). Apply directly the modulation and Jensen proof of 3744 to this symmetrized measure and the minimizer: only the constant −λ in the energy changes. The positive gaps of its support must converge in density to 2π/L. All are positive multiples of 2π/P; by discreteness this requires P/L to be an integer. Sufficiency of that commensurability is not claimed. The construction distinguishes the approximating periodic certificates from the exact comparator at the critical level.

### Periodic certificate with finitely many parameters for every level strictly below the bottom

For each fixed L and b<λ_W(L/2) there is a certificate using only one period P, explicit smooth cutoffs and an even real trigonometric polynomial Q with rational coefficients. On the circle, the distribution
    B + χ_ext Q,    B=periodization of χ₀(T−bδ₀),
coincides exactly with T−bδ₀ on |t|<L and all its Fourier coefficients have a common strictly positive floor. χ₀ is even, equals 1 near the data interval and has support in (−P/2,P/2); χ_ext is even and vanishes on the data interval. Integer periods and cutoff transitions from a countable list with rational endpoints can be chosen, for computable L. Conversely a certificate of this type implies λ_W(L/2)>b by Parseval on the circle. This turns the abstract existence of weights into an exhaustive criterion for STRICT sign with a finite number of parameters per certificate. No a priori bound on that number is given.

Indeed, take L'>L so close that λ_W(L'/2)>b by continuity. By 3863 choose P sufficiently large and a periodic positive extension C on the datum L' at level b, reserving a strict constant ρ>0 in ALL coefficients (first represent a higher level and add a delta). Symmetrize it. Choose χ₀=1 on [−L',L']; the residual C−B is supported outside (−L',L'). The base alone has
    Bhat_k ≥ [log(1+|2πk/P|)−K]/P
with K depending only on b and the base cutoff. For the archimedean term write m(ξ)=log(1+|ξ|)+e(ξ), ||e||∞ bounded by digamma. In the convolution with χhat₀/(2π), the integral of the kernel equals 1 and the difference between the two shifted logarithms is bounded by log(1+|shift|). Thus it suffices to include in K the integral of |χhat₀(s)|(log(1+|s|)+||e||∞)/(2π). It is bounded explicitly using the L¹ norm of χ₀ and of its second derivative and integration by parts. The prime contacts, the truncated polar term and the shift b cost their finite total variations. This allows certifying the tail using only estimates of the known kernel.

Smooth the residual by periodic convolution with an autocorrelation of arbitrarily small support and integral one (start from a nonnegative mollifier of integral one); its multiplier m_k lies between 0 and 1 and tends to 1 for each fixed k as the support shrinks. The smoothed R still has free space around [−L,L]. The coefficients of B+R are (1−m_k) Bhat_k+m_k Chat_k. For |k| large both base and certificate terms have floor ρ before weighting; for the remaining finite set take the support small enough to obtain floor ρ/2. Choose χ_ext=1 on supp R and 0 on [−L,L]. By uniform trigonometric approximation and rationalization, there is an even real Q with ||χ_ext Q−R||₁/P<ρ/4. The floor is preserved. The exterior cutoff is essential to preserve the exact identity on the interval.

For a given candidate, ||χ_ext Q||₁ and the explicit floor of Bhat_k give a finite threshold beyond which there is margin without integrating further coefficients. Below that threshold it suffices to certify a finite number of integrals with error bounds. With computable parameters and data and strict slack this allows a search by interleaved enumeration; numerical feasibility is not claimed, nor termination if no positive margin exists. The period may need to grow as b approaches the bottom; equivalence at fixed P is not claimed.

### Effective trial at S=2.77: certified obstruction for a basis of exterior corrections

The basis B given by periodization of the sharp restriction of the physical kernel to |t|<L=5.54 was tested, with period P=18 and level b=0. The cutoff equals one near the origin and preserves the renormalized archimedean distribution; there is no prime contact at the edge. Exterior corrections by symmetric translates of the normalized triangle of half-width w=1/25 were tried. In double precision the minimum of the coefficients multiplied by P was optimized for k=0,…,64,128,256 with 40,60,100 equispaced centres between L+0.05 and P/2−0.05 and absolute budget 500 in cosine coordinates. The best minima reported were −0.4963, −0.7158 and −0.8760. These are numerical trials, with no inference about λ.

There is an exact obstruction, independent of the budget and of the number or choice of centres: at k=450 the multiplier sinc²(πkw/P) is zero. For each fixed z with b>0, L^(3/2)F_l(z)−√2 π/(z−iω)²→0 uniformly for bounded ω. Indeed the amplitude on cell j is √(2/((M+1)h))sin((j+1)π/(M+1)). Rescaled by L^(3/2) it tends locally to √2 π t, with modulus ≤C(t+h), and the phase exp(iω jh) approximates exp(iωt) on compact sets. Integrate against exp(−zt) by domination. For b≥Δ/2 these rescaled functions, multiplied by exp(−bt) and extended by zero, have uniformly bounded L¹ norm and total variation: each interior jump before the weight is ≤C h(1+t) by the difference of sines and by bounded |ω|, the initial jump is O(h) and the final weighted one too. Between jumps integrate the derivative of the weight using C(t+h). By parts L^(3/2)|F_l(z)|≤C/(1+|γ|). For 0≤b<Δ/2 the same bounds without the decay of the exponential give instead a polynomial in L divided by 1+|γ|. By reflection, after normalizing the energy, those terms are o(1) in sum, since Σ_ρ (1+|γ|)^(−2)<∞. For b≥Δ/2 the summable majorant and the factor exp((b−Δ)L) allow suppressing ALL zeros with b<Δ by domination, even if they accumulate in abscissa. The reflected pairs contribute twice the real part. Use exp(−iωL)=(−1)^l and exp(iωh)=1+o(1). The formula follows.

Assume the front is nonempty. From any sequence of L extract by diagonalization one along which each exp(iγL) converges to a unimodular number. The real profile of the right-hand side without (−1)^l converges uniformly on real compact sets to a real-analytic function: the rational series converges normally away from the poles, by the zero count. No limit profile is identically zero. Extending the real part as the half-sum of the series and its conjugate reflection, at ω=γ−iΔ there remains a pole of order four with nonzero coefficient; the reflected poles lie above and distinct ordinates on the front give distinct poles. On each compact interval the limit has only finitely many zeros. Outside neighbourhoods of arbitrarily small total length of those zeros, the sign alternates by parity in each component for the late subsequence. Counting along the mesh of step π/L gives half of each sign, and the subsequence argument gives it for the whole sequence. For the size, if there were no uniform constant c, extract a failing subsequence with c→0. Its limit profile is bounded away from zero on some subinterval of positive length, where each parity contains ≫L points of the declared magnitude, a contradiction. It has not been established that the front of ζ is nonempty nor that an exterior supremum must be attained.

### Lower rate for the minimum of each table without requiring an attained abscissa

Let m(L) be the smallest unit energy of 3967 with L=2^n, h=1/L. For Δ=sup Re(ρ−1/2)>0 one has
    liminf log(1+max(0,−m(L)))/log L ≥ 2Δ/(1/2−Δ).
For Δ=1/2 the conclusion is +∞. No maximal distance, separation of abscissas or choice of favourable scales is presupposed. A floor −L^{o(1)} along any subsequence would already suffice for the global sign. Here the rate is for the minimum over the whole table, without locating its frequency.

Fix 0<a<Δ. The cardinal construction of lines 45–51 supplies for EVERY sufficiently large physical length B a test f_B of norm one, energy ≤−exp(aB) and ||f_B'||₂≤C_a. For the last property choose a reflected pair at distance b>a, shift its two cardinals towards opposite ends and cut as there with (1−η)b>a. Removing the common scalar factor exp(−Rb), they are two fixed profiles with coefficients of fixed modulus and centres separated by 2R; their cross products in L² tend to zero, and the cuts lose norm o(1). Their difference then has norm bounded below and derivative bounded above. The same proof works for complex data by sesquilinearity.

Let P be the projection by cell averages of width h and e=f_B−Pf_B. One has ||e||≤h||f_B'|| and ||Pf_B||²=1−O_a(h²). For any shift s, |⟨e,τ_s f_B⟩|=|⟨e,(I−P)τ_s f_B⟩|≤h²||f_B'||². Expand the autocorrelation after projecting, applying the computation also to the opposite shift and bounding the e,e term. The contact error is O_a(h²), uniform in s. Only q≤exp(B+2h) intervene, with sum of weights Λ(q)/√q≤C(1+B)exp(B/2) for h≤1 by comparison with log(q)/√q. For each polar moment take an aligned interval of length ≤B+2h containing both supports. On it each exponential g=exp(±t/2) has ||g−Pg||≤h||g'||=h||g||/2, hence |⟨e,g⟩|≤C_a h²||g||. The product of the norms of the two opposite exponents is O(exp((B+2h)/2)), independent of the initial position. The archimedean error only needs a polynomial bound in B: both data have total variation O_a(√B), by Cauchy–Schwarz and contraction of variation by cell averages, and L¹ norm ≤√(B+2h). In Fourier their squares are integrated against O(log(2+|ξ|)) using the majorant O_a(√(B+2)/(1+|ξ|)). Thus W(Pf_B)≤−exp(aB)+O_a((1+B)^C(1+h²exp(B/2))).

In the average of 3967 one can also take C_B≤C(1+B)^C exp(B/2): the weights (rh)² are ≤(B+2)², the prime contacts are summed as above, the polar kernel costs O(h exp((B+2)/2)) per cell and the archimedean term summed with those weights is O((B+2)²). The degree is <M when B+2h<L. Choose B=(log L)/k with 2k>1/2−a. Then both the physical projection and the phase average lose o(exp(aB)), by h²=L^−2. The normalized projected test therefore gives m(L)≤−exp(aB)/2 eventually. Let k↓(1/2−a)/2 and then a↑Δ. The criterion still requires an independent arithmetic floor for those energies; the rate is an implication under existence of an exterior zero.

### A polynomial floor for any fixed position of the table would suffice

Let m_{K+1}(L) be the (K+1)-th smallest energy of the sinusoidal table of 3967. If Δ>0, for every fixed K and every p>0 one has m_{K+1}(L)<−L^p for ALL sufficiently large dyadic lengths. It is not required that the supremum Δ be attained. The improvement over 3977 and 3999 consists in estimating the projection and modulation loss over the full divisor, keeping its abscissa Δ instead of paying the abscissa 1/2 of the separated terms. It is a statement about entries, not about the negative index.

**Projection loss.** Let f be a unit vector of length B, with ||f'||₂≤C and centred support, and g its projection by averages of width h=1/L. Both have total variation and L¹ norm ≤C'(1+B), and ||f−g||₁≤C'(1+B)h. At z=b+iγ, the bilateral transform of each datum is O(poly(B) exp(|b|(B+2h)/2)/(1+|γ|)), by parts on the function of bounded variation multiplied by exp(−bt). For the difference one can use the minimum of this bound and the L¹ bound with the factor h. Subtracting reflected products one obtains
    |W(f)−W(g)| ≤ C poly(B) exp(ΔB) √h,
since min(h,1/(1+|γ|))≤√h/(1+|γ|)^(1/2) and the sum of (1+|γ|)^(−3/2) converges. Weil holds for these BV data by mollification, with the same quadratic majorant for the product and convergence in H^s for s<1/2. One can centre with respect to a middle cell, enlarging the margin by O(h).

**Envelope loss.** The weighted average of the table energies of 3967 with |P|², P with the coefficients of g, is exactly ∫W(g_t)dν(t), where g_t multiplies cell j of g by exp(ijt) and ν is the probability |Σ v_j exp(ijt)|²dt/(2π) on [−π,π]. Both expressions are Σ c_r κ_r b_r by orthogonality. The weights of the table average sum to ||g||². Subtracting a central cell index from j does not alter W. If ω=t/h, the modulation factor minus one has sup ≤(B+2h)|ω| on the support; its variation between consecutive cells is ≤h|ω| per jump. By the product rule and bounded ||g||₁, both the total variation and the L¹ norm of g_t−g are ≤poly(B)|ω| (the jumps due only to the factor are summed with weight equal to the absolute value of the cell). The previous BV computation gives |W(g_t)−W(g)|≤poly(B)exp(ΔB)(|ω|+ω²). Since t²≤(π²/2)(1−cos t) and κ_1=cos(π/(M+1)), the mean of ω² is O((Mh)^−2)=O(L^−2). A loss O(poly(B)exp(ΔB)/L) remains, uniform in the polynomial of the test as long as the H¹ control of the original datum is kept.

**Uniform erasure in the amplified witness.** Mark any K phases θ. Apply to the continuous datum the product Q_h of the filters (I−exp(−iθ)τ_h)/(|1−exp(−iθ)|+h) before projecting. At each fixed point w of nonzero abscissa its symbol q_h(w) (here q_h denotes the product) is bounded above and below in modulus, uniformly for small h. For one factor, if |1−exp(−iθ)|/h→∞ the ratio of moduli tends to one. In the bounded case extract θ/h→ξ real using principal representatives; the limit symbol is (w+iξ)/(1+|ξ|), nonzero. As an operator each factor is a combination with bounded coefficients of I and (I−τ_h)/h, and the latter is an average of translations of the derivative. Hence Q_h has bounds on all necessary seminorms with loss of at most K derivatives, even in L¹ with weight exp(|t|/2).

For 0<a<Δ choose a reflected exterior pair with b>a and (1−η)b>a. Repeat the witness of 3999 with its two cardinals, dividing each by the value q_h at its own point BEFORE the cut. Apply Q_h to the cut datum. Before the cut and after the filter the pair preserves exactly its evaluations at all zeros. The Weil error of the cut tends to zero at the scale of cardinals with evaluation one, uniformly in the phases: use the weighted cut bounds of line 51 with K+2 derivatives (the cardinals have that decay at every order; choose cutoffs with derivatives of all orders uniformly bounded). The support lengthens by Kh. After removing the common scalar factor exp(−Rb), the H¹ norms remain bounded and the L² norms bounded away from zero. For the last claim, extract a subsequence of the coefficients of each combination I,D_h: on the fixed profile they converge strongly in H¹ to combinations I,∂. The limit profile normalized by q_h(w) still has evaluation one at w by weighted decay. The two profiles are translated to ends that separate without limit, so their scalar product tends to zero. The cuts, after removing the scalar, lose o(1) in H¹. One obtains a unit f with W(f)≤−exp(aB) eventually (reserve a margin in (1−η)b), support B+O(Kh) and uniformly bounded ||f'||₂. Its projection has polynomial vanishing at the K phases, by commutation with τ_h. For K=0 the witness of 3999 suffices directly.

Fix p, take C so large that CΔ>p and then choose a<Δ with Ca>p and C(Δ−a)<1/2. For B=C log L both losses are o(exp(aB)), and the degree of the projected test is less than M. The average over the remaining phases divided by its mass ||g||²→1 lies below −L^p. Erasing the K smallest proves the result. In particular any polynomial lower bound for that statistic along a subsequence excludes Δ>0. This proof does not obtain the required arithmetic bound.

### Finite arithmetic comparison between the ordered phases and a triangular prime count

In each table of 3967 put N=2M=2L², h=1/L and A_K=max(0,−m_{K+1}(L)). For μ of 193, let
    D(L)=max_{1≤r<M} |∫ (1−|t−rh|/h)_+ dμ(t)|,
    dμ=Σ Λ(n)n^(−1/2) δ_{log n}−1_{t≥0}exp(t/2)dt.
For fixed K one has, unconditionally and scale by scale,
    |log(1+A_K)−log(1+D(L))| ≤ O_K(log(2L)).
The comparison is deterministic and preserves any exponential rate with respect to L. In particular the permission to erase K phases is equivalent, up to polynomial scale factors, to controlling the maximal discrepancy of these counts. Neither direction uses zeros for the comparison. Arithmetic antecedent 193, which already identifies the centred measure; 3967 introduces the table whose discrete transform is inverted here.

Let E_l be the energies and ⟨·⟩ the mean over the N phases. Their discrete coefficients at distance |r|<M are c_r κ_r, without aliasing, and ⟨E⟩=c_0. For the first K lags |c_r|≤C_K log(2L). Indeed the unit pulse has Fourier density O(h min(1,(h|ξ|)^−2)), whose integral with weight log(2+|ξ|) is O(log(2L)); this bounds every archimedean crossing by Cauchy–Schwarz with the symbol shifted by a constant. In the first K lags there are no prime contacts for (K+1)h<log 2 and the polar term is bounded. Adjust constants for the remaining finitely many L with K<N.

Mark up to K lowest negative energies and form U(x)=∏_{j marked}|x−exp(iθ_j)|² on the circle. It is zero at the marked ones, has sum of moduli of Laurent coefficients ≤4^K and at every unmarked phase is ≥(4/N)^(2K) for N≥4 by chord separation. Hence |⟨UE⟩|≤C_K log(2L) (for L large, K<M). At unmarked phases E_-≤A_K, and U≤4^K. Since no positive one was marked,
    ⟨E_+⟩ ≤ (N/4)^(2K) [ C_K log(2L)+4^K A_K ].
The mean of |E| is 2⟨E_+⟩−c_0, so it dominates in modulus each c_r κ_r. For |r|<M, κ_r≥2 sin²(π/(M+1))/(M+1) ≳M^(−3) by a single term of the product of sines. This bounds max|c_r| by C_K M^(2K+3)(log(2L)+A_K). In the reverse direction |E_l|≤(2M−1)max|c_r| directly. The mean identity also explains why an extremely negative phase requires positive energies compensating it.

For r≥1 the overlap of unnormalized pulses in frequency is exactly the tent (1−|t−rh|/h)_+ in the translation variable; the use of unit pulses fixes its height at one. By 193 the centred comb contributes to c_r minus the indicated integral (the reflected tent has no mass on t>0). The residual kernel exp(−|t|/2) costs O(h), the archimedean term is O(log(2L)) by the previous bound. Thus |D(L)−max_{1≤r<M}|c_r||≤C log(2L). Together with the diagonal this gives the logarithmic inequality. In particular under Δ>0 the result 4011 forces D(L)>L^p at all sufficiently large scales for each fixed p. This does not establish the polynomial upper bound of D(L) along any subsequence.

### Separate excesses and deficits, in primes only, on a prescribed logarithmic band

If Δ>0, given p>0 and C with CΔ>p+1, at each sufficiently large scale L=2^n there are two tents of 4027 with centres in [C log L−D,C log L+D], one with discrepancy >L^p and another <−L^p. This holds when counting only PRIMES with weight (log q)/√q and keeping the same continuous integral. D is fixed once the parameters and the zero used are chosen. The centres correspond to multiplicative sizes comparable to L^C, far below exp L. Thus a one-sided polynomial bound on the maximum of excesses (or of deficits) over the whole table along a subsequence suffices. Essential antecedent: positive annihilation filter and recurrence for the Gaussian sum in entry 2244. The additional step is to realize nonnegative weights on the tent mesh itself, keeping both margins.

All power orders k≥3 contribute O(1) in total, even without a window, by Σ_{q prime}(log q)q^(−3/2)/(1−q^(−1/2))<∞. For k=2, on a tent of width 2h≤2 the prime bases lie in [Y,eY]; their sum of (log q)/q is O(1) by θ(eY)≪Y, adjusting Y<2. Removing all composite powers changes each discrepancy by O(1) uniformly.

Fix 0<σ<b=Re w≤Δ for a centred zero w=b+iγ, with Cb>p+1 and C(Δ−b)<1/2. Use the compact probability of entry 2244 in the centred coordinates: each conjugate pair b_j±iγ_j with b_j≥σ is annihilated by a Bernoulli on 0,π/γ_j with weights proportional to 1 and exp(−b_jπ/γ_j). The sum of supports is finite by the Ingham count used there with abscissa 1/2+σ. Convolve with a smooth compact nonnegative density. The bilateral transform G(z)=∫g(y)e^{zy}dy is entire, not identically zero. If m is the order of G at w, Q(z)=G(z)/(z−w)^m is nonzero at w and vanishes at the other distinct points with Re z≥σ. It is the transform of a smooth compactly supported q: after each division solve the first-order differential equation with solution zero before the support; vanishing of the moment ensures it is also zero after (as in 3798, changing the Laplace convention).

Choose g₀=g*η, with η smooth nonnegative, a sufficiently large constant on supp(q)−supp(g); then g₀≥|q| and its transform still vanishes on the whole front Re z≥σ. The two tests H_±=g₀±Re(exp(iα)q) are nonnegative, with supports and seminorms uniform in α.
