Fix A>0, X sufficiently large, B=A+10 and v=B log log X/log X. There is E_X⊂[X,2X] of measure O_A(X/(log X)^A) such that for each center R₀ in [X,2X] outside E_X both conclusions hold:
1. For all t≥1 and n=⌊t R₀²⌋ one has |exp(n)(t/n)^n M_n(t)|≪log X exp(2v²t).
2. For all 1≤t≤1/(100000 v), the same monomial has strictly positive sign. By 4346 and 4334, positivity also extends to exact centers R=√(n/t) outside the same set for all 0<t≤1/(100000 v). The statement with rounding for t<1 only follows while the exact center remains in the covered range.

This controls the fixed slopes of 4368 at arbitrarily large temperature for the first conclusion. Along those slopes the difference P_+−P_− of the two prime masses, each of exponent 1/2, has limsup of log(1+|P_+−P_−|)/t ≤2v². Indeed the archimedean side in the normalization h of 4346 is O(log(2+R₀)) for t≥1 by its logarithmic density and the Gaussian envelope, the poles are O(1) for large R₀ and the other prime powers are O(1) by 4368. In particular the ceiling of the exponent of the difference tends to zero with X outside the indicated sets. It does not assert that it is exactly zero at a fixed good height.

Proof. Exclude a radius 1002 around each |γ| in [X−1002,2X+1002] with |δ|>v. By symmetry and Ingham's uniform density of 4095, the measure is O(X^q log^5 X), q=3(1/2−v)/(3/2−v), since it suffices to count up to 3X. Since 1−q=2v/(3/2−v)≥4v/3, the declared bound follows. The exact center R=√(n/t) is at distance less than 1 from R₀ for t≥1. Within |γ−R|≤1000 on the positive half-axis one therefore has |δ|≤v. In that band, the phase of 4334 satisfies
    |2tδγ−2n arctan(δ/γ)| ≤ 6t v |γ−R| + 6t v³/R
for large R, separating the linear term and the cubic remainder of arctan. For t≤1/(100000 v) the right-hand side is <0.1. On [R,R+100] the count of 3517 gives ≫log R zeros. Each contributes normalized real part ≥0.9 exp(−21000t): r=√(γ²+δ²)∈[R,R+101], and (log h)″≥−4t above R. All other summands within radius 1000 have positive real part.

Outside radius 1000 the absolute ceiling of 4356 is used: exp(t/2)exp(−t(r−R)²), with |r−γ|≤1/2. Group into strips j≤|γ−R|<j+1 from j=1000 on, each with O(log(3+R+j)) zeros; for t≥1 the sum is O(log R exp(−990000t)). To compare without implicit constants in the sign, the explicit counting ceiling in 4334 with unit strips gives here ≤100(j+2)log R per strip (low endpoints included via their prefix); the sum is ≤log R exp(−980000t). The floor on [R,R+100] contains ≥10 log R zeros by the same difference of main terms and error ≤2 log(2R). This proves the sign. For the first conclusion there is no need to control the phase: in the core the cost in modulus is ≤exp(2v²t)Σ exp(−t(r−R)²)≪exp(2v²t)log R for all t≥1, and outside one already has the previous tail. Negative heights double the real part.

Antecedents: moving density in 4095, local phase cancellation in 4334 and comparison of two exponential masses in 4368. It is a measure bound on the centers and does not allow eliminating a fixed exceptional band containing an exterior zero.

### How much can be recovered between two observation heights

For fixed u>0 the envelope can be measured exactly using only the positive part (without shifts):
    L(u)=limsup_n (u/n) log(1+[exp(n)u^(−n) M_n(n/u)]_+)
        = max(0, max_ρ [2δ²−I(u,v)]),    I(u,v)=u log(u/v)−u+v,    v=|−(ρ−1/2)²|=γ²+δ².
The formula takes into account crossings between maxima and coincidences of phases on the discrete mesh. Indeed the normalized signal is a sum of powers B_w^n with positive multiplicities, B_w=(e/u)w exp(−w/u). The maximal modulus is attained by a finite set, separated from the smaller moduli, and Σ|B_w| converges. Along a sequence n→∞ the phases of all maximizers tend simultaneously to 1 by simultaneous approximation on a torus (if the return is periodic use its multiples). Thus the positive real part attains the same exponent as the sum of moduli. u log|B_w|=2δ²−I(u,v). Antecedent 4356: optimizing the center and varying the degree proves an ordinary limit for the negative part. Here the center is kept exactly and the opposite sign is used.

An arithmetic bound L(u)≤η at a single point is equivalent to 2δ²≤η+I(u,v) for ALL zeros, for η≥0. Let 0<a<b be two centers in the squared variable and suppose L(a),L(b)≤η. On the whole gap a≤v≤b one obtains
    2δ² ≤ η+C(a,b),   C(a,b)=I(a,v*)=I(b,v*),
    v*=exp((b log b−a log a)/(b−a)−1).
Indeed I(a,v) increases and I(b,v) decreases as functions of v on [a,b], so the maximum of their minimum is at the intersection. The value v* belongs to the interval by the mean value theorem. For a=R², b=(R+h)² and h/R→0, v*=a+(b−a)/2+O((b−a)²/a), and C=(b−a)²/(8a)(1+O(h/R))=(h²/2)(1+O(h/R)). In particular with η=0 the loss in horizontal distance is h/2 to first order. On the integer mesh u, two contiguous controls with exponent zero would give |δ|≤(1+O(1/u))/(4√u) for v in that cell. These are implications conditional on data at the centers; the density estimate of 4382 does not provide such data on the whole mesh.

The loss of the gap is not eliminated by interpolation of these exponents. In an auxiliary symmetric divisor on the axis, insert a quartet with v=v*, 0<2δ²≤C(a,b), γ=√(v*−δ²), choosing δ<1/2 and the gap at admissible height. The exponent L remains zero at ALL centers u outside (a,b) because I(u,v*) increases when moving away from v* on both sides. At u=v* it takes the value 2δ². If C(a,b)<1/2 and the height is large enough, equality can be taken and the example attains the loss. This bounds the reach of interpolation alone, even with controls on a continuum outside the gap. The modified divisor is not attributed to ζ and the example does not preserve the arithmetic identity of its primes.

### Transfer to arbitrary poles via the time of a sum of exponentials

Fix H=3·10¹² and t₀=10^(−4). Let u_j>1/2 be arbitrary, j=1,…,m, allowing repetitions. If
    Σ_j 1/(u_j²+H²−1/4) ≤ t₀/4,
the full form of POWER is strictly positive for F(z)=z^n/Π_j(u_j−z), simultaneously for ALL integers 0≤n<m. More generally it holds for every nonzero real N of degree <m such that N(z)N(−z)=Σ c_n(−z²)^n with c_n≥0. In particular for m≤225000000000000000000 (2.25·10²⁰) no additional restriction on the poles is needed, since each denominator of the budget is strictly larger than H². Any number of poles is also admitted if they grow sufficiently. The conclusion is about this class of numerators; the statement for each isolated monomial does not imply semidefiniteness on their linear span.

Proof. For n≤10⁹ the stronger result M_n(t)>0 at all t comes from 1700. For n>10⁹ strengthen 4334 to
    M_n(t) ≥ 0.8 A_n(t),   A_n(t)=Σ_ρ |w|^n exp(−t Re w),   0<t≤t₀.
If R=√(n/t)>H/2, within |γ−R|≤10/√t the phase of each summand satisfies |phase|<0.31 on the positive half-axis. The total modulus outside is <10^(−38) W log R f(R) while the real part of the core is ≥0.004 W log R f(R) in the units of 4334. By symmetry the same quotient holds for the total. If R≤H/2, 4324 bounds the absolute mass beyond H by 0.46^n H²·0.049 times a single verified term, and the rest of the verified heights sum without loss. This gives the declared margin in both regimes.

Let K be the convolution on [0,∞) of the m functions exp(−u_j²t). The form of F is ∫K(t) M_n(t)dt in the spectral normalization: the Laplace transform of K is Π(u_j²+w)^−1 and the reflected numerator equals w^n. The interchange is absolute because after integrating the modulus each term costs |w|^n Π(u_j²+Re w)^−1=O(|γ|^(2n−2m)). For each zero with |γ|>H, write a=Re w≥H²−1/4. The density proportional to K(t)exp(−at) is exactly the law of the sum of m independent exponential variables with rates u_j²+a (normalize each convolution factor). Its mean is Σ_j 1/(u_j²+a)≤t₀/4. By Markov the mass after t₀ does not exceed a quarter of its total mass, i.e. it does not exceed a third of the mass up to t₀. The factor |w|^n, independent of t, preserves this comparison. Summing, the late absolute cost of the high zeros is ≤(1/3)∫₀^t₀ K A_n. The low zeros contribute positively also after t₀, so the total floor is ≥(0.8−1/3)∫₀^t₀ K A_n>0. For n≤10⁹ it suffices to integrate the pointwise sign without the margin. Finally use linearity in the reflected product for c_n≥0. Antecedents: 1700 for bounded scalar orders; 4281 for the mixture of denominators; 4294 for arbitrary numerator of degree 32. Here the comparison of late masses only imposes the budget on the high zeros, which introduces H² in each denominator.

### One sign change in the coefficients of each parity, with free width and degree

Let t₁=10^(−8) and suppose Σ_j(u_j²+H²−1/4)^−1≤t₁/4. For N(z)=z^n[P(−z²)+z Q(−z²)], n≥10000 and deg N<m, the full form is strictly positive if N≠0 and each real list of coefficients of P,Q, in increasing degree and omitting zeros, changes sign at most ONCE. Both polynomials may have any degree and coefficients of any magnitude. In particular, this includes any pair of powers of the numerator with integer exponents ≥10000, with no restriction on the distance between exponents nor on the two coefficients. The powers are of the rational numerator of the bridge; these are not the real exponents of the original generators. The budget allows up to 2.25·10¹⁶ arbitrary poles. With a smaller absolute budget, not quantified below, one can take n≥0.

Analytic step. For k≥10000, 0<t≤t₁ and real c, the thermal sum of w^k(w−c)² has real part at least 0.7 times the sum of moduli, counting the factor exp(−tw) in both. Use R=√(k/t)≥10⁶, W=t^(−1/2)≥10000, B=RW and A=R²−c. Normalize the terms by f(R)=R^(2k)exp(−k) and work at positive heights. For positive γ let w=a+ib. On |γ−R|≤10W one has γ≥0.9R and the phase θ of w^k exp(−tw) satisfies |θ|<0.004 by 4334. Consequently Re(exp(iθ)(w−c)²)≥0.75|w−c|²−4b² (expand and apply 2|b(a−c)|≤b²+(a−c)²). In this zone |b|≤1.1R and the normalized modulus of the monomial is ≤exp(t/2). The cost of the summed error term is ≤500t W log R B²: the count in the interval of length 20W is <90W log R by the main term and the endpoint errors of 3517.

To pay that error even if c coincides with R², take x=(γ−R)/W in [1/2,1] when A≥0 and in [−1,−1/2] when A<0. There |a−c|≥0.9(|A|+B) since a=R²+2Bx+W²x²−δ², W/R≤0.01. The normalized modulus of the monomial is ≥exp(−3): between r=√(γ²+δ²) and R one has |(log f)″|<4.1t and |r−R|≤W+1/2. The count in either of these two bands is ≥0.04W log R for R≥10⁶: the main density is ≥0.13 log R and the endpoint cost ≤8 log(2R) by Bellotti–Wong. Therefore the total normalized absolute mass is ≥0.001 W log R (|A|+B)².

In the tail jW≤|γ−R|<(j+1)W, j≥10, one has |w−c|≤5(j+2)²(|A|+B) expanding around R. Its cost relative to W log R (|A|+B)² is ≤2500 exp(t/2)Σ_{j≥10}(j+2)^5 exp(−(j−0.005)²)<10^(−30), by the strip count of 4334 (100(j+2)W log R suffices). Collect the bounds: from the 0.75 of the absolute mass one loses at most 500t/0.001 and less than 10^(−25) through the tail. More than 0.7 remains. The conjugates double the real part. The argument of 4412 integrates this margin: the additional factor |w−c|² is independent of t, so at most 1/3 of the early mass is still lost through the high zeros. The interchange requires numerator degree <m as before.

Algebraic step. If P has exactly one sign change, after reversing its sign if necessary, its lower coefficients are negative and the upper ones positive. It has a root c>0 by continuity, omitting an initial power of w. On dividing by w−c the quotient has non-negative coefficients: its coefficient at w^j is −c^(−j−1)Σ_{i≤j}p_i c^i; all these partial sums are ≤0 because they first decrease and then increase up to zero. Hence P²=(w−c)² times a polynomial with non-negative coefficients. Without a sign change P² already has non-negative coefficients. Apply the same observation to Q and sum by linearity in the reflected product w^n(P(w)²+wQ(w)²). No bound is imposed on the number of summands so obtained. The sign change is counted in the coefficients of the polynomial in w, distinct from the count of residue signs of 3533.

Existential extension to all small k. For fixed k between 0 and 9999 rescale γ=W x, and normalize w−c by W²+|c|. On compact sets of x the difference between the rescaled complex summand and the real x^(2k)(αx²−β)²exp(−x²) tends uniformly to zero as W→∞, with α=W²/(W²+|c|), β=c/(W²+|c|), α+|β|=1. Here one has additionally divided by W^(2k); the transverse deviation δ/W tends to zero. By Riemann–von Mangoldt, the measure Σ_{γ>0} δ_{γ/W}/(W log W) converges vaguely to dx/(2π); the tail of the integrands and their moduli is dominated by a Gaussian times a polynomial of fixed degree, using the strip count. Thus both the real and the absolute sums tend, after normalization, to the same real integral (uniformly in α,β by compactness). The integral has a positive minimum on that compact set because αx²−β is not the zero polynomial. For the finitely many k one obtains a t*>0, t*≤t₁, for which the margin 0.7 holds simultaneously. Using t*/4 in the budget of 4412 gives the statement without minimal degree shift, without carrying over the explicit number of poles to this version.

### Any fixed number of arbitrarily separated monomials: compactification around their maxima

For each integer s≥1 there is τ_s>0 such that, simultaneously for ALL nonzero real numerators N with at most s monomials, with no restriction on degrees, signs or separation,
    Σ_ρ exp(tλ²)N(λ)N(−λ) ≥ 0.7 Σ_ρ |exp(tλ²)N(λ)N(−λ)|,    0<t≤τ_s.
In fact the quotient tends uniformly to one as t decreases to zero. By 4412 strict positivity follows for any proper denominator with poles u_j>1/2 and Σ_j 1/(u_j²+H²−1/4)≤τ_s/4. It is a qualitative extension of 4424 to any sign pattern with s fixed terms. No rate of decrease of τ_s is provided here. The construction controls the near-dependencies of monomials of high and close degrees, which prevent summing diagonal estimates.

Sequential proof. Let W=1/√t→∞. Separate the parities of N and evaluate at z=(γ−iδ)/W. After absorbing powers of i and W into the real coefficients of each sector and removing the common i from the odd one, the trace at positive heights is the sum of COMPLEX squares of functions of the type f(z)=exp(−z²/2)Σ c_k z^k. Indeed the cross term of the parities cancels exactly in the reflected product. It suffices that in each sector Σ Re(f²) and Σ|f|² be asymptotically equal in ratio. The conjugates double the real part, and the modulus of the sum of the sectors is dominated by the sum of their moduli.

From any sequence of data, extract a subsequence with the same number of degrees and such that each distance between their centers √k has a limit in [0,∞]. Group by bounded distance. The centers of a bounded group can be treated together with B=0: the degrees become fixed after extraction and the usual basis x^k exp(−x²/2) on x≥0 is used. For a divergent group choose B=√min k of the group and p=(k−B²)/B. The p are bounded and converge after extraction, although they may coalesce. Start from the basis
    f_p(z)=exp((B²−z²)/2)(z/B)^(B²+Bp)
and replace it by its nested divided differences in the first j parameters, j=1,…,l (Newton interpolation). At the original nodes the exponent is an integer, so the new basis spans exactly the original group and the change is real. To interpolate in p one uses log on the right half-plane and the limiting value on its boundary. At z=B+y+iη with y in compact sets and |η|≤1/(2W), the functions of the new basis converge uniformly to exp(−y²) times the corresponding divided differences of p↦exp(py) at the limiting nodes. This follows by expanding log(1+(y+iη)/B) to second order and using the simplex integral formula for divided differences. The limits are linearly independent even with repeated nodes: the difference of order j−1 has a series in y beginning exactly with y^(j−1)/(j−1)!.

Uniform majorant for all x=Re z≥0. By the simplex formula each difference is bounded using |B log(z/B)|^(j−1) and the maximum of the modulus of f_p on the real interval of parameters. With r=|z|≥B/2 one has B|arg z|=O(1) for the shifts considered; with r<B/2 one has B|arg z|≤C B|log(r/B)|. Thus the polynomial factor is ≤C_s exp(B|log(r/B)|). The modulus of the remainder is evaluated at r at cost exp(η²). The majorant reduces to a sum of two profiles exp((B²−r²)/2)(r/B)^(B²±CB) with C fixed for the group. Their maxima occur at √(B²±CB)=B+O(1) and equal O_C(1) by Taylor expansion of the logarithm. The second derivative of the logarithm in r is ≤−1 for large B. The result is a ceiling C′ exp(−c(x−B)²) uniform for each basis vector, also for every fixed bounded imaginary shift (with corresponding constants). At r=0 one proceeds by a limit. The bounded group likewise has a Gaussian tail with constants depending on its fixed degrees.

Divide each vector of the group by √(W log(W(1+B))). In the coordinate y=γ/W−B, the normalized count converges locally to dy/(2π), on the whole line if B→∞ and on the positive half-line if B=0. For a fixed interval subtract the Riemann–von Mangoldt main term at its endpoints: for B→∞ the density log(W(B+y)/(2π))/log(W(1+B)) tends to one and the endpoint error divided by W log(W(1+B)) is O(1/W). For B=0 one first uses x>0 and then the count from zero. In every cell of width one the normalized count is ≤C(1+log(2+|y|)), by the same formula, including the low endpoints. The Gaussian ceiling allows truncating with a tail of arbitrarily small norm uniformly along the sequence. The products between two distinct groups tend to zero: split halfway between their centers and use Cauchy–Schwarz with the tail of the far group on each side. This holds even when the normalization factors are different.

Consequently the matrices of the real form Σ Re(f²) and of Σ|f|², in the divided basis, converge to THE SAME block matrix: in each block it is the real Gram matrix of the limit profiles with measure dy/(2π), positive definite by their independence. This holds for all real coefficient vectors, even if in the original basis there were arbitrarily large cancellations. Normalizing the new coefficients on the sphere, any putative sequence violating the comparison would have precisely a subsequence with this positive limit, a contradiction. The integral transfer of 4412 applies because the absolute factor of the product N(λ)N(−λ) does not depend on t; m>deg N ensures convergence.

Another consequence of the same control of profiles. For fixed positive t and fixed s, the trace is strictly positive for all polynomials of at most s monomials whose minimal degree is sufficiently high (threshold depending on t,s). Indeed in any contrary sequence all groups diverge; now W=1/√t is fixed and the sphere of coefficients is normalized in the divided basis without the counting divisor. On the real axis the Lebesgue Gram matrix of each group tends to a positive block and the mass concentrates on the union of bands of fixed radius around the centers, with arbitrarily small error. In the physical frequency variable v=Wx the bands escape to infinity. The archimedean term of the explicit formula then tends to +∞ uniformly on that sphere, by its logarithmic density and the uniform lower bound on the rest. On the other hand the absolute integrals of the test function on the lines Im v=±1 are uniformly bounded by the Gaussian majorant of the groups (negative frequencies follow by parity). The Fourier shift of 4346 bounds the prime term by a constant, and the poles at ±i/2 also stay bounded. This extends 4346 to sparse combinations at fixed temperature; it does not give uniformity when t and the degrees grow together.

### An unbounded number of monomials with separation in the square root of the degree

Fix q>0. For all nonzero real numerators N with |√k−√l|≥q between distinct degrees of the same parity sector, there exist τ(q),κ(q)>0 INDEPENDENT OF THE NUMBER OF TERMS such that S_N(t)≥κ(q)Σ_ρ |exp(tλ²)N(λ)N(−λ)| for 0<t≤τ(q). This includes all square degrees j² with coefficients of any sign, with no restriction on the length. By 4412 there is a positive budget depending only on q for the sum of reciprocals of the poles that gives a rational sign to this whole class. Moreover, at EACH fixed temperature t>0 there is a minimal degree K(t,q) above which the entire thermal block of any set of degrees so separated is positive, also without restricting the length. The constants are existential. Antecedents: 4438 for fixed length; 3637 for geometric separation of poles, here the separation is in the degrees of the numerator.

Continuous lemma. For B=√k, k an integer ≥0, put φ_B(x)=exp((B²−x²)/2)(x/B)^k, x≥0; when B=0 take exp(−x²/2). In any q-separated family its synthesis c↦Σ c_B φ_B satisfies upper and lower bounds in L²(0,∞) by positive constants times ||c||₂ depending only on q. For the upper one: on |Im z|≤b, Re z=x≥0, |φ_B(z)|≤C_b exp(−c(x−B)²) by concavity in |z| as in 4438. Sums of translates of this envelope at q-separated centers are bounded; weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and integration give the bound. For the lower one, the Gaussians g_B(x)=exp(−(x−B)²) on the WHOLE line have a uniform floor: by Plancherel it suffices to integrate |Σ c_B exp(iBξ)|² over [−K,K] with weight (1−|ξ|/K)_+. The Gram matrix has diagonal K and off-diagonal entries K sinc²(K(B−D)/2); the sum of off-diagonal moduli per row is ≤(8/Kq²)Σ_{j≥1}1/j². Choose K large depending on q and use the positive minimum of the Gaussian transform on that interval. Extending φ_B by zero on the negative half-line, the difference φ_B−g_B tends to zero uniformly in x−B as B→∞, by local Taylor expansion and the Gaussian tails. In fact |φ_B−g_B|≤ε_J exp(−c′(x−B)²) for B≥J, ε_J→0, reducing the exponent of the envelope. The upper synthesis bound applied to this difference transfers the floor to the tails uniformly.

If the floor failed on the whole set there would be finite configurations with vectors of norm one and synthesis tending to zero. Extend the coefficients by zero to the integer indices k and extract limits coordinate by coordinate. After multiplying the synthesis by exp(x²/2), the series converge locally uniformly to the power series of the limit coefficients: on every disk the tail is dominated by Σ_{k>M}(e/k)^(k/2)r^k. The limit is zero by L² convergence on the positive axis, so all limit coefficients are zero. The finitely many terms B<J vanish in norm, contradicting the uniform floor of the tail. This proves the lemma without assuming that the configurations are subsets of a single fixed mesh.

Arithmetic application. Let W=1/√t and work by parity in x=v/W with f(x)=Σ c_B φ_B(x), real coefficients after absorbing the scalars and the common phase. The even Weil test in frequency v is f(v/W)² and is ≥0 on the line. For large W write L_B=log(W(1+B)), d_B=√L_B c_B. Multiplying f by √log(W(1+x)) differs from synthesizing d in L² norm by O_q(||d||₂/log W): the quotient of square roots of weights differs from one by ≤log(1+|x−B|)/log W and the Gaussian envelope applies. The lemma thus gives a quadratic floor c_q||d||₂² for the weighted integral. On 0≤x≤a≤1 its contribution is ≤C_q a||d||₂² by the envelope and pointwise Cauchy–Schwarz. Fix small a>0 depending on q. For x≥a the archimedean symbol at v=Wx is ≥c log(W(1+x)) for W large enough; on the rest it is ≥−C. Consequently the archimedean contribution is ≥c′_q W||d||₂², minus O_q(W||c||₂²). Shifting Fourier to Im v=±1 costs O_q(W||c||₂²) in the integral of |f(v/W)²| by the shifted upper lemma and parity on the negative half-axis; thus the prime term costs O_q(W||c||₂²) by ΣΛ(j)j^(−3/2)<∞. The poles are bounded pointwise by O_q(||c||₂²). Since ||c||₂²≤||d||₂²/log W, a floor c″_q W||d||₂² remains. For the ceiling of the spectral sum of moduli, in each cell j≤γ/W<j+1 the count is O(W log(W(2+j))). The envelope for the shifts |δ|/W and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz give O_q(WΣ L_B |c_B|²) when summing cells (the ratio of weights grows at most logarithmically in the distance to the center). Therefore the floor is a uniform positive fraction of the absolute cost. The parities are summed as in 4438. In the transfer of 4412 it suffices to require Σ1/(u_j²+H²−1/4)≤τ(q)κ(q)/(2+2κ(q)), by Markov.

For arbitrary fixed W and all centers B≥J, the lemma gives a fixed norm floor and the envelope leaves o_J(1)||c||₂² of mass in x<J/2 (sum Gaussian tails using separation). On the rest the archimedean symbol grows at least like log(WJ)−O(1); the comb and the poles still cost O_{W,q}(||c||₂²) by the same estimates on fixed strips. Making J large proves the second statement. The open regime includes clusters of square roots of degrees with separation tending to zero and temperatures growing simultaneously with the degrees.

### Blocks of consecutive degrees of growing length: direct bound on all cross terms

Let N(z)=z^k P(z) be real and nonzero, deg P≤d. There is no restriction on coefficients, separation, or number of sign changes. Put R=√(k/t). For each fixed temperature t>0 and 0<ε<1/4, for all sufficiently large R one has S_N(t)>0 simultaneously on the full block when
    td ≤ (1/4−ε)(log log R)² .
Both variables may also grow: having fixed t_min>0, b>1/2 and 0<σ<1, it suffices that t≥t_min and 2b²t+4b√(td)≤(1−σ)log log R with R sufficiently large. It does not follow from 4458 by separation, since in these blocks the gap in √k tends to zero. Close antecedent: 4346 for a single monomial; 4438 fixes the number of terms. Here one uses the cost of translating an ENTIRE polynomial in Gaussian norm, keeping all its cancellations.

Proof. Separate the parities as in 4438; each sector in frequency has real form up to a removed constant phase, and its contribution comes from the square of that real function on the axis. In x=√t v, B=√k and y=x−B, the positive half-line of each sector is written, after scalar normalization,
    f(x)=φ_B(x)p(y),     φ_B(x)=exp((B²−x²)/2)(x/B)^k,
with p real of degree ≤d. Its reference norm is ∫_ℝ exp(−2y²)|p(y)|²dy=1, choosing the scalar separately in each nonzero sector. The other half-line is treated by parity, valid also when shifting the contour with a change of sign of the imaginary part.

In the indicated regime B→∞, t=O(loglog R), d=O((loglog R)²), and B≥√t_min R. For |y|≤L=B^(1/5) and |η|≤b√t, Taylor in (y+iη)/B gives, uniformly,
    φ_B(B+y+iη)=exp(−(y+iη)²)(1+o(1)),
since the exponent error is O((L+b√t)³/B). Outside that interval, for x≥0, the radial envelope of 4458 gives |φ_B(x+iη)|≤exp(Cη²)exp(−c(x−B)²) with absolute constants: use r=|x+iη|, |r−x|≤|η| and concavity of the logarithm in r. The reference norm implies sup_{[−1,1]}|p|≤C(d+1) by Legendre. Equally spaced Lagrange interpolation gives |p(y+iη)|≤C(d+1)(C(1+|y|+|η|))^d, including d=0. Therefore the integrated cost of the tail is O(exp(−c′L²)), uniformly in p, both for φ_B and for the Gaussian model. In particular the real mass in [B−L,B+L] tends to one.

In L²(exp(−2y²)dy) differentiation in degree ≤d has norm ≤2√d, by the ladder relation of the orthonormal Hermite functions of that weight (equivalently, change of variable u=√2 y). Finite Taylor gives ||p(·+iη)||≤exp(2|η|√d). Thus the integral over x≥0 of |f(x+iη)|² is ≤(1+o(1))exp(2η²+4|η|√d)+o(1). The bound retains √d, essential for obtaining the square of the double logarithm instead of a single logarithm.

In the explicit formula of 4346, the real mass just localized gives ≥c(log R)/√t for the archimedean contribution: the density is (log R+O(1))/(2π) in that zone, and outside it is bounded below, with total mass O(1/√t). On the lines Im v=±b, the absolute integral of the quadratic test is O(t^(−1/2)exp(2b²t+4b√(td))) by the previous change of variable and parity. By ΣΛ(j)j^(−1/2−b)<∞ the same ceiling holds for the whole prime term. The poles v=±i/2 lie in the tail x=0 and cost O(exp(−c′B²)) by the same pointwise envelope and the interpolation bound. Thus the archimedean term dominates with the margin σ in the exponent. For fixed t and td≤(1/4−ε)(loglog R)², choose b>1/2 with 4b√(1/4−ε)<1 and absorb 2b²t in the margin. This sign refers to the thermal block at high frequencies; it does not enlarge the Weil support window nor treat the limit t→∞ at fixed R.

### Stability of the prime comparison and optimal threshold for sparse perturbations at fixed height

For the signed prime sum of 4368, bounded weight changes at O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) primes up to x (for all ε>0) cost only exp(o(t)) as a ceiling at fixed center R₀≥4, n=tR₀²+O(1). Indeed for fixed small b>ε, 4346 bounds |ĥ(u)|≪exp(2tb²−bu)/√t, and Σ_altered (log p)p^(−1/2−b) converges by partial summation. Letting b↓0 gives limsup t^−1 log(1+|change|)=0. Hence a subexponential ceiling could be transferred from another model of primes to each fixed slope if the symmetric distance between their weights satisfies this bound. By 4324/4356 bounds per slope in an open detecting band suffice, allowing bounded changes of the degree. The result does not provide the positive model that would be needed.

The exponent 1/2 is optimal even keeping the support on the ordinary primes, non-negative integer weights, completely multiplicative extension and any finite prefix. Fix Γ>4, 0<δ<1/2, β=1/2+δ, α=1−β. There are weights b_p∈{0,1,2}, equal to 1 except at O(x^β/log x) primes up to x, for which the change of the signed sum at height R₀=√(Γ²+δ²) has both signs with modulus ≫exp(2δ²t) at EACH large t, allowing a fixed number of degrees around tR₀². This concerns the change, not a statement about the sign of the true primes.

Construction. For p>P₀ sufficiently large put l_p=−2p^(−α)cos(Γ log p). Round down separately the prefix sums of positive l_p and of positive (−l_p); e_p is the increment of the first integer part minus that of the second. Since |l_p|<1 and only one of them is updated at each prime, e_p∈{−1,0,1}, the prefix discrepancies of e_p−l_p are bounded by 2 and Σ_{p≤x}|e_p|≤Σ|l_p|+2≪x^β/log x by Chebyshev and partial summation. Put b_p=1+e_p and keep b_p=1 up to P₀. In particular the model preserves the prime number theorem and the total mass of changes in θ up to x is O(x^β).

Thermal effect. Use the transform without 2π of 4368. In Σ (log p)e_p p^(−1/2)ĥ(log p) replacing e_p by l_p costs O_Γ,δ(1), including the prefixed primes: the weight u exp(−u/2)ĥ(u) has bounded total variation since ||ĥ||∞+||ĥ′||∞≤∫(1+|v|)h(v)dv=O_Γ,δ(1) for t≥1 on the chosen slope. PNT allows replacing in the result dθ(exp u) by exp(u)du with error o(exp(2δ²t)). Detail: on 0≤u≤4t, ĥ=ĥ(0)exp(−u²/(8t))Y, with |Y|+|Y′| bounded by 4368, uniformly for the finitely many degree shifts. The envelope after integrating in u is O(t^(−1/2)exp(2δ²t)exp(−(u−4δt)²/(8t))). The same bound, up to a constant, serves when integrating by parts the differentiated weight against θ(exp u)−exp u after dividing that discrepancy by exp u. On |u−4δt|≤K√t that ratio tends uniformly to zero; for the rest use Chebyshev and then K→∞. For u>4t the shift b=1 costs O(t^(−1/2)exp((4δ−2)t)) in integral or sum, negligible for δ<1/2. The interval u<0 added in Fourier has cost O(1) via exp(δu). Thus the change is
    −2∫_ℝ exp(δu) cos(Γu) ĥ(u)du + o(exp(2δ²t))
    = −4π Re h(Γ−iδ) + o(exp(2δ²t)).
Here the negative integral in u was added to the positive one, without duplicating it. At n=tR₀²+O(1), log|h(Γ−iδ)|=2δ²t+O(1/t) by Taylor expansion of n(1+log(tR₀²/n)). Its phase advances by 2arg(Γ−iδ) when n increases by one; as in 4356 a fixed number of degrees suffices to obtain cosine ≥1/2 and ≤−1/2 for each t. In this model the responsible region even moves to log p≈4δt, distinct from the center 2t where the original absolute mass concentrates.

Independent Euler control. Extend b_p completely multiplicatively, with local factor (1−b_p p^(−s))^−1, and call Z the resulting series. In Re s>1,
    Z(s)/ζ(s) = exp(G(s))/[ζ(s+α+iΓ)ζ(s+α−iΓ)],
where G extends holomorphically to Re s>1/2. Indeed the linear terms of the logarithms leave Σ(e_p−l_p)p^(−s), holomorphic by locally uniform partial summation; the degrees ≥2 are absolutely convergent there after omitting the prefix and the finite corrections are holomorphic (choose P₀>4, do not alter the small ones). The identity continues meromorphically. At s=β+iΓ the factor with argument 1 contributes a zero and the other is regular and nonzero on Re=1, so Z has a zero there. The weights differ from those of ζ and the construction does not prove a completed functional equation for Z. Nor does it change its coefficients at any integer formed only by primes of the prefix. If Σ_altered p^(−β)<∞, the logarithm of the quotient by ζ remains bounded when approaching that abscissa from the right, so it cannot insert an additional zero of the quotient there. Thus changes O(x^β/(log x)^(1+ε)) do not suffice for the same insertion. Antecedents of models: periodic sieve in 4231, auxiliary divisor in 4398 and Helson entries in the index; here a sparse list of integer weights at real primes is altered and its signed thermal signal computed.

### Unconditional construction of an Euler model without right zeros on the ordinary primes

There is a rule on finite blocks of primes producing b_p∈{0,1,2}, with any prescribed prefix equal to 1, such that:
(i) The product Z(s)=Π_p(1−b_p p^(−s))^−1 has continuation Z(s)=exp(G(s))/(s−1) with G holomorphic in Re s>1/2.
(ii) At any fixed height R₀≥4, for n=tR₀²+O(1) and t→∞, the signed prime sum Σ b_p (log p)p^(-1/2) ĥ(log p) of 4368 is O_{R₀,O(1)}(1/√t). This is proved directly on primes, without resorting to a functional equation of the model.
(iii) If E(x)=#{p≤x:b_p≠1}, unconditionally E(x)≪_A x/(log x)^A for every fixed A. More precisely E(x)≪_ε x^(Θ+ε), Θ=sup Reρ of ζ. If there is at least one right zero, limsup log(1+E(x))/log x=Θ. The rule does not use the zeros or Θ. Thus the comparison model pending in 4488 is constructed; what remains open is the square-root-scale bound FOR THE DISTANCE, not the control of the model.

Construction. On e^j<p≤e^(j+1) use v=log p−j and L=e^j/j. Let μ=L^−1Σ_p δ_v and ν=dv·e^v j/(j+v) on [0,1]. The latter measure comes from dx/log x. Write D_j=L sup_{0≤v≤1}|(μ−ν)([0,v])|. By PNT with remainder of any logarithmic power, D_j/L≪_A j^(−A) for each A. On polynomials of degree ≤j use the Lebesgue-orthonormal Legendre basis, ℓ_i, with sup≤√(2j+1) and derivative ≤2j²√(2j+1) by Markov. The matrix M=(∫ℓ_iℓ_l dμ) differs in norm from its analogue for ν by O(j^5 D_j/L) by entrywise partial summation and the size j+1; the latter has floor ≥1/2 by its density. Thus M has floor ≥1/4 for large j. Solve M c=(∫ℓ_i d(ν−μ))_i and put l_p=Σ c_i ℓ_i(log p−j). Partial summation, the above bounds and Cauchy–Schwarz give max|l_p|≪j^6 D_j/L, and the measure with weights 1+l_p has EXACTLY the moments of ν up to degree j. The first blocks can be omitted and, operationally, all those with M singular or max|l_p|>1/2, which are finitely many. One takes l_p=0 on these. Round the positive and negative sums of l_p separately as in 4488, putting b_p=1+e_p. The prefix discrepancies of e_p−l_p have modulus ≤2. The count of changes up to x is ≤2+Σ_{p≤x}|l_p|, hence O(1+Σ_{j≤log x} j^6 D_j). This gives (iii) in the upper direction by PNT and by the classical ceiling π(y)−Li(y)=O_ε(y^(Θ+ε)) when Θ<1 (if Θ=1 the bound is immediate).

Euler continuation. For s in any complex compact set, the error in replacing exp(−sv) by its Taylor polynomial of degree j on [0,1] is O_K(C_K^(j+1)/(j+1)!). The cancellation of moments implies that the difference between Σ(1+l_p)p^(−s) and ∫_A^∞ x^(−s)dx/log x, initially in Re s>1, is entire: the block cost is O_K(exp(C_K j) C_K^(j+1)/(j+1)!), summable. Here A>1 is fixed and any finite discrepancy or integral over a compact set only adds entire terms. The rounding correction Σ(e_p−l_p)p^(−s) is holomorphic in Re s>0 by partial summation. The terms of degree ≥2 of the Euler logarithm converge normally in Re s>1/2: leave b_p=1 up to p>4 so that the small factors do not introduce local singularities. The derivative of the continuous integral plus log(s−1) is (1−A^(1−s))/(s−1), entire. This proves (i). If E(x)=O(x^a) with a<Θ and Θ>1/2, the logarithm of Z/ζ converges locally to a holomorphic function in Re s>max(a,1/2) by absolute convergence over the changed primes, including higher powers. The quotient would be nonzero and would preserve some right zero of ζ there, contradicting (i). This gives the exponent floor in (iii). In fact this floor holds for any model of bounded weights of this type without right zeros and without singularities of its local factors in that strip.

Direct control of the signal. For large t≥1 and n=tR₀²+O(1), the normalization h of 4346 satisfies ∫(1+|y|)exp(2|y|)h(y)dy≪_{R₀}1/√t by the Gaussian envelope around ±√(n/t). Hence ĥ and its first derivative are bounded by C/√t on |Im u|≤2, uniformly in Re u. In block j the function F(v)=(j+v)exp(−(j+v)/2)ĥ(j+v) satisfies |F(v)|≤C(j+2)exp(−j/2)/√t on the disk |v|≤2. Its Taylor polynomial of degree j has remainder ≤C′(j+2)exp(−j/2)2^(−j)/√t on [0,1]. The exact moments of the weights before rounding eliminate the polynomial. The unnormalized masses of both measures are O(e^j/j), and Σ(exp(1/2)/2)^j converges. The total cost is O(1/√t), including the omitted blocks, which are finitely many. Rounding also costs O(1/√t) because u exp(−u/2)ĥ(u) has total variation of that order on u≥log 2. What remains is ∫_{log A}^∞ exp(u/2)ĥ(u)du, which by inversion on the whole line is 2πh(−i/2) minus a tail O(1/√t) on (−∞,log A]. The polar term is o(1/√t) on the given slope. This gives (ii).

Scope. The procedure keeps ordinary primes and completely multiplicative integer coefficients, but changes some weights and does not establish the functional equation of ζ for Z. The comparison is useful because the signal of the model is already controlled, not because the number of changes has been bounded at square-root scale. A ceiling E(x)≪_ε x^(1/2+ε) for this specific rule would be equivalent to HR by (i) and (iii).

### What the adjustment really costs: comparison with the optimum and diagonal at square-root scale

In block j of 4505 let d=j, L=e^j/j, a(v)=(ℓ₀(v),…,ℓ_d(v)) the Lebesgue-orthonormal Legendre vector, T the continuous counting measure dx/log x in the coordinate v, and
    r=∫a(v)dT(v)−Σ_p a(v_p),     V_j=||r||₂² .
Let C_j be the REAL number of integer weights changed in that block by the rule of 4505 and B_j the minimum of Σ_p |l_p| among real corrections that exactly match their d+1 moments before rounding, imposing |l_p|≤1. For all large j,
    √V_j/(j+1) ≤ B_j ≤ Σ_p |l_p of 4505| ≤ C √V_j,     |C_j−Σ_p |l_p of 4505|| ≤2 .
Hence not even an ideal optimizer of the changes within the block can improve the original rule by an exponent of x=e^j. Rounding only preserves a bounded prefix discrepancy; it is not required to preserve the polynomial moments exactly.

Indeed ||a(v)||≤j+1 because |ℓ_i|≤√(2i+1). Thus any solution of r=Σ l_p a(v_p) satisfies the first bound. The raw Gram matrix G=Σ a(v_p)a(v_p)^T has spectrum in [cL,CL] by PNT and the argument of 4505 for the two bounds. Its least-squares solution l_p=a(v_p)^T G⁻¹r has Σ l_p²=r^TG⁻¹r≤V_j/(cL). Since the number of primes in the block is O(L), Cauchy–Schwarz gives the announced upper bound. That solution satisfies |l_p|≤1/2 eventually. The edit count differs from the absolute mass by less than two by subtracting the two sums of integer parts between endpoints. This controls the cost from both sides using data from a single block, without invoking Θ to estimate it.

Split V_j with K(v,w)=a(v)·a(w). It is exactly D_j+U_j, where in this subsection
    D_j=Σ_p K(v_p,v_p)=tr G,
    U_j=Σ_{p≠q}K(v_p,v_q)−2Σ_p∫K(v_p,v)dT(v)+∫∫K(v,w)dT(v)dT(w).
Pairs are counted with order. Unconditionally c e^j≤D_j≤C e^j, because tr G lies between cL(j+1) and CL(j+1). Thus the whole diagonal already has the quadratic size required by the sign. What would suffice is the one-sided ceiling U_j≤C_ε exp((1+ε)j) for each ε>0 and all large j. By the previous comparison and the geometric sum over blocks it would imply E(x)≪_ε x^(1/2+ε), and by 4505 the global sign. Conversely under HR the bound of 4505 and the floor in terms of √V_j give that ceiling for U_j. Always U_j≥−D_j since V_j≥0. The one-sided ceiling for the centered distinct pairs has not been proved. Antecedent: the separation into diagonal and pairs by differences in 4187 concerns another observable and another scale; here the kernel is imposed by the cost of the Euler model of 4505.

### Recurrence of both types of edit in a fixed number of blocks

If there is a right zero, there is a fixed D such that in EACH band e^(J−D)<p≤e^(J+D), J real sufficiently large, the model of 4505 must both remove primes (b_p=0) and add weight to them (b_p=2). For each type separately, the logarithm of the count divided by J has ordinary limit Θ, not only an accumulated upper limit. Thus to prove HR it would suffice to have a sequence of stretches of consecutive blocks, of length tending to infinity and with center J→∞, on which a single type of edit had total count ≤exp((1/2+o(1))J). The existence of such stretches has not been proved.

The recurrence of prime discrepancies in 4044 is an essential antecedent, but its smooth compact detectors are not polynomials and the construction of the model matches only j moments in block j. To transfer them at exponential precision without losing their annihilation of the other zeros, smooth the detector with a Gaussian of variance 100/J. Details: fix σ=Δ/2>0 and use 4044 with any w=b+iγ, b>σ. Let μ_pr be the difference between the prime mass (log p)/√p at log p and the density exp(u/2)du on u≥log 2. Passing from all prime powers to this measure costs O(1) uniformly for a smooth translated test of fixed support and bounded amplitude, by the squares bound of 4044. For H_± of that entry and the phase chosen at J, the discrepancy when translating the center to J+h, for h in a fixed compact set, equals a main term of opposite signs proportional to Re(exp(iα+w(J+h))Q(w)) and an error O_w(exp(σJ)). The supports of H_± stay in [−S,S] with S independent of w once σ is fixed: take the same annihilating g, the division defining q preserves its support, and for g₀ vary only the amplitude of the majorant η with prescribed support. The constants and thresholds do depend on w.

Average in h against the previous Gaussian. The multiplier of the main term is exp(50w²/J)→1. The average outside |h|≤M can be neglected: the absolute mass of a compact test at center J+h is O_w((1+J+|h|)exp((J+h)/2)) for positive center, by Chebyshev, and remains bounded or zero for low centers. Choose, for example, M=40. The tail term is o(1) by the Gaussian exp(−Jh²/200). This gives, for the smoothed non-negative test H_{±,J}, a discrepancy of prescribed sign and modulus ≫_w exp(bJ). One can also restrict the sum and the integral to the union I_J of whole blocks touching [J−S−M,J+S+M], at cost o(1): at distance >S+M from the center only translations with |h|>M enter. The same estimate holds for the weights b_p≤2.

On I_J the model differs from the continuous integral for these tests only by o(1). In block j=J+O(1) approximate F(v)=(j+v)exp(−(j+v)/2)H_{±,J}(j+v−J) by its Taylor polynomial of degree j. On |v|≤2 the modulus of the complex convolution is ≤||H_±||∞ exp(2J/100), by integrating the modulus of the shifted Gaussian. The unnormalized mass per block is O(e^j/j). After cancelling the moments, the cost is O_w(exp(j/2+0.02J)2^(−j))=o(1). The globally rounded weights change the result by O_w(poly(J)exp(−J/2)) via the bounded prefix discrepancy and partial summation (on the axis the derivatives of the smoothed test are bounded by those of the compact test). Sum over the finitely many blocks.

By difference, Σ_{I_J}(1−b_p)(log p)/√p H_{±,J}(log p−J) takes both signs with the indicated margins for the two respective tests. Each test is non-negative, and an individual prime contributes at most O_w(J exp(−J/2)). Therefore ≫_w exp((1/2+b)J)/J primes of each type are needed within the same band with D=S+M+2. Taking b↑Δ and using the accumulated ceiling of 4505 for the upper end gives the announced limit. This locates the arithmetic difficulty inside blocks close to a chosen scale, even when only one of the two signs of the adjustment is counted. The proof does not give a numerical D independent of the spectral hypothesis.

### An average of the same pairs with all small congruences fixed at their real value

In the block X=e^j<n≤eX there is an explicit family of weights F_r(n) between zero and one that reproduces exactly the prime indicator for r=0. For r uniform over a period, the mean at each integer n is exactly 1/log n. If r≡0 is fixed modulo EACH prime up to (log X)² and only the remaining classes are averaged, the energy of the moment vector of 4520, centered at the same continuous measure, satisfies
    E_r ||Σ_n F_r(n) a(log(n/X))−∫a dT||₂² ≤ X^(1+o(1)).
Thus the one-sided ceiling required for the centered pairs holds ON AVERAGE even with all those congruences fixed. The value required in 4520 is one specific shift inside the average. Its pointwise ceiling does not follow. Antecedents: 589 reaches a log² sieve in a different Gevrey test; the index records variances of translations of a calibrated primorial. The use of two cutoffs here makes simultaneously coincide the exact prime count of the block at r=0 and the intensity 1/log n of the adjustment of 4505.

Construction. Take z₁=√(4eX), z₂=X^(3/4), P_i=Π_{p≤z_i}p, V_i=φ(P_i)/P_i. By Mertens V₁ log X→2exp(−γ_E)>1 and V₂ log X→(4/3)exp(−γ_E)<1. Hence for large X a_n=(1/log n−V₂)/(V₁−V₂) belongs to [0,1] and is monotone in the block. Define F_r(n)=a_n 1_{(n+r,P₁)=1}+(1−a_n)1_{(n+r,P₂)=1}. The period is P₂. For |r|≤X/2, every n+r lies between z₂ and z₁² for sufficiently large X, so BOTH indicators are exactly 1_{n+r prime}. For uniform r each has mean V_i. The convex combination calibrates the mean without altering the real value.

Elementary variance bound. For P a product of primes from a finite set, V=φ(P)/P, the expansion of 1_{(k,P)=1}/V in frequencies with denominator d|P has coefficient μ(d)/φ(d) at each reduced fraction a/d (product of the identities at each prime). When translating an interval of N integers, orthogonality gives for its centered count variance ≤C N V² Π_{p|P}(1+p/(p−1)²). Indeed for d>1 the sum over coprime a of |Σ_{k in interval}exp(2πiak/d)|² is O(d²) by the geometric progression bound and, if d>N, it is ≤dN by orthogonality including all a. Always use ≤C dN and sum d/φ(d)². The final product is O(1/V) by factor-by-factor comparison with relative error 1+O(p^(−2)). Hence variance O(NV). Abel summation transfers this bound to any weight with multiplicative cost in quadratic norm at most the supremum plus the total variation of the weight. For each ℓ_i, i≤j, composed with log(n/X) and multiplied by a_n or 1−a_n, that cost is O(j^(5/2)) by Markov and monotonicity of a_n. Without conditioning one obtains O(X j^5) after summing the j+1 coordinates, since V_i≍1/j. Passing from Σ a(log(n/X))/log n to the integral costs only poly(j) by partial summation against the bounded discrepancy between integers and Lebesgue measure.

Conditioning. Put y=j², P_y=Π_{p≤y}p, V_y=φ(P_y)/P_y. At r≡0 mod P_y the small factor equals 1_{(n,P_y)=1} and the remaining factor of each wheel keeps a uniform phase by the Chinese remainder theorem. The conditional mean of F_r(n) is 1_{(n,P_y)=1}/(V_y log n). For the fluctuation around that mean, expand the small factor over d|P_y, d|n. In the progression n=dk the remaining primes are coprime to d. Dividing r by d modulo the remaining period gives a uniform translation in k. Only d≤eX are involved, and any prefix of the block contains O(X/d) multiples. By the variance bound and the triangle inequality in L², the cost of each centered coordinate is
    ≪ poly(j) √X Σ_{d|P_y} d^(−1/2) = poly(j) √X Π_{p≤y}(1+p^(−1/2)).
For the conditional bias, the error of the coprime count against V_y T on a prefix of the integers up to T≤eX is bounded by Σ_{d|P_y}min(1,T/d)≤√(eX)Π_{p≤y}(1+p^(−1/2)). Dividing by V_y and applying Abel summation to ℓ_i/log n gives the same scale up to powers of j. Chebyshev and partial summation give Σ_{p≤j²}p^(−1/2)=O(j/log j), and 1/V_y=O(log j). Squaring and summing the coordinates leaves the declared ceiling. In the expansion of the energy, the diagonal in F_r(n)² is non-negative; hence the centered signed remainder also satisfies that mean ceiling from above.

Limit of the inference. The period of the still-free phases is enormous. Even if a violation at scale X^(1/2+δ) persisted at many integer shifts near zero, the average over the full period does not exclude it. Concretely, for |r|≤X/2 replacing n+r by the prime m preserves the weights except for the change of argument in ℓ_i and the endpoints; the value of the vector differs from that at r=0 in norm O((1+|r|)poly(j)) using only integers and the Legendre derivative. A neighbourhood of length a power of X is still tiny relative to the period. What is pending is an estimate of the remaining phases valid at the arithmetic translation, not the variance over all of them.

### Real phase of the two sieves: the block of large primes has only three functionals not paid at square-root scale

Keep the CRT model and z₁,z₂ of 4547. Split the prime coordinates into S={p≤z₁}, L={z₁<p≤z₂}. Put I_S,I_L for the survival indicators, V_S,V_L for their densities, m(n)=1/log n and a_n for the mixture. Exactly
    F−m = A+B+C,
    A=(m/V_S)(I_S−V_S),   B=(1−a_n)V_S(I_L−V_L),   C=(1−a_n)(I_S−V_S)(I_L−V_L).
Each coordinate refers to n+r. A and B are the conditional biases after fixing only S or only L respectively; C is the interaction under the product mean. At phase r=0 we obtain a pointwise estimate of B for all moments of degree ≤j, not only on average over translations.

Indeed, let P(v) be a polynomial of degree ≤j with L²[0,1] norm one, f(y)=V_S(1−a(y))P(log(y/X)), and a(y) the same continuous formula of 4547. Define
    λ=1−V_L−Σ_{p∈L}1/p,   H(y)=(1−V_L)(1/2−{y})−Σ_{p∈L}(1/2−{y/p}).
Then at the real phase
    Σ_{X<n≤eX} P(log(n/X)) B(n) = λ∫_X^{eX} f(y)dy + H(eX)f(eX)−H(X)f(X) + O(√X poly(j)).
The error is uniform in P. Only a volume term and two boundary evaluations, with explicit arithmetic coefficients, can exceed the requested scale. In particular the block B satisfies the square-root bound at phase zero on a subspace of codimension at most three of the whole moment space, whose dimension is j+1.

Proof. Since z₁²>eX, at phase zero I_L(n)=1−Σ_{p∈L}1_{p|n} exactly. For d=1 or p∈L, Euler–Maclaurin on the multiples of d gives (1/d)∫ f plus the endpoint terms (1/2−{y/d})f(y) evaluated at eX minus X, with remainder O(d(||f′||∞+∫|f″|)). This also follows by integrating by parts the periodic mean-zero function 1/2−{y/d}, whose bounded primitive costs O(d). The conventions at integers correspond to (X,eX]. Legendre and Markov bound ||f′||∞+∫|f″| by poly(j)/X, since V_S and a(y) have the bounds of 4547 and successive derivatives in log(y/X) have polynomial cost. Summing the remainders costs O(poly(j)(1+Σ_{p≤z₂}p)/X)=O(poly(j)√X) given z₂=X^(3/4). This bound estimates the entire dual norm of the remainder. Annihilating the three written functionals eliminates the whole main term for B; it does not automatically eliminate A or C.

The constant part of the bias shows why A, B and C should not be bounded separately without that recentering. Let N=∫_X^{eX}dy/log y, c=2exp(−γ_E)>1, v=2/3. For P=1 the sums of A, B, C at the real phase, divided by N, have limits
    1/c−1,   ((c−1)/(1−v))(1−log(1/v)−v),   minus the sum of the two previous ones.
Both first ones are strictly negative. For A use I_S(n)=1_{n prime} and PNT. For B, V_L→v, Σ_L1/p→log(1/v), (1−a_n)V_S log X→(c−1)/(1−v) uniformly; the boundaries cost O(z₂ poly(j))=o(N). The limit for C follows from the fact that F_0 counts primes and the total sum is o(N) by PNT. Thus freezing either of the two groups first produces a deviation of order X/log X already in the constant moment, which the interaction compensates in the main term. This happens unconditionally and is not evidence of an exterior zero.

How atypical the last step is. With S fixed at phase zero, for L not to eliminate any of the true primes of the block, its coordinate modulo each p∈L must avoid all the classes −q with q a prime of the block. There are ≫X/log X primes and each class contains ≤1+(e−1)X/p integers, so ≫p/log X classes are occupied for each p. CRT independence bounds the probability of that total survival by exp(−c′ X^(3/4)/(log X)²), using PNT to count L. The zero shift realizes exactly that event. This explains the obstacle to estimation by averaging; it does not prevent estimating the signed interaction via its arithmetic.

### A single shift of the blocks eliminates both boundary costs; identity of the interaction

The translation r of the congruences is kept EXACTLY at zero. Instead, choose once θ∈[0,1] to fix the geometric endpoints X=exp(j+θ), j integer. For almost every θ, in all sufficiently large blocks and simultaneously for all polynomial moments of 4563 of norm one, the contribution of the group L at real phase satisfies
    Σ_{X<n≤eX} P(log(n/X)) B(n) = λ∫_X^{eX} f(y)dy + O_{θ,ε}(X^(2/5+ε))
for each ε>0. The volume with its exact arithmetic coefficient is preserved. The proofs of the model of 4505 and of the recurrence of 4535 work in these shifted blocks: the coordinate v stays in [0,1], j=log X+O(1), and only those comparisons and the gapless covering are used. The result is at real prime phase; do not confuse the cutoff parameter θ with the modular translation r.

For the proof fix, for each j, M=exp j, z₁=√(4e²M), z₂=M^(3/5) while θ varies. On the whole range X∈[M,eM] one still has z₁²>eX, and the densities multiplied by log X tend respectively to 2exp(−γ_E)>1 and (5/3)exp(−γ_E)<1. Hence the mixture remains convex and the sieve exact at r=0. The same formulas of 4563 give an Euler–Maclaurin error O(poly(j) M^(1/5)) after the volume and the two endpoints. What remains is to treat H at the endpoints.

Write B₁(y)=1/2−{y}, with any value at its discontinuities for the measure estimate. The frequencies of B₁(y/p) are h/p (h a nonzero integer) with coefficients of modulus 1/(2π|h|). For H=(1−V_L)B₁(y)−Σ_{p∈L} B₁(y/p), group equal frequencies. Non-integer fractions with distinct prime denominators do not coincide. At the integers k≠0 the total coefficient is bounded by (1+Σ_L 1/p)/(2π|k|), and Σ_L 1/p=O(1) by Mertens. The sum of squares of the coefficients is thus O(z₂). Two distinct frequencies are at distance at least z₂^(−2). On a band of Y of length O(M), the quadratic integral is O((M+z₂²)z₂). Elementary justification of the continuous large sieve used here: majorize the indicator by C sinc²((Y−Y₀)/D) with Y₀ the center and D a large constant times (M+z₂²). Its triangular transform vanishes at all nonzero differences of frequencies, and its integral is O(D). Apply first to finite sums; the Fejér truncations of each of the finitely many sawtooth functions are uniformly bounded for fixed j and converge almost everywhere. The same coefficient bound holds for those truncations, also when grouping the integer frequencies.

For Y=X and Y=eX the density of uniform θ is dY/Y, so both quadratic expectations are O((1+z₂²/M)z₂)=O(M^(4/5)). The probability of exceeding M^(2/5+ε) is O(M^(−2ε)), summable over j. Borel–Cantelli and a countable intersection over ε give the claimed simultaneous ceilings; the polynomial factors in j of the evaluations are absorbed into ε. In this way the same θ serves for a complete sequence of blocks, without randomizing any prime.

Audit of the possible shortcut via the interaction. At phase zero I_S=1_{n prime} and I_S I_L=I_S. Hence pointwise
    B+C=(1−a_n)I_S(I_L−V_L)=(1−m(n)/V_S)1_{n prime}.
Adding A recovers exactly 1_{n prime}−m(n). Thus, after estimating B and subtracting its volume, the rest of the interaction contains the same prime count with an explicit weight. An argument that replaces that interaction by the identity and adds A back is circular. The boundary control above does reduce three pending functionals to one for the group L, but it does not provide a new estimate of the original count. Repeating the Bonferroni depth as a pivot was likewise discarded: the index already records that computation with the same threshold in 213-043-A.

### Identity of the divisors: exact diagonalization of the defect and test of Jacobi stability

For the completely multiplicative integer weights b of 4505 (or 4488), Λ_b(p^k)=b_p^k log p. Comparing the true identity Σ_{d|n}Λ(d)=log n with its modelled analogue and keeping only the primes p>X, the defect is
    D_X(n)=Σ_{p>X,k≥1:p^k|n}(b_p^k−1)log p.
Define T_X=Σ_{p>X:b_p≠1}(log p)²/p and V_X=sup_{N≥1}(1/N)Σ_{n≤N}|D_X(n)|². In both constructions T_X is finite. One has V_X=(1+o(1))T_X as X grows (both are zero if there are no edits in the tail). In this mean over the INTEGERS the signs cannot hide each other: the limiting variance splits exactly by primes. For the model without right zeros of 4505, a ceiling V_X≪_ε X^(−1/2+ε) for all ε>0 would be equivalent to the target. Mere convergence to zero is proved, but its rate at square-root scale remains pending.

Proof. By CRT the divisibility indicators by powers of distinct primes are independent for the limiting natural mean, with probabilities 1/p^k. For a large edited p, the term k=1 has coefficient ±log p; the contributions to its second moment with max(k,l)≥2 cost O((log p)²/p²), summing O(Σ_{m≥2}m4^m/p^m). Its mean costs O(log p/p). Hence the limiting variance of D_X is the sum of the variances per prime, equal to T_X(1+O(1/X)). Justification of the infinite limits: for each N one has P_N(d|n)≤1/d. The absolute part of the second moment of distinct primes is bounded uniformly by O((Σ_edit,p>X log p/p)²)=o(T_X) by Cauchy–Schwarz and Σ_edit,p>X 1/p→0. The diagonal is bounded by T_X(1+O(1/X)). These ceilings allow truncating primes and powers in mean quadratic norm and passing to the limit; they also bound the supremum V_X, while the limiting variance is a floor. In 4505 the ceiling of any logarithmic power for E(x) even ensures T_X≪_A(log X)^−A. If E(x)≪_ε x^(1/2+ε), partial summation gives the required ceiling for T_X; conversely, the edits between X and 2X each cost ≥(log X)²/(2X), so the ceiling for V_X implies the same square-root exponent for E by dyadic summation. Apply 4505.

Test of what small defects fail to certify. Fix the SAME exterior β+iΓ of 4488 and delay the start of its changes beyond P₀→∞. The edit count is ≤C_β x^β/log x+O(1) with a constant independent of P₀, by the rounding construction. Consequently the mean square error of the FULL divisor identity, uniformly in N, tends to zero and is O_β(P₀^(β−1)log P₀) for large P₀. Even so the model has the zero fixed exactly at β+iΓ. Nor does it suffice to add a uniform relative control of the theta equation on the whole half-axis together with any fixed number of derivatives.

In detail, let Θ_b(y)=1+2Σ_{n≥1}b(n)exp(−πn²y), and let Θ be the same series with b=1. If h=b*μ, then b=1*h, h(1)=1 and Σ_{n≥2}|h(n)|/n ≪ Σ_edit,p>P₀ 1/p =: ε₀ for large P₀. Indeed h(p^k)=b_p^(k−1)(b_p−1) with the convention at k=1, so the product of the absolute local factors, 1+O(1/p) at the edited primes, suffices. For each fixed k, Σ_{m≥1}|(y∂_y)^k exp(−π(dm)²y)|≤C_k/(d√y) using a decreasing Gaussian majorant after absorbing the polynomial. The convolution gives |(y∂_y)^k(Θ_b−Θ)(y)|≤C_k ε₀/√y. Apply the exact Jacobi identity to Θ, the product rule and the inversion y↦1/y:
    sup_{y>0} |(y∂_y)^k[Θ_b(y)−y^(−1/2)Θ_b(1/y)]|/(1+y^(−1/2)) ≤ C′_k ε₀.
The same family simultaneously satisfies these controls and the divisor one. The example rules out deducing absence of exterior zeros from sufficiently small defects in THESE norms without an additional hypothesis. It does not rule out the use of the exact functional equation nor of norms with more weight at the extreme scales. Antecedent of the Euler implant: 4488; here one additionally checks how much of the factorial identity and of the theta symmetry on the whole real axis the implant preserves.

### Rigidity of local Euler defects when imposing simultaneously exact symmetry and factorial control

Let Z be a real Euler series differing from ζ only at a FINITE set S of primes; the local factors may change in powers of arbitrary order and complete multiplicativity is not required. Suppose that for Re s>1 the logarithm of the quotient Q=Z/ζ has an absolutely convergent expansion Σ_{p∈S,k≥1} c_{p,k}p^(−ks)/k, with real data and normalization at +∞. If the factorial defect
    D(n)=Σ_{p^k|n} c_{p,k} log p
has uniformly bounded mean second moment for n≤N, and Z satisfies the meromorphic functional equation with the same gamma factor, even symmetry and conductor one as ζ, then Z=ζ. Even if a positive change of conductor q is allowed, the same hypotheses force q=1. This does not assert HR: it specifies what kind of modification can survive when the TWO restrictions are used together. Rationality of the modified factors is not presupposed.

Proof. Fix p∈S and restrict to the n with v_p(n)=ν and no other prime of S. Its density is C_p p^(−ν), C_p>0 independent of ν, and D(n)=(log p) Σ_{k≤ν}c_{p,k}. Apply the second-moment ceiling first to finitely many ν and then pass to the limit. One has Σ_ν p^(−ν)|Σ_{k≤ν}c_{p,k}|²<∞; subtracting successive prefixes gives Σ_k |c_{p,k}|²/p^k<∞. By Cauchy–Schwarz with the sequence 1/k and the finiteness of S, the series of log Q is absolutely and uniformly convergent on the closed half-plane Re s≥1/2. It gives a bounded determination of the logarithm, and a continuous non-vanishing quotient, also on the boundary. At the regular points of the line where ζ does not vanish, the functional equation of both objects gives Q(1/2+it)/Q(1/2−it)=q^(−it); by continuity it holds on the whole line. The difference of the two logarithms plus it log q is a continuous integer multiple of 2πi and is zero at t=0. By boundedness of the logarithms q=1 follows. With that conductor, the difference of logarithms vanishes identically. Its mean square over [−T,T] tends exactly to 2Σ_{p,k}|c_{p,k}|²/(k²p^k) by orthogonality of the frequencies ±k log p, all distinct by unique factorization, and uniform convergence. Hence each c_{p,k}=0.

Counter-test for exact symmetry alone. Fix a prime p and a checking order K. Choose a large even integer d>K, L=p^(d/2), an integer 2L<A<L²+1, and put y=p^(−ds),
    Q(s)=(1+A y+L² y²)/(1−Ly)²,    Z(s)=ζ(s)Q(s).
The substitution y↦1/(L²y) leaves Q invariant. Z therefore satisfies the same MEROMORPHIC functional equation with conductor one; its series has non-negative integer coefficients that are multiplicative by expansion of the single modified factor. It coincides with ζ at all primes, at their powers up to order K and at any integer not divisible by p^d. However, if r_+=(A+√(A²−4L²))/2, one has L<r_+<L², and at Re s=(log r_+)/(d log p)∈(1/2,1) zeros of the numerator appear at heights (2m+1)π/(d log p). They are not cancelled by the denominator nor by the pole of ζ. The denominator introduces potential poles on the critical line (at s=1/2 there is a genuine pole), so no entire completion is obtained. Nor is there complete multiplicativity. The second moment of the factorial defect is necessarily unbounded by the preceding theorem. Thus this rigidity test does distinguish the example with exact symmetry from the sparse implant of 4488/4600 with factorial control. The latter has infinite edit support; extending the conclusion by mere truncation would require verifying a symmetry that the truncations do not inherit.

### Passage to infinitely many primes without truncating the functional equation

Let Q=Z/ζ as in 4614, now with possibly infinite edit support S, and the local expansion of log Q absolutely convergent in Re s>1. Suppose Q admits a global meromorphic continuation and the exact symmetry Q(s)=Q(1−s) (same gamma and conductor one). Two separate conclusions are obtained.

1. For general local factors, if sup_N N⁻¹Σ_{n≤N}|D(n)|²≤K, then
    Σ_{p,k} |c_{p,k}|²(log p)²/p^k ≤12K.
This requires no density or symmetry hypothesis. If moreover #{p∈S:p≤x}≪(log x)² loglog x for large x, the exact symmetry forces Q=1 even with infinitely many modified primes.
2. For factors (1−b_p p^(−s))⁻¹, b_p∈{0,1,2}, leaving b_p=1 for p≤4, a different condition allows many more edits. If limsup_{x→∞} #{p≤x:b_p≠1}·log x/√x < 2, the same exact symmetry forces Q=1. The constant 2 is a sufficient threshold of this proof, with no claim of optimality or converse. Neither of these two rigidity hypotheses has been proved for the model of 4505 together with the exact functional equation.

Extraction of the energy. Take N random with law P(N=n)=n^(−s)/ζ(s), s>1 real. By partial summation the expectation of |D(N)|² is ≤K, since each prefix sum is ≤K times the length. The valuations of all primes are independent geometric variables. Each contribution f_p(ν)=(log p)Σ_{k≤ν}c_{p,k} is in L² for this s: first restrict to the event that the other valuations are zero, of positive probability under this law. For every finite list of primes, their contributions are independent of each other and of the remaining contribution, which is L² by subtraction. Hence Σ Var(f_p)≤K. In the two-copy identity for each variance keep the pairs with exactly one zero valuation: the floor is (1−p^(−s))² Σ_{ν≥1}p^(−sν)|f_p(ν)|². Letting s↓1 with Fatou gives the sum of weighted squared prefixes ≤4K. By differences of two prefixes, |u−v|²≤2|u|²+2|v|² and 1/p≤1/2, one obtains the 12K. No symmetry has been passed to any truncation.

Continuation for sparse S. With h>0, the auxiliary sum Σ_{p∈S,k≥1}p^(−2hk)/(k log p)² is O(1+log²(1/h)) for small h. In the coordinate v=log p, the count is O(v²log(2+v)); summing by parts the weights v^(−2)exp(−2hv) up to and after v=1/h gives the ceiling, and Σ_k 1/k² is finite. Cauchy–Schwarz with the energy proves absolute convergence of log Q in Re s>1/2. Separating a finite prefix of the energy and making its tail arbitrarily small gives
    sup_t |log Q(1/2+h+it)|=o(log(1/h)).
This bound excludes any meromorphic zero or pole on the line: its nonzero integer order would produce growth at least log(1/h) in the real part of the logarithm under radial approach. Q has no zeros or poles to the right by the exponential, nor to the left by symmetry. It is entire. Near the line one has, for example, |Q(s)|≪|Re s−1/2|^(−1/2) on both sides; outside that strip the series and the symmetry give a uniform bound. The sub-mean-value inequality on disks of fixed radius controls even the axis, because the majorant is locally integrable in area uniformly in the height. Thus Liouville and the limit at +∞ give Q=1.

For the second conclusion, c_{p,k}=b_p^k−1 and the linear term has modulus one per edited prime. The terms k≥2 of the logarithm are uniformly absolutely convergent even on Re s=1/2: they cost O(Σ_{edit}1/p), finite under the postulated ceiling (the first primes were preserved). If the limsup is <C<2, partial summation gives
    Σ_{edit}p^(−1/2−h) ≤ O_C(1)+(1/2+h) C ∫_{x₀}^∞ x^(−1−h) dx/log x
                      ≤ (C/2+o(1))log(1/h).
The coefficient is strictly less than one. All nonzero meromorphic orders on the line are excluded and the previous sub-mean-value argument applies with any exponent between C/2 and 1. This pins down the difference between a cost x^(1/2+o(1)) and a bound with a constant and a logarithm: the former by itself does not give this identity argument.

### Obstruction at the central point for the concrete model of 4505

For that Z there is c>0 such that √h |Z(1/2+h)|→c as h↓0. In particular it is impossible to apply the previous meromorphic rigidity criteria directly to the model, even assuming HR.

Indeed, by the moment construction and the rounding of 4505, the exponential of the degree-one contribution, multiplied by s−1, continues holomorphically and without zeros to Re s>0 (use the entire primitive described there and the holomorphic rounding error). For the squares, Σ_edit 1/p is finite by the unconditional ceiling of 4505 with A=2 and partial summation. Thus the difference between their degree-two logarithms, (1/2)Σ(b_p²−1)p^(−2s), has a finite real limit under radial approach. For k≥3 the series of the logarithm converge absolutely up to the central point because Σp^(−3/2)<∞ and 2/√5<1 for the edited factors. Finally Σ_p p^(−1−2h)=log ζ(1+2h) minus a series with finite limit, by the ordinary Euler product. The result is log|Z(1/2+h)|=(1/2)log(1/h)+constant+o(1). A meromorphic function has integer order. Since ζ(1/2) is finite and nonzero (alternating eta series), Q also has the same obstacle. The comparison by edit distance in the open half-plane remains valid. Any redesign that keeps the degree-one smoothing up to the center and the summable cost Σ_edit 1/p inherits the obstacle with these local factors.

### Separate floors for adding and removing weight, without the hypothesis of an exterior zero

Let A(h),B(h) be the sums of p^(−1/2−h) over b_p=2 and b_p=0 respectively. For any zero of ζ at 1/2+iγ, γ≠0, of multiplicity m, one has
    liminf A(h)/log(1/h) ≥ m/2+1/4,    liminf B(h)/log(1/h) ≥ m/2−1/4
as h↓0, allowing infinity. Consequently the limsup of the respective counts up to x, multiplied by log x/√x, are at least m+1/2 and m−1/2. This fixes a cost floor for the comparison of 4505 even if HR is true.

Justification of the domain: in Re s>1 the difference of the two edit series is log(Z/ζ) minus the correction for powers k≥2. This correction is absolutely convergent up to Re s=1/2 by 4646, since only edited primes appear. The difference therefore admits a local holomorphic continuation along the whole real interval s>1/2: at 1 both simple poles cancel and elsewhere Z/ζ has no real zeros or poles. If the larger abscissa of convergence of the two positive series exceeds 1/2, both abscissae coincide: if they were distinct, the continuation of the difference plus the series with the smaller abscissa would continue the other at its real abscissa, contrary to Landau's theorem. In that case both floors are infinite.

In the remaining case there is absolute convergence to the right of 1/2. At the center 4646 gives A−B=(1/2)log(1/h)+O(1). At height γ, |Z(1/2+h+iγ)| has a finite positive limit: the exponentiated linear term is regular and nonzero by 4505, and in the ordinary quadratic term the modulus is controlled by ζ(1+2iγ), finite and nonzero by the prime number theorem. The remainders converge as in 4646. Thus the real part of the difference of the series twisted by p^(−iγ) equals m log(1/h)+O(1), and is at most A+B. Adding and subtracting the central identity gives the floors. For the counts apply separately the partial summation of 4626: an eventual ceiling C√x/log x gives upper coefficient C/2. The distance at scale x^(1/2+ε) needed for the sign still has no upper bound.

### No fixed constant suffices for the additions at scale √x/log x

For N₊(x)=#{p≤x:b_p=2} of the model of 4505 one has unconditionally limsup N₊(x) log x/√x=+∞. With a right zero 4535 already gives it. It remains to consider HR. The mechanism uses the simultaneous recurrence to the origin of a finite but arbitrary number of phases and the common sign of their coefficient in an autocorrelation.

Fix g real, smooth, non-negative, with positive integral and support in [−1/2,1/2]. Take w=g*(reflected g) and w_H(v)=w(Hv), H≥1. The support is in [−1,1], the maximum is independent of H and the transform is H⁻¹|ĝ(γ/H)|², non-negative. Its sum S_H over all zeros with multiplicities is finite for fixed H and ≥c log H for large H: near frequency zero |ĝ| has a floor and there are ≫H log H zeros up to a small fixed fraction of H. Under HR, for centers J→∞ the explicit formula applied to w_H(u−J) gives for the discrepancy of prime powers with weight Λ(n)/√n against exp(u/2)du the value −Σ_γ exp(iγJ)ŵ_H(γ)+o_H(1). Indeed, integrating the explicit formula for ψ by parts, the pole gives the indicated integral, the trivial zeros give O_H(exp(−J)) and the constant term disappears. The spectral series converges absolutely. Truncate with tail ≤S_H/10 and take J arbitrarily large with all retained phases close to 1 by Dirichlet simultaneous approximation. No rational independence is required. The discrepancy is ≤−S_H/2. Removing composite prime powers only decreases it.

To compare with the moments of the model, first average the test in the translation with the Gaussian of variance 100/J of 4535. The series for the prime powers is multiplied term by term by exp(−50γ²/J), with total error o_H(1) relative to the unsmoothed series by dominated convergence. To justify the formula after averaging, initially restrict the shift to |h|≤40: the error of the trivial zeros is uniform there and discarding the complement costs o_H(1) by the Gaussian estimate of 4535 (also for Λ by Chebyshev). The test stays non-negative. On the whole blocks touching [J−41,J+41] the discrepancy of the model for that test is o_H(1) by the Taylor and rounding argument of 4535; the tails cost o_H(1). Each addition contributes at most C J exp(−J/2), with C independent of H, because the enlarged band and the maximum of w are fixed. Removals decrease the correction. Thus for x=exp(J+42) one has N₊(x) log x/√x ≥ c' log H, with c' independent of H and arbitrarily large centers for each fixed H. Letting H grow afterwards proves the claim. Neither a rate of divergence nor an obstruction to the ceiling x^(1/2+ε) is obtained.

### Compression of the moments via the exponent of the signed discrepancy

For any fixed c>0 it suffices to use d_j=⌈c j/log(j+2)⌉ in the vector r of 4520. If ||r||₂≪_ε exp((1/2+ε)j) for each ε>0, then HR. Conversely HR gives that ceiling by partial summation. Thus the coefficient c can be fixed arbitrarily small before attempting the bound. There is no need to build another Euler model or establish its functional equation.

Proof. Write Δ_j for the signed measure prime count minus dx/log x in the block, in the coordinate v∈[0,1]. With Θ from 4505, its prefix discrepancy has modulus O_η(exp((Θ+η)j)) for each η>0, also when Θ=1 by the trivial ceiling. For s in a compact set K approximate exp(−sv) by its Taylor polynomial P of degree d_j. Both the remainder and its first derivative are bounded by O_K(C_K^(d_j+1)/d_j!)=exp(−cj+o_K(j)). Integrating the remainder BY PARTS against Δ_j gives O_{η,K}(exp((Θ−c+η+o_K(1))j)). This use of the signed mass avoids paying exp(j) and is decisive when Θ is very close to 1/2. The polynomial P has L²[0,1] norm bounded on K, so its integral against Δ_j is O_K(||r||₂) by orthonormality. Multiply by exp(−sj) and sum: the difference between the prime series and the continuous integral (from a fixed block endpoint) has holomorphic continuation to Re s>max(1/2,Θ−c). The derivative of the integral plus log(s−1) is entire as in 4505, and the degrees k≥2 of the Euler logarithm are holomorphic in Re s>1/2. By exponentiation, (s−1)ζ(s) has no zeros in the obtained half-plane. If Θ>1/2 this contradicts the definition of supremum even without a zero of maximal abscissa. In the reverse direction the prefix ceiling under HR and the polynomial bounds in d_j for the Legendre derivatives give the bound on the vector. The diagonal of 4520 for this degree is ≍e^j(d_j+1)/j, and the one-sided ceiling for the distinct pairs of the compressed kernel is still missing. This conclusion does not follow for fixed d_j nor for every degree o(j/log j).

### An Euler model that fools every degree o(j/log j) and vanishes radially at an exterior point

Fix β∈(1/2,1) and any integer sequence d_j≥0 with d_j=o(j/log j). On the ordinary primes themselves there are completely multiplicative weights b_p∈{0,1,2} (on powers, b(p^k)=b_p^k) for which the vector of weighted counting discrepancies of degrees 0,…,d_j against dx/log x is O(poly(j)), but the continuation of their product Z from the right satisfies Z(β+h)→0 as h decreases to zero. It is a radial limit; meromorphic continuation through β is not claimed. This prevents using only those moments and the positive factors to deduce the analytic conclusion of 4670.

Construction in the coordinate v of 4505: n=d_j+1, q_n(v)=(−1)^n P_n(2v−1), with P_n the usual Legendre polynomial. By Rodrigues and integration by parts,
    I_n(s)=∫₀¹ e^(−sv)q_n(v)dv=(s^n/n!)∫₀¹ e^(−sv)[v(1−v)]^n dv.
In particular I_n(β)>0 and 1/I_n(β)=exp(o(j)) by restriction to [1/4,3/4] and n log(n+1)=o(j). Subtract from the continuous counting density in the block the perturbation a_j q_n(v)dv, with a_j=exp(βj)/(j I_n(β)). The resulting density is positive for large j, since |q_n|≤1 and the original density is ≍exp(j)/j. All retained moments remain exact by orthogonality.

Apply the Gram adjustment of 4505 up to degree j with this new target density, omitting a finite prefix. The new fractional correction per prime changes by O(poly(j) a_j/(exp(j)/j))=o(1) by the floor of the normalized Gram matrix and the uniform bounds of the basis. Thus the same prefix rounding produces the allowed weights and each retained moment changes only by O(poly(j)) by Abel and Markov. As in 4505, the error of the prime series against this density is holomorphic in Re s>0: the error before rounding is entire by Taylor up to j and mass O(exp(j)), and that of the rounding converges by Abel.

The additional term in the logarithm of the product is −Σ_j exp(−sj)a_j I_n(s), holomorphic in Re s>β by a_j=exp(βj+o(j)) and |I_n(s)| locally bounded. The degrees k≥2 are regular there and even near β. The exponential of the original density term has only the simple pole of 4505. For h>0 each summand before the minus sign at s=β+h is positive and tends to 1/j as h↓0. Fatou implies divergence to +∞, so the modulus of Z tends to zero. Any prefix of primes can be preserved. The model does not impose the functional equation nor the identity b_p=1 of the original arithmetic. Consequently the obstacle identifies the need for additional data to compress further within this class, without ruling out a lower-degree criterion specific to ζ.

### A single positive weight of fixed formula and a quantile bound per block

In the coordinate v=log p−j of 4505 let F_j(t)=∫ exp(tv)dΔ_j(v), with Δ_j the prime counting measure minus the continuous one of the block. It suffices for HR that, for each ε>0 and all large j, |F_j(t)|≤exp((1/2+ε)j) on a measurable set of t∈[0,1] of measure ≥m_j, with log(1/m_j)=o(log j). The set may vary with j and ε. In particular the median per block suffices; a pointwise bound with constant depending on t for all t in a single set of positive measure and each ε also suffices (by exhaustion in the threshold for j, for fixed ε using a small margin). Under HR the ceiling holds uniformly on [0,1] by partial summation. The weight exp(tv) has a formula independent of the degree and always lies between 1 and e on the real interval.

Elementary propagation proof. On a complex compact set |z|≤R, with R≥1, truncate the series of exp(zv) at D=⌈3j/log(j+2)⌉. The variation of Δ_j is O(exp(j)); by Stirling the resulting polynomial P_j(z) approximates F_j(z) with error ≤exp((−2+o_R(1))j). In the good set choose D+1 ordered real nodes with separation ≥m_j/(3(D+1)): a greedy procedure removes per node an interval of length ≤2m_j/(3(D+1)) and allows all the choices. In Lagrange the denominator of node i has modulus ≥[m_j/(3(D+1))]^D i!(D−i)!, 0≤i≤D. The numerators cost ≤(R+1)^D. Summing with the binomial formula, the total loss is ≤(C_R/m_j)^D=exp(o_R(j)). Thus sup_{|z|≤R}|F_j(z)|≤exp((1/2+ε+o_R(1))j). For any compact subset of Re s>1/2, choose ε smaller than its distance to the boundary. The sum of exp(−sj)F_j(−s) converges normally there and continues the difference between the prime series and its continuous integral. The conclusion follows by exponentiating as in 4670.
