This extrapolation uses the factorial of the exponential in the test variable and does not require prior uniformity in the good parameters. Verifying a single prescribed t is not enough. The pending arithmetic step is to exhibit sufficiently many good real parameters for each block.

### The quantiles of fraction j^(−K) detect exactly the exterior exponent

Fix any K>0. Let q_j be the smallest threshold for which |F_j(t)|≤q_j on a subset of [0,1] of measure at least j^(−K), with F_j from 4688. If Θ>1/2 then limsup j⁻¹ log(1+q_j)=Θ. Under HR that upper limit is ≤1/2. In particular, to close the sign a fraction j^(−100), for example, would suffice. The conclusion is obtained even in the case Θ=1. The smallest threshold exists by continuity from above of the measure.

Let B be the maximal prefix discrepancy of the block; by 4670, B≪_η exp((Θ+η)j). By Abel, for |w|≤r one has |F_j(w)|≤B(1+r)exp(r). This already gives the ceiling of exponent Θ for q_j. Denote its upper exponent by α and suppose α<Θ with Θ>1/2. Choose D=⌈c j/log(j+2)⌉, with c>0 so small that α+Kc<Θ. Choose D+1 nodes from the good set as in 4688. For fixed |z|≤R the interpolant of the EXACT values of F_j at those nodes has modulus ≤q_j(C_R j^K)^D, of upper exponent ≤α+Kc.

Now the remainder is not multiplied by the separation cost of the nodes. If ω(w) is the monic product of its D+1 factors, the remainder is the integral over |w|=D+2 of F_j(w)ω(z)/[2πi(w−z)ω(w)]. It is justified by residues and by continuity at the nodes. For large j |ω(w)|≥(D+1)^(D+1) and |ω(z)|≤(R+1)^(D+1). With the Abel ceiling the remainder costs exp((Θ+η−c+o_R(1))j). Letting η↓0 one obtains an upper exponent on each disk ≤max(α+Kc,Θ−c)<Θ. By the normal sum of 4688 and the degrees ≥2 of the Euler logarithm, there are no zeros to the right of the maximum between 1/2 and that exponent. This contradicts the supremum Θ. The proof links the quantile of a polynomially small fraction with the full exterior abscissa, without yet giving its arithmetic value.

### Quantile of a divisor tail without unknown density term

Use X=e^j and the signed weight W_t(y)=y^t on (1,e], −e⁻¹(y/e)^t on (e,e²], zero outside. Its integral is exactly zero for all t. Define
    H_j(t)=−Σ_{√X<d≤e²X} μ(d) log d Σ_{m≥1} W_t(dm/X).
It suffices to prove |H_j(t)|≤exp((1/2+ε)j) on a fraction j^(−K) of [0,1] per block for a fixed K, for each ε>0 eventually. Conversely HR implies that ceiling (with margin ε) for all parameters. Unlike the average over starting points of 4131, here the cutoff is pointwise in the prefixed logarithmic blocks and the quantile corresponds to the exponent of the weight.

Indeed, by the exact identity Λ=−(μ log)*1 the full observable G_j(t)=Σ_n Λ(n)W_t(n/X) differs from H_j(t) by O(√X log X) uniformly on [0,1]. For each d≤√X the quadrature over the multiples differs from (X/d)∫W_t=0 by at most the total variation of the weight, absolutely bounded. This eliminates even the continuous contribution of the small divisors without estimating Σ μ(d)log d/d.

To justify that subtracting the next band preserves detection, put B_j(z)=Σ_{X<n≤eX}Λ(n)(n/X)^z−X∫₁ᵉ y^z dy. Then G_j=B_j−e⁻¹B_{j+1}. By partial summation and the classical ceiling for ψ(x)−x with exponent Θ+η (trivial if Θ=1), on |z|≤r one has |G_j(z)|≪_η exp((Θ+η)j)(1+r)e^r. If Θ>1/2, apply the interpolation of 4694 to G_j with α=1/2 (arbitrary margin ε); for each fixed disk one obtains a ceiling of exponent λ=max(1/2+Kc,Θ−c)<Θ by choosing c small. By PNT, for each fixed z B_j(z)/e^j→0, uniformly on compact sets by Abel. Telescoping towards infinity recovers B_j=Σ_{k≥0}e^(−k)G_{j+k}, with the same ceiling λ+η<1 uniformly on each compact set. Finally Σ_j exp(−sj)B_j(−s) continues −ζ′/ζ minus the integrated polar term to Re s>λ. There there can be no zero of ζ, a contradiction with Θ. Under HR the prefix bound for ψ and the above quadrature give the converse. The signed tail, whose cofactors m are ≤e²√X, still lacks a sufficient estimate.

### Exact cutoff d≤X with a band-limited additive weight that detects each exterior zero

One can exactly eliminate the whole sum over multiples of each divisor d≤X, at the price of requiring a one-sided ceiling in continuous real X and admitting an infinite tail of cofactors. This differs from the approximate Gevrey cutoff to polylogarithmic cofactors already recorded in the index.

Let B(u)=(1−|u|)_+², T B(u)=B(2u), and W the inverse Fourier transform (2π convention) of b=(1−T)(1−2T)B. Then b(0)=0 and W(0)=∫b=0. W is even, real and O((1+|y|)^(−2)) by two piecewise integrations by parts. Poisson (absolutely convergent series and continuous periodization) gives Σ_{m≥1}W(dm/X)=0 for each d≤X: on the dual side the nonzero arguments fall outside (−1,1), b also vanishes at the endpoints, and both central terms are zero. Thus for X>0 one has exactly
    A(X)=Σ_n Λ(n)W(n/X)=−Σ_{d>X} μ(d)log d Σ_{m≥1} W(dm/X).
The rearrangement is absolute for each X by the quadratic decay. In particular there is no quadrature error below the cutoff.

For 0<Re s<1, the Mellin transform M(s)=∫₀∞W(y)y^(s−1)dy is
    2 Γ(s) cos(πs/2)(2π)^(−s) (1−2^(s−1))(1−2^s) Beta(1−s,3).
It is obtained by inserting exp(−δy) in the cosine integral and letting δ↓0 by domination (u^(−Re s) integrable at the origin). It does not vanish in the open strip. M is holomorphic up to Re s<2 in that region and M(1)=b(0)/2=0 by inversion. For 1<Re s<2 the Mellin transform ∫₀∞ A(X)X^(−s−1)dX is M(s)(−ζ′/ζ)(s); the part X<1 is holomorphic in Re s<2 since A(X)=O(X²).

A ceiling A(X)≤C_ε X^(1/2+ε) for all X≥1 and each ε>0 would suffice; the floor of opposite sign also suffices. Indeed, fix 0<ε<1/2 and apply Landau to the Mellin transform over [1,∞) of C_ε X^(1/2+ε)−A(X)≥0. The preceding continuation is regular at every real s between 1/2+ε and 2, including 1 by M(1)=0, and the integral converges for real s >1 (A(X)=O(X log(2X)) suffices). Its abscissa is therefore ≤1/2+ε. Each exterior zero above that abscissa would give an uncancelled pole. Conversely under HR, Abel with ψ(x)−x and W′(y)=O((1+|y|)^(−2)) (apply the same integration by parts to u b(u)) gives |A(X)|≪_ε X^(1/2+ε), using ∫W=0 over the half-axis. This identity still requires cancellation among d>X: the bound via moduli is O(X log X).

### Finite Möbius sum over integers, with an explicit periodic weight and no cofactors

One can keep the exact cutoff of 4712, sum the lattice in closed form and pay via moduli the whole tail d>N^(5/4). Now use b=P(T)B, P(z)=(1−z)(1−2z)(1−z/2)=Σ_{l=0}³ a_l z^l. The new Mellin transform acquires the factor 1−2^(s−2), without zeros in the critical strip. The two central terms remain zero; moreover P(2)=0 cancels the cusp of b at the origin.

Define B₃(x)=x³−3x²/2+x/2 and
    V(y)=Σ_{l=0}³ a_l 4^l B₃({y/2^l}).
It is odd, 8-periodic, with mean zero and C¹ with bounded derivative. The inverse Fourier transform of B equals 4/u²−4 sin(u)/u³ with u=2πy, by direct integration. On applying P(T) the first term disappears by P(2)=0. Using Σ_{m≥1} sin(2πmx)/m³=(2π³/3) B₃({x}) (Fourier series by integration by parts) one obtains exactly
    Σ_{m≥1} W(my)=−V(y)/(3y³),    y>0.
Poisson still gives V(y)=0 for 0<y≤1. Hence the one-sided criterion of 4712 applies to A(X)=(X³/3)Σ_{d>X}μ(d)(log d)V(d/X)/d³. Cutting at d≤X^(5/4) loses O(√X log(2X)) via moduli. For X≥2 one has |A′(X)|≪log(2X): differentiate the kernel V(y)/y³, zero up to 1 and with derivative O(y^(−3)) afterwards; sum with the factor d/X². The convergence is locally uniform. Consequently it suffices to verify for each integer N≥2 a one-sided ceiling O_ε(N^(1/2+ε)) for the FINITE sum
    (N³/3)Σ_{N<d≤N^(5/4)} μ(d)(log d)V(d/N)/d³.
The integer squares N=k² also suffice, with interpolation cost O(√X log X). For integer N the periodic numerator of the weight depends only on d modulo 8N and is rational. This symmetry belongs to the weight: the sign of μ(d) in opposite classes is not controlled. The use of square samples has antecedents in 4213; the exact elimination of the cofactors and the summation window refer to this specific kernel.

### Exact cancellation of the common logarithm and cost of the entry boundary

Let K(y)=V(y)/(3y³) as in 4726. The identity Σ_d μ(d)K(d/X)=−W(1/X) is exact: substitute K(y)=−Σ_m W(my) and use Σ_{d|n}μ(d)=1_{n=1}. The cubic decay of W at infinity allows the reordering. Since W is even, has bounded derivatives near zero and W(0)=0, the right-hand side is O(X^(−2)). Therefore
    A(X)=Σ_d μ(d)log(d/X)K(d/X)−(log X)W(1/X).
The sum with the centred weight costs O(X) in absolute value, by summing log(y)/y³ over dyadic bands for y>1. The identity gains the factor log X before imposing any hypothesis on signs. Logarithmic centring has antecedents in the quadrature of the phase; here the removed constant is evaluated exactly with inversion over divisors.

Moreover V(y)=−3(y−1)² on [1,2]: on (0,1) the polynomial without fractional parts is identically zero, and on crossing 1 only the term l=0 changes, by B₃(y−1)−B₃(y)=−3(y−1)². Hence |log(y)K(y)|≤(y−1)³ on that interval. In absolute value, N<d≤N+L costs O((L+1)^4/N³) for L≤N, so the stretch of length N^(7/8) already satisfies O(√N). The tail d>N^(5/4) still costs O(√N log N). It therefore suffices to have the one-sided square-root ceiling with margin ε on N+N^(7/8)<d≤N^(5/4), with the centred weight and the same N squares of 4726.

Limit of the centring: even on [3N/2,7N/4], |log(d/N)K(d/N)| has a strictly positive floor. There are ≍N squarefree integers there: summing μ²(n)=Σ_{k²|n}μ(k) gives length/ζ(2)+O(√N). Hence the absolute sum of the centred weight with |μ| is ≍N. To pass from that order to square root, effective cancellation in the signed total is required; removing more terms solely by their size does not suffice if this band is kept.

### Exact extraction of the small prime marks over the whole tail

With K,W of 4726 and each prime p one has
    Σ_{p|d} μ(d)K(d/X)=Σ_{a≥1} W(p^a/X).
Indeed K(y)=−Σ_m W(my), and Σ_{d|n,p|d} μ(d) equals −1 if n is a positive power of p and zero otherwise, by the product over the other primes of n. The sum is absolute for fixed X. Since μ only contributes on squarefree integers, log d can be split exactly as Σ_{p|d} log p. The part marked by p≤X^(5/6), even on integers that also have large factors, costs O(√X log(2X)) in total. For a=1 use W(y)=O(y²) on [0,1] and Chebyshev: X^(−2)Σ_{p≤X^(5/6)}p² log p≪√X. For a≥2, the weighted count of all powers p^a≤u is O(√u log(2u)) by Chebyshev; sum over dyadic bands on both sides of X with |W(y)|≪min(y²,y^(−3)). This proves aggregate cancellation over all d, without a claim per subinterval of d.

Only the mark p>X^(5/6) remains. Cutting d at N^(5/4) for X=N also costs O(√N log N) with these marks, since their positive sum of log p is ≤log d. In the retained interval there is at most one large mark, d=pr, with r≤N^(5/12)<p, so that μ(d)=−μ(r). Thus it suffices to have the one-sided inequality at scale N^(1/2+ε) on N squares for
    −Σ_{r≤N^(5/12)} μ(r) Σ_{p>N^(5/6), N<pr≤N^(5/4)} (log p) K(pr/N).
This separation uses log d before centring; the boundary saving of 4738 does not transfer automatically. The identity per mark is an elementary divisor inversion and in the infinite sum returns the prime powers of 4712. The quantitative content for the finite tail is the explicit range of the unique large factor and of the residual cofactor. There is as yet no square-root ceiling for this bilinear form.

### Cofactor of arbitrarily small exponent with exact detection and fixed weight

Given δ>0 one can fix a single weight, independent of N, so that in the bilinear criterion of 4748 only r≤N^δ appear. To construct it take m≥2 even, B_m(u)=(1−|u|)_+^m, and P_m(z) with simple roots 1, 2^i for odd i between 1 and m−1, and 2^(−i) for those same i (choose constant coefficient one). With T of 4712, let b=P_m(T)B_m, W its inverse Fourier transform and K(y)=−Σ_{k≥1}W(ky).

The root 1 gives b(0)=0. The roots 2^i cancel exactly the odd terms in the polynomial expansion of b near the origin, so that b is smooth there. At the other junction points, the copies of B_m have contact of order m with zero. The m-th derivative of b is of bounded variation, also for u b(u), whence W,W′=O_m(y^(−m−1)) at infinity. The roots 2^(−i) cancel the moments ∫u^(i−1)b(u)du by change of scale. Parity gives the odd ones, hence W(y)=O_m(y^m) at zero. Poisson gives K=0 up to 1 and |K(y)|≪_m y^(−m−1) afterwards. In 0<Re s<1 the Mellin transform of W contains P_m(2^(s−1)) Beta(1−s,m+1) and the same gamma-cosine factor of 4712. No root has modulus strictly between 1/2 and 1. Hence the one-sided equivalence with the sign persists. The passage to N squares also persists by the derivative bound of K obtained by summing k W′(ky).

Set a=1−1/(2(m+1)), b₀=1+1/(2m). By 4748, the marks p≤N^a cost O_m(√N log N): for their first power use N^(−m)Σ_{p≤N^a}p^m log p≪N^(a(m+1)−m)=√N, and for the higher ones the same count of powers. In absolute value, d>N^b₀ costs O_m(N^(m+1−mb₀)log N)=O_m(√N log N). Therefore it suffices to control
    −Σ_{r≤N^(b₀−a)} μ(r) Σ_{p>N^a, N<pr≤N^b₀} (log p) K(pr/N)
from above at scale N^(1/2+ε) on the squares. Here b₀−a=1/(2m)+1/(2(m+1))<δ for m sufficiently large; moreover b₀<2a ensures uniqueness of the marked prime. The case m=2 recovers the two previous cuts. The constants and the weight depend on m. The argument does not authorize m growing with N nor a bounded cofactor. The index includes Gevrey reductions of cofactors for other observables; here a single band-limited weight is kept, with Mellin transform without exterior zeros and the exact inversion by marked prime.

### Two explicit terms for all cofactors without an active lower cut

Fix m and the notation of 4758, R=N^(1−a)≤N^(1/6), Y=N/r. For r≤R the kernel vanishes automatically on p≤N^a. The upper cut pr≤N^b₀ can be extended with aggregate error O_m(√N log N) by the same absolute tail (keep p>N^a when counting the tail; for p≤N^a the kernel is zero). For the complete prime sum one has
    S(Y)=Σ_p(log p)K(p/Y)=C₁Y−C₂√Y+O_{m,η}(Y^(Θ/2+η)+Y^(1/3)log²(2Y)),
    C₁=−∫₀∞W(u)log u du,    C₂=∫₀∞K(v²)dv.

Indeed Σ_n Λ(n)K(n/Y)=−Σ_k(log k)W(k/Y) by Σ_{n|k}Λ(n)=log k, absolutely. The latter sum differs from its integral with the same sign by O_m(log(2Y)), by the variation of W and W(u)log u. The term Y log Y disappears by ∫W=0. To remove the second powers apply Abel to θ(x)−x=O_η(x^(Θ+η)) with weight K(x²/Y). The derivative integrated against x^(Θ+η) costs O_m(Y^((Θ+η)/2)) by the change x=√Y v and the decay of K′ (choose η small); the main integral is C₂√Y. For powers of degree ≥3 the count up to u costs O(u^(1/3)log²(2u)), and the decay of K gives the error by bands. In particular the main term of cofactor 1 is genuine: C₁=−M′(1)≠0 by the simple root of P_m at 1 and the nonzero limit of the cosine-beta product at 1.

In the criterion of 4758 replace the part r≤R by
    −C₁N Σ_{r≤R} μ(r)/r + C₂√N Σ_{r≤R} μ(r)/√r .
Under RH the aggregate error fits in O_ε(N^(1/2+ε)). In the case Θ>1/2 it has exponent strictly smaller than Θ: summing in absolute value one gets at most max(1/2, Θ/2+(1−Θ/2)/6, 1/3+2/18)+η. Thus a one-sided square-root ceiling for the substituted observable on the squares still implies RH: added to the error it would give for A a ceiling of exponent <Θ, one interpolates as in 4726 and Landau contradicts the supremum. It is not claimed that the first explicit term is small in isolation. This evaluation makes visible the balance that the cofactors with active lower cut must compensate.

### Band of intermediate cofactors with the prime centred by its density

In 4758 replace P_m(z) by P_m(z)(1−z)(1−√2 z). The cut K=0 on (0,1], both decay orders and detection in 1/2<Re s<1 are kept: the additional zeros of the Mellin multiplier lie on the verticals 1 and 1/2. The root at 1 is now double, hence C₁=−M′(1)=0. For C₂, applying T in frequency the kernel K(y) becomes K(y/2)/2. Thus the integral of K(v²) is multiplied by 1/√2 under T and the factor 1−√2 T cancels it exactly. By the same change of variable ∫K(v)dv=0 by the factor 1−T.

With R=N^(1−a), U=N^(b₀−a), it suffices to have the one-sided square-root ceiling on squares for the CENTRED sum
    −Σ_{R<r≤U} μ(r) ∫_{N^a<p≤N^b₀/r} K(rp/N) [dθ(p)−dp].
Under RH that ceiling is also obtained. Indeed, the prime part with r≤R can be omitted by 4768: after cancelling the two main terms its error has exponent <Θ if Θ>1/2, and O_ε(N^(1/2+ε)) under RH. To centre the remaining band, first extend the continuous part to all r≥1, p>N^a, without upper cut. By 4738 and Fubini its sum with μ(r) equals −∫_{N^a}^∞W(p/N)dp=O_m(√N) since ∫W=0 and W(y)=O_m(y^m) near zero. Absolute convergence for fixed N follows from the decay of K and the positive lower limit in p. The continuous part r≤R without upper cut is exactly zero, because rN^a/N≤1 and ∫K=0. Trimming rp>N^b₀ in the whole continuous part costs O_m(√N log N): for r≤U integrate the majorant (rp/N)^(−m−1) from N^b₀/r, at cost O_m(√N/r); for r>U integrate from N^a and sum r^(−m−1), at total cost O_m(√N). Thus the aggregate continuous integral subtracted from the intermediate band is already controlled without a zero hypothesis. The final inference by interpolation on squares and Landau is that of 4768. In particular, the term r=1 and the whole continuous density disappear from the criterion; the correlation between μ and the prime error above the moving cut remains open.

### An exterior zero forces simultaneous excursions of Möbius and of primes at two scales

Fix m≥4 even, a of 4758, P=N^a and R=N^(1−a). For each κ>0 and ν>0, if Θ>1/2 there exist arbitrarily large squares N for which SIMULTANEOUSLY
    sup_{R≤u≤R N^κ}|M(u)−M(R)| > R^(Θ−ν),
    sup_{P≤v≤P N^κ}|θ(v)−θ(P)−(v−P)| > P^(Θ−ν).
Here M is the prefix sum of μ. This is equivalent to a joint obstruction: to close the sign it would suffice, for example, to prove that on each large square at least one of the two excursions has a square-root ceiling with margin ε (for every ε and windows with κ>0 as small as needed in terms of ε). The type of small excursion may change with N.

Detail of the localization. Extend the form of 4780 to the full quadrant r>R,p>P at cost O_m(√N log²N) in absolute value: for rp>N^b₀ group by product d in the discrete part, where Σ_{p|d}log p≤log d, and use the computation of 4780 in the continuous part. Write D=y∂_y. For h=0,1,2 one has |D^h K(y)|≪_m y^(−m+1) on y≥1, by the decay of W and its first two derivatives (u^h b(u) has the same piecewise regularity), summing the powers of k in the series of K. In the dyadic box r≍2^i R, p≍2^j P, i,j≥0, double Abel with prefixes from each left endpoint bounds the absolute value by
    C_m (2^(i+j))^(−m+1) · sup|increment of M| · sup|increment of θ−id|.
It includes the boundaries by the same estimate of derivatives up to mixed order, even when shortening either of the two intervals.

Use the classical ceilings M(x), θ(x)−x=O_η(x^(Θ+η)); for M this is Littlewood's theorem on convergence of 1/ζ to the right of the supremum abscissa of zeros, and for Θ=1 the trivial estimate suffices. Outside the rectangle [R,R N^κ]×[P,P N^κ], at least one of 2^i,2^j is ≥N^κ/2. The preceding geometric sum costs O(N^(Θ+η−κ(m−1−Θ−η)/2)) for small η. Inside, if the first excursion is small, all its increments cost ≤2R^(Θ−ν); the other ceiling is O_η((2^jP)^(Θ+η)). The geometric sum costs O(N^(Θ−(1−a)ν+aη)). If the second is small one obtains O(N^(Θ−aν+(1−a)η)). Take η small in terms of κ,ν. If on each large square at least one excursion were small, the whole form would have exponent strictly smaller than Θ. The transfers of 4780 and 4768 and Landau would give the contradiction. It is not proved that the large excursions cannot coincide. The conclusion concerns increments from two prescribed origins linked by RP=N; the points of maximum inside the intervals may be different.

### The cut can be chosen after seeing N, even with both scales equal

For every compact [a₀,a₁]⊂(0,1) and fixed κ,ν>0, the conclusion of 4788 holds under Θ>1/2 on arbitrarily large squares N SIMULTANEOUSLY for all a∈[a₀,a₁], with R=N^(1−a), P=N^a. In particular a=1/2 places both excursions in the same interval with origin √N. An N-dependent cut can be chosen when searching for a small excursion. The proof needs to recover cancellation in μ for the small cofactors when R is large.

Choose a single even m≥4 such that a₁≤1−1/(2(m+1)), with the filter of 4780. Work directly with the infinite quadrant. The inversion Σ_r μ(r)K(rp/N)=−W(p/N) holds for each p, without a coprimality condition or a unique marked prime. By decay of the kernel all sums with p>P are absolutely convergent for fixed N. In A(N) the prime powers of degree ≥2 and the primes ≤P are removed at cost O_m(√N log N), uniformly by 4748 and the order m at zero. The inversion then gives the prime form over all r and p>P. The continuous integral over that quadrant is O_m(√N) as in 4780. For r≤R the weight is zero on p≤P, and its complete integral is zero. Therefore it suffices to control the contribution of small cofactors Σ_{r≤R}μ(r)S(N/r), with S of 4768.

Set β=max(Θ/2,1/3)<Θ. After the double adjustment of 4780 both S(Y) and Y S′(Y) are of order O_η(Y^(β+η)) for Y≥2. For the derivative repeat 4768 with −DK and −DW: the lattice identity is preserved by differentiation, ∫DW and ∫DW log u are zero by parts and the two vanishing moments of W, and ∫(DK)(v²)dv=−(1/2)∫K(v²)dv=0. The derivative bounds used in Abel persist: the first two ordinary derivatives of W decay like y^(−m−1), m≥4, and D loses at most one power. Now summing by parts against M(r)=O_η(r^(Θ+η)) one obtains, including the boundary at R,
    |Σ_{r≤R} μ(r) S(N/r)| ≪_η N^(β+η)R^(Θ−β) ≪ N^(Θ−a₀(Θ−β)+η).
This gives a uniform saving even when R is a large power of N.

The rest is the centred quadrant of 4788. In its double Abel only RP=N and fixed m are used. Outside the rectangle the gain in exponent is uniform in a. Inside, if either excursion fails, one gains at least min(a₀,1−a₁)ν before the O(η) margins. Choose η sufficiently small. If for each large square there were some a with failure, the same A(N), independent of the choice, would have an upper-bound exponent strictly smaller than Θ, contradicting 4712 by interpolation on the squares. Thus one obtains a single N for the continuum of cuts without exchanging a limit with an infinite intersection. The result does not force equal sign nor equal point of maximum for both increments.

### Total variation of the signed balance when moving the cut

Let Q_N(P)=−Σ_{r>N/P} μ(r)∫_{p>P}K(rp/N)(dθ(p)−dp), with the fixed filter of 4801. On any interval P>1 there is an exact formula, including the values at the discontinuities:
    Q_N(P)=∫_{p>P} W(p/N)(dθ(p)−dp) + Σ_{r≤N/P} μ(r)S(N/r).
Inversion over all r gives the first term; for the r that are restored, p≤P does not contribute and the complete continuous integral of K is zero. The same strict convention is used at both cuts. Thus the variations come from a signed integral in one variable and from explicit individual jumps, with no mixed boundary term.

Fix 3/4≤a₀<a₁<1 and m as in 4801. For P∈[N^a₀,N^a₁] the total variation of the first term is O_m(√N), by |W(p/N)|≪(p/N)^m and Chebyshev, including dp. For the staircase of cofactors, the total variation costs at most Σ_{r≤N^(1−a₀)} |S(N/r)|. With β=max(Θ/2,1/3) as in 4801 this is O_η(N^(1−a₀(1−β)+η)). If Θ>1/2, even at a₀=3/4 this exponent before the margin is strictly smaller than Θ: for Θ≤2/3 it is ≤1/2, and for Θ≥2/3 it is ≤1/4+3Θ/8. This bound is for the sum of ALL oscillations over any finite partition, not only for the difference between two chosen balances.

Consequence for the sign of the bilinear balance: given an exterior zero there exist arbitrarily large squares where Q_N(P)>0 for all those cuts, and others where Q_N(P)<0 for all of them. Indeed, by 4712 and the passage to squares each side of A(N) exceeds N^σ in magnitude along some sequence of squares, for each 1/2<σ<Θ (otherwise Landau applied to the bounded side would exclude the zeros with real part >σ). By 4801 the difference at the initial endpoint between A and Q has exponent <Θ; choose σ larger than that exponent and than that of the total variation. Along both sequences the total variation divided by |Q_N(N^a₀)| tends to zero. This rules out seeking a forced sign change of the balance simply by sweeping P in this band. The possibility of directly proving an arithmetic bound at one cut remains open.

### At the symmetric cut, the product kernel has unbounded negative index

At a=1/2 the two normalized variables lie in [1,∞) and the same kernel acts on both sides. For the weight of 4780, given any h≥1 there exist 2h real nodes >1 whose Gram [K(x_i x_j)] has exactly h positive and h negative eigenvalues. Therefore not even correcting the kernel by a fixed number of squares can make it semidefinite on the space of all test measures. The fact concerns the kernel; the two arithmetic measures of 4801 are specific.

Proof. Let L be the degree of the total dilation polynomial (including the two factors of 4780), D=2^L. There is a nonzero odd D-periodic function V_m with K(y)=V_m(y)/y^(m+1) for y>0. Indeed, integrating by parts m+1 times the inverse Fourier transform of b, which is piecewise polynomial of degree m, only the jumps of its m-th derivative at the endpoints ±2^(−l) intervene. There is no jump at 0 by the cancellation of the odd powers. The opposite jumps form sines by parity and m even. The lattice sum giving K produces absolutely convergent sine series with coefficients proportional to k^(−m−1). It cannot vanish identically: Σ_r μ(r)K(ry)=−W(y), with W not identically zero by the Mellin formula. The argument extends the cubic computation of 4726.

Take x_i=D i for 1≤i≤h. Their Gram block is zero, because all products are multiples of D. The functions t↦K(x_i t) are linearly independent on t>1: after multiplying by t^(m+1), their periodic series have first positive frequencies i k₀, where k₀ is the smallest positive Fourier index of V_m with nonzero coefficient (in units of 1/D before dilating). In a relation, the lowest frequency of the smallest i with nonzero coefficient cannot be cancelled. By independence one can choose h nodes t_j>1 with B=[K(x_i t_j)] invertible; otherwise their evaluation vectors would span a proper subspace. The full Gram is [0,B;Bᵀ,C]. By a change of basis B is brought to the identity and by a linear translation of the first variable C is eliminated in the quadratic form, leaving 2u·v. This gives the announced inertia. By continuity, the same inertias are preserved under sufficiently small perturbations of the nodes, also when approximating them by integers divided by √N with N a growing square for fixed h. It is not a counterexample to Weil's sign. It rules out obtaining it from intrinsic positivity of the symmetric kernel, even allowing a defect of fixed rank.

### Common frequency necessary for the two arithmetic tails

At the symmetric cut X=√N define, for real t, the two absolutely convergent tails
    U_X(t)=Σ_{r>X} μ(r)(r/X)^(−2−it),
    V_X(t)=∫_{v>X}(v/X)^(−2−it)(dθ(v)−dv).
If Θ>1/2, for each ε,ν>0 there are arbitrarily large integers X and a SAME frequency |t|≤X^ε for which both magnitudes exceed X^(Θ−ν). The inference uses the product at the same t without conjugation and does not require the two complex phases to coincide. In particular it suffices for RH that, for each arbitrarily small positive ε,ν (or for fixed positive ε and every square-root margin), at every large integer X and each |t|≤X^ε at least one of the two tails satisfies a ceiling X^(1/2+ν). Which one may be chosen depending on t and X.

Proof: fix even m ≥10 in 4801. In the coordinate w=log y the function exp(2w)K(exp w) and its first five derivatives are integrable: it is zero for w≤0, the derivatives at 1 match by the smoothness of the weight (or by the lattice series, normally differentiable up to order five), and at infinity D^jK=O_m(y^(−m−1+j)) for j≤5. Its transform with positive sign H(t) is O((1+|t|)^(−5)). By Fourier inversion and Fubini,
    Q_N(X)=−(1/(2π))∫ H(t) U_X(t)V_X(t) dt .
Here RP=X²=N. Partial summation against the increments from X of 4788 gives, uniformly in t, |U_X(t)|+|V_X(t)|≪_η (1+|t|) X^(Θ+η), taking Θ+η<2. Thus the tail of the integral for |t|>X^ε costs O_η(X^(2Θ+2η−2ε)). If at each interior frequency at least one magnitude is ≤X^(Θ−ν), the interior integral costs O_η(X^(2Θ−ν+η)) because |H(t)|(1+|t|) is integrable. Choose η<min(ε,ν)/2. If such a separation held for every large integer X, Q_N(X) would have exponent in N strictly smaller than Θ. By 4801, A(N) would also have that ceiling on the squares, which contradicts Landau. This excludes that the large arithmetic signals live only at disjoint frequencies under an exterior zero. A bound separating them for the actual arithmetic is missing.

### Almost-logarithmic common frequency without losing the divisor cut

In 4831 one can replace X^ε by T_X=log X (log log X)² for large X, keeping exactly the same two tails U_X,V_X. The convolution of boxes and the absence of zeros off the axis have an antecedent in 2017. Here other lengths and only positive shifts are chosen in order to preserve simultaneously the inversion over lattices and the cut r p≤N.

Let h be the sum of independent uniform variables on [0,l_k], l_k=1/(k log²(k+1)), k≥1. It lies in [0,L] with L=Σl_k<∞. Replace jointly W(y), K(y) of 4831 by their means W(y exp(−h)), K(y exp(−h)). One keeps K(y)=0 for y≤1, the identity K=−Σ_n W(ny), the two cancelled moments of 4780 by change of scale and all the derivative and decay ceilings used in 4801 (constants uniform on [0,L]). The Mellin transform of W is multiplied by J(s)=E exp(sh)=Π_k (exp(l_k s)−1)/(l_k s). The product converges normally, without zero in Re s>0, by Σl_k<∞ and because each factor is nonzero there. Thus Landau and the passage to squares still apply. The representation of 4831 multiplies H(t) by J(2+it); U_X and V_X do not change.

For large |t|, each factor of J(2+it) costs ≤exp(2l_k) min(1,2/(l_k |t|)). For all k≤c|t|/log²(2+|t|) one has l_k |t|≥4 with absolute c sufficiently small. Therefore |J(2+it)|≪exp(−c' |t|/log²(2+|t|)). On |t|>T_X this factor is O(X^(−c'')) for some fixed c''>0 by eventual monotonicity and log T_X∼log log X. The rest of the integral converges with the polynomial majorant of 4831; choose η<c''/4 and η<ν/2. The same argument by contradiction gives the announced range. This provides no arithmetic estimate of the tails in the remaining band.

Limit of the mechanism: a uniform exponential bound exp(−c|t|) for the complete transform of the kernel in the log coordinate would make the function exp(2w)K(exp w) analytic in a strip, by inversion. It vanishes on w<0 and would therefore be identically zero. This obstruction refers to imposing absolute exponential decay together with the exact cut, not to the possibility of improving the range by cancellation in the arithmetic product.

### Transfer of the common frequency to two intervals of integers without twist

Set U_n=U_n(0), V_n=V_n(0) with the tails of 4831. For κ>0 and 0<ν<Θ, if Θ>1/2, there are arbitrarily large integers X such that in [X,2X^(1+κ)] there exist two intervals of integers of length at least c X^(Θ−ν)/log X. On one U_n keeps its sign and |U_n|≥X^(Θ−ν); on the other V_n keeps its sign and |V_n|≥X^(Θ−ν). The intervals may differ. This concerns the complete tails from n and not only the increments of 4788. It has not been proved that they intersect.

For either of the two signed measures dD (Möbius or dθ−dv) write Z_y=y²∫_{(y,∞)} v^(−2)dD(v). Integrating the factor (v/X)^(−it) by parts one obtains the identity
    Z_X(t)=Z_X−it ∫_X^∞ (v/X)^(−2−it) Z_v dv/v.
The Abel ceilings of 4831 give |Z_v|≪_η v^(Θ+η). For |t|≤T_X of 4842 the part beyond X^(1+κ) costs O_η(T_X X^(Θ+η−κ(2−Θ−η))). Apply 4842 with a positive loss ν' smaller than ν/4 and κ(2−Θ)/4, and then η sufficiently small. For each measure, the untwisted maximum on [X,X^(1+κ)] must exceed c X^(Θ−ν')/(1+T_X), because ∫_X^∞(v/X)^(−2)dv/v=1/2. That floor exceeds 4X^(Θ−ν) for large X.

To pass from a real maximum to a discrete interval, between integers there are no arithmetic atoms; the continuous term of the second tail is exactly −v. By differentiation away from the jumps |Z′_v|≪1 using the trivial ceilings |Z_v|≪v by Chebyshev and partial summation. At each integer the jump has absolute value ≤log(2v) for both measures. Thus traversing H consecutive integers costs O((H+1)log(2v)). This gives the announced intervals, extending them to the right if needed. The real data evaluated are explicitly U_n=n²(1/ζ(2)−Σ_{r≤n}μ(r)/r²) and V_n=n²(C−Σ_{p≤n}(log p)/p²)−n with C=Σ_p(log p)/p². What is new compared with the twisted proof is the persistence on integers for these two real approximations; the allowed separation between their intervals remains a loss.

### Number of integers with large real tails in the same band

If Θ>1/2, for every κ>0 and 0<ν<min(Θ,1) there are arbitrarily large integers X such that, on [X/2,X^(1+κ)], at least X^(1−ν) integers satisfy |U_n|>X^(Θ−ν), and at least X^(1−ν) satisfy |V_n|>X^(Θ−ν). These are two separate counts in the same band. κ can be reduced before the proof.

Detail that avoids depending on a peak at the endpoint of the cut: in the representation of 4801 for N=X² use both cuts equal to an integer y∈[X/2,X]. The quadrant r≤y,p≤y still has K(rp/N)=0, so that restoring the r≤y one gets the same S(N/r). All the errors of 4801 are uniform in y and of exponent <2Θ in X (use 1/2 as the cut in exponent and absorb constants). For the formula with U_y(t),V_y(t) of 4831 only the factor (N/y²)^(2+it) appears in the integrand, of modulus ≤16. The filter of 4842 is used. Therefore, if for all large X there were some y with one of the twisted tails uniformly ≪X^(Θ−g) on |t|≤T_X for some fixed g>0, a contradiction would follow by the same integration and Landau.

Suppose that at each large X one of the two counts is smaller than X^(1−ν), and call Z that tail. Choose 0<λ<min(κ,ν/8), and an integer y∈[X/2,X] outside the bad set, which exists by cardinality. On [y,X^(1+λ)] the unit intervals with bad left endpoint have logarithmic measure O(X^(−ν)); a possible boundary interval is absorbed by O(1/X). There |Z_v|≪_η X^((1+λ)(Θ+η)), and on the rest |Z_v|≤X^(Θ−ν)+O(1) by the derivative between integers of 4852. In the Abel integral of 4852 the total mass ≤1/2 of the kernel can be used for this second part. The tail v>X^(1+λ) costs O_η((1+T_X)X^(Θ+η−λ(2−Θ−η))). Including |Z_y|≤X^(Θ−ν), the three contributions give a fixed saving in the exponent relative to Θ for small η, because (1+λ)(Θ+η)−ν<Θ and T_X=X^o(1). This contradicts the previous observation and proves the two counts. The result attributes no common sign nor intersection to the sets; it improves the number of forced integers compared with using only the persistence length of 4852 when Θ<1 and small margins are taken.

### Pairs with large common divisor in the square of the real Möbius tail

For U_n of 4852 expand U_n² in ordered pairs k,l>n with weights μ(k)μ(l)n⁴/(kl)². Given fixed 0<δ<1, the contribution F_n of all pairs with gcd(k,l)>n^δ satisfies, for each ε>0,
    |F_n| ≪_{δ,ε} n^(2Θ−δ(2Θ−1)+ε).
Under RH it is of order at most n^(1+ε); under an exterior zero it saves a power relative to the exponent 2Θ. It is a control of a signed sum of pairs that includes many off-diagonal pairs. The diagonal by itself is O(n) by the sum of k^(−4). The inversion separates common divisors without an independence hypothesis between μ(k) and μ(l).

For D=n^δ use c_d=Σ_{e|d,e>D}μ(d/e), so that Σ_{d|g}c_d=1_{g>D} and c_d=0 for d≤D. Then F_n=Σ_{d>D}c_d B_d², with B_d=Σ_{k>n,d|k}μ(k)(n/k)². The absolute reordering holds since |c_d|≤τ(d) and B_d with μ in absolute value costs O((n/d)²) for d>n. For squarefree d, B_d=μ(d)(n/d)² Σ_{j>n/d,(j,d)=1}μ(j)/j²; if it is not squarefree, B_d=0. The prefix sum of μ(j) with that coprimality is bounded by O_η(y^(Θ+η)d^η) for y≥1: convolve μ with the indicator of integers supported on the primes of d and use the classical ceiling of M. The extra factor is ≤Π_{p|d}(1−p^(−Θ−η))^(−1)≪_η d^η, separating the finitely many small primes. Abel gives |B_d|≪_η d^η(n/d)^(Θ+η) if d≤n (η small). With τ(d)≪_η d^η, summing up to n gives O_ε(n^(2Θ+ε)D^(1−2Θ)) including the logarithm if Θ=1/2. For d>n one gets O_ε(n^(1+ε)). This proves the statement.

Consequence for 4862: if Θ>1/2, choose ν sufficiently small relative to δ(2Θ−1). On the ≥X^(1−ν) integers with large Möbius tail, the remainder of pairs with gcd≤n^δ must be positive and of order ≥X^(2Θ−2ν)/2, taking κ,ε sufficiently small to transfer the ceiling from n to X. Thus the large signal cannot be attributed to repeating a large common divisor. The threshold n^δ still includes pairs with small shared factors and all coprime ones; their signed sum remains open.

### Positive reconstruction from strictly coprime pairs in nearby rectangles

Let f(k)=μ(k)1_{(k,6)=1}, U*(x)=Σ_{k>x} f(k)(x/k)². Define C(x,y)=Σ_{k>x,l>y,(k,l)=1} f(k)f(l)(x/k)²(y/l)². For any fixed δ∈(0,1) it suffices for RH to have the ONE-SIDED ceiling C(x,y)≪_ε(xy)^(1/2+ε) on the rectangles x=n/a, y=n/b with n a large integer and a,b integers ≤n^δ. Here f(k)f(l)=μ(kl)1_{(kl,6)=1} on all admitted pairs. Under RH the ceiling holds even two-sidedly. 2 and 3 are omitted so that the reconstruction converges at every exponent >1/2.

In the two formal variables u,v of a prime p≥5, the independent product has factor (1−u)(1−v) and the coprime one has 1−u−v. Their quotient is 1+uv/(1−u−v), with all coefficients nonnegative. Multiplying these quotients obtain h(a,b)≥0 and the identity
    U*(n)²=Σ_{a,b} h(a,b) C(n/a,n/b).
For σ>1/2, Σ h(a,b)/(ab)^σ is finite: 2·5^(−σ)<1 and the factors differ from 1 by O_σ(p^(−2σ)). The identity is verified on coefficients before summing; at exponent 2 the sums are absolutely convergent and allow imposing the cuts.

To control the omitted rectangles one has uniformly |C(x,y)|≪_η(xy)^(Θ+η) for positive x,y and small η. Indeed insert Σ_{d|k,l} μ(d), apply the bound of 4870 with 6d in the coprimality condition to each sum of multiples (zero if (d,6)>1), and use (x/d)²≤(x/d)^(Θ+η) if x/d≤1. Choose the loss in d arbitrarily small: the product series converges since 2(Θ+η)>1. If Θ>1/2, fix 1/2<σ<Θ. For max(a,b)>n^δ the weight h and ab>n^δ give in total O(n^(2Θ+2η−δ(Θ+η−σ))). The rest, by the one-sided hypothesis and h≥0, costs O_ε(n^(1+2ε)). For small η,ε this forces |U*(n)|≪n^λ with λ<Θ. The bound passes to real x between integers by the factor x². For 1<Re s<2 the Mellin transform over [1,∞) of U*(x) with measure x^(−s−1)dx is (F(s)−F(2))/(2−s), where F(s)=1/[ζ(s)(1−2^(−s))(1−3^(−s))]. By continuation the bound would exclude every zero with real part >max(λ,1/2), a contradiction. This inversion shows why pairs with gcd exactly one with somewhat different cuts and only an upper ceiling suffice; it does not estimate that ceiling.

### A single threshold for coprime pairs by contraction between scales

Fix 1/2<σ<1. Choose finite Y such that q=Π_{p>Y}(1+(p^σ−1)^(−2))−1<1; it exists by 2σ>1. For f(k)=μ(k)1_{p|k ⇒ p>Y}, U(x)=Σ_{k>x} f(k)(x/k)², let C(x) be the square of 4880 restricted to coprime pairs, now with BOTH cuts at x and this new f. If C(n)≤A n^(2σ) for every large integer, then |U(x)|≪x^σ for x≥1. This excludes zeros to the right of σ by the Mellin transform of 4880 with the new finite prefix. Consequently a single family of diagonal sums suffices for each σ↓1/2, with Y fixed in n but dependent on σ. Under RH the converse is verified by the divisor expansion of 4880 with the fixed prefix.

Proof without a zero hypothesis: C(x)=Σ_d μ(d)B_d(x)², where B_d is the tail restricted to multiples of d. For squarefree d with all its primes >Y,
    B_d(x)=μ(d)Σ_{h: p|h ⇒ p|d} U(x/(dh)).
This follows from convolving f with the indicator of numbers supported on d, which removes its Euler factors at those primes. The other d>1 do not contribute. The interchanges are absolute at exponent 2. Set M(X)=sup_{0<t≤X}|U(t)|/t^σ, finite for fixed X because U(t)=O(t²) near zero. Then |B_d(x)|≤M(X)x^σ Π_{p|d}(p^σ−1)^(−1) for x≤X. Isolating d=1 in the diagonal identity and paying for the others in absolute value gives
    |U(x)|² ≤ C(x)+q M(X)² x^(2σ).
The integer one-sided ceiling passes to real x≥1 by C(x)=(x/⌊x⌋)^4 C(⌊x⌋). Adjust the constant on the prefix and on 0<x<1 where C(x)=O(x⁴). Take the supremum up to X and absorb q<1. The final constant is independent of X. An independent check confirmed the convolution identity, the convergence and the absorption step. The control of the pairs that share primes is now paid with a strict fraction of the sought norm itself. The arithmetic ceiling for C(n) remains pending; taking σ=1/2 directly does not give this contraction.

### Growing sieve up to (log N)² with estimates only on a window of scales

Fix 0<c<1. For each large integer N set Y=(log N)². Let C_Y(j) be the diagonal coprime sum of 4890 with that Y. For RH it suffices that for each σ∈(1/2,1) one has C_Y(j)≤A_σ j^(2σ) at all integers N^c≤j≤N, uniformly in N. Under RH the two-sided ceiling with exponent margin also holds. Thus a growing set of primes can be removed without checking this same cut down to small scales. The index contains other uses of the log² primorial in averages over congruences; here the point is to invert the variable sieving in the original tail.

Proof of sufficiency by contradiction. If Θ>1/2, fix 1/2<σ<Θ and small η>0 with Θ+η<2. For 0<x≤N, the original tail U(x) has ceiling O_η(x^(Θ+η)), using Abel and the ceiling of M for x≥1 and the factor x² for x<1. On removing the primes p≤Y the convolution of the integers supported on those primes gives U_Y(x)=Σ_h U(x/h). Hence |U_Y(x)|≪ x^(Θ+η)N^o(1): the cost is Π_{p≤Y}(1−p^(−Θ−η))^(−1). Both this product and Π_{p≤Y}(1+p^(−σ)) are N^o(1), since for any fixed exponent b>1/2 one has Σ_{p≤Y}p^(−b)=o(log N) even summing over all integers ≥2. For x≤2N^c one concludes |U_Y(x)|/x^σ≪N^(c(Θ+η−σ)+o(1)).

Let M_N=sup_{0<x≤N}|U_Y(x)|/x^σ. For 2N^c<x≤N the contraction of 4890 and the ceiling on the integer part give |U_Y(x)|²/x^(2σ)≤16A_σ+q_Y M_N², where q_Y→0. Combining with the initial interval yields M_N≪N^(c(Θ+η−σ)+o(1)). The restoration of the removed primes is exact: U(N)=Σ_{h|Π_{p≤Y}p} μ(h)U_Y(N/h). By the second product above,
    |U(N)| ≪ N^(σ+c(Θ+η−σ)+o(1)).
Since c<1, choosing η small leaves an exponent strictly smaller than Θ, impossible by the Mellin transform of the original tail. For the converse under RH apply the bound for coprime tails of 4870 with the local factors of p≤Y treated by the same product N^o(1), and absorb it in an arbitrary margin in j because j≥N^c. The uniform ceiling over the window still has no unconditional proof. Here one does not pass to a single j per N nor to a cut of size N^α.

### A single diagonal suffices with the growing cut chosen at the integer itself

Let L(t)=(log max(1,⌊t⌋))² and C_Y the coprime diagonal of 4890. For the global sign it suffices to have C_{L(n)}(n)≪_σ n^(2σ) for each 1/2<σ<1 and every large integer. The converse under RH is in 4900. The quantifier over the whole window j∈[N^c,N] is eliminated. The one-sided ceiling of this diagonal has not been proved.

Fix σ and E(Y)=Π_{p≤Y}(1−p^(−σ))⁻¹. On the domain 0<t≤N, L(t)≤Y≤L(N) the supremum of |U_Y(t)|/[t^σ E(Y)] is exactly its supremum D_N over Y=L(t). It is finite for fixed N by the finite prefix of primes and |U_Y(t)|≪t² near zero. Proof by induction on the number of removed primes. If the cut Y removes some additional prime relative to L(t), take p the largest removed. By inversion of the local factor,
    U_p(t)=Σ_{k≥0} U_{p−}(t/p^k)
where p− means removing only the primes smaller than p. Since L(t/p^k)≤L(t)<p, each summand lies in the domain with fewer removed primes. The inductive hypothesis and the geometric series give exactly D_N t^σ E(p−)/(1−p^(−σ))=D_N t^σ E(p). If there is no additional prime, one is in the boundary case. The argument does not require the supremum to be attained.

On the boundary Y=L(t) apply 4890. Now, for each d,h of the formula for B_d, t/(dh) belongs to the domain with this SAME Y. Therefore |B_d(t)|≤D_N E(Y)t^σ Π_{p|d}(p^σ−1)^(−1). The bound on C is only needed on the boundary and passes to large real t by L(t)=L(⌊t⌋). Choose t₀(σ) such that q_{L(t)}≤1/2 for t≥t₀. After dividing by t^(2σ)E(Y)², the diagonal identity bounds the square of the boundary norm by O_σ(1)+D_N²/2. On the prefix t<t₀ the boundary norm is bounded independently of N. Taking the supremum and absorbing gives D_N≪_σ1.

Restore at scale N all the primes p≤L(N) by the identity of 4900, using the complete domain for U_{L(N)}(N/h). One concludes
    |U(N)|≪_σ N^σ E(L(N)) Π_{p≤L(N)}(1+p^(−σ))=N^(σ+o(1)).
By the Mellin transform of the original tail, this excludes zeros with real part >σ. Take all σ↓1/2. The local restoration induction uses only the monotonicity of the cut. The choice log² ensures simultaneously q_{L(t)}→0 and that the two restoration products are subpolynomial.

### Finite criterion on a single block (n,2n] with both factors inside

The index already records in 213-378-A the obstruction to truncating the parity layers in absolute value using reserved primes. For the diagonal of 4910 one can completely avoid truncating layers or estimating an infinite tail: change the linear observable from the start to a block and keep its stability under dilation. Let Y=(log n)². It suffices to have the one-sided ceiling
    Σ_{n<k,l≤2n; (k,l)=1; p|kl ⇒ p>Y} μ(kl) ≤ A_ε n^(1+ε)
for all large integers and each ε>0. It is an unweighted sum, exactly finite. Equivalently, on n²<q≤4n² one sums μ(q) times the number of divisors k of q with n<k≤2n and n<q/k≤2n, removing the q with primes ≤Y. If q is not squarefree its contribution is zero. The ordered pairs are not lost. Under RH the ceiling also holds in absolute value.

Details of the change of observable. Let S_Y(t)=Σ_{t<k≤2t} f_Y(k) and C^I_Y(t) the coprime form on that same interval. For t<1/2 the sum is empty. The two identities of 4890 and 4910 are preserved without scale factors: each condition on k=dhj becomes exactly t/(dh)<j≤2t/(dh). The auxiliary sums are now finite. To extend the assumed ceiling to real t, with n=⌊t⌋ the set gains at most one integer at the upper endpoint; at most O(n) pairs change, all of absolute value ≤1, and L(t)=L(n). The difference is absorbed in t^(2σ) for σ>1/2.

Apply literally the induction with norm |S_Y(t)|/(t^σ E(Y)) of 4910, using the new form C^I. The prefix is bounded by the vanishing for t<1/2. The restoration of primes gives |Σ_{n<k≤2n} μ(k)|≪_σ n^(σ+o(1)); the same bound holds for real t by the endpoint adjustment. Summing over the intervals (x/2^(j+1),x/2^j] one obtains M(x)=O_η(x^(σ+η)) and, by Abel, 1/ζ continues without poles to Re s>σ. The converse under RH is obtained by inserting Σ_{d|k,l}μ(d), estimating each sum over multiples with M and the Euler factors of 4870 and 4900, and summing d^(−2σ+o(1)) with fixed margin. The pending quadratic term confronts in a single block the parity of products of two factors; neither finiteness nor the absence of weights implies that ceiling.

### Real compensation of a layer of semiprimes and sensitivity to their large factors

For Y=(log n)², mark the primes n/Y<p≤1.1n/Y. Every admissible integer of (n,2n] divisible by a mark is pq with Y<q≤2Y prime, since the cofactor is smaller than Y² and larger than 1. The number B of such integers is ≍n/(log n log Y): for the floor use all q between 1.1Y and 1.5Y, with p in the marked band; for the ceiling allow up to 2Y. Both counts use the PNT and the representation is unique. Each has μ(pq)=+1.

The linear sum S of the genuine signs of the whole block is O_A(n/log^A n) for each fixed A. Indeed, in the inversion of 4900, S=Σ_h [M(2n/h)−M(n/h)] with h supported on primes ≤Y. Up to h≤√n use the PNT for M with any logarithmic saving and Σ_h1/h≪log Y by Mertens. For h>√n use the trivial cost O(n/h) up to 2n; the harmonic tail of those h is ≪n^(−1/(2 log Y))Π_{p≤Y}(1−p^(−1+1/log Y))⁻¹. The product is a bounded power of log Y by Σ_{p≤Y}1/p=O(log log Y) and p^(1/log Y)≤e (separate the small primes). The announced ceiling is obtained. Hence the complement of the marked semiprimes has balance −B+O_A(n/log^A n) with the real arithmetic signs. It is an effective compensation at logarithmic precision, still far from square root.

Its effect on the quadratic count can be isolated without assuming cancellation of signs in non-coprime pairs. The number D of admissible pairs with a common prime satisfies D≪n²/[Y(log Y)³]+O(n^(3/2)). For Y<p≤√n, the number of admissible multiples is O(n/(p log Y)): for the cofactor ≤2n/p sieve by primes up to z=c log n, with small fixed c so that their primorial is ≤n^(1/4) by Chebyshev; count whole periods and one additional and use Mertens and log z≍log Y. Sum the squares with Σ_{p>Y}p⁻²≪1/(Y log Y). For p>√n use O(n/p) and sum their squares. Since Y=log² n, D=o(B²). For any choice of signs on the same support, its coprime count differs from the square of the linear balance by at most D.

In particular, keeping the support, multiplying the genuine signs by the completely multiplicative function that is −1 only at the marked primes and +1 at the other primes changes S to S−2B. The new coprime count is (4+o(1))B², larger than n^(1+ε) for each fixed ε smaller than 1. It keeps all signs at the primes of the block itself and at the primes up to n/Y. It is a scale-dependent modification and not a claim about μ. The genuine quadratic balance is o(B²); the compensation between the layer and its complement is proved at that precision. The control of D in absolute value is still too large to deduce the required bound at scale n^(1+ε).

### Only 2 and 3 are removed: coercivity in the average over scales of the coprime diagonal

Set f(k)=μ(k)1_{(k,6)=1}, S(x)=Σ_{x<k≤2x}f(k) and C(x)=Σ_{x<k,l≤2x,(k,l)=1}f(k)f(l). It suffices for RH to have the accumulated ONE-SIDED bound Σ_{n≤X} C(n)≪_ε X^(2+ε) for every ε>0. Under RH even |C(n)|≪_ε n^(1+ε) holds by 4880 applied to blocks. Thus the two removed primes can be fixed, a single threshold used and compensation between scales allowed. The pointwise contraction of 4890 paid in absolute value the cost of all common divisors and did not achieve this for a fixed prefix.

Let b be the abscissa of convergence of ∫_1^∞ S(x)²x^(−2λ)dx/x in the real variable λ; b≤1 by trivial counting. Suppose b>1/2. Set F(t)=exp(−λt)S(exp t), zero for t<−log 2. In the diagonal identity e^(−2λt)C(e^t)=Σ_d μ(d)|A_d F(t)|² only squarefree d coprime to 6 are taken. Here
    A_d g(t)=Σ_{h supported on d}(dh)^(−λ)g(t−log(dh)),   q_d(λ)=Π_{p|d}(p^λ−1)^(−1).
It is obtained by the exact convolution of 4890, which holds equally for blocks. For g∈L² the operator norm is ≤q_d. For λ>1/2 the sum Σ_d q_d(λ)² is finite. By Plancherel and the Euler product, Σ_d μ(d)||A_d g||²≥c(λ)||g||², with
    c(λ)=Π_{p≥5}(1−(p^λ−1)^(−2))>0.
Indeed the quadratic multiplier is Π_{p≥5}(1−|p^(λ+iξ)−1|^(−2)); each factor is positive even at the worst ξ and the product converges uniformly. This floor uses that the first prime is 5.

To use it WITHOUT presupposing F∈L², take w(t)=exp(−η(t−T)_+) and g=wF. If λ+η>b then g∈L². For every shift v=log(dh) the ratio w(t)/w(t−v) lies between exp(−ηv) and 1. By the triangle inequality,
    ||w A_d F−A_d g||₂ ≤ (q_d(λ)−q_d(λ+η))||g||₂.
Both norms compared before subtracting are ≤q_d(λ)||g||₂. The difference between the two signed integrated sums of squares therefore costs ≤2Σ_d q_d(λ)(q_d(λ)−q_d(λ+η)) ||g||². On a compact set of λ around b and contained in (1/2,∞), this constant tends uniformly to zero with η by dominated convergence, and c has a positive floor. Choose η small and λ=b−η/2 in that compact set. One obtains, uniformly in T≥1,
    ∫ w(t)² e^(−2λt) C(e^t)dt ≥ (c(λ)/2)||wF||₂².
All the interchanges with w are justified by Σ q_d²<∞.

The integer accumulated ceiling gives ∫_1^X C(x)dx≪_ε X^(2+ε): between integers the variation is O(x) by the single additional integer at the upper endpoint, and the last partial interval costs O(X²) trivially. Integrate by parts against the positive decreasing weight x^(−2λ−1)w(log x)². The absolute value of its derivative is ≤(2λ+1+2η)x^(−2λ−2); for ε<2λ−1 the resulting upper bound is uniform in T (truncate first and use the same ceiling for the boundary term). The stretch x<1 is bounded. By the preceding floor and monotone convergence as T→∞ one deduces F∈L² at λ<b, a contradiction. Hence b≤1/2.

Finally the Mellin transform ∫₀∞ S(x)x^(−s)dx/x converges absolutely and is holomorphic on Re s>1/2 by Cauchy–Schwarz. On Re s>1 it equals (2^s−1)/[s ζ(s)(1−2^(−s))(1−3^(−s))] by integrating over x∈[k/2,k). It does not cancel an exterior pole. Thus the accumulated ceiling would suffice. The arithmetic estimate of the accumulated sum itself remains open; the proved floor refers to the integrated expression in the logarithmic variable.

### Exact count and cost of requiring an absolute constant in the accumulated sum

On 1≤X≤200000 the quantity A(X)=Σ_{n≤X}C(n) of 4944 was computed exactly, checking C(n) against enumeration of all pairs up to n=85. The first positive accumulated value is A(4)=2 and the first negative one A(118)=−24. The observed maximum of A(X)/X² is 100/289 at X=17, the minimum −633200/1190². A(200000)=4225526972. Reproduce with python3 check_4944_blocks.py 200000. One keeps B_d=Σ_{n<k≤2n,d|k}f(k); changing an integer of weight v=±1 alters C by Σ_{d|k}μ(d)(2vB_d+1). The extremes are only for the finite range.

A uniform bound A(X)≤K X², which these data alone do not decide, would moreover imply that ALL nontrivial zeros are simple. Indeed 4944 already implies RH under that bound. Let λ=1/2+h, h↓0. In Plancherel without taper (integrability was proved in 4944), the floor c(λ) is ≍h: on dividing its product by Π_{p≥5}(1−p^(−2λ)) the quotient and its inverse remain bounded by uniform convergence of the logarithmic errors O(p^(−3λ)) except for a fixed prefix, strictly positive down to λ=1/2. The reference product is comparable to 1/ζ(1+2h)≍h. By partial summation the accumulated ceiling gives ∫ C(x)x^(−2λ−1)dx≤O(1/h), including the error O(x) of the discrete step. Consequently ∫|S(x)|²x^(−2λ−1)dx≪h^(−2). But a critical zero of multiplicity m gives in the Mellin transform of S a pole of that same order, since (2^s−1)/s and the factors at 2,3 do not cancel it. Integrating the squared modulus over |Im s−γ|≤h at Re s=1/2+h one obtains by Plancherel a floor ≫_ρ h^(1−2m). If m≥2 there is a contradiction. Simplicity is not required for the criterion with X^ε. This diagnosis advises against interpreting the observed maximum as support for a universal constant without addressing that additional obligation.

### It suffices to sample the accumulated sum on an almost geometric mesh

Let X_j be a strictly increasing sequence of integers with X_j→∞ and X_{j+1}/X_j→1. For RH it suffices to check A(X_j)≤K_ε X_j^(2+ε) only along that sequence for each ε>0. One can fix X_j=⌊exp(√j)⌋ discarding initial repetitions, which gives O(log² X) checks up to X. A mesh chosen according to the data also works if it satisfies the same hypotheses. The accumulated sum may change sign and is not interpolated by assuming monotonicity.

Proof: in the argument by contradiction of 4944 fix λ,η with stable floor c_*>0 in the integrated inequality, and write G=wF. Besides the floor we have the two-sided mass control
    ∫ w(t)² exp(−2λt)|C(exp t)|dt ≤ B ||G||₂²,    B=Σ_d q_d(λ)²<∞,
by divisor expansion and ||w A_d F||≤q_d||G||. The physical weight v_T(x)=x^(−2λ−1)w(log x)² is decreasing and its logarithmic derivative with respect to log x has absolute value ≤D=2λ+1+2η independently of T. On [X_j,X_{j+1}) replace it by v_T(X_j). After a fixed index the relative difference is ≤(X_{j+1}/X_j)^D−1<c_*/(2B). Integrated against |C|, the loss is absorbed in half of the floor. The prefix costs a constant independent of T.

For the step weight only the continuous primitives P_j=∫_1^{X_j} C(x)dx at the nodes are required; P_j≤O_ε(X_j^(2+ε)) by the integer error O(X_j²) of 4944. Summation by parts up to a node J weights each interior P_j by v_T(X_{j−1})−v_T(X_j)≥0 and leaves the boundary v_T(X_{J−1})P_J. The upper boundary is O(1) if ε<2λ−1; the interior sum is uniformly bounded by a constant by ∫_1^∞ x^(2+ε)x^(−2λ−2)dx, since the ratios are bounded and |v_T′|≤D x^(−2λ−2). J can be taken to infinity by the preceding mass control for fixed T. ||G||₂ is bounded uniformly in T and one concludes as in 4944. Thus, given an exterior zero, even on a prescribed mesh such as this one there must be excesses incompatible with the ceiling for some ε>0. It is still necessary to control infinitely many nodes; checking a finite list does not decide the bound.

### Completely smooth part of the accumulated sum and second moment when keeping all small signs

In the accumulated sum A(X) of 4944 regroup by the squarefree product q=kl. Its multiplicity c_X(q) is nonnegative, vanishes for q>4X² and is ≤X τ(q)≤X^(1+o(1)) uniformly (X integer). Let Y=(log X)². The q with all primes ≤Y contribute O_ε(X^(2+ε)) even in absolute value. Indeed for σ>1/2 the number of such q≤Z is ≤Z^σ Π_{p≤Y}(1+p^(−σ))=Z^σ X^o(1), by the cost of 4900. With Z=4X² and σ arbitrarily close to 1/2 the ceiling follows. This does control a subfamily of the original count without a probabilistic hypothesis.

For each squarefree r with all its primes larger than Y write
    b_X(r)=Σ_{a with primes ≤Y} μ(a)c_X(ar),
with a squarefree (the exclusion of 2,3 is already in c_X). Then A(X)=Σ_r μ(r)b_X(r). Moreover, the deterministic energy of these coefficients satisfies
    Σ_r |b_X(r)|² ≪_ε X^(4+ε).
Indeed by the same absolute count |b_X(r)|≤X^(1+o(1))(4X²/r)^σ X^o(1). Sum r^(−2σ) and choose σ sufficiently close to 1/2. No cancellation in a is postulated. For primes p>Y choose independent Rademacher signs ε_p, a single choice per prime for all blocks n≤X. Keep μ exactly at the primes ≤Y. By orthogonality of the squarefree products, the second moment of the modified accumulated sum is precisely Σ_r |b_X(r)|². Chebyshev gives, for example, probability O_ε(X^(−ε)) of exceeding X^(2+ε) in absolute value (use the energy bound with margin ε). At each X the real case is ε_p=−1 for all p>Y; the probability estimate provides no bound for that choice. F-03 of the index already records random multiplicative models; here the retained deterministic datum is the bound on the smooth sector and on the grouped energy with growing prefix in the concrete coprime accumulated sum.

### The mixed sector with an almost smooth coordinate loses exponent against any exterior zero

In A(X) of 4944 take Y=(log X)², Z=exp(√log X), and call k≤2X exceptional if the product of its prime factors >Y, with multiplicity, is ≤Z. Let A_dos(X) be the real accumulated sum restricted to pairs where NEITHER coordinate is exceptional. One has
    |A(X)−A_dos(X)| ≪_η X^(3/2+Θ+η)
for every η>0. The one-sided ceiling A_dos(X)≪_ε X^(2+ε) suffices for RH and under RH it also holds in absolute value. In comparison with 4980, here even pairs where one coordinate is exceptional and the other has arbitrarily large factors are eliminated. Coprimality is still required and the real weights μ are kept.

Indeed there are at most X^(1/2+η) exceptional integers that can contribute: write k=ar with a smooth squarefree, r≤Z, and use the count of 4980 with exponent σ>1/2 close to 1/2. The additional sum Σ_{r≤Z} r^(−σ) costs X^o(1). For each admissible exceptional k, the sum over l of the block with (l,6k)=1 is O_η(X^(Θ+η)) uniformly: convolve μ with the indicator of numbers supported on 6k and apply Abel or the ceiling of M at both endpoints. The local product Π_{p|6k}(1−p^(−Θ−η))⁻¹ is O_η(k^η), absorbable by readjusting η. Summing first with its REAL sign over l and then in absolute value over k and the ≤X blocks proves the ceiling for one orientation. By symmetry there are two orientations; their intersection costs O_η(X^(2+η)) in absolute value by the same count. This gives the bound for the union.

If Θ>1/2 and the proposed ceiling for A_dos held, the complete accumulated sum would have an exponent γ strictly smaller than 1+2Θ. To make the transfer used precise: the proof of 4944 with ∫_1^X C≪X^γ (raising γ to 2 if needed for discretization) gives b≤max(1/2,(γ−1)/2), since if b exceeded this maximum one can choose λ just below b with 2λ+1>γ in the integration by parts. By the Mellin transform of S, Θ is contradicted. Under RH the estimate of the mixed sector already gives the required budget and 4944 controls the total. In particular, if there is an exterior zero, the signal of exponent 1+2Θ requires on both sides of the pair a part with large primes exceeding Z. This describes where cancellation is needed; the estimate of the mixed sector by itself does not give exponent 2 without information on Θ.

### The conditioned second moment exceeds X⁴ through distinct factorizations

In the exact grouping of 4980 one has for every large X
    Σ_r |b_X(r)|² ≫ X⁴ log X/(log log X)⁴.
Therefore its bound X^(4+ε) cannot be replaced by O(X⁴). The floor already comes from products formed entirely of primes larger than Y=(log X)². It does not assert an excess of the signed Möbius accumulated sum.

Take powers of two A in [X^(1/5),X^(3/10)], and four integers a,b∈[A,1.05A], u,v∈[1.3X/A,1.37X/A], all Y-rough, squarefree and pairwise coprime. The two ordered pairs (au,bv), (av,bu) have the same product q=abuv, and the four coordinates lie between 1.3X and 1.44X. Each pair is counted in ≫X blocks n≤X (for example 0.8X≤n≤0.9X). Here q>X², (q,6)=1 and its whole prime part is >Y, so b_X(q)=c_X(q): every smooth multiplier other than 1 with a contribution would have to be ≥5, and 5q>4X². In the square of the multiplicity each pair of factorizations therefore contributes ≫X² choices of the two blocks. They are not counted twice: the greatest common divisor of the first coordinates recovers a, and then u,v,b are recovered; the band of A is determined by a.

In each interval of scale L used above there are ≫L/log Y Y-rough integers, uniformly. Elementary justification: truncate inclusion-exclusion at an odd integer J close to log log X for a Bonferroni floor. The error of the floors is O((2Y)^(J+1))=X^o(1). In the density terms, the distance to the complete product is at most Σ_{j>J} H^j/j!, with H=Σ_{p≤Y}1/p=O(log log Y), and is o(1/log Y). The product is ≍1/log Y by Mertens. All lengths are ≫X^(1/5). Thus there are ≫X²/(log Y)⁴ rough quadruples per A. Among them, those with a prime square >Y in some coordinate, or a prime >Y shared by two, cost O(X²/Y) even without requiring roughness in the remaining ones: by multiples in intervals of scale L the proportion with p² divisor is O(1/p²) for p²≤O(L), and the proportion for a divisor shared in two independent coordinates is O(1/p²) for p≤O(min(L₁,L₂)). Sum over p>Y. Since 1/Y=o((log Y)^(−4)), the intended floor remains. There are ≫log X disjoint bands. The argument isolates a logarithmic cost of the exact coincidence of products that persists even if the large marks are randomized; it still fits within the margin X^ε of the target.

### Explicit positive main term with a large prime in each coordinate

Let A₁₁(X) be the part of A(X) of 4944 where each of k,l has exactly one prime factor >Y=(log X)². With all other factors and their genuine signs included,
    A₁₁(X) ∼ X³/(3 log²X) · Π_{5≤p≤Y}(1−2/p).
The product over primes is ≍1/log²Y. The complement has the opposite main term, unconditionally. This is an evaluation of the signed balance of that whole class and not only of the prime-prime pairs.

For √X≤n≤X write k=ap, l=bq with a,b squarefree supported on primes between 5 and Y. Cut a,b≤H=exp(√log X). The absolute-value count discarded per block is ≪ n² Σ_{a>H,smooth}1/a: for each a only a≤2n and ≤2n/a prime candidates are possible; the other coordinate has ≤2n possibilities. By Rankin at 1−1/log Y, as in 4934, the harmonic tail is ≪exp(−log H/log Y)(log Y)^O(1), smaller than every inverse power of log X. In the retained stretch p,q>Y automatically. One requires (a,b)=1 and p≠q; the cases p=q cost O(n H²), negligible uniformly. By the PNT with logarithmic error, the count on (n/a,2n/a] is n/(a log n) with relative error O(1/√log X) uniform in a≤H. On multiplying and summing with signs, the error normalized by n²/log²n is O((log Y)²/√log X)=o(1/log²Y), since Σ_{a smooth, squarefree}1/a≪log Y. The main sum extended to all a,b (same Rankin for the tail) is Σ_{(a,b)=1}μ(a)μ(b)/(ab)=Π_{5≤p≤Y}(1−2/p): each small prime is assigned to none or only one of the coordinates. The product is comparable to the square of Mertens' by convergence of the local quotients. The n<√X cost O(X^(3/2)); summing n²/log²n over the rest gives the factor 1/3.

To make the balance of the complement precise, the genuine total satisfies A(X)≪_B X³/log^B X for every fixed B. In C(n)=Σ μ(d) B_d² of 4890 (block and prefix 2,3), the part d>log^(B+2)n costs O(n²/log^(B+2)n) by counting multiples with d≤2n. For smaller d, the sum of μ over the block divided by d and with coprimality to 6d admits O_B((n/d)/log^B n) by the convolution of 4870: up to h≤√(n/d) apply the PNT for M with logarithmic margin; afterwards use Rankin at 1−1/log z with z=6log^(B+2)n for those supported on 6d, as in 4934. Thus the sum of the squares also satisfies the ceiling. Therefore A−A₁₁∼−A₁₁. The cancellation needed at precision X^(2+ε) between those quantities of exponent 3 remains open. Antecedents of semiprime sectors in the index and in 4934; here all small factors of both coordinates enter without truncation and the local constant is determined by coprimality.

### An adaptive macroscopic cut where the class of one prime per coordinate already costs O(X²)

Let D_X(P) be the accumulated balance of the pairs of 4944 where each coordinate contains exactly one prime >P. For each large X there exists P∈[2X/79,X] such that |D_X(P)|≪X² unconditionally. This ceiling is not claimed for the complement, which changes with P. The positive sign of 5010 for P=log²X does not persist for every threshold proportional to X.

For P=αX with fixed α>0, k=ap and l=bq with a,b≤2/α, (ab,6)=1. For large X the large primes do not divide those cofactors; the remaining condition is (a,b)=1, p≠q. The coincidences p=q cost O_α(X²) in the accumulated sum. By the PNT uniform on the intervals contained in [αX,2X] with additive error o_α(X/log X) (subtract prefix counts), and then by Riemann sum,
    D_X(αX)=(X³/log²X)(α³ J(1/α)+o_α(1)),
    J(T)=∫₀ᵀ Σ_{(a,b)=1} f(a)f(b) h_a(t)h_b(t)dt,
    h_a(t)=[2t/a−max(1,t/a)]₊,   f(a)=μ(a)1_{(a,6)=1}.
At α=1 only a=b=1 enters on intervals of positive length, so that J(1)>0. At the other endpoint the rational evaluation gives
    J(79/2)=−185832369345342308549209005727/10861248159799739773499019592.
Reproducible finite verification: divide [0,79/2] into intervals [j/2,(j+1)/2] for j=0,…,78. On each the integrand is a quadratic polynomial: h_a goes from 0 to 2t/a−1 at a/2, and to t/a at a. Therefore Simpson at the two endpoints and the midpoint with weights (1,4,1)/12 is exact; one only has to sum over a,b≤79 with (a,b)=1. The comparison of signs does not depend on the PNT error at a prescribed numerical scale.

When sweeping P between those two endpoints, the arithmetic balance changes only on crossing a prime p. In the union of all blocks there are at most 2X/p≤79 multiples of that prime that can change class. Each appears with ≤2X pairs per orientation in ≤X blocks, so that every jump costs O(X²) with an absolute constant. By the strictly opposite signs for large X, some value of the balance falls within O(X²) of zero. The cut may vary with X and is chosen using only this class. The argument resolves its cancellation at the required precision, not that of the total sum, which is independent of the cut.

### The complete union of coordinates with a prime >P can be removed at cost o(X²)

For each large X there exists a cut P_X∈[2X/79,X/39] such that the accumulated sum A(X) differs by O(X²/log X) from the same count with ALL primes of both coordinates ≤P_X. The selection uses the first sign inversion of the contribution of the union when sweeping that interval. It may not coincide with the cut of 5020 that controls the intersection.

Let B_X(P) be the contribution of the pairs with the first coordinate marked by a prime >P and the second without additional restriction; the union has balance U_X(P)=2B_X(P)−D_X(P). Uniformly in that band, each marked k is ap with a≤79. For the sum over l of the block with (l,6k)=1, it suffices to start from the ceiling O_A(X/log^A X) for μ with coprimality to 6a (only finitely many a) and remove ≤79 multiples of p. The active blocks have n≥X/79. In all blocks there are O(X) choices of k per block, hence B_X(P)≪_A X³/log^A X. In particular at the endpoints U has main term opposite to D. For the upper endpoint, the same exact Simpson of 5020 gives J(39)=178760612650219967799520779983/81459361198498048301242646940>0; the lower endpoint uses J(79/2)<0.

Each jump of B costs O_A(X²/log^A X) by the same row ceiling and the ≤79 multiples that change. For D, each row that changes only sees other marked coordinates: in the union of blocks there are ≤79π(2X)=O(X/log X). There are two orientations and ≤X blocks, so that the jump of D, and therefore that of U, costs O(X²/log X). The opposite signs force a cut with |U| within that limit. Even for the strengthened bound at scale X² the difference is asymptotically negligible. The cut is defined from U and does not presuppose a bound on the total A. The remaining arithmetic is still a signed count of uncontrolled size; nor can P_X be replaced by one of the endpoints in the conclusion.

### Monotone jumps prime by prime and distance between two crossings

Write F_X(P)=A(X)−U_X(P), the balance of the pairs with both coordinates without a prime >P. On I=[2X/79,X/39] and for every sufficiently large X, each jump on crossing a prime p makes U DECREASE and F INCREASE by an amount between cX²/log X and CX²/log X, with positive absolute constants. Both cross zero by strict opposite signs at the endpoints: for F also use the ceiling O_B(X³/log^B X) of 5010. Order the primes of I after the left endpoint and call i_U the first index with U≤0 and i_F the first with F≥0. The one-sided bound of 4944 is equivalent to
    (i_U−i_F)_+ ≪_ε X^ε    for each ε>0.
It is not required to bound the reverse order nor the physical length of the intervals between primes.

Justification of the individual jump, which is not deduced by differentiating a discrete asymptotic: let H_b(s,α)=[2s/b−max(α,s/b)]₊, s=n/X, and G(α)=∫₀¹ Σ_{(a,b)=1} f(a)f(b) H_a(s,α)H_b(s,α)ds=α³J(1/α). When p is removed from the marked set, the affected first coordinates are ap with s<a p/X≤2s. In each row the other prime must exceed p (including p on both sides would produce a non-coprime pair). Its count with cofactor b is X H_b(s,p/X)/log X+o(X/log X) uniformly in n,p,b by the additive PNT on [2X/79,2X]. The sum is finite in a,b≤79. Removing those rows and their transposes one obtains
    Δ_p D_X=(X²/log X)(G′(p/X)+o(1)).
Indeed G′ is −2 times the integral with H_a replaced by the indicator of the affected row; the boundary equalities are null in the integral. The passage from sum to integral is uniform by bounded variation in s, including the two moving boundaries. The same estimate with the second coordinate unmarked gives Δ_p B_X=O_B(X²/log^B X) by 5034. The two orientations removed in D are disjoint on coprime pairs.

Floor of the derivative: G′(α)=α²(3J(T)−TJ′(T)), T=1/α. On [39,79/2], J′ is quadratic. Its three Bernstein coefficients, obtained by evaluating the sum of 5020 at 39,157/4,79/2 with values u,v,w and taking u,2v−(u+w)/2,w, are all strictly between −40 and −37 by rational arithmetic. Hence J decreases and J≥J(79/2)>−18; therefore 3J−TJ′>39·37−54>0. The upper bound is finite by compactness. For U=2B−D this gives the two asserted ceilings of the jump.

After the crossing of U its value lies between −CX²/log X and zero, and after that of F between zero and CX²/log X. Summing the differences between the two indices shows that A(X)_+ lies between (c(i_U−i_F)_+−C)X²/log X and C(1+(i_U−i_F)_+)X²/log X, enlarging constants. This proves the equivalence, absorbing log X in an arbitrary margin ε. The two statistics have distinct arithmetic definitions (pairs entirely unmarked, pairs with at least one mark), but their jumps are exactly opposite because the sum is A(X). The proved monotonicity does not establish arithmetic proximity of the crossings.

In both directions the offset already satisfies |i_U−i_F|≪_B 1+X/log^B X for each fixed B: sum the jumps with floor in the corresponding order and apply |A(X)|≪_{B+1}X³/log^(B+1)X. It is a saving over the ≍X/log X positions of the band, not yet reaching X^ε.

### The cubic profile of the macroscopic cuts by itself preserves the whole global problem

The J(T) evaluated in 5020 satisfies the equivalence RH ⇔ J(T)≪_ε T^(2+ε) one-sidedly for every ε>0. If Θ>1/2 then limsup log(1+max(0,J(T)))/log T=1+2Θ. Therefore evaluating more cubic stretches does describe new fixed cuts, but postulating that the profile has quadratic growth with margin already requires the same global information. This equivalence does not use uniformity in α when taking X→∞ in 5020.

Let f be as in 4944, S(t)=Σ_{t<a≤2t} f(a) and H(t)=Σ_a f(a) h_a(t). The identity h_a(t)=∫₁∞ 1_{t<au≤2t}du gives H(t)=t∫₀ᵗ S(v)dv/v². Its Mellin transform on Re s>1 is (2^s−1)/[s(s−1)ζ(s)(1−2^(−s))(1−3^(−s))], by Fubini. The factor 1/(s−1) is exactly the effect of the continuous profile; at 1 the singularity is removable. For Θ<1 the moment ∫₀∞ S(v)dv/v² is zero by continuity from the right of the Mellin transform of S and its zero at 1, using S(v)≪_η v^(Θ+η). Thus H(t)=−t∫ₜ∞ S(v)dv/v²=O_η(t^(Θ+η)). If Θ=1 the trivial bound O(t log(2t)) for t≥1 suffices. H vanishes up to t=1/2.

For h_a(t)=h_1(t/a) the same divisor expansion of 4944 gives, exactly, e^(−2λw)J′(e^w)=Σ_d μ(d)|A_d F(w)|² with F(w)=e^(−λw)H(e^w) and the same A_d. Each sum is finite before integrating because it vanishes below 1/2. By the ceiling of H and the sum of q_d(λ)² one obtains |J′(t)|≪_η t^(2Θ+η) (use exponent Θ+η/2 for each tail). In particular RH gives the sought ceiling. Conversely, if J(T)≤O(T^γ) with γ≥2, the argument of 4944 with the same weight and the same floor bounds the quadratic abscissa of H by max(1/2,(γ−1)/2): now the continuous primitive is exactly J, without discretization error. By Cauchy–Schwarz its Mellin transform is holomorphic to the right of that abscissa. No exterior zero is cancelled in the formula for H, so γ<1+2Θ is impossible if Θ>1/2. This also proves the positive-exponent claim. It does not prove that J again takes negative values at arbitrary heights nor does it allow exchanging the limits X→∞ and T→∞.

### A positive sum at each scale by dilations in the common divisor

Let c be completely multiplicative with c(2)=c(3)=1 and c(p)=4 for p≥5. For any finite real family v_i the matrix
    L(i,j)=c(g) f(i/g) f(j/g),   g=gcd(i,j),   f=μ 1_{(·,6)=1}
is positive semidefinite. Therefore K_+(T)=Σ_{d≤2T} c(d)J′(T/d)≥0 for each T, although J′ changes sign. Its primitive
    B(T)=Σ_{d≤2T} d c(d) J(T/d)
is nonnegative and monotone. The ceiling B(2^j)≪_ε (2^j)^(2+ε) for every large integer j and every ε>0 is equivalent to the global sign.

Pointwise proof. On expanding the filter over d in the coprime form of 5020, the new indices are i=da,j=db. By (a,b)=1 only d=gcd(i,j) contributes, exactly L. Divide row i and column j by √c(i),√c(j). In the two valuations at a prime p≥5, the local factor is 1 if they coincide, −1/2 if they differ by one and 0 otherwise. This is the Gram of the vectors (e_v−e_{v+1})/√2 in an orthonormal basis. For 2,3 the factor is the identity on valuations. The product of the factors is the Gram of their tensor products (the primes dividing some index suffice). It is applied with v_i=h_i(T), with support i≤2T, and also holds for the block indicator of 4944. The 4 is minimal in this uniform family: if 0<c(p)<4 is used for some p≥5, the submatrix on consecutive powers of that prime has normalized minimal eigenvalue 1−2 cos(π/(k+1))/√c(p)<0 for large size k. The positivity obtained is that of the transformed sum; by itself it does not establish its ceiling.

Transfer of growth. J and B vanish for T≤1/2. For each ε>0, Σ c(d)/d^(1+ε)<∞ by Euler product (4<5 and Σ_p p^(−1−ε)<∞). A one-sided ceiling of J with exponent 2+ε transfers to B by positivity of the dilation weights. Conversely,
    J(T)=Σ_{d≤2T} μ(d)d c(d) B(T/d)
by finite inversion over divisors. Since B≥0, an upper ceiling of B is an absolute ceiling, and the same majorant series transfers it to |J|. Monotonicity allows checking that ceiling only at powers of two by comparison with the next one. Apply 5058. In the original profile J, checking signed values on a mesh did not give this direct interpolation. Here an equivalent monotone object is constructed; its growth between scales remains the pending arithmetic inequality.

### Explicit squares and a band of exact size T² log²T

For the B of 5066 there is a decomposition with one square per integer d:
    B′(t)=Σ_{d≤2t} a(d) [Σ_k f(k) h_1(t/(dk)) Π_{p|k} 2(v_p(d)+1)/(v_p(d)+2)]².
Here a is multiplicative, a(2^j)=a(3^j)=1 and a(p^j)=4^j(j+2)/(2(j+1)) for p≥5. The correction factor differs from 1 only if p|d. In particular d=1 recovers exactly H(t)² of 5058. To verify the formula, the lower Cholesky factor of the normalized local matrix of 5066 is bidiagonal. In row j the diagonal is √((j+2)/(2(j+1))) and the subdiagonal −√(j/(2(j+1))); this is checked by multiplication, omitting the subdiagonal at j=0. Restore the row factor 2^j. The ratio between the entry of row j+1 and the diagonal of row j in column j is −2(j+1)/(j+2). The factors at 2,3 are identities. Multiplying the factorizations and summing by columns gives the statement on finite support.

After integrating in t from 0 to T, the contribution of ALL the squares with T/2≤d≤2T is ≍T²(log T)² unconditionally. For those d one has k≤2T/d≤4, so f forces k=1. Each integral is ≤O(T); for T/2≤d≤3T/4 it is ≥cT, for example integrating t between 0.8T and T, where h_1(t/d)=t/d. Therefore it suffices to estimate the mean of a.

Write a=1*g by Dirichlet convolution. One has g≥0 since a(p^j) increases for p≥5, g(p)=2 for those primes, and g(p^j)=0 for p=2,3 and j≥1. The sum of a up to 2T costs ≤2T Π_{p≤2T}(1+Σ_{j≥1}g(p^j)/p^j)≪T(log T)². The factors of degree ≥2 cost O(p^(−2)) uniformly for p≥5 by 4/5<1. For the floor on [T/2,3T/4] retain divisors e≤√T in the convolution, each with ≫T/e multiples. Their mass Σ g(e)/e is ≫log²T: restrict to squarefree e supported on 5≤p≤T^δ, with small fixed δ. The mass without the ceiling e≤√T is Π(1+2/p)≍_δ log²T, and the weighted mean of log e is Σ 2log p/(p+2)≤Cδ log T. By Markov at least half of the mass stays below √T on choosing δ sufficiently small.

Consequently B(T)≪T² is impossible for this positive object, even under RH. The evaluated band does fit in T^(2+ε); for the target one only needs to control the remaining positive sum d<T/2. The floor of this entry corresponds to B and does not transfer as a floor of J, whose inversion has signs.

### Prime-adapted pivots: all squares d≥T^(2/3) fit in the budget

A NEW positive primitive B_*(T) is constructed, also equivalent to the sign through its ceiling T^(2+ε). For it the band T/2≤d≤2T has exponent 3/2 instead of 2 and the whole tail d≥T^(2/3) costs O_ε(T^(2+ε)) without hypothesis. The previous B keeps its floor of 5080.
