In this construction only the primes ≤16 are removed from f. The arguments of 5058 are preserved under this finite change (the Mellin transform only changes by factors invertible on Re s>0).

The weight c is multiplicative across distinct primes; complete multiplicativity is no longer required. For p≤16 set c(p^j)=1. For p≥17 let r=r_p be the smaller root of r(1−r)=1/√p and, for j≥1, set c_j=c(p^j)=p^((j−1)/2)/(1−r), c₀=1. The local factor of the raw kernel of 5066 has diagonal c_j and subdiagonal −c_{j−1}. Its pivots satisfy a₀=1, a_j=c_j−c_{j−1}²/a_{j−1}=r c_j for j≥1: for j=1 it is c₁−1 and the subsequent recurrence uses exactly the equation of r. At the excluded primes the factor is the identity and the pivots equal one. All are positive. If a is the multiplicative extension of the pivots, one has
    Σ_d a(d)d^(−1/2−ε)<∞,     Σ_d c(d)d^(−1−ε)<∞.
Indeed r≍p^(−1/2); for the first series, summing all powers of p costs O_ε(p^(−1−ε)/(1−p^(−ε))) apart from the term 1. For the second the first power costs O(p^(−1−ε)) and the following ones form a geometric series of ratio p^(−1/2−ε).

Define B_* as in 5066 with this c and the new f. Do not use the inverse μc from there. Under RH the direct transfer of the ceiling for J suffices by the second series. In the opposite direction, the Cholesky column d=1 is exactly H(t) of 5058 with the new f: at each allowed prime the first raw subdiagonal is −1 and the first pivot 1. Hence ∫₀ᵀ |H|²≤B_*(T). A ceiling T^(2+ε) for all ε implies by dyadic summation that ∫ |H(t)|² t^(−2λ−1)dt is finite for λ>1/2; its Mellin transform excludes the exterior zeros. B_* is monotone by the sum of squares.

In the general column d, after extracting √a(d), the ratio for adding a prime p to k is −1 if p does not divide d, and −c_j/a_j=−1/r_p if j=v_p(d)≥1. Therefore in absolute value the interior summand at scale y=t/d is bounded by
    Σ_{k≤2y} (y/k) Π_{p|gcd(k,d), p≥17} (1/r_p)
    ≪ y log(2+2y) Π_{p|d,p≥17}(1+C/√p) ≪_η y log(2+2y) d^η.
Here h₁(y/k)≤y/k; for the first ceiling expand the factors as 1+(1/r_p−1)1_{p|k} and sum the multiples with weight 1/k. Consequently the integrated contribution of d≥D is O_ε(T^(3+ε) D^(−3/2)) for 1≤D≤2T, absorbing the margins with the first series of pivots. For D=T^(2/3) it already suffices. More precisely, on T/2≤d≤2T only k=1 survives; the cost lies between cT^(3/2)/log T and O_ε(T^(3/2+ε)), by the primes T/2≤d≤3T/4 for the floor and by the sum of pivots for the ceiling. The estimate of the squares with d<T^(2/3), including the column d=1, is missing.

### Domination at critical scale by the first column, without loss in T

Let E(V)=sup_{0<u≤V} u^(−2)∫₀ᵘ |H(t)|²dt for the first column of 5092. For 1≤D≤2T, if B_{*,≥D}(T) denotes the contribution of all columns with d≥D, then for any 0<δ<1/2
    B_{*,≥D}(T) ≤ C_δ T² D^(−1/2+δ) E(T/D).
Therefore E(T)≤sup_{0<u≤T} B_*(u)/u²≤C E(T) with an absolute constant (fix δ=1/4). The comparison is unconditional, uniform over finite horizons, and includes the critical exponent without a factor T^ε.

Indeed the interior column H_d(y) (before the factor √a(d)) has at each p≥17 dividing d the local polynomial 1−z/r_p versus 1−z in H. Dividing formally gives 1+(1−1/r_p)Σ_{j≥1}z^j. Thus H_d(y)=Σ_h g_d(h) H(y/h), with g_d multiplicative supported on the allowed primes dividing d and g_d(p^j)=1−1/r_p for j≥1 at those primes. The identity is finite for fixed y by the support of H. Its cost in norm at exponent 1/2 is
    L_d=Σ_h |g_d(h)|/√h=Π_{p|d,p≥17}(1+(1/r_p−1)/(√p−1)) ≪_η d^η.
Each factor is uniformly bounded because r_p(1−r_p)=1/√p. The final inequality again separates the small primes for each η.

Changing variable t=dhv gives ||H(t/(dh))||_{L²(0,T)}≤T (dh)^(−1/2) E(T/d)^(1/2). Minkowski and the preceding identity bound the energy of the column by T² E(T/d) a(d)L_d²/d. For d≥D extract E(T/D) and use Σ a(d)d^(−1/2−η)<∞ of 5092, taking the losses η sufficiently small relative to δ. This gives the inequality. In particular, if T is a horizon where ∫₀ᵀ H²/T²≥E(T)/2, the fraction of B_* coming from d≥D is ≤2C_δ D^(−1/2+δ), independently of T. The equivalence by envelopes does not give a numerical ceiling for E(T); it prevents attributing an additional growth in exponent or logarithms to the sum of columns by itself.

### Exact, positive deficit of order log⁵ in the sum of dilations of the first column

With H of 5092 and c₀=Π_{p≤16}(1−1/p)⁻¹ one has for every x>0
    c₀x−Σ_{m≥1}H(x/m)=Σ_{b supported on 3,5,7,11,13} min(1,2x/b).
The left-hand side, even including H with sign, is nonnegative, increasing and concave. As x grows its value is
    (log(2x))⁵/(5! log 3 log 5 log 7 log 11 log 13) + O((1+log x)⁴).
This cancellation of the linear column is evaluated without an assumption on the zeros or averages over x.

Proof: by f*1, Σ_m H(x/m)=Σ_{a supported on p≤16}h₁(x/a), with effectively finite sums. Write c₀x as Σ_{a} x/a. Directly from the piecewise definition, y−h₁(y)=min(1,2y)−min(1,y). Grouping a=2^j b, b odd, and telescoping in j gives the identity. For the asymptotic set L=log(2x): the count of b≤2x is the number of points of the nonnegative lattice in the five-dimensional simplex Σ e_p log p≤L. The union of their unit cubes contains the simplex and lies inside the simplex with L increased by Σlog p. Their volumes give L⁵/(5!Πlog p)+O((1+L)⁴). The strips L+j<log b≤L+j+1 contain O((1+L+j)⁴) points by the same comparison. Weighting them by exp(−j) controls the tail b>2x with O((1+L)⁴).

What inverting this datum would imply: the Mellin transform of Σ_m H(x/m) on Re s>1 is ζ(s) times the Mellin transform of H, and the cancellation of 1/ζ is exact. The energy problem reappears on dividing by ζ; the smallness or sign of the aggregate deficit does not by itself provide a ceiling for the individual column. This identifies explicitly the information lost in this average over dilations; the bound on E(T) remains open.

080 was reproduced with python-flint 0.9.0, exit 0 and 4096/4096 panels passed. SHA256 of the verifier: 640d8eb8ecf2bce7e782e08333a722171744af8fc0c9831582fcfcb796fb09bc. DET and GAP of 079 were also checked. With the exterior of 078 and the hypotheses of 073 the strict positivity of the complete form on nonzero real combinations of up to three powers with exponents greater than one is confirmed. It is a reproduction.

The audit of 002/014/017 confirmed that all the atoms of 017 at a fixed admissible rate would suffice for the sign in all windows of paper 46. Continuity uses an auxiliary positive norm. The conclusion is nonnegativity, without coercive margin. The uniform hypothesis remains open.

## What the sign can hide in all blocks of fixed order

**Model theorem.** Given any integer r≥1 there exists an even real polynomial Z, with simple zeros and one quartet off the imaginary axis, for which the kernel of M=Z'/Z, K(u,v)=(M(u)+M(v))/(u+v), is positive definite on *each* set of up to 2r distinct rates u≥1/2. On *each* set of 2r+4 distinct rates it admits a negative direction. Even the residue +1 at all poles of M is kept.

Take T=r+1 and
```
Zδ(s) = ∏_{j=1}^r (s²+j²) · ((s−δ)²+T²)((s+δ)²+T²).
```
For F(s)=Σ c_h/(s+u_h), the form is Σ_z F(z)F(−z), counting zeros with multiplicity. Indeed, the symmetry of the divisor allows replacing 1/(v−z) by 1/(v+z) in the sum of the second summands of M(u)+M(v); the sum of the two fractions cancels u+v.

Let n=2r. Write F=P/D with D(s)=∏(1+s/u_h), degree of P<n. It suffices to consider real coefficients of P with Euclidean norm one. The parameters are compactified by taking all the inverses of the rates in [0,2], collisions included. For δ=0 the contribution of the first n zeros is 2Σ_j |P(ij)/D(ij)|², strictly positive because P cannot vanish at n distinct points. The remaining double pair also contributes positively or zero. On the compact set of parameters and numerators there is therefore a positive minimum. The form is jointly continuous even for 0≤δ≤1/4, since the evaluated points have nonzero imaginary part and D never vanishes there. There thus exists a single δ>0 that works for all rates. Smaller blocks are included by completing them with zero coefficients.

In dimension n+4, for any distinct rates, interpolate P at the n+4 zeros prescribing F=0 at the n axial zeros, F=1 at the two with real part δ and F=−1 at the two with real part −δ. This prescribes P=FD, gives real coefficients by conjugation and degree ≤n+3. The partial fractions of P/D provide the coefficients of the test. Its form equals exactly −4.

A smaller rational falsifier (independent review): M=M₁+M₂−M₃/64, M_t(u)=u/(u²+t²). The form is |F(i)|²+|F(2i)|²−|F(3i)|²/64. For real cubic P with P(i)=A+iB, P(2i)=C+iD, one has P(3i)=(−5A+8C)/3+i(−5B+4D). By Cauchy and the monotonicity of the modulus of the denominator, |F(3i)|²≤41(|F(i)|²+|F(2i)|²). At five rates the numerator (s²+1)(s²+4) gives a strictly negative direction.

**Scope.** POWER_TABLE_AUDIT_018 §3 already falsified propagation via an atom of negative weight. E101.074 and E101.078 already study quartets and their detection by projections or jets. Here the quantification covers simultaneously *all* admissible positions of the rates, for a single polynomial with genuine multiplicities and prescribed order. The polynomial depends on the order. The proof excludes deducing the uniform step solely from the certified finite degree, the symmetry of the divisor and the positive multiplicities. The theta identity and the arithmetic of ξ lie outside the model.

### Necessary central budget of every positive extension at radius five

**Necessary condition for the form of ξ.** If Q=S₁₀+P≥0 on the whole line and P preserves the value of the form on all radius-5 data, then ∫_{−1}¹ Q(t)dt < 8·10⁻³². It also holds for a positive measure representing the form with normalization ∫|F|² dQ=2π W(f). It is a constraint on the mass, independent of how the corrections are designed.

Proof. Set a=5/28 and take f equal to the convolution of 28 uniform densities on [−a,a]. Its transform is F(t)=sinc(at)²⁸; f has integral one, support [−5,5] and ||f||₂²≥1/10. It is an admissible datum for the explicit formula by its regularity (compact C²⁶ spline); it can also be dilated slightly inwards and smoothed, with convergence of the zero series by domination. For z=γ+i(1/2−β) the zero formula and the symmetry and parity of F give |W(f)|≤Σρ |sinc(az)|⁵⁶. Rounding of the sign of the imaginary part does not affect this bound.

By R156_003 §D4, |γ|>14 and Σγ⁻²<0.0465, counting multiplicities and both signs. For x≥5/2, |sin(x)|/x≤1/4: on [5/2,π] use monotonicity of the sine and sin(5/2)<5/8; on [π,4], use x−π≤x/4; from 4 on |sin x|≤1 suffices. If |y|≤a/2, the complex sine identity gives |sinc(x+iy)|²≤1/16+(sinh(a/2)/(5/2))²<(253/1000)². Apply this bound to 54 factors and to the other two the bound cosh(a/2)/(a|γ|). Thus

    |W(f)| ≤ 0.0465 (cosh(a/2)/a)² (253/1000)⁵⁴ < 9·10⁻³³.

On [−1,1], |F|²≥sinc(a)⁵⁶; by global positivity of the representing measure its mass there is ≤2π·9·10⁻³³/sinc(a)⁵⁶ <8·10⁻³². In particular the real Rayleigh infimum at radius 5 is ≤9·10⁻³² even without assuming the sign. The quantitative argument uses the normalization of 193 and the box profile for the specific window.

**Why repaired bands should not be counted as progress on the sign.** For every compact K, the Schwartz corrections whose transform has compact support outside [−10,10] are dense in C(K) by restriction (take real parts for real targets). A measure on K annihilating them has entire transform vanishing on the two exterior half-lines by duality with smooth functions; it is identically zero. Hahn–Banach concludes. ### Global detector with two copies of a single triangle and square separations

Let φ(x)=(1−|x|)₊ and C(t)=W(φ,φ(·−t)) the real polarized form. Let Δ=supρ(Reρ−1/2). If Δ>0, for a residual set of steps h>0, the two functions φ±φ(·−k²h) each give negative energies without lower bound along subsequences of k. More precisely the excursions of C(k²h) of each sign have upper exponent Δ in the physical time k²h. The same holds for every prescribed increasing sequence n_k→∞ with n_{k+1}/n_k→1, replacing k² by n_k. The residual set may depend on the sequence.

**Proof.** Set w=ρ−1/2 and A(w)=(sinh(w/2)/(w/2))⁴, product of the two two-sided transforms of the triangle. The explicit formula and the symmetries give C(t)=Σ A(w)exp(wt), real and even. The series of moduli of A converges by fourth-order decay in the strip. The one-sided Laplace transform of C is Σ A(w)/(s−w), initially to the right of Δ. It converges normally away from the divisor on compact sets and has poles at each exterior w, even if the supremum Δ is not attained: the residue is the multiplicity times A(w)≠0. There are no positive real poles.

Fix 0<b<Δ. If one of ±C(t) were eventually bounded above by Kexp(bt), the nonnegative difference would have a meromorphic transform without real singularity on (b,∞) and with some pole of real part >b. This contradicts Landau's lemma: at the finite abscissa of convergence of an eventually nonnegative function its transform has a real singularity (subtract the compact stretch; the expansion at a real point to the right has positive moments when expanding to the left). The existence of the pole forces that abscissa to be >b, and |C(t)|≤const·exp(Δt) gives its finiteness. Both signs thus present arbitrarily large late excursions after dividing by exp(bt).

For any interval (a,d) of positive steps, the union of (a n_k,d n_k) from any index on contains a half-line: the intervals eventually overlap. Every sufficiently late excursion therefore reaches some n_k h with h in (a,d). By continuity, the sets of steps witnessing an excursion larger than a given threshold after a given index are open dense. Intersecting over indices, thresholds, signs and rational b in (0,Δ) proves the claim. Finally W(φ±φ(·−t))=2C(0)±2C(t).

**Bridge to the target.** To prove the global sign it would suffice to prove, on a non-meagre set of steps, a finite lower bound (depending on the step) for W(φ+φ(·−k²h)) at all k. Even a subexponential loss in k²h suffices. Under RH these energies are nonnegative. What is pending is that one-sided arithmetic estimate. The residual step does not fix h=1 nor identify a particular rational step. The antecedents in the index on Landau oscillation and translated profiles give the continuous mechanism; the simultaneous restriction to a single triangular profile, a single sign of the combination and square separations for generic steps adds the discrete conclusion. It is a reduction and conditional detector, not a proof of the estimate.

All changes are fixed once and for all. In any prefix only one modified cell can remain incomplete, whose change is O(x exp(−cB(log x))) (B varies by o(1) in a band). In each block the counts in the chosen cells and all zeros of μ are preserved.

For every X=X_j exp(s), |s|≤δ, each swap increases the detector −X⁻¹ᐟ²Σ ε_d g(d/X) by ≫η/√X_j. The gain of the block is ≫√X_j η. The true detector is O(√X_j exp(−3cB(t_j))) decreasing c: apply partial summation with Mertens to g in the annulus of 5241, with polylogarithmic endpoints and bounded variation, and its tail bounds. The explicit correction of 5241 is negligible. The earlier and later blocks lie outside the annulus and the absolute Gaussian bounds are uniform for |ε_d|≤1, even after the factor log y. Thus the increase dominates on that whole fixed interval, also proving the claim on area. With the true prime side no substitution is made: equality of both sides of the detector is an additional property that the falsifier does not presuppose. This computation rules out inferring the one-sided ceiling solely from the counts, the squarefree support and the class of prefix estimates.

**Quantitative gate for genuine μ.** For each microcell of the large residual weight of 5259 take its centre u_j in the coordinate u=log(d/X). Its contribution is determined, up to a global error o(1), by the local moments Σ μ(d)(u−u_j)^l of orders 0≤l≤K, K=⌈3L/(cB(L))⌉. Indeed |b_X(exp u)|≤X² on discs of fixed radius around the band (5303). Taylor and Cauchy give a pointwise remainder O(X²(Cη)^(K+1)); it suffices to sum over O(X√L) sites and divide by √X. The total remainder is X^(−1/2+o(1)). The coefficients are the derivatives of the weight divided by l!, so the remaining problem is to estimate the signed combination of moments, not to estimate them all individually. It is not claimed that the proposed number of moments is minimal.

### Moving sieve of the detector: only integers without prime factors up to t²

The fixed weight g(y)=log(y)h(y) of 5259 is used. For each centre t freeze Y=t² over the whole window |v−t|≤L(t)=log t+B and define
```
A_t(v)=−exp(−v/2) Σ_{d : p|d ⇒ p>Y} μ(d) g(d exp(−v)).
```
If Δ>0, for each sign the limit of t⁻¹ log(1+∫(±A_t)₊dv) over that window is Δ. Under RH the two areas are exp(o(t)) as an upper bound. Therefore a subexponential ceiling for just one of them along any subsequence of centres tending to infinity still suffices for the global sign. The filter is on the divisors of d, and g is used before the correction of the central strip. The two trimmings have not been combined.

**Arithmetic identity.** Write E(X)=−Σ μ(d)g(d/X) and E_Y the same sieved object. Since μ*1_{k with all its primes ≤Y}=μ·1_{(d,∏_{p≤Y}p)=1} by local factors, E_Y(X)=Σ_{k Y-smooth} E(X/k). The interchange converges by the decay of g at infinity. Fix 1/2<σ<1. For every Z>0,
```
E(Z)=−Σ_{Reρ>σ} F(ρ) Z^ρ + Oσ(Z^σ).
```
For Z≥1 it follows from 5241 including the explicit correction of the centring. The absolute sum of |F(ρ)| converges by the gamma factor. For Z<1, E has Gaussian decay in 1/Z and the retained series costs O(Z^σ). Consequently
```
E_Y(X)=−Σ_{Reρ>σ} F(ρ)D_Y(ρ)X^ρ+Oσ(D_Y(σ)X^σ),
D_Y(s)=∏_{p≤Y}(1−p^(−s))⁻¹.
```
For Y=t², log D_Y(σ)=o(t) by summing over integers up to t². Uniformly in Reρ>σ, exp(−o(t))≤|D_Y(ρ)|≤exp(o(t)), also using |1−p^(−ρ)|≤1+p^(−σ). The same proof allows Y=t^(2+o(1)) for fixed σ greater than 1/2.

**Uniformity of the detector.** Suppose Δ>0. Fix a zero ρ₀ with β₀>1/2 and take σ between 1/2 and β₀. The high series normalized by X⁻¹ᐟ² is real by conjugation and, with Y frozen, is bounded in the real argument z by C D_Y(σ)exp(|z|/2). K=Φ*Φ of 5219 annihilates it exactly after any translation. The same fixed cardinal of 5219 extracts at the centre t a term of modulus ≥c exp((β₀−1/2)t−o(t)), including multiplicity. The tail |y|>log t+B costs O(exp(−t+o(t))) by the preceding global ceiling, the same K and sufficiently large B. Both sign masses of the high series in the window are thus ≥exp((β₀−1/2)t−o(t)); taking the positive part is Lipschitz and the integrated error of the expansion is ≤exp((σ−1/2)t+o(t)). For the ceiling use |high series|≤C D_Y(σ)exp(Δv) for positive v. The supremum over β₀ gives the limit without assuming a maximum. Under RH the original representation gives E(Z)=O(√Z) for all Z>0; the cost is then D_Y(1/2), whose logarithm for Y=t² is O(t/log t) by Chebyshev and partial summation. The zero upper rate can also be deduced using fixed σ and then taking the infimum over σ>1/2.

**Size of the sieve and scope.** The absolute tails of 5241 remain negligible after sieving because |sieved μ|≤|μ|. In any proportional band [x,2x] of the annulus, log x=t+O(log t), at most O(x/log t) integers remain: it suffices to exclude primes ≤√t. Inclusion-exclusion gives the ceiling x∏_{p≤√t}(1−1/p)+O(2^√t), and the product is O(1/log t) even bounding its inverse from below by the harmonic sum up to √t. The earlier trimming of small prime marks of 4748 and the gcd work in 052 did not give this preservation of both local rates for the detector of 5241 when deleting whole integers. The models of Euler edits of 4488–4610 motivate using the exact local factor, instead of assuming stability from the density of the deleted numbers. The one-sided inequality on the survivors remains open.

### Favourable square and remainder with both indices around the square root

For large t now freeze Y=log t and P=∏_{p≤Y}p. This weaker cut preserves the detector of 5329 by the same proof. P≤t² for sufficiently large t by the eventual Chebyshev bound θ(Y)≤2Y (also by the PNT). Write a(n)=μ(n)1_{(n,P)=1}, u(n)=1_{(n,P)=1}, κ=φ(P)/P. For |v−t|≤log t+B set X=exp(v), L=log X, S=Σ a(n)g(n/X), with g of 5259. There are large fixed positive constants C₁,C₂ such that, with
```
M=⌈√X(C₁L)^(1/4)⌉,    Z=X/[P(C₂L)^(3/2)],
H_P(y)=Σ_{(r,P)=1}g(ry),    I=∫₀∞g(y)dy=ξ′(1)>0,
R= X^(−1/2) Σ_{d,m≤M, dm>Z} a(d)a(m)[H_P(dm/X)−κ I X/(dm)],
```
one has
```
−S/√X = κ I √X (Σ_{d≤M}a(d)/d)² + R + O(X⁻¹).
```
Thus it would suffice to control the negative part of R in the windows of 5329, even along a single subsequence of centres. Both Möbius arguments in R lie between Z/M and M, that is, between ≫√X/[P L^(7/4)] and ≪√X L^(1/4). The cofactor r is already summed in the centred kernel. The individual sign of that kernel is not determined.

**Symmetric hyperbola.** a*u=δ₁, so that a*a*u=a. In the triple sum weighted by g(dmr/X), cover d≤M or m≤M by inclusion-exclusion. Each of the two sums with a single restricted index collapses to Σ_{m≤M} a(m)g(m/X); by the decay at zero it is negligible. The intersection is the double sum with H_P. On the complement d,m>M the argument is ≥√(C₁L). In absolute value, group by n=dmr and use τ₃(n)≤n² and |g(y)|≪exp(−c y²) for large y: choosing C₁ sufficiently large makes the normalized tail O(X⁻¹). The minus sign of the intersection and the minus sign of the detector give the plus sign of the square. The value of I is the derivative at s=1 of the Mellin transform ζ(s)F(s)=ξ(s); the even theta representation around s=1/2 gives ξ′(1)>0.

**Cost of centring for small products.** Extend g evenly in the real variable, with value zero at the origin. On complex circles of radius εx around x>0 with small fixed ε, the theta series and h(z)=z⁻¹h(1/z) give |g(z)|≪exp(−c(x²+x⁻²)), reducing c to absorb powers and logarithms. Cauchy and integration give ||g^(j)||₁≤C^(j+1)(j!)^(3/2): the additional factor beyond j! comes from integrating x^(−j)exp(−c/x²) near zero. One obtains |ĝ(τ)|≤C exp(−c|τ|^(2/3)) by integration by parts of order ≍|τ|^(2/3). Poisson, using g(0)=0, gives |H₁(y)−I/y|≪y⁻¹exp(−c y^(−2/3)) for 0<y≤1. By inclusion-exclusion H_P(y)=Σ_{l|P} μ(l)H₁(ly); the main term is κI/y. If y≤1/[P(C₂L)^(3/2)], the error is ≪τ(P)X⁻⁴/y on increasing C₂. Its normalized sum over both indices costs ≪τ(P)X^(−7/2)(1+log M)², which suffices. The main terms of all products are summed together before the trimming and constitute the single square written above.

The symmetric separation is a classical hyperbola identity. The specific contribution compared with earlier rectangular cuts is the sign of the main term for this detector, together with the uniform absolute error outside the band of products and the survival of the one-sided criterion at all centres. The hole of 5259 is not used; the prime sieve is weakened from t² to log t so that the period P costs only a power of log X. The remaining problem requires cancellation in R.

### Vanishing of the mean of each primitive quotient and joint removal up to uv≤X^(1/3)

The sieve of 5352 is kept, Y=log t and P≤t². Write K_P(z)=H_P(z)−κI/z. The functional symmetry of ξ gives a vanishing distinct from the extraction of the square:
```
∫₀∞ K_P(z) dz/√z=0.
```
Indeed for Re s>1 the Mellin transform of H₁ is ζ(s)ξ′(s). Subtracting I/z on (0,1) and continuing leaves the term I/(s−1); for 0<Re s<1 this coincides with the integral of −I/z on (1,∞). Poisson at zero and the Gaussian at infinity justify both integrals. Thus the Mellin transform of K₁ in the strip is ζ(s)ξ′(s). At s=1/2 it is zero by parity of ξ around that point. For K_P use Σ_{l|P} μ(l)K₁(lz). No hypothesis on the nontrivial zeros intervenes.

To make the endpoint error small now take M=⌈X^(5/6)⌉ in the symmetric hyperbola. The two short sums remain negligible since m/X≤2X^(−1/6), and the complement with d,m>M is negligible by Gaussian decay. In the complete centred double sum classify d=ku, m=kv with (u,v)=1. Omit u,v that are not squarefree or coprime to P. On each ray the sign is μ(u)μ(v) and the weight of the common factor is μ²(k)1_{(k,uvP)=1}. Let Q=√(X/(uv)); the remaining weight is K_P((k/Q)²). By the preceding vanishing its integral with respect to k over (0,∞) is exactly zero.

The error in replacing the count of k by its density over the whole half-line, after normalizing, is
```
≪ τ(uvP) τ(P) X^(−1/4)(uv)^(−1/4).
```
The elementary counting formula of 5283 with error O(τ(uvP)√k) is used and one integrates by parts. The variation constant for K₁ is finite: ∫₀∞√s |(K₁(s²))′|ds<∞. At zero also apply Poisson to z∂_zH₁ via the function xg′(x) (its integral is −I); its transform decays faster than any power. At infinity the derivative of the term −I/z is integrable with that weight. For K₁(ls²) the cost of the integral is multiplied by l^(−1/4). The bound follows after rescaling by Q. To return to the endpoint M/max(u,v), use |K_P(z)|≪1/z uniformly (the sum of |g(rz)| costs O(1/z) and κ≤1). Thus the normalized tail is ≪√X/(M min(u,v)) when M/max(u,v)≥1.

Sum the moduli of the **balances per ray** over uv≤V=X^(1/3). The sum of quadrature errors costs X^(−1/4+o(1))V^(3/4)=X^o(1), by divisor counting. That of the tails costs O(√X V/M), since Σ_{uv≤V}1/min(u,v)≤2VΣ_u u⁻². Both bounds are uniform in the frozen window. Consequently all these rays can be deleted at subpolynomial absolute cost after grouping each ray. The small-product trimming of 5352, if used, is done after this separation; for the retained rays the same Poisson bound holds with (1+log M)².

In the rest, the negative part remains the sufficient obligation since the extracted square is nonnegative. In particular only primitive quotients with uv>X^(1/3) remain. The cut M was enlarged deliberately: it is not claimed that these rays cost X^o(1) under the previous cut of almost √X. The conclusion concerns the cost of all deleted rays together and is independent of cancellations between signs μ(u)μ(v) of different rays. For a shorter cut, M=⌈X^(2/3)⌉, the same argument allows deleting the square u,v≤X^(1/6), since on that square Σ 1/min(u,v)≪X^(1/6)log X.

The independent audit allows making the cost explicit: it is O((1+log X)^7) for the variant uv≤X^(1/3). Indeed τ(uvP)≤τ(uv)τ(P) and τ(P)²≤P²≪(log X)^4. Grouping uv=n, τ(n)²≤τ₄(n); by the harmonic sum in three variables Σ_{n≤V}τ₄(n)≪V(1+log V)^3 and by parts the weight n^(−1/4) leaves V^(3/4)(1+log V)^3. The joint endpoint tail is O(1).

### Fourth-power filter that removes the denominator of the squarefree integers

**The whole region uv≤√X** can be deleted at joint cost X^o(1), even summing the moduli of the balances for each reduced quotient. The cut of the original variables is now M=⌈X^(3/4)(C log X)^(1/4)⌉. The detector changes, but it keeps the one-sided criterion for the global sign with the same window around each centre.

**Design.** With E=y∂_y and g of 5259, use
```
g₄(y)=Σ_{j≥1} [ (−E−1)(−E−1/4)g ](j⁴y),
B(s)=Mellin(g₄)(s)=(s−1)(s−1/4)ζ(4s)ξ′(s).
```
The formula is obtained first by absolute convergence to the right. B is entire and decreases rapidly in height on each fixed vertical strip by the gamma factor of ξ and of its derivative. Inversion and shifting give g₄(y)=O_N(y^N) at zero for every fixed N, also after any fixed number of Euler derivatives. At infinity the physical sum of differentiated Gaussians gives O(exp(−c y²)). In particular I=B(1)=0 exactly.

**Retention of the arithmetic signal.** For the unsieved detector −Σμ(n)g₄(n/X), the Mellin transform in X with convention X^(−s) dX/X is −B(s)/ζ(s). On shifting to Re s=−1 as in 5241, the previous residues −mρ F(ρ) appear, multiplied by (ρ−1)(ρ−1/4)ζ(4ρ) (mρ is the multiplicity). The justification by good heights is that of 5241 with factors of polynomial growth against gamma; no trivial zeros are crossed. On Reρ>1/2 the multiplier never vanishes. For the expansion it suffices to retain the zeros with Reρ>σ for fixed σ greater than 1/2 and absorb the rest in Oσ(X^σ) for X≥1; the residue expression is interpreted by continuation at possible removable singularities. The series are absolutely convergent. For X<1 use physical decay at infinity. Freezing Y=log t, the sieve by (n,P)=1 with P the product of primes up to Y multiplies each retained coefficient by D_Y(ρ), with the same error as in 5329. By the positive annihilation with K and the cardinals, both masses in the window, normalized by √X, keep exponent Δ if Δ>0. Under RH the subexponential ceiling of 5329 suffices. Simplicity is not presumed.

**Computation per ray.** H_P(z)=Σ_{(r,P)=1}g₄(rz) already has zero main integral. For N=uvP and Q=√(X/(uv)), the sum over all k of the ray (without the sign μ(u)μ(v)) admits Mellin inversion on 1<c<2 with integrand
```
(Q^s/2) ζ(s/2)B(s/2) ∏_{p|P}(1−p^(−s/2))
            · [ζ(s)/ζ(2s)] ∏_{p|N}(1+p^(−s))⁻¹ .
```
Indeed H_P decays rapidly at zero for fixed P by Poisson applied to the even flat extension of g₄, of zero integral. Its Mellin transform is the indicated one by continuation from Re(s/2)>1. The sum in k converges absolutely for c>1. The factor ζ(2s) of B(s/2) cancels exactly the arithmetic denominator. The pole at s=1 disappears by ξ′(1/2)=0 and that at s=2 by the factor s/2−1. On Re s≥ε>0 each local product is bounded by O_{ε,δ}((uvP)^δ) for any δ>0, separating the small primes and using p^δ for the large ones. The integral over Re s=ε costs O_{ε,δ}(Q^ε(uvP)^δ) by vertical decay. The constants may depend on ε,δ but are uniform over the rays and the window.

For uv≤√X, the first term omitted by k>M/max(u,v) has z=k²uv/X ≥M²/(X√X)≥√(C log X). In this regime |H_P(z)|≪exp(−c z²) uniformly. For example, extracting exp(−c C log X/2) leaves a Gaussian sum in k of cost O(1+Q) per ray. Increasing C absorbs all polynomial quantities after summing the rays. The sums with a single short index of the hyperbola identity are also negligible by the decay of arbitrary order of g₄ at zero and M/X=X^(−1/4+o(1)); the complement d,m>M by the Gaussian tail. There are O(√X log X) ordered rays in the region; after normalizing by √X and taking ε,δ arbitrarily small, their joint cost is X^o(1). The remaining contribution carries a plus sign in the negative Möbius detector. Its one-sided bound of 5329 suffices. Unlike 5352 no main square remains: its coefficient is zero by design.

The new ingredient relative to 5372 is adapting the Mellin transform to the series of squarefree k before bounding the error of each ray. The exponent 1/2 is the reach obtained by summing this per-ray bound in absolute value; it is not claimed to be optimal.

### Signed grouping of the rays by their primitive product

For the filter of 5394 write Θ=sup Reρ, Δ=Θ−1/2. Fix 0<δ<1, V=X^(1−δ) and a smooth cut χ(n/V) equal to one up to V and zero from 2V on. The normalized contribution of this group with its signs is Oε(X^(−1/8+ε)V^(Θ−3/8+ε)). Under failure of RH it has exponent strictly smaller than Δ on taking ε small; under RH it decreases by a power. This statement allows a much higher cut than the estimate of moduli of rays, at the price of depending on Θ in the comparison.

In the complete ray integral of 5394 set Re s=3/4. For n=uv squarefree and coprime to P, all assignments give sign μ(n) and there are 2^ω(n) of them. After extracting the factors of P the arithmetic coefficient is μ(n)2^ω(n)∏_{p|n}(1+p^(−s))⁻¹. Its Dirichlet series in z is ζ(z)⁻² times an absolutely convergent product for Re z>1/2: the linear coefficient of the correction costs O(p^(−Re z−3/4)), and the higher ones O(p^(−2Re z)). The factors at p|P cost X^o(1). Inverting χ on the line Re(z−s/2)=Θ+ε−3/8 allows bounding the sum by V^(Θ+ε−3/8) with polynomial losses in the heights absorbed by the smooth Mellin transform and the gamma decay. Here 1/ζ(z) has polynomial growth in the strip at distance ε from Θ by the classical Mertens ceiling recalled in 4799, or by absolute convergence if Θ=1. The pole of the Mellin transform of χ at zero is not crossed. The normalized prefactor is X^(−1/8). With M=⌈√(2XV)(C log X)^(1/4)⌉ the error on returning to the truncated rays is Gaussian and the two single-index sums cost O(X⁻ᴬ) for fixed A because M/X=X^(−δ/2+o(1)). The rate of each sign mass is preserved in the group with weight 1−χ. It is not a discard theorem for the sharp cut at V.

### Global detector with coprime pairs, both in the square-root band

Change the weight to w=(−E−1)g, E=y∂_y and use Y=log t, P=∏_{p≤Y}p frozen in the window of 5329. Its Mellin transform is (s−1)ξ′(s); the factor s−1 removes no exterior zero and the ordinary integral of w is zero. Let W_P(y)=Σ_{(r,P)=1}w(ry), a=μ·1_{(·,P)=1}, M=⌈√X(C₁ log X)^(1/4)⌉, Z=X/[P(C₂ log X)^(3/2)]. Consider only
```
B_t(v)=X^(−1/2) Σ_{d,m≤M, (d,m)=1, dm>Z} a(d)a(m) W_P(dm/X),  X=exp(v).
```
If Δ>0 the areas of both signs of B_t in each window |v−t|≤log t+B have limiting exponent Δ. Under RH they are subexponential. Therefore a one-sided subexponential ceiling along a subsequence of centres suffices. All nontrivial common factors are left out of the new detector, and both indices lie simultaneously between Z/M and M, at multiplicative distance from √X bounded by powers of log X.

**Why coprimality can be imposed.** Before the hyperbola, sum d,m without cut, coprime, with cofactor r coprime to P and weight w(dmr/X); call S this unnormalized sum. For p∤P the factor of the two indices is 1−2p^(−s), since the prime can appear in only one. That of the cofactor is (1−p^(−s))⁻¹. The series of the coefficients of S is therefore
```
 ζ(s)⁻¹ D_Y(s) C_P(s),    C_P(s)=∏_{p∤P}(1−2p^(−s))/(1−p^(−s))² .
```
For each σ>1/2 the absolute sum of coefficients of the corrector product weighted by n^(−σ) is bounded uniformly in P: each factor is 1−p^(−2s)/(1−p^(−s))². Also |C_P(s)| has a uniform positive floor on Re s≥σ for large t, since 2·5^(−σ)<1 and Σ_p p^(−2σ)<∞. The factor D_Y satisfies 5329. The expansion of −Σ μ(n)w(n/X) has the same residues of 5241 multiplied by ρ−1, by its Mellin transform −(s−1)ξ′(s)/ζ(s). Convolve this global expansion truncated to Reρ>σ with the coefficients of D_Y C_P as in 5329: the absolute error is Oσ(X^σ exp(o(t))) and each retained zero carries the new factor D_Y(ρ)C_P(ρ), of modulus between exp(−o(t)) and exp(o(t)). By the same cardinal and the same positive annihilator the two local rates for −S/√X are preserved. Under RH apply the argument with σ↓1/2 after the limit in t. This proves preservation of the capacity to detect a zero, not an absolute bound for the non-coprime portion of the previous detector.

**Why both indices can be shortened at once.** In the sector d≤M, m free with (d,m)=1, the sums over m and r reduce EXACTLY to Σ_{k with all prime divisors dividing d} w(dk/X), for each d coprime to P: at the other allowed primes μ*1=δ₁. For any fixed 0<λ<1, |w(y)|≪λ y^(−λ) (the constant depends on λ) and ∏_{p|d}(1−p^(−λ))⁻¹≪_{λ,ε}d^ε. Thus the cost of this normalized sector, summed in absolute value over d, is O(X^(λ−1/2) M^(1−λ+ε))=O(X^(λ/2+ε+o(1))). Take λ,ε arbitrarily small. The same holds for m≤M. The contribution with both >M is O(X⁻¹) by the Gaussian tail. By inclusion-exclusion, −S/√X and the double sum with both ≤M differ by X^o(1), uniformly in v.

Finally w and xw′(x) have the same Gevrey and tail bounds of 5352 by the sectorial formula; the zero integral suppresses the term κI/y. One obtains |W_P(y)|≪τ(P)y⁻¹exp(−c(Py)^(−2/3)) for Py≤1. The sum with dm≤Z costs O(X⁻¹) on increasing C₂. The announced formula remains, without an auxiliary square and without the loss towards X^(3/4) of 5394. The sign of B_t remains pending.

Additional elementary identification from the audit: (1−2q)/(1−q)=1−q−q²−⋯. Therefore the exact coefficient of the complete detector S is (−1)^ω(n)1_{(n,P)=1}, with ω the number of distinct primes, also for n not squarefree. In the reduction to the coprime band the genuine Möbius function in d and m is still used.

### Hyperbola with a growing number of indices and uniform detection of the sign

There is an alternative to keeping two coprime Möbius indices. At each large centre t take k=2⌊t^(1/3)/2⌋, Y=log t and freeze both on |v−t|≤log t+B. Set X=exp(v), a=μ·1_{(·,P)=1}, u=1_{(·,P)=1} with P the primorial of 5424. Write T₂g(y)=g(2y), g_k=(1−2T₂)^k g and A=⌈k log t⌉. Define M=(Xt²)^(1/k) and q=d₁⋯d_k. The resulting detector is
```
X^(−1/2) Σ_{d₁,…,d_k≤M, q>X exp(−t/A)}
              a(d₁)⋯a(d_k) Σ_{r≥1} u^{*(k−1)}(r) g_k(rq/X).
```
Its difference from −X^(−1/2)Σ a(n)g_k(n/X) is O(exp(−t/2+o(t))). Therefore both sign masses have limiting exponent Δ in all windows if Δ>0 and under RH both are subexponential. All indices satisfy uniformly log d_i=(1+o(1))t/k, in particular d_i=exp((1+o(1))t^(2/3)). The indices may share primes. The sum over r is included in the weight and carries no Möbius signs.

**Survival with growing k.** The Mellin transform of g_k is (1−2^(1−s))^k ξ′(s). The filter multiplies the residue of each fixed exterior zero by a quantity of modulus between exp(−Oρ(k)) and exp(O(k)), since Reρ<1. On the whole strip of zeros the common ceiling is 3^k. The finite difference can be applied directly to the truncated global expansion of the detector of 5329 before sieving, evaluating at X/2^l with binomial coefficients times (−2)^l. The error Oσ(X^σ) is multiplied by at most (1+2^(1−σ))^k. The convolution with the Y-smooth numbers costs at most D_Y(σ). These losses are exp(o(t)). The fixed cardinal and positive weight of 5219 are applied as before to the high series, with the same ceilings on the tail |y|>log t+B. For a zero with abscissa β>1/2 take σ strictly between both; the loss exp(o(t)) respects the exponential margin. Under RH the same argument with arbitrary σ>1/2 gives the zero-rate ceiling.

**Vanishing of the proper faces.** One starts from a^{*k}*u^{*(k−1)}=a. Inclusion-exclusion over the k events d_i≤M. In an intersection of j events with 1≤j<k, the convolution of the free factors produces u^{*(j−1)} (δ₁ for j=1). For the partial product q of the j indices, the kernel at y=q/X has Mellin transform

where sinc(z)=sin(z)/z and sinc(0)=1. The diagonal costs O(1+W). Consequently it suffices to bound from above the signed off-diagonal sum by exp(o(t)) along a divergent sequence of centres. The first bound counts the negatives between the two endpoints, with the endpoint convention that includes the larger and excludes the smaller. For the second, in 5574 there remain ≫H representations of each sign per interval of length H=√x log²x. By Shiu applied to τ², the sum of τ(n)² over the interval is O(H log³x): its estimate with modulus one involves τ(p)²=4 and the factor 1/log x. Cauchy–Schwarz gives ≫H/log³x distinct integers of each sign. Since v_k∼u_k, tile from the smaller endpoint toward the larger with complete intervals of length √y log²y starting at y, all of length comparable to H, and one incomplete one. The negatives over the whole stretch are exactly |M(x)| counting (minimum,maximum]; discarding the incomplete stretch costs O(H) in length. The inequality follows. Thus the root scale is reached in every range whose excess at u_k is O(√x), even inside an excursion. [P. Shiu, A Brun–Titchmarsh theorem for multiplicative functions](https://doi.org/10.1515/crll.1980.313.161).

A criterion allowing exceptions is obtained without Shiu. If M(x)=m>0, exactly m equal-rank pairs cross the integer x, all with orientation u_i≤x<v_i. Write i=N_−(x)+j, 1≤j≤m, with N_− the negative count. Then u_i≤x−(m−j) and v_i≥x+j. Hence EACH distance v_i−u_i is ≥m. For m<0 the lists are swapped. The ranks are consecutive and comparable to x by the densities. If Θ>1/2, for every 1/2<s<Θ there are arbitrarily large x of each orientation with |M(x)|>x^s: in the case of an eventual one-sided ceiling, Landau's argument from 5574 applied to Cx^s±M(x) would add to its transform only the term C/(z−s), regular on the real axis above s, while a non-real pole to the right of s persists.

Consequently it suffices to prove the following even in ONE chosen orientation: for each ε>0 and each large dyadic K, there are Oε(K^(1/2+ε)) indices i∈[K,2K) with v_i−u_i>K^(1/2+ε). Indeed, if there were an exterior zero, choose s>1/2+ε and s<Θ, and take positive excursions as above. The ≥x^s crossed indices occupy at most O(1) dyadic blocks with K≍x. One of them contains ≫K^s exceptions, a contradiction. Under RH the criterion holds by 5560 with a smaller ε. That rank-frequency estimate for μ has not been proved. The criterion tolerates a growing set of exceptions, but requires control in every large dyadic block.

### Frequency of large displacements: any power saving suffices

Put g_k^+=(v_k−u_k)_+ and g_k^-=(u_k−v_k)_+. For each orientation separately and each 0<s<Θ,

    limsup_{K dyadic→∞} log(1+#{K≤k<2K : g_k^±>K^s})/log K = 1.

Indeed M_+(x) counts exactly the intervals [u_k,v_k) of positive orientation containing x, and M_−(x) counts the reversed ones. Thus by Tonelli and u_k,v_k∼2ζ(2)k the integral of M_±(x)x^(−σ−1) is comparable to Σ g_k^± k^(−σ−1), for each fixed real σ (in convergence or divergence). Both abscissas of convergence are ≤Θ by 5560. If both were smaller, the difference of their transforms would continue 1/(zζ(z)) holomorphically to a half-plane containing a pole at a zero. If only one were smaller, the other would have by Landau a real singularity at Θ; yet the difference is holomorphic in a neighbourhood of that point, as is the transform with smaller abscissa. The identity by continuation from the right contradicts that singularity. Hence both abscissas equal Θ.

If the count were O(K^(1−δ)) in all large blocks for some δ>0, then Σ_{K≤k<2K} g_k^± ≪ K^(1+s)+Oη(K^(1+Θ−δ+η)) by 5560. The block series would have strictly smaller abscissa. This proves the limsup. Consequence: for each ε>0 it suffices to obtain SOME δ(ε)>0 in the ceiling Oε(K^(1−δ(ε))) for the exceptions of 5586, in a fixed orientation. Logarithmic density of exponent 1 of the count along a subsequence does not imply positive ordinary density.

A two-sided variant allows choosing only a sequence of centres. If Θ>1/2 and 1/2<s<Θ, in EACH window J_t=[exp(t)/t²,exp(t)t²] of ranks there are exp((1+o(1))t) indices with |u_k−v_k|>exp(st). To see this, by 5241 there exists X with |log X−t|≤log t+C and |J(X)|≥exp((Θ−1/2−o(1))t), passing from area to maximum while losing only O(log t). Use the complete sum of μ in 5241, with weight w_X(n)=X^(−1/2)g(n/X), g(y)=log(y)H(y)/√y. It has sup|w'_X|≪X^(−3/2) by the two-sided decay of theta, also after differentiation. Pair by rank before truncating: keep the complete pair if one of its endpoints lies in [X/√(2log X),X√(2log X)]. The other pairs cost O(X^(−1)) by both absolute tails of 5241. All kept ranks lie in J_t by the densities of the lists and the margin t^(1/2) against constants. The explicit correction of J is negligible. From the derivative bound one deduces Σ_{k∈J_t}|u_k−v_k|≥exp((1+Θ−o(1))t). Ranks with distance ≤exp(st) contribute at most exp((1+s+o(1))t) and each other rank contributes ≤exp((Θ+η+o(1))t) for every η>0. Letting η↓0 proves the count. The two-sided window does not identify the large orientation. In particular a fixed power saving in the two-sided count along a divergent sequence, for each threshold s>1/2, would suffice. Neither of the two savings for the genuine ranks has been proved.

### The theta mean of M forces an exact return and both orientations in the same annulus

Let h(y)=H(y)/√y=Σ_{m≥1} f(my)>0 as in 5241. For every X>0 there is an identity WITHOUT zeros on its right-hand side:

    ∫ M(Xy) h(y) dy/y = (2π/X²−1)exp(−π/X²),     ∫ h(y)dy/y=1/2.

In the first integral (over y>0) expand M and h and substitute z=my. One obtains Σ_{n,m} μ(n)∫_{mn/X}^∞ f(z) dz/z. Absolute convergence for each fixed X allows grouping by mn; μ*1 leaves only the product one. The remaining integral is evaluated by differentiating (2πz²−1)exp(−πz²). For the total mass, the Mellin transform of h in Re s>1 is ζ(s)F(s)=ξ(s), by 5241. The two-sided decay gives entire continuation, so at s=0 it equals ξ(0)=1/2.

Unconditional consequence. For each sufficiently large X there is an integer n between ⌊X/R⌋ and ⌊XR⌋ with M(n)=−2, where R=√(2log X). In fact the mean of M(Xy)+2 is O(X^(−2)). The region outside [1/R,R] contributes o(1) even in absolute value, using |M(Xy)|≤Xy and h(y)=y^(−1)h(1/y) with Gaussian decay. Inside remains kernel mass 1/2+o(1). If −2 is not attained, the integer function M(Xy)+2 has constant sign and modulus ≥1 on that region, since it only jumps by 0,±1, a contradiction. At that point the lists of 5560 carry counts differing by only two. The supply of both signs from 5586 in (n,n+√n log²n] therefore leaves ≫√n/log n consecutive common ranks whose endpoints both lie in that interval. This locates synchronized blocks in ALL the specified annuli, without controlling the interior excursions.

Consequence under Θ>1/2. For each 1/2<s<Θ, in each J_t=[exp(t)/t²,exp(t)t²] there are exp((1+o(1))t) ranks of EACH orientation with displacement >exp(st). To see this, take the same X as in 5598 and put g(y)=log(y)h(y). Integration by parts in the sum of 5241 gives ∫M(Xy)g'(y)dy=√X J(X)+log(X)f(1/X). The tails outside [1/R,R] cost o(1), by the Gaussian bounds also for the derivative. Inside, |yg'(y)|/h(y)≪(1+R²)log(2R) holds: for y≥1 the first positive term dominates h from below and the derivative is bounded by the differentiated Gaussian series; for y≤1 use reciprocity. Thus ∫_{1/R}^R |M(Xy)| h(y)dy/y ≥exp((Θ−o(1))t). The difference of the positive and negative parts is bounded by the first identity. Both parts then have that floor separately.

Now h(y)/y is globally bounded. With z=Xy one deduces that the ordinary area ∫M_±(z)dz over [X/R,XR] is at least exp((1+Θ−o(1))t) in each orientation. Every rank interval meeting it has index in J_t by the densities and the margins of 5598. The crossing identity of 5598 majorizes that area by Σ_{k∈J_t}g_k^±. The same cut at exp(st) and pointwise ceiling of 5598 produce the count per orientation. Consequently, in the single-sequence-of-centres criterion it suffices to monitor a single orientation. The power saving along that sequence is still missing. The mass identity comes from the theta kernel already present in 5241 and from Möbius inversion; the new application uses its positivity directly on M before separating the orientations.

### Root-scale excursions in both directions and a limit to narrowing the kernel

There is c>0 such that, for every sufficiently large Z, between Z/(log Z)^2 and Z(log Z)^2 there are integers with M≥c√Z and integers with M≤−c√Z. This conclusion is unconditional. Hence in that whole annulus ALL integer levels between −c√Z and c√Z are attained.

If Θ>1/2, the proof of 5610 gives in the same annulus, in the physical variable, weighted masses of M_± of at least Z^(Θ−o(1)). Since the positive measure has total mass 1/2, both magnitudes are attained, and they exceed √Z. To cover the case Θ=1/2 without logarithmic loss, consider h_*(y)=h(2y)+h(y/2). Then |yg'(y)|≤C h_*(y) for all y>0: for large y, h(y/2) absorbs any additional power or logarithm from differentiating the Gaussian, for small y one uses h(2y) and reciprocity, and on compacts the denominator is positive. Each dilate has signed mean of M given by 5610 with X/2 or 2X, so the total mean against h_* is O(1). Its mass as a measure dy/y is 1.

When Θ=1/2, the zero series of 5241 for J(exp v) is an absolutely convergent trigonometric series, up to a remainder O(exp(−3v/2)). Fix an ordinate γ and group multiplicities: the corresponding coefficient is nonzero. On each interval [v,v+D], the mean of the series multiplied by exp(−iγw) differs from that coefficient by less than half its modulus if D is sufficiently large, independently of v. It suffices to truncate in uniform norm and bound the means of the other finite exponentials by 2/(D|γ'−γ|). Thus there exists X between Z and exp(D)Z with |J(X)|≥c₀. By the differentiation identity of 5610, the integral of |M(Xy)| against h_* is ≫√X. Together with the signed mean O(1), both parts have integral ≫√X. For R=4√log X, the tails y outside [1/R,R] cost o(1) by |M(Xy)|≤Xy and the dilated Gaussians. Both excursions therefore occur between Z/(C√log Z) and CZ√log Z in this case. The wider annulus of the statement covers both alternatives. This controls magnitudes that are attained, not the maximal ones allowed.

Obstruction to narrowing both tails of 5610. Suppose a fixed nonzero kernel k, locally integrable, satisfies absolute bounds Ce^(−c y^p) at infinity and Ce^(−c y^(−q)) at zero and that its Mellin transform cancels all nontrivial zeros with multiplicity. Necessarily 1/p+1/q≥1. Indeed choose a real s₀ where the Mellin transform K does not vanish. At s=s₀+r exp(iθ), σ=Re s, the absolute integral gives log|K(s)|≤(σ_+/p+σ_−/q)log(2+|σ|)+O(1+|σ|), σ_± the positive and negative parts. This follows from the gamma integral after substituting y^p or y^(−q). The angular mean is at most (1/p+1/q)r log r/π+O(r). By Riemann–von Mangoldt the disc centred at s₀ contains at least (r/π)log r+O(r) zeros, counting both signs of the ordinate. Integrating the count against dr/r, Jensen requires a mean of at least (r/π)log r+O(r).

Even with p=q=2 it is impossible to strengthen both Gaussian tails by multiplying y² and y^(−2) in their exponents by (log y)^b and |log y|^b respectively with fixed b>0. For large u=|σ| each logarithmic moment is bounded by (u/2)(log u−b log log u)+O(u). In the coordinate w=|log y|, split into w≤(log u)/4, where the integral is ≤exp((u/4)log u+O(u)), and the remaining part where w^b≥((log u)/4)^b and the gamma integral suffices. On averaging, (b/π)r log log r+O(r) is subtracted from the Gaussian ceiling, contradicting Jensen. For that mean one may exclude |cos θ|<r^(−1/2), of negligible contribution, and on the rest log log(2+|σ|)=log log r+O(1). The kernel of 5610 attains p=q=2 (absorbing the prefactors into c). The obstruction is for absolute envelopes of ONE fixed kernel with complete spectral cancellation. In 2506 a different hypothesis was treated, a continuous bound on a strip for the spectral tail.

### Direct detector on M at the centre itself: one primitive per zero

The shift of the centre used above can be removed entirely. For EACH nontrivial zero ρ, β=Re ρ, there exist c_ρ>0 and X_ρ such that, for EVERY X≥X_ρ, with R=√(2log X), in [⌊X/R⌋,⌊XR⌋] both M≥c_ρ X^β and M≤−c_ρ X^β are attained. A single known zero on the critical line suffices to obtain the root scale unconditionally in this narrower annulus. Simplicity of the zero is not imposed.

Define k_ρ(y)=y^(−ρ)∫_y^∞ h(v)v^ρ dv/v. Since ξ(ρ)=0 one may use minus the integral from zero to y at the other end. Thus |k_ρ(y)|≤C_ρ h(y): for y≥2 one uses h(y)≍y⁴exp(−πy²) and the incomplete Gaussian integral (even gaining y^(−2)); for y≤1/2, the left-tail formula and h(y)=y^(−1)h(1/y) give the gain y². On compacts use strict positivity. The differential identity is (y∂_y+ρ)k_ρ=−h.

Put I(X)=∫M(Xy)k_ρ(y)dy/y and B(X)=(2π/X²−1)exp(−π/X²). Differentiate after changing the variable to u=Xy (the kernel and its derivative decay at both ends). One gets (X∂_X−ρ)I(X)=B(X) by 5610. As X↓0, M(u)=0 for u<1 and the Gaussian tail gives X^(−ρ)I(X)→0. Hence

    I(X)=X^ρ∫₀^X B(z)z^(−ρ) dz/z = X^ρ F(ρ)/ρ + O_ρ(1).

Indeed B(z)=∫_{1/z}^∞ f(v)dv/v; Fubini in the complete integral gives F(ρ)/ρ since β>0. The tail from X is O_ρ(X^(−β)). F(ρ)=ρ(ρ−1)Γ(ρ/2)π^(−ρ/2)/2 is nonzero. By domination, the integral of |M(Xy)|h(y) is ≫_ρ X^β in the measure dy/y. Its signed version is O(1). Removing both tails with the same R as in 5610 loses o(1) in absolute value. Each sign mass inside the annulus is therefore ≫_ρ X^β, and the fixed mass of the kernel carries that inequality to pointwise extremes. A single primitive also works for multiple zeros: the differential equation already has a single forced mode X^ρ.

If Θ>1/2, the crossing argument of 5610 now gives the exponent-1 count FOR BOTH orientations in [X/(C√log X),CX√log X] of ranks, with C fixed sufficiently large. For each s<Θ first take β>s and then β arbitrarily close to Θ when estimating the lower exponent of the count: the mass of lengths is ≫_ρ X^(1+β) by the boundedness of h(y)/y, each length is ≤X^(Θ+η+o(1)), and the short ranks sum to ≤X^(1+s+o(1)). The global sign conclusion still requires an independent arithmetic upper bound.

### Excursions survive signed averaging over an entire interval

Let L_λ(v)=(λ−1)^(−1)∫_1^λ M(vu)du, with 2≤λ≤3. At each centre X one may choose λ anew, keeping it fixed while traversing the annulus of that centre. For each zero ρ with real part β, in [X/R,XR], R=√(2log X), there are v_+,v_− with ±L_λ(v_±)≥c_ρ X^β, uniformly in λ. In particular the root size is attained for the signed average of M over ALL of [v,2v] in both orientations. The average has the exact arithmetic expression

    L_λ(v)=Σ_{n≤λv} μ(n) [λv−max(v,n)]_+ / ((λ−1)v).

Indeed the two tests of 5636 with L_λ in place of M are the averages in u of the identities in Xu. For h there is still a mean O(1); for k_ρ the mean is

    (F(ρ)/ρ) X^ρ (λ^(1+ρ)−1)/((1+ρ)(λ−1)) + O_ρ(1).

The multiplier has modulus bounded below on the allowed compact set because |λ^(1+ρ)|=λ^(1+β)>1. By |k_ρ|≤C_ρh the masses of both orientations of L_λ are ≫_ρ X^β. The physical cut and the passage to extremes are the same since |L_λ(v)|≤3v. The count in measure of starting points v with ±L_λ(v)>X^s is X^(1+o(1)) separately for s<Θ: each mass is ≫_ρ X^β, h(y)/y is bounded, the part below the cut contributes O(X^s), and the amplitude is Oη(X^(Θ+η+o(1))). First choose β arbitrarily close to Θ and then η small. These macroscopic intervals may overlap.

For DISJOINT intervals there is another conclusion. Fix 0<δ≤1 and divide the positive line into cells of the integer mesh of step H=⌊X^(1−δ)⌋. Keep all cells touching [X/R,XR]. For each s<Θ, the number of cells with signed average of M greater than X^s has exponent δ on the log X scale, and the same holds for the averages smaller than −X^s, at every sufficiently large centre.

To prove it, write d=H/X and a_j=j d. In the two integrals of 5636 replace q(y)=h(y)/y or k_ρ(y)/y by q(a_j) inside its cell. Both derivatives are globally bounded by two-sided decay and the equation for k_ρ. The error is Oη(d R X^(Θ+η+o(1))) by |M(z)|≪η z^(Θ+η); the region outside the union of cells costs o(1). Let A_j be the average of M over the physical cell. The discretized integrals are Σ_j d q(a_j) A_j. For β>max(s,Θ−δ) and η sufficiently small the error is o(X^β). By domination, and by the small signed mean for h, both discretized masses of A_j are ≫_ρ X^β. The positive weights sum to O(1) by the derivative bound and are individually O(d). Discarding |A_j|≤X^s costs O(X^s), and each remaining cell weighs at most X^(Θ+η−δ+o(1)). For each ε>0, taking β close to Θ and η small, eventually ≥X^(δ−ε) cells of each orientation remain. The total number is X^(δ+o(1)).

Therefore a fixed power saving in the frequency of excesses of ONE sign for these averages along a sequence of centres at each threshold s>1/2 suffices. A one-sided ceiling X^(1/2+o(1)) on the macroscopic averages over the whole annulus of starting points of a sequence would also suffice. Neither of those ceilings follows from the transfer. The internal novelty relative to 5636 is taking the sign AFTER the arithmetic average.

### Short recurrence and exponential exactness for a Riesz mean of growing order

Fix a centre X=e^t, m=⌈√t⌉ and keep m fixed throughout its annulus. Write W(y)=(1−y)_+^m and A_m(v)=Σ μ(n)W(n/v). It is a positive average of M(vu) over 0<u<1 with density m(1−u)^(m−1). This choice preserves the one-sided criterion of 5636. Indeed, the mean against h is still O(1), and integrating the identity for k_ρ yields

    (F(ρ)/ρ) X^ρ Γ(m+1)Γ(1+ρ)/Γ(m+1+ρ) + O_ρ(1).

The remainder O_ρ(1) of 5636 also holds for 0<Xu≤1 since there both I and the main term are bounded. For each fixed zero the complete gamma quotient has modulus ≍_ρ m^(−Reρ) by Stirling. When truncating the tails one uses |A_m(v)|≤v. Both excursions inside [X/R,XR], R=√(2log X), thus have magnitude ≫_ρ (X/m)^Reρ. No operator with variable m was derived inside the identity.

Let P=2^(m+1), and for d=2^i define a_d by the polynomial

    Σ_i a_(2^i) z^i = ∏_{h=−1}^{m−1}(1−2^(−h) z).
    c_j = Σ_{d|j, d=2^i, d≤P} a_d.

Thus c_1=1 and |c_j|≤Σ|a_d|≤∏_{h=−1}^∞(1+2^(−h))=O(1) uniformly. Let J be the smallest multiple of P that is ≥exp(3√t). Throughout the annulus one has

    A_m(v) = −Σ_{2≤j≤J} c_j A_m(v/j) + O(1)

with an absolute constant; the discarded tail even has modulus ≤X^(−1+o(1)). To see this, first sum over all j: since c=1*a and μ*1 is the convolution unit, the total sum is Σ_{d≤P} a_d W(d/v)=O(1). In every period the moments Σ_{j=1}^P c_j j^k vanish for 0≤k≤m. Indeed Σ_{d|P} a_d d^k Σ_{l≤P/d}l^k is a combination of Σ_d a_d d^h with −1≤h≤k−1, since Faulhaber has no constant term. All those moments vanish by the roots of the polynomial. By periodicity and translation they also vanish in each later complete period.

For a fixed n, W(nj/v) is polynomial up to j=v/n and zero afterwards. In the tail j>J only the period containing that cut can contribute; its nonzero terms are ≤(nP/v)^m. It suffices to consider n≤v/J. Summing their moduli and using the uniform bound on c gives O(P^(m+1) v/J^(m+1)). Since log v=t+O(log t), log P=(m+1)log 2 and log J≥3√t, this is ≤exp((log 2−2+o(1))t). The number of remaining dilations is exp(O(√log X)).

The pending part thus admits a formulation independent of the tail: a one-sided ceiling X^(1/2+o(1)) for −Σ_{2≤j≤J} c_j A_m(v/j) at all v of the annulus of a sequence of centres suffices. The suppression of the tail is unconditional. An induction majorizing each term separately in the norm with weight √v is not contractive: already |c_2|/√2=(3−2^(1−m))/√2>1 for m≥2. The required cancellation remains in the short sum. As antecedents, 5444 introduced a filter of growing order for the hyperbola faces and 5650 preserved the sign under averages; here the vanishing of moments in each period eliminates the tail of the recurrence.

The O(1) can also be removed: in the annulus v≥P, on expanding W(d/v) all powers below m disappear and the complete term is exactly −v^(−m)∏_{r=1}^{m+1}(2^r−1). Its modulus is exp(−(1+o(1))t^(3/2)). Hence the truncated recurrence has total error O(X^(−1)) for large X with the above choice of J.

### Moving all arguments to root scale and the cost of the move

With the data of 5668, take D=⌊√X⌋ and b the Dirichlet inverse of c. For odd r one has b_(2^i r)=μ(r)B_i with 2^i≤B_i≤C2^i uniformly: the inverse local series is (1−2z)^(−1)∏_{h=1}^{m−1}(1−2^(−h)z)^(−1). Hence Σ_{d≤D}|b_d|/d≪log²(2D). For each d≤D use the cut L_d=P ceil(max(J,2D/d)/P). On summing the recurrences at v/d with coefficients b_d, the coefficient of A_m(v/q) is K_q=Σ_{d|q,d≤D,q/d≤L_d} b_d c_(q/d). For q≤D only q=1 survives. For D<q≤2D one has K_q=−b_q. The upper support is O(DJ). By 5668, the tail error is O(P^(m+1)v J^(−m−1)log²(2D))=O(X^(−1)). The explicit term at v/d is still exp(−(1/2+o(1))t^(3/2)) even when summing the moduli, because d≤D. Hence A_m(v)=−Σ_{D<q≪DJ}K_q A_m(v/q)+O(X^(−1)): all arguments are X^(1/2+o(1)).

The critical absolute norm Σ_{q>D}|K_q|/√q is D^(1/2+o(1)): for the floor use the power of two in (D,2D]; for the ceiling first sum over d, using |c_j|≪1, and obtain O(√(DJ) log²(2D)). The truncated inversion is a classical hyperbola identity. The move with control of the tail does work, but it costs X^(1/4+o(1)) in the induction norm and increases the number of dilations.

### Tent identity: a square with favourable sign and the oscillating remainder

To look for a ONE-SIDED ceiling use instead W(y)=(1−y)_+−(1−2y)_+ and U(v)=Σ μ(n)W(n/v). This weight preserves the previous detection: U(v)=∫_0^1 [M(vu)−M(vu/2)]du. The mean against h is O(1), and against k_ρ one gets (F(ρ)/ρ)v^ρ (1−2^(−ρ))/(1+ρ)+O_ρ(1) when evaluating the detector at the centre v (integrating U(vy) against the kernel). The multiplier does not vanish. The argument of 5636 gives both excursions in the same annulus. Under RH the bound |U(v)|≪ε v^(1/2+ε) follows by integration.

For v≥4 and D=⌊√v⌋, put a_d=μ(d)1_{d≤D}. The identity μ=2a−a*a*1+(μ−a)*(μ−a)*1 agrees with 2a−a*a*1 up to v. The tent sum along a progression has an exact evaluation for every z>0:

    Σ_{l≥1} W(l/z) = z/4 − dist(z,2ℤ)^2/(4z).

It is obtained by subtracting the triangular sums at z and z/2; equivalently, the correction is −r²/(4z) if r=z mod 2 lies in [0,1], and −(2−r)²/(4z) in [1,2]. Hence

    U(v) = (2/v) Σ_{d≤D} d μ(d) − (v/4)(Σ_{d≤D} μ(d)/d)^2
           + (1/(4v)) Σ_{d,e≤D} μ(d)μ(e) de dist(v/(de),2ℤ)^2.

The first term is O(1). The second is always ≤0. In the last sum every de≤v^(3/4) costs O(√v log(2v)) in absolute value: the distance is ≤1 and Σ_{de≤Y}de≪Y² log(2Y). This localizes the pending ceiling to de>v^(3/4), with both indices between v^(1/4) and √v. It suffices to bound this last block by the positive square v(Σ μ(d)/d)^2/4 plus v^(1/2+o(1)), with the normalization 1/(4v) already included in the block. The credit of the square may be retained even if it is large. The hyperbola is classical; the choice of the tent here gives the distance to the even integer, the sign of the main term and an unconditional cut at root precision.

### Averaged tent: extraction of the constant mode and stable compression of the remainder

In 5352 the favourable hyperbola square and a remainder at nearly root scale already appeared, with a sieve and another weight. Here the distance to the even integer from 5699 is used to remove exactly an UNFAVOURABLE square (the constant mode of the remainder), keep the favourable one and obtain an explicit matrix with bounded coefficients.

At a centre X=e^t freeze q=⌈t⌉. Let Z=1+Σ_{j=1}^q V_j with V_j independent uniform on [0,1/q]; Z'=Z+1. The expectations are deterministic integrals. Use the detector T(v)=E[Z'U(Z'v)−ZU(Zv)]. In the identities of 5636 and 5699 the previous multiplier is multiplied by E[(Z')^(1+ρ)−Z^(1+ρ)]. As q tends to infinity, Z→3/2 in mean square and the new factor tends to (5/2)^(1+ρ)−(3/2)^(1+ρ), nonzero by the moduli. The mean against h remains bounded and |T(v)|≪v, so both excursions in the annulus of X are preserved for each fixed zero.

For each v in that annulus take the SAME D=⌊√(3v)⌋ in both hyperbolas. Indices >D in both factors do not contribute. The short term 2a of 5699 disappears in the difference, since d≤D≤v/2 for large v and zW(d/(zv))=d/v for 1≤z≤3. Write F(s)=dist(s,2ℤ)^2, z=v/(de), K_q(z)=E[F(Z'z)−F(Zz)]. One has exactly

    T(v)=−v (Σ_{d≤D}μ(d)/d)^2
          + (1/4)Σ_{d,e≤D} μ(d)μ(e) (de/v) K_q(v/(de)).

Here E[(Z')²−Z²]=2E[Z]+1=4. F has an absolutely convergent Fourier series of period 2 (coefficients O(1/n²) by piecewise integration). The constant mode cancels. For each nonzero n, the multiplier of the difference is (exp(iπnz)−1) E exp(iπnZz), with modulus ≤2 min(1,2q/(π|n|z))^q.

Put L=√v/(100q). If d<L or e<L, then z≥100q/√3 and the kernel is O(exp(−4q)). In ALL pairs one has z≥1/3; removing also |n|>200q costs O(exp(−4q)) pointwise. Since Σ_{d,e≤D}de/v=O(v), both errors together are O(X^(−2)). There remain the complete rectangle L≤d,e≤D and an averaged trigonometric polynomial with O(q) harmonics. No additional cut on de is imposed. Every index below L has been removed in absolute value, after the signed average.

A version with separated moments has only O(q³) coordinates and coefficients bounded independently of X. Take w=√v/d, w'=√v/e in I=[1/√3,100q]. In the finite sum replace each exponential exp(iπnZww') (and likewise with Z') by its Taylor polynomial of degree N=C q³, rounded, with C absolute and sufficiently large. On all of I² the real argument has modulus ≤6π·10⁶ q³. The remainder bound for real phase |s|^(N+1)/(N+1)! allows an error ≤exp(−4q) by choosing C sufficiently large. Take the real part. The polynomial P(w,w') so obtained is symmetric, of degree ≤N in each variable and uniformly bounded on I²: it uniformly approximates a sum of absolutely summable Fourier coefficients, independently of q. In particular, its coefficients b_ij in the Chebyshev basis in both variables, mapping I affinely to [−1,1] by l, have modulus O(1) by the orthogonality formula. This avoids deducing stability in the monomial basis from the Taylor bounds. It is a mathematical representation, not a numerical certification of its eigenvalues.

If S_i=Σ_{L≤d≤D} μ(d)(d/√v) T_i(l(√v/d)), where T_i is the Chebyshev polynomial, one gets

    T(v)=−v (Σ_{d≤D}μ(d)/d)^2 + (1/4)Σ_{i,j≤N} b_ij S_i S_j + O(X^(−2)).

It remains to prove the ceiling of this form evaluated at the genuine Möbius moments, allowing the credit of the square. The number of coordinates grows with the centre; the bound on the coefficients alone does not control the sums S_i.

### Odd steps, partial squares and a test with genuine signs

For the detector T of 5714 there is another exact decomposition of the COMPLETE form (including the favourable square). With D=⌊√(3v)⌋ and x=de/v, its kernel with minus sign is

    G_q(x)=E ∫_Z^{Z+1} N(t/x)dt,     N(y)=floor(y)−floor(y/2)=#{r odd: 1≤r≤y}.
    T(v)=−Σ_{d,e≤D} μ(d)μ(e)G_q(de/v).

Indeed zW(lx/z) has derivative 1_{lx<z<2lx} except at the two endpoints. Summing the derivatives and then integrating gives the formula; the values at discontinuities do not affect the integral. The earlier cancellation of the short term remains exact.

For each t and each odd r≤tv, put b=tv/r and H=min(D,⌊√b⌋). The sector d,e≤H contributes EXACTLY −M(H)^2 before integrating. Only the two orientations of pairs with d≤√b<e and de≤b remain, both indices ≤D. All partial squares are therefore extracted simultaneously, each with favourable sign. In these cross terms the whole band |log(e/d)|≤v^(−1/4) can be removed at cost O(√v log v), even summing moduli. Indeed both d and e are within O(√b v^(−1/4)) of the cut √b. For two distinct integers to exist in that interval, its length must be ≥1. Hence the number of pairs per cut is O(b v^(−1/2)) even when the interval is short. Summing over r≤3v and integrating proves the ceiling. This decomposition operates on all indices and is an alternative to the rectangular trimming of 5714; adding the two credits without redoing the accounting would count the main term twice.

There is a quantitative obstruction to controlling any remaining arithmetic block separately. Let v=(7T)^2, T a large integer and q=⌈log v⌉. Take an integer t between T and (1+η)T, coprime to 70 and with μ(t)=+1; η>0 will be a small constant. Retain the indices 7t and 10t. They lie within D, are distinct even across the two groups for small η and carry their genuine signs −1 and +1. There are ≍η T values of t for each fixed η: positive density of squarefree numbers coprime to 70 and PNT for the mean of μ sieved by the divisors of 70. For two indices in these groups, the uniform limit of the kernel as Z concentrates at 3/2 is G(x)=∫_{3/2}^{5/2}N(s/x)ds. On a compact set of x>0 the error bound is O(q^(−1/2)) by the displacement of the endpoints and the boundedness of N. G is continuous there by integration. At the three central products x=1,10/7,100/49 the respective entries of G are 1,1,45/98 (in the last only s≥100/49 contributes). The balance per ordered pair of labels t,t' on summing both orientations is therefore close to −1+2−45/98=53/98. Choosing η small and then T large keeps it above 1/4 uniformly. The restricted block of the complete form is thus ≫v, even including the corresponding part of the favourable square. For the genuine total, on the other hand, T(v)≪_A v/(log v)^A for each fixed A by the classical Mertens ceiling, integrated in the representation of 5699 and the bounded dilations of 5714 (for small arguments use the trivial bound). The non-retained terms together with the mixed ones must compensate that block to order v. It is an obstacle to block-by-block domination, not a violation of the proposed global bound.

### Simultaneous removal of rows and columns preserving two local moments

In the rectangle I=[N/(100q),√3N] of 5714, with N=√v, there is a subset S of integers with their original μ coefficients, of cardinality O_J(N/(log N)^J) for EACH fixed J with one and the same selection. Replacing μ(d) by μ(d)1_S(d) in both variables of the remainder of 5714 costs IN TOTAL O(N(log N)^C) for an absolute constant C, including the mixed terms. The favourable square can be kept complete. The result does not separately control a block chosen in advance like that of 5737.

Use cells of length H=⌊√N(log N)^2⌋ and keep the two incomplete edges whole. In a complete cell (b,b+H], let E be the maximal modulus of a partial sum of μ from b, and u=(d−b)/H. The two moments C₀=Σμ and C₁=Σuμ have modulus ≤2E by partial summation. One can retain O(1+E) sites of genuine sign, keeping C₀ exact and C₁ with error ≤2. To verify this, if E≥cH with c fixed and small retain everything. Otherwise each of the extreme quarters contains ≫H sites of each sign: the squarefree count gives H/(4ζ(2))+O(√N) and the imbalance is ≤2E. Rounding the endpoints costs O(1).

For the selection argument first allow fractions between 0 and 1 at the sites. In each of the four groups (extreme quarter and sign) any mass ≤K uniformly distributed in the group can be chosen, with K=C'(E+1) and C' absolute and large. Choose c small enough beforehand so that the capacities allow it, eventually in N. The sum of the four segments of mass vectors times ±(1,mean u) contains a disc of radius c'K centred at zero. Indeed, for every unit vector (a,b') some group direction has inner product ≥c' absolute: if the affine function a+b'u changes sign between quarters, at one of the extremes the appropriate sign gives a value separated from zero; formally, if ALL the products were ≤0, the values in the two quarters would have to cross zero in each quarter or be identically zero. Both alternatives are impossible for a unit vector. Uniform compactness over the four mean abscissas in [0,1/4] and [3/4,1] gives c'>0. By convex separation this proves the inclusion of the disc. Thus there is a fractional solution of mass O(E+1) with both moments exactly prescribed. Minimize the mass with those two equalities and boxes [0,1]; a vertex has at most two fractional entries. If their signs coincide their fractions sum to one, and if they are opposite they are equal, by integrality of C₀. Rounding while preserving C₀ alters C₁ by at most two units. The retained sites again have genuine weight ±1.

The mesh offset is chosen by minimizing the sum of 1+E over the complete cells. As in 5546, the maximal Theorem 1.1(i) over progressions gives ∫ E(b)db≪_J NH/(log N)^J for starting points in I (sum over dyadic domains comparable to their endpoints; H is in the admissible range uniformly). Averaging over the offset divides by H. Adding O(N/H+H) for cells and edges keeps the announced count. [Theorem of Matomäki, Radziwiłł, Shao, Tao and Teräväinen](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-026-01408-6).

For the cost use the real kernel R(d,e)=(de/(4v))K_q(v/(de)) truncated to |n|≤200q as in 5714. On I², its derivatives of orders j=1,2 in one variable are bounded by (log N)^C/N^j uniformly in the other: differentiate the finite exponentials with Z,Z' bounded, |n|≤200q and v/(de)=O(q²). The truncation error O(X^(−2)) by moduli remains valid on any subset. For each e, the sum removed in d costs on a cell O(H sup|∂R|+H³ sup|∂²R|) by first-order Taylor, the exact zeroth moment and the normalized error ≤2 of the first moment. Summing over cells it costs O((log N)^C(1+H²/N)), still polylogarithmic. Apply first to all columns and then to the retained rows; one obtains O(N(log N)^C') for both substitutions. In particular, if one also wants to perform the substitution inside the square only for d in I, apply the same one-dimensional estimate to N/d. The reciprocal sum changes by O((log N)^C/N), so its square multiplied by v changes by O(N(log N)^C') using the harmonic bound. Indices smaller than I remain in that square. The cardinality is still of exponent one in N according to the available ceiling; the inequality for the retained sub-block remains open.

### A single selection of indices for the whole annulus and its optimal size in exponent

It is possible to fix the subset BEFORE choosing v in the annulus. Moreover, the smallest number of genuine sites needed to preserve the following moments has exact exponent Θ on the scale N=√X. This improves the selection of 5750 (separately for each v) and pins down how far mere cardinality could close the sign.

Fix q=⌈log X⌉, R=√(2log X), D=⌊√(3XR)⌋ and L=(X/R)/(100qD). Throughout the annulus use the same D in the hyperbola of 5714: (D+1)²>3v and D≤v/2 eventually. For v/(de)=z, the pairs with some index <L have z>100q. For all others z≥1/(3R²), so the harmonics can be cut at 200qR² by the same exponential bound. The sum of the error by moduli is O(X^(−2)), uniformly, since Σ de/v=O(X polylog X) and the damping factor is ≤exp(−4q). In coordinates w=N/d, w'=N/e, the fixed rectangle is [N/D,N/L]² and z=(v/X)ww'. The argument of the exponentials is polylogarithmic: |n|≪qR², |w|,|w'|≪qR^(3/2) and v/X≤R. Taylor as in 5714 allows the same degree p−1 for the whole annulus, for example p=⌈C q^8⌉ with C absolute and sufficiently large. The amplitude of the approximating polynomial and its Chebyshev coefficients on this rectangle are O(1) independently of v. With l the affine map from [N/D,N/L] to [−1,1], define

    φ_i(d)=(d/D)T_i(l(N/d)), 0≤i<p;    y_i=Σ_{L≤d≤D} μ(d)φ_i(d).

The remainder in T(v) is (D²/(4v))Σ b_ij(v)y_i y_j +O(X^(−2)); D²/v is polylogarithmic. The favourable square uses the common D and remains intact.

Let m_X be the minimal cardinality of a subset of the d with μ(d)≠0 in [L,D] for which each signed moment differs from the original by at most p. Then

    ||y||∞−p ≤ m_X ≤ (log X)^C₁(1+||y||∞).

For the right-hand side, let G=Σ μ(d)² φ(d)φ(d)^T. Its smallest eigenvalue is ≥N/(log X)^C₂. Indeed, for a real vector c of Euclidean norm one, P_c=Σ c_i T_i has supremum at least 1/√2 by orthogonality. Markov's inequality gives a subinterval of length ≫1/p² in the normalized coordinate where |P_c|≥sup|P_c|/2. The preimage in d has length ≥N/polylog X by the explicit derivative of N/d and the endpoints L,D. There d/D≥1/polylog X; the squarefree estimate with error O(√D) leaves ≫N/polylog X sites. This proves the Gram bound uniformly in c.

Put λ=G^(−1)y and U=max|φ(d)·λ|≪(log X)^C₃||y||∞/N. If U≤1 take α=U/(1+U), otherwise α=1. On the squarefree sites, the weights θ_d=α+(1−α)μ(d)φ(d)·λ belong to [0,1] and reproduce y exactly when summed against μφ. Their mass is O(polylog X (1+||y||∞)), also if U>1 by the bound on U. Minimize the mass with the same p equalities and boxes. A vertex has at most p fractional entries. Discarding them changes each moment by ≤p, without introducing new labels. The left-hand side follows from |φ_i|≤1. Using that single subset in the form, the uniform error is O(N polylog X) by the bound on b_ij, the cardinality of the basis and |y_i|≤D. Indices smaller than L may still appear in the favourable square.

In particular m_X≪ N exp(−c(log N)^(3/5)/(log log N)^(1/5)) unconditionally, decreasing c. Indeed, by partial summation, each |y_i| costs only a polylogarithmic factor over the maximum of |M| on [L−1,D]. The variation of φ_i is polylogarithmic by Markov and monotonicity of l(N/d). Apply the Mertens estimate used in 5309; the logarithmic factors are absorbed by adjusting c. Likewise m_X≤N^(Θ+o(1)) by the classical bound in terms of Θ.

For the floor, 5714 gives for each fixed zero ρ a v in EACH annulus with T(v)≫_ρ X^Reρ. Discarding the negative square one obtains T(v)≤polylog X·||y||∞²+O(X^(−2)). Hence m_X+p≥N^Reρ/polylog X with a constant depending on the zero. Taking first the lower limit and then the supremum over the zeros, log(1+m_X)/log N→Θ. This includes Θ=1/2: the lower bound uses the original moments and does not subtract the rounding error of the form. To close, a construction with m_X≤N^(1/2+o(1)) along a divergent subsequence of centres would suffice. The unconditional subexponential saving above does not reach this exponent. The claimed optimality refers to preserving these moments with the stated tolerance.

### Selection using only primes and doubles of primes; structure of the intervals

For the p common moments of 5762 it suffices to choose sites among the primes r of [L,D] and the integers 2r with r an odd prime of that band in the variable 2r. Their labels are, respectively, −1 and +1. More precisely, for the genuine vector y there is a selection of O(polylog X (1+||y||∞)) sites of those two classes with error ≤p per coordinate. It can be described by O(p) intervals: in each one either all members of an indicated class are retained or none, with O(p) possible additional boundary sites. The count is still that of the sites, not of the intervals. The credit of the favourable square of 5762 is evaluated with complete μ.

Proof. For each real unit vector c, the polynomial P_c=Σ c_i T_i has supremum ≥1/√2 and, by Markov, an interval of length ≫p^(−2) where it keeps its sign and modulus ≥1/(2√2). The preimage in d has length ≥N/(log X)^C and d/D≥(log X)^(−C) (enlarge the fixed C). By the PNT with remainder of any logarithmic power, that interval contains ≥N/(log X)^C' primes, and also ≥N/(log X)^C' doubles of odd primes, uniformly in c. For the second class apply PNT to the interval divided by two. All constants here depend only on the fixed powers in 5762. Choose the class whose sign makes μ(d)P_c positive. Each site of that class in the preimage has projection c·(μφ)≥(log X)^(−C'').

Consider the convex body of sums of these vectors with fractions θ_d∈[0,1] and Σθ_d≤K. For K≤N/(log X)^C' its support function in EVERY unit direction is ≥K/(log X)^C'', filling K favourable sites (if K is not an integer, the last one is fractioned). By separation it contains the Euclidean ball centred at zero of that radius. Take K=(log X)^C''(1+||y||₂). It is admissible for large X by the unconditional Mertens estimate and the polylogarithmic variation used in 5762. Thus the p moments are represented exactly with fractional mass ≤K in these two classes.

To obtain the interval structure, minimize Σ[1+(d/D)^2]θ_d with the p exact equalities and boxes [0,1], without imposing K. The mass at the optimum does not exceed 2K. By finite duality there is a λ such that the sites with λ·μ(d)φ(d)>1+(d/D)^2 are necessarily retained and those with the strict reverse inequality are omitted. In the variable w=N/d the equality, for sign s=±1, is

    s (N/D) w P_λ(l(w)) = w²+(N/D)².

The difference polynomial has degree ≤max(p,2) and nonzero constant term. There are thus O(p) tie sites and O(p) decision intervals for the two classes together. Since the cost is positive, at the same w at most one sign satisfies the strict inequality. An optimal vertex has ≤p non-integer fractions. Discarding them adds error ≤p to each coordinate without inventing weights. The lower bound ||y||∞−p for the number of sites also holds for these structured selections. By 5762 their minimum preserves the exact exponent Θ with respect to N.

The application of PNT here only ensures the availability of vectors of both signs. Both the selected intervals and their occupation still depend on the moments of μ over ALL the original integers. Replacing, in the computation of y, the original sum by the unselected sum over primes and doubles of primes is not justified. In particular a ceiling √N for the number of occupied sites has not been proved.

### Two arithmetic cuts with reciprocal mass exactly zero
