After multiplying by N^(−s), the series of discrepancies by blocks converges locally uniformly in Re s>0. In Re s>1 it coincides with the series that changes the coefficients. This proves the continuation and the preservation of the principal parts.

Application to the nodes of 5894 and their shifts x with X^a≤x≤X², a>0 fixed. The SAME S changes D_λ(x) by O_a((log X)^C) uniformly, with C absolute and sufficiently large. Take all blocks touching |log(n/x)|≤5√(λ log X). Outside them the absolute cost is o(1) by the Gaussian tails even for x≤X². In each included block log N≍_a log X, and v↦Gλ(log(N/x)+v log 2) has supremum O(λ^(−1/2)) on the real interval. On the complex circle of radius 2 centred at 1/2 it is bounded by O(λ^(−1/2) exp(O(1/λ)))=X^o(1). Taylor gives error ≪X^o(1)4^(−m) on [0,1]. Only the rounding O(m/√λ) per block and a polylogarithmic number of blocks remain. The finite version of 5894 removes the tails at cost o(1) at its original nodes since coefficients of modulus ≤1 are erased.

The set is no longer recomputed when moving the centre; the linear observables keep the exponent. Compared with 6212, coherence across scales is obtained for the linear sum. Simultaneous preservation of the coprime balance for this fixed S has not been proved: removing the small primes from the labels of the semiprimes would be an additional constraint on the moments. Nor has cancellation at root scale been proved for the remaining series.

### Fixed support without small cofactors preserving the aggregate balance of the maximum

In each large block [N,2N) put Z=exp(log N/loglog N). There is a single fixed selection of indices to erase, with their genuine signs of μ, that includes ALL squarefree n=mr with r prime and m≤Z. The only additional indices it erases are of the same form with Z<m≤Z^10. Thus each survivor in the block satisfies n/P⁺(n)>Z (referring to nonzero coefficients). The remaining support preserves the principal parts of 1/ζ in Re s>0 and the linear Gaussian sums with the polylogarithmic error of 6230.

Moreover, for K(X)=⌈exp(30 log X/loglog X)⌉, this SAME selection, without adapting to the centre, preserves the signed sum Σ_{d≤K} E_d with error ≤x X^o(1) uniformly in X^a≤x≤X², a>0 fixed, in the common cut profile of 6138. It includes all crossings and the pairs between different bands. At the maximum of 6156 this precision suffices: the original aggregate sum is (1+o(1))D(x*)² when the maximum is nonzero. A one-sided ceiling x* X^o(1) for the aggregate sum on the remaining support, along a sequence of X, would exclude every exterior zero. There is no need to transfer each E_d individually.

Construction. For the admitted m require μ²(m)=1. Its prime r is unique and larger than Z^10 for large N. In the coordinate y∈[N,2N) the continuous density of each label is dy/(m log(y/m)) and the sign is −μ(m). The absolute mass of forced labels m≤Z has density ≤(1+o(1))log Z/log N. For EACH sign of the optional labels Z<m≤Z^10 the density is (9/(2ζ(2))+o(1))log Z/log N, uniformly in y. It follows by partial summation from Σ_{m≤v}μ²(m)∼v/ζ(2) and Σ_{m≤v}μ(m)=o(v); moreover log(y/m)∼log N uniformly. The coefficient 9/(2ζ(2)) exceeds one with a fixed margin.

To cancel the signed moments of the forced part with optional weights between zero and one, apply the convex separation of 6230. For any real polynomial P of the degree chosen there, the support function of the optional labels sums the positive part of their sign times P. In the continuous densities there is a margin ≫(N log Z/log N)∫|P| against the absolute cost of all the forced ones, whatever the sign of P. On passing to real counts each label m introduces by PNT and Abel an error O_J((N/m)(log N)^(−J)(1+degree²)‖P‖∞); the sum costs only O(log Z) in reciprocals. Markov absorbs the error exactly as in 6230. A vertex leaves at most degree+1 fractional coordinates in the WHOLE block. After rounding, the argument of 6230 for analytic functions and Gaussians applies unchanged because there are at most O(N) distinct indices. In the common cut-profile version, the additional error is o(1) by the tails of 6138 in the indicated range of centres. The initial blocks only change a Dirichlet polynomial.

Quadratic transfer. The change in the square without gcd restriction is ≤x X^o(1) by the linear estimate and the trivial ceiling of the profile. Now consider the pairs touching an erased index n=mr and having gcd>K. In the current support n≤x exp(O((loglog X)²)), so m≤Z(N)^10≤K(X) eventually (the factor 30 allows x≤X²). If the other coordinate were not a multiple of r, the gcd would divide m and be ≤K. So only multiples of r have to be paid for. Since r≥x X^(−o(1)), each erased row admits at most X^o(1) such multiples in the support; there are ≤x X^o(1) rows and each product of weights is ≤1/(4πλ). The absolute cost of the change in gcd>K is ≤x X^o(1). Subtracting both changes gives the estimate for gcd≤K. This argument also explains why, for the selection of fixed labels 2,3,5 of 6230, a cut K≥5 suffices to transfer the aggregate with the same error. The maximum is still selected on the original lists; the proof does not confer multiplicativity on the resulting support nor prove its ceiling.

### Concentration of the linear signal on products of primes of comparable size

In each block [N,2N), L=log N, k=⌊√L⌋, it suffices to keep a selection of squarefree integers with exactly k or k+1 prime factors. For j=k,k+1 the factors can ALL be taken between T_j=(N/8)^(1/j) and 16T_j. There is a single fixed selection across blocks that preserves the principal parts of 1/ζ in Re s>0 and the linear Gaussians of 6230 with polylogarithmic error. Moreover the selection can be made with ≤N exp(−c L^(3/5)/(log L)^(1/5)) integers per block for a constant c>0. The selection uses the moments of μ of the original block; the mere condition on the factorization does not prescribe which indices to keep.

Local supply. On any subinterval of the block of length ≥c₀ N/L⁴ (c₀ fixed positive), for EACH j there are at least N exp(−O(√L log L)) admissible integers. Choose j−1 distinct primes in [T_j,(1+1/j)T_j]. The PNT with remainder of arbitrary power of the logarithm gives ≫T_j/(j log T_j) primes. There are ≥(T_j/(C j² log T_j))^(j−1) subsets of that size. For each product d so chosen, the last prime must fall in the subinterval divided by d: its endpoints lie between (8/e)T_j and 16T_j, and the length is ≫T_j/L⁴. The same PNT guarantees ≫T_j/(L⁴ log T_j) choices uniformly, since log T_j≍√L. The largest prime identifies the last coordinate uniquely. Multiplying these bounds gives the announced supply. The two values of j provide opposite signs of μ.

For the moments in v=log(n/N)/log 2, of degree m=⌈L²⌉, let F=L^(3/5)/(log L)^(1/5). The SIGNED sum over the whole block against a polynomial P costs ≤N exp(−c₁F)‖P‖∞ by Mertens (5309), Abel and Markov, reducing the constant to absorb m². On the other hand the support function of the vectors μ(n)(1,v,…,v^m) of the available integers, with weights in [0,1], is ≥N exp(−O(√L log L))‖P‖∞ in each direction P. Indeed near a maximum of |P| there is an interval of length ≫1/m² in v where the sign is constant and |P|≥‖P‖∞/2. Apply the supply of the appropriate sign. Since √L log L=o(F), even with all weights limited by exp(−c₁F/2) the convex body contains the complete moment vector for every sufficiently large N.

Consequently there is a fractional solution of total mass ≤N exp(−c₁F/2), up to an irrelevant absolute factor. To make it integral, return to the cube [0,1], keep that bound on the total mass and the moment equalities, and choose a vertex. At most m+2 fractional coordinates remain. Rounding them to zero preserves the budget and alters each bounded test by ≤(m+2)‖P‖∞. The analytic argument of 6230, now for the difference between complete μ and retained μ, proves the continuation and sampling claims.

There is a characterization of the cost that avoids choosing the budget in advance. In each block choose the solution of minimal mass for the exact moments in the unit cube and round an optimal vertex as above. If Θ=sup Reρ, the limsup exponent in N of the retained count (adding 1 inside the logarithm) is exactly Θ. For the ceiling, replace the Mertens estimate in the separation by |M(y)|≪ε y^(Θ+ε); since the lower capacity is N^(1−o(1)), one obtains mass ≤N^(Θ+ε+o(1)) when Θ+ε<1 (otherwise use N). For the floor, a counting exponent smaller than Θ would give absolute convergence of the retained series in a half-plane containing some pole of 1/ζ with positive real part. This contradicts the preservation of its principal part. Hence a ceiling N^(1/2+o(1)) for this minimal cost would close the global sign; the local supply is proved, that budget not yet. This concentration only transfers the linear detector; it does not claim control of the gcd aggregate on this new support.

### The optimal cost separates from the abundance of candidates with relative precision

For the block and the degree m of 6260 define T(P)=Σ_{N≤n<2N} μ(n)P(log(n/N)/log 2) and B= sup_{deg P≤m, ‖P‖∞≤1}|T(P)| over real polynomials. Let M be the fractional minimum of 6260. For every fixed J and N sufficiently large,

    B ≤ M ≤ (1+O_J((log N)^(−J))) B.

If B=0 the minimum is zero. The result quantifies the loss relative to the ideal of being able to place mass of any sign at any point of the interval. In particular a more clever assignment of the same candidates cannot produce the root budget without bounding the functional on the original data.

The floor is immediate from any representation of the moments. For the ceiling fix δ=L^(−J) with J>0, L=log N. The supply proof of 6260 still gives N exp(−O_J(√L log L)) candidates of each sign on each interval of length ≥c δN/m²: for the last prime the relative window is now ≫L^(−4−J), and the PNT with any fixed saving of logarithms still applies at scale log T≍√L. For each P≠0 there is an interval of that length where P keeps its sign and |P|≥(1−δ)‖P‖∞, by Markov, even if the maximum falls at an endpoint. On that interval there are more than 2B+1 candidates of the correct sign, since B≤N exp(−cF) by 6260 and √L log L=o(F). In the cube of weights [0,1] impose the budget b=B/(1−δ). Its support function in direction P is at least b(1−δ)‖P‖∞: invest all the mass b there, allowing a last partial coordinate. Since this majorizes T(P) for every direction, the moment vector belongs to the body with budget b by separation. The conclusion for arbitrary J is obtained by taking N large; the rounding of an optimum costs at most m+2 in the count independently of J.

An arithmetic proof equivalent at the level of the exponent can use only m+1 prescribed sums: let H_j=T(C_j(2v−1)), 0≤j≤m, for the Chebyshev polynomials C_j. With H=(Σ H_j²)^(1/2), one has H/√(m+1)≤B≤√2 H. For the floor test each C_j separately; for the ceiling expand P in cosines after 2v−1=cos θ and use Parseval with dθ/π, which gives Euclidean norm of coefficients ≤√2 when ‖P‖∞≤1. Hence the root budget is equivalent to Σ H_j²≤N^(1+o(1)) on the large dyadic blocks. The diagonal term of this sum is unconditionally ≤N(m+1), since |C_j|≤1. What remains is exclusively a one-sided ceiling N^(1+o(1)) for the off-diagonal sum with its genuine signs and explicit kernel Σ_j C_j(2v_n−1)C_j(2v_r−1). The main diagnosis is that the supply of almost-primes is already optimal to arbitrary relative precision in powers of the logarithm; an improvement of the exponent would have to come from arithmetic cancellation.

### A moving set of good twists of logarithmic measure would suffice

Define per dyadic block F_N(z)=Σ_{N≤n<2N} μ(n)(n/N)^(−z). Let J>0 be fixed. At each N one may choose ARBITRARILY a measurable set E_N⊂[0,1] of length ≥(log N)^(−J). Then

    limsup_N log(1+sup_{τ∈E_N}|F_N(iτ)|)/log N = Θ.

In particular, to close the sign it suffices to obtain |F_N(iτ)|≤N^(1/2+o(1)) on some set of that length in EACH large block. Neither the sets nor the individual frequencies need to coincide between blocks. Equivalently, for almost every fixed τ in [0,1] the limsup over N is Θ: this last claim is justified at the end, and by itself it does not authorize choosing an exceptional twist in advance.

Proof. The classical Mertens bound at exponent Θ+η and Abel over the block give, for all complex z,
    |F_N(z)|≪η N^(Θ+η)(1+|z|) exp((log 2)|z|).
It is important to use this ambient exponent even at growing radii. If the limsup of the statement were <Θ, there would be δ>0 such that on the indicated sets the ceiling N^(Θ−δ) holds for all large N. Put t=log N and m=⌊c t/log t⌋ with 0<c<δ/(4(J+1)). In E_N one can choose m+1 real nodes τ_j in order with separations ≥|E_N|/(3(m+1)); for example use alternating strips of equal Lebesgue mass restricted to the set. The differences between nodes separated by h indices are ≥h times the minimal separation. Interpolate F_N at the points iτ_j. For |z|≤R fixed, the sum of moduli of the Lagrange cardinals is ≤(C_R/|E_N|)^m by the factorials j!(m−j)! of the denominator and Stirling. Thus the interpolant costs ≤N^(Θ−δ+cJ+o(1)).

Use the integral remainder formula on the circle |w|=m. The ratio of nodal products has modulus ≤((R+1)/(m−1))^(m+1), and the Cauchy factor for length and distance is O_R(1). By the ambient ceiling the remainder costs N^(Θ+η−c+o(1)). Choose η<c/4. One obtains the same fixed saving κ>0 relative to Θ for F_N on any fixed disc (the onset of the bound may depend on R). But Σ_N N^(−s)F_N(s) would then converge locally uniformly in Re s>Θ−κ, reducing κ if necessary. The sum coincides with 1/ζ in Re s>1 and its continuation would be holomorphic in a half-plane containing a zero of ζ, a contradiction. The opposite ceiling already comes from Abel.

For the almost-every-frequency claim, if there were a set of positive measure where the limsup were smaller than Θ, by a countable union some δ>0 and a common start would give the ceiling N^(Θ−δ) on a part of positive measure for all subsequent blocks. This contradicts what was proved. As a variant, it suffices that the mean of |F_N(iτ)|² over E_N be ≤N^(1+o(1)) (mean normalized by its measure): by Chebyshev at least half of the set is retained for the pointwise bound with a constant factor. The exact exponent of this result uses the argument by contradiction with Θ, without presupposing a fixed zero-free strip. It has not been proved that sets of twists with that arithmetic second moment exist in each block.

### Height of a moving window of twists and a limit to extrapolation

With F_N from 6284, L=log N, fix 0<α<1 and J>0. The limsup Θ is preserved for any E_N⊂[−L^α,L^α] of length ≥L^(−J). For the direct ceiling use Abel on that band. For the floor repeat the contradiction of 6284 with m=⌊cL/log L⌋. On a fixed compact set the cardinals sum to ≤[C_R(1+L^α)/|E_N|]^m. In the integral remainder over |w|=m the nodal ratio is bounded by [(R+L^α)/(m−L^α)]^(m+1). The costs in the exponent are respectively +c(J+α)+o(1) for the data and −c(1−α)+o(1) for the remainder relative to the ambient exponent Θ+η. Choose c with c(J+α)<δ/2 given a supposed saving δ, and then η<c(1−α)/2. The same continuation absurdity is obtained. Thus one may look for root cancellation even far from zero, with growing height of this magnitude.

At the extreme log T_N/log L→1, 1≤T_N≤L, there is instead a concrete model on the same integers: a fixed block-wise selection of the balanced products of 6260, with genuine μ coefficients on the retained ones and zero on the rest, whose untwisted sum is N^(1−o(1)) in EACH block, but whose transform has modulus O(L²) on the WHOLE window |τ−T_N|≤1. This is not a counterexample for complete μ. It excludes an extrapolation based only on coefficient size, balanced support and smallness on that window.

Real construction. In the coordinate u=log(n/N) put j=⌈2L/log L⌉, d=min((log 2)/(4j),1/T_N), θ=T_N d. Take the j-th convolution power of the real measure (δ₀−2cos(θ)δ_d+δ_{2d})/4. Its variation is ≤1 and its support lies in [0,log 2]. At frequency zero its transform equals [(1−cos θ)/2]^j=N^(−o(1)): 0<θ≤1 and log(1/θ)=o(log L) by the hypothesis on T_N. For |τ−T_N|≤1, the numerator factors as (1−exp(−i(τ−T_N)d))(1−exp(−i(τ+T_N)d)), so the modulus of the transform is ≤(d/2)^j≤exp(−(2+o(1))L).

Multiply the measure by N exp(−L^(7/10)). Its vector of polynomial moments up to degree ⌈L²⌉ belongs to the body reachable by the candidates of 6260: in each direction its projection in modulus is ≤N exp(−L^(7/10))‖P‖∞, smaller than the uniform capacity N exp(−O(√L log L))‖P‖∞. Choose a vertex and round. The moment at zero changes only by O(L²). For all frequencies of the window, approximate exp(−iτu) by a polynomial of degree ⌈L²⌉, with uniform error o(N^(−2)) by Taylor and the factorial since |τ|≤L+1. The variation of both measures costs O(N) and the rounding error O(L²), as claimed. Join the block selections. The decisive difference on going to the extreme regime is that a mass of exponent one may be hidden by a zero of growing multiplicity at moving height. To use an estimate for complete μ there, a property beyond those preserved by the model would be needed.

### Balance between height and length of the favourable region up to o(log N)

Put L=log N and choose any 1≤T=T_N=o(L). For fixed J it suffices that E_N⊂[−T,T] have measure w≥T(T/L)^J. The limsup of the exponent of sup_{E_N}|F_N(iτ)| is again Θ. In particular, even though T=L/log L lies above every fixed power L^α, α<1, a region of length L/(log L)^(J+1) suffices. The same result admits the normalized mean-square ceiling of 6284, reducing the measure by a factor 2.

Proof. Let A=log(L/T)→∞. Given a supposed saving δ in the exponent take m=⌊cL/A⌋ with c>0 small compared with δ/(J+1). At the separated nodes of 6284 the interpolant on each compact set costs N^(Θ−δ) times (C_R T/w)^m, which is ≤N^(Θ−δ+cJ+o(1)) including the first factor. On the circle of radius m the ambient ceiling is N^(Θ+η+o(1)), since m=o(L). Here m/T∼c exp(A)/A→∞ and log(m/T)=A−log A+O(1). The Cauchy remainder gains a factor ((R+T)/(m−T))^(m+1)≤N^(−c+o(1)). Choose η<c/4 and use the continuation contradiction of 6284. The ceiling on E_N comes from Abel since T≤L.

The relation has a limit for extrapolations based only on size and support. If 0<w≤T and B=log(T/w) satisfies B/A→∞, there is a block-wise selection with genuine μ signs, untwisted sum N^(1−o(1)) and transform O(L²) on [T−w,T]. To see this, apply the real construction of 6300 with j=max(1,⌈2L/B⌉), d=min((log 2)/(4j),1/T). On the moving window the modulus of the factor is ≤wd/2≤w/T; its j-th power costs ≤exp(−2L). At zero the logarithmic loss is O(j(1+log⁺(j/T)))=o(L), since j≪1+L/B, log⁺(j/T)≤A+O(1) and A≤log L. The support still lies in [0,log 2]. The same separation by moments and the rounding of 6300 realize the model for all blocks, also when w→0. Hence the thin-window example of 6300 does not contradict detection at nearby heights when a greater favourable length is available. The counterexample refers to selections, not to all coefficients of μ.

An operational case consists in averaging over [T/2,T] for T=L/g(L) with any g→∞ and T≥1. If that average of |F_N|² were N^(1+o(1)) in each block, the criterion with J=1 would hold eventually. The geometric result does not establish that average.

### Test in the real variable via a difference of growing order: exact diagonal

One can abandon the search for a set of twists and work with ONE mean square of interval sums. For the block [N,2N) put L=log N, T=√L, h=π/T and k=⌊L⌋. Give the point u_n=log(n/N) mass μ(n) and call ν that finite measure. Write A(u)=ν((u−h,u]) and

    Z(u)=2^(−k) Σ_{j=0}^k (−1)^j binom(k,j) A(u−jh),
    J_N=h^(−2)∫_R |Z(u)|²du.

Then the global sign is equivalent to the ceiling J_N≤N^(1+o(1)) on all large dyadic blocks. The real-variable form annihilates every polynomial trend of degree <k added to A at all points entering the difference. The intervals use the measure restricted to the block; the effects of its edges are included.

In Fourier, with the convention exp(−iτu), the multiplier from ν to Z/h has modulus |sinc(hτ/2)| |sin(hτ/2)|^k. On |τ−T|≤1 this modulus has a positive absolute floor: the first factor tends uniformly to 2/π, and the second is at least cos(h/2)^k, with kh²→π². By Plancherel the ceiling on J_N implies a root mean for |F_N(iτ)|² on a window of length 2 at height √L. Chebyshev and 6300 give the global sign (one may use [T−1,T] to respect the endpoint). Conversely under RH the root Mertens bound with margin implies |A(u)|≪_ε N^(1/2+ε), even at the two edges; the coefficients of Z have sum of moduli one and the support has length ≤log 2+(k+1)h. On integrating and dividing by h² only a polylogarithmic factor is lost.

One can also dispense with the integrator. J_N=Σ μ(n)μ(r) K_N(log(n/r)), with both indices in the block, where

    K_N(v)=h^(−2)4^(−k) Σ_{l=−k}^k (−1)^l binom(2k,k+l)(h−|v−lh|)_+.

It is obtained by overlapping two intervals and applying Vandermonde to the binomial coefficients. In particular K_N(0)=4^(−k)binom(2k,k)/h→1/(π√π). The diagonal of J_N is therefore asymptotic to N/(π√π ζ(2)), using the squarefree count. Thus the one-sided bound N^(1+o(1)) for the signed sum over n≠r with THIS real kernel suffices. Only |l|≤1+log(2)/h intervene; the alternating sign and the linear interpolation between lags are specified, with no favourable choice of data. The diagonal at scale N does not control the rest. The criterion uses 6300 and the normalized difference so that the observed part of the spectrum keeps constant gain even with k of order log N; no unconditional improvement of the energy ceiling is claimed.

### Energy of all primes and angle with the vector of composites

With the definitions of 6320 write P=Z_primes/h (including the − sign of μ) and C=Z_composites/h in the space L²(du). Put l=log 2, T=√L, L=log N. Unconditionally

    ‖P‖²=(N²/L³)(A(Tl)+o(1)),
    A(s)=4/(π³√π) Σ_{m odd in ℤ} [5−4 exp(−l²/π²)cos(ms)]/m⁴.

A is bounded above and below by strictly positive constants. The contribution of the prime-prime pairs exceeds the target diagonal by a power. The composites produce an almost opposite vector: for every fixed J, |‖C‖/‖P‖−1| and |⟨P,C⟩/‖P‖²+1| are O_J(L^(−J)). This includes all prime-composite cross terms of this energy, without removing indices.

Computation. The PNT replaces the prime mass in the block by N exp(u)/(L+u) du, 0≤u≤l, with discrepancy on every interval O_J(N/L^J). The error in the norm of the filtered vector is O_J(N L^(−J) h^(−1)√(l+(k+1)h)) by 6320. Replacing the density by N exp(u)/L costs O(N/L²) in norm: the convolution with the normalized box and the normalized binomial difference have L² operator norm ≤1. Both errors are o(N/L^(3/2)). The sign does not affect the norm. The squared modulus of the transform of exp(u)1_[0,l] is [5−4cos(lτ)]/(1+τ²).

In the Plancherel integral, centre at τ=mT+v for odd m, |v|≤T/2. The weight sin^(2k)(hτ/2) tends for fixed v to exp(−π²v²/4) and is dominated by exp(−c v²) there. The factor L sinc²(hτ/2)/(1+τ²) tends to 4/(π²m⁴) and is dominated by C/m⁴. Outside the union of those bands the sine has modulus ≤1/√2; its contribution after multiplying by L tends to zero. Dominating separately the constant, cos(lv) and sin(lv) terms allows keeping the moving phase mlT with uniform error after the absolutely convergent sum. The Gaussian integral equals 2/√π and its Fourier ratio at l is exp(−l²/π²). With the factor 1/(2π) this gives A.

For the complete balance, the Mertens bound of 5309 gives ‖P+C‖≤N exp(−c L^(3/5)/(log L)^(1/5)) by the same interval control and the norm of the difference, absorbing powers of L. Dividing by the floor obtained for ‖P‖ and using the triangle inequality and Cauchy proves both approximations, even with relative error exponential in that fractional power of L, reducing c. The oscillation of A comes from the two edges of the block, visible in the factor 5−4cos(lτ). This compensation still leaves a ceiling of exponent two for the residual energy; exponent one is needed.

### Exact arithmetic annihilation of the first layers by number of primes

There is a way to remove the prime term before choosing frequencies or estimating the edges of 6337. For EACH fixed integer k≥2 count r(n)=#{p|n:p>k²}. Let w_k(r) be the number of surjections from a set of r elements onto one of k elements. Put b_k(n)=μ(n) w_k(r(n)). Every n with fewer than k distinct prime factors >k² is removed exactly. On the remaining support the sign is the original one and the weight is computed integer by integer without data from other indices. For any fixed k the global sign is equivalent to the ONE-SIDED ceiling

    Σ_n b_k(n) exp(−n/x) ≤ O_{k,ε}(x^(1/2+ε)) for each ε>0 and every large x.

The reduction changes the weights. It does not claim that erasing those layers from the sum without reweighting suffices. For k=2, for example, the weight for r≥1 is 2^r−2; r=0 has weight zero by the combinatorial definition.

Proof. By inclusion-exclusion w_k(r)=Σ_{j=0}^k (−1)^(k−j) binom(k,j) j^r, with 0^0=1. For Re s>1 the Dirichlet series of b_k is the same combination of
    F_j(s)=∏_{p≤k²}(1−p^(−s)) ∏_{p>k²}(1−j p^(−s)).
In Re s>1/2 each F_j=H_j/ζ^j, with H_j holomorphic and zero-free. The correcting factors for p>k² are (1−j p^(−s))/(1−p^(−s))^j=1+O_{k,σ}(p^(−2σ)) in Re s≥σ>1/2. The threshold p>k² avoids the zeros of the numerators; the small finite factors are (1−p^(−s))^(1−j). This also gives uniform boundedness of H_j on each indicated closed half-plane. At every exterior zero ρ of multiplicity m the term j=k has a pole of order km with nonzero leading coefficient, while the others have smaller order. At 1 all terms are regular. On the whole real half-line s>1/2 the combination is analytic, since ζ has no zeros there.

Exponential smoothing multiplies this series by Γ(s) in Mellin with measure x^(−s)dx/x, without eliminating any pole. The integral over 0<x<1 is entire by the decay in 1/x (the coefficients have polynomial growth for fixed k). Under RH, for σ>1/2 the classical Mertens ceiling gives 1/ζ(s)=O_σ(1+|s|) in Re s≥σ by Abel; the decay of Γ allows shifting the inversion to that line, giving the two-sided ceiling. Conversely, if there were ρ with Reρ>σ>1/2, subtract the smoothed sum from C x^σ for x≥1, choosing C to obtain a nonnegative function under the assumed ceiling. Its Mellin transform keeps the pole at ρ and remains analytic on the whole real line to the right of σ. This contradicts Landau's theorem for transforms of nonnegative functions: its abscissa of convergence would be ≥Reρ and there must be a real singularity there. The proof does not need the exterior zero to be simple or extreme.

Antecedent of a local product in 611: factors 1+l p^(−s) and a subtraction were used to remove primes in another sum. Here the finite differences and the factors with minus sign allow removing any prescribed number of layers and guarantee that the exterior pole of maximal order survives. The arithmetic bound has not been proved for any of these sums.

### Deterministic removal of layers with weights between zero and one

Fix k≥2 and a set S of k−1 primes, for example the first ones. For n≥2, let e_k(n) be the sum of the products of log p over the subsets of k distinct primes dividing n and lying outside S. Put

    a(n)=μ(n) [∏_{p∈S,p|n}p / ∏_{p∈S}p] k! e_k(n)/(log n)^k,     a(1)=0.

Always |a(n)|≤|μ(n)|: the expansion of (log n)^k includes all permutations of each distinct product. The weight is strictly positive on the original sign when the squarefree integer has ≥k primes outside S, and zero otherwise. For each fixed k, the one-sided ceiling Σ a(n)exp(−n/x)≤O_{k,ε}(x^(1/2+ε)) for all ε>0 is equivalent to the global sign. No indices are selected by optimization and no coefficient is amplified. Compared with 6352, this is a modification of the weights themselves, not a normalization by a constant of the surjection weights, which grow without bound.

Proof. Let A(s)=Σ a(n)n^(−s), initially in Re s>1, and B(s)=(−∂_s)^k A(s). Put c=k!/∏_{p∈S}p and u_p=(log p)/(p^s−1). Marking k distinct factors in the Euler product of μ gives

    B(s)=(−1)^k c ζ(s)^(−1) ∏_{p∈S}[(1−p^(1−s))/(1−p^(−s))] · e_k((u_p)_{p∉S}).

To continue it use Newton's identities. The first power sum is −ζ′(s)/ζ(s)−Σ_{p∈S}u_p; each power sum j≥2 converges absolutely in Re s>1/2. In e_k the term of maximal degree in the first sum is its k-th power divided by k!; the other terms contain at most k−2 copies of that first sum. At s=1 there is at most a pole of order k in e_k, and in front there are k zeros counting that of 1/ζ and the k−1 finite factors. At an exterior zero ρ of multiplicity m the situation is different: none of the finite factors vanishes since Reρ<1. The first sum has residue −m and 1/ζ has a pole of order m. B therefore has a pole of order EXACTLY m+k. It is analytic on the whole real half-line s>1/2.

To recover A from B, in Re s>1 integrate B(s+t)t^(k−1)/(k−1)! over t≥0, by the Laplace identity for (log n)^(−k). The formula also provides continuation through neighbourhoods of the real half-line s>1/2: on each real compact set the bounded portions of the ray avoid the poles in a sufficiently small neighbourhood and the tail converges normally by the initial series without the term n=1. There is no need to postulate a global meromorphic continuation of A across the zeros. If A were holomorphic in a whole half-plane containing ρ, so would be its k-th derivative, contradicting the computed pole of B by uniqueness.

Under RH the same integral defines A in all of Re s>1/2 with at most polynomial growth on closed interior strips. In the bounded part of the integral this follows from the polynomial ceiling of 1/ζ by Abel, that of ζ′ outside a disc at 1 and the convergence of the higher power sums; in the disc the regularity already proved is used. For the tail in t use absolute convergence with uniform exponential decay. The Mellin shift with Γ(s) gives the two-sided ceiling with margin. Conversely, the one-sided Landau argument of 6352 holds because Γ(s)A(s) is analytic on the real axis s>1/2. Explicitly, a ceiling with exponent σ makes the difference with C x^σ nonnegative for x≥1; its Mellin transform cannot have abscissa of convergence >σ without a singularity on the real axis. Thus the integral gives A holomorphic in Re s>σ after dividing by Γ and restoring the range x<1. This excludes every zero with Reρ>σ via the k-th derivative. The arithmetic ceiling for the bounded coefficients remains open.

### Keeping almost all of the typical support with integer coefficients and removing both tails of ω

In each block [N,2N) put L=log N, U=loglog N. There is a fixed subset of the squarefree numbers, on which the EXACT values ±1 of μ are kept, with these simultaneous properties:

- Every survivor satisfies |ω(n)−U|≤U^(2/3) apart from finitely many initial blocks.
- In total O(N U^(−1/3)) squarefree indices of the block are removed, including all exceptions and the moment correction. Hence the retained support has density 1/ζ(2) among the integers.
- The difference of the two Dirichlet series continues holomorphically to Re s>0. The linear Gaussians of 6230 are likewise preserved with polylogarithmic error.

Local proof. Split the coordinate v of 6230 into equal cells of step ≍L^(−12), of physical length H≍N/L^12. In each cell the number of atypical integers is O(H U^(−1/3)) uniformly. Indeed, truncate ω to the primes ≤N^(1/10). The larger ones contribute O(1) factors to each integer of the block. The mean of the truncated sum is U+O(1) by Mertens and by counting multiples with unit error. The mean of the square of the difference from Σ_{p≤N^(1/10)}1/p is O(U): for distinct primes the count of multiples of pq has error O(1), and the aggregated errors after dividing by H are O((N^(1/5)+U N^(1/10))/H). The diagonal costs O(U). Chebyshev proves the local bound. In each cell there are moreover ≫H typical squarefree numbers of EACH sign: the count of μ² has error O(√N), that of μ is o(H) by quantitative Mertens, and at most the above atypical ones are removed.

Force the erasure of all atypical squarefree numbers. To compensate their moments allow erasing weights in [0,θ] of each typical squarefree number, with θ=C U^(−1/3). For any real polynomial P of degree ≤m=⌈L²⌉, the modulus of the forced contribution is bounded by C₁ N U^(−1/3)∫₀¹|P|dv. The support function of the optional part, without the factor θ, is at least c₁N∫|P|dv. Justification of both comparisons: in each cell the supremum and infimum of P differ by O(L^(−12)m²‖P‖∞), and likewise for its positive and negative parts. In the second comparison use the supply of the sign corresponding to each part. On summing, the discretization error relative to N∫|P| is O(L^(−12)m⁴)=o(1) by Markov and the bound ‖P‖∞≪m²∫|P|. In the first comparison the error also carries U^(−1/3) by the local count. Choose C so that the optional body contains the negative of the forced moments by convex separation.

The optional mass used is at most θN. Return to the unit cube with that budget constraint, take a vertex and round its ≤m+2 fractional coordinates toward zero. Erase the indices so designated, join the decisions by blocks and apply the analytic approximation argument of 6230 to the discrepancy. The conclusion about natural density follows by summing the errors of dyadic blocks; even a fraction of a block costs at most the total error of that block.

In particular a one-sided root ceiling for the exponential smoothing of this restricted μ suffices: the correction is holomorphic near each real point >1/2 and preserves the exterior poles; for the converse under RH the correction to the smoothing costs X^o(1). To see the latter directly, truncate the blocks above x(log x)² paying o(1); in the others, on a fixed circle around v=1/2 of radius between 1/2 and 1, Re(2^v)>0 and |exp(−N2^v/x)|≤1. Taylor and the rounding leave O((log N)²+1) per block, also for small N. Landau applies as in 6352. The theorem eliminates both tails, but inside the typical strip a moment-dependent selection must still be removed; the same detector is not claimed for the entire typical strip without that correction.

### The literal typical strip already has a bias of exponent one

For the uncorrected strip of 6386 put U=loglog N, a=⌈U−U^(2/3)⌉, b=⌊U+U^(2/3)⌋. Let S_N be its Möbius sum over [N,2N). With q(U)=exp(−U^(1/3)/2)/√(2πU),

    S_N = (−1)^b N q(U)/(2ζ(2)) · [exp(1/6)+(−1)^(a−b) exp(−1/6)+o(1)].

In particular the eventual sign in each block is that of the UPPER endpoint, even when the endpoints have different parities. The magnitude is N^(1−o(1)). Hence to reproduce the constant moment of μ with polylogarithmic error one must remove ≫N q(U) additional indices from the strip itself. The rarity of the tails in density does not allow ignoring them at root precision.

Computation. Use the classical uniform Selberg–Delange theorem for Σ_{n≤y} μ²(n) z^ω(n) on the compact set |z|≤1. In this case the regular factor comes from ∏_p(1+zp^(−s))(1−p^(−s))^z, locally convergent for Re s>1/2, uniformly in bounded z near s=1. The leading coefficient is H(z)=∏_p(1+z/p)(1−1/p)^z /Γ(z). Subtracting the endpoints of the block one obtains on |z|=1 the generating polynomial G_N(z)=N exp((z−1)U)H(z)+O(N/log N); changing y=N to 2N in the slow factor costs that same error. H is holomorphic on fixed discs in z, H(1)=1/ζ(2) and H(−1)=0. By Cauchy the error affects the partial sum of the first r+1 coefficients with alternating signs by O((r+1)N/log N).

The alternating sum from 0 to r is (−1)^r times the r-th coefficient of G_N(z)/(1+z). To apply the previous estimate divide only the MAIN term by 1+z and sum the individual errors. Q(z)=H(z)/(1+z) has a removable singularity at −1. For r=U±U^(2/3)+O(1),
    [z^r] exp(Uz) Q(z) = U^r/r! · [Q(r/U)+O(1/U)].
It follows by expanding Q: the exact multiplier for its j-th term is (r)_j/U^j (zero for j>r). For j≤r it deviates from (r/U)^j by at most (r/U)^j j²/r, by the product of the factors 1−i/r. The coefficients of Q decrease geometrically on any fixed disc of radius >1, and r/U→1. Hence Q(r/U)→1/(2ζ(2)). Stirling gives exp(−U)U^r/r!=q(U) exp(±1/6+o(1)); the cubic term of the expansion of the exponent has opposite signs and the integer rounding variations cost o(1) in that exponent. Subtracting the cumulative sums up to b and a−1 proves the formula. The complete moment Σμ(n) is o(N q(U)) by 5309.

One can also reach a cost O(N q(U)) for the INTERIOR moment correction (apart from the mandatory tails). In the cells of 6386, of length H₀≍N/(log N)^12, the same bias formula holds with H₀ in place of N and error o(H₀ q(U)), uniformly with a,b frozen. To justify this localization use Selberg–Delange up to 20 terms: on |z|=1 the remainder of the cumulative count is O(N/(log N)^20). The terms in y are y(log y)^(z−1−j) times holomorphic coefficients bounded on the circle. On subtracting endpoints, the derivatives of the terms with j≥1 cost O(H₀/log N) in total. The main term has derivative exp((z−1)U)H(z)+O(1/log N) throughout the cell. After extracting O(U) coefficients the remainders are still o(H₀ q(U)). Mertens controls the total balance in each cell with that same precision. Thus the SIGNED mass of the exceptions in each cell is O(H₀ q(U)). To prove the separation inequality replace P by a constant on each cell: in the error the absolute mass ≤H₀+1 is indeed paid, but its loss after summing is O(N L^(−12)m⁴∫|P|)=o(N q(U)∫|P|), with L=log N and m=⌈L²⌉. The constant part costs O(N q(U)∫|P|). The typical supply of both signs from 6386 then allows θ=C q(U), and the same vertex and rounding complete the construction. The upper and lower orders for the number of interior corrections coincide. This does not provide the root ceiling after the correction.

### Optimal correction only in the top layer and two spectrally distinct selections

Use a,b,U,q(U) from 6402 and ε_b=(−1)^b. All layers a≤ω<b can be left INTACT and only the layer ω=b corrected, with integer final coefficients. There are two fixed selections: one preserves, after rounding, the moments of complete μ to the precision of 6230; the other approximates them to zero with the same precision, unconditionally. In the CONSTANT moment exact equality can be obtained in each large block in both selections. In both, the fraction removed from the top layer is

    f_N + o(1),    f_N=[1+(−1)^(a−b) exp(−1/3)]/2.

In the selection that preserves μ, the amount removed is exactly |S_N−Σ_block μ|; in the other it is exactly |S_N|. These amounts are the smallest possible for the respective constant moments. Moreover, the two selections can be chosen so that they differ in ≤N exp(−cF) integers per block, F=L^(3/5)/(log L)^(1/5), L=log N. Only in those differences of the top layer can the two series be told apart.

Proof. In each cell of 6402 of physical length H₀, the number of squarefree integers of the top layer is (1+o(1))H₀ q(U) exp(1/6)/ζ(2), uniformly. It suffices to extract the coefficient b of the same Selberg–Delange expansion WITHOUT dividing the main term by 1+z. The signed balance of the band, multiplied by ε_b, is f_N times that quantity with error o(H₀ q(U)). Let V(P) be the sum of P over the top layer, W(P) the balance over the band and T(P) the balance of the full μ. For degree m=⌈L²⌉ the mesh and Markov of 6402 give
    |ε_b W(P)−f_N V(P)| ≤ o(1) N q(U)∫|P|,       V(|P|) ≫ N q(U)∫|P|.
In the first estimate, replace the polynomial by a constant per cell before using the local balances; the cost in modulus is o(N q(U)∫|P|). In the second, use the local density of the layer directly. The integrals are in the variable v of 6230.

The image of the symmetric box of perturbations |h_n|≤h over the layer has support function hV(|P|). By separation, the target ε_b W is attained by deletion weights t_n=f_N+h_n with max|h_n|=o(1). A fixed margin to 0 and 1 remains for the two possible values of f_N. Furthermore |T(P)|≤N exp(−c₁F)‖P‖∞ by 6260 and ‖P‖∞≪m²∫|P|. The same separation represents −ε_b T by new perturbations of supremum ≤exp(−c₂F), c₂<c₁ fixed, since m²/q(U)=exp(o(F)). Added to the previous ones they produce the other target ε_b(W−T). Both weight vectors lie in the unit cube.

To preserve closeness when rounding, assign at each site four probabilities to the deletion states (0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1), with the two marginals obtained. Couple their common ones first, so that the probability of disagreement is the absolute value of the difference of marginals. Preserve all moments of both marginals and impose a total disagreement cost ≤N exp(−c₂F). A vertex of this product of simplices cut by ≤2(m+1)+1 constraints has at most that number of non-deterministic sites: otherwise there is an admissible direction in the active faces respecting all constraints. At those sites round each marginal separately preserving its sum: the sum to be completed is an integer by the constant moment, between zero and the number of sites. Each bounded test loses only O(m‖P‖∞), and the additional disagreements are O(m). This fixes the two integer sets with the announced counts and closeness. A lexicographic rule allows fixing the choices per block.

By the proof of 6230, the series corrected toward zero is holomorphic in Re s>0 and its sums with exponential smoothing are polylogarithmic by 6386. The one corrected toward T differs from 1/ζ by a function holomorphic there. Thus the density of the layers, and even the asymptotically optimal fraction removed from the last layer, are compatible with two different behaviours. The correction toward T uses arithmetic moments of μ; proving the root ceiling for it remains pending.

### Deleting the primes while keeping each fixed prime dilation up to a finite error

There is a fixed selection f(n)∈{0,μ(n)}, supported on composites, whose series differs from 1/ζ by a function holomorphic in Re s>0 and which SIMULTANEOUSLY satisfies, for each fixed prime p,

    f(pn)=−f(n)  for (p,n)=1 and every n sufficiently large depending on p.

In particular, if A_f(s)=Σ f(n)n^(−s) and A_{f,p} restricts the sum to p∤n, then A_f(s)−(1−p^(−s)) A_{f,p}(s) is a Dirichlet polynomial in its initial half-plane. No global multiplicativity is claimed (it would be incompatible with deleting all primes). One obtains a finite repair per prime, explicit once the selection is fixed.

Construction by blocks of kernels [N,2N), N large dyadic. Put z=loglog N. Form a negative list with all primes r of the block and a positive one of semiprimes qr of the block with prime label z²<q≤z¹⁰ and r a large prime. The same moment procedure of 6230 allows choosing from the positive list an integer subset that matches the moments of the negative one, up to the ≤m+1 roundings of degree m=⌈(log N)²⌉. Indeed the ratio of continuous densities relative to the primes is (1+o(1))Σ_{z²<q≤z¹⁰}1/q→log 5>1. The PNT error per label costs O_J((N/q)(log N)^(−J)) in counting, and the sum of reciprocals is bounded. Markov and separation apply as in 6230. All representations qr are unique because r≫z¹⁰.

For EACH selected kernel c (also all primes of the block), delete ALL dc with d a divisor of the product of the primes ≤z. The Dirichlet expansion of each block is thereby multiplied by ∏_{p≤z}(1−p^(−s)). The packets are disjoint even across blocks: r is the largest prime of the deleted integer. For c=r or c=qr one has loglog r∼z uniformly. Hence the primes of d are ≤2loglog r, while q, if present, is >2loglog r. One recovers c from dc by keeping r and any other factor >2loglog r. The kernel in turn determines N and d. The initial block can be chosen so large that these separations hold in all packets; the initial primes and 1 are deleted separately, with a finite modification.

On any compact subset of Re s>0 the finite product costs ≤2^π(z)≤exp(O(z))=(log N)^O(1). The discrepancy of the kernels per block is O_compact(N^(−Re s) ((log N)²+1)) by 6230. The series of discrepancies of the packets therefore converges normally. For the dilation identity, outside the finitely many packets with z<p and the initial modifications, every family of multiples dc is closed under adding or removing p if the integer stays squarefree. Concretely p≤z is foreign to the kernel and is one of the free options of d. This proves the identity in both directions. Each exceptional packet is finite; a non-squarefree n does not cause an exception either.

The same fixed support preserves exponential smoothing with polylogarithmic error: for blocks N≤x(log x)² and each d, Taylor from 6386 is applied to exp(−dN2^v/x), whose modulus is ≤1 on the same complex disc, uniformly in d. One pays only (log N)^O(1) times the error per block. For the upper blocks use that the deleted indices are distinct and ≥N; the absolute tail is o(1). Thus the one-sided root criterion remains sufficient and necessary. Moreover all n with a FIXED squarefree cofactor multiplying a sufficiently large prime are already deleted by the packet of that prime. The gain over 6230 is that here a divisibility argument can reuse the local identity at each fixed p. An argument summing over p growing with x needs to control the exceptions in that range.

### Logarithmic threshold of the uniform identity at moving primes

One can choose ONE fixed selection f of 6436, supported on composites and preserving all principal parts of 1/ζ in Re s>0, such that for each positive c<1 and every sufficiently large n one SIMULTANEOUSLY has
    f(pn)=−f(n)   for every prime p≤c log n with p∤n.
The coefficient 1 is the largest possible supremum. For each c>1, any sign selection of μ that deletes all primes and satisfies that same law for all sufficiently large n is eventually zero. These statements leave undecided whether the supremum is attained exactly at c=1.

Subcritical construction. In the block of kernels [N,2N) now use L=log N and z=L log L. Keep labels z²<q≤z¹⁰, the same moments and all copies dc with d|∏_{p≤z}p. The PNT in the kernels remains uniform because log q=O(log L), and the supply in reciprocals tends to log 5. To recover c from the integer, use on the other factors the threshold 2(log r)loglog r, where r is the largest prime: the ratio of z to (log r)loglog r tends to 1 both for kernels r and qr. This separates labels and free factors and avoids counting an index twice.

In Re s≥σ>0 the product of costs in modulus is ≤∏_{p≤z}(1+p^(−σ))=exp(o_σ(L)); it suffices to sum over all integers up to z, since z=L log L. Thus the discrepancy per block remains summable on compact subsets of Re s>0. For exponential smoothing the total error is O_σ(x^σ) for every σ>0: for each d use on the complex disc of 6386 the bound |exp(−dN2^v/x)|≪_σ (x/(dN))^σ. Taylor and rounding cost O_σ((1+L²)(x/(dN))^σ); sum over d with the same product and then over the dyadic blocks. The initial finite error is bounded. Hence the sign criterion by smoothing is preserved.

In a packet log(dc)≤L+log 2+θ(z)=(1+o(1))z by PNT, where θ(z)=Σ_{p≤z}log p. For every c<1, if a deleted n grows, its z tends to infinity and p≤c log n is then one of the free options of the packet; if p∤n it can be added. If instead pn is deleted, p≤c log n≤c log(pn) is also free in that packet and can be removed. The packets of bounded blocks and the initial correction are finite. On squarefree integers this proves the equivalence of membership in both directions; outside them both coefficients are zero.

Supercritical obstruction. On squarefree integers write g(n)=f(n)/μ(n). Each allowed edge n↔pn preserves g. For c>1 the PNT implies that, for every sufficiently large index j, the next prime p_{j+1}≤c θ(p_j), since θ(p_j)∼p_j and p_{j+1}/p_j→1. From any sufficiently large squarefree n, first add the missing primes up to such a fixed initial p_j (all ≤c log n). The current integer contains the primorial of p_j and has logarithm ≥θ(p_j). The next prime can be added if missing, and one can continue indefinitely. Once the largest prime of n is passed, the integer obtained is EXACTLY the corresponding primorial. Hence any two sufficiently large squarefree integers are connected to a common primorial. g is constant there; a single deleted large prime fixes that constant at zero. An eventually zero sequence cannot preserve the poles of 1/ζ. The obstacle is one of arithmetic connectivity, not a failure of the Mertens estimate. The subcritical construction keeps a genuine uniform identity, but does not by itself give a root ceiling.

### The endpoint p≤log n is attained while preserving the detector at root precision

The pending endpoint of 6452 can be attained for the sign target. There is a FIXED selection f∈{0,μ}, supported on composites, satisfying f(pn)=−f(n) for all sufficiently large n and all primes p≤log n with (p,n)=1. Its discrepancy with μ is holomorphic in Re s>1/2 and the error of exponential smoothing is O(√x). Therefore a one-sided root ceiling with margin for f remains equivalent to the global sign. Here preservation is claimed in the open half-plane containing the exterior zeros; 6452 gave continuation of the discrepancy to Re s>0 in the subcritical regime.

Arithmetic barrier. For EVERY large Y there is z∈[Y/R,YR], R=√(2log Y), with z−θ(z)≥c√Y, c>0 absolute. Use the positive weight h of 5610 whose Mellin transform is ξ(s)=F(s)ζ(s), with F from 5241. The integral of ψ(Yv) against h(v)dv/v is computed on Re s>1 by the integrand Y^s ξ(s)(−ζ′/ζ)(s)/s. The product simplifies to −Y^s F(s)ζ′(s)/s and therefore has no poles at the nontrivial zeros. Shift to Re s=−1 by the gamma decay and the polynomial growth of ζ′; at 1 the residue is Yξ(1) and at 0 there is at most a constant. Thus the mean of ψ(Yv)−Yv is O(1). By PNT, ψ(t)−θ(t)∼√t from the contribution of squares of primes, and that difference is O(√t) uniformly (the higher powers cost O(t^(1/3)log t)). By dominated convergence the mean of Yv−θ(Yv) is (ξ(1/2)+o(1))√Y, with ξ(1/2)>0 since h>0. Both tails v outside [1/R,R] cost o(1) by |θ(Yv)−Yv|≪Yv and the reciprocal Gaussian decay of h. The fixed total mass ξ(0)>0 gives the announced point. Neither RH nor attainment of the supremum of real parts has been assumed.

In each block [N,2N) choose Y=D(log N)² with D fixed and large enough that the deficit exceeds 2log(2N). z can be chosen deterministically, for example as the first admissible rational in a fixed enumeration with deficit >log(2N) in the slightly enlarged annulus. The slack in the deficit and right-continuity between jumps allow that choice. One has z≪(log N)²√loglog N. Build packets of 6436 with this cut and with labels q in ((log N)^4,(log N)^12], of reciprocal mass tending to log 3>1. The same moment and rounding construction applies. To make the packets disjoint use the largest prime r of the integer and the separator (log r)^3: all free factors ≤z fall below and the label, if present, above. By construction, EVERY integer of the packet satisfies log(dc)≤log(2N)+θ(z)<z. Consequently the proof of closure under adding or removing p from 6452 works literally for p≤log n.

Control of the analytic cost. In Re s≥1/2, by partial summation and Chebyshev, Σ_{p≤z} p^(−1/2)≪√z/log z=o(log N) (for the z above). The product of costs is N^o(1). As in 6452, the discrepancy per block on compact subsets of the closed half-plane costs O(N^(−Re s+o(1))), summable over dyadic N, and for exponential smoothing σ=1/2 is used directly in the Taylor bound; the sum over blocks costs O(√x). The series of discrepancies converges normally in the open half-plane and is continuous on compacts up to the boundary from the right. Continuation to a neighbourhood of the whole boundary has not been proved. Under RH the smoothing of μ satisfies the root ceiling with margin; conversely the O(√x) error transfers a one-sided ceiling for f to that of μ, which excludes the exterior zeros by Landau. Together with 6452 this fixes the EXACT uniform threshold for preserving the sign criterion without primes. The root estimate for the sum of f remains pending.

### Exact components of the critical dilations and membership test by tail products

On squarefree integers join n with pn when p∤n and p≤log n. Each component has a unique maximum M for divisibility. To see this, choose by 6466 a z larger than all factors of n with θ(z)<z. The primorial P(z) contains n and every divisor of it has logarithm <z: no edge leaves the set of divisors. From n add admissible primes until stopping, in a finite set. Every terminal squarefree multiple of n contains each prime that is added: by induction its logarithm dominates that of the current state, and being terminal it already contains that prime. Thus the final state is the smallest terminal multiple; it is independent of the order. The endpoints of each edge have the same terminal multiples. Conversely each integer is connected to its final state. This classifies even the components whose maximum has isolated factors larger than log M.

For terminal M, membership of d|M in its component has a search-free test: for each prime p|M absent from d require
  p ≤ θ(p−) + log(product of the q|d with q≥p).
Also require that d contain all primes of M larger than log M. In the formula only the absent p≤log M need to be tested; by terminality of M all primes smaller than those p divide M. Add the absent ones in increasing order: the right-hand side is exactly the logarithm of the state before adding p. If it fails, no larger absent prime is admissible and the process terminates. If it passes to the end one obtains M. This exact test makes explicit the dependence between the choices of divisors.

In particular, if m is the smallest integer of the component and b satisfies θ(b)+b≤log m, all primes up to b can be removed or added independently: from each d removing any of them leaves an integer of logarithm ≥log m−θ(b)≥b, so each step is reversible. Hence the component decomposes into disjoint cubes u·{v:v|P(b)} with (u,P(b))=1. For components with m in the range of validity of 6466, f/μ is constant. Its contribution to the smoothing is exactly the sum over the bases u of f(u)·[∏_{p≤b}(I−D_p)]w(u/x), with D_p w(t)=w(pt), w(t)=exp(−t). Finiteness of each component does not authorize summing bounds without controlling how many bases u intervene; that joint estimate remains open.

### Two-sided obstruction to absolute control by critical components

For the concrete selection of 6466, let S_C(x)=Σ_{n∈C} f(n)exp(−n/x). The two parts of the sum by components of 6476 satisfy, for all sufficiently large x,
  Σ_C max(S_C(x),0) ≫ x/(log x)²,     Σ_C max(−S_C(x),0) ≫ x/(log x)³.
Thus the one-sided root ceiling requires compensation between components even after summing each one exactly.

Proof. For k=2,3 take u a product of k distinct primes in [(2x)^(1/k),2(2x)^(1/k)]. Then 2x≤u≤2^(k+1)x. By PNT and unique factorization there are ≫x/(log x)^k products. A single cut z of the barrier of 6466, with Y=D(log x)² and D fixed and sufficiently large, satisfies θ(z)+log(16x)<z and z≪(log x)²√loglog x. All primes of u exceed z. The family u·{d:d|P(z)} is closed under edges in both directions: each element has logarithm <z, every admissible prime when going up or down is smaller than z and does not divide u. Consequently the component of u has minimum u and two distinct u give distinct components (also between k=2 and k=3).

The element u survives deletion: with r its largest prime, all its remaining factors are of the same order as r, while the factors other than r in any deleted packet of 6466 are at most O((log r)^12), by kernel recovery and log N asymptotic to log r. Hence f(u)=(−1)^k. All other elements of its component are multiples ju with j≥2, and |f|≤1. For t=u/x∈[2,16], the total error they can introduce is bounded by exp(−t)/(exp(t)−1). There remains (−1)^k S_C(x)≥exp(−16)(1−1/(exp(2)−1))>0. Summing over the above minima proves the bounds. The series over components converges absolutely for each fixed x by comparison with Σ exp(−n/x). The estimate does not determine the sign of the balance.

### Common profile of components with kernel free of small factors at aggregate root precision

Fix B>1. Take the cut z of 6486 with θ(z)+log(Bx)<z and z>log(Bx), adjusting the constant D. Let U be any set of squarefree u in [x/2,Bx] whose prime factors are all >z. Their components are disjoint and contained in u·{d:d|P(z)}, by the closure argument of 6486. Deleted kernels are also admitted. Define K(t)=Σ_{d≥1} μ(d) exp(−dt). Uniformly in U one has
  Σ_{u∈U} |S_{C(u)}(x)−f(u)K(u/x)| ≪_B √x.
Indeed, for every squarefree d composed of primes ≤log u one obtains ud from u by adding those primes successively. Along these edges f changes sign. For d≤log u the coefficients therefore coincide exactly, including the squares whose coefficient is zero. For d>log u the difference of coefficients is at most 2. With t=u/x≥1/2 the geometric tail costs O(exp(−t log u))=O(x^(−1/2)) per kernel and there are O_B(x) kernels. The conclusion holds for any number of large factors and any sign selection made after constructing f.

Comparison corollary. For any disjoint pairing of surviving kernels of opposite signs in U, the sum of the absolute values of the paired contributions is
  ≪_B √x + (1/x) Σ_{pairs (u,v)} |u−v|.
This follows from the uniform bound |K′(t)|≤Σ d exp(−d/2) and from summing the previous error only once. In this way a total distance cost O(x^(3/2)) suffices to control all pairs at root precision. No such pairing with control of leftovers has been constructed, nor have the minima below x/2 or with factors ≤z been covered here.

### First inaccessible prime and full cube for a minimum with protected factors

In the setting of 6496, with u≤Bx, u squarefree and all its factors >z, let h be the first prime p satisfying p−θ(p−)>log u. It exists and is ≤ the first prime after z: for that prime θ(p−)=θ(z) and θ(z)+log u<z. From u add the primes p<h in order. At each step the available logarithm is precisely log u+θ(p−), and all primes added are ≤z. On reaching h the state M=u∏_{p<h}p is terminal: its logarithm is smaller than h and it contains all smaller primes. Each ud with d a divisor of that product reaches the same M following the same order and omitting the primes already present, since at each step the state contains at least the factors available in the ascent from u. Conversely every member of the component divides M by 6476 and is a multiple of u by the barrier of 6486. The whole component is therefore exactly that cube. For u sufficiently large the dilation identity, applied to the paths up to M, gives f(ud)=μ(d)f(u) throughout it.

By the quantitative PNT used in 6436, for every fixed A one has |p−θ(p−)|≪_A p/(log p)^A (the difference θ(p)−θ(p−)=log p is admissible). In particular h>log u and h≫_A (log u)(loglog u)^A. The profile K(u/x) coincides coefficient by coefficient up to d<h: every squarefree d<h divides the product, and both coefficients vanish on non-squarefree integers. For t=u/x the discrepancy of the group is bounded by exp(−th)/(1−exp(−t)). Fixing B>1, a≥0 and H>0, the absolute sum of these discrepancies over the WHOLE range x/(loglog x)^a≤u≤Bx with factors >z is O_{B,a,H}(x^(−H)). Indeed log u∼log x uniformly; choosing A>a one gets th/log x→∞ and the inverse denominator costs O(1+(loglog x)^a). There are O_B(x) terms. This control concerns the approximation by the profile, not the value of the sum of profiles. The sign pairing and the unprotected kernels remain open.

### Exact exponent of the absolute mass with subpower large-prime part

Keep the cut z of 6486, so that z=(log x)^{2+o(1)}. For squarefree n let R_z(n) be the product of its factors >z (empty product 1). For any U=U(x)≥1 with log U=o(log x),
  Σ_{R_z(n)≤U} |f(n)| exp(−n/x) = x^{1/2+o(1)}
(summing over squarefree integers). In particular this portion, even taken in absolute value, is o(x^β) for each fixed β>1/2.

Upper bound: write n=ud, u≤U and d|P(z). Use exp(−ud/x)≤(x/(ud))^{1/2}, Σ_{u≤U} u^(−1/2)≤2√U and ∏_{p≤z}(1+p^(−1/2))≤exp(O(√z/log z))=exp(o(log x)) by the specific bound z≪(log x)²√loglog x of 6466. This includes all divisors d and all components to which they may belong.

Lower bound: R_z(n)=1 suffices. Choose k=⌊log x/log z⌋ distinct primes in [z/2,z]. The product n≤x has weight ≥1/e. No packet of 6466 deletes n for large x: all its factors, including the second largest, exceed any fixed constant times (log r)^12 where r is the largest. There are m∼z/(2log z) eligible primes; m/k→∞, and log binom(m,k)≥k log(m/k)=(1/2+o(1))log x, using log z∼2loglog x. Thus the upper exponent is optimal for the absolute mass. The o(1) notation in the exponent does not provide O(√x). To exclude an exterior oscillation of fixed exponent this precision does suffice. The balance of the terms with R_z(n)>U remains pending.

### Threshold 2β−1 for localizing an oscillation and saturation of both signs in each layer

For fixed 0<δ<1, the layer x^δ/4≤R_z(n)≤x^δ has positive and negative exponential mass (taken in magnitude) both x^{(1+δ)/2+o(1)}. The same upper exponent holds when including all R_z(n)≤x^δ. Indeed 6512 with U=x^δ gives the upper bound √(xU)exp(o(log x)), by the same Euler product.

For each sign take u=qr with q,r distinct primes between x^{δ/2}/2 and x^{δ/2}. There are x^{δ+o(1)} unordered pairs. Multiply by the product d of k distinct primes in [z/2,z], where k is the largest integer of the desired parity ≤(1−δ)log x/log z. The choice of parity alters k by O(1). There are x^{(1−δ)/2+o(1)} choices on a logarithmic scale, by the same binomial lower bound of 6512 and the upper bound binom(m,k)≤(em/k)^k. The integers ud are distinct by factorization, have R_z(ud)=u and ud≤x. The two large factors prevent deletion by 6466, hence f(ud)=(−1)^k. The weight ≥1/e completes both lower bounds.

Consequence for the detector: given an oscillation of size at least c x^β along a subsequence, β>1/2, every fixed cut δ<2β−1 removes only o(x^β) in absolute value. The complement R_z>x^δ preserves the sign and magnitude of that oscillation up to a relative error o(1). For δ>2β−1 the layer itself contains separately more mass of each sign than x^β: extending this removal requires cancellation. The equality case is not decided by exponents. This quantifies the forced region without assuming a pointwise oscillation exactly at the real part of a zero; if the available bound loses an ε, it is applied to the exponent actually obtained.

### A single logarithmic cut groups the full detector with absolute root remainder

For large x put y=(49/100)log x, P=∏_{p≤y}p, J=2^{π(y)} and U=√x/J. Then, with W_y(t)=Σ_{d|P}μ(d)exp(−dt),
  Σ_{n≥1} f(n)exp(−n/x) = Σ_{u>U, (u,P)=1} f(u) W_y(u/x) + E(x),       |E(x)|≤√x.
Each kernel contributing to the sum on the right is composite. The identity covers all sizes u>U, even those with factors between y and the cut z of 6486.

Indeed each squarefree n has a unique decomposition ud, (u,P)=1 and d|P. The u≤U produce at most UJ=√x integers, counting even the deleted ones. For u>U we have log u≥log U=(1/2−o(1))log x>y since π(y)=o(log x). Each prime of d can be added in any order using 6466, and therefore f(ud)=μ(d)f(u). The regrouping is absolutely convergent at fixed x. Here the family of divisors need not be a maximal component. The cut is chosen to apply the identity to all retained kernels, without requiring a barrier above each group. With the same y, the range R_y(n)≤x^δ contains at most x^{δ+o(1)} squarefree integers for every fixed positive δ; for an oscillation x^β any δ<β can be removed. R_y and R_z are different quantities.

The remaining signed problem is concentrated in a single sum over composite kernels with explicit weight. The error of the reduction was obtained by counting integers, without hypotheses on the sign. Neither this count nor the dilation identity controls the balance of the large kernels.

### Detector on a dyadic interval with composite kernels between x/A(x) and 2x

For any A(x)→∞ as slowly as desired, with A(x)≤√x, a detector of every exterior zero can be localized in that interval of kernels, with exact equality. Let y be the largest prime for which the primorial P(y)≤A(x), and P=P(y); then y→∞ and y=O(log A) by PNT. To guarantee y≤log(x/A) throughout the construction use P≤min(A,x^{1/4}), which preserves the announced range. For large x, y≤(1/3)log x. Write
  D(x)=Σ_{x<n≤2x} f(n)=Σ_{x/A<u≤2x,(u,P)=1} f(u) Σ_{d|P, x<ud≤2x} μ(d).
Indeed each squarefree term has a single decomposition, and ud>x forces u>x/P≥x/A. In all those kernels log u≥(1/2)log x>y, so that 6466 gives the exact coefficient. The primes are deleted. The inner weight is an integer sum of signs over an interval of divisors consecutive in order of size.

By 6466, F(s)=Σ f(n)n^(−s) has the polar part of 1/ζ in Re s>1/2. For Re s>1 one has ∫₀^∞ D(x)x^(−s−1)dx=F(s)(2^s−1)/s by integrating each indicator; the portion x<1 is entire because D vanishes below 1/2. The multiplier does not vanish in Re s>0. Every exterior zero of real part β therefore gives a pole in this detector. More precisely, for each σ between 1/2 and β, D(x) cannot be bounded one-sidedly by C x^σ for all large x, in either direction. If it were, the transform of C x^σ±D(x) on [X,∞), with X sufficiently large and the appropriate sign, would by Landau have a real singularity at its abscissa of convergence (≥β by the pole), while its continuation is regular at all reals ≥β; ζ has no real zeros there. Hence proving a one-sided ceiling D(x)≪_ε x^{1/2+ε} for every ε>0 would suffice for the global sign. The exponential smoothing error of 6466 is not transferred to this sharp cut, nor is the converse direction under RH claimed here for this selection.

### Compact window equivalent in both directions for the critical selection

For the same f of 6466 write H(s)=F(s)−1/ζ(s). In 1/2≤σ≤2 its blockwise continuation satisfies |H(σ+it)|≤exp(C√(1+|t|)), increasing C for the initial blocks. Indeed, for L=log N≤K√(1+|t|) the absolute bound of the block is O(N·exp(o(L))) by the Euler cost of 6466, summable in that range within the announced majorant. In the rest the degree m≥L² dominates K²|t|. On the disc |v|≤2 the function 2^(−sv) has modulus ≤exp(C₁(1+|t|)); the Taylor polynomial truncated at m leaves on [0,1] an error O(exp(C₁(1+|t|))2^(−m))≤N^(−3) choosing K large. Applying the rounding of 6230 gives O(N^(−σ)(1+m)exp(o(L))) per block, summable uniformly in the tail. This estimate explicitly controls the vertical growth that was missing in the sharp cut.

Build a density k on [0,log 2] as the law of the sum of independent uniforms on [0,a_j], a_j=c j^(−3/2), with Σa_j=log 2. Its transform B(s)=∫exp(sv)k(v)dv is the product of (exp(a_j s)−1)/(a_j s), convergent and zero-free in Re s>0 (Σa_j<∞ and no factor vanishes). Uniformly in the previous strip, each factor costs ≤exp(σ a_j)min(1,2/(|s|a_j)). For j≤c'|t|^{2/3}, with c' small, the minimum is ≤1/2. Thus |B(s)|≪exp(−c''|t|^{2/3}), which moreover proves by inversion that the law has a smooth density. This decay dominates the vertical bound of H. With w(t)=k(log t), the discrepancy between the sums of f and of μ with weight w(n/x) is O(√x): invert B(s)H(s)x^s at σ=2, shift to σ>1/2 and pass to the limit by domination and continuity at the boundary from 6466.

Under RH, the classical Mertens bound O_ε(x^{1/2+ε}) and Abel give the same two-sided ceiling for the sum of μ with w (fixed variation). Conversely B preserves each exterior pole and the one-sided Landau argument of 6540 applies literally. Hence for this single explicit weight, positive in the sense w≥0, smooth, supported on [1,2], the one-sided ceiling with every margin ε>0 is sufficient and necessary. The same exact grouping of 6540 works replacing the indicator by w(ud/x) (the endpoints of the support have value zero). The ceiling for the grouped sum remains unproved.

### Fixed selection with equivalence for the sharp count, without hypotheses in the selection rule

Change the selection of kernels of 6466, keeping the labels, the cuts z and all divisor packets. With L=log N divide [N,2N) into J=max(1,⌊√N exp(−√L)⌋) intervals of equal length H=N/J. Attempt the moment feasibility of 6230, of degree m=⌈L²⌉, separately in ALL of them. If all pass, use the vertex and rounding in each interval; if any fails, apply 6230 to the original full block, feasible by 6466. It is a single deterministic selection g independent of RH. In each subinterval use the normalized affine coordinate of log n. Fractional exactness for polynomials in that coordinate includes, by affine change, the polynomials in the coordinate of the full block.

Unconditionally there are at most J(m+1) roundings. By 6230, approximating n^(−s) on the full block and summing the approximation errors over the number of kernels, the cost on compact subsets of Re s>1/2 is O(N^(−Re s)(N^(1/2+o(1))+1)), before the Euler factor N^o(1). It is summable over dyadic blocks. Thus G(s)−1/ζ(s) is holomorphic there. g preserves the critical identity and the support on composites because the geometric rules of 6466 are the same.

Under RH all subintervals pass for large N. On any prefix of one of them the prime count differs from the integral dt/log t by O(√N L^2) by the PNT under RH. For each label q≤L^12 the same result is used in the variable t/q, and even summing crudely over the O(L^12) labels the total error is O(√N L^14). The continuous density of semiprimes dominates the prime one by a ratio tending uniformly to log 3>1. For a polynomial of sup norm 1 on the subinterval, the variation of it and of its positive part costs O(m²) by Markov in the normalized coordinate. In the support inequality of 6230 there remains a continuous margin ≫H/(L(1+m²)), since the integral of the modulus in normalized coordinate is ≫1/(1+m²) and the Jacobian is comparable to H. The discrete error O(√N L^14(1+m²)) is absorbed by H∼√N exp(√L). This verifies simultaneously all real polynomials and all subintervals.

On any prefix of the block the integer discrepancy of kernels then costs O(J(m+1)+H+1)=N^(1/2+o(1)): use the constant moment on the complete intervals and the length on the last. For the count of packets up to X, only d|P(z) with d≤X/N intervene; their number is ≤(X/N)^(1/2)∏_{p≤z}(1+p^(−1/2))=(X/N)^(1/2)N^o(1), as in 6466. For each d the prefix up to X/d is used and |μ(d)|≤1. Summing over dyadic N≤X and absorbing the finitely many initial blocks one obtains ∑_{n≤X}(g(n)−μ(n))=O_ε(X^(1/2+ε)) under RH. The Mertens criterion gives the same ceiling for g. Conversely the exterior pole of G prevents even the one-sided ceiling with all margins for the interval (x,2x] by 6540. There thus remains an equivalence for INTEGER COUNTS on the sharp interval, with the exact grouping described there. It is another selection, with no new claim about the prefixes of the original f. The unconditional estimate of its balance remains open.

### Optimal prefix cost subject to moments and dual certificate of a block

In the lists P (primes) and S (labelled semiprimes) of 6466, impose the same global fractional moments of degree m as in 6230. Minimize the absolute maximum of the prefix discrepancy over the admissible weights b∈[0,1]^S; call E_N the minimum (it exists by compactness). Its value has the exact certificate
 E_N = sup_{Q,h} [Σ_P(Q+h) − Σ_S (Q+h)_+].
Here Q is any real polynomial of degree ≤m in the coordinate of the block and h(n)=Σ_{v≥n} a_v, with v running over the points of both lists and Σ|a_v|≤1. Indeed, the vector of moments and prefixes of the prime list must belong to the image of the cube of weights plus the box of errors {0} in moments and [−E,E] in each prefix. The support inequalities in all directions are exactly the formula after normalizing the prefix coefficients by their ℓ¹ norm. The purely polynomial directions already pass by 6230. This proof also admits E=0.

One obtains a single integer selection with prefix cost between E_N (for the restricted fractional problem) and E_N+1 as an effective upper bound after rounding; the lower bound E_N refers only to weights that satisfy the moments exactly. Order S, let B_j be the partial sums of the minimizer and select the increments of ⌊B_j⌋. The accumulated errors have modulus <1 and the rounding error of the full block is zero because the constant moment makes B_final an integer. For any test of bounded variation the error is bounded by its variation by summation by parts. In particular for n^(−s) it costs O((1+|s|)N^(−Re s)); the fractional part is estimated with the same Taylor of 6230. Multiplying by the packets preserves the continuation of the discrepancy in Re s>1/2 and the vertical estimate of 6548 (the polynomial factor is absorbed). Under RH the fractional subinterval weights of 6556 are candidates with E_N≤H+1, since each complete interval has zero error. Thus the conclusions of 6556 survive with an accumulated rounding smaller than one unit per prefix in each block.

Unconditionally E_N≪_A N/(log N)^A for each fixed A: subdivide into intervals of length comparable to N/(log N)^A. The margin proof of 6556 applies with the unconditional PNT with any fixed logarithmic saving in the prefix error (also when summing the labels, by summing 1/q or paying a logarithmic power). Choose the saving larger than A plus the fixed losses of Markov and density. The fractional concatenation verifies the moments of the block and all its prefixes cost at most the length of one interval plus one. Minimization makes these bounds simultaneous without choosing A in the selection. The certificate identifies which test can prevent a larger saving. Even a root bound for E_N would only transfer the sharp count between g and μ; the balance of g remains a distinct obligation.

### Simultaneous rounding of all surviving balances and dual of positive windows

In each dyadic block N of 6466 take ANY fractional vector b_N admissible for the moments of 6230. Delete integers of the prime packets and the fraction b_c of each semiprime packet with kernel c, and call g_b the remaining coefficient. Round cumulatively by increasing kernel within each block as in 6566 and call g the integer result. Uniformly in all b,
    |Σ_{n≤X}(g−g_b)(n)|=o(√X).
Indeed, for each d|P(z_N) the error on the kernels up to X/d is smaller than 1 by the telescoping sum of the roundings, and it is multiplied by μ(d). Only d≤X/N count. After dividing by √X the block costs at most N^(−1/2)∏_{p≤z_N}(1+p^(−1/2))=N^(−1/2+o(1)), summable over dyadic N. For fixed N, its packets are finite and when all enter the error is exactly zero by the integer constant moment. Domination with uniform dyadic tail proves the little o, also for differences of prefixes in (X,2X]. The initial blocks are treated in the same way or left whole. Hence the convex freedom can be used to optimize the REAL balance of the survivors in many windows at once, without paying a root cost per window in the passage to a single integer selection.

Explicit criterion for budgets B_i on windows I_i=(x_i,2x_i], x_i positive integers. Let D_0(I_i) be the balance with all prime packets deleted and still no removal of semiprime packets. For finitely supported λ_i≥0 put a_c(λ)=Σ_i λ_i Σ_{d|P(z_N)} μ(d)1_{dc∈I_i}, for each semiprime kernel c in block N. There exists ONE choice b satisfying Σ_{n∈I_i} g_b(n)≤B_i for all i if and only if for each λ
    Σ_i λ_i(D_0(I_i)−B_i) ≤ Σ_N max_{b_N admissible} Σ_c b_c a_c(λ).
The sign comes from deleting the positive coefficient of c and all its copies with μ(d). For a finite family the linear image of the moment polytopes is compact and convex, and on adding the orthant of slacks the separation uses only nonnegative normals. Only blocks N≤2 max x_i intervene. For all windows the finite intersection property in the compact product of polytopes is used. Integer windows suffice for asymptotic budgets by the O(1) error from moving the endpoints. Several budgets for the same window can be included simultaneously. If the budgets C_ε x_i^(1/2+ε) pass for ε reciprocals of positive integers with constants fixed per ε, one rounds ONCE; 6540 excludes every exterior zero. Under RH the fine weights of 6556 do give budgets of that form by the prefix estimate there and that of Mertens. The unconditional obligation is the inequality for all positive combinations of windows. Verifying each window separately would allow b to change with i and does not resolve that obligation.

### If there is an exterior zero, a single local template of windows suffices as a common dual witness

Let k be the fixed density of 6548 and D_a(t)=Σ_{t<n≤2t}a(n). For integer X put M=⌈√X⌉; split [X,2X] into M equal pieces, use as centre t_j the floor of the left endpoint and as weight λ_j the mass of k(v)dv with Xe^v in that piece. They are weights positive in the broad sense, summing to one, independent of the primes, of the putative zero and of the selection. Uniformly in ALL fractional weights b of 6576,
   Σ_j λ_j D_{g_b}(t_j) = ∫ k(v) D_μ(Xe^v)dv + O(√X).
First, discretizing changes each count by O(X/M+1) by movement of both endpoints and |g_b|≤1. Second, the continuous average has multiplier B(s)(2^s−1)/s by 6540 and 6548. For the fractional discrepancy H_b=G_b−1/ζ the same estimates of 6548 hold with constants uniform in b: in large blocks the equality of moments is exact and the total variation norms of the lists cost O(N), while in the small ones only |b|≤1 is used. Thus H_b grows at most like exp(C√(1+|t|)) in the closed strip. Multiplying by B and shifting to the boundary gives O(√X); the additional dyadic factor is bounded in the strip. This also applies to the selections rounded by 6576.

If there is a zero of real part β>1/2, the continuous average of μ exceeds C X^σ for any C>0 along a sequence, for each 1/2<σ<β, by the preserved pole and Landau as in 6540 (the function of X vanishes near zero). Rounding X to an integer alters the average by O(1) by movement of endpoints. Thus, along ONE sequence of scales, the combinations with these λ exceed the budget for ALL choices b, even if they are chosen after knowing X. The two-sided conclusion is obtained by applying the argument to the opposite sign.

Hence it suffices to prove, for each ε>0 and each large X, the existence of a choice b_X that controls THIS finite average by O_ε(X^(1/2+ε)), with no compatibility of choices between different scales. Under RH this budget holds even for all b by the uniform comparison and Mertens. It is a genuine restriction of the necessary dual tests of 6576, but the same comparison shows that optimizing b on this template alters the balance by only O(√X). Local flexibility could not compensate an exterior oscillation. The arithmetic bound of the average remains pending.

### The hyperbola of the local template admits an adverse block with genuine Möbius signs

Let w(t)=∫k(v)1_{e^v<t≤2e^v}dv, the continuous weight of 6586. It is continuous, supported on [1,4], zero at 4 and strictly positive at 2 (indeed w(2)=1). With K(y)=Σ_{r≥1}w(ry), K is continuous on (0,∞), K(4)=0 and K(2)>0. For D=⌈2√X⌉, the hyperbola of 5366 gives exactly
    Σ_n μ(n)w(n/X)=−Σ_{d,e≤D} μ(d)μ(e) K(de/X)
for large X: use μ*μ*1=μ; the two terms with only one restricted index collapse to terms with n≤D outside the support, and with both indices >D there are no contributions.

For each large X there is a subset S of those indices, all squarefree, such that the same restricted form (without the leading minus) is ≤−c X/log² X. To see this, choose fixed small intervals of d/√X around 1 and just to the left of 2. By continuity they can be arranged so that K on cross products is ≥b>0, K on the first square is ≤A with A≥1, and K on the second is ≤η for η arbitrarily small. First choose b and A valid on fixed neighbourhoods and then shrink the second interval.
