In the first take numbers 2p and in the second primes q; by PNT both lists have ≫√X/log X elements with respective signs +1 and −1. Take m elements of the second and ⌊αm⌋ of the first, with α=min(1,b/(2A)) and m≍√X/log X small enough for both capacities. The form is ≤m²(Aα²−2bα+η)+O(m), negative of the announced size choosing η<bα/2. The constants do not depend on X.

The counterexample is to a bound by positivity of the matrix or one stable under passing to partial supports, even keeping the genuine value μ at the chosen indices. It is not a counterexample to the full sum. It indicates that a block argument in this hyperbola must quantitatively exploit the contribution of the omitted indices; the adverse value already exceeds root precision with any margin ε<1/2.

### Unconditional compensation of all rows of the edge of the local hyperbola

For the weight and matrix of 6596, fix A>0. The strip 2√X(1−η)<d≤D, with η=c_A/√log X, can be removed simultaneously from both indices at cost O_A(X^(−A)) in the full form, using the genuine coefficients. The width in integers is of order √(X/log X).

Detail of the edge of the weight. With the uniforms V_j of 6548, the distance of their sum to the endpoint log 2 has the same law as Σ V_j. For small h take J=⌊κ/h²⌋. Between J and 2J there are ≍J variables of length ≥c(2J)^(−3/2). If at least a quarter of them exceed their half-length, the sum exceeds h choosing κ fixed and sufficiently small. By the binomial bound for independent coins, Pr(Σ V_j≤h)≤exp(−c'/h²). Since 2e^v≥t is necessary in the definition of w(t), for t≥4(1−η)^2 one has w(t)≪exp(−c''/η²) (and it is zero beyond 4).

For an edge row complete the sum in e to infinity. By μ*1=δ one gets Σ_{e≥1}μ(e)K(de/X)=w(d/X)=0 for large X. The truncated row is the negative of the tail e>D. There de/X>4(1−η) and only r=1 can contribute to K. There are O(√X) terms per row and each costs O(exp(−c''/η²)). The intersection of two strips satisfies the same bound per term since de/X>4(1−η)^2. By inclusion–exclusion the union of rows and columns costs O(X exp(−c''/η²)), smaller than X^(−A) on choosing c_A. The argument also controls any subset of edge rows if the columns are kept complete. It does not remove a strip of fixed relative width nor the interior blocks of 6596; the bound of the interior remains open.

### Threshold of the absolute tail for the original weight and widening by a different detector

For the weight of 6586 the edge law also satisfies Pr(ΣV_j≤h)≥exp(−C/h²). Take J=⌈K/h²⌉ with K large, so that Σ_{j>J}a_j≤h/2. For the first J require V_j≤h/(2J); the product probability is ∏ min(1,h j^{3/2}/(2cJ))≥exp(−C J), since J!≥(J/e)^J and h√J≍1 (each factor dominates c₀(j/J)^{3/2}). For 2<t<4, w(t) is exactly this probability at h=log(4/t), by symmetry. If η→0 and η√log X→∞, take d/(2√X) between 1−η and 1−3η/4 and e/(2√X) between 1+η/8 and 1+η/4. These are indices in the edge rows and tail columns, and h≍η. In each interval there are ≫η√X squarefree integers: Σ_{n≤v}μ²(n)=v/ζ(2)+O(√v) by inclusion–exclusion. Hence the sum of moduli of the genuine tail is ≥cη² X exp(−C/η²)=X^{1−o(1)}. This fixes the order of width attainable by charging that tail in modulus for THIS weight.

One can go further by changing the detector. Keep half of the logarithmic length for the product of uniforms of 6548 (scaled by 1/2). Use the other half on independent uniforms of lengths b_j=c/[j(log(j+1))²], j≥2, normalized by the sum. The product multiplier remains zero-free in Re s>0 and the first half keeps the decay exp(−c|t|^{2/3}); 6548 and 6586 hold for the new weight. To prove the edge bound take J=⌊exp(κ/h)⌋ with κ small. The sum Z of the new uniforms between J and J² has expectation ≍1/log J (by the integral of 1/(t log²t)), which exceeds 2h with such a choice. The sum of squares of their lengths is O(1/(J log⁴J)). Hoeffding's inequality gives Pr(Z≤h)≤exp(−c J log²J), in particular ≤exp(−exp(c'/h)). Since all summands are positive, the same bound holds for the distance to the upper endpoint by symmetry. The complete-rows proof of 6606 now gives error O(X exp(−exp(c''/η))) for small η. With η=c₀/loglog X and c₀ sufficiently small it is O_A(X^(−A)) for any fixed A. This strip has width ≍√X/loglog X. The better edge results from the new weight; it does not prove additional cancellation in the signed tails of the previous one nor reach the interior of fixed relative width.

### Interior pairs with factors of the quotient chosen for each greatest common divisor

For the compact hyperbola of 6596 put I=∫w(t)dt>0 and R(y)=K(y)−I/y. Comparing the sum with the integral over the intervals [(r−1)y,ry] gives |R(y)|≤Var(w) uniformly. Thus the main term of the form with minus sign is −XI(Σ_{d≤D}μ(d)/d)^2≤0; it is retained in full before trimming the remainder.

For each g≤D choose arbitrarily its own set of primes S_g, even looking at the block. Suppose that L_X=sup_g Σ_{p∈S_g,p≤D/g}p^(−1/2)=o(log X). Then the sum of moduli of the remainder over ALL pairs with gcd(d,e)=g and factors of (d/g)(e/g) in S_g costs X^(1/2+o(1)), summing over g. Indeed, after d=ga,e=gb, only squarefree coprime a,b matter. With Y=D/g, the indicator a,b≤Y is majorized by Y/√(ab) in the summation region. On extending a,b to the possible products of primes ≤Y, each prime has three options: absent, in a or in b. The number of admissible pairs costs ≤Y∏(1+2/√p)≤Y exp(2L_X). Summing the harmonic series in g gives the explicit bound Var(w)D(1+log D)exp(2L_X). It still holds for every subset of these pairs and for any sign of their coefficients of modulus ≤1.

Included are, for example, all quotients whose factors are ≤(log X)^2 (by Chebyshev), plus lists of large primes distinct for each g, with the same reciprocal budget. It is not required that the reduced product ab be small. 5396 already cuts by size of ab with another filter and another endpoint; here the selection by factors and by g is controlled within the original compactly supported matrix. To prove the ceiling one still needs to control the remaining quotients relative to the favourable square.

### Optimal exponent of the absolute cost for quotients with primes up to (log X)^k

For fixed k>0 put y=(log X)^k. The mass Σ|μ(d)μ(e)R(de/X)| over d,e≤D with all primes of the reduced quotient ≤y is X^{max(1/2,1−1/k)+o(1)}. The floor is attained even with contributions adverse to the ceiling, that is −μ(d)μ(e)R(de/X)>0.

For the ceiling take σ=max(1/2,1−1/k) in the argument of 6620. Each g costs O((D/g)^{2σ}∏_{p≤y}(1+2p^(−σ))). Chebyshev and partial summation give log of the product O_k(y^(1−σ)/log y)=o(log X); the sum of g^(−2σ) costs O(log D). For the root floor use d=e squarefree just below 2√X. There R is uniformly bounded away from zero from below because R(4)=−I/4 and R is continuous. There are ≫√X such indices.

For k>2 form products of j=⌊(log(2√X)−√log X)/log y⌋ distinct primes in [y/2,y]. The PNT and the binomial bound of 6512 give at least exp((1−1/k+o(1))log(2√X)) distinct products. All have the same sign μ and are ≤2√X exp(−√log X). Split [1,2√X] into O(log X) multiplicative intervals of ratio 1+δ with δ>0 fixed and small. One interval [V,(1+δ)V] retains the same cardinality exponent (it can be truncated at the last maximal product). By PNT choose a single prime g between (1−3δ)2√X/V and (1−2δ)2√X/V, possible since √X/V≫exp(√log X) and therefore g>y. Thus all chosen indices d=ga lie below 2√X and as close in proportion as desired by fixing δ. Every pair of them has sign μ(d)μ(e)=+1, reduced quotient with factors ≤y and R(de/X)≤−c by continuity. The square of the number of indices gives the floor X^{1−1/k+o(1)}. It is only required that the reduction remove g, not that the two remaining products be coprime beforehand. This floor of a subfamily does not estimate the signed balance of the full family.

### Exact compensators of the adverse family within its class of quotients

Return to the UNcentred matrix K of 6596 and expand K in its cofactor r. Fix any y, a column e, the product m=dr and the part h of d formed by primes >y. The class "reduced quotient with primes ≤y" is equivalent for squarefree indices to e having that same part h. Write s for the product of the DISTINCT primes ≤y dividing m/h. For h squarefree, h|m and with no factors ≤y, the exact fibre at fixed e,m,h is
    μ(e) μ(h) w(em/X) Σ_{a|s, a≤D/h} μ(a).
This enumerates each d=ha and r=m/(ha) once, with no coprimality restrictions between r and the other indices. The choice of a does not change the class of the quotient. If s>1 and hs≤D the full fibre equals zero. Even when hs>D, with p the smallest prime of s the inner coefficient is exactly
    Σ_{b|s/p, D/(hp)<b≤D/h} μ(b).
Indeed the pairs b,pb have opposite signs and only those crossing the cut survive. This interval may also be empty. s=1 gives the coefficient 1 if h≤D.

In the example of 6628, d=ga and e=gb were just below 2√X and therefore K(de/X)=w(de/X) (r=1). Each of those terms of K lies in a fibre with m=d, h=g, s=a>1 and hs=d≤D. The fibre vanishes exactly within the SAME class of quotients. The fibres for distinct (d,e) of the example are disjoint by (m,e); in them the compensators have r>1. There is no contradiction with the floor for R: the term −I/y of its definition (with y there the argument of the kernel) lacks that cofactor r; its recombination with the main term is indispensable. The adverse subset of the centred remainder does not constitute an autonomous arithmetic obstruction of that size for the uncentred form. The fibres s=1 and the partial divisor intervals remain; their collective balance has not been bounded.

### Exact coefficient after completing the two small indices

In the UNcentred form of 6596, fix n=der in the support, so that n≤4X≤D². Write n=sR, where s contains all prime powers of n up to y and R only primes >y. Fix the rough parts h,k of d,e with hk|R. The sum of coefficients for this fibre, before the outer minus sign and the weight w(n/X), is exactly
    μ(h)μ(k)μ(s) [1−1_{hs>D}−1_{ks>D}].
Indeed, write d=ha,e=kb. The small coefficient is Σ_{ab|s,ha≤D,kb≤D} μ(a)μ(b). Without cuts it is μ(s) by μ*μ*1=μ. To remove ha>D first sum over b|s/a, and by μ*1=δ only a=s remains. Analogously for removing kb>D. The intersection of the two tails is empty since (ha)(kb)≤n≤D². The indicators hs>D and ks>D can both be one: they correspond to two distinct terms of the expansion. The proof allows any y and also h≠k.

Hence all fibres where s has a square factor or exactly one of hs,ks crosses D cancel exactly. If both are on the same side there remains a single coefficient of modulus at most one, with sign reversed if both exceed D. In the class of quotients of 6636 one takes h=k and h²|R: its aggregate coefficient at n is μ(s) Σ_{h²|R} μ(h)^2 (1−2·1_{hs>D}). The identity preserves the sign and the individual arithmetic multipliers before summing over n; it does not allow deducing a ceiling when summing the surviving n. Additional check by enumeration: 26764 small fibres for 2≤D≤18, n≤D² and y∈{2,3,7}, including different and non-squarefree rough parts, agree in the small coefficient.

### Sign of the complete class of small quotients in the uncentred form

Let Q_= be the sum of μ(d)μ(e)K(de/X), d,e≤D, over all pairs having the same part of primes >y. For 2≤y≤exp((log X)^α), with fixed 0<α<1, and every fixed A one has uniformly
  Q_= = XI ∏_{p≤y}(1−1/p)^2 · Σ_{(h,P(y))=1} μ²(h)/h² + O_{α,A}(X/(log X)^A).
Hence the contribution of the WHOLE class to the detector −Q is strictly favourable for large X, even for y=(log X)^k with arbitrary fixed k. The main magnitude is comparable to X/(log(2y))². Here the specific main term of this class is used; the global square of 6620 is not additionally kept as a separate credit.

Proof. For every y'>0 one has |K(y')|≤C/y' by support and boundedness of w (if y'>4 it is zero). Replacing K by I/y' on d,e≤B=X^(1/4) costs O(B²) by 6620. To estimate the other pairs write d=ha,e=hb, a,b|P(y) with no obligation of mutual coprimality. Both the original kernel and the main term cost O(X/(h²ab)) per pair. A bound for ha>B suffices; extend all sums to infinity. With τ=min(1/4,1/log(2y)), the cost is
  ≪ X B^(−τ) Σ_h h^(−2+τ) ∏_{p≤y}(1+p^(−1+τ))(1+p^(−1)).
Since p^τ≤e, the product costs at most an absolute power of log(2y) by Mertens. B^(−τ) saves exp(−c(log X)^(1−α)), sufficient for the announced error. The same count allows removing the cuts from the main term. In the main sum without cuts the two small indices give two copies of Σ_{a|P(y)}μ(a)/a and the equal rough parts give μ²(h). This proves the formula. By Mertens and the term h=1, the main term dominates the error uniformly. The global ceiling still requires Q_distinct+Q_= ≥ −C_ε X^(1/2+ε), where Q_distinct comprises the pairs with different rough parts. The logarithmic precision of the individual formula is not enough to resolve this comparison at root scale.

### An unpaired large prime reverses the balance when adding the first complete layer

Denote by M_y the positive main term of 6654 (including XI). Let Q_p be the sum in the same convention, before the minus sign, over pairs whose reduced quotient has EXACTLY one prime >y, namely p. For fixed δ∈(0,1/2), α∈(0,1), 2≤y≤exp((log X)^α) and y<p≤X^(1/2−δ),
  Q_p = − M_y · 2p/(p²+1) + O_{α,δ,A}(X/[p(log X)^A]).
The error is uniform and keeps the factor 1/p even for primes of power scale.

Proof. In one of the two orientations write d=pha,e=hb, with h squarefree, without primes ≤y or factor p, and a,b|P(y). The other orientation gives the same sum. In the main term I X/(de) the Möbius coefficient is −μ²(h)μ(a)μ(b). Compared with M_y one gains 1/p, two orientations, and the local factor 1+p^(−2) of the sum over h is removed. To control the replacement use B=X^min(δ/2,1/8). If ha,hb≤B the indices are within D and the cost of centring is O(B²) per orientation: (ha,hb) determines h by extraction of factors >y, and R is bounded. This error is O_A(X/(p log^A X)). In the rest the absolute bound of both kernels is CX/(ph²ab). The same Rankin estimate of 6654 on ha>B or hb>B gains exp(−c_{δ}(log X)^(1−α)) up to logarithmic factors. Thus the indicated error is proved even when extending the main term to infinity.

Sign consequence: for y=(log X)^2 and Z=X^(1/2−δ), the classes are disjoint and
  (Q_= + Σ_{y<p≤Z} Q_p)/M_y = 1 − Σ_{y<p≤Z} 2p/(p²+1) + o(1) → −∞.
Indeed the sum of errors is O_A(X loglog X/(log X)^A), and Mertens gives Σ_{y<p≤Z}1/p=loglog Z−loglog y+o(1). The first favourable credit of 6654 is more than consumed by the pairs with a single unpaired large prime. The complete set still includes the layers of several distinct primes and the primes beyond Z. The sign reversal for this partial union is unconditional, and does not determine the full balance.

### Simultaneous compensation of all layers of the rectangle of large quotients

Put L=log X, y=exp(√L), Z=X^(1/2−δ), with fixed 0<δ<1/2. For each squarefree pair write the parts >y of d,e as hu,hv with h the greatest common divisor of those parts. Let Q_rect be the UNcentred form restricted by u,v≤Z, with no additional limit on the number of primes of uv. One has unconditionally, for some c_δ>0,
  Q_rect = M_y (Σ_{u≤Z,(u,P(y))=1} μ(u)/u · ∏_{p|u}(1+p^(−2))^(−1))² + O_δ(X exp(−c_δ√L)).
The square has favourable sign for the detector −Q. In particular the large adverse excess of the first layer of 6664 is compensated up to that error when the other layers of the rectangle are incorporated.

Uniform detail: fix (u,v)=1 squarefree and rough, d=uha,e=vhb with a,b|P(y), h rough coprime to uv. Take B=X^min(δ/2,1/8). On ha,hb≤B the cost of replacing K by its main term is O(B²) per pair (u,v) and both indices are within the cut. Since uv≤X^(1−2δ), this is O((X/(uv))X^(−δ)) for δ≤1/4, and also with some fixed saving for δ>1/4. In the rest the Rankin count of 6654 gives error O((X/(uv))exp(−c_δ√L)), absorbing polylogarithmic factors. The main term is M_y b(u)b(v), with b(u)=μ(u)∏_{p|u}(1+p^(−2))^(−1)/u on rough integers. Summing the errors costs at most (1+log Z)², absorbable by reducing c_δ. To extend the main term from the coprime set to the full square, the added pairs share some prime >y and their total normalized cost is ≤(1+log Z)² Σ_{p>y}p^(−2)≪L²/y. This proves the formula. The quotient of the single layer plus diagonal by M_y also tends to minus infinity with this y by 6664 and Mertens. So the claimed compensation has quantitative content. The use of squares and coprimality has antecedents in 4876 and 5972; here it is applied uniformly to the reduced rough parts of power size and absorbs the layers of 6664 together. The error exceeds root scale and the complement with max(u,v)>Z is missing.

### Exterior hyperbola with explicit positive kernel and square of favourable sign for the floor

Reuse W from 4712 in the detector S(X)=Σμ(n)W(n/X). Its Mellin transform Ŵ_M(s)/ζ(s) preserves the exterior poles by the non-vanishing of 4712; the Landau argument there also allows using the FLOOR S(X)≥−O_ε(X^(1/2+ε)). With D=⌊√X⌋ and K(t)=Σ_{r≥1}W(rt), the identity μ*μ*1=μ gives exactly S=2Σ_{d≤D}μ(d)W(d/X)+Σ_{d,e>D}μ(d)μ(e)K(de/X). The small intersection is zero by 4712. All sums are absolutely convergent at fixed X by the quadratic decay. The short term is O(X^(−1/2)) because W is even, smooth and W(0)=0.

Poisson gives K(t)=t^(−1)Σ_{m≥1}b(m/t). For t>1 one gets
  K(t)=1/(2t²)−[B₃({t})−12B₃({t/2})+32B₃({t/4})]/(3t³),
with B₃(v)=v³−3v²/2+v/2. Indeed Σ_{m≥1}(1−m/t)_+²=t/3−1/2+1/(6t)−B₃({t})/(3t²) by the sum of integer squares. Applying the coefficients 1,−3,2 to the arguments t,t/2,t/4 cancels the first two terms. K(t)>0 for EVERY t>1: on (1,2] only (1−1/t)²/t remains and for t≥2 use |B₃|≤1/(12√3). This pointwise positivity does not imply positivity of the matrix.

In the exterior quadrant de>X, the first term gives exactly +(X²/2)(Σ_{d>D}μ(d)/d²)^2, favourable for the floor. For the rest, already centred, the zone de>X^(5/4) costs in modulus O(√X log X) by X³Σ_{n>X^(5/4)}τ(n)n^(−3) and the elementary sum of τ. Thus the sufficient obligation is a floor for the periodic remainder ONLY on d,e>√X, X<de≤X^(5/4), keeping the credit of the full square. 4712 made the exact cut for a single divisor with Λ, whereas here two Möbius indices, a tail square and an unconditional root bound at the infinite end are used. The intermediate band remains to be bounded.

### Compression of the exterior power band to a polylogarithmic factor with a fixed weight

Average the weight of 6684 as W_*(t)=∫k(v)W(e^(−v)t)dv with the fixed density of 6548 on [0,log 2]. Its Mellin transform is B(s)Ŵ_M(s), zero-free in 1/2<Re s<1 by 4712 and 6548. The one-sided floor criterion carries over by Landau. W_* keeps the controls O(t²) at zero and O(t^(−2)) at infinity. The new K_*(t)=∫k(v)K(e^(−v)t)dv is still exactly zero for t≤1. For t≥2 one has
    K_*(t)=c₂/t²+O(t^(−3) exp(−c t^(2/3))),    c₂=(1/2)∫exp(2v)k(v)dv>0.

Indeed, in the formula of 6684 expand the periodic B₃ in its absolutely convergent series, without constant mode, with coefficients O(|j|^(−3)). With λ=e^(−v) the amplitude of the periodic term is H(λ)=λ^(−4)k(−log λ), supported on [1/2,1], and the frequencies are jt, jt/2, jt/4 in the 2π convention. Its Fourier transform satisfies |Ĥ(ξ)|≪exp(−c|ξ|^(2/3)). Regularity detail: the convolution of uniforms of lengths a_i=c₀ i^(−3/2) gives ‖k^(m)‖∞≤a_(m+1)^(−1)∏_{i≤m}(2/a_i)≤C^(m+1)(m!)^(3/2) by differentiating the first m factors as measures. Composition with −log λ preserves the bound: in the normalized derivative formula of order m, the coefficients of each normalized derivative of log are ≤C^i on this interval, and the sum over ordered compositions of m into j parts has binom(m−1,j−1) terms, multiplied by ‖k^(j)‖∞/j!≤C^(j+1)(m!)^(1/2). The analytic factor λ^(−4) also preserves it by Leibniz. Integrating by parts m≍|ξ|^(2/3) times with a sufficiently small constant gives the estimate. Applying it to each frequency proves the formula.

Extract the full square +c₂X²(Σ_{d>D}μ(d)/d²)^2. Given fixed A, the absolute sum of the remainder on de>XT, T=C_A(log X)^(3/2), is O_A(X^(−A)): extract exp(−cT^(2/3)) and use X³Σ_{n>X}τ(n)/n³≪X log(2X). Hence the floor for the remainder on d,e>√X and X<de≤C X(log X)^(3/2), with the credit of the square and root margin, would suffice. In particular both pending indices lie between √X and C√X(log X)^(3/2). The weight, the criterion and the decomposition are independent of X. The tail has been improved by oscillatory averaging before taking moduli; the band near de=X still has no sign estimate. 5366 used Gevrey in the reciprocal argument within a hyperbola; here the exact interior hole persists and decay is obtained in the exterior direction.

### Limit of the exterior compression method for a fixed weight

In the scheme K(t)=Σ_{r≥1}W(rt) with exact hole K=0 on (0,1), suppose W=O(t²) at zero and O(t^(−2)) at infinity, K locally bounded and not identically zero as an almost-everywhere function. If K(t)=c₂/t²+O(exp(−c t^p)) for t≥2, necessarily p≤1. In particular no such weight leaves only a constant band after extracting the square.

Proof. In 1<Re s<2 the Mellin transform of K is ζ(s)M_W(s) by absolute convergence. By the hole and the hypothesis on the tail,
 F(s)=(2−s)∫₁^∞[K(t)−c₂/t²]t^(s−1)dt+c₂
is entire and coincides there with (2−s)ζ(s)M_W(s). The identity extends to the critical strip (meromorphically across 1); M_W is holomorphic there. Hence F has all the nontrivial zeros of ζ, with multiplicity. F is not identically zero by uniqueness of Mellin. Choose fixed real s₀ with F(s₀)≠0. On the circle s=s₀+Re^(iθ), σ=Re s, the compact portion of the integral costs exp(O(R)); for the rest use ∫₂^∞ exp(−ct^p)t^(σ−1)dt and Stirling for σ≥1, and a constant for σ≤1. Thus log⁺|F(s)|≤(R/p)(cos θ)_+ log R+O(R), uniformly. The circular mean is ≤R log R/(πp)+O(R). By Riemann–von Mangoldt, counting both halves of the plane, the disc of radius r centred at s₀ contains at least (r/π)log r−O(r) zeros (it suffices to limit the ordinates by r−O(1)). Jensen gives a mean ≥(R/π)log R−O(R) after integrating the count with dr/r. Comparison forces p≤1. The density argument has an antecedent in 3142; here the one-sided growth constant determines the physical exponent of the exterior tail.

Constructively each exponent 0<p<1 is indeed attained as a decay bound of the remainder, keeping the detector of 6694: replace the lengths j^(−3/2) by j^(−1/p) normalized to the same sum. The Mellin product remains zero-free in the strip, and the derivative bound becomes C^(m+1)(m!)^(1/p). The same composition, Fourier and integration by parts give O(t^(−3)exp(−ct^p)). For each fixed η>0 take p=1/(1+η); de≤CX(log X)^(1+η) suffices. The endpoint p=1 is not decided by Jensen. This limit affects the procedure that charges the tail in modulus via a uniform exponential majorant; it does not limit a signed arithmetic cancellation in the band.

### Arbitrarily unbalanced exterior band, with no pending quadratic credit

Fix 0<δ≤1/2 and η>0. There is a single fixed weight for these parameters that preserves each exterior pole and for which the floor only requires bounding the signed sum over
    d>X^δ, e>X^(1−δ), X<de≤CX(log X)^(1+η).
In particular X^δ<d≤CX^δ(log X)^(1+η). No cross product of Möbius tails needs to be estimated. The price is changing the detector; the constant is not claimed uniform as δ tends to zero.

Let U(t) be the averaged weight of 6703 with p=1/(1+η), and T U(t)=U(t/2). First apply (1−T/4): the kernel of multiples is transformed by the same operator, exactly cancels the mode c₂/t² and remains zero for t≤1. For an integer m≥1 with (2m+1)δ≥1/2 also apply ∏_{j=1}^{m−1}(1−2^{2j}T). The weight U is even, smooth and O(t²) at zero, so each factor removes the Taylor term of degree 2j and the final weight V is O_m(t^{2m}) near zero. For large t, the final kernel J(t)=Σ_r V(rt) is O_{δ,η}(t^(−3)exp(−c_{δ,η}t^p)) by the FINITE combination of dilations. The Mellin transform gains (1−2^(s−2))∏(1−2^(s+2j)), zero-free in the open critical strip. V keeps the decay O(t^(−2)) at infinity. By 6684 and Landau a floor for Σμ(n)V(n/X) with root margin still excludes all exterior zeros.

In the double identity cut the first index at A=⌊X^δ⌋ and the second at B=⌊X^(1−δ)⌋. The short intersection is zero since AB≤X and J(t)=0 up to 1. The two terms with only one short index collapse by μ*1 and cost O((A+B)(B/X)^(2m))=O(X^(1−(2m+1)δ))=O(√X). In the long quadrant d>A,e>B, extract exp(−cT₀^p) for de>XT₀ with T₀=C(log X)^(1+η). The divisor bound of 6694 makes that tail O(X^(−1)) by increasing C. The announced band remains and its sum is the detector up to O(√X). For δ=1/10, m=2 suffices: the short index stays at scale X^(1/10) up to logarithmic factors while the other is at scale X^(9/10). The short range still grows like a power; the floor of the bilinear form in that range has not been proved.

### Constant short threshold on incorporating the long prefix into the detector

Choose V=(1−T/4)U from 6713, without the higher-order filters, with fixed η. Let J be its kernel of multiples. For each fixed a∈(1,2) take the NEW detector S_a(X)=Σ_{n>X/a} μ(n)V(n/X). Then exactly
   S_a(X)=μ(1)V(1/X)+Σ_{d≥2, e>X/a} μ(d)μ(e)J(de/X).
Indeed the identity of 6713 with cuts ⌊a⌋=1 and ⌊X/a⌋ has zero short intersection; the short term in e is subtracted on defining S_a. The tail de>X C(log X)^(1+η) costs O(X^(−1)) uniformly in a by 6713. Hence the required index d runs from 2 to 2C(log X)^(1+η). The cofactor e is still of order X up to polylogarithmic factors.

Independent check of the signal after the cut. The Mellin transform is H_a(s)/ζ(s) in 1<Re s<2, with H_a(s)=∫_{1/a}^∞V(t)t^(s−1)dt holomorphic in Re s<2. The part X<1 introduces no poles in that strip since S_a(X)=O(X²) at zero. For each exterior zero ρ, H_a(ρ) does not vanish identically on any open interval of a: its derivative is a^(−ρ−1)V(1/a). V is real analytic by compact additive band and bounded dilations, and nonzero by its previous Mellin transform. Thus for almost every a∈(1,2) the detector preserves ALL exterior poles at once (countable union of discrete sets). This does not select a particular rational.

A FINITE family of rational cuts also suffices, without quantifying its cardinality. Choose a rational a₀ with V(1/a₀)≠0. Uniformly in 1/2≤σ≤1,
   H_{a₀}(s)=−a₀^(−s)V(1/a₀)/s+O_{a₀}(|s|^(−2)),   |Im s|→∞.
Integrate twice by parts in log t: the logarithmic derivatives of V up to order two are O(t^(−2)) at infinity, since in the logarithmic average they are passed by parts to derivatives of k, of compact support. Thus H_{a₀} does not vanish in the strip at sufficiently large heights. For the finitely many zeros at the remaining heights ONE second rational a₁ avoiding the finite union of isolated zeros suffices. Landau applied separately gives the sufficiency of the floors for those two detectors; under RH their bounds with margin follow from Mertens and Abel, including the jump of the weight. Without identifying the concrete pair, a version effective in its quantifiers is to ask for the floor for every rational in (1,2), with a constant allowed per cut. The reduction to polylogarithmic d changes the detector and neither proves cancellation in the long variable nor reduces the obligation to evaluating a fixed number of terms.

### Audit of the first row: an explicit interval already recovers Mertens with positive inverse

In 6723 choose a=3/2, d=2, and restrict to 3X/4<e≤X (contained in e>X/a). Let H(t)=J(2t), c=3/4. On [c,1] it is positive and strictly increasing. Indeed for 1<u≤2 the filter (1−T/4) in J changes nothing, since the previous kernel is zero at u/2≤1. Before averaging, K(u)=(u−1)^2/u³ for 1<u≤2 and zero for u≤1, with positive derivative on (1,2). The average k only dilates by factors between 1/2 and 1 and has positive mass in any neighbourhood of v=0 (in the construction by uniforms, first bound the tail by its length and then a finite number of variables). This preserves positivity and strict increase for u>1 in the range.

Write M(X)=Σ_{n≤X}μ(n), F(X)=Σ_{cX<n≤X}μ(n)H(n/X); the real row has sign −F since μ(2)=−1. EXACT summation by parts, including the endpoints:
    H(1) M(X) = F(X) + H(c) M(cX) + ∫_c^1 M(tX)dH(t).
The measure ν=[H(c)δ_c+dH]/H(1) is a positive probability, with mass at t<1. For any σ>0, q_σ=∫t^σ dν<1. Consequently for both signs and each Y≥1,
   sup_{1≤X≤Y} (±M(X))_+/X^σ ≤ [H(1)(1−q_σ)]^(−1) sup_{1≤X≤Y} (±F(X))_+/X^σ.
It suffices to take the supremum in the identity, since M(tX)=0 below 1. The inverse inequality in two-sided norm follows from the same identity. Thus a one-sided root ceiling with margin on THIS stretch of ONE row would already exclude the exterior zeros by the one-sided Landau criterion for M (Mellin 1/(sζ(s))); under RH it holds two-sidedly by Mertens. It is an explicit test and does not use a generic choice of cuts. It is not legitimate to deduce its bound from the joint sum: other rows and other stretches can cancel. The consequence for the plan is to avoid attempting an absolute root bound row by row and per subinterval as a supposed simplification.

### In the first overlap, two rows reinforce the same parity in linear mass of both signs

In 6723 fix a=3/2. For n=de the coefficient of J(n/X) over all rows together is exactly λ(n) b_X(n), with λ(n)=(−1)^Ω(n) and b_X(n)=Σ_{d|n, 2≤d<3n/(2X)} μ²(d)μ²(n/d). Indeed every surviving pair has μ(d)μ(e)=λ(de), even if d,e have common primes. Hence there is no sign cancellation when regrouping the same product; 5006 already used regroupings of equal product in another form. Here the reinforcement in the first overlap of the short rows is quantified.

By 6735 and continuity there is a fixed interval [l,r]⊂(2,8/3) with J(t)≥c>0. In it the only possible d are 2 and 3. For n=6m, m squarefree and (m,6)=1, both survive and the joint coefficient equals 2μ(m). In lX≤n≤rX each sign occurs ≍X times and their contributions, with both rows already joined, are each of magnitude ≍X. More precisely the mass of each sign in this subfamily is
   (κX/6)∫_l^r J(t)dt + O_A(X/log^A X),   κ=(1−1/2)(1−1/3)∏_{p>3}(1−1/p²).
To check this use 1_{μ=±1}=(μ²±μ)/2. The count of squarefree integers coprime to 6 is κv+O(√v) by inclusion–exclusion. The sum of μ over integers coprime to 6 is O_A(v/log^A v) by the quantitative Möbius PNT: it is obtained from the ordinary sum by summing M(v/(2^i3^j)), separating 2^i3^j≤√v and the tail by the geometric convergence of Σ(2^i3^j)^(−1/2). Abel transfers both computations to the fixed weight J on the interval. Thus there is proven compensation BETWEEN products in this subfamily up to every logarithmic saving; it does not yet reach root scale. The audit rules out using permutations of divisors at fixed n to obtain that gain in the already compressed bilinear band.

### Pairing between distinct products in the overlap, with total root cost

In the interval [l,r] of 6745 there is for each large X an explicitly selectable subfamily of products of the overlap contributing separately in each sign ≫X^0.735/log X, while the sum of the MODULI of the balances of its pairs is O(√X/log X). No signed Mertens estimate on the long factors is used.

Take Y=√X/10 and a subinterval [Y,(1+ε)Y] with fixed small ε. Split it into cells of length H=Y^0.53, discarding the last incomplete one. In each cell choose a prime p and a multiple 5q with q prime, for example the first admissible ones. Existence in all large cells follows from the Baker–Harman–Pintz short-interval theorem already cited in phase 164, R164_291_AUDIT_201, line 81: both H and H/5 dominate the exponent 0.525 at the corresponding scale. Thus there are ≫Y^0.47 pairs and, by disjointness of the cells, Σ|p−5q|≤O(Y).

Fix a common interval of primes m of length ≍X/Y centred near ((l+r)/2)X/(6Y) such that 6mv/X∈[l,r] for each v of the cells. It exists after shrinking ε and the relative width of the interval of m; all those m exceed (1+ε)Y. By PNT there are ≍(X/Y)/log X of them. Form the pairs n=6mp, n'=6m·5q. All the integers are distinct, since m is their largest prime and the remaining factor allows recovering cell and type; the factors 2,3,5 are distinct from p,q,m. By 6745 the JOINED coefficients of rows 2 and 3 are +2 and −2, respectively. Since J≥c on the interval, both masses have the announced floor. By the mean value theorem the difference of weights per pair costs O((m/X)|p−5q|), with a fixed constant by the smoothness of J. Summing over all cells and all m gives O((X/Y)/(log X) · Y/Y)=O(√X/log X). The improvement over 6745 is root precision for this subfamily, at the cost of losing positive density. The construction does not estimate the products left unpaired.

### Simultaneous replacement of the two Möbius factors by a single fixed sparse support

Reuse 5546 without sieve, now on a permanent dyadic partition of the integers. In each [Y,2Y) pair within cells of length ⌊Y^(2/5)⌋ with the translation that minimizes leftovers. Leave both incomplete edges unpaired. Let b(n)=μ(n) only on the leftovers and zero elsewhere. A single selection satisfies, for every fixed A, #supp(b)∩[Y,2Y)≪_A Y/log^A Y. On EACH prefix of the line, the sum of μ−b is O(X^(2/5)): only one cell can cut pairs. This is a uniform prefix statement, in addition to the sparsity estimate of 5546. By Abel, H(s)=Σ(b(n)−μ(n))n^(−s) is holomorphic in σ>2/5, with O_ε(1+|s|) in 2/5+ε≤σ≤2.

For V,J of 6723, without the sharp cut a, one has unconditionally
   Σ_{d,e≥1} b(d)b(e)J(de/X) = Σ_n μ(n)V(n/X) + O_ε(X^(2/5+ε))       (0<ε<1/10).
Both indices are restricted to the SAME sparse set, with no additional separate trimming in d,e. Physical absolute convergence follows from the exterior decay of J and its hole. In 1<σ<2 the difference of transforms is
   M_V(s) [2H(s)+ζ(s)H(s)^2],
since M_J=ζ M_V and Σ b(n)n^(−s)=1/ζ(s)+H(s). The terms with poles at zeros of ζ cancel exactly. The real pole of ζ at 1 is removable because M_V(1)=0 by 4712 and the subsequent filters. M_V decays faster than any vertical power in closed strips inside 0<σ<2 by the average k and the absolute bound of the Mellin transform of W. With the polynomial growth of ζ and H, inverting and shifting to 2/5+ε gives the error. The cancellation μ*1=δ is not being applied to b here. That is why the sparse double detector covers all pairs in X<de≤CX(log X)^(1+η), with tail O(X^(−1)) by 6713, but the individual cut e>X/a is not inherited. The one-sided floor for that sparse sum remains equivalent to RH by 6684 and the non-vanishing of M_V in the critical strip. The bilinear structure is preserved at better than root precision; the sign bound on the residual support remains open.

### Two indices on prescribed squares, with only O(log³ X) positions up to X

For the detector V,J of 6761 there is an integer sequence c(n) supported on a FIXED set of squares, independent of μ in its admissible positions, with O(log³(2X)) positions up to X. It satisfies, for each 0<σ₀<1/2,
   Σ_{d,e} c(d)c(e)J(de/X)=Σ_n μ(n)V(n/X)+O_{σ₀}(X^σ₀).
The price is integer coefficients of variable magnitude that incorporate sums of μ over each block. Simple transfer to the nearest square would only gain a power 1/2 in the position error; interpolating between the TWO neighbouring squares gains a whole power.

Construction. In [N,2N), N dyadic, use m+1 Chebyshev nodes (roots, affinely scaled), m=⌈log²(2N)⌉, and their cardinal polynomials l_j. At the node x_j accumulate A_j=Σ_{N≤n<2N}μ(n)l_j(n). One has Σ|A_j|≪N log(m+2) by the classical Lebesgue constant (any polynomial bound in m also suffices). Distribute A_j between the consecutive squares enclosing x_j, with positive affine weights reproducing x_j; if it is a square use it directly. Round the two masses to the nearest integer and add all incident contributions at each position. Each block has O(m) positions, at distance O(√N) from the block, and total variation O(N log(m+2)+m). Coincidences are sums, not conflicting assignments.

For s in σ₀≤Re s≤3/2, the Dirichlet discrepancy H=Σ c(n)n^(−s)−1/ζ(s), initially to the right of 1, is holomorphic blockwise in Re s>0 and satisfies |H|≤exp(C_{σ₀}√(1+|Im s|)) after increasing constants. Detail: the error of interpolating n^(−s) at the Chebyshev nodes is ≪N^(−Re s)(1+log(m+2))exp(C(1+|s|))2^(−m), by Taylor approximation in n/N around 3/2 on the disc of radius 1, where the logarithm is analytic. For L=log N>K√(1+|s|), multiplying by O(N) and summing gives O(1) choosing K large. The physical replacement of each node by its two squares costs O((1+|s|)^2 N^(−Re s−1)) per unit of mass, by the second derivative and the gap O(√N); rounding costs O(m N^(−Re s)) per block. Both bounds are summable in that tail, with at most polynomial growth. In L≤K√(1+|s|) use the total variation per block. On compact subsets of Re s>0 the same argument gives normal convergence, preserving the polar part throughout that half-plane.

Use η=1/2 in 6713, that is, the average with Mellin decay exp(−c|t|^(2/3)) of 6548. It dominates the growth of H even squared. The identity of transforms of 6761 and the zero of M_V at 1 then allow shifting to any indicated σ₀. The result refers to this fixed weight. To keep de≤CX(log X)^(3/2) with error O(X^(−1)), the absolute mass on de≤Y is O(Y log^C(2Y)) by the dyadic bound of total variation in each index and summation by parts; apply the exponential tail of J as in 6713. There remain O(log⁶(2X)) candidate pairs and de is always a square. This neither reduces the cost of building c to polylogarithmic time nor proves its sign. The nodes are prescribed, but each A_j uses data of a whole block. The additional step relative to 5546 is the preservation of the transform with sub-root error when compressing both indices onto square nodes in advance.

### Coefficient-by-coefficient one-sided criterion and forced oscillation at individual squares

For the integer selection c of 6771, RH is equivalent to c(n)≤C_ε n^(1/2+ε) for every ε>0. It is also equivalent to the same condition for −c. This concerns individual values, without summing pairs or assuming beforehand any control on the opposite sign.

Under RH use M(t)≪_ε t^(1/2+ε) and Abel in each A_j. In the rescaled coordinate, the variation of l_j over the whole block is O(m² log(m+2)) by Markov and the Lebesgue bound; the endpoint terms satisfy the same bound. The distribution between squares has weights ≤1 and a square n can only receive contributions from O(1) blocks with N comparable to n, with O(log² n) nodes per block. Rounding and absorbing the logarithmic powers gives the two-sided ceiling. Conversely, a positive ceiling implies that P(s)=Σ c⁺(n)n^(−s) is absolutely convergent for σ>1/2, by dyadic sparsity. In that region P(s)−(1/ζ(s)+H(s)) continues the series of c⁻. It is regular at every real >1/2. By Landau the nonnegative series c⁻ converges throughout that half-plane (otherwise its real abscissa would be singular). Thus the difference has no exterior poles. For the other sign exchange the parts.

More quantitatively, any zero ρ with β=Re ρ≥1/2 forces, for EACH sign, limsup c^±(n)(log n)^2/n^β>0. Indeed if one part were o(n^β/log² n), its absolute series at β+t would be o(1/t) as t↓0 by the count O(log² N) IN EACH octave and the geometric sum (the initial terms are O(1)). The other series converges for σ>β by the same real Landau argument, and at β+t it also costs o(1/t) because its difference with the first is bounded there by real regularity at β. Consequently the full series at ρ+t would have modulus o(1/t), impossible for the pole of 1/ζ+H at ρ. This already applies to a known zero on the critical line, without assuming RH. The compression, even being exact to the precision of the detector, requires coefficients of both signs and of size at least root up to two logarithms infinitely often. The required one-sided ceiling remains unproved.

### Correlation with nonnegative weights for the energy of all moments of a block

On dyadic [N,2N) take m from 6771, M=2m+2 and θ_n=arccos(2(n−N)/N−1). Write S_j=Σ μ(n)cos(jθ_n). Let F_M(t)=M^(−1)|Σ_{k=0}^{M−1}exp(ikt)|² and
    P(n,r)=[F_M(θ_n−θ_r)+F_M(θ_n+θ_r)]/(2M).
This weight is nonnegative and ≤1 pointwise. The finite Fourier identity gives
    E=Σ_{n,r} μ(n)μ(r)P(n,r)
      = [S₀²+2Σ_{j=1}^{M−1}(1−j/M)S_j²]/M.
The ceiling E≪_ε N^(1+ε) for each ε is equivalent to the global sign. Under RH, Abel and Markov on the block give S_j≪_ε (1+j²)N^(1/2+ε). Conversely the first m moments cost individually ≤√(M E) because their weights do not approach zero. The discrete cosine expansion of each cardinal function of the Chebyshev roots has constant coefficient 1/(m+1) and remaining coefficients of modulus ≤2/(m+1), by orthogonality at the nodes. Thus |A_j|≤2 max_{k≤m}|S_k|, and the distribution and rounding of 6771 imply the ceiling of 6783, absorbing polylogarithmic factors.

The diagonal is computed without RH: P(n,n)=1/2+F_M(2θ_n)/(2M). With r_n=min(n−N,2N−n), the excess over 1/2 costs O(min(1,N/(M²r_n))) for r_n>0 by the sine formula. The sum of the excess is O(1+N(1+log M)/M²), separating r_n≤N/M². By Σμ²=N/ζ(2)+O(√N) on the block, the diagonal is N/(2ζ(2))+O(√N+N(1+log M)/M²). Hence it suffices to bound FROM ABOVE the weighted difference between the distinct pairs of equal sign and those of opposite signs. The lower bound −O(N) of that difference is already automatic since E≥0.

As a reference for magnitude, the total mass of pairs with both indices squarefree, without signs, is ≍N²/M. The floor comes from the zero mode of the same identity with μ². For the ceiling extend to all integers using P≥0: the density in θ of the continuous measure in n is (N/2)sin θ, and its j-th moment is O(N/(1+j²)) by explicit integration. The sum–integral discrepancy is O(1+j) by total variation of cos(jθ). Substituting these bounds in the energy gives O(N²/M) for polylogarithmic M. There thus remains an off-diagonal correlation whose required ceiling is N^(1+ε), against an available mass ≍N²/M. It is a reformulation of the sign, not a proven bound for that correlation.

### Cancellation of the diagonal by four-term rectangles in the Fejér energy

Use on [N,2N) the fixed pairs of 6761, with distance ≤H=N^(2/5), and the weight P of 6791. Denote by a the restriction of μ to paired indices and by b the complementary restriction. For two ordered pairs (u,v),(u',v') oriented from + to −, first sum their four contributions including repetitions if it is the same pair. Then
 Σ_{pairs,pairs'} |P(u,u')−P(v,u')−P(u,v')+P(v,v')| ≪ H² M⁴.
Indeed the expression is a mixed difference. The weight is a polynomial in each real coordinate rescaled to the block: by the cosine expansion of 6791 and |T'_j|≤j² on [−1,1], its mixed derivative is O(M⁴/N²) even at the endpoints. Each rectangle costs at most that bound times H² and there are O(N²) rectangles. In particular E(a)=O(N^(4/5)M⁴)=o(N). This bound needs no cancellation BETWEEN rectangles.

The diagonal of a is N/(2ζ(2))+o(N) by 6791 and because b has o(N) indices and 0≤P≤1. A signed asymptotic follows, without RH:
    Σ_{n≠r} a(n)a(r)P(n,r)=−N/(2ζ(2))+o(N).
The paired indices already generate the compensation of their whole diagonal. The unsigned mass among them is still ≍N²/M: removing the leftovers costs at most 2N·#supp(b)=o(N²/M) by 6761.

Regarding the mixed terms, write E(u) as the squared norm of the weighted moments of 6791. The triangle inequality gives |√E(μ)−√E(b)|≤√E(a)≪N^(2/5)M². Thus the global ceiling is equivalent to E(b)≪_ε N^(1+ε) on the leftovers ALONE; there is no need to postulate an independent bound for the mixed pairs. Since the diagonal of b is o(N), the one-sided ceiling on its off-diagonal correlation suffices. Sparsity alone does not prove that inequality.

### Adaptive selection of crossings of the leftovers at root scale

In each dyadic block of 6804 run through the leftovers b in order and sum their signs, starting at zero. Fix K=⌈√N⌉. For each step between consecutive integers h,h+1 mark its lower level h. Group levels by h modulo K. Choose the least visited class r, with a fixed tie-break; keep only the steps of that class, with their orientation ±1, in a sequence z. It is a simultaneous selection for all moments and both indices. If there are B leftovers, ≤B/K crossings remain, hence O_A(√N/log^A N) positions per block for every fixed A.

The approximation contains more information than the count. Let L_r(h)=⌊(h−r−1)/K⌋. Its increment in the ascending step from h to h+1 is one exactly if h≡r mod K; in the descent the sign changes. By telescoping, on any prefix with original balance H, the sum of z is L_r(H)−L_r(0). The difference between H and K times that sum has modulus <K (also for negative H), by the remainders of Euclidean division. This bound allows discarding all back-and-forth moves that do not alter the net crossing of the marked level, without counting how many there were. Abel and |T'_j|≤j² give for any j<M an error O(K(1+j²)) when replacing b by Kz in the moment S_j. In the norm of 6791 one gets
    |√E(b)−K√E(z)| ≪ K M².
Together with 6804, RH is equivalent to E(z)≪_ε N^ε on each block for every ε>0. In this last test all crossings have coefficient ±1 and the factor √N has already been extracted. A polylogarithmic growth of the error at the normalized level is absorbed in each margin. That ceiling has not been proved: the count controls the total number of crossings but not the oriented balance of the levels sharing the chosen class. This step is deterministic once the leftovers are fixed and requires no new short-interval hypothesis.

### When the crossings disappear and what an exterior zero cannot hide

Let R_N=max H−min H for the balance of leftovers of 6816, counting the empty prefix. The number of DISTINCT lower levels crossed is exactly R_N, all consecutive, because the nonzero jumps are unitary. Hence an empty class exists exactly when R_N<K; for any class the number of distinct levels visited is ⌊R_N/K⌋ or ⌈R_N/K⌉. At the individual level the orientations alternate. Moreover, for any two classes the difference of their oriented balances on each prefix has modulus ≤1: both count with sign how many levels of their class lie between 0 and the current balance. By Abel each cosine moment of the difference costs ≤1+2j (variation of cos(jθ) on [0,π]); by 6791 their energy norms differ by O(M). Choosing the sparsest class can save indices, but cannot reduce a norm of power growth to a subpower one.

If ζ has a zero of real part β>1/2, there are a constant c>0 and infinitely many dyadic blocks in which ALL classes visit at least c N^(β−1/2) distinct levels. Indeed R_N=o(N^β) would imply by 6761 that the oscillation of the prefixes of μ on each block is also o(N^β). Summing the geometric progression of blocks one gets M(x)=o(x^β). Then 1/(sζ(s))=∫₁^∞M(x)x^(−s−1)dx in Re s>β, and at s=ρ+t its modulus would be o(1/t) by taking moduli and splitting the integral into a fixed stretch and its tail. This contradicts the pole. Thus limsup R_N/N^β>0 and the level count gives the floor. This argument gives no upper bound for R_N.

Exact finite check: sieve of μ for 1≤n<2^20; at N=2^k, 4≤k≤19, H=⌊N^(2/5)⌋, use the first integer shift of minimal cost, pair in increasing order and leave the two incomplete cells untouched. For increasing k the R_N were 3,4,6,11,10,17,26,42,51,82,141,204,254,272,492,662. Only for k=14,15 was an empty class missing; in both blocks the least visited class had exactly TWO steps. The other fourteen blocks had zero steps in it. These are data of those sixteen blocks, not a window T nor an asymptotic ceiling.

### Leftovers with exact dilations for a growing family of primes in the test block

On the dyadic block [N,2N), one can impose at once the sparsity of 6761, the prefix error N^(2/5+o(1)) and the exact sign rule under all primes p≤y=(loglog N)logloglog N (N sufficiently large). Local construction: fix P=P(y); for every squarefree n write n=du, d|P and (u,P)=1. In each dyadic block [Y,2Y) of kernels between N/P and 2Ny (including the blocks that cut the endpoints) apply 5546 to μ(u)1_{(u,P)=1}, once only, and keep the leftover b₀(u). Define b_N(du)=μ(d)b₀(u), zero on non-squarefree integers. The same b₀ serves for ALL d. For all N≤n<2N and each p≤y with p∤n, the same kernel is also defined at pn<2Ny, and exactly b_N(pn)=−b_N(n); the rule can be extended outside the block in all packets already formed. No compatibility of masks between different centres is claimed.

Uniformity: P=exp(O(y))=N^o(1), 2^π(y)≤(log N)^C by Chebyshev and log Y∼log N. In the proof of 5546 the sieve expansion uses at most that power of log N progressions; the maximal theorem cited there admits any fixed logarithmic saving. There remain ≪_A Y/log^A N kernels per block of kernels, for each A. The sum over d|P of the remaining number with N≤du<2N costs ≪_A (N/log^A N)∏(1+1/p), and the product of order O(log(2y)) is absorbed by adjusting A. For any subinterval of the original block and each d only the cells cut by its endpoints contribute error between μ and b_N: within complete cells the pairs sum to zero and nothing was deleted at the mesh edges. The error is O((N/d)^(2/5)), since [N/d,2N/d] cuts at most two dyadic blocks of kernels, of comparable sizes. After multiplying by μ(d) and summing, the total error is O(N^(2/5)∏_{p≤y}(1+p^(−2/5)))=N^(2/5+o(1)). Thus the energy reduction of 6804 keeps its precision with these structured leftovers.

Additional arithmetic consequence: for an interval I⊂[N,2N) with |Σ_I μ|≥c N^β, β≥1/2 fixed, one has |Σ_{n∈I} b_N(n)|≥(c−o(1))N^β. Decomposing by d and charging only at the end, for some d|P the excess of rough leftovers in I/d has magnitude ≥(c−o(1))N^β/2^π(y). It remains to control the excess on the rough kernels or its recombination with the signs μ(d). The fixed construction of 6466 admitted more primes but only guaranteed composite support; here support O_A(N/log^A N) is indeed guaranteed simultaneously with the local dilations.

### Local dilations up to log² N with sparse support and root precision with margin

The local selection of 6832 admits y=(log N)^k for fixed 1≤k≤2. The sparsity O_A(N/log^A N) and the exact rule for ALL p≤y remain. The error on any subinterval is N^{σ_k+o(1)} with σ_k=max(2/5,1−1/k). Thus k=5/3 keeps the exponent 2/5, and k=2 still allows transferring every ceiling with margin ε. The supercritical threshold of 6452 was for a single global mask; here the cut is frozen for each N.

For the pairing of kernels use the identity μ·1_{(·,P(y))=1}=μ * 1_{y-smooth integers} (the function on the right includes powers and 1). It is verified prime by prime. In blocks of kernels [Y,2Y) with Y≥√N and Y≤2Ny, and for H=⌊Y^(2/5)⌋, the integral of the sieved short sum in modulus is ≪_A YH/log^A N. Indeed, open the smooth factor d. If d≤Y^(1/40), change x=dv and apply the theorem of 5546 without sieve at scale Y/d and length H/d: the latter exceeds (Y/d)^(1/3+1/30) by a fixed power. The integrated cost is O_A(YH/[d log^A N]); replacing non-integer lengths by their floor costs O(Y) per d, negligible after summing up to Y^(1/40). The reciprocal sum of the smooth d is O(log(2y)) by Mertens. For d>Y^(1/40), each possible multiple occupies an interval of starting points of measure ≤H and there are ≤3Y/d multiples up to 3Y, so the cost is ≤3YH times the smooth reciprocal tail. That tail is ≤Y^(−τ/40)∏_{p≤y}(1−p^(−1+τ))^(−1) with τ=min(1/4,1/log(2y)); the product is polylogarithmic in y by Mertens, and the saving exceeds every inverse power of log N. The same count of leftovers as in 6832 is recovered by mesh shifting. Leave the blocks Y<√N complete and unpaired.

Propagate one and the same selection on the kernels through all d|P(y), with sign μ(d). The kernels of small blocks that reach [N,2N) require d>√N/2; their cost in counting is ≤2N Σ_{smooth d>√N/2}1/d, negligible by the same tail. In large blocks the count is summed as in 6832, using Σ_{d|P}1/d≪log(2y). For the prefix discrepancy, the cost per d is O((N/d)^(2/5)) if there are pairs and zero in unpaired blocks. Since d≤2N, the exponent can be replaced by σ_k paying a constant. The sum costs O(N^σ_k ∏_{p≤y}(1+p^(−σ_k)))=N^{σ_k+o(1)} by Chebyshev, since y^(1−σ_k)≤log N and the denominator log y is gained. This gain covers all moving primes in the block; it provides no cancellation bound for the rough leftovers.

### An exterior zero forces a rough excess in a single band near the record

Let ρ be a zero of real part β>1/2. Fix 1/2<σ<β and put α=2(1−σ)<1. There are arbitrarily large integers N, y=log² N, and intervals (t/2,t] with
    N exp(−C_σ(log N)^α) ≤ t ≤ N
on which |Σ_{t/2<n≤t,(n,P(y))=1} μ(n)| ≥ N^β exp(−C_σ(log N)^α).
It also holds, changing the constant, for the rough leftovers of the kernel pairing of 6840 in the blocks cutting that interval. It suffices to freeze y at N: the construction and the proof admit integer N and dyadic auxiliary blocks. It is a necessary condition under the zero, of magnitude with no prescribed sign.

Proof. The pole argument of 6824 gives |M(X)|≥cX^β infinitely often. Choose N≤X where |M(n)|/n^σ attains its maximum up to X. Then R=|M(N)|/N^σ≥cN^(β−σ), N→∞ and |M(v)|≤Rv^σ up to N. By the smooth convolution of 6840, the rough prefix F_y(v) costs ≤R v^σ A, A=∏_{p≤y}(1−p^(−σ))^(−1). Inverting, write M(N)=Σ_{d|P(y)}μ(d)F_y(N/d) and divide each prefix into bands (t/2,t], t=N/(d2^j), j≥0. Each band costs ≤2R t^σ A. Cut at d2^j≤D. With η=1/log y for large N, the tail costs at most
    2R N^σ A D^(−η) ∏_{p≤y}(1+p^(−σ+η)) /(1−2^(−σ+η)).
By Chebyshev partial summation and p^η≤e, the logarithms of the two products cost O_σ(y^(1−σ)/log y). Hence D=exp(C_σ y^(1−σ)) makes the tail smaller than |M(N)|/2. In what is retained there are at most O(D log(2D)) terms, all with t≥N/D. Some term has modulus ≫|M(N)|/(D log(2D)), which gives the bound. Replacement by rough leftovers on that interval costs O(t^(2/5)) by the prefixes of the cells, since t=N^(1−o(1)). This is smaller than the floor. It has not been assumed that β is the largest real part of the zeros. Here the record avoids paying 2^π(y) or attributing the signal to kernels of size N^δ with fixed δ smaller than one.

### Intrinsic cut at the edge of the band: one and the same arithmetic function at all scales

Put y(v)=max(2,log² v) for v≥1 and A(v)=Σ_{v/2<n≤v, p|n⇒p>y(v)} μ(n). The cut is evaluated at the endpoint v, not at each n. In 6848 the frozen band can be replaced by THIS fixed function: given 1/2<σ<β there are arbitrarily large record scales N and v∈[N exp(−C(log N)^{2(1−σ)}),N] with |A(v)|≥N^β exp(−C(log N)^{2(1−σ)}).

Exact identity. Write L_z(v) for the same band with constant cut z≥y(v). By local products, μ restricted to primes >z is the convolution of μ restricted to primes >w with the indicator of integers whose primes belong to (w,z], for w=y(v). Thus L_z(v)=A(v)+Σ_{d≥2, p|d⇒w<p≤z} L_w(v/d), omitting arguments <1. Repeat. In each branch the successive factors d use strictly descending and disjoint bands of primes. For a given total product l the branch is unique: at the start d must collect ALL powers of l above w, and afterwards the same rule applies to the rest with the new endpoint. It terminates because the steps divide the endpoint by at least two. Consequently L_z(v) is a sum with positive coefficients of A(v/l) over a subset of the z-smooth integers, each l at most once. This uniqueness avoids paying for all ordered factorizations.

Apply this to the expansion of M(N) of 6848 with z=y(N), initial factors d₀|P(z) and dyadic divisor 2^j. The total scale product is q=d₀2^j l. The sum of the absolute weights q^(−s) is majorized for s>0 by (1−2^(−s))^(−1)∏_{p≤z}(1+p^(−s))/(1−p^(−s)). At the record scale, |A(u)|≤2R u^σ∏_{p≤z}(1−p^(−σ))^(−1) as in 6848. The same Rankin with s=σ−1/log z removes q>exp(C(log N)^{2(1−σ)}) at a cost smaller than |M(N)|/2. If the cut is D, at most O(D²(1+log D)) choices of (d₀,l,j) remain; this is absorbed in the constant of the exponent. The announced floor is obtained. Under RH, the smooth convolution and Mertens give |A(v)|≪_ε v^(1/2+ε): at σ=1/2+ε/2<1 the Euler product costs v^o(1); for large ε the result with smaller ε suffices. Hence the two-sided ceiling with every margin for this single function is necessary and sufficient. The positivity of the coefficients of the inner recursion does not fix the sign of A nor remove the outer sign μ(d₀).

### For the intrinsic rough band a single orientation suffices

The ceiling A(v)≤C_σ v^σ for each σ>1/2 implies RH. The ceiling of −A also suffices, separately. Thus the modulus of 6859 can be removed. The key is to use the theta average of 5610 before inverting the small factors with sign.

Proof for fixed σ between 1/2 and 1. Fix large X, z=max(2,log²(X²)) and B=∏_{p≤z}(1−p^(−σ))^(−1)=X^o(1). By the POSITIVE expansion of 6859, L_z(v)≤C_σ B v^σ for v≤X² (zero if v<1). Let w(u)=1_{[1,2]}(u), and choose C with 0≤w≤C h by continuous positivity of h there. For 0<t≤X the theta average of the frozen band satisfies unconditionally
   |∫ h(u)L_z(tu)du/u| ≪_σ B t^σ.
Indeed open the convolution with z-smooth integers of 6840. By 5610 each integrated term is G(t/l)−G(t/(2l)), with G(v)=(2π/v²−1)exp(−π/v²). Its absolute value is O_σ((t/l)^σ) for all v=t/l>0, and the smooth reciprocal sum gives B. The interchange is absolute for fixed t,z by the counting bound and the decay of h (or using a power >1 before applying the identity).

Apply the ceiling of L_z both to the positive weight w and to the positive weight Ch−w. For tu>X² use |L_z(tu)|≤tu and the Gaussian tail of h: since u>X²/t≥X, the contribution is O_σ(t^σ) uniformly, extracting t^(1−σ)≤X^(1−σ). By difference with the controlled theta average, the TWO-SIDED ceiling follows
   |∫ w(u)L_z(tu)du/u| ≪_σ (1+C_σ)B t^σ.
By symmetry everything holds starting from the ceiling of −A. Now invert with μ(d), d|P(z), on the ordinary band L(v)=M(v)−M(v/2). Summing moduli of the frozen averages at t=X/d one obtains
   |∫₁² L(Xu)du/u| ≪_σ (1+C_σ) X^σ B ∏_{p≤z}(1+p^(−σ)) = X^{σ+o(1)} O_σ(1+C_σ).
The Mellin transform of this last average in X is (2^s−1)(1−2^(−s))/(s²ζ(s)) in Re s>1, with no loss of any exterior pole. The bound gives holomorphy in Re s>σ (the average vanishes for X<1/2). Hence even a single exponent σ excludes every zero with real part >σ. Under RH the two-sided converse is 6859. Corollary: each exterior zero of real part β forces both orientations of A(v) to exceed every multiple of v^σ along arbitrarily large sequences for each 1/2<σ<β; the sequences need not coincide. Neither of the two required one-sided bounds has been proved yet.

### The model with all genuine prime powers and continuous simple primes already costs root

Freeze y=(log X)^2, h=log y and use the additive coordinate t=log n, with non-normalized weight. The rough arithmetic measure is the convolution exponential of −Σ_{p>y,j≥1} δ_{j log p}/j: locally the series are finite and each factor exponentiates to δ₀−δ_{log p}. Replace ONLY the terms j=1 by the density −1_{t>h}e^t dt/t; keep all j≥2 at their exact arithmetic positions. Call B_y the resulting measure. One has
    ∫_{[0,log X]} e^(−t/2) d|B_y|(t) = X^o(1).
Hence its total mass on the band (log(X/2),log X], even charged in modulus, is O(X^(1/2+o(1))). It is a uniform control in the moving cut that does not follow by substituting variable η in the arithmetic equivalent of 6045.

Proof. The exponential of the continuous term is, by 6041, δ₀+e^t D′(t/h)dt/h, with D the Dickman function. For a=h/2 its variation weighted at 1/2 over the WHOLE half-axis is 1+∫ e^(au)(−D′(u))du=2+a I(a), I(a)=∫₀^∞e^(au)D(u)du. These moments exist since D(u)≤1/⌊u⌋! (iterate uD(u)=∫_{u−1}^uD). With D=0 on u<0, the last identity extends to 0<u<1, and by Fubini gives I′(a)=[(e^a−1)/a] I(a). Thus log I(a)=O(1+e^a/a) for a≥1, by integration. Since e^a=√y=log X, the cost is exp(O(log X/loglog X)). The separate factor of prime powers has weighted variation truncated at log X at most exp(Σ_{p>y,j≥2,p^j≤X}p^(−j/2)/j). For j=2 Mertens suffices and for j≥3 there is uniform absolute convergence; the cost is polylogarithmic. Convolving multiplies the bounds, since both supports are nonnegative.

The complete identity before truncating is B_y * exp_*(E_y), where E_y=1_{t>h}e^t dt/t−Σ_{p>y}δ_{log p}. In particular EVERY contribution that can exceed root scale with margin lies in B_y*(exp_*(E_y)−δ₀). This last convolution has not been estimated: it also contains all repeated interactions of the discrepancy between simple primes and continuous density. The total variation statement refers to the hybrid model after carrying out its continuous cancellation, not to the variation of the true sieve.

### Complete discretization of the simple intensities by quantiles, for a fixed smooth weight

Fix y=log² X. Put a real point r_j>y where ∫_y^{r_j}dv/log v=j, for positive integer j. In 6881 also replace the continuous density of simple primes by atoms −δ_{log r_j}, keeping the genuine terms of powers p^k, k≥2. For the convolution exponential measure thus obtained, Q_y, one has
    |∫ w(exp(t)/X)dQ_y(t)| ≤ √X exp(O(log X/loglog X))
with the fixed compact weight w(t)=k(log t) of 6548, supported on [1,2]. It is a SIGNED sum bound after discretizing all factors. The total variation bound of 6881 does not carry over to Q_y.

Proof. Omit genuine powers p^k>2X, which does not change the sum on the support of the weight, since all increments are positive. The continuous model with those truncated powers has variation norm weighted at 1/2 over the whole half-axis ≤exp(O(log X/loglog X)) by 6881: there the continuous part was already estimated over the whole half-axis and the weighted mass of the truncated power factor costs only polylogarithms. Its transform is therefore uniformly bounded by that norm in σ≥1/2.

The logarithmic quantile correction has transform E(s) of the simple continuous measure minus the atomic one in multiplicative variable. Its cumulative from y equals the fractional part of ∫_y^v du/log u, between zero and one. For 1/2≤σ≤3/2 one has |E(s)|≤C√(1+|Im s|), with C independent of y≥2. Cut at U=max(y,2+|Im s|). Up to U, if U>y, both positive measures cost O(√U) after weighting by v^(−σ), by bounded density and quantile count up to v of order O(v). After U, by integration by parts the cost is O((1+|s|)U^(−σ)/σ). If U=y there is no initial stretch. The same integral gives holomorphic continuation for σ>0. On exponentiating, the transform of the discrete model is the continuous one times exp(E(s)), at first for σ>1 by absolute convergence. The Mellin multiplier of the weight of 6548 decays like exp(−c|Im s|^(2/3)) in this strip. It dominates exp(C√(1+|Im s|)) and allows moving the inversion from 3/2 to 1/2 (or arriving by dominated limit). This proves the bound.

One can even choose an arbitrary representative in EACH cell [r_{j−1},r_j], r₀=y, with the same uniform bound: the accumulated discrepancy stays bounded by an absolute constant, including possible ties at endpoints. Hence the position mismatch WITHIN cells of unit mass is tolerable in the smooth detector. For the true primes it remains to control the excess and deficit of the number of primes per cell, including their repeated convolutions. The bound for the band with sharp endpoints of 6867 is not inferred.

### Discrete model on true primes with integer multiplicities and all powers

Fix y=log²X and number the primes p>y; for the first one use p_previous=y. Put C(v)=∫_y^v du/log u and m_p=⌊C(p)⌋−⌊C(p_previous)⌋. Use the Euler product ∏_{p>y}(1−p^(−s))^{m_p}, with integer coefficients a_y(n). For a fixed compact weight w with Mellin decay exp(−c|t|^(3/4)) built with the uniforms of 6703, one has unconditionally
   |Σ a_y(n) w(n/X)| ≤ √X exp(O(log X/loglog X)).
The prime support is taken on the ORDINARY primes and only the multiplicity is altered (it admits zero and values larger than one). The bound also holds if in the logarithm ALL terms of powers p^j, j≥2, are kept genuine, with weight one, and only the multiplicity at j=1 is altered.

Detail that allows keeping the true positions. The cumulative E(v)=C(v)−Σ_{y<p≤v}m_p has modulus ≤1 on reaching a prime, and between primes it grows at rate 1/log v. The Heath-Brown bound Σ_{p≤V}(p_next−p)²≪_ε V^(23/18+ε), recorded in R184_093_REVIEW_009_010_012:37, implies ∫_V^{2V}|E(v)|dv≪_ε V^(23/18+ε) for V≥y. It suffices to sum areas in each gap; the gaps crossing the endpoints, including the one containing y, are included completely (Bertrand). The transform of the simple continuous measure minus the atoms m_p continues via s∫ E(v)v^(−s−1)dv to σ>5/18+ε, from σ>1. In 1/2≤σ≤3/2 its modulus is O((2+|Im s|)^(7/10)), uniform in large y. Indeed take U=(2+|Im s|)^(7/5). If U≥y cut at a prime between U and 2U; the weighted variation up to that point costs O(√U) by partial summation and Σ_{y<p≤v}m_p≤C(v), and the boundary term costs O(1). If U<y start directly at y, with zero cumulative. In the tail the dyadic means give O((1+|s|)max(U,y)^(5/18+ε−σ)); choose for example ε=1/1000. Both contributions fit in the exponent 7/10. This continuation does not require ordinary convergence of the Stieltjes integral without integrating by parts at the boundary.

In 6891 now take the factor of higher powers with weights m_p. For p^j≤2X its logarithmic cost at abscissa 1/2 is O(loglog X) (even O(log X) would not suffice here): Σ m_p/p≪1+loglog X by the cumulative bound C(v)≪v/log v and Abel, and Σ m_p/p^(3/2)≪1. Omitting larger powers does not alter the physical support of the test. By 6881 the model with continuous simple intensity keeps its cost exp(O(log X/loglog X)). Multiplying it by the exponential of the previous correction costs exp(O((2+|t|)^(7/10))), dominated in the Mellin inversion by the decay of order 3/4. Shifting to 1/2 as in 6891 proves both versions. Compared with R184_093 the use here is deterministic for a complete integer Euler product. The comparison with rough μ still has the differences 1−m_p; the square-gap theorem controls the transport of the continuous intensity but not that balance.

### Multiplicity one except for an exceptional mass smaller than V/log^A V

In 6903 one can choose integer multiplicities m'_p≥0 on the true primes so that in EACH block [V,2V), V=2^k y, k≥0 (here y=log² X and 2^k y denotes the product), one has Σ|m'_p−1|≪_A V/log^A V for every fixed A. At the same time the Euler product with those weights keeps the signed estimate √X exp(O(log X/loglog X)) with the SAME compact weight of order 3/4. The exceptional sum counts all additional copies, besides the removed primes.

Split each block with integer step H=⌊V^(3/10)⌋ and a shift to be chosen. In each complete cell redistribute among its primes the integer mass M of 6903; if there are k primes, put one on as many as possible and distribute the remaining excess, if any. If k=0 also M=0. Thus Σ|m'_p−1|=|M−k| in each cell. On the two incomplete edges leave the old mass. The endpoints can be treated with intervals (a,b] consistently.

For a cell starting at t, |M−k| is bounded by |π(t+H)−π(t)−∫_t^{t+H}du/log u| plus |E(t)|+|E(t+H)|, with the cumulative E of 6903. By 2909 and Cauchy–Schwarz the integral over the starting points of the first modulus is ≪_A VH/log^A V: replacing log p by log t inside the interval costs at most O(H(H+1)/V) before dividing by log t, and the same when varying the continuous denominator. The integral of the endpoint errors is O_ε(V^(23/18+ε)) by 6903. Averaging over the real shift and dividing both bounds by H gives ≪_A V/log^A V, taking ε<3/10−5/18. Choose a mesh satisfying this; the real cost of the cells, independent of A, can be minimized. The edges cost O(H+1+V^(23/36+ε)) by the pointwise bound for a gap deduced from the second moment (or by Baker–Harman–Pintz). This is still negligible compared with V/log^A V.

To check the detector, the new cumulative E' differs from E only by redistributions within cells, with absolute area per cell ≤HM. Over the whole block the original mass is O(V), so that ∫_V^{2V}|E'|≪V^(13/10) uniformly. This also holds on dyadic intervals translated above y by covering. In σ≥1/2, T=2+|Im s|, cut the Stieltjes integral with a smooth partition at U=T^(10/7), equal to one up to U and zero from 2U. The low part costs O(√U) by the cumulative count O(v) even after redistribution (always within the same block). In the tail integrate by parts with E', zero at the initial endpoint and growing on average as just proved. The derivative of the cut costs O(1/U) on [U,2U], and the dyadic series gives O(T max(U,y)^(3/10−σ)) for the continuation, with no pointwise term at U. Thus the logarithmic correction continues with growth O(T^(5/7)) in the strip of 6903. The higher powers with m'_p cost polylogarithms there after truncating them at 2X: the cumulative mass is O(v/log v) using the original count up to the end of the block comparable with v. Since 5/7<3/4, the same inversion proves the announced ceiling. The higher powers can also be left with multiplicity one. The signed effect of removing the exceptional corrections from the simple prime term has not been estimated.

### The exceptional defect admits a fixed linear criterion, even one-sided

Run 6903 and 6913 ONCE with y=2 on dyadic blocks up to infinity, ignoring the prime 2. Write C(x)=∫₂^x dt/log t. In a cell with mass M≥k>0, assign the excess M−k to the FIRST prime and one to each other; if M<k, use only zeros and ones as before. On the incomplete edges leave the initial weights. The same proof of 6913 gives Σ_{V<p≤2V}|1−m'_p|≪_A V/log^A V and for EVERY prime p>2
    |Σ_{2<q≤p}m'_q−C(p)| ≪ p^(3/10)+1.
Indeed at the last prime r of the cell the new and old cumulative masses coincide, with value ⌊C(r)⌋. From any prime p of that cell, each subsequent prime up to r carries at most one; hence the difference between the two new cumulatives at p and r costs O(H+1). Also C(r)−C(p)=O(H+1), H=⌊V^(3/10)⌋. This holds even when the first original mass was very large due to a previous gap. On the edges, equality with the old cumulative is exact. On freezing y=2, the exceptional positions and their multiplicities no longer change with the test point.

Let D(x)=Σ_{2<p≤x}(1−m'_p), an ordinary sum of integer defects over the exceptional primes. At primes D(p)=π(p)−1−C(p)+O(p^(3/10)+1). Thus RH is equivalent to D(x)≤C_ε x^(1/2+ε) for every ε, and separately to the ceiling of −D. Justification: RH gives the classical two-sided bound for π−C. In the other direction, a ceiling for D at primes transfers a ceiling for π−C to every x using the previous prime and the monotonicity of C. For the floor use the next prime and subtract one, comparable with x by Bertrand. For σ>1/2, the corresponding one-sided ceiling for π−C excludes zeros with real part >σ: its Mellin transform multiplied by s in Re s>1 is Σ_p p^(−s)−∫₂^∞ v^(−s)dv/log v. The first term is log ζ(s) up to the powers j≥2, holomorphic in Re s>1/2; the second cancels the real logarithmic singularity at 1 (its derivative is −2^(1−s)/(s−1)). The continuation is regular on the real axis >1/2 and its derivative has a pole at any exterior zero. Landau applied to the one-sided majorant minus the error, or to the symmetric one for the floor, gives the exclusion. Since D is constant between exceptions, it suffices to impose the ceiling at its jumps (and adjust an initial term). The inequality does not require estimating products of defects; it amounts to controlling their accumulated signed sum. The previously proven sparsity does not yet allow replacing the signed sum by the sum of moduli.

### Unconditional sign of the exceptional balance in the theta average of atoms

With the FIXED weights of 6923 and the positive h of 5610, with Mellin transform ξ, for all X→∞ one has
    Σ_{p>2}(1−m'_p) log p h(p/X) = −(ξ(1/2)/2+o(1))√X.
More precisely, on adding to the left-hand side the genuine terms Σ_p log p [h(p²/X)+h(p³/X)], the result is O(X^(3/10)log(2X)). This computes a signed average exclusive to the defects at a precision strictly better than root after the two explicit corrections.

Proof. For the redistributed part, integrating log v h(v/X) against dC(v)=dv/log v produces Xξ(1) with a rapidly decreasing error from the endpoint 2. The difference with the atoms m'_p is O(X^(3/10)log(2X)) by parts: in each octave [V,2V] the absolute integral of E'=C−Σm'_p costs O(V^(13/10)) by 6913. The derivative of the test costs O_B(V^(−1)log(2V) min((V/X)^B,(X/V)^B)) for each fixed B by the two-sided decay of h and of its derivative. Sum the dyadic series. For the genuine part with ALL powers, Mellin gives the integrand X^s ξ(s)(−ζ′/ζ)(s), without the divisor s that appeared in 6469 for prefixes. The same shift to Re s=−1 gives Xξ(1)+O(1): there are no poles at the zeros, and the only main term is that of 1. The powers of order ≥4 cost O(X^(1/4)log²(2X)) by Chebyshev in each octave and the decay of h. The isolated term p=2 that distinguishes both conventions is negligible. The cubes cost O(X^(1/3)log(2X)); the squares, by PNT and partial summation, equal (ξ(1/2)/2+o(1))√X, with a strictly positive constant. This proves both versions.

In particular, in EVERY annulus [X/R,XR], R=√(2log X), there are ≫√X/log X exceptional copies of negative sign, counting multiplicity (m'_p−1)_+. Indeed outside the annulus the weighted masses are o(√X) by the reciprocal Gaussian decay and the cumulative bound O(v/log v) for primes and copies; inside, log p h(p/X)≪log X. This does not fix the sign of the unweighted prefix D(x): the chosen average cancels precisely the contributions of the exterior zeros. The antecedent 6469 already computed the bias for θ against the continuous measure; the new control is that the fixed exceptional set reproduces that signal in full, with its own sub-root error.

### Removing log p turns the exceptional theta bias into an eventual sign criterion

For the same fixed defects d_p=1−m'_p put U(X)=Σ_{p>2}d_p h(p/X), without log p. Then RH is equivalent to U(X)≤0 for all sufficiently large X. Under RH, more precisely,
    U(X) = −(ξ(1/2)/2+o(1)) √X/log X.
In the presence of a zero of real part β>1/2, U takes both orientations of magnitude larger than any multiple of X^σ, for each 1/2<σ<β, along sequences of scales. This conclusion is for the positive weight h and for exceptional atoms without logarithmic weighting.

Detection direction. By 6913 with y=2 the difference of transforms between the copies m'_p and the density dv/log v is holomorphic in Re s>3/10, integrating the cumulative by parts on average. In the strip Re s>1/2 the series of the defects therefore has locally the singularity of log ζ(s) at each zero, while the density term cancels the singularity at 1 as in 6923. The Mellin transform of U is ξ(s) times that series (product), initially to the right of 1. At a zero of multiplicity m its germ contains a nonzero constant times (s−ρ)^m log(s−ρ) times an analytic unit; the monodromy is 2πi m ξ(s), not identically zero. The function is regular on the real axis >1/2. Landau applied to a ceiling of either sign, after removing the rapidly decaying stretch X<1, prevents such a singularity to the right of the exponent of the ceiling. This explains why the zero of the weight does kill the derived logarithmic pole in 6931 but not the branching of the logarithm itself.

Sign direction under RH. Write L=log X, v=log(p/X) and T_j=Σ d_p log p h(p/X)v^j. T₀ comes from 6931. For fixed j=1,2,3, under RH T_j=O_j(√X). Indeed, in the computation of 6931 for ψ the multiplier is now ξ^(j)(s); by the explicit formula the contribution of zeros is bounded by √X Σ_ρ m_ρ |ξ^(j)(ρ)| over distinct zeros, finite by gamma decay and the zero count. The shift is justified by good heights as in 5241. The residue at 1 cancels with the continuous integral and the replacement by copies still costs O_j(X^(3/10)log X) by the same control of area and derivatives. The squares cost O_j(√X) by Chebyshev and the rest of the powers less. To divide by log p use the finite identity 1/(L+v)=Σ_{j=0}^3(−v)^j/L^{j+1}+v^4/[L^4(L+v)]. On X^(1/2)≤p≤X^(3/2), the remainder integrated against the logarithmic defects costs O(√X/L³): by Abel, the prefix of those defects is O(√t log²(2t)) under RH. This bound comes for the true primes from θ(t)−t; for the copies one uses 6923 at primes, between them the gap O(√t log²(2t)) under RH (or one uses directly the area of 6913 against the test). More explicitly the unweighted cumulative of the defects is O(√t log t) under RH at primes by 6923 and π−C, and constant between primes; a single application of Abel gives the declared weighted prefix. The remainder test has factor L^(−5), with derivative in log p dominated by that factor times a fixed polynomial in |v| multiplied by h and its derivative on logarithmic scale. The Gaussian decay at both ends makes the outer tails negligible even in modulus. Thus U=T₀/L+O(√X/L²), which fixes the sign under RH. The eventual sign without RH has not been obtained.

### Joint restriction on height and real part if the sign fails at one scale

Fix 0<c<π/4. If U(X)≥0 at a sufficiently large scale, there is a zero ρ=β+iγ satisfying
   (β−1/2)log X ≥ loglog X + c|γ| − O_c(1).
It is a necessary condition at that SAME scale, not merely a statement of excursions along a sequence. In particular the violation requires an exterior zero at height O_c(log X). The constants are not numerically certified.

Proof. Put L=log X and b=3/4. By 6913 the sum of copies with h(p/X) differs from ∫₂^∞ h(v/X)dv/log v by O(X^(3/10)), by parts. In both simple measures introduce log v∫₀^b v^(−t)dt=1−v^(−b); omitting the remainder costs O(X^(1−b)) using the decay of h and comparison with the integer count. For t∈[0,b], first sum all prime powers with weight Λ(n)n^(−t)h(n/X). The explicit formula with multiplier ξ(s) gives the main term X^(1−t)ξ(1−t) and the terms −Σ_ρ m_ρ X^(ρ−t) ξ(ρ−t) (distinct zeros). The line Re s=−1 leaves O(X^(−1)) uniformly, since Re(s+t)∈[−1,−1/4] crosses no trivial zeros, and good heights and gamma decay are used; no hypothesis on the zeros. The main term cancels the continuous integral, on extending it down to zero with a rapidly decreasing error. Integrating in t and removing powers k≥2 gives −Σ_{p,k≥2} h(p^k/X)(1−p^(−kb))/k. The squares give −(ξ(1/2)/2+o(1))√X/L by PNT, the k≥3 cost O(X^(1/3)log²X). One concludes
   U(X)=−(ξ(1/2)/2+o(1))√X/L − Σ_ρ m_ρ X^ρ ∫₀^b exp(−Lt)ξ(ρ−t)dt.
Here the series is absolute, the formula is unconditional and the o(1) of the main term includes no zero terms.

Choose c<c₁<π/4. By Stirling, polynomial growth of ζ in fixed strips and Cauchy for ξ′, |ξ(ρ−t)|≤C t exp(−c₁|γ|) on that segment, since ξ(ρ)=0. Each integral costs ≤C exp(−c₁|γ|)/L². Extract the supremum of exp((β−1/2)L−c|γ|) and sum m_ρ exp(−(c₁−c)|γ|), convergent by the zero count. To counteract the main term that supremum must be ≳_c L; it is attained because the penalized height tends to minus infinity. This proves the statement. The restriction does not exclude the existence of such zeros nor does it by itself certify the sign for a numerical scale.

### Exceptional bias with doubly exponential height penalty

The Fourier filter of 2496 already reaches heights loglog X for another observable. For the fixed defects of 6923 one can simultaneously keep the negative bias of the squares and the necessary branching at multiple zeros. Let w₀(v) be the density, positive in the broad sense, of 2496 (square of the inverse of exp(−cosh), normalized), and let H be the convolution in log of h with w₀(v)dv, that is H(t)=∫h(te^(−v))w₀(v)dv. It is strictly positive. Its Mellin transform is K(s)=ξ(s)B(s), with B(s)=∫w₀(v)e^(sv)dv holomorphic for |Re s|<π. Define U_H(X)=Σ_{p>2}(1−m'_p)H(p/X). For X sufficiently large, if U_H(X)≥0 there is a zero β+iγ with
    (β−1/2)log X ≥ loglog X + c exp(|γ|/2) − C
