for constants c>0, C. In particular |γ|≤2loglog X+O(1). This statement uses another observable and does not change the wedge of 6951 for U.

Indeed, by the product integral of 2496, in −2≤Re s≤2 one has |B(s)|≪exp(−c₀ exp(|Im s|/2)): the real part of the parameter 2cosh((Im s−i Re s)/2) is ≥2 cos(1)cosh(Im s/2). In a smaller fixed neighbourhood, Cauchy and the gamma bound give the same for K′ with reduced c₀. The physical logarithmic derivatives of H are O(min(t²,t^(−2))) by the decay of w₀ and of h; any fixed exponent <π can be used. These bounds suffice in the arguments of 6951: the replacement by density costs O(X^0.3), the endpoints of the continuous integral when introducing 1/log p cost o(1) at the lower endpoint, the powers ≥3 cost O(X^(1/3)log²X), and one can shift to Re s=−1. The formula of 6951 remains with K instead of ξ, with bias −K(1/2)√X/(2log X), in the asymptotic sense for the contribution of squares. The residue per zero is bounded by C mρ X^β exp(−c₁ exp(|γ|/2))/(log X)² using K(ρ)=0. Extracting the penalized supremum with 0<c<c₁ and summing the multiplicities as in 6951 proves the result.

Under RH the sum over zeros is O(√X/log²X), so U_H is eventually negative. Conversely the argument of 6941 applies because K(s)logζ(s) keeps branching at each zero whatever its finite order as a zero of K. Hence the new eventual sign remains equivalent to the target. The suppression of large heights was known in the corpus; what is specific is the joint inequality with the term loglog X due to the bias and to the zero of the multiplier. The constants have not been made effective nor has negativity been proved without RH.

### Sign criterion on a positive mesh of O(log X loglog X) scales up to X

Construction independent of the zeros. In the coordinate u=log X take blocks [L,2L] with L=2^j≥4. Divide each into ⌈log L⌉ equal panels of length b and use on each panel the Gauss–Legendre quadrature with m=⌈100L⌉ nodes, with its positive weights for du. Let G be the union of the nodes in u. Then RH is equivalent to U_H(exp u)≤0 at all sufficiently large nodes. There are O(log X loglog X) nodes up to X in the original scale. It is an infinite condition on prescribed scales. It is not claimed that the sign at the nodes interpolates the sign between them by monotonicity.

Proof of fidelity. F(z)=U_H(exp z) extends to an entire function: invert at Re s=3/2 the Mellin transform K(s)Σ d_p p^(−s), with absolutely convergent series and K from 6963. Uniformly in z, with R=|Im z|, its modulus costs at most C exp((3/2)Re z+3 R log(2+R)+O(R+1)). Indeed the height envelope exp(−c exp(|t|/2)) allows extracting the maximum of R|t|−(c/2)exp(|t|/2), which is ≤2R log(2+R)+O(R+1); the remaining factor is integrable. In the disc of radius 2b around the centre of each panel, Re z>0 for large L and R≤2L/log L. For s in any compact subset of Re s>0 one has |F(z)exp(−sz)|≤exp(12L) eventually: the additional factor costs exp(O_s(b)) and the term (3/2)Re z≤(3+o(1))L. Truncating Taylor at degree 2m−1 gives on the panel an error O(exp(12L)4^(−2m)). The weights are positive, sum to b and are exact up to that degree; both the integral and the quadrature of the error cost ≤b times that supremum. The errors of all panels thus form a function holomorphic in Re s>0 by normal convergence.

Hence the discrete transform Σ_{u∈G} w_u F(u)exp(−su) keeps the branching of K(s)logζ(s) at each exterior zero and the real regularity for s>1/2. It coincides with the continuous Mellin transform up to a function holomorphic there: besides the quadrature error, u<4 has been omitted, whose integral is holomorphic in the relevant strip (at −∞ F(u)=O(exp(2u)) by the physical decay). The initial comparison is made in 3/2<Re s<2. If the values were eventually nonpositive, Landau for the discrete measure of fixed sign would exclude that branching. Even under a zero with β>1/2, the mesh has values of both signs exceeding any multiple of exp(σu) for 1/2<σ<β: in Landau subtract the majorant of that size, whose series of weights converges in Re s>σ because they sum to the length of each panel and this has length o(L). Under RH the eventual sign at all points comes from 6963. This mesh reduces the points where the sign would have to be proved without altering the observable. It does not supply the sign at those points.

### Minimal mass of the excursions of both signs at the exponent of the zero

With G, F, K and the previous weights, put F₊=max(F,0), F₋=max(−F,0). RH is equivalent to the finiteness of Σ w_u F₊(u) exp(−σu) for each σ>1/2. Under RH the positive part has finite support by the eventual sign already proved. For the converse the following quantitative obstruction holds. If ρ=β+iγ is a zero with β>1/2 of multiplicity m, then for each sign
```
limsup (j→∞) Σ_{2^j≤u<2^(j+1)} w_u F±(u) u^m exp(−βu)
    ≥ (log 2) m |K^(m)(ρ)| / 2 > 0.
```
K^(m) denotes the derivative of order m. The constant depends on the zero.

Indeed, let α± be the abscissae of the positive series P± and D=P₊−P₋ in the initial half-plane. Both abscissae are ≤3/2 by the bound on F and the mass of the weights per block. If one exceeds the other and 1/2, the regularity of D along the real axis continues the series of larger abscissa to its real limit point of convergence, contradicting Landau. If both are smaller than β, D would be holomorphic in a half-plane containing ρ, incompatible with its branching. Hence both have the same abscissa α≥β. This proves the converse of the criterion.

If α>β, the masses per block of each sign in the formula are unbounded, since a bound would allow summing the blocks with the additional discount exp(−εu) for every ε>0. If α=β, the derivatives of order m of the series converge absolutely to the right of β. Near ρ, K has order m by the previous factorization; the branched part of D is m K(s)log(s−ρ). Approaching horizontally from the right, D^(m)(ρ+t)=m K^(m)(ρ)log t+O(1). The real value D^(m)(β+t) stays bounded. By the triangle inequality, the two positive sums A±(t)=Σ w_u F±(u) u^m exp(−(β+t)u) have sum ≥|D^(m)(ρ+t)| and bounded difference. Each therefore has liminf A±(t)/log(1/t) ≥ m|K^(m)(ρ)|/2. If M is the finite limsup of the masses per block of one of the signs, for every ε>0 its sum A(t) is ≤Oε(1)+(M+ε)Σ exp(−t2^j). This last series is log(1/t)/log 2+O(1), splitting into 2^j≤1/t and its tail. This proves the bound. A one-sided arithmetic majorization for F₊ remains open.

### Removal of the centre of radius X^(3/4) in the positive mass

Let dν(v)=Σ_{p>2}δ_p−1_{v≥2}dv/log v. At each node u of 6973, X=exp u, keep only
    J(X)=∫_{|v−X|>X^(3/4)} H(v/X)(1−log v/u) dν(v).
Then |F(u)−J(X)|≪√X/u unconditionally. In particular the finiteness of the discounted positive sum of 6981 is equivalent to the same test with J. The removal is around each observation scale X.

Indeed, replacing the copies by the continuous intensity in F costs O(X^0.3) by 6963. For the test log v H(v/X), the integral against ν is O(√X): in the computation of 6931 use K instead of ξ, whose zero cancels each pole of −ζ′/ζ at the zeros. The main term cancels with the continuous integral; the squares cost O(√X) by Chebyshev and the decay of H, and the higher powers O(X^(1/3)log²X) as in 6963. Divide by u. In the removed centre |1−log v/u|≪X^(−1/4)/u; there are at most 2X^(3/4)+1 integers, and the continuous mass is O(X^(3/4)). The total cost is therefore O(√X/u). The positive part is 1-Lipschitz and the additional discount exp(−εu) makes those errors summable by blocks. In the remaining integrand the factor changes sign at X: the excesses of primes below and the deficits above contribute in the dangerous direction. The estimate does not control their balance.

### Removal of |v−X|≤X^θ for every fixed θ<1 by dilations

Write g(y)=H(exp y). For each integer r≥1 there are r fixed translations a_i such that the columns (g^(j)(a_i))_{0≤j<r} form a basis. If all vectors of this type lay in a hyperplane, g would satisfy on the whole line a linear ODE with constant coefficients not all zero. In Fourier we would have P(iτ)ĝ(τ)=0; impossible, since g is integrable and positive and ĝ is continuous and nonzero near 0. The necessary fixed derivatives exist and decay at both ends by the Mellin inversion of 6963.

With u=log X choose G_u(y)=Σ c_i(u)g(y+a_i) making its first r Taylor coordinates (degrees 0,...,r−1) coincide with those of g(y)/(u+y) at zero. The fixed inverse gives c_i=O_r(1/u). Then W_u(y)=g(y)−(u+y)G_u(y) satisfies |W_u(y)|≤C_r |y|^r for |y|≤1 and large u, by Taylor and the uniform bound of the r-th derivative. The integral of the subtracted term against ν costs O_r(√X/u) by 6994 applied at the fixed scales X exp(−a_i) to the test log v H(v exp(a_i)/X).

For 0<θ<1 choose r with (r+1)(1−θ)≥1/2. In |v−X|≤X^θ there are O(X^θ) integers and continuous mass O(X^θ); moreover |log(v/X)|≪X^(θ−1). The joint cost is O_r(X^[1−(r+1)(1−θ)])=O_r(√X). Thus, if Jθ integrates only W_u(log(v/X)) against ν outside that interval, F(u)=Jθ+O_θ(√X). This suffices to transfer in both directions the positive summability of 6981. Example: r=4 allows θ=9/10. The constants depend on the fixed matrix; the argument does not allow passing to radius proportional to X and the new exterior weight may change sign.

### Obstruction to absolute control of the exterior for bounded translations

Fix any nontrivial zero ρ of ξ, of real part β and multiplicity m in K (one on the critical line suffices). Any number of translations is now allowed, |a_i|≤A and Σ|c_i|≤u^D, with A,D fixed. For some fixed sufficiently large B and R=B log u, the previous weight W=g−(u+y)G satisfies
    ∫_{−R}^R |W(y)| exp(βy)dy ≫ u^(−m).
Indeed, the integral of each translate of g against exp(ρy) over the whole line is exp(−ρa_i)K(ρ)=0. The tails omitted in the integral of G are O(u^D exp(−cR)) with c>0, by the two-sided decay of 6963. In the same band expand 1/(u+y) up to degree m in y; the remainder integrated against g exp(ρy) costs O(u^(−m−2)) by the absolute moment of order m+1. The complete moments are K^(j)(ρ), zero for j<m. Extending the truncated moments to complete ones costs O(u^(−m−2)) choosing B large. Hence the integral of W exp(ρy)/(u+y) over the band is (−1)^m K^(m)(ρ)/u^(m+1)+O(u^(−m−2)). Take moduli and use u+y≥u/2.

In particular the cost with the positive density dv/log v alone on that band is ≫ X/u^[m+1+B(1−β)] by change of variable. For the weights of 7002 the absolute contribution of the removed centre is O_θ(√X), so the same lower order persists on the exterior. This unconditional obstruction excludes separate majorization in modulus of the continuous measure and of the prime measure with these translations. It gives no lower bound for their signed difference.

### Pairs by rank: only odd shifts up to order O(√log p)

Let p_n be the n-th prime larger than 2 and q_n=C^{-1}(n), with C from 6923. Let b_n=(log p_n+log q_n)/2, d_n=(log p_n−log q_n)/2. The classical PNT with exponential remainder gives |d_n|≤exp(−c√b_n) eventually: first p_n/q_n→1, then apply the mean value theorem to C(p_n)−C(q_n)=O(p_n exp(−c'√log p_n)) and absorb the factor log p_n. Write g(y)=H(exp y). For a sufficiently large fixed constant A put k_n=ceil(A√b_n). Then, uniformly for X≥2, u=log X,
    F(u)=2 Σ_n Σ_{1≤j≤k_n, j odd} g^(j)(b_n−u) d_n^j/j! + O(X^0.3+1).

Indeed the passage from the copies to the density costs O(X^0.3) by 6963. The quadrature of that density with q_n costs at most the total variation of g, independent of X: in the coordinate C the right endpoint of each unit interval is used. For each pair, symmetric Taylor at the midpoint cancels all even terms. In the complex disc of radius one around b_n−u, g is bounded by a uniform constant by Mellin inversion at Re s=0 and the vertical decay of 6963. Cauchy bounds the tail by O(|d_n|^(k_n+1)) when |d_n|≤1/2. Choosing Ac>2 makes that bound summable even before fixing X, since exp(b_n) is comparable with p_n. The initial pairs cost O(1) uniformly by the same derivative bounds. The series over pairs converge by the physical decay of the original test and the summability of the remainder.

Antecedent 103_61: it uses von Mangoldt cells and finds both signs per tower. Here the comparison is between the ordinary prime and a single point of equal rank; the additional conclusion is a summable absolute remainder when truncating only the odd moments, without assuming RH. Cancellation between shifts in the displayed sum is still needed; the PNT used for the remainder does not even control the linear term at the required scale.

### The linear term detects the frontier of zeros when it is smaller than one

Let Θ be the supremum of the real parts of the nontrivial zeros and S(u)=2Σ_n d_n g′(b_n−u), with the pairs of 7018. If Θ<1, for each ε>0
    |F(log X)−S(log X)| ≪_ε X^(max(0.3,3Θ−2)+ε).
Hence, if 1/2<Θ<1, the abscissae of the positive series of S₊ and S₋ on the mesh of 6973 are both exactly Θ. In particular a summable ceiling at every discount σ>1/2 for S₊ leaves only two possibilities: RH or Θ=1.

Detail: for every θ between Θ and 1, π(x)−C(x)=Oθ(x^θ). In the truncated explicit formula for ψ at half-integers with height comparable to x, the zeros cost O(x^Θ log²x) summing 1/|ρ|; the truncation costs O(log²x). Monotonicity, subtraction of powers and Abel give the statement absorbing logarithms. By the mean value theorem as in 7018, |d_n|≪exp((θ−1)b_n) enlarging θ arbitrarily little. In an octave exp(b_n)≈V, the remainder of the symmetric linear Taylor per pair costs O(|d_n|³ min((V/X)²,(X/V)²)), by the third derivative of g (Mellin at ±2). There are O(V) pairs; the dyadic sum is O(X^(3θ−2)) since −2<3θ−2<2. Add the replacement error X^0.3 and take θ close to Θ. Likewise |S|≪X^θ by the identical computation with the first power of d_n. The weights per block in u sum to its length and ensure convergence for σ>Θ. Conversely, by 6981 the two abscissae of F are ≥Θ; the error has abscissa strictly smaller than Θ and the positive and negative parts are 1-Lipschitz. This proves the equality without requiring a zero on the frontier. Under RH the error is o(√X/log X) and S inherits the eventual negative sign of F. If Θ=1 the strict separation of exponents is lost; the ordinary PNT does not provide a fixed strip here.

### One fixed point per pair approximates the linear balance even if Θ=1

With b_n,d_n of 7018 there is a deterministic selection t_n∈I_n=[b_n−|d_n|,b_n+|d_n|], independent of X and of the test g, such that for every fixed A
    F(log X)=Σ_n 2d_n g′(t_n−log X)+O_A(√X/(log X)^A).
In particular the new linear balance has eventually negative sign under RH and its positive-mass ceiling of 6981 is equivalent to RH with no hypothesis on Θ. The selection changes the midpoint of 7027.

Construction: group by dyadic V≤exp(b_n)<2V, processing each group by increasing rank. The exact difference of values of g at the oriented endpoints is 2d_n by the uniform average of g′ on I_n. To replace the uniform λ_n by a point t, use as vector h_t(z)=2d_n(1_{t≤z}−λ_n((−∞,z])) in L²(dz). It has mean zero when t is uniform, support in I_n and squared norm ≤8|d_n|³. From an accumulated B initially zero in each group, take the smallest minimizer of ||B+h_t||² on I_n (continuity in L²); the minimum is ≤||B||²+8|d_n|³ by averaging. Update B. For d_n=0 choose b_n. By induction the final vector has norm ≤(8Σ_group |d_n|³)^(1/2) ≪ √V exp(−c√log V) by 7018 adjusting c. All supports of the group occupy an interval of bounded length around log V. Integrating by parts the joint error against g′ one obtains in modulus ≤||B||₂ ||g″(·−log X)||₂ over that interval. The second factor costs O(min((V/X)²,(X/V)²)) by 6963. Sum over V: the exponential saving gives any logarithmic power for V≥√X; for V<√X the sum without saving costs O(X^(−3/4)). Absorb O(X^0.3+1) from the two substitutions of 7018. The series converge absolutely for fixed X by the decay of g′. The ceiling for the selected balance remains to be proved. The construction controls only the error with which each uniform is replaced by a sample.

### Enclosure of the signed prefix by two evaluations of one and the same integral

Let N(x)=#{2<p≤x}, E=N−C, I(x)=−∫₂ˣ E(t)dt/t and D_n=Σ_{k≤n} log(p_k/q_k). Then, with the same δ_n at both ends,
    I(q_n) ≤ D_n+δ_n ≤ I(p_n),     0≤δ_n≤log(q_n/2).
In particular I(p_n)≥I(q_n) for each rank, whatever the orientation of its shift. The upper gap has the exact positive formula
    I(p_n)−(D_n+δ_n)=∫_{q_n}^{p_n} (C(t)−n)dt/t.
By PNT it is asymptotic to (p_n−q_n)²/(2p_n log p_n) when p_n≠q_n and n→∞.

Proof: define A(x)=∫₂ˣ N(t)dt/t and B(x)=∫₂ˣ C(t)dt/t. The function n log x−A(x) attains its maximum at p_n, with value Σ_{k≤n} log p_k, by the sign of its derivative outside the jumps. For B the maximum occurs at q_n and equals ∫₀ⁿ log(C^{-1}(s))ds by parts. By monotone comparison between integral and right sum, the latter is Σ log q_k−δ_n with the indicated error. Evaluating the difference of the two maxima first at q_n and then at p_n gives the bounds; integrating the derivative between both points gives the gap. The quadratic equivalence follows from q_n/p_n→1 and C′(t)=1/log t uniformly on the segment after normalizing by 1/log p_n. The enclosure is for prefixes by rank. In the sum proved in 7035 the factors g′(t_n−u) vary; the comparison of prefixes alone does not fix its sign.

### Inverse duality: a ceiling for the primorial at its own rank suffices

P_n=Σ_{2<p≤p_n}log p. Exactly D_n+δ_n=P_n−q_n+2, because ∫₀ⁿ log(C^{-1}(s))ds=q_n−2. RH is equivalent separately to each of the two bounds P_n−q_n≤Oε(q_n^(1/2+ε)) or q_n−P_n≤Oε(q_n^(1/2+ε)), for every ε>0. It is not necessary to transfer the ceiling to the weight g′ of 7035.

For the inverse enclosure, Q_n=Σ_{k≤n}log q_k, M=⌊C(x)⌋, N=N(x), with empty prefixes zero. The functions A and B of 7043 satisfy A=max_n(n log x−P_n), with maximum at N, and B_dis=max_n(n log x−Q_n), with maximum at M. Hence D_N≤B_dis−A≤D_M, evaluating each maximum at the index of the other. Moreover 0≤B−B_dis=∫₂ˣ {C(t)}dt/t≤log(x/2). Thus a ceiling for D gives the same ceiling for I=B−A and likewise with the opposite sign, since q_M and q_N are comparable with x for large x. Under RH one has |I(x)|≪ε x^(1/2+ε) by the classical bound for N−C, and the direct enclosure of 7043 returns both ceilings.

For the necessity of RH given a single ceiling, the Mellin transform ∫₂^∞ I(x)x^(−s−1)dx is −(Σ_{p>2}p^(−s)−∫₂^∞ t^(−s)dt/log t)/s² initially in Re s>1 (two integrations). By 6923 it is regular on the real axis >1/2 and branched at each exterior zero. Landau applied to the positive majorant Cε x^(1/2+ε) minus the controlled side excludes any zero of abscissa >1/2+ε. The O(log x) cost of discretizing ranks is admissible for both ceilings. Compared with 213-127-A, here the logarithm of the primorial is confronted with the continuous position of its own rank and the ceiling admits every ε. That arithmetic ceiling has not been proved.

### One-sided ceiling at pairs of primes of the same rank cell and dyadic anchors

For the upper side of 7053 it suffices to check two sets. First, the ranks n=2^j. Second, the n whose two consecutive primes satisfy
    q_n≤p_n<p_{n+1}≤q_{n+1}.
On this second set the ceiling P_n−p_n≪ε p_n^(1/2+ε) suffices, without inverting C to evaluate the balance. The selection condition can also be written C(p_n)≥n and C(p_{n+1})≤n+1. The gap of such a pair costs at most log q_{n+1}, since q′(s)=log q(s).

Indeed use D_n of 7043, which differs from P_n−q_n by O(log q_n). In each block of ranks [2^j,2^(j+1)] take a maximum. If it is interior, D_n−D_{n−1}=log(p_n/q_n)≥0 and D_{n+1}−D_n≤0, exactly the displayed condition. Moreover |q_n−p_n|≤q_{n+1}−q_n≤log q_{n+1}. If it is an endpoint, it is an anchor. By PNT the q_n of the block are uniformly comparable; a ceiling of the maxima transfers to all ranks and 7053 concludes. Necessity comes from the same criterion and from the distance ≤log q_{n+1} in the pairs. It is not assumed that the crossings occur with a determined frequency, which is the reason for keeping the anchors. Even for such pairs a bound for P_n−p_n is required, which includes the history before the short gap.

### One favourable rank per block between fourth powers suffices

Let R_n=P_n−q_n as in 7053. RH is equivalent to
    for every ε>0, min_{j^4≤n<(j+1)^4} R_n ≪_ε q_{j^4}^(1/2+ε).
Only an upper ceiling is required. The ceiling on the average of the block, or on the ranks n=j⁴ alone, serves as well. These are blocks in the INDEX of the true primes; the proof uses no hypothesis on gaps between primes.

Indeed, take a minimizer in each block. Between two consecutive minimizers a,b one has b−a≪a^(3/4) for large a. The increments log p_n of P_n are increasing, so P_n lies below the chord between P_a and P_b. On the other hand q(s)=C^{-1}(s) satisfies q″(s)=log q(s)/q(s)≪1/a for a≤s≤b, since q(s)~s log s. By interpolation, with L the linear interpolant between endpoints, 0≤Lq(n)−q_n≤(n−a)(b−n) sup q″/2. One gets
    R_n ≤ max(R_a,R_b)+O((b−a)²/a) ≤ max(R_a,R_b)+O(√a).
Since q_b~q_a~q_n, the ceiling of the minimizers gives that of 7053 at all integers. Conversely RH gives the ceiling at every rank. The average implies the minimum and RH controls the average. Unlike 213-127-A, where θ(m⁴)−m⁴ was averaged in the physical variable, here even a single favourable sample at an unknown place suffices per block, for the primorial of rank n against C^{-1}(n). It remains to prove that each block contains such a sample.

### The lower side of the primorial admits threshold zero

RH is equivalent to P_n≥q_n for all sufficiently large n. More precisely, under RH,
    (2−c₀−o(1))√q_n/log q_n ≤ P_n−q_n ≤ (2+c₀+o(1))√q_n/log q_n,
where c₀=2+γ_E−log(4π)<0.047. The converse is the lower ceiling of 7053. The band is conditional.

Detail of the direct direction. Let θ_o(t)=Σ_{2<p≤t}log p and J(x)=∫₂ˣ(t−θ_o(t))dt/t. The integrated explicit formula for ψ gives, under RH,
    J(x)=2√x+Σ_ρ x^ρ/ρ²+o(√x).
Indeed the integral of t−ψ(t) contributes the indicated series and O(log x) from the constant and trivial terms (one can first integrate the truncated formula in the distributional sense; the integrated series converges normally on compacts). The squares in ψ−θ_o contribute ∫₂ˣ θ(√t)dt/t~2√x by PNT; exponents ≥3 and the omitted prime cost O(x^(1/3)log²x+log x). Under RH Σ|ρ|^(−2)=Σ1/[ρ(1−ρ)]=c₀ by the product of ξ and its symmetry at 0 and 1. Hence J=O(√x).

For I of 7043, Abel gives C(x)−N(x)=(x−θ_o(x))/log x+∫₂ˣ (t−θ_o(t))dt/(t log²t)+O(1). The last integral is O(√x/log²x) by integrating dJ/log²t by parts. Now integrating (C−N)/t gives I(x)=J(x)/log x+O(√x/log²x), again by parts. The enclosure of 7043 and D_n+δ_n=P_n−q_n+2 transfer the two bounds, since p_n/q_n→1. Thus the target on this side is purely ordinal: prove that the logarithm of the product of the first n odd primes eventually exceeds the continuous mass point n. The sign has not been established unconditionally.

### A single primorial exceeding the threshold per block of ranks suffices

RH is equivalent to the existence, for each sufficiently large j, of n∈[j⁴,(j+1)⁴) with P_n≥q_n. Requiring it only at the predetermined ranks j⁴ also serves. Necessity follows from 7079. For sufficiency one needs to control how far the primorial can sink between two samples; the upper chord of 7069 alone does not serve.

Let a be a sample and b the next one, with h=b−a≤K a^(3/4) by the geometry of the blocks. The PNT in short intervals used in 238 and 2420 gives p_b−p_a≪a^(3/4)log a uniformly, even if h is small: start at x=p_a~a log a and count in length Y=4K a^(3/4)log a. Since Y is above x^(7/12+δ) with fixed margin, the count is (1+o(1))Y/log x>h. Thus the increments log p_k of P between a and b range over an interval of length O(a^(−1/4)). If L interpolates at a,b, its slope for P is the mean of those increments. Summing slope differences, LP(n)−P_n≤h O(a^(−1/4))≪√a uniformly. Convexity of q gives Lq≥q, so that P_n−q_n≥L(P−q)(n)−O(√a)≥−O(√a). The lower criterion of 7053 concludes RH, even though this direct step allows a deficit between samples. The same proof accepts as hypothesis that in each block the average of P_n−q_n be nonnegative. The short intervals only control the increments within the block; the sign of at least one prefix per block remains pending.

### Unconditional runs of entirely favourable blocks

For every integer k there are, arbitrarily far out, k consecutive blocks of fourth powers of rank in which EACH primorial satisfies R_n=P_n−q_n>0. If there is a zero of abscissa β>1/2, there are also runs of both signs: for each 3/4<η<(1+β)/2, intervals of length ≫n^η occur at ranks comparable with n→∞ that are entirely positive, and others entirely negative.

Under RH the first statement follows from 7079. In the presence of the zero choose 2η−1<σ<β. There are excursions of I(x) of both signs beyond ±x^σ arbitrarily far out: if there were an eventual ceiling for one of the sides, the Landau argument of 7053 applied with discount σ would exclude the zero. By the inverse enclosure of 7053 and the error O(log x), they transfer to R_m of magnitude ≫m^σ in both signs, since both indices of the enclosure are asymptotic to x/log x.

Take h=⌊m^η⌋. If a positive excursion has a point of balance ≤0 in each of [m−h,m] and [m,m+h], the chord between those two points gives R_m≤O(h²/m) by convexity of P and the bound on q″ of 7069. Contradiction, since 2η−1<σ. For the negative excursion, two points of balance ≥0 in those intervals would give R_m≥−O(h²/m): on all of [m−h,m+h] the range of log p_i costs O(h/m) by the same short count of 7091 in length K h log m, admissible because η>3/4. Hence on at least one of the two sides the strict sign is kept at all ranks. Each stretch contains ≫m^(η−3/4) complete blocks. This guarantees repeated existence of positive runs without resolving whether all sufficiently late blocks contain a favourable rank.

### Sum over odd integers of fixed rank with uniform error relative to the primorial

Define s_n=q_n^(1/4) log q_n and Z_n(s)=Σ m^(−s), summing over odd squarefree m with exactly n prime factors. RH is equivalent to Z_n(s_n)≤exp(−s_n q_n) eventually. Here the whole multiplicity of products alternative to the minimum is controlled: without RH,
    0≤P_n+s_n^(−1)log Z_n(s_n) ≪ √q_n/(log q_n)².
The cross-check with phase 104 is the partition function; here the configurations are ordinary integers of fixed rank and the quantitative estimate compares their sum with the real primorial.

Proof. For x=p_n and s=s_n, each configuration is obtained by removing primes ≤x from the primorial and inserting as many primes >x (always odd). Its weight relative to the minimum is the product of (p/x)^s over those removed and (x/p)^s over those inserted. Relaxing the equality of cardinalities only increases the sum of relative weights. Taking logarithms and using log(1+v)≤v leaves a ceiling Σ_{3≤p≤x}(p/x)^s+Σ_{p>x}(x/p)^s. Even summing over all integers the two tails cost in total ≤1+x/(s+1)+x/(s−1), by monotone integral comparison. The minimal configuration contributes 1 to the relative weight. Divide by s and use x~q_n. Under RH the positive gap of 7079 dominates that error; in the other direction the minimal summand exp(−sP_n) suffices to pass from the proposed ceiling to P_n≥q_n. It remains to bound the arithmetic sum from above with the exact threshold. The tail estimate controls the loss from replacing the minimum, not the size of the minimum itself.

### Exact asymptotic cost of smoothing the primorial at the critical scale

For s=c q_n^(1/4), c>0 fixed, unconditionally
    P_n+log Z_n(s)/s ~ [π²/(6c²)] √q_n/log q_n.
In particular already with c=1 the equivalence of 7105 persists, since π²/6<2−c₀ in 7079. On the contrary, for c with π²/(6c²)>2+c₀ that ceiling of Z_n eventually fails even under RH.

Proof. Take x=p_n and M=x/(s log x)→∞. In the coordinate t=s|log(p/x)|, each fixed band [a,b) on each side of x has (b−a+o(1))M primes by the short PNT of 238, since its physical length is asymptotic to (b−a)x/s. Relaxing cardinalities as in 7105, the logarithm of the relative weight normalized by M is bounded above in the limit by 2∫₀^∞ log(1+exp(−t))dt. To justify tails: on [x/2,2x] each unit band has O(M) primes uniformly by the same short PNT, and the summand costs ≤exp(−t); outside that octave the integral comparison over integers costs O(x 2^(−s)+1), negligible compared with M.

For the floor, first subdivide [0,T) into a fixed number of bands. In each [a,b) keep on each side the smaller of the two counts, m=(b−a+o(1))M. Removing and inserting exactly k primes in the same band costs a relative factor ≥exp(−2bk). Its options sum to ≥(1+exp(−b))^(2m)/(m+1) by Cauchy–Schwarz applied to binom(m,k) exp(−bk). Multiplying bands produces valid and distinct configurations of rank n; the logarithmic cost of the denominators is o(M). Refining the partition and then T→∞ matches the ceiling. The double integral is π²/6 by the alternating series of 1/k². Finally M/s~√q_n/(c² log q_n). This evaluates the contributions of the substitutions; the base value P_n−q_n remains pending unconditionally.

### Count of integers below the threshold and exact cost of the substitutions

Put q=q_n, v=q^(3/4)/log q, b=√q/log q and A=π²/6. For fixed λ>0, let H_n(λ) be the number of odd squarefree integers with n primes and log m≤P_n+λ b. Unconditionally
    log H_n(λ)/v → 2√(Aλ).
In particular, if B_n counts those integers with log m<q_n, then RH is equivalent to the single ceiling log(1+B_n)=O(v). Under RH B_n=0 eventually, but the proposed ceiling allows exponentially many exceptions at each rank.

Indeed for E_m=(log m−P_n)/b≥0, (7113) gives v^(−1)log Σ exp(−cv E_m)→A/c for every c>0. Majorizing H_n by exp(cvλ) times that sum, with c=√(A/λ), gives the ceiling. For the floor take 0<d<λ and c=√(A/d). Under the normalized weights exp(−cv E_m), the probability of |E_m−d|>δ is exponentially small in v for each δ>0: for the upper tail apply Markov with parameter hv, 0<h<c, whose upper limit exponent is A/(c−h)−A/c−h(d+δ)<0 for small h. For the lower one obtains A/(c+h)−A/c+h(d−δ)<0. On the band [d−δ,d+δ]⊂[0,λ] the unnormalized mass is therefore exp((A/c+o(1))v), and each term weighs at most exp(−cv(d−δ)). Letting δ→0 and d→λ gives the floor.

If RH fails, by the contrapositive of 7053 there are ε>0 and a sequence with (q_n−P_n)/q_n^(1/2+ε) unbounded and tending to infinity after extraction. Along it B_n≥H_n(λ) eventually for each fixed λ. The formula implies limsup log(1+B_n)/v=∞. Unique factorization alone identifies the candidates and quantifies their multiplicity; it has not given the upper bound for B_n at the absolute level q_n.

### The local statistics of substitutions do not even determine the side of the threshold

Countermodels of formal sizes, with no claim to be ordinary primes. Use the same generators labelled by the odd primes and the same free factorization in both models. Give them log-sizes log p ± f(log p). Choose increasing prime cuts x_j with x_{j+1}>x_j³ and put f(log p)=δ_j φ(p/x_j) on [x_j/8,x_j/4], zero outside those bands. Here δ_j=exp(−(log x_j)^(1/3)) and φ≥0 is a fixed smooth nonzero function with compact support in (1/8,1/4). The sizes preserve order when starting sufficiently far out, since the derivative of the log-size with respect to log p is 1+O(δ_j). On [x_j/2,2x_j] the generators and their sizes are exactly the genuine primes in both models; the cut x_j keeps its same rank n.

At that rank the formal primorial has log-size P_n±S_j, with S_j~δ_j (x_j/log x_j)∫φ(t)dt by PNT, and the previous bands contribute O(x_j^(1/3)log x_j). By the PNT with remainder of 7018, P_n−q_n=O(x_j exp(−c√log x_j)) for some c>0 (apply the remainder to θ and to the count and invert C). Thus the two differences against the SAME q_n have opposite signs and moduli ≫δ_j x_j/log x_j. For every fixed A the modified global counts still differ from C(x) by O_A(x/log^A x): in the bands the change of count only uses an interval of length O(δ_j x_j+1), and outside their images and preimages the count coincides.

In the model of positive sign the strict count B_n is zero. In the negative one, for each fixed λ the configurations of fixed bands in t=s|log(p/x_j)| used in the floor of 7113 are available with no change in relative cost. More directly, pair k disjoint pairs on both sides of the cut in bands 0<t<L with s=q_n^(1/4), k~L x_j/(s log x_j) for fixed L. Exchanging any subset costs in log-size ≤2Lk/s=O_L(√q_n/log q_n), far below the deficit. This yields 2^k configurations below the threshold. Since L is arbitrary, log(1+B_n)/(q_n^(3/4)/log q_n) tends to infinity at those cuts. The multiplicity is counted in the labelled free monoid. The contrast rules out deducing the ceiling using only the local substitutions, the rank, the formal factorization and global errors smaller than any inverse power of the logarithm. The joint additive and multiplicative structure of the ordinary integers remains available.

### A fixed number of macroscopic factorials does not determine the logarithmic prefix

Fix any positive proportions a₁,…,a_k. At arbitrarily large prime cuts x, even imposing exactly the k valuation identities of (⌊a_i x⌋)! on logarithmic weights assigned to the prime labels, the prefix up to x admits a perturbation of both signs of size ≫x exp(−(log x)^(1/3))/log x. The weights outside two bands strictly below x/2 remain log p. It is a sufficiency test of linear data per cut; it is not a model satisfying the identities at all integers.

Choose t>4 such that 0<{a_i t}<1/2 for all i. For this take, by simultaneous approximation, arbitrarily large integers T with dist(a_i T,Z) arbitrarily small (including the periodic case), and add a fixed small positive quantity h with 0<a_i h<1/4. In small fixed neighbourhoods of p/x=1/t and 1/(2t) the valuation rows are constant, respectively l_i=⌊a_i t⌋ and 2l_i, since p²>a_i x for large x. In each neighbourhood choose a fixed smooth nonnegative bump, not identically zero, in p/x; write U,V for the respective sums of the bumps over primes, both asymptotic to positive constants times x/log x. Add to the log-size the first bump multiplied by 2δV/U and subtract the second multiplied by δ, with δ=exp(−(log x)^(1/3)). Each factorial row changes by 2δV l_i−2δV l_i=0 exactly. The prefix changes by δV, and on reversing both signs it changes by −δV. The derivatives of the perturbation in log p cost O(δ), so order is preserved. As in 7133 the shift dominates |P_n−q_n| at the rank of x. The valuations used are those of the genuine integers at the labels p; only non-identification from those k rows and the local data has been proved. Cross-check: 213-128 treats the resolution of a ladder of averages; here the null test uses only two bands and works for every fixed list of real proportions.

### Upper rank via a quotient of divisor counts in the lcm

The dyadic lcm already appears in 2808; the additional operation here also recovers the approximate rank, with error on the necessary side. For integer x≥3 take N_j=⌊x/2^j⌋ down to N_j=1, A_j=N_j!/(⌊N_j/2⌋!)² and L=lcm_j A_j. Let τ be the number of divisors and define r=log(τ(L²)/τ(L))/log(3/2). Then the criterion C(log L)≥r−2√x/log x eventually for all integers x is equivalent to RH. C is the integral from 2 of 1/log t.

Indeed each prime p≤x has a level with N_j≥p>N_{j+1}; there it divides A_j. No larger prime divides L. For each power p^k the difference of floors in v_p(A_j) is 0 or 1 (⌊⌊N_j/2⌋/p^k⌋=⌊N_j/(2p^k)⌋). Thus v_p(L)≤⌊log x/log p⌋, and log L=θ(x)+O(√x) by Chebyshev on the higher powers. For exponent e≥1 the factor of τ(L²)/τ(L) is (2e+1)/(e+1), increasing from 3/2 to 2. Indeed 0≤r−π(x)≤(log 2/log(3/2)−1)π(√x)<1.5√x/log x eventually by PNT. Under RH log L≥θ(x) and by 7079 C(θ(x))≥π(x) eventually (the margin √x/log x in the physical coordinate absorbs adding one rank). Conversely the tolerance implies for x=p_n that θ(x)≥q_n−O(√x) by the mean value theorem and log L−θ(x)=O(√x); 7053 concludes. The zero-tolerance criterion for the upper rank has not been established here.

### Repetitions allow removing the explicit tolerance of the criterion

Let κ=log(10/9)/log(3/2)<0.26. With L and r as above one has unconditionally
    C(log L)−r ≥ C(θ(x))−π(x)−O(x^κ/log x).
Consequently RH is equivalent to C(log L)≥r for every sufficiently large integer x. The same quotient of divisors is kept without adjusting its normalization.

Indeed h(e)=log((2e+1)/(e+1))/log(3/2) is increasing and concave in e≥1 (its derivative is 1/[(2e+1)(e+1)log(3/2)]). Hence h(e)−1≤κ(e−1), with κ=h(2)−h(1). Moreover h(e)−1<1. Let Y=log L~x. The increment C(Y)−C(θ) is at least (Y−θ)/log Y, and Y−θ=Σ(e_p−1)log p. For p≥Y^κ this contribution per prime fully pays for h(e_p)−1. For the others the deficit per prime is smaller than 1 and their number is O(x^κ/log x). This proves the comparison. Under RH the lower bound of 7079 implies C(θ(x))−π(x)≫√x/log²x: at the prime cuts by the mean value theorem, and between primes both functions on the left-hand side remain constant with p_previous~x. This margin dominates the loss x^κ/log x. Conversely the inequality without tolerance implies that of 7147. The sign without RH remains unproved.

### Maximal envelope of the divisor quotient over ALL integers

Let K be the largest rank with the primorial of ALL the first K primes ≤exp Y, and z the next prime, so z~Y. Write r(m)=log(τ(m²)/τ(m))/log(3/2). Unconditionally, with κ from 7153,
    max_{log m≤Y} r(m) = K + (1+o(1)) z^κ/(κ log²z).
Hence RH is equivalent to C(log m)≥r(m) for every sufficiently large integer m, and it suffices to check the successive strict records of r. The computed sub-root term describes the optimal benefit of the repetitions.

Proof. Value each unit of logarithmic cost at 1/log z. With h(0)=0, h from 7153, the first copy of p adds net benefit 1−log p/log z, positive precisely for p<z. Summing those positives and the budget Y/log z gives K+O(1) by the definition of z. The second copy adds κ−log p/log z, with total positive sum
    S=Σ_{p≤z^κ}(κ−log p/log z)=(1/log z)∫₂^{z^κ}π(t)dt/t ~ z^κ/(κ log²z).
For the following copies the increments are decreasing and at most κ₃=h(3)−h(2)<κ; even giving away the cost of the profitable copies, the gain per prime is bounded by h(∞), and only p≤z^κ₃ participate. This proves the ceiling K+S+o(S).

To realize it, duplicate each prime ≤z^κ in the initial primorial; finance the cost θ(z^κ) by removing the largest primes of the primorial until it is covered. d=θ(z^κ)/log z+o(S) primes are removed: by the short PNT of 238 there are ≫z^(3/4)/log z primes in [z−z^(3/4),z), each with logarithm log z+O(z^(−1/4)); the excess at the end costs ≤log z. This band suffices and stays separated from the duplicates. The realized increment is κπ(z^κ)−d=S+o(S). For the global criterion, under RH, at the primorial of rank K the margin C(log primorial)−K is ≫√Y/log²Y by 7079, absorbing the prime 2 and the shift by one rank; by monotonicity the margin persists up to the next primorial. It dominates S. The converse is obtained by evaluating at the primorials and applying 7053 (one rank or a factor 2 cost O(log Y) in physical coordinate). Between records r does not exceed its previous record while C grows. The sign bound at the records remains open.

### Unconditional ceiling for the number of integers violating the divisor criterion

For some d>0, the number E(Y) of integers with Y≤log m≤Y+1 and r(m)>C(log m) satisfies
    log(1+E(Y)) ≪ Y exp(−d√log Y).
In particular, the inequality already holds unconditionally except for at most exp(o(Y)) integers in a band containing ≍exp Y. The ceiling includes every multiplicity pattern.

Indeed take s=exp(d√log Y) and weight each m by W=m^(−s)Y^(s r(m)). Each exception weighs at least exp(s[C(Y)log Y−Y−1]). The total sum factors into local factors Σ_{e≥0}Y^(s h(e))p^(−se). For p≤Y^(4/5) the logarithm of each factor costs O(s log Y), since h is bounded and the geometric tail converges. For larger p, after the first copy the ratio between successive weights is ≤(Y^κ/p)^s by 7153. Against the factor 1+(Y/p)^s, the total logarithmic excess costs O(Σ_{p>Y^(4/5)}(Y^κ/p)^s)=o(1) by integral comparison. Thus the logarithm of the full product is at most
    s[π(Y)log Y−θ(Y)]+O(s Y^(4/5)log Y+1+Y/s).
Here the smoothing term of the first copies is obtained exactly as in 7105, using all integers for the two tails around Y (the cut point may be real). After dividing by the minimal weight, the remaining main part is s[Y−θ(Y)+(π(Y)−C(Y))log Y+1]. The PNT with exponential remainder of 7018 bounds it in modulus by O(sY exp(−c√log Y)), absorbing logarithms into c. Choosing 0<d<c/3 gives the announced ceiling. For primorials of exceptional rank, this estimate still allows many more integers than the level exp(O(Y^(3/4)/log Y)) of criterion 7123; it does not exclude an exceptional record.

### Exact exponent of the band count if an exterior zero exists

With E(Y) of 7173, if Θ=sup Reρ>1/2, then over integers Y→∞
    limsup log log(3+E(Y))/log Y = (1+Θ)/2.
Under RH the left-hand side is zero by 7161. Consequently a ceiling log(1+E(Y))≪ε Y^(3/4+ε) for every ε>0 suffices. The unconditional estimate of 7173 still has exponent one.

For the ceiling with Θ<1 fix Θ<α<1. The truncated explicit formula as in 7027 gives θ(Y)−Y and π(Y)−C(Y) of order O(Y^α), absorbing logarithms with an intermediate exponent. Repeat 7173 with s=Y^((1−α)/2) and small-prime cut Y^(1/3) instead of Y^(4/5): the same geometric excess is o(1) because 1/3>κ. The cost s Y^(1/3)log Y is smaller than Y^((1+α)/2); likewise, with a logarithmic loss, for the main term s Y^α and the smoothing Y/s. Let α↓Θ. For Θ=1 the trivial count suffices.

For the floor take any 1/2<σ<Θ and 3/4<η<(1+σ)/2. By 7053 and its Landau argument there exist arbitrarily large n with P_n<q_n−q_n^σ (apply to a zero with β>σ, using a strictly intermediate exponent to absorb logarithms in the passage between rank and scale). Put x=p_n~q_n, H=x^η. Each of the bands [x−H,x] and (x,x+H] contains ≫H/log x primes by the short PNT. Form k≈H/log x disjoint pairs with one factor of the odd primorial and one exterior. Swapping any subset keeps n factors and raises the total log-size by at most O(kH/x)=o(q_n^σ). Thus the 2^k distinct products satisfy log m<q_n and r(m)=n>C(log m). Their log-sizes are asymptotic to x, distributed over O(x) integer bands; some band contains at least 2^k/O(x) violators. This forces limsup ≥η. Take σ↑Θ and η↑(1+Θ)/2. The ceiling with exponent 3/4 independently of the zeros has not been obtained.

### Exact dual test: one explicit extremal integer per slope

For h of 7153, h(0)=0, let δ_j=h(j)−h(j−1), in particular δ₁=1, δ₂=κ. Define A(v)=Σ_{p≤v}log(v/p), zero for v<2. For each x>2 one has exactly
    max_m [r(m)log x−log m]=Σ_{j≥1} A(x^δ_j).
A maximizer is m_x=∏_{j≥1}∏_{p≤x^δ_j}p. The sum is finite: δ_j↓0. For each prime the successive copies are taken while their marginal benefit δ_j log x−log p is non-negative; since it is decreasing, the choice is compatible with a single exponent. This eliminates the budget constraints and the separate Euler-product estimates of 7173.

By strict concavity of C, RH is equivalent to the following inequality for all sufficiently large x:
    C(x)log x−x−A(x) ≥ Σ_{j≥2} A(x^δ_j).
Under RH, m_x→∞ and 7161 gives r(m_x)≤C(log m_x); the tangent line to C at x gives the ceiling shown. Conversely use x=log m for each sufficiently large m and the maximum identity. It even suffices to check r(m_x)≤C(log m_x) on the explicit family of maximizers. The left-hand side is exactly ∫₂ˣ(C(t)−π(t))dt/t−2, by differentiation and value at 2. The right-hand side is positive and asymptotic to x^κ/(κ log x): the first term A(x^κ) has that equivalent by PNT; the remaining ones cost O(x^δ₃ log x), since at each prime ≤x^δ₃ the sum of marginal benefits is bounded by h(∞)log x. Thus the cost of all repetitions is known from data up to x^κ. The signed integral on the left-hand side still requires information on the primes up to x. This duality makes precise that improving only the smoothing estimates in 7173 does not remove that obligation.

### A favourable scale in every interval [X,X^(2+ε)]

For every ε>0 and every sufficiently large X there exists x∈[X,X^(2+ε)] where the integrated deficit I(x)=∫₂ˣ(C(t)−π(t))dt/t exceeds x^(1/3). In particular it exceeds 2+R(x) of 7193. The statement is unconditional and locates a point starting from each X.

In the coordinate y=log x write i(y)=I(exp y) and J(y)=∫₂^exp(y)(t−θ(t))dt/t with all primes. One has J(y)=y i(y)−2∫_{log 2}^y i(t)dt+O(y+1): by parts, θ(exp y)=yπ(exp y)−∫π(exp t)dt, and the same identity for C has a constant endpoint term. Replacing i by f=i−exp(y/3) on the right-hand side changes it by O((1+y)exp(y/3)).

Let a=log X, D=√a, w(v)=h(exp v)>0 the theta weight of 6931 of Mellin ξ, truncated to |v|≤D in all the following averages. For a+D≤u≤(2+ε)a−D one has ∫w(v)J(u+v)dv ≥ c exp(u/2) uniformly. Indeed the integrated formula of 7079 before using RH has the same series Σ exp(ρy)/ρ² (without extracting exp(y/2)), absolutely convergent for each y>log 2 by Σ|ρ|^(−2)<∞. On integrating against the full weight each term vanishes by ξ(ρ)=0; replacing the truncated integral by the full one in that series costs o(1) uniformly by the two-sided Gaussian decay in exp(|v|) and exp(u)≤exp((2+ε)a). The squares term (2+o(1))exp(y/2) integrates uniformly to (2ξ(1/2)+o(1))exp(u/2); the others are of lower order as in 7079. Thus the average of (u+v)f(u+v)−2∫^{u+v} f also has that floor after reducing c.

If f≤0 on the whole interval, put N(u)=−∫w(v)f(u+v)dv≥0 and K(u)=−∫w(v)∫_{log 2}^{u+v} f(t)dt dv. Then K′=N and c exp(u/2)≤−(u−D)K′+2K. In particular K>0 and, for large a, K′≤4K/u, hence K(u)≤K(a+D)(u/(a+D))⁴≪ε exp(a+O(√a)) by the trivial initial bound |i(y)|≪exp(y). But at the endpoint u=(2+ε)a−D the inequality requires 2K≥c exp(u/2), a contradiction. The width is due to the initial cost exp(a+o(a)) compared with the square-root bias; the argument does not prove a favourable point in every fourth-power block nor an eventual sign.

### Reappearance before X² with the full leading coefficient of the squares

There exist d>0 and X₀ such that every X≥X₀ admits some x between X and X² exp(−d√log X) with
    I(x) > (2√x/log x)(1+3/log x).
This uses only the PNT with classical remainder and the unconditional theta average of 7203.

Write a=log X and take D=2log a. The tail of the reciprocal Gaussian of 6931, even multiplied by exp(2a+|v|), costs o(1) for |v|>D. In the average of J the squares term equals 2ξ(1/2)exp(u/2)+O(exp(u/2)/u²) uniformly for a+D≤u≤2a−D: in θ(√t) use the remainder O(√t exp(−c√log t)), split the physical integral into t≤exp(y/2) and its complement, and use the bound already given for cubes and higher powers. For b(y)=2exp(y/2)(1+3/y)/y, integration by parts gives
    y b(y)−2∫_{log 2}^y b(t)dt=2exp(y/2)−2exp(y/2)/y+O(exp(y/2)/y²).
Therefore on replacing i by f=i−b, the averaged force in 7203 is ≥c exp(u/2)/u for large a (the average of exp((u+v)/2)/(u+v) is comparable to exp(u/2)/u by positivity).

The PNT with remainder gives |i(y)|≪exp(y−c₁√y) on integrating (C−π)/t at physical scale; the same bound, reducing c₁, holds for the primitive of f. In the notation of 7203 one gets |K(a+D)|≪exp(a−c₂√a) since 2D=O(log a). If f≤0 on [a,2a−d√a], the differential inequality gives simultaneously K(u)≤16K(a+D) and 2K(u)≥c exp(u/2)/u up to u=2a−d√a−D. Choosing 0<d<c₂ and comparing exponents gives a contradiction. The sign in the intermediate interval between favourable points remains open.

### Mandatory mass above the full bias in every reappearance interval

Let Y=X² exp(−d√log X) and I be those of 7213, with d>0 sufficiently small. Unconditionally
    ∫_X^Y [I(x)−(2√x/log x)(1+3/log x)]₊ dx/x ≫ √Y/(log X)³.
This quantifies the necessary mass even allowing negative excursions inside the interval.

Use a,D,w,b,f of 7213, write A=a+D and B=log Y−D. For A≤u≤B put F₊(u)=∫w(v)f₊(u+v)dv and K(u)=∫w(v)∫_{log 2}^{u+v} f₋(t)dt dv, where f₋=max(−f,0). The weights are truncated at |v|≤D. K≥0, K′ is the average of f₋ and K(A)≪exp(a−c₂√a) by the initial absolute control. Separating the two signs in the force of 7213 and discarding the primitive of f₊, which enters with negative sign, one obtains
    c exp(u/2)/u ≤ (u+D)F₊(u)−(u−D)K′(u)+2K(u).
Divide by (u−D)³ and recognize the derivative of K/(u−D)². On integrating, K(B)≥0 gives
    ∫_A^B (u+D)F₊(u)/(u−D)³ du ≥ c∫_A^B exp(u/2)/(u(u−D)³)du − K(A)/(A−D)².
The integral over the last unit interval is ≫exp(B/2)/a⁴ and dominates the initial cost for d<c₂. The weight of F₊ is O(a^(−2)), hence ∫F₊≫exp(B/2)/a². By positivity and Fubini this mass is ≤||w||₁∫_a^{log Y} f₊(t)dt. Finally exp(B/2)=√Y/a. The result is an area bound with amplitude, not a bound on the proportion of favourable scales.

### If RH fails, the deficits persist on intervals of length x^η for every η<1

Let Θ=sup Reρ>1/2. For each 0<η<1 and 1/2<σ<Θ there exist arbitrarily large x such that I(t)<−x^σ for ALL t∈[x,x+x^η], and others with I(t)>x^σ on the whole interval. Hence, for any fixed η strictly less than 1, it suffices to prove that every sufficiently late [x,x+x^η] contains a point with I≥0. Likewise a rank with P_n≥q_n per block [j^k,(j+1)^k) suffices for any fixed integer k≥2, however large. The earlier bound of 7097 followed a concrete zero; here excursions near the supremum are used, which need not be attained.

Proof. Choose τ between max(σ,Θ+η−1) and Θ, and δ>0 such that Θ+δ+η−1<τ. Landau applied as in 7053 to I (using all primes only changes O(log x)) gives values I(x)>2x^τ and others I(x)<−2x^τ arbitrarily far out. On x≤t≤2x, |I′(t)|≤Oδ(x^(Θ+δ−1)) almost everywhere by the bound for π−C of 7027; for Θ=1 the trivial bound suffices. The variation over length x^η is o(x^τ), which proves both physical statements. Under RH 7079 gives the eventual floor of I.

For ranks apply the same to D_n of 7043. The excursions transfer through the inverse enclosure of 7053 with n~x/log x and using, if necessary, an exponent between τ and Θ. The increment D_n−D_{n−1}=log(p_n/q_n) costs Oδ(n^(Θ+δ−1)) by the inversion of C of 7027, and for Θ=1 p_n/q_n→1 suffices. D_n and P_n−q_n differ by O(log n). Negative and positive runs of length n^η result. For a given k choose η>1−1/k: each of those runs contains complete blocks [j^k,(j+1)^k), since their width is O_k(n^(1−1/k)). Under RH all sufficiently large ranks are favourable. The reappearance theorem of 7213 still has length larger than x, outside this criterion.

### Attained frontier: stretches of both signs in every sufficiently long multiplicative interval

If there exists some zero with Reρ=Θ=sup Reρ>1/2, there exist constants B>b>1 and c>0 such that in every sufficiently late [X,BX] there appear two subintervals [z,bz], one with I(t)≥c t^Θ/log t on all of it and another with I(t)≤−c t^Θ/log t on all of it. Multiple extremal pairs and approach to the frontier from the left without gap are allowed. Cross-check 213-244-A: there the small-nodes result is stated for another count with a single extremal pair.

By the integrated formula of 7203, with y=log x,
    exp(−Θy) J(y)=G(y)+o(1),   G(y)=Σ_{Reρ=Θ} exp(i Imρ y)/ρ²
counting multiplicities. Indeed the contribution of the squares is o(exp(Θy)), and for zeros strictly to the left dominated convergence holds by the finite sum of |ρ|^(−2). Thus J=O(exp(Θy)); the two Abel integrations of 7079, now with exponent Θ, give y exp(−Θy)i(y)=G(y)+o(1). Switching between all primes and the odd ones costs O(y) in i.

The series of G converges absolutely, is real and uniformly continuous. On intervals of length L→∞ its mean tends to zero and the mean of G² tends to V=Σ_γ|a_γ|²>0 uniformly in the origin of the interval; here a_γ groups the multiplicity at that frequency. It suffices to truncate uniformly and average the exponentials of the finite polynomial; there is no zero frequency in G. If M=Σ|a_γ|, then |G|≥G²/M, so that on every sufficiently long interval both parts G₊ and G₋ have mean ≥V/(4M). In particular both reach that threshold. Uniform continuity extends each sign with margin V/(8M) over a fixed positive length around the point found. Searching for the points in the interior part of the interval and returning to the physical variable gives B,b and c as claimed. If Θ>1/2 is not attained, the same dominated-convergence argument only gives y exp(−Θy)i(y)→0; the uniform multiplicative length does not follow in that case.

### Geometric sampling: synchronization of the negative sign in any base if Θ is attained

In the case of 7245, for any finite list b₁,…,b_k>1 there are integer exponents n with bounded gaps for which simultaneously
    I(b_j^n) ≤ −c b_j^(nΘ)/(n log b_j),   1≤j≤k.
One may take c=|G(0)|/2 independent of the bases; the bound on the gaps does depend on them. In particular an eventual sign only at 2^n would already exclude every attained exterior frontier.

Indeed G(0)<0: each conjugate pair contributes 2m(Θ²−γ²)/(Θ²+γ²)²<0 since the non-trivial zeros have |γ|>1. Truncate the absolute sum with error <|G(0)|/16. On the finite torus of the phases of all those frequencies and bases, the rotation with step (γ log b_j) returns to any neighbourhood of the origin with bounded gaps. To see this, the closure of its powers is a compact group; finitely many translates by powers cover that group with copies of the neighbourhood. No independence between phases is required. At sufficiently close returns all the G(n log b_j) differ from G(0) by less than |G(0)|/4. Apply the o(1) of 7245 to the fixed list.

Even without attaining Θ, RH is equivalent to the set of bases with I(b^n)≥0 eventually being non-meagre in (1,∞). If RH fails, fix a rational 1/2<σ<Θ. For each N the union over n≥N of {b:I(b^n)<−b^(nσ)} is open dense. In any interval of bases (l,r), choose x from an arbitrarily late strict negative excursion of 7237; the interval (log x/log r,log x/log l) contains an integer n≥N and b=x^(1/n) falls inside. Baire and intersection over N and the rational σ give detection of excursions up to Θ on a residual set of bases. Under RH all are eventually favourable by 7079. Residual is here a category property, with no claim about measure; it does not decide base 2 for an unattained exterior supremum.

### Obstruction to propagating from J in a window without the incoming count

There are continuous positive measures that satisfy the PNT with classical exponential remainder, with the same exact values of θ(t)=∫log v dN(v) and J(t)=∫₂ᵗ (v−θ(v))dv/v for ALL t≥X, but with opposite signs of I(t) on all of [X,X^(2−ε)] for each fixed ε in (0,1) and X sufficiently large. The measures depend on the cut X. This proves a limit of the information of θ,J restricted to the window and of the PNT remainder, without replacing the global identities of the primes.

Construction: take an increasing base count N₀(t)=C(t)−√t/log t for large t, spliced by an initial positive density. Then I₀~2√t/log t. With a=log X, place three smooth densities of mass one in the coordinate log v, translates of the same even compactly supported bump of variance v₀, at centres a−2,a−3,a−4, with disjoint supports below a. Form a signed measure Δ with masses λ_j such that its moments of log v of orders 0,1,2 are M,0,0, with M=X exp(−2√a)/a³. The moment matrix has columns (1,z_j,z_j²+v₀); by quadratic interpolation at the three centres separated by one there is a solution with |λ_j|≪Ma². In the logarithmic coordinate the base density on those bands is ≍X/a, so N₁=N₀+Δ (in the sense of measures) remains positive. At every point the accumulated change is O(Ma²) and after the cut it is M; both counts satisfy |N−C|≪t exp(−√log t) with constant uniform as X grows.

By Fubini, for t≥X the change in θ is the first moment, zero; the change in J is −∫log v log(t/v)dΔ, also zero. But the change in I is −∫log(t/v)dΔ=−M log t. This term dominates I₀ uniformly up to X^(2−ε), so I₁<0 on that whole window. Thus, improving the waiting time by a fixed exponent from the J signal alone in that window requires some additional control of the incoming mass. The countermodels do not satisfy the factorization of the integers.

### Optimal resolution of the count by two moments over integer primes of a band

For a=log X large there are two disjoint sets S,T of ordinary primes in [X exp(−5),X exp(−1)] with cardinality difference ≍X/a³, but differences of Σlog p and Σ(log p)² of sizes O(1) and O(a), respectively. Their products are squarefree integers and their quotient lies between absolute constants. The order X/a³ for the count discrepancy is optimal under those two tolerances.

Construction: in the variable v=log(p/X) take three disjoint very narrow intervals of fixed width around −4,−3,−2. Each contains ≍X/a primes by PNT. The three columns of empirical averages of (1,v,v²) form a matrix with uniformly bounded inverse, by proximity to a fixed Vandermonde. Choose an integer M=⌊cX/a³⌋ and solve for signed masses in the three columns with target vector (M,−aM,a²M). Each mass has modulus O(a²M) and the fixed c sufficiently small allows distributing it uniformly among the primes of its band with coefficients in [−1,1]. The uncentred moments of degrees 1 and 2 are then exactly zero.

Rounding: keep for each band the chosen sign and use selection variables in [0,1]. At a vertex of the polytope preserving the three centred moments there are at most three fractional variables (if there are more, a linear dependence allows moving in both directions). Round those variables preserving exactly the total signed mass M: in the negative ones replace the variable by its complement to turn the constraint into a sum with integer target and round up the required number. The centred errors of degrees 1 and 2 are O(1), since |v|≤5; the mass term is exact, hence the original errors are O(1), O(a). The selected ones of opposite sign give S,T.

For optimality sum (1−log p/a)² with the signs of any pair so controlled. Its total modulus costs O(X/a³) since there are O(X/a) primes in the band and each term costs O(1/a²). Expanding the square recovers the cardinality discrepancy at cost O(1/a). This delimits the use of integrality: exact equality of products does determine the set by unique factorization, but measuring the two moments with the stated precisions admits count differences much larger than √X. The construction does not alter the set of all primes nor decide the sign of their deficit.

### Exact recovery by rounding in bands of length c X^(2/3) log X

Let a=log X and H=c X^(2/3)a. On [X,X+H] the number of elements of ANY subset of primes is recovered exactly from its moments S_j=Σ(log p)^j, j=1,2, known with errors O(1) and O(a), respectively. It suffices to round 2S₁/a−S₂/a² to the nearest integer, for fixed sufficiently small c>0 and large X. Indeed the exact defect per prime is (1−log p/a)²≤(H/(Xa))². By the short PNT of 238 there are (1+o(1))H/a primes; the accumulated defect is ≤(1+o(1))c³. Choose c³<1/2. The measurement errors add up to O(1/a). It also holds on subintervals with the same initial endpoint and smaller length, by monotonicity of the majorant. Rounding per cell eliminates the accumulation of errors when reconstructing the prefix through a mesh of this step.

The scale is sharp in order for those tolerances. For H=C X^(2/3)a with fixed sufficiently large C, put w=H/X and v=log(p/X)/w. Choose three fixed small separated bands in 0<v<1/2. Each contains ≍H/a primes by the short PNT, with constants independent of C in the limit for fixed C. As in 7273, the centred system for obtaining signed mass 1 and zero original moments has right-hand side (1,−a/w,a²/w²). The necessary masses are O(a²/w²), smaller than the capacities of the bands on choosing C large, since their ratio to H/a is O(C^(−3)). The same rounding preserving the mass exactly incurs errors O(w) and O(aw+w²) in the two original moments; both are even o(1). Two subsets with counts differing by one are obtained. This proof indicates how much local data suffices to reconstruct the count lost in 7265; the global inequality on the sum of the real counts remains pending.

### Critical identification constant for two moments in the short band

In 7283 the strict transition is at c=16^(1/3). For each smaller c, the two moments with errors O(1), O(log X) determine a unique count for large X. For each larger c there exist two subsets with cardinality difference one and differences o(1) in BOTH moments. The equality case is not decided.

Proof. Let w=H/X, t_p=log(p/X)/w and B=a/w. The empirical measure of the t_p in the band converges, normalized by H/a, to the uniform measure on [0,1] by the short PNT applied to fixed subintervals. The maximal fractional mass D=Σu_p with |u_p|≤1 and Σu_p(log p)^j=0 for j=1,2 is, by finite linear duality, the minimum of Σ|Q(t_p)| over quadratics Q with Q(−B)=1 (every 1−Q is a combination of log p and its square). Then D→c³/16. In detail, writing P=B²Q, the condition is P(−B)=B². The minimum normalized by (H/a)/B²=c³ converges to the minimum of ∫₀¹|P| over monic quadratics. For the ceiling use any monic rescaled to satisfy the condition; for the floor the coefficients of the minimizing P are bounded by uniform equivalence of norms: if they diverged, divide by their largest coefficient and extract a nonzero limit with zero absolute integral, a contradiction. The condition forces the leading coefficient to tend to one. The optimal monic is P₀(t)=(t−1/4)(t−3/4): its sign has zero integrals against 1 and t, which certifies optimality, and ∫|P₀|=1/16.

For two sets compatible with the tolerances, use the explicit test Q=P₀/P₀(−B). The coefficients of log p and (log p)² of 1−Q are O(1/a), O(1/a²), respectively, by the substitution t=(log p−a)/w. Thus the integer mass discrepancy in modulus is ≤c³/16+o(1), and vanishes if c³<16. If c³>16, scale the fractional optimum to mass exactly 1 preserving the two zero moments. Fix the sign of each variable, pass to a vertex and round as in 7283 preserving that mass. In the centred degrees 1 and 2 the errors are O(1), so that in the original moments they are O(w), O(aw+w²)=o(1). This proves the transition without assuming RH. The result delimits the resolution of these local data, not the sign of I.

### A power saving in the frequency of deficient ranks would suffice

Fix any σ with 0≤σ≤1/2. Count in [N,2N) the ranks n with P_n−q_n<−n^σ and call the count Bσ(N). Then RH is equivalent to the existence of some δ>0 with Bσ(2^j)≪(2^j)^(1−δ) for all j. It holds even for σ=1/2, which allows ignoring ALL deficits smaller than √n. If RH fails the limsup exponent of log(1+Bσ(2^j))/log(2^j) is exactly 1. It is a condition on frequency without weighting by magnitude.

By 7237, given 0<η<1 and any τ between 1/2 and Θ, there exist arbitrarily far out rank intervals [m,m+m^η] with balance less than −m^τ at all their integers. For large m each satisfies the threshold −n^σ. Cutting by dyadic octaves, one of at most two octaves contains ≫m^η of these integers, and its lower endpoint N is comparable to m. This gives the floor of exponent 1 on taking η↑1. The trivial ceiling is N and under RH Bσ eventually becomes zero by 7079. The same statement holds for the physical measure of {x∈[N,2N):I(x)<−x^σ} by the physical stretch of 7237. The argument does not convert an o(1) density without rate into a power saving.

A possible mean estimate can be quantified: if in each octave one proves Σ_{N≤n<2N} ((q_n−P_n)₊)² ≪ N^(2−δ), then by Chebyshev B_(1/2)(N)≪N^(1−δ) and RH follows. More sharply Oε(N^(2+ε)) for every ε>0 suffices: in the presence of an exterior zero the previous stretches contribute ≫N^(η+2τ) for any τ<Θ larger than 1/2 and η arbitrarily close to 1, which violates the ceiling. This only requires the negative part of the prefixes. The mean arithmetic bound over the ordinary ranks remains unproved.

### Tail of the second moment of the unsmoothed deficit: height X^(1/4) suffices

In the physical octave X≤x≤2X, the part of I(x) coming from |γ|>X^(1/4) costs O(√X log^C X) even pointwise, with absolute C. The zeros below the cut and the arithmetic term of powers are kept; the statement is for the integral I without theta convolution. This leaves the high part within the budget Oε(X^(2+ε)) on integrating the square in dx.

Detail. Fix T=X^(1/4) over the whole octave. For J(log t) of 7203 the tail is Σ_{|γ|>T} t^ρ/ρ². Uniformly in 2≤t≤2X, its modulus is ≪√X log^C X. For β≤1/2 the total zero count suffices. For β>1/2 use the real-part bands of width 1/log X with left endpoint σ≥1/2 and of height H<|γ|≤2H, H=2^j T. By Ingham (230), the contribution is ≪X^σ H^(q(σ)−2)log^5(2H), q(σ)=3(1−σ)/(2−σ). The sum over j costs the same order in T since q≤1. At T=X^(1/4) the exponent is σ−1/2+q(σ)/4≤1/2 since q(σ)≤3(1−σ). Sum O(log X) bands. The same argument with 2X replaces t≤2X even in the initial part of the integral.

The Abel relation of 7079 acts on any component J₀ vanishing at log 2 through i₀(y)=J₀(y)/y+2y∫_{log 2}^y J₀(v)dv/v³ (inversion of y i₀−2∫i₀=J₀). The initial value of the tail, of modulus O(1), can be subtracted by assigning it to the elementary term. Hence the cost for I is at most another logarithmic power above that of J, uniform over the octave. The part of zeros β≤1/2 at any height already fits by convergence of Σ|ρ|^(−2); squares and other powers fit too. For the physical target of 7297 the one-sided majorization of the second moment of the contribution of the zeros with β>1/2 and |γ|≤X^(1/4) remains open. The cut grows with X and its finite verification alone does not resolve the sign.

### How many zeros remain outside the quadratic budget in an octave

In 7305 it suffices to retain Oε(X^(d+ε)) zeros counted with multiplicity, with d=max_{1/2≤s≤1} 6(1−s)(s−1/2)/(5−s)<0.089 (maximum at s=5−√18). The contribution of ALL the others to the deficit I has second moment Oε(X^(2+ε)) on [X,2X]. It is an upper bound on cardinality, with no information about the sign of the retained sum.

Separate as before β>1/2 into strips of width 1/log X with left endpoint σ. Put q=3(1−σ)/(2−σ) and Tσ=max(2,X^((σ−1/2)/(2−q/2))). Retain in each strip only |γ|≤Tσ. Ingham bounds their number by O(Tσ^q log^5(2Tσ)), giving d on summing strips.

To make the quadratic saving precise, at height H<|γ|≤2H and a logarithmic window [v,v+1]⊂[0,log(2X)+1] the block of Σ exp(ρy)/ρ² has L²(dy) norm ≪ X^σ H^(q/2−2)log^C(2H). On squaring, use a smooth positive majorant of the translated window with fixed support. By two integrations by parts the cross term is bounded by O(X^(2σ) H^(−4)/(1+|γ−γ′|²)), uniformly in the real parts; the factor X^(2/log X) is constant. Each row of the kernel sums to O(log(2H)) by the local count of zeros per unit interval, even with multiplicities; the number of rows is O(H^q log^5(2H)). This proves the stated norm. The heights H≥Tσ sum geometrically by Minkowski up to O(√X log^C X) in each window. Summing the strips, and using Cauchy–Schwarz window by window in the Abel integral of 7305, costs at most powers of log X. Passing from dy to dx in the octave costs O(X) in the quadratic moment. The zeros β≤1/2 and elementary terms already fit in 7305. It is not claimed that the quadratic error controls pointwise. The permitted number grows with X and even a single fixed exterior zero remains in the list at large scales.

### The tail also fits in the maximal second moment over cells of length X^(3/4)

Let E_X be the discarded part of I when using the set of zeros of 7313, keeping that set fixed over the octave. Divide [X,2X] into cells of lengths comparable to X^(3/4). Then
    Σ_cells |cell| sup_cell |E_X|² ≪ε X^(2+ε).
Hence the same budget holds when summing over the primes of the octave or over the quantiles q_n of 7043, even with adversarial choice of the location of the maximum in each cell. The retained zeros are the same Oε(X^(d+ε)) of 7313.

Detail. By 7305 the part |γ|>2X^(1/4) is already controlled uniformly (in each strip the cut of 7313 is ≤X^(1/4), since q(σ)≤3(1−σ)). In the intermediate blocks of J the derivative in y=log x multiplies each coefficient by ρ, and the row argument of 7313 gives for the intermediate tail L²(dy) norm ≪√X log^C X and for its derivative ≪X^(1/4)√X log^C X, in any window of length one up to log(2X). The first bound and Cauchy–Schwarz in Abel give for intermediate E the same two bounds, increasing C: differentiating J(y)/y+2y∫J(v)dv/v³ uses only J′, J and the integral of J. The elementary terms and β≤1/2 can be left in the uniformly O(√X log^C X) part without differentiating them.

For a logarithmic cell of length l≈X^(−1/4), l sup|f|²≤2∫|f|²+2l²∫|f′|², choosing a point below the quadratic mean and using Cauchy–Schwarz. Summing the cells and multiplying by O(X) gives the statement. In each cell the number of primes is ≤1+|cell|, and the q_n are separated by at least one unit for large n. In particular, to bound the deficits of P_n−q_n in 7297 the negative part of the retained sum at q_n suffices: by 7043, P_n−q_n+2≥I(q_n) in the odd convention (the difference of conventions only costs O(log X)). X≈N log N in ranks [N,2N], which fit in a bounded number of octaves. The bound of the retained part at those points remains open.

### Reconstruction from arithmetic means with error smaller than the squares bias

Let i(y)=I(exp y) with all primes. In log x, around the octave X≤x≤2X, take a uniform mesh of step h=X^(−1/4), extended by one cell at each end. Assign at each centre the integral mean of i over its cell, and interpolate linearly between centres. The interpolant A_X satisfies unconditionally
    sup_{X≤x≤2X}|I(x)−A_X(log x)| = o(√X/log X).
Here the data of contiguous cells are used, since a single mean does not recover the slope.

Indeed i′(y)=C(exp y)−π(exp y) except for jumps of the derivative. On any logarithmic block of length ≤3h the oscillation of i′ is o(Xh/log X), uniformly in its location in the enlarged octave. To see this subdivide a complete block of length 3h into K equal pieces with K fixed. Each complete piece has physical length comparable to X^(3/4)/K; the short PNT of 238 approximates its count by the increment of C with error o_K(Xh/log X), uniform in the location. Between arbitrary endpoints there remain at most two partial pieces, with both increments bounded by O(Xh/(K log X)) by monotonicity. First X→∞, then K→∞. Thus on the whole block i is at uniform distance o(Xh²/log X) from an affine function, by integration. The centred means and their interpolation reproduce affine functions exactly and have positive weights summing to one. This gives the announced error without hypotheses on zeros.

In particular, for octaves X=2^j, RH is equivalent to ALL these means (including the necessary adjacent ones) eventually exceeding √X/log X. Under RH this follows from the margin 2−c₀ of 7079, uniform also in the boundary cells; conversely the reconstruction gives an eventual positive sign and one applies 7053 with the enclosure of 7043 or directly its Landau argument for I. Compared with the averages criterion of 7091, the new datum is that the pointwise physical reconstruction costs little-o at the precise scale of the bias and does not require the position of the primes inside the cell once their means are given. That floor for the means has not been proved.

### A negative stretch in a polylogarithmic band forces a quantified earlier deficit

Fix L>4. If I(t)≤0 on ALL of [X,X(log X)^L], then there exists z∈[X,X(log X)^4] with
    −∫₂ᶻ I(t)dt/t ≫_L √X (log X)^(L/2−1).
It is the signed balance of the history, prior to the end of the band. The converse by contraposition allows excluding that run using data only up to X(log X)^4. It is not claimed that the antecedent occurs.

Proof. In 7203 use f=i without subtracting the bias and take a=log X, D=2log a, A=a+D, B=a+L log a−D. For A≤u≤B the truncated support of the average lies entirely in the negative band. By 7213 the force of J is ≥c exp(u/2), absorbing O(u) from the identity of primitives. With K the averaged negative signed primitive of 7203, one has K′≥0 and
    c exp(u/2)≤−(u−D)K′(u)+2K(u).
Thus K(B)≥c exp(B/2)/2 and K(B)≤K(A)((B−D)/(A−D))² on integrating the differential inequality. The ratio tends to one. Hence K(A)≫exp(B/2)=√X a^(L/2−1). The positivity of the weight and its uniformly bounded mass give at least one point z with the announced bound, since log z∈[a,a+2D]. For the negative historical deficit taken in absolute value it is not necessary to assume that I was non-positive before X. The signed balance allows discounting all earlier credit. The antecedent 103_63 rules out inferring this historical control from the mere positivity of a centred Selberg measure; that argument is not reopened.

### Arithmetic localization of the historical balance that a run requires

Let dν(t)=Σ_p δ_p−dt/log t on [2,∞), a=log z and U=√z exp(c√a) with fixed sufficiently small c>0. By Fubini,
    −∫₂ᶻ I(t)dt/t = (1/2)∫_[2,z] log²(z/t) dν(t).
The right-hand side can be restricted to U<t≤z−z^(5/6) with error o(√z/log z), unconditionally.

To remove [2,U], put E(t)=π(t)−C(t) and apply Abel. The upper endpoint costs O(a²|E(U)|), and the remaining integral is bounded by O(a∫₂ᵁ |E(t)|dt/t), with the lower value taken before the atom 2. By PNT with remainder |E(t)|≪t exp(−c₀√log t), both are O(a² U exp(−c₁√log U)) for c₁>0, splitting at √U if needed; choose c<c₁/3. For the upper band of length H=z^(5/6) the discrepancies accumulated from its lower endpoint are uniformly o(H/log z), by fixed subdivision and short PNT as in 7331. The quadratic weight is decreasing with variation O((H/z)²), hence the cost is o(H³/(z² log z))=o(√z/log z). The signed discrepancy at the upper edge is used.

By 7341, if I≤0 on [X,X(log X)^L], L>4, some z∈[X,X(log X)^4] has in that intermediate region a weighted prime EXCESS ≫_L √X(log X)^(L/2−1). Indeed the error is o(√X log X), smaller than the margin for L>4. This localizes which prime–integral comparison prior to the end of the run would have to fail. The corresponding ceiling in that region has not yet been obtained.

### Disjoint multiples of the large primes: exact inversion reintroduces a sign

Put W(v)=(log v)²/2 for v≥1 and zero for v<1. To express the weight of 7351 by summing the same size test over all multiples, the only function g, zero on v<1, with W(v)=Σ_{k≤v}g(v/k) is
    g(v)=Σ_{k≤v} μ(k)W(v/k).
Hence for any subset S of the primes of (U,z] one has exactly
    Σ_{p∈S} W(z/p)=Σ_{m≤z : there exists p∈S dividing m} g(z/m).
The equality uses that U>√z, and each integer is counted only once. Unlike 213-379-A, here one requires recovering the prescribed quadratic weight with a single size test and without weighting by cofactor.

Obstruction: for EVERY 0<σ<1/2 and every C>0, g(v)>C v^σ and g(v)<−C v^σ arbitrarily far out. Indeed, in Re s>1 its Mellin transform is 1/(s³ζ(s)) by Möbius inversion and the transform of W. This function is regular on the positive real half-axis s>0, including 1, but has a pole at a zero on the critical line. An eventual ceiling C v^σ for either of the two signs would allow applying Landau to the fixed-sign difference with the ceiling. Regularity at every real >σ would force convergence in that half-plane and exclude that pole. Uniqueness follows from the same finite inversion for each v. Thus the genuine disjointness of the classes of multiples does not authorize replacing them by all integers via positivity of the test; for this weight the forced size test oscillates. Weights that also depend on the cofactor, or inequalities that do not require the exact identity, are not excluded.

### The harmonic cofactor gives a strictly positive exact test

With W(v)=log²(v)/2 for v≥1, zero before, put G(v)=Σ_{k≤v} μ(k)W(v/k)/k. Then G(v)>0 for ALL v>1 and W(v)=Σ_{k≤v}G(v/k)/k. For the set S of 7361 one obtains the sum over disjoint multiples with positive contributions G(z/m)/(m/p). The identity is finite inversion.

Elementary proof of the sign. If 1<v≤exp(3), the sum of the moduli with k=1 omitted is strictly less than ∫₁ᵛ W(v/t)dt/t=log³(v)/6≤W(v), by strict monotonicity (and trivial if v<2). For v≥exp(3) compare W(y) with L(y)=Σ_{n≤y}(log n)/n. For all y≥1, |L(y)−W(y)|≤1/e: by parts with f(t)=log(t)/t the error is −{y}f(y)+∫₁ʸ {t}f′(t)dt. The increasing variation of f is ≤1/e, and for y≥e its decreasing variation is 1/e−f(y), which also gives the floor. By Σ_{d|n}Λ(d)=log n, the harmonic inversion of L is Σ_{n≤v}Λ(n)/n. This is ≥log(⌊v⌋!)/v, using the identity of valuations of the factorial. Moreover Σ_{n≤v}log n ≥∫₁ᵛ log t dt−log v by monotonicity. With Σ_{k≤v}1/k≤1+log v one gets
    G(v) ≥ (1−1/e)log v−1−2/e >0   for log v≥3.
Here log v/v≤1/e was used. Thus the sign rests on the actual factorization of the integers and holds at all scales. The ceiling needed for the excess of 7351 still requires comparing this positive sum with the continuous integral to the prescribed precision; the positive identity alone does not give that comparison.

### Strict positivity of the harmonic kernel for the unintegrated deficit

Define g(v)=Σ_{k≤v} μ(k)log(v/k)/k and g(v)=0 for v<1. Then g(v)>0 for all v>1. In particular G of 7371 is strictly increasing and Σ_{k≤v}g(v/k)/k=log v for v≥1. This recovers the prime weight of I directly, even before the additional integration of 7351.

Proof: write H_⌊y⌋=log y+γ+r(y), with |r(y)|≤2/(3y) for y≥1. At integers n one has 1/[2(n+1)]≤H_n−log n−γ≤1/(2n) by summing from k=n the differences log(1+1/k)−1/(k+1): the integrand 1/t−1/(k+1) gives a floor 1/[2(k+1)²] after integrating, and the trapezoidal rule gives the telescoping ceiling. Between n and n+1 the product yr(y) decreases (derivative r−1<0), and its left limit at N=n+1 is ≥N/[2(N+1)]−1≥−2/3. The exact harmonic inversion of H_⌊y⌋ equals 1. If m(v)=Σ_{k≤v} μ(k)/k, the identity Σ μ(k)⌊v/k⌋=1 gives m(v)≤3/4+2/v since at most 3v/4+1 integers are not multiples of four. By the same count, Σ|μ(k)r(v/k)|/k≤(2/3)(3/4+1/v). Thus g(v)≥1−0.58(3/4+2/v)−(2/3)(3/4+1/v)>0 for v≥32.

For 1<v≤2, g=log v. On [2,32] it is linear in log v between integers and continuous at the nodes. Reproducible rational verification of the 31 endpoints: for t=n/k=2^e u, 1≤u<2, use ℓ(t)=eL(2)+L(u), where L(u)=2Σ_{j=0}^{15} ((u−1)/(u+1))^(2j+1)/(2j+1). The remainder of L is bounded by 2(1/3)^33/[33(1−1/9)]; for n≤32 the error in the signed sum is <10^(−10). For each n=2,…,32 it was checked with exact fractions that Σ μ(k)ℓ(n/k)/k−10^(−10)>2/3. Inversion and differentiation of G with respect to log v conclude. The positive test serves equally for the continuous part by integration, but the comparison between the selected multiples and the continuum still requires a signed bound.

### Exact cost of enlarging primes to sieve survivors near the root

Let R=√x, D=c x^(1/3)(log x)^(1/3), y=R−D with fixed c>0. In Σ_{p≤x} log(x/p) keep the primes ≤y and replace the larger ones by ALL integers 1<m≤x without a prime divisor ≤y. The unconditional excess is
    (8c³/3+o(1)) √x/log x.
It is an enlargement by inclusion also valid before regrouping the multiples with the harmonic cofactor of 7379; the cost is computed here on the original prime sum.

Indeed y³>x, hence the added composites are exactly pq≤x with y<p≤q. The two factors lie between R−D and R+D+O(D²/R). In coordinates u=(p−R)/D, v=(q−R)/D the prime measures normalized by D/log R tend weakly to Lebesgue on any fixed compact set, by the short PNT of 238, since D exceeds R^(7/12+δ) for some δ>0. The positive weight (R/D)[log(x/pq)]₊ converges uniformly to [−u−v]₊. On counting ordered pairs and dividing by two, the additional diagonal costs O(D²/(R log R)), negligible. Hence the excess is asymptotic to D³/(R log²R) times the constant (1/2)∫_{u,v≥−1}[−u−v]₊du dv=2/3. This gives the formula.
