By Fubini I(x)=∫₂ˣ log(x/t)dt/log t−Σ_{p≤x}log(x/p). If the enlarged sum is used, the resulting deficit is smaller than I. For 8c³/3<2−c₀ (7079), RH is equivalent to its eventual non-negativity: under RH the margin of the original deficit dominates the excess, and the converse follows from I≥0 eventually and 7053. For 8c³/3>2+c₀ the enlarged deficit is eventually negative under RH. The computation controls the loss from stopping the sieve before R, but does not prove the upper bound on the survivors.

### Sieve up to the cube root with lower subtraction of semiprimes by bands

Let y=x^(1/3). Sum log(x/m) over the primes ≤y and the integers 1<m≤x free of prime divisors ≤y. From this sum subtract the following correction, which only uses counts of primes and sums of their logarithms in O(x^(1/4) log³ x) bands up to x^(2/3). The result is a majorant of the true prime sum with excess O(√x/log³ x), unconditional and uniform.

The surplus composites are exactly semiprimes pq, p,q>y, including squares. Divide [log y,log(x/y)] into an even number of equal intervals of length h comparable to x^(−1/4)/log²x, with the centre at log√x. Use intervals open on the left and closed on the right. Compute the ORDERED sum over all pairs of bands whose joint upper endpoint does not exceed log x. On a complete rectangle the exact result is N_i N_j log x−S_i N_j−N_i S_j, where N_i counts primes and S_i sums log p. For each i the admissible j form a prefix, so the sum uses O(number of bands) operations once the data are known. Add the exact diagonal Σ_{y<p≤√x}log(x/p²), computable from the same prefixes, and divide everything by two. This counts a lower bound for the semiprimes without distinguishing or enumerating individual pairs.

In each row there are O(1) rectangles cut by log p+log q=log x. For ranges p≈P, q≈Q in such rectangles, PQ≍x, and there are O(Ph) and O(Qh) integers respectively since the smaller product times h tends to infinity. Each omitted weight costs ≤2h. The total cost is O(x h³ (log x)/h)=O(√x/log³x). Membership at an endpoint with product exactly x does not matter because its weight is zero. This version reaches the cubic threshold, against the almost-square-root one of 7387, by discounting the composites. The margin of 7079 implies that the eventual sign of the deficit with the new majorant is equivalent to RH. The error is proved without RH; the comparison of the sieved and corrected total with the integral is missing. Prime data in the bands up to x^(2/3) are still needed, besides the sieving by primes up to y.

### Unconditional floor for the central part of the quadratic semiprime error

Put R=√x, y=x^(1/3), dν=dπ−dt/log t restricted to (y,x/y], and E(t)=ν((y,t]). On expanding the ORDERED semiprime correction with the weight log(x/pq) against the continuous density, the exact quadratic term is
    Q=∫_y^(x/y) E(t) E(x/t) dt/t.
Indeed [log(x/pq)]₊ is the logarithmic length of [p,x/q] when it is non-empty; Fubini holds for the finite signed measures. For the unordered correction there is in addition the diagonal of 7397 and a factor 1/2.

For every fixed c>0 let H=c x^(1/3)(log x)^(1/3). The contribution to Q of R exp(−H/R)≤t≤R exp(H/R) has negative part, even before integrating, bounded in mass by o(√x/log x). Indeed, for those t the two positions t and x/t remain within a band of length O(H) around R, and E(t)−E(x/t) is the error on an interval between them. Uniformly its modulus is o(H/log R): apply the short PNT to a fixed subdivision of that band and bound the incomplete pieces by monotonicity, as in 7331. H≫R^(7/12+δ) for some δ>0 is admissible. For reals a,b one has (ab)₋≤(a−b)²/4. The adverse mass is thus o(H³/(R log²R))=o(√x/log x), whatever the size of the common error accumulated from y.

On the whole band, Q is exactly the difference between the integral of the square of (E(t)+E(x/t))/2 and that of the square of (E(t)−E(x/t))/2. For a floor of Q only imbalances between reciprocal scales are harmful; the central part of that second square already fits unconditionally in the margin. That imbalance has not been controlled up to the endpoints, and the expansion also contains two linear terms.

### Positive average of the quadratic error of all pairs, with finite closure of the endpoint

Freeze a band of factors (A,B], dν=dπ−dt/log t on it, without balancing any mass. Let Q(s)=∬[log(s/(pq))]₊dν(p)dν(q) be the ordered quadratic error, with factors restricted to that band for all s. For each λ>0:
    ∫_{A²}^{B²} Q(s)s^(−λ)ds/s + (B^(−2λ)/λ) Q(exp(1/λ) B²)
       = (∫ p^(−λ)dν(p))²/λ² ≥0.
It is a positive average of values of the error, with a single boundary sample. The formula includes all pairs far from the diagonal and uses the real prime count without corrections at its endpoints. In particular, if the interior average is negative, it forces a positive boundary Q of size at least λ B^(2λ) times the modulus of the interior average.

Proof. By Fubini, integrating up to infinity factors the moment: the integral for fixed p,q is (pq)^(−λ)/λ². Beyond B² every product is included, and Q(B² exp u)=Q(B²)+u M², with M=∫dν. The mean of u under density λ exp(−λu) is 1/λ, so the tail is evaluated exactly with the indicated sample. This closure introduces no coefficients of opposite signs. If one requires an exact formula with a single positive sample of the tail valid for any measure, the weight is fixed by the constant part and the position by the slope; these are independent when a point mass in (A,B] is varied. If M=0, Q vanishes from B² onwards and the interior average suffices. To apply this sign at the cut x of 7405 one must pass from the average over s to that cut and control the linear terms; in the original sieve the band of factors also changes with x.

### The moving cubic band also gives an exact sum of squares on integrating in log x

Let ν be any finite real signed measure with compact support in p>1, for example dπ−dp/log p restricted to a prime interval. In Q_m(x) use the measure restricted again to the MOVING band x^(1/3)<p≤x^(2/3), in both factors of the kernel [log(x/(pq))]₊. Then
    ∫₁^∞ Q_m(x) dx/x = 2∫_{0<l≤r≤2l} ν([exp l,exp r])² dl dr ≥0.
If the initial support is in [A,B], only A²≤x≤B³ intervenes. Thus the motion of both endpoints is preserved without an additional boundary sample.

Proof. Write u=log p, v=log q, s=log x. For u≤v there is a contribution when u+v≤s≤3u and s≥3v/2. If v≤2u, the last condition already follows from u+v≤s; if v>2u the band is empty. Hence the integral of the weight is (2u−v)₊²/2. Symmetrically it is half the square of the length of the overlap of [u,2u] and [v,2v]. That value is the area of the ordered pairs a≤b contained in both intervals. Fubini gives the square of the mass of the u with b/2≤u≤a, and the change a=r, b=2l has Jacobian 2 and effective domain l≤r≤2l. Open or closed endpoints are indistinguishable on integrating. The identity holds for measures with atoms and counts the ordered diagonal correctly.

The positivity obtained is for the full average with compact cutoff on the factors. On the subinterval of x where the moving band falls inside the chosen support it coincides with the original cubic contribution. Neither pointwise positivity, nor that of an arbitrary subinterval of the average, nor that of the two linear terms follows from the identity.

### Positivity for ALL tails of the average with moving band

For Q_m of 7424 and any X₀>1 one has ∫_{X₀}^∞ Q_m(x)dx/x≥0. It is valid for any compact real signed measure on the factors. Let S=log X₀, a=S/3. In variables u,v>a the kernel after integrating is
    K(u,v)=((2min(u,v)−max(u,v))₊²−(S−u−v)₊²)/2.
It is zero if either is below a. Indeed, the full triangle of 7424 loses exactly the stretch before S; if u,v>a and u+v<S one has 3min(u,v)>S. K vanishes continuously on reaching u=a or v=a.

The distributional mixed derivative in the open quadrant is 3u δ(v−u)−w(u,v), where
    w(u,v)=2·1_{max(u,v)<2min(u,v)}+1_{u+v<S}.
This follows by differentiating the truncated squares: the first contributes −2 off the diagonal in its cone and a diagonal jump 3u; the second contributes −1 in its triangle. The decisive identity is ∫_a^∞ w(u,v)dv=3u. For a<u<2a the weighted lengths add up to 2(2u−a)+(2a−u); for u≥2a they add up to 2(2u−u/2).

Let F(u) be the mass of ν on factors of logarithm ≥u. Integrating the mixed derivative from the two boundaries (where K=0) and applying Fubini gives exactly
    ∫_{X₀}^∞ Q_m(x)dx/x = (1/2)∫_a^∞∫_a^∞ w(u,v)(F(u)−F(v))²du dv.
Values at atoms do not affect these Lebesgue integrals. For support up to B, the tail ends at B³ and only factors above X₀^(1/3) intervene. Unlike the total average, the lower limit of the product can be chosen freely without a boundary sample. The difference of two positive tails does not yet give the sign of a two-sided window nor of the term at a cut; the linear terms remain open.

### No two-sided window of the moving band is positive for every balanced measure

For any 1<X₀<X₁, there is a signed measure of four atoms with zero mass and zero first logarithmic moment such that the integral of Q_m over [X₀,X₁] is strictly negative. In particular the positive tails of 7434 are not monotone in general.

Write S=log X₁, S₀=log X₀ and choose 0<d<min((S−S₀)/2,S/6). In logarithmic coordinates use u_j=S/2+j d with indices j=−1,0,2,3 and respective masses 1,−3,5,−3. Σm_j and Σj m_j vanish. The two high atoms do not interact with any atom in this window because even their smallest sum with u_(−1) exceeds S. In the active pairs the start of the contribution is u_i+u_j≥S−2d>S₀ and the end of the moving band 3min(u_i,u_j)>S. One has max(u_i,u_j)≤2min(u_i,u_j). Thus the integrated matrix for the first two atoms has diagonal 2d²,0 and cross entries d²/2. The value with masses 1,−3 is −d². The measure with only the first atom gives +2d²; to obtain the same positive sign with zero moments one can also compensate its mass and moment in the two high atoms, without changing the result.

More generally, any logarithmic degrees 0,…,k can be cancelled leaving the negative value intact: place k+1 distinct atoms above S−u_(−1) and solve the Vandermonde system for their masses. Hence adding a finite number of global moment balances does not suffice to deduce the ordering of the tails for arbitrary measures. None of these measures is identified with the real error dπ−dt/log t: the two-sided comparison for that measure and the full form remain open.

### Certified negative window for the quadratic term with the ordinary primes

For ALL x∈[24.99,25.01] the ordered term Q_m(x) of 7405 with dν=dπ−dt/log t satisfies −0.072<Q_m(x)<−0.055. In particular its integral with weight dx/x is also negative on that window, even for the real arithmetic measure. The fixed compact cutoff [2,9] on the factors can be imposed, since it contains all the moving bands considered. For that same cutoff, the two tails of 7434 are non-negative but the tail from 24.99 is strictly smaller than the tail from 25.01.

Reproducible certificate: verify_rough_pair_q25.py, mpmath.iv at 30 decimals and 512 cells. With a=log(x)/3 and t=exp(a(1+s)), 0≤s≤1, the reciprocal factor corresponds to 1−s and dt/t=a ds. The only primes in the set of bands are 3,5,7. The continuous mass from the lower endpoint has derivative exp(a(1+s))/(1+s) in s. In each cell that derivative is enclosed by intervals and lower and upper masses are accumulated; for the count both endpoints of the t interval are used. The product of the discrepancy intervals of cells j and 511−j encloses the integrand even when there is a jump. The final interval obtained is contained in [−0.07119,−0.05598]. This counterexample concerns the isolated quadratic term; it does not infer the sign of the linear terms, of the full deficit, or of any window T of Paper 46.

### The full semiprime correction jumps by more than a root at each prime cube

Let D₂(x) be the ORDERED sum with weight [log(x/(pq))]₊ in the moving band, minus the double integral with continuous densities. In 7405 it contains Q_m plus the two linear terms. The extension of the certificate verify_rough_pair_q25.py gives D₂∈[0.6294,0.7188] on [24.99,25.01] despite the negative Q_m, and D₂∈[−1.848,−1.745] on [27.01,27.03] despite positive Q_m. The linear term is integrated as 2∫ E(t) C_y(x/t)dt/t, with C_y the continuous mass from y=x^(1/3).

For every prime p, the jump (value at p³ minus left limit) is exactly
    −log p − 2Σ_{p<q≤p², q prime} log(p²/q) ∼ −p²/log p.
The continuous density has no jump. Among the atoms only the factor p at the lower endpoint is lost: (p,p) weighed log p, and the distinct pairs appear in both orders. The upper endpoint p² is composite and the weight vanishes on crossing any product boundary. The equivalent follows from Σ_{q≤p²}log(p²/q)=∫₂^(p²)π(t)dt/t~p²/log(p²) and the portion q≤p costs O(p). Hence a uniform TWO-SIDED bound Oε(x^(1/2+ε)) for D₂ alone is impossible for ε<1/6, even at arbitrarily large scales.

In the unordered count the corresponding jump is −log p−Σ_{p<q≤p²}log(p²/q). The survivor sum of 7397 loses those same composites on passing to the sieve by p; the prime p that leaves the survivors is incorporated into the sum of small primes. The multiples p³ born exactly at the threshold have weight zero. Thus the jumps cancel exactly in the arithmetic subtraction before the error of approximating by bands. To seek a joint uniform bound it matters to retain this cancellation. The jump identity does not exclude a one-sided bound for D₂ nor decide the global sign.

### The cubic jumps force a second moment above the root budget

For D₂ of 7462 and all sufficiently large X one has
    ∫_X^{2X} |D₂(x)|² dx ≫ X^(7/3)/(log X)³.
In fact |D₂|≫X^(2/3)/log X on a set of measure ≫X/log X in that octave.

Between two prime cubes, D₂ is Lipschitz on [X,2X] with constant O(1/log X). For the discrete sum its almost-everywhere derivative is the number of active pairs divided by x: those entering through pq=x enter with weight zero and the ceiling q≤x^(2/3) is already implicit in pq≤x with p>x^(1/3). By Chebyshev the number costs ≪(x/log x)Σ_{x^(1/3)<p≤x^(2/3)}1/p≪x/log x by parts. For the continuous integral the same ceiling holds for the derivative of the weight; on moving the lower boundary y=x^(1/3) there are in addition two terms of modulus
    (y/(3x log y)) ∫_y^{x/y} log(x/(yq))dq/log q ≪1/log²x.
The inequality uses ∫₀^H log(H/q)dq=H and log q≥log y. These bounds are uniform, and the variations on each stretch are absolutely continuous.

Take p³∈[5X/4,7X/4]. The jump has modulus ≥c X^(2/3)/log X by 7462. Hence one of the two one-sided limits has at least half that modulus. Towards that side the value keeps at least a quarter over length c′X^(2/3), choosing c′ small by the slope bound. The neighbourhoods of distinct cubes can be taken disjoint since even cubes of consecutive integers in that range are ≫X^(2/3) apart. By PNT there are ≫X^(1/3)/log X prime cubes in the interior interval. Summing the lengths and then the squares proves the statements. This rules out the separate two-sided estimate of D₂ in the very second moment of 7297; the proof does not determine which sign predominates and does not prevent a joint estimate with the survivors.

### Positive slope between cubes and large discrepancy on a fixed proportion

Between prime cubes D₂′(x)=(3+o(1))/log²x almost everywhere, uniformly for large x. To justify the precision, let y=x^(1/3), H=x/y, P and V the discrete and continuous ordered counts of p,q>y, pq≤x. Then P−V=O(x exp(−c√log x)) for some c>0. In the outer sum over p first replace the inner count π(x/p)−π(y) by C(x/p)−C(y). The PNT error is O((x/p+y)exp(−c√log x)), and the sum costs O(x exp(−c′√log x)) by Chebyshev and partial summation of reciprocals on [y,H]. Then replace the outer sum against primes by dC: by parts the inner function is zero at H, costs O(H) at y and has derivative of modulus ≤x/(p² log y). With |π(p)−C(p)|≪p exp(−c√log x) over the whole band the same budget results (reducing c). RH is not presupposed.

By 7472, D₂′=(P−V)/x+2y/(3x log y) ∫_y^H log(H/q)dq/log q. This integral is (1+o(1))H/log H by scaling q=Ht and dominated convergence (log H/log q≤2). Since log H=2log x/3 and log y=log x/3, the coefficient 3 remains. In particular each continuous stretch is strictly increasing. There are O(X^(1/3)/log X) stretches in [X,2X]. On each stretch, by the lower slope, the length with |D₂|≤b X^(2/3)/log X costs O(b X^(2/3)log X). Summing and fixing small b>0, the total measure of such points is ≤X/2. Hence the two-sided second moment satisfies the improved floor ≫X^(7/3)/log²X. This comparison controls the slope and the frequency of large moduli, but leaves free the initial level of the stretches, on which the one-sided sign depends.

### Difference between consecutive minima: the normalized gap minus one unit

For large consecutive primes p<q, put V(t)=∫_t^(t²) log(t²/u)du/log u and h=C(q)−C(p). With the values of D₂ just after the jumps,
    [D₂(q³)−D₂(p³)]/[2V(q)] = h−1 + O((1+h) exp(−c√log p))
for some absolute c>0. In particular if h≥1+ε the minimum rises and if h≤1−ε it falls for p sufficiently large, at fixed ε>0.

Indeed, changing x=t³ in the precise formula for D₂′ of 7484 gives, between p and q, 2V(t)dt/log t plus O(t² exp(−c₁√log t))dt. By 7462 the final jump is −2V(q)+O(q² exp(−c₂√log q)): replace dπ by dC on (q,q²] through Abel with log(q²/u), using the PNT with remainder at both endpoints, and include the diagonal term of size log q. To keep the error small even near h=1 the full V is used as normalization, instead of replacing it by its leading term only. The PNT with remainder also gives q−p≪p exp(−c₃√log p): over a length p exp(−c₃√log p) the expected increment exceeds the error if c₃ is taken smaller than the remainder constant. By differentiation V′(t)=−1+(2/t)∫_t^(t²)du/log u=O(t/log t), and V(t)~t²/(2log t). Thus V(t)/V(q)=1+O(exp(−c₄√log p)) uniformly over the gap. Integrating and dividing by 2V(q) concludes, absorbing logarithmic powers into c.

On summing the NORMALIZED differences between two extreme primes P and Q, the main term telescopes to C(Q)−C(P)−(π(Q)−π(P)). The sum of the absolute error bounds over an octave may cost O(P exp(−c′√log P)/log P), still above the root scale. The formula decides the direction of a step outside the narrow strip around h=1; it does not decide the level of a minimum nor the global sign.

### One atom of the earlier count cancels both the jumps and the drift of D₂

Put y=x^(1/3), E=π(y)−C(y), S=Σ_{y<p≤y²}log(y²/p). The function
    D̃₂(x)=D₂(x)+2 E S+E² log y
is continuous and locally absolutely continuous; for large x it satisfies |D̃₂′(x)|≪exp(−c√log x) almost everywhere for some c>0. In contrast, the drift of D₂ alone is ~3/log²x and its jumps are of order x^(2/3)/log x. The corrector only uses primes up to y².

Identity: in the ordered prime part add to the measure of primes >y a signed atom E at y, leaving the continuous part of D₂ intact. The two cross terms give 2ES and the diagonal E²log y. On crossing y=p, the moving atom gains exactly the unit of mass that the set of primes >y loses at the same point p. This gives continuity of the functional, also when the product endpoint crosses an integer, since the weight there is zero. On compact sets there are only finitely many breaks.

Between cubes, E′=−y′/log y (derivatives in x), S′=(2/(3x))(π(y²)−π(y)) almost everywhere. By 7484, D₂′=O(exp(−c₁√log x))+2y′V(y)/log y. On differentiating 2ES the part with E′ cancels that drift except for 2y′(V−S)/log y. By Abel and PNT on [y,y²], |V−S|≪y² exp(−c₂√log y) as in 7490, and |E|≪y exp(−c₂√log y). With y′=y/(3x), S′≪y²/x, y³=x, all remaining terms, including those of the derivative of E²log y, fit in the bound. In particular the variation of the residue over any stretch of length O(√x) is o(√x/log x) even if it crosses one or more cubes. The correction is signed and would also have to be transferred to the survivor side when estimating the original subtraction; the slope control does not bound the level of the residue.

### Exact level after cancelling the jumps: average of deficit increments and pure correlation

Write e(t)=π(t)−C(t) on the whole line, I′(t)=−e(t)/t and y=x^(1/3). For the D̃₂ of 7500 one has exactly
    D̃₂(x)=−2∫_y^(y²) [I(t)−I(y)] (x/t)/log(x/t) dt/t
            + ∫_y^(y²) e(t)e(x/t)dt/t.
The first term is an average with positive weight, multiplied by −2, of increments of the deficit at scales strictly smaller than x. If it is discounted with its real values, the boundary error e(y) no longer appears in the second as a constant subtracted from each factor.

Proof: the cumulative of the modified prime measure on [y,t] is π(t)−π(y)+e(y)=C(t)−C(y)+e(t). Fubini as in 7405 and expansion against the continuous cumulative give the quadratic term shown and the linear one 2∫[C(x/t)−C(y)] e(t)dt/t. Integrate the latter by parts against −d(I(t)−I(y)); both endpoint terms vanish. The identity needs neither RH nor density estimates.

To quantify the difference between the two terms, if |e(t)|≤A t^α on that whole band, 1/2≤α<1 fixed, the pure correlation costs ≤A² x^α log y and the linear one costs O_α(A x^((2+α)/3)/log x), by |I(t)−I(y)|≤(A/α)t^α and integration of t^(α−2) from y. The first exponent α is strictly smaller than (2+α)/3. More locally, the negative part of the pure correlation is majorized by
    (√x/2) ∫_y^(y²) [e(t)/√t−e(x/t)/√(x/t)]² dt/t,
also for the total negative balance, by symmetry and the square identity (the constant 1/4 already suffices for the pointwise negative mass). Thus the hypothesis of root-scale bounds at the smaller scales controls the quadratic term at root scale with logarithms, but leaves the linear one potentially at level x^(5/6); its cancellation in the joint functional is a distinct obligation. No floor of I has been assumed in the identity.

### The corrected discrepancy has a negative bias of order x^(5/6)/log²x under RH

Write x=y³, L=log y and D̃₂ as in 7500. Under RH one has
    −L² D̃₂(y³)/y^(5/2) = 2 + Σ_ρ y^(i Imρ)/[ρ(1−ρ)] + o(1).
The total coefficient of the oscillations in modulus is ≤c₀<0.047 of 7079. In particular the magnitude of the large term of 7510 persists even in the target scenario: requiring D̃₂ alone to be Oε(x^(1/2+ε)) for every ε is incompatible with RH. The sign here is a conditional consequence.

Indeed, 7079 gives I(t)=√t(2+Σ t^(i Imρ)/ρ²+o(1))/log t with absolutely convergent series. In the linear integral of 7510 change t=yv, 1≤v≤y. After normalizing by −L²/y^(5/2), the limit operator on a component t^ρ/log t of I is multiplication of y^(i Imρ) by ∫₁^∞ (v^ρ−1)dv/v²=ρ/(1−ρ). The logarithmic factors L/(L+log v) and 2L/(2L−log v) tend to one for fixed v, the second is ≤2; the majorant in dv is O((√v+1)/v²). This justifies the uniform o(1) even with y-dependent phases, by absolute and dominated convergence. For the squares term ρ=1/2 the multiplier is one. The pure correlation costs O(y^(3/2)log³ y) by the classical bound for e under RH and is negligible here.

If there is an attained exterior frontier 1/2<Θ<1, the same computation with 7245 gives
    −L² D̃₂(y³)/y^(2+Θ) = Σ_{Reρ=Θ} y^(i Imρ)/[ρ(1−ρ)] + o(1).
For the correlation use 7510 with α=Θ+δ and 3δ<2(1−Θ), via 7027. The majorant in v changes to (v^Θ+1)/v², integrable. The extremal series lacks a constant term and has positive quadratic mean, so in that case the corrected sign oscillates in both directions at arbitrarily large scales. For unattained Θ the oscillation is not deduced here from this profile.

### Arithmetic gate at the upward crossings of the sum of prime reciprocals

Let B₁=lim(Σ_{p≤t}1/p−log log t), m(t)=Σ_{p≤t}1/p−log log t−B₁. RH is equivalent to: for every sufficiently large prime with 0≤m(p)≤1/p one has π(p)≤C(p). The filter selects the primes at which the reciprocal error crosses zero upwards (including contacts). It is a criterion on prefix data. It does not claim that the selected inequality is proved.

The infinite-scale operator associated with the multiplier of 7523 is
    F(y)=y∫_y^∞ I(t)dt/t²−I(y)=C(y)−π(y)+y m(y).
The PNT with remainder guarantees convergence; two integrations by parts give first y∫_y^∞(C−π)dt/t² and then the prefix formula using B₁. F is continuous at each prime since the jumps cancel exactly; away from them F′=m, F″=−1/(y log y)<0. Thus every interior local minimum is attained at a prime and requires m(p−)≤0≤m(p).

Under RH use 7079 in the integral operator with t=yv. Domination by (√v+1)/v² gives F(y)log y/√y=2+Σ y^(i Imρ)/[ρ(1−ρ)]+o(1) as in 7523. On the filter 0≤p m(p)≤1 and therefore C(p)−π(p)>0 eventually.

Without RH, F has excursions of both signs above any multiple of y^σ for 1/2<σ<β, for each exterior zero β+iγ, without requiring β to be maximal. Indeed, if A(s)=∫₂^∞ I(y)y^(−s−1)dy and K=∫₂^∞ I(t)dt/t², the Mellin transform of F is [s A(s)−2^(1−s)K]/(1−s), initially for Re s>1 by Fubini. The apparent pole at 1 cancels by A(1)=K (absolute convergence by PNT). The continuation of 7053 preserves branching at the zero and real regularity >1/2. Apply Landau to the one-sided ceiling minus the function as in 7053, for each sign. Then there are negative minima of unbounded depth between arbitrarily late positive excursions. Each requires a prime of the filter, where π(p)≤C(p) would imply F(p)≥0. This gives the converse. The operator F is auxiliary: the identity does not replace the kernel of the discrepancy D̃₂ at finite cut by this operator without error.

### Unconditional two-gap restriction for witnesses by supporting lines

If there exists an exterior zero, there are arbitrarily large primes p with π(p)−C(p) arbitrarily large, m(p)≤1/p and, for their prime neighbours a<p<b,
    (p−a)/(2p log p)+(b−p)/(2b log b) ≤ 1/p.
In particular b−a≤(2+o(1))log p. In this variant m(p)<0 is allowed. It suffices to prove π(p)≤C(p) eventually on the intersection of these two filters (the one-sided m filter and the gap filter). Under RH this necessary condition also holds by 7535, since F(p)≫√p/log p and p m(p)≤1.

Proof. Minimize G(x)=F(x)+εx on [2,∞), with positive ε tending to zero. F=o(x) by PNT and m=o(1), so the minimum exists. Its value tends to minus infinity by the excursions of 7535: first fix a point with arbitrarily negative F and then make ε small. The minimizers escape every compact set and are primes by strict concavity. At p write u=m(p)+ε. The one-sided slopes give 0≤u≤1/p. Hence π(p)−C(p)=pu−G(p)≥−G(p).

On [p,b] the loss relative to the right tangent at p on reaching b is ∫_p^b(b−t)dt/(t log t)≥(b−p)²/(2b log b). Since G(b)≥G(p), u≥(b−p)/(2b log b). On [a,p] the analogous loss is ∫_a^p(t−a)dt/(t log t)≥(p−a)²/(2p log p), and G(a)≥G(p) requires 1/p−u≥(p−a)/(2p log p). On adding, the tilt ε disappears. The PNT gives b/p→1 and the asymptotic conclusion. The use of the tilted global minimum is essential to compare both neighbours simultaneously. The control of π at the selected primes remains unproved.

### A single relative tent on [p/2,2p] eliminates the prefix in the sign proof

Define w_p(t)=2(t−p/2)/3 on [p/2,p] and (2p−t)/3 on [p,2p], zero outside. RH is equivalent to the eventual strict inequality, at prime centres p,
    Σ_{p/2<q<2p prime} w_p(q)/q < ∫_{p/2}^{2p} w_p(t)dt/(t log t).
It even suffices to require it at centres satisfying the exact two-gap inequality of 7547. The centre filter and both sides are local. The tent as a class of weights already has antecedents in the index (phase 213, filter 2244); what is deduced here is this fixed choice of slopes, relative scale and centres, with explicit margin under RH.

Indeed, the difference sum minus integral is exactly D(p)=(2F(p/2)+F(2p))/3−F(p). It is obtained by integrating by parts twice: the distributional second derivative of F is Σ δ_q/q−dt/(t log t), and that of w_p consists of masses 2/3,−1,1/3 at its three vertices. Under RH, by 7535,
    limsup D(p)log p/√p ≤ (2+0.047)·(2√2/3)−(2−0.047)<−0.023.
The changes of logarithm at the two endpoints cost o(1) after normalizing. Without RH, at the arbitrarily late minimizers of 7547, the chord of F+εx between p/2 and 2p lies above the minimum at p, hence D(p)≥0 by affine cancellation. Those primes satisfy the gap filter. The reduction eliminates B₁, π(p) and every sum over q<p/2 from the pending statement. The unconditional sign for this fixed tent remains open.

### Mandatory excursions of the tent and the budget of the squares

For each exterior zero with real part β and each 1/2<σ<β one has limsup D(p)/p^σ=+∞ even on the exact two-gap filter of 7547. Indeed fix A>0 and minimize F(x)+A x^σ+εx. By 7535, F(x)+A x^σ takes arbitrarily negative values; as in 7547 the minimizers escape to infinity as ε decreases to zero. The added perturbation is concave, hence the minima are still primes. The slopes at p jump by 1/p and the losses relative to the tangents only increase, which preserves the two gap inequalities added in 7547. By the chord of 7557,
    D(p) ≥ A p^σ [1−(2·2^(−σ)+2^σ)/3].
The bracket is strictly positive by strict concavity of x^σ. Taking A arbitrary proves the statement without requiring a zero of maximal real part.

Let H(u)=w_1(u)/u, and J(p)=Σ_{q prime,k≥1} H(q^k/p)/k−∫ H(t/p)dt/log t, with the integral over [p/2,2p]. Unconditionally
    J(p)−D(p)=[2(1−2√2/3)+o(1)]√p/log p.
For k=2, PNT after scaling q=√p v gives the coefficient ∫H(v²)dv=(1/2)∫w_1(u)u^(−3/2)du. Two integrations by parts against (√u)″=−u^(−3/2)/4 give the stated value. Convergence by PNT suffices by continuity and compact support of the weight. The powers k≥3 contribute O(p^(1/3)log p) by trivial counting and support. In particular J has the same infinite limsup at scale p^σ in the presence of that zero. It would suffice to prove J(p)≪_δ p^(1/2+δ) one-sidedly for each δ>0 at the filtered centres: choose δ<σ−1/2. The explicit constant of the squares does not require RH; the one-sided bound for the term J remains open.

### Absolute cost of the quadrature on the tent after centring the logarithm of the divisor

Internal antecedents: ROUND_046_A (variation of the derivative), index 35890 (difference between blocks and telescoping), and 4708 ff. (zero-mean weights). Here the individual tent of 7557, which has positive mean, is kept. The specific estimate improves the cut up to D=x^(3/4)√log x with error O(√x), without Möbius cancellation. The telescoping subtraction is not tried again.

Let I=∫ H(t/x)dt/log t over [x/2,2x], D as above and c_d=μ(d)log(D/d). For large x, the following decomposition is unconditional and uniform:
    J(x)= I(Σ_{d≤D} c_d/d−1)
        + Σ_{m≤2x/D} Σ_{D<d≤2x/m} c_d H(dm/x)/log(dm) + O(√x).
It suffices to restrict the summand to the support; the cofactor m is at most 2x^(1/4)/√log x. Indeed Σ_{d|n} c_d=Λ(n) for n>1, since Σμ(d)=0 over divisors of n. For d≤D the inner sum over m differs from I/d by O(d/(x log x)). To see this extend f(u)=H(u)/log(xu) by zero outside [1/2,2]. The variation of f′, counting the three jumps, is O(1/log x) by the rational formulas of H on the two segments. On a mesh of step h=d/x the error of the trapezoidal rule, divided by h, costs O(h Var(f′)): in each cell the deviation of the linear interpolant is at most h times the variation of f′ in the cell. Finally Σ_{d≤D} d log(D/d)≪D², by dyadic blocks. The total cost is O(D²/(x log x)). The additional factor √log x in the cut comes from centring log d at log D in the integer convolution. The continuous mass of the short stretch is kept explicit: only its sampling error is paid. The joint upper bound of the two exposed terms remains pending.

### The two pieces of 7577 separately exceed the root scale even under RH

Assume RH only for this obstruction proof. For each 0<η<1/8, the continuous term B(x)=I(x)(A(D)−1), with A(v)=Σ_{d≤v}μ(d)log(v/d)/d, has quotients B(p)/p^(5/8−η) unbounded in both directions over the prime centres. On the same sequences the cofactor tail has the opposite sign and compensates B(p) up to O(√p). This excludes a separate one-sided root-scale bound at all prime centres. The additional two-gap condition is not imposed in this obstruction.

Indeed the Mellin transform of A(v)−1 on [1,∞), with measure v^(−s−1)dv, is 1/[s²ζ(1+s)]−1/s for Re s>0 by termwise integration. The apparent pole at zero is removable. At s=ρ−1 for any non-trivial zero it is singular, and on the real axis s>−1 it is regular (ζ has no real zeros in (0,1)). Under RH the real abscissa of those poles is −1/2. By Landau applied to K v^(−1/2−ε)±(A(v)−1), both signs of A(v)−1 exceed K v^(−1/2−ε) arbitrarily for any K>0 and 0<ε<1/2. Otherwise the transform of the eventually non-negative combination would be regular on the whole real interval (−1/2−ε,∞) and by Landau would converge there, contradicting the non-real pole.

Write v=D(x) (increasing and surjective on a tail). Since I(x) is comparable to x/log x, the exponent for B(x) is 1−(3/4)(1/2+ε), up to logarithmic powers. Choose positive ε sufficiently small depending on η. To pass to primes, under RH there is p in [x,x+O(√x log²x)] by the bound for ψ and the contribution of higher powers, enlarging the absolute constant. The derivative of A with respect to log v is Σ_{d≤v}μ(d)/d=O(log v) almost everywhere and A is continuous; hence the change in A on passing from D(x) to D(p) is O(x^(−1/2)log³x), negligible against D(x)^(−1/2−ε) if ε<1/6. The compensation follows from 7577 and J(p)=O(√p/log p) under RH by the two-sided formula for F in 7535, the chord of 7557 and 7567. The exponent 5/8 measures the cost of separating the mass at that cut, not a new margin for the sign.

### The cut obstruction persists on the exact two-gap filter

Under RH, in 7586 the neighbour inequality of 7547 can be imposed on p. It is first proved that for each large x there is one of those centres in [x,x+4x^(9/10)]. Choose inside an interval [u,v] of length comparable to x^(9/10) where ceil(log t)=k is constant and k−log t≥c x^(−1/10) for an absolute c. In log coordinate the available interval measures (4+o(1))x^(−1/10); removing neighbourhoods of radius x^(−1/10)/4 of the integers leaves a subinterval of the required length. Under RH the number N of primes in [u,v] is ∫_u^v dt/log t+O(√x log x). It exceeds (v−u)/k+2, because the gain is ≫x^(8/10)/log²x. If at all interior centres the stretch between their neighbours exceeded 2 log p, by parity that stretch would measure at least 2k. Summing the N−2 stretches gives 2k(N−2)≤2(v−u), a contradiction. Some centre has b−a≤2 log p, a sufficient condition for the exact inequality since b log b≥p log p.

To transfer the excursion of A to that centre the continuity used in 7586 must be refined. Under RH the classical Mertens bound is M(v)=O_δ(v^(1/2+δ)) for δ>0; by Abel and Σμ(d)/d=0 one gets Σ_{d≤v}μ(d)/d=O_δ(v^(−1/2+δ)) for δ<1/2. This is the derivative of A with respect to log v away from integers. Hence in the transfer the error is O_δ(x^(−1/10)D(x)^(−1/2+δ)), negligible against D(x)^(−1/2−ε) for positive ε,δ with (3/4)(δ+ε)<1/10. Moreover ε can be chosen arbitrarily small depending on η as in 7586. Thus both sequences and their signs are preserved inside the filter. The RH hypothesis is used to refute the strategy of separate bounds even in the target scenario; the unconditional cancellation between mass and tail remains pending.

### Smoothed harmonic cut: continuous mass exactly one and a single cofactor residue

Use the harmonic inversion of 7383 BEFORE separating the divisors of the tent of 7577. Fix a non-negative C∞ density φ with integral 1 supported in (1,2). Put L(v)=∫φ(s) H_{⌊sv⌋}ds (H₀=0), c=γ+∫φ(s)log s ds and R(v)=log v+c−L(v). For D=x^(3/4)√log x and large x one has, for each fixed 0<ε<1/4,
    J(x)= Σ_{dm∈[x/2,2x], d>D x^(−ε)} μ(d) R(D/d) H(dm/x)/log(dm) + O_ε(√x).
In particular no Möbius density term remains outside the sum and m≤2x^(1/4+ε)/√log x. The one-sided bound for this sum remains open.

Proof. For sD≥1 the identity Σ_{d≤sD} μ(d)H_{⌊sD/d⌋}/d=1 follows by grouping by the product dk. Hence Σ_d μ(d)L(D/d)/d=1 exactly. On the tent, the contribution of μ(d)L(D/d) is I+O(√x) by the quadrature of 7577: there are only d≤2D, and Σ_{d≤2D} d L(D/d)≪D², by summing 1+log(2D/d) with weight d. The divisor sum of μ(d)[log(D/d)+c] is Λ(n) for n>1. On subtracting the comparator precisely R remains with the same μ(d).

For every fixed N, R(v)=O_N(v^(−N)) when v≥1. Indeed, with Φ(t)=∫_t^∞ φ(s)ds one has L(v)=Σ_{k≥1}Φ(k/v)/k and v L′(v)=v^(−1)Σ_{k≥1}φ(k/v)=1+O_N(v^(−N)) by Euler–Maclaurin, since φ is smooth with interior support. The limit L(v)−log v→c follows from the harmonic asymptotic uniformly in s. Integrating the derivative gives the bound for R. Thus for d≤Dx^(−ε) its absolute contribution is O_N(x^(1−Nε)) by counting multiples and Σ_{d≤2x}1/d≪log x, which compensates the denominator log(dm). Take Nε≥1/2. The smoothing removes the separate term with excursions of 7586 without assuming it is small: it changes both sides of the cut simultaneously and preserves the total convolution.

### Fixed-sign harmonic residue with exact cut

In 7600 one can achieve simultaneously R(v)=0 for v≥1 and R(v)<0 for 0<v<1. Take φ(s)=K s² sinc(s/4)^8 for s>0, sinc(t)=sin(πt)/(πt), K normalizing the integral. Keep L,c,R of 7600. The pending sum only has d>D and m≤2x/D without loss x^ε. Its factor other than μ has known sign. Antecedent: 4712 uses Poisson on the observation weight; here the physical tent stays fixed and a harmonic comparator with one-sided residue is constructed.

Details. Extend φ evenly. Let B be the transform of sinc(s/4)^8 with convention exp(−2πist); it is the convolution of eight boxes on [−1/8,1/8] with positive factors. By repeated integration of boxes, for t≥0 it is proportional to Σ_{j=0}^8 (−1)^j binom(8,j)(1−t−j/4)_+^7. Then the transform of φ is −K B″/(4π²). For 2/5≤t<1 one has B″>0: the first term (1−t)^5 exceeds in modulus the second 8(3/4−t)_+^5, since (1−t)/(3/4−t)≥12/7 while the denominator is positive. Only the third term, positive, can additionally remain. For t≥1 the transform vanishes. Poisson with φ(0)=0 gives vL′(v)=1+Σ_{j≥1}φ̂(jv), hence vR′(v)=−Σ_{j≥1}φ̂(jv). Convergence of the physical sums follows from the O(s^(−6)) decay; R(∞)=0 by dominated convergence in the harmonic asymptotic (the stretch s<1/v costs O(v^(−3)) even with |log(sv)|). It follows that R=0 on [1,∞) and R<0 on [2/5,1).

On (0,2/5] use L≥0 and Jensen: c≤γ+(1/2)log ∫s²φ(s)ds=γ+log(4/π)<log(5/2). The second moment is −B⁽⁴⁾(0)/(4π²B″(0))=16/π² by the box formula (the alternating sums of (4−j)^3 and (4−j)^5 for 0≤j≤4 with binomial coefficients equal 16 and −80). Thus log v+c<0 there.

The mass of the comparator now equals ∫_{1/D}^∞φ=1−O(D^(−3)), sufficient at root scale. The quadrature cost remains O(D²/(x log x)) by positivity and Σ d H_{⌊sD/d⌋}≪(sD)², integrating against φ with finite second moment. The formula of 7600 is obtained with d>D by exact vanishing and uniform O(√x). The fixed sign converts the pending ceiling into a comparison between the masses of squarefree d with odd and even number of prime factors; it does not establish that comparison.

### Positive balance of the products with all primes larger than the fourth root

In the joint sum of 7610 select n=dm with all its prime factors larger than z=(2x)^(1/4). Its contribution is unconditionally
    [κ/4+o(1)] (x/log x)∫H(u)du,
    κ=1−log 3+∫₂³ log(t−1)dt/t>0.03.
The complement contributes the opposite at the same order. Here one groups by the integer n, keeping all its active divisors, and the conclusion holds for all large x.

Indeed n≤2x admits at most three factors >z, counted with multiplicity. Every proper divisor is ≤2x/z<D for sufficiently large x. Only d=n survives and its weight modulus is [1/4+o(1)] H(n/x) uniformly, since R(D/n)=log(D/n)+c−o(1) by L(v)→0 at zero. Repeated powers, if they appear in auxiliary counts, cost O(x/z) by summing x/q². The signs are +,−,+ for one, two and three primes.

To make the coefficients precise, the PNT in each variable gives for k unordered products the main term (x/log x)∫H multiplied by f_k(4), where f_k(U) is 1/k! times the integral of 1/(a₁···a_k) over a_i≥1/U, Σa_i=1, in the first k−1 coordinates. To justify the step, successively replace dπ by dt/log t with error o(x/log x): with the other primes of product M fixed, the inner endpoint lies between z and 2x/M, and the uniform error by PNT and bounded variation of the weight is o(x/(M log x)); the sums or integrals of 1/M are O(1) by Mertens on [z,2x]. Then put n=xu in the last variable and a_i=log t_i/log(xu) in the others, with threshold log z/log(xu)→1/4 uniform. The Jacobian gives the stated integral. f₁=1; differentiating the k lower faces of the simplex gives f'_k(U)=f_{k−1}(U−1)/(U−1) for U>k (rescale the other k−1 variables by 1−1/U). With f_k(k)=0 for k≥2 one gets f₂(4)=log 3 and f₃(4)=∫₂³ log(t−1)dt/t. Concavity gives log(t−1)≥(t−2)log 2, whence κ≥1−log 3+(1−2log(3/2))log 2>0.03. By PNT the total tent J(x)=o(x/log x) (higher powers cost O(√x log x)); the error of 7610 is also negligible at this scale. This proves the complementary balance. The computation forces pairing with integers that do have some small factor; it does not control the joint error at root scale.

### Per-integer cancellation when the small-prime part has two distinct bases

With z=(2x)^(1/4), write n=ab uniquely by putting into a all the powers of primes ≤z present in n. Fix A=x^(3/20)/(log x)^(3/10). In the sum of 7610 over 1<a≤A the contribution, up to a total absolute error O(√x), is
    Σ_{n=ab} H(n/x) μ(b)Λ(a)/log n
with the same selection of n. In particular the family of ALL n in this band whose a contains at least two distinct primes already costs O(√x), even summing the moduli after grouping the divisors of each integer. The powers of a single prime are the only family of the band with a possible main term. The case a=1 corresponds to the previous sector and stays separate.

Indeed any divisor of n omitting at least one copy of some prime of b is ≤2x/z<D and has zero residue. The remaining ones are d=bs, s|a, with μ(bs)=μ(b)μ(s). If b is not squarefree the contribution vanishes exactly. For the others, in Σ_{s|a}μ(s)R(D/(bs)) the logarithmic part plus the constant equals Λ(a) by the two divisor identities for a>1. The rest is at most C(D/b)^5 in modulus: from φ(t)≪t^(−6) and L(v)=Σ Φ(k/v)/k one gets L(v)≪v^5 for 0<v≤1, and Σ_{s|a}s^(−5)≤ζ(5). Here D/b≤2DA/x=o(1). For each a there are O(x/a) possible values of b, even without requiring roughness. The absolute sum of errors after the weight H/log n is ≪(x/log x)(D/x)^5 Σ_{a≤A}a^4≪√x with the indicated choice. This transfers root precision to a whole family, without invoking cancellation between integers or RH. The terms with a a prime power, those with a=1 and the band a>A still require a joint comparison.

### An interior cut cancels the main term between the rough ones and those with one small base

For fixed 0≤α<3/20, the full contribution of a≤x^α of 7631, including a=1, divided by (x/log x)∫H, tends to
    S(α)=k(4)/4−∫₀^α k(4−4r)dr/(1−r),
    k(u)=1−log(u−1)+∫₂^(u−1) log(t−1)dt/t.
There is a unique α* between 1/8 and 7/50 with S(α*)=0. At that cut the two sectors a≤x^α* and a>x^α* are each o(x/log x). Root precision is not claimed for either.

For a>1 apply 7631. With y=x/a, U=log y/log z, the signed count of rough b, with weight H(b/y), is [−k(U)∫H+o(1)] y/log y. It is the simplex integral of 7620 with sign μ(b); the error is uniform for 1≤a≤x^α, since U remains in a compact subset of (3,4] for large x, all prime variables are ≥z and the shift of the threshold on replacing log y by log(yu) is O(1/log x) on the support. Replacing 1/log(ab) by 1/log x costs a relative error O(1/log x) for each unsigned count. Normalize and sum with Λ(a)/a: the measure Σ Λ(a)δ_{log a/log x}/(a log x) converges to dr on [0,α] by partial summation and PNT. The factor 1/(1−r) comes from log x/log y. The non-prime powers of a have mass o(1) in that measure. Add the case a=1 of 7620.

To verify the crossing, k′(u)=[log(u−2)−1]/(u−1)<0 in the range and k(4)>0 by 7620; the outer integrand is positive increasing. In the inner integral log(t−1)/t is increasing on [2,3]. Use the left and right sums of 100 equal subintervals in each integral, with the appropriate endpoints when subtracting. It was verified with interval logarithms (mpmath.iv, 24 decimals): 0.0003800<S(1/8)<0.0012863 and −0.0020287<S(7/50)<−0.0010668. Strict monotonicity gives uniqueness. Unlike the Dickman balance for m|6 recorded in the index, here the whole small part a varies and the main mass of the comparator of 7610 is cancelled.

### A computable divisor cut with the interior sector cancels it in each window

There are constants θ>1/4, α∈(1/8,7/50) and 1−θ<β₋<β₊<3/4 with the following unconditional property. Define z=x^θ and a as in 7631 with respect to this z. For every sufficiently large x there exists D∈[x^β₋,x^β₊] for which the full contribution of the sector a≤x^α to the residue of 7610 is exactly zero. Knowing the integers of that sector suffices to choose D. The total quadrature keeps error O(√x) for any of these cuts. Hence the pending inequality can be restricted to the n with a>x^α using this x-dependent D.

Proof. Put β₀=3/4−(θ−1/4)/2 and take θ sufficiently close to 1/4 from above. The normalized coefficient of the sector a≤x^α for D=x^β is
    S(θ,α,β)=(1−β)k(1/θ)−∫₀^α k((1−r)/θ)dr/(1−r).
Indeed for a=1 all proper divisors lie below D since 2x/z<D for β>1−θ; −R(D/n)/log n→1−β uniformly. For a>1 the same argument of 7631 holds, with error O(x(D x^α/x)^5/log x)=O(√x) since β<3/4 and α<7/50. Apply the simplex integrals of 7639, now with log z=θ log x. All their arguments remain in (3,4) on choosing θ sufficiently close to 1/4. The normalization factor is still (x/log x)∫H.

By the strict margins of 7639 and continuity, S(θ,1/8,β₀)>0 and S(θ,7/50,β₀)<0. Fix the unique intermediate α that cancels S(θ,α,β₀); k is positive in the range. Choose β₋,β₊ interior to (1−θ,3/4), one on each side of β₀. The slope in β is −k(1/θ)<0. Thus the exact contributions of the sector at the two extreme cuts have opposite signs for each sufficiently large x. Their dependence on D is continuous: it is a finite sum over divisors of the continuous kernel R, which is zero from D/d=1 on. The intermediate value theorem gives the announced cut, accessible by bisection. The total cost of replacing the comparator by the integral is O(D²/(x log x)+x D^(−3)/log x)=O(√x) uniformly on that band by 7610 (choose θ close to 1/4). The cut redistributes the residue; the conclusion does not give an additional saving for the sum over the complement.

### Global monotonicity of the residue and per-integer sign in the whole one-small-base family

The residue R of 7610 satisfies 0≤vR′(v)≤1 for all v>0, with strictly positive derivative for 0<v<1. On [2/5,1) positivity already follows from Poisson in 7610, and the upper bound follows from L′≥0. For 0<v≤2/5 use v L′(v)=v^(−1)Σ_{k≥1}φ(k/v)≤K(4/π)^8ζ(6)v^5. Integrating the unnormalized density on [0,1], where sinc(s/4)≥2√2/π, gives K≤3(π/(2√2))^8. Hence v L′≤48(6/5)(2/5)^5<1 by integral comparison for ζ(6). For v≥1 R is identically zero.

For the cuts of 7650 and n=ab in the window with a=q^j, q≤z prime, j≥1 arbitrary, the divisor sum of the residue, before multiplying by H/log n, equals exactly
    μ(b)[R(D/b)−R(D/(bq))].
Indeed every divisor not a multiple of b lies below D on omitting a factor >z; the only multiples of b with coefficient not necessarily zero are b and bq. The enclosed difference lies between 0 and log q, and is positive exactly when bq>D. This covers all sizes of a even beyond the approximate band of 7631. If b=1 both terms are zero. The case of non-squarefree b is also zero. Since four factors >z already exceed 2x for large x, in this family the only strictly positive contributions are those with b a product of TWO distinct large primes and bq>D (for n in the interior of the support). A single large prime or three distinct ones give a non-positive contribution for all large x. The remaining families with a of several bases and the comparison with these semiprimes remain open. Not all negative contributions can be discarded without accounting for the lost compensation.

### Uniform sign with any number of small bases when b≥16D

For 7650, if a has at least two distinct primes and b≥16D, the individual contribution of n=ab in the interior of the support has sign −μ(b), including the value zero. The constant 16 is independent of the number and size of the factors of a. In this zone the positive contributions can only have b prime or a product of three distinct primes. The direction of the sign is reversed with respect to the one-base family of 7660.

Indeed write v=D/b. The active divisor sum is μ(b)Σ_{s|a}μ(s)R(v/s). Since there are two or more bases, the affine part in log(v/s) disappears exactly. What remains is −μ(b)Σ_{s|a}μ(s)L(v/s). To control this last sum use φ(t)=K(4/π)^8 t^(−6) sin^8(πt/4). The eighth power of sine has period 4 and mean M>0. On consecutive intervals of length 4 from u>4, bound t^(−6) by its two endpoints and compare both series with the decreasing integral. This gives for Φ(u)=∫_u^∞φ the double bound C (u+4)^(−5)≤Φ(u)≤C (u−4)^(−5), C=K(4/π)^8 M/5. For 0<v≤1/16, from L(v)=Σ_{k≥1}Φ(k/v)/k one deduces
    C ζ(6) v^5 (5/4)^(−5) ≤ L(v) ≤ C ζ(6) v^5 (3/4)^(−5).
Thus Σ_{s|a,s>1} L(v/s)/L(v) ≤ (5/3)^5 (ζ(5)−1)<1: it suffices that ζ(5)−1≤2^(−5)+∫₂^∞t^(−5)dt=3/64. The first summand dominates all others in absolute value. More precisely, as v→0 the interior balance divided by Cζ(6)v^5 is ∏_{q|a}(1−q^(−5))+O(v) uniformly in a, by the same bounds with factors (1±4v)^(−5) and the convergent sum of s^(−6). This decides the individual sign also for a>x^α whenever b≥16D. Neither the multiple-base strip b<16D nor the balance of the already determined signs is estimated globally.

### Counterexample in the complement: both orientations with b=1 and identical parity

For the moving cut of 7650, even fixing b=1, μ(a)=+1 and n squarefree, there are two subfamilies of the complement with opposite signs, each of absolute mass ≫x/log x. It holds uniformly for every admissible D, so it includes any root chosen in 7650. The sign of 7668 does not extend to the rest merely by knowing the two parities.

Take k=4 or 6 and n a product of k distinct primes with |log q/log x−1/k|<h, in x≤n≤1.1x. Fix θ and the endpoints of 7650 close enough to 1/4 and 3/4 respectively so that 2/3<β₋<β₊<3/4. There exists a fixed sufficiently small h>0 such that all primes are ≤x^θ, every n/q exceeds D by a factor ≥x^δ and every n/(qr) with q,r distinct lies below D, for some common δ>0. This uses 1−1/k≥3/4 and 1−2/k≤2/3. By the exact cut only n and its k divisors n/q contribute. Since k is even, the balance before the weight H/log n is
    R(D/n)−Σ_{q|n} R(Dq/n) = (k−2)log n−(k−1)log D+(1−k)c+O(x^(−5δ)).
Here L(v)≪v^5 is used for each active term. For β=log D/log x the coefficient of log x is 2−3β<0 with four and 4−5β>0 with six, with uniform margins. H is positive and bounded away from zero on [1,1.1].

To count at least c_h x/log x integers of each class, choose the first k−1 primes in [x^(1/k−h/(3k)),x^(1/k+h/(3k))], distinct, with product P. The sum of 1/P is bounded below by a positive constant: Mertens gives a positive limit for the sum of reciprocals in the band and the repeated diagonals cost o(1). For the last prime use [x/P,1.1x/P], which lies in the wide band; by PNT there are ≫x/(P log x) options even excluding the first primes. The multiplicity does not exceed k!. In all of them a=n>x^α. Thus the two signs far exceed the root budget even in the same parity class and without large factors. The proof does not quantify the net balance between the two classes nor with the other integers.

### Aggregate cancellation at root scale over all multiples of the first primes

For D in the whole band of 7650 there exists a fixed λ>0 such that the joint residue of 7610 over the integers n with some prime divisor ≤λ log x is O(√x), without RH. The bound is for the aggregate balance, including all a. It allows using the n coprime to the primorial as an alternative restriction of the criterion, without claiming that this restriction and a>x^α can be intersected for free.

Let W be the product of the primes ≤λ log x. On the n coprime to W the weighted sum of Λ loses only powers of primes of W in the window; even counting all powers up to 2x the loss with weight H/log n is O(log² x). For the comparator of 7610 only d coprime to W appear and the multiples m must also be coprime to W. On expanding this second condition by h|W, the quadrature with step dh/x gives for the comparator sum I·B plus error O(D² Σ_{h|W}h/(x log x)), where
    B=(φ_E(W)/W) Σ_{(d,W)=1} μ(d)L(D/d)/d
and φ_E is Euler's function. Σ d L(D/d)≪D² of 7610 was used. By PNT and ∏_{p|W}(1+1/p)=x^o(1), Σ_{h|W}h=x^(λ+o(1)); choose 0<λ<3/2−2β₊.

To control B write M(v)=Σ_d μ(d)L(v/d)/d=∫_{1/v}^∞φ(s)ds as in 7610. On inverting only the prime factors of W one obtains exactly
    B=(φ_E(W)/W) Σ_{k with all its primes in W} M(D/k)/k.
Indeed the convolution of μ with the indicator of those k gives μ(d)1_{(d,W)=1}. The series are absolutely convergent for each x by the decay of L at zero and the finite product of geometric factors. The weights are positive and sum to one. Since φ(s)≪s² at zero, 0≤1−M(v)≪min(1,v^(−3)). Fix 1/(2β₋)<t<1. Then
    0≤1−B≪D^(−t) ∏_{p≤λ log x}(1−p^(t−1))^(−1) ≤ x^(−β₋t+o(1)).
The logarithm of the product costs O_t(Σ_{j≤λ log x}j^(t−1))=o(log x). Thus I|1−B|=o(√x), while the previous quadrature cost is o(√x) by the choice of λ. The residue sum restricted to the coprime ones is therefore J(x)+O(√x), the same as the full one; subtracting proves the statement. The calibration is applied to the same tent and its signed residue, unlike the comparison of translated classes of the primorial in index 35450. The products of four and six primes of 7676 persist among the coprime ones.

### Simultaneous calibration and size of the correction by the primorial

With y=λ log x as in 7686 there exists a cut D₁ in the same band as 7650 such that it suffices to sum the residue over n coprime to W AND with a>x^α, with total error O(√x). With respect to any root D₀ of 7650 one has log(D₁/D₀)=(1+o(1))log y. Using the same cut without recalibrating would have lost a mass of order x log y/log²x, above root scale.

Details. Let P_D be the exact contribution of a≤x^α, and I_D the contribution of its intersection with (n,W)>1. Put K₀=k(1/θ)∫H>0. Uniformly over the band of cuts,
    I_D=−(K₀+o(1)) x log y/log²x.
By 7631 and 7650 the total per-integer error of the substitution by μ(b)Λ(a)H(n/x)/log n for 1<a≤x^α costs O(√x) even on subsets. The case a=1 is coprime to W. In the intersection only a=q^j with q≤y remains in the main term. For j=1 the uniform simplex computation of 7639, with log q/log x=o(1), gives for q a contribution −(K₀+o(1))x log q/(q log²x). Sum using Σ_{q≤y}log q/q∼log y by PNT. For j≥2 the unsigned count of the rough b in each window is O((x/a)/log x) uniformly for a≤x^α, by the same unsigned simplex. The convergent series Σ_{q,j≥2}log q/q^j gives O(x/log²x).

Since I_D=o(x/log x), P_D−I_D keeps the opposite signs at the endpoints of 7650, is continuous and has a root D₁ computable only from the data of the coprime interior sector. At that cut the full sum decomposes into three disjoint sets: non-coprime (O(√x) by 7686), coprime interior (zero) and coprime exterior. To measure the displacement, P_D is affine in log D up to O(√x) uniformly: for a>1 the main term is independent of D, and for a=1 the cost of L(D/n) is O(x(D/x)^5/log x). Its affine slope is Σ_{a=1} μ(n)H(n/x)/log n=−(K₀+o(1))x/log²x by the rough simplex. Subtracting P_{D₀}=0 from P_{D₁}=I_{D₁} and dividing by that slope proves the equivalence. The coprime exterior balance remains open, including the examples of 7676.

### Root-scale threshold of the continuous deficit as the primorial grows

Let y=(log x)^A with fixed A>1, W the primorial up to y and D=x^β with β in the compact band of 7650 (it may depend on x). For the continuous mass B of 7686 one has unconditionally
    1−B=x^(−β/A+o(1)).
There is no need to control the quadrature over this larger primorial to compute B. Since I is comparable to x/log x, the continuous loss has exponent 1−β/A. If A>2β₊, the loss exceeds the root scale by a fixed power for all admissible cuts, including the recalibrated ones. If 1<A<2β₋, this loss is o(√x) uniformly after multiplying by I; in that band the control of the arithmetic quadrature over the coprime ones remains pending.

Proof. The upper bound of 7686 applies with any positive t<1/A: the logarithm of the Rankin product is O_t(y^t)=o(log x). Take t arbitrarily close to 1/A. For the floor use in the positive average the k that are products of ℓ=ceil(log D/log(y/2)) distinct primes of (y/2,y]. Then k≥D and 1−M(D/k)≥∫₀¹φ(s)ds>0. There are N≫y/log y eligible primes by PNT and ℓ=o(N), since A>1. Their total weight before normalization is ≥binom(N,ℓ)y^(−ℓ)≥(N/(ℓ y))^ℓ. The logarithm of this bound is ≥−ℓ(log ℓ+log log y+O(1))=−(β/A+o(1))log x. The normalization φ_E(W)/W costs only O(log log y) in the logarithm by Mertens. This gives the uniform floor. At the threshold A=2β the exponent alone does not decide an O(√x) bound. The obstruction refers to paying this loss separately; it does not exclude compensating it with the discrete quadrature.

### Second term of the primorial deficit and decision at the critical exponent

Put X=log x, y=C X^A, with fixed C>0 and A>1. Uniformly for β in the previous compact band and D=x^β,
 log(1−B)=−βX/A + (βX/log y)[1+log(A/β)+(log C)/A+o(1)].
In particular on fixing A=2β and C=1, I(1−B)/√x grows like exp((β+o(1))(1+log 2)X/log y). For C<(1/(2e))^A at that same exponent the loss is o(√x); for C>(1/(2e))^A it exceeds √x by a divergent factor. The equality in C is not decided here.

Proof. Under the distribution on integers k with primes ≤y that gives the mass B in 7686, the exponents of each prime p are independent geometric with ratio 1/p. Write Z=log k and K(t)=log E exp(tZ). For 0<t<1 the change of measure proportional to exp(tZ) preserves independence with ratio p^(t−1). Choose t with K′(t)=βX+2X^(2/3). For t in a compact subset interior to (0,1), PNT and partial summation give uniformly
    K′(t)=(1+o(1))y^t/t,  K(t)=(1+o(1))y^t/(t log y),  K″(t)≪ y^t log y.
Indeed the main summands are (log p)p^(t−1) and p^(t−1) for the first two formulas; the terms of powers ≥2 are little-o of the main ones by separation into small and large p. The logarithm of the normalization in K costs O(log log y). For the variance, sum (log p)^2 p^(t−1)/(1−p^(t−1))². By monotonicity of K′ and the estimates on both sides of 1/A, t exists and tends to 1/A. Taking logarithms in the formula for K′ one obtains
    t=1/A+[log(β/A)−(log C)/A+o(1)]/log y,
    K(t)=(β+o(1))X/log y.
Since 1−M(D/k)≪(k/D)^t, the ceiling for log(1−B) is K(t)−tβX+O(1). For the floor, under the tilted measure the probability of βX≤Z≤βX+4X^(2/3) tends to one by Chebyshev since K″≪X log y. There 1−M(D/k) is bounded away from zero and the return to the original measure costs at most t(βX+4X^(2/3))−K(t) in the negative logarithm. The separation of both extremes is o(X/log y). Substituting t proves the second term; log I=X−log X+O(1). This proof refers to the mass loss of the comparator in isolation. The precision x^(1/2+δ) for every δ>0 admits factors exp(O(X/log y)) and the discrete quadrature remains open at this scale.

### Exact size in exponent of the unsigned discrete error

For y=C(log x)^A, fixed A>1, define E(l)=Σ_{j≥1}H(lj/x)/log(lj)−I/l, summing only on the support as before. After inclusion-exclusion over W, the cost of taking absolute values BEFORE grouping is
    Σ_{(d,W)=1}|μ(d)| L(D/d) Σ_{h|W}|E(dh)| = x^[1−(1−β)/A+o(1)].
In particular not even for A barely larger than one does this procedure reach root scale. The floor is for the actual errors of the meshes, not only for a chosen majorant. It is not a floor for their signed sum.

For the ceiling one has |E(l)|≪min(l/x,x/l)/log x: first bound by variation of the derivative, second by trivial counting if l≤2x and absence of samples if l>2x. For −1<r<1/A−1, majorize the minimum by (l/x)^r. The factor of h costs ∏_{p≤y}(1+p^r)=exp(O(y^(1+r)))=x^o(1). The factor of d costs O_r(D^(1+r)) since L(v)≪1+log v for v≥1 and L(v)≪v^5 for v≤1. The exponent is β−(1−β)r; let r approach 1/A−1 from below. The same count restricted to d≤x^u≤D gives exponent at most 1−(1−u)/A+o(1), absorbing a logarithm. Thus for 1<A<2 the stretch u<1−A/2 is paid below root scale without cancelling signs.

For the floor take primes d∈[D,2D] (coprime to W, L(D/d) bounded below by L(1/2)>0) and h a product of ℓ=ceil(log(3x/D)/log(y/2)) distinct primes in (y/2,y]. There are x^(β+o(1)) choices of d. Since N=π(y)−π(y/2)≍y/log y and ℓ=o(N), there are at least (N/ℓ)^ℓ=x^((1−β)(1−1/A)+o(1)) distinct choices of h. Each mesh has 3x≤dh≤x^(1+o(1)) because ℓ log 2=o(log x). Then |E(dh)|=I/(dh)≥x^(−o(1)). Adding the exponents gives the announced floor, uniform over the band of β. The result locates an excessive cost even where the discrete sum is empty and only its integral correction remains.

### The large meshes admit a reduction with saving to the prime discrepancy at a smaller scale

Fix 1<A<2β₋, y=C(log x)^A, H₀=2x/D and σ=1/2. Let Q(D)=1+sup_{1≤u≤D}|ψ(u)−u|/u^σ, with ψ(u)=Σ_{n≤u}Λ(n). There exists a fixed η>0 such that the sum of errors of 7731 over h≥H₀, grouping first with μ(d), costs in modulus
    O(x^(1/2−η) [1+Q(D)]).
RH is not assumed for the inequality; Q(D) stays explicit. The gain over the absolute cost of 7731 comes from the kernel being exactly affine for all divisors of the samples in this range.

Indeed write f(t)=H(t/x)/log t on the support and zero outside. For each large h every integer m with f(hm)≠0 satisfies m≤D; by 7610 L(D/d)=log(D/d)+c for all its divisors. Decompose m=kr with k having primes ≤y and (r,W)=1. Then Σ_{d|m,(d,W)=1}μ(d)L(D/d) equals Λ(r) for r>1 and log D+c for r=1. In the discrete part one can use Σ_{k smooth}Σ_{r≥1}Λ(r)f(hkr) up to terms supported on smooth m (including r=1). For each smooth m the surplus weights cost O(log x) before f, since Σ_{q^j|m}log q=log m. Summing over h|W, their total cost is ≤ x^(s+o(1)) for any s between 1−1/A and 1/2: use 1_{hk≤2x}≤(2x/(hk))^s and the products ∏(1+p^(−s)) and ∏(1−p^(−s))^(−1), both x^o(1) by A(1−s)<1.

For each h,k replace the sum against Λ by I/(hk). By Abel the error is O(Q(D)(x/(hk))^σ/log x), by variation of f and 2x/(hk)≤D; if 2x/(hk)<1 the bound follows from the size of the integral alone. On summing, use h^(−σ)≤H₀^(s−σ) h^(−s). The previous products give a cost O(Q(D)x^σ H₀^(s−σ)x^o(1)). Finally the original continuous coefficient of each I/h is Σ_{(d,W)=1} μ(d)L(D/d)/d, while the new one is Σ_{k smooth}1/k. Their absolute difference is (W/φ_E(W))(1−B) by 7686 and by 7710 equals x^(−β/A+o(1)). Even summing 1/h over all divisors of W, its cost is x^(1−β/A+o(1)), with exponent below 1/2 by the hypothesis on A. The three savings have a fixed margin, whence some η>0. This reduction does not give an inductive start for Q, since the target inequality of the tent is one-sided and the meshes h<H₀ are not yet controlled.

### The polylogarithmic sieve preserves all the excursions needed to decide RH

Let Θ be the supremum of the real parts of the non-trivial zeros. For every fixed 1<A<2β₋, y=C(log x)^A, uniformly over the cuts of 7650, the residue of 7610 over (n,W)>1 is O(x^(Θ−η)) for some η>0 (η may be reduced at each step). In particular it is O(√x) under RH. Without RH the error stays below exterior excursions chosen sufficiently close to Θ. This is an enlargement of the sieve as an equivalent criterion; it does not claim unconditional O(√x) for the removed sector.

Proof for h<2x/D. Fix s with 1−1/A<s<1/2. For every τ>Θ close to Θ, M(u)≪u^τ holds by Mertens' theorem in a zero-free half-plane, as in ROUND_279_A; if Θ=1 use τ=1 trivially. By convolution with the indicator of the smooth k, the partial sum of μ(d)1_{(d,W)=1} up to U is ≪U^τ x^o(1), using Σ_{k smooth} k^(−s)=x^o(1). On each band d∈[U,2U] the weight E(hd) has modulus and total variation O(1/log x) independently of h,U. For the variation, write F(u)=H(u)/log(xu) extended by zero and t=hd/x. Differentiating with respect to log t gives Σ_j (j t)F′(jt)+(1/t)∫F. This is the quadrature discrepancy of G(u)=uF′(u), since ∫G=−∫F. Its modulus is O(Var G)=O(1/log x) by the first-order rule, counting the jumps at the three vertices. Differentiation is almost everywhere and E is locally absolutely continuous. The modulus bound follows from 7731. Since L(D/d) is positive decreasing in d, by Abel the band costs ≪x^o(1) U^τ L(D/U) for each h. The dyadic sum is O(D^τ) before the factor x^o(1), using the logarithmic growth of L and its fifth-order decay. The number of admissible h is ≤(2x/D)^s Σ_{h|W}h^(−s)= (x/D)^s x^o(1). The exponent βτ+(1−β)s remains, strictly smaller than Θ for τ close enough to Θ, uniformly in β.

For the large meshes use 7741 and Q(D)≪D^(Θ−1/2+δ) by the explicit formula of 7027 (for Θ=1 Chebyshev suffices). The exponent is also <Θ, even if Θ=1/2 by taking δ small. The density deficit of 7710 costs x^(1−β/A+o(1)), below root scale. In the full quadrature without W the cost is O(D²/(x log x)+I/D³)=O(x^(1/2−η)) by β₊<3/4. The excluded prime powers of W cost at most a polylogarithm. Subtracting comparators gives the result.

Moreover one can require simultaneously (n,W)=1 and a>x^α: repeat the calibration 7700, whose estimate of the interior only uses that y is polylogarithmic, log y=o(log x), and the PNT. The coprime interior sector is exactly zero for the new D. Under RH the coprime exterior is O(√x) by 7567 and the previous estimate. If Θ>1/2, choose σ between max(1/2,Θ−η) and Θ and a zero with real part >σ. By 7567 the selected prime centres have positive excursions of J larger than any multiple of x^σ along a subsequence. The quadrature and the removed sector, even with variable D, cannot absorb them. Hence the one-sided ceiling O_δ(x^(1/2+δ)) for every δ>0 on the coprime exterior of this enlarged primorial at the two-gap centres suffices. That ceiling remains open.

### The interior cut absorbs the continuous deficit and allows sieving up to C(log x)²

For y=C(log x)^A, 1<A≤2, there exists a D in the band of 7650 computable from the interior data and the mass B of 7686 such that the one-sided ceiling O_δ(x^(1/2+δ)) on the same coprime exterior sector suffices to decide RH. The correct calibration is to equate the coprime interior contribution to I(1−B), which may exceed root scale. In particular the barrier A=2β of 7710 does not restrict this joint criterion.

Details. Let r=1−1/A. For the discrepancy E_W of the quadrature of the coprime comparator relative to IB, if Θ>r one obtains E_W=O(x^(Θ−η)) for some η>0; if Θ=r=1/2 one obtains O_δ(x^(1/2+δ)) for every δ>0. For h<2x/D repeat 7751 with r<s<τ, τ>Θ arbitrarily close (or τ=1 for Θ=1), obtaining x^(βτ+(1−β)s+o(1)). For h≥H₀=2x/D use the decomposition of 7741 and Abel with |ψ(u)−u|≪u^τ (including the trivial τ=1), giving the same exponent by Σ_{h≥H₀,h|W}h^(−τ)≤H₀^(s−τ)x^o(1). The cost of the smooth m is x^(s+o(1)). The adjustment of the continuous coefficients in this last stretch NOW carries the tail of 1/h: it costs at most
    I (1−B)(W/φ_E(W)) H₀^(s−1) Σ_{h|W} h^(−s)
    ≤ x^[1−β/A−(1−β)(1−s)+o(1)].
Its exponent tends to r as s↓r. This uses 7710 and allows avoiding the larger cost of summing over all h. If Θ>r choose s close to r and τ close to Θ; if there is equality leave a margin δ. The band of β is compact in (0,1) and all these choices are uniform.

The total coprime contribution of the residue is J+I(1−B)−E_W up to the polylogarithmic cost of the excluded prime powers. At the endpoints D=x^β₋,x^β₊ the coprime interior contribution still has main terms of opposite signs by 7650/7700. Since I(1−B)=o(x/log x) uniformly by 7710, its difference with this target also has opposite signs. Both are continuous in D, for B by its convergent positive average and domination by 1, hence an interior root exists. With it, the coprime exterior contribution is J−E_W up to the polylogarithmic cost. Under RH the required ceiling holds even at A=2; with an exterior zero always Θ>r and the strict saving preserves positive excursions with exponent between max(Θ−η,1/2) and Θ as in 7751. An unconditional ceiling on the exterior is not obtained this way.

### The witness can be restricted to squarefree integers with at most 6 log log x primes

At the endpoint y=C(log x)^2 of 7761 one can impose simultaneously on the coprime exterior that n be squarefree and ω(n)≤6 log log x. It suffices to recalibrate D in the same band. An unconditional root bound for the integers removed at fixed D is not presumed.

Let U_D be the contribution of the coprime exterior violating either of the two conditions. Uniformly in D its absolute mass, grouped by n, is o(x/log x). To see this, the modulus of each grouped summand is O(τ(n)), since the active factors d>D satisfy |R(D/d)|≪log x and the weight is O(1/log x). If q²|n then q>y in the set considered; τ(q²m)≤3τ(m). Using Σ_{m≤v}τ(m)≪v log(2v) and Σ_{q>y prime}1/q²≪1/(y log y) by Chebyshev and Abel, the cost of the squares is O(x log x/(y log y))=o(x/log x). For the second exception, 2^ω(n)τ(n)≤τ₄(n) by comparison of local factors (2(j+1)≤binom(j+3,3) for j≥1). Summing τ₄ up to 2x costs O(x log³x) by counting quadruples. Hence the tail costs O(x(log x)^(3−6 log 2))=o(x/log x). These are estimates over all integers and admit any overlap of the exceptions.

Replace in 7761 the equation for D by «coprime interior + U_D = I(1−B)». Continuity and the strict signs at the two endpoints persist by the uniform absolute estimate. The sum remaining at the root is exactly J−E_W up to the small prime powers of the previous result. Under RH it satisfies the ceiling O_δ(x^(1/2+δ)); any exterior zero imposes larger excursions at the selected centres. The two families of four and six factors of 7676 both pass the restrictions.

The added datum U_D can be computed to precision O(√x) without values of μ(d) above x^(9/10): in Λ(n)−Σ_{d|n}μ(d)L(D/d), Λ can only survive in the exceptions for powers with base ≤√(2x); the accumulated error from truncating the comparator is ≪(x/log x)Σ_{d>x^(9/10)}(D/d)^5/d ≪x^(1/4) for D≤x^(3/4). Identifying ω(n) only requires divisions by primes ≤√(2x) and counting the remaining cofactor if any. The exact existence statement uses the full U_D.

### Test of the reach of recalibration: two families suffice, but the cut retains the excess

Work with the full residue of 7610 and β₋,β₊ of 7676. There exist two fixed families of balanced products of four and six primes, defined by intervals of exponents and of n/x, whose sum F_D has a unique root D_F in the band. The contribution of its complement also has a root D_C there. At any root of the complement, F_{D_C}=J(x)+O(√x). More precisely, with a constant K>0,
    log(D_F/D_C)=[J(x)+O(√x)] / [(K+o(1))x/log²x].
It is a proof that the apparent size of the surviving set under recalibration does not by itself measure progress on the sign.

Construction. Use the fixed narrow exponent bands of 7676. For k=4,6, restrict further 1≤n/x≤t_k≤1.1. The sum of H(n/x) is (c_k(t_k)+o(1))x/log x with c_k(t)=b_k∫₁ᵗH(u)du and b_k>0: it is the same iterated PNT of 7620 on an open subset of the simplex around (1/k,…,1/k), with boundary of measure zero and without diagonals in the main term. Hence two arbitrarily small positive constants in prescribed proportion can be chosen. Fix an interior β₀ and choose c₄,c₆ so that c₄(2−3β₀)+c₆(4−5β₀)=0. Then at the endpoints F_D has opposite signs with margins ≍x/log x, by the exact identity of 7676. Moreover, uniformly over the band,
    dF_D/dlog D=−(3c₄+5c₆+o(1))x/log²x.
Indeed for each active divisor v=D/d≤x^(−δ) by a fixed margin; vR′(v)=1+O(v⁵) by 7660, while the inactive ones vanish. This gives K=3c₄+5c₆ and proves uniqueness of D_F.

The full residue is J(x)+O(√x) uniformly by 7610 and J(x)=o(x/log x) by PNT. Thus the complement has at the endpoints the signs opposite to F_D and admits a root by continuity. Applying the mean value theorem to F between the two roots proves the formula. In particular controlling the one-sided excess is equivalent, at these centres and up to logarithmic factors, to bounding from above the oriented separation of the two cuts to relative precision x^(−1/2+o(1)) in the sense of bounds for every δ>0. Choosing D_F by computing only four and six factors leaves D_C uncontrolled: the latter also uses the primes of the window. An independent estimate of that separation is not obtained.

### At fixed dyadic centres the frequencies of the attained frontier do not cancel on coinciding

Return to H of 7567 without calibration. For the different observable P(x)=Σ_n Λ(n)H(n/x)−x∫H, if Θ>1/2 is attained, then the quadratic mean of P(2^j)/2^(jΘ) over j=1,…,N has a strictly positive limit. In particular a two-sided root-scale bound with arbitrarily small losses on this single sequence rules out every attained exterior frontier. The proof covers exact coincidences between ordinates modulo 2π/log 2 without assuming linear independence. Antecedents: 115 controls continuous intervals of translations and 193 uses a triangular profile for another symbol.

The Mellin transform of H is
    M(s)=∫H(u)u^(s−1)du=[1−(2^s+2^(1−s))/3]/[s(1−s)].
It is obtained by integrating twice by parts in w₁(u)u^(s−2). The explicit formula gives P(x)=−Σρ M(ρ)x^ρ+O(1) for x≥4. One justification is to integrate the formula for ψ against the derivative of the piecewise weight (or smooth H in log u and pass to the limit); the second derivatives as measures have uniformly bounded total mass under smoothing, giving the summable majorant O((1+|Imρ|)^(−2)) at fixed x; the trivial-zero terms add up to O(1) by support in [x/2,2x]. Normalizing by x^Θ leaves only the frontier with error o(1) by dominated convergence. At x=2^j group those ordinates by the class γ log 2 modulo 2π. Within a class the numerator of M is identical and nonzero, since 2^Θ+2^(1−Θ)<3 for 0<Θ<1 (the attained frontier satisfies Θ<1). Moreover Re[1/(ρ(1−ρ))]>0 since Re[ρ(1−ρ)]=Θ(1−Θ)+γ²>0. Thus no occupied class has zero coefficient. By mean orthogonality of distinct geometric progressions, the limit is the sum of squared moduli of the grouped coefficients; one passes from finite sums by absolute convergence. Under RH the formula itself gives P(2^j)=O(2^(j/2)). No one-sided excursion on that grid is inferred, nor detection if the exterior supremum is not attained.

### At the attained frontier a floor on dyadic runs suffices

For the same fixed tent P of 7794, if Θ>1/2 is attained, there exist ε>0 and a fixed integer L such that every sufficiently late stretch of L consecutive integers j contains one with P(2^j)<−ε·2^(jΘ). Thus a one-sided floor P(2^j)≥−C·2^(jσ), σ<Θ, even only on late runs of unbounded lengths, suffices to exclude that frontier. L and ε may depend on the zeros. This uses only centres 2^j, without changing the weight. Increasing density through Gevrey/Poisson was already investigated in entry 35430; that route is not repeated.

Proof. The grouped series g(j) of 7794 includes the minus sign of the explicit formula and satisfies P(2^j)/2^(jΘ)=g(j)+o(1). Its mean is the coefficient of the class γ log 2=0 modulo 2π. If that class exists, its numerator 1−(2^Θ+2^(1−Θ))/3 is real positive and the sum of the reciprocals of the denominators is real strictly positive by conjugation. Hence the mean is strictly NEGATIVE in the presence of exact resonance; in its absence it is zero. In both cases there is some integer j₀ with g(j₀)<0: otherwise g²≤||g||∞ g for j≥0 contradicts the positive quadratic mean of 7794.

To make the recurrence explicit without a Diophantine hypothesis, approximate g by a finite sum with uniform error less than |g(j₀)|/8. For its frequencies ω₁,…,ω_k the closure of the powers of the vector (exp(iω₁),…,exp(iω_k)) is a compact group, with every orbit dense in it. There is an open neighbourhood of the power j₀ where the finite sum falls below −|g(j₀)|/2; the backward translates of that neighbourhood by non-negative integers cover the group. By compactness a finite subcover gives a uniform maximal waiting time. Reincorporating the tail and the o(1) gives the statement. A positive-sign excursion is not needed, which the possible resonant mean does not guarantee by this argument. For unattained Θ a mechanism on this same fixed grid is still missing.

### A compact average per octave forces recurrent deficits even if the frontier is not attained

Let 0<a<log 2 and let U_i be independent uniform on [−a,a]. Put S_j=j log 2+Σ_{i≤j}U_i and Z_j(a)=E[e^(−S_j/2)P(exp S_j)] with the fixed tent of 7794. The data entering belong to a compact interval of log-scales of half-width aj around the octave. Under RH all Z_j(a) are uniformly bounded for large j by 7794. If there is any exterior zero, there exist arbitrarily small rational widths a for which there are R>1, c>0 and finite L such that every late block of L indices contains a j with Z_j(a)<−cR^j and another with Z_j(a)>cR^j. Thus it would suffice to prove, for each rational width, arbitrarily long late runs with a constant floor (even with floor −exp(o(j))). This does not claim the result for the pointwise tent at 2^j.

Indeed, after writing z=ρ−1/2 the explicit series now has bases
    λ_a(z)=2^z sinh(az)/(az),
and coefficients −M(ρ) with multiplicity. The error of the normalized explicit formula is O(exp(−j(log 2−a)/2)). One can integrate term by term by summability of M and compact support for each j. Given a right zero, for a sufficiently small its base has modulus >1. The left or critical bases have modulus ≤1 by the interpretation as expectation of exp(z(log 2+U)). On every compact interval of positive widths the moduli are O(1/|Im z|) at large height, uniformly; hence the maximum greater than one is attained among finitely many conjugate pairs even if the original supremum is not attained.

Choose a compact interval of widths, as close to zero as desired, where the chosen base exceeds 1 by a margin. Among the finitely many candidates, the real-analytic functions |λ_a(z)|² of two distinct zeros of the right half-plane with positive ordinate are not identical: at a=0 the value distinguishes the real parts, and for equal real part the second-order term distinguishes the ordinates through Re(z²). Moreover Im λ_a(z) does not vanish identically: if 2^z is real, the second-order term contains Im(z²)=2 Re(z) Im(z)≠0. Avoiding the finitely many exceptional points in that compact set leaves an open set containing rationals. The dominant pair is unique, with non-real base and modulus R separated from the others. Its coefficient does not vanish by 7794. After dividing by R^j a cosine of positive amplitude remains, with fixed phase, plus o(1). If the rotation is rational it has period ≥3 and both signs by zero mean; if irrational its orbit is dense. In both cases there is return with bounded waiting to values of both signs bounded away from zero. This proves the statement. Antecedents: 115 and entry 35434 penalize heights by Gaussians; here the integer step introduces phase resonances and the iterated average uses only displacements bounded per step. The arithmetic bound for these averages remains open.

### Five positive prime averages give a Hankel defect without phase or subtraction of the integral

Let A_j=E[exp(−S_j/2) Σ_n Λ(n) H(n/exp S_j)] of 7810, B=E exp((log 2+U₁)/2)>1 and I₀=∫H. Then RH is equivalent to: for each rational a∈(0,log 2) there are arbitrarily large indices j with
    det[A_{j+r+s}]_{r,s=0,1,2} ≥ −A_j.
