Only five nearby readings are used and no density is subtracted in the inequality. An exterior zero forces, for some rational width, the quotient of the determinant by A_j to tend to minus infinity at ALL indices, even with unattained frontier. The pending step is to prove the subsequential floor for these arithmetic sums; positivity of the entries does not give it.

Proof. A_j=I₀B^j+Z_j exactly. Under RH in fact Z_j→0 exponentially for fixed a: the bases on the critical line have modulus |sinc(aγ)|<1 (here sinc(t)=sin(t)/t), tend to zero in height and no γ is zero. The series is absolutely summable and the trivial remainder in 7810 also decreases. On expanding the determinant by columns as a sum of a rank-one matrix and errors, at most one column of size O(B^j) and at least two of size o(1) survive. Hence the quotient by A_j tends to zero.

In the exterior case use the width and the unique pair of 7810, with λ non-real, |λ|=R>1 and nonzero complex coefficient c. R<B since at the attained maximum Re z<1/2, and log 2+U is strictly positive. For v(t)=(1,t,t²)^T the matrix is a sum of three rank-one matrices, with vectors v(B),v(λ),v(λ̄) and coefficients I₀B^j,cλ^j,conj(cλ^j), plus a matrix o(R^j) in each entry. By multilinearity and rank one, the error of the determinant is o(B^j R^(2j)); with two columns of the B term it vanishes exactly. The main determinant is I₀B^j |c|² R^(2j) times the square of the Vandermonde in B,λ,λ̄. Dividing by A_j~I₀ B^j leaves
    det/A_j = −[4 |c|² (Im λ)² |B−λ|⁴+o(1)] R^(2j).
The phase disappears exactly. The condition does not claim Hankel positivity at each index under RH; the floor −A_j leaves the necessary margin.

### Unconditional Hankel floor for verified widths and strict sign of the defect

With G=3·10^12, the height certified by Platt–Trudgian (entry Z2, ROUND_364_A), the floor det≥−A_j of 7820 holds eventually for each 2/G≤a<log 2, without hypotheses on the zeros above G. Moreover, for 2/G≤a≤0.08 the determinant is strictly negative for all sufficiently large j and its quotient by A_j tends to zero. Thus imposing a positive semidefinite Hankel matrix as an elementary route would be false in the very arithmetic of ζ.

Indeed for |γ|>G the base of 7810 has modulus ≤√2 cosh(a/2)/(aG)≤√2 cosh((log 2)/2)/2=3/4. For |γ|≤G all bases are critical and have modulus |sin(aγ)/(aγ)|<1. They are finitely many; the remainder of the explicit formula also decreases exponentially for fixed a. Hence Z_j=o(1) and det/A_j→0 as in 7820.

On the shorter subinterval, the first pair, with ordinate γ₁∈(14.13,14.14) (enclosure in ROUND_409_A), has modulus R₁≥1−(0.08·14.14)²/6>0.78. It is the unique maximal pair: |sinc t| decreases on (0,π) and for t≥π is bounded by 1/π. The unverified tail has modulus ≤3/4. The normalized trivial remainder of 7810 has base ≤exp(−(log 2−0.08)/2)<0.74. The base λ₁ is non-real because 3π<γ₁ log 2<4π. Hence Z_j=cλ₁^j+conj(cλ₁^j)+o(R₁^j), with c≠0. The Vandermonde expansion of 7820 also holds here with 0<R₁<1 and gives det/A_j∼−4|c|²(Im λ₁)²|B−λ₁|⁴ R₁^(2j). Uniformity down to a=0 is not obtained; the pending part of the criterion still contains arbitrarily small widths.

### The exponential defect requires three distinct primes separated in absolute value

One can replace Λ by primes only in the five readings of 7820 and remove from the expansion of the determinant all triples containing a pair at distance ≤exp(√j). If D_j^sep is the remaining balance and A_j^p the positive reading with primes only, RH is equivalent to the floor D_j^sep/A_j^p≥−exp(2√j) at arbitrarily large indices for each rational width. The error of removing those triples is unconditional and is estimated in absolute value; in particular twin pairs or pairs with gaps polynomial in j cannot by themselves create the exponential defect.

Indeed, the difference A_j−A_j^p is O(1) uniformly for large j: by Chebyshev Σ_{p^k≤2u,k≥2}log p≪√u (separate squares and bound the higher powers by O(u^(1/3)log²u)). At each scale multiply by u^(−1/2)H(p^k/u) and average. Under RH the matrix of prime readings is therefore the sum of the same rank-one term and O(1) entrywise; the normalized determinant is O(1) by multilinearity. If there is an exterior zero choose the width of 7820. The O(1) is o(R^j) and the same Vandermonde computation keeps the exponential negative main term. By PNT over the whole physical band, for each fixed width A_{j+i}^p∼I₀B^(j+i) for 0≤i≤4, without RH (the minimal scale grows).

Write w_i(p)=(log p)E[exp(−S_i/2)H(p/exp S_i)] and expand by permutations and then by primes in each row. For i=j,…,j+4 the support implies p≤exp(O(j)), and w_i(p)≤C log p/√p because in every active sample exp S_i∈[p/2,2p]. Hence Σ_p w_i(p)^2≪j³ even summing the majorant over all integers. For an integer shift h, Cauchy–Schwarz (extend by zero outside primes) gives Σ_p w_i(p)w_l(p+h)≪j³ uniformly in h. Summing the O(exp(√j)) permitted shifts and leaving the third prime free costs O(j³exp(√j) A_j^p), even summing the moduli of the six permutations and the three pairs. This is o(exp(2√j) A_j^p) and also o(R^(2j) A_j^p) for every R>1. This proves both directions. The estimate does not determine the sign of the separated triples nor their balance at the required precision.

### Only counts in cells of length x^(11/20), with error below root scale

Fix c=9/20 and replace each prime p by t(p)=(⌊p^c⌋+1/2)^(1/c), also inside its logarithmic weight. Uniformly for large x, the sum Σ_p log p H(p/x) changes by O(x^0.49). Thus only the prime counts between m^(20/9) and (m+1)^(20/9) suffice, without products or interior moments. The distinction from ROUND_224_A (counts between squares) is that the cells exceed √x by a fixed power and arithmetic cancellation in the rounding is required.

Detail of the cancellation. On every subband of [X,2X], uniformly in 1≤h≤X^.07, one has |Σ Λ(n)e(h n^c)|≪_ε X^(.91+ε), e(t)=exp(2πit). Use Vaughan's identity with U=V=X^.2, decomposing dyadically and the logarithm by parts. In type I the outer divisor is ≤X^.4 and its coefficients O_ε(X^ε); with F=h X^c van der Corput's second-derivative test in the inner variable gives O(√F+(X/d)/√F). In type II both variables exceed X^.2 and have coefficients O_ε(X^ε). Let M≥N be their dyadic lengths, MN comparable to X. Cauchy in the long variable and expansion of the pairs in the short one give, after dividing by X^(1+ε), a bound O((1/N+√F/M+1/√F)^(1/2)). For a pair with difference l>0, the second derivative in the long variable has modulus comparable to Fl/(NM²); the sum costs O(√(Fl/N)+M/√(Fl/N)), also over the interval imposed by the two product constraints. Summing over l and adding the diagonal gives the cited bound. With X^.45≤F≤X^.52 these exponents leave the announced margin. The identity used is Λ=Λ_≤V+μ_≤U*log−μ_≤U*1*Λ_≤V+(μ_>U*1)*Λ_>V, with * Dirichlet convolution. Removing higher powers and removing log p by Abel preserves the ceiling for the unweighted prime count. Erdős–Turán with cut X^.07, applied to the fractional parts of p^c on each subinterval, and the discrepancy inequality for the bounded-variation function u−1/2, give
    |Σ_p ({p^c}−1/2)| ≪ X^.935
on every subinterval of the octave (absorbing logarithms with margin).

For f(t)=log t H(t/x), on each smooth segment |f′|≪log x/x and |f″|≪log x/x² in the band. The displacement t(p)−p is (1/2−{p^c})p^(1−c)/c+O(x^(1−2c)). Outside the cells crossing the three vertices, the linear term is bounded by Abel, since f′(p)p^(1−c) has variation and modulus O(x^(−c)log x). The cost is O(x^(.935−c)log x); the aggregated Taylor remainder costs O(x^(1−2c)log x). The three exceptional cells cost the same by Lipschitz and counting integers. The O(x^.49) results. After normalizing and averaging as in 7810 the error of each prime reading even decreases as O(exp(−.01j(log 2−a))). By 7840 the five-prime-reading criterion preserves both regimes when using only these counts (subexponential normalized floor, for example −exp(√j), for the full determinant). The precision has been proved for the rounding; the inequality between the counts remains open.

### For the rounded counts a strictly positive sign on a subsequence suffices

Let V_j(a) be the rounded prime reading of 7848 (each prime also replaced in the logarithm by the centre of its cell). RH is equivalent to: for each rational 0<a<1/1000 there are arbitrarily large j with det[V_{j+r+s}]_{0≤r,s≤2}>0. Under RH both signs recur with bounded waiting for each of those widths. This differs from the matrix with all powers of 7832: in the prime reading, removing the squares introduces a nonzero constant component that changes the main term of the determinant.

Indeed, assuming RH, by Abel with θ(t)=t+O(√t log²t),
    Σ_p log p H(p²/x)=√x C₂+O(x^(1/4)log²x),   C₂=∫₀^∞ H(v²)dv>0.
The exponents ≥3 cost O(x^(1/3)log²x). In the normalized and averaged reading, both error bounds and the rounding of 7848 are O(q^j) for some q≤0.995: in particular exp(−.01(log 2−.001))<0.994. The formula of 7810 under RH then gives
    V_j=I₀B^j−C₂+cλ^j+conj(cλ^j)+o(R^j),
with λ=2^(iγ₁)sinc(aγ₁), R=|λ|>0.9999 and c≠0. The first pair is unique by the monotonicity of sinc on its first lobe and the ceiling 1/π on the others; the phase γ₁ log 2 is not a multiple of π. The remaining series has strictly smaller maximal base for each fixed a. All margins exceed the rounding error.

Now expand the determinant in the four bases B,1,λ,conj(λ). The two main terms use B and 1 with one of the two complex bases. By Vandermonde, dividing by I₀ B^j R^j leaves
    2 Re[K (λ/R)^j]+o(1),  K=−C₂ c (1−B)²(λ−B)²(λ−1)² ≠0.
The terms B,λ,conj(λ) cost O(B^j R^(2j)) and any entry error costs o(B^j R^j) by the rank one of the pole. The non-real rotation visits values bounded away from zero of both signs with bounded waiting, as in 7810. In the absence of RH choose a rational width smaller than 1/1000 that isolates the exterior pair of 7810. Removing powers costs only O(1) per reading, and the rounding o(1); thus 7820 keeps its strictly negative main term at all sufficiently large indices. The converse needs no assumption on the location of the other zeros. An unconditional reason for the existence of positive determinants in the five count readings is still pending.

### Simultaneous signs without RH for the counts in the verified corridor

For G=3·10¹² and all widths 2/G≤a≤10^(−3), in every sufficiently late block of 17 indices there is one and the same index with strictly positive determinant of V for ALL those a, and another with negative sign for all. There is no effective threshold in j in this argument. Unlike 7832 these are the rounded counts of simple primes, whose sign does oscillate. Only the height verification Z2 is used.

To control the squares without RH put H₂(u)=H(u²) and replace Σ_p log p H₂(p/√x) by Σ_n Λ(n)H₂(n/√x) with error O(x^(1/4)log² x) by Chebyshev. The explicit formula of 7794 applied to H₂ has mass C₂ and identical absolute convergence (its Mellin transform is M(s/2)/2). After dividing by √x and averaging, the base of each zero is 2^w sinh(aw)/(aw), w=(ρ−1)/2. Up to height G its modulus is ≤exp(−(log 2−.001)/4)<.85. Above G, t=a|γ|/2≥1; use |sin t|/t≤sin 1 for t≥1 and |a Re w|≤.001/2. Writing |sinh(aw)|²=sin²t+sinh²(a Re w) and noting |aw|≥t and |2^w|≤1, a bound <.85 also remains. The trivial contribution of the formula weighs O(exp(−j(log 2−.001)/2)). Thus the squares reading is C₂+O(.9^j) uniformly in this corridor. The powers ≥3 and the rounding still have base <.995.

In the term with Λ of 7832 the first pair dominates uniformly: the verified critical zeros are finitely many, the modulus inequality against the first is strict on the compact set of a, and the unverified tail has base ≤3/4. One therefore obtains the final formula of 7858 with uniform o(1), with phase of λ/R equal to γ₁ log 2 independent of a. Also arg K(a) stays within 0.01 radians of arg K(0), using only the algebraic expression of K in 7858 at a=0, without passing to the limit in the series of zeros. In detail, |λ(a)−λ(0)|<0.0001 by Taylor, |B(a)−√2|<0.0001 by B=√2 sinh(a/2)/(a/2), Re λ(a)<0 on the whole interval. The two complex factors B−λ and λ−1 are at distance ≥1 from the origin and vary by less than 0.0002; their arguments vary by less than 0.001 each and appear squared. The other factors do not change argument.

Finally 0.73<2γ₁ log 2−6π<0.76 (use 14.13<γ₁<14.14). The nine points of step 2 in a block of 17 indices form on the circle a mesh with maximal gap less than 0.76: eight steps add up to between 5.84 and 6.08. One falls at distance <0.38 from the direction maximizing the cosine with K(0), and another from the one minimizing it. The same indices give opposite signs uniformly in a, by the angular margin and the uniform error. The compact set stays away from zero; neither the starting index nor the domain of the first frequency is extrapolated to the remaining interval.

### Sign witnesses at the pointwise octave under RH via two finite arithmetic computations

Under RH there exist ε>0 and finite L such that in every late block of L indices there is a j with positive determinant simultaneously for 0≤a≤ε/√j, and another index with negative determinant on its corresponding band. a=0 and the rounded reading in the cells of 7848 are included. Here the separation by the first zero ceases to be uniform. Instead, two certified values of the full series on the critical line and the recurrence of their phases are used. It is an implication under RH, not an unconditional advance down to a=0.

Let B₀=√2, g(k)=−Σρ M(ρ)exp(ikγ log 2), e(k)=g(k)−C₂. Under RH it is an absolutely convergent series plus the constant. After removing the exact pole I₀B(a)^(j+i), the five entries V_{j+i}(a) differ from e(j+i) by an arbitrarily small amount uniformly for 0≤a≤ε/√j and i≤4, taking first ε small and then j large. Indeed the factor per frequency is sinc(aγ)^(j+i); on a finite list 0≤1−sinc(aγ)^(j+i)≪ε²γ² for large j. The tail has modulus bounded by the absolute sum, and the errors from squares, powers and rounding of 7858 decrease uniformly. The pole is not approximated by B₀^j. Applying column and row differences with the vectors (1,0,0), (−B,1,0), (0,−B,1) of determinant one, the pole contributes only to the first diagonal entry. Dividing by I₀B^j leaves, up to an arbitrarily small error, d(j)=f(j)f(j+2)−f(j+1)^2, f(k)=e(k+2)−2B₀e(k+1)+2e(k), since B(a)→B₀ and the error entries are bounded.

For k=2,…,8, x=2^k, the explicit formula of 7794 with all trivial zeros gives
    e(k)=[Σ_{p^h≤2x}log p · max(0,min(2p^h−x,2x−p^h))/(3p^h) −x log(2)/3 + Σ_{m≥1}M(−2m)x^(−2m)]/√x−C₂.
∫H=M(1)=log(2)/3 and C₂=2(1−2√2/3) were used. Truncating at m=12 the absolute tail costs ≤(4/3)(2/x)^26, since |M(−2m)|≤2^(2m). Interval evaluation (mpmath.iv, 30 decimals, primes by trial division up to the root): 0.00053589<d(2)<0.00053590 and −0.00147654<d(4)<−0.00147652. These signs are for the determinant of the difference block of the series, not those of a supposed asymptotic computation at indices 2 and 4. By compact recurrence of the phases as in 7802, the five entries e(j+i) approximate to any fixed precision both respective blocks with bounded waiting. The certified margins and the uniform approximation for a≤ε/√j preserve the two signs. Linear independence of the ordinates is not needed.

### A single favourable index for all widths down to zero via a symmetric difference

For V_j of 7858, E the index shift at fixed width, B=B(a), take
    Y_j=K+[1+B²−B(E+E^(−1))]V_j,   T_j=Y_{j−1}Y_{j+1}−Y_j².
RH is equivalent to the existence of constants K>0, 0<a₀≤.001 and arbitrarily large indices j such that T_j(a)>0 SIMULTANEOUSLY for 0≤a≤a₀. Under RH those indices have bounded waiting. In the absence of RH every K and every such interval contain a fixed width with T_j<0 eventually. The determinant is changed, but five rounded readings still suffice. This simultaneity is not claimed for the unmodified determinant of 7858.

Proof. Write F_B(z)=1+B²−B(z+z^(−1)), D(z)=z+z^(−1)−2. The pole B is annihilated. Under RH the readings minus the pole are −C₂−Σ m_γ λ_γ^j+O(.995^j), uniformly in 0≤a≤.001, by 7858; m_γ=M(1/2+iγ)>0 by 7794, summable with multiplicities. λ_γ=exp(iγ log 2)sinc(aγ). Put R₁=|λ_{γ₁}|>.9999. For all zeros |λ_γ|≤R₁ by the first lobe and the ceiling 1/π. In the second difference D(E)Y the coefficient of the frequency at a=0, after extracting exp(ijγ log 2), is −m_γ D(z)F_B(z)≥0, since D(z)=2cos(γ log 2)−2 and F_B(z)=|B−z|² for |z|=1. For the first pair it is strictly positive. Call d>0 the contribution of that pair with aligned phases at a=0.

Choose a finite list of pairs with tail mass so small that its contribution to D(E)Y is <d R₁^j/8. This is uniform: expand the Laurent polynomial with shifts from −2 to 2, bound each |λ|^(j+i)≤R₁^(j−2) and use bounded coefficients (also if λ=0). For that list choose a₀>0 so small that all the sinc are positive and D(λ)F_B(λ) is so close to its value at zero that the sum of errors, with weights m_γ, is <d/8 before the factor R₁^j. By compact recurrence there are indices with bounded waiting where all the phases exp(ijγ log 2) of the list are close enough to 1 to cost another dR₁^j/8. The factors sinc(aγ)^j are non-negative and ≤R₁^j; that of the first pair is exactly R₁^j. One deduces D(E)Y_j≥dR₁^j/2 at those sufficiently late indices, simultaneously down to zero.

Write Y_j=K−C₂(1−B)²+u_j. For i=−1,0,1 one has |u_{j+i}|≤C R₁^j uniformly, by the same shift argument. Thus T_j=[K−C₂(1−B)²]D(E)Y_j+u_{j−1}u_{j+1}−u_j². Choose fixed K large enough for the first term to exceed 2C²R₁^(2j). For the converse use the dominant non-real pair of 7810 at some rational within the interval. F_B(λ)≠0 since its roots are B and 1/B. The pole disappears and the pair grows over the constant and the error from squares/rounding. The 2×2 determinant has main term −4|cF_B(λ)|²(Im λ)²R^(2j−2) by Vandermonde. This contradicts any common favourable subsequence. The unconditional existence of such arithmetic indices remains open.

### Unconditional transport from width zero via three prime masses

Let x=2^j, ℓ=log 2, q(a)=sinh(a/2)/(a/2) by continuity at zero and Ω(x)=(log x/log log x)^(1/3). There exists κ>0 such that for the rounded counts of 7848 one has unconditionally
    V_j(a)=q(a)^j V_j(0)+o(1)
uniformly for 0≤a≤x^(−1/4)exp(κΩ(x))/√j. In particular, if a=t x^(−1/4)/√j with fixed t, the difference WITHOUT rescaling tends to I₀ t²/24. This is an estimate of the entries, not of the signs of the determinants.

Identity at fixed cut. For the unrounded reading use g(t)=e^(−t/2)H(e^(−t)). By the two linear formulas of w₁, g″−g/4=(√2/3)(δ_{−ℓ}+δ_ℓ)−δ₀; the three jumps of the derivative are √u times the jump of w₁′ at u=2,1,1/2. Let U be the sum of j uniforms on [−a,a] and h=|U|. For any t, the symmetric average [g(t+h)+g(t−h)]/2 minus cosh(h/2)g(t) is the convolution of g″−g/4 with K_h(v)=sinh((h−|v|)/2) for |v|≤h, zero outside. This is verified by integrating the ordinary equation on both sides of t and holds also at the vertices by continuity. Hence the exact rescaled change for simple primes is the expectation of
    (√2/3)[N_h(x/2)+N_h(2x)]−N_h(x),
    N_h(X)=Σ_p (log p)/√p · K_h(log(p/X)).
E cosh(U/2)=q(a)^j was used. Only the primes near the three vertices intervene in the difference.

For h≤ja=o(1), replace dθ by dt in N_h(X). The continuous term is √X∫e^(v/2)K_h(v)dv and cancels in the combination by (√2/3)(2^(−1/2)+2^(1/2))=1. The remainder by Abel costs
    O(h X^(1/8)log X + √X h² exp(−cΩ(X))).
Indeed the variation of the weight on the interval is O(h/√X). The increments of θ(t)−t from the lower endpoint, at distances ≤O(Xh), cost O(X^(5/8)log X + Xh exp(−cΩ(X))) by the short PNT already verified in ROUND_238_A. Take expectations with E h²=ja²/3, E h≤a√j, and choose 2κ smaller than the exponential constant valid at the three scales. o(1) is obtained. The substitution by t(p) in the two readings only adds o(1) by 7848, since q(a)^j=1+o(1). Finally V_j(0)∼I₀√x by PNT and j log q(a)∼ja²/24 for a>0, giving the stated limit. The transport only covers a corridor that narrows with j; it does not prove pointwise positivity nor cover an arbitrarily small fixed positive width.

### Transport of the two eigenvalues that decide the sign with decreasing absolute error

Write the matrix of five counts of 7858 as [[v,bᵀ],[b,C]], with v=V_j(a)>0 and S_j(a)=C−bbᵀ/v. For certain κ,d>0 and x=2^j, unconditionally,
    ||S_j(a)−S_j(0)|| ≪ exp(−dΩ(x))
on 0≤a≤x^(−1/4)exp(κΩ(x))/√j. Hence each ordered eigenvalue changes by at most that absolute error, even if the other one is large. Since det of the full matrix is v·det S, a sign bounded away from zero in both eigenvalues at width zero transports to the whole corridor. More precisely it suffices that the smaller modulus exceed the constant of the bound multiplied by exp(−dΩ). This result does not guarantee the existence of that margin nor its orientation either.

Proof. The proof of 7904 for the five readings, reducing κ and d, gives O(exp(−dΩ)) instead of o(1): the first term is O(x^(−1/8)exp(O(κΩ))log x), the second O(exp((O(κ)−c)Ω)), and the rounding O(x^(−.01+o(1))). The four finite shifts only modify constants. Thus the matrix at width a is q^j D_q H_j(0)D_q+O(exp(−dΩ)) in norm, D_q=diag(1,q,q²), H_j(0) the full matrix. Taking S preserves this error: all pivots are ≍√x and all entries O(√x), so that, on subtracting bbᵀ/v between matrices, each perturbation of b or of v is multiplied by a bounded factor. Consequently S_j(a)=q^j diag(q,q²) S_j(0) diag(q,q²)+O(exp(−dΩ)).

To remove the rescaling without losing precision, the version of the PNT with classical remainder gives V_{j+i}(0)=I₀√(2^(j+i))+O(√x exp(−c₁√log x)) for 0≤i≤4. Abel is applied to θ(t) with the weight H and the rounding of 7848 is added. The main term is rank one and its Schur complement is zero, hence ||S_j(0)||≪√x exp(−c₁√log x) by the same pivot stability. Since q^(j+4)−1≪x^(−1/2)exp(2κΩ), the additional correction is O(exp(2κΩ−c₁√log x)), absorbable. The variational principle for symmetric matrices gives the result on the eigenvalues. The precision obtained is on the object that decides the sign and does not depend on an RH bound for the second minor.

### Factorial recurrence at root precision with a single boundary term in the tail

For the fixed tent P of 7794, K≥2 an even integer, U=x/K≥2, one has without RH
    P(x)=Σ_{k=2}^K (−1)^k P(x/k) − P(U)/2 + O(U²/x + log(2x)/x).
In particular even K comparable to x^(1/4) eliminates all arguments below U≍x^(3/4) paying O(√x); if K/x^(1/4)→∞ the remainder is o(√x) for U≥2. The sign and the factor 1/2 of the boundary are preserved. The factorial alternating sum already appears in index 35708; the specific part here is the uniform truncation error for this tent and its consequence at the necessary scales.

Indeed Σ_{k≥1}(−1)^(k−1)Σ_n Λ(n)H(kn/x)=Σ_n log n [H(n/x)−2H(2n/x)] by Σ_{d|n}Λ(d)=log n. The two quadrature integrals give x I₀ log 2 together; the discrepancies add up to O(log(2x)/x) by the variation of the first derivative of the scaled weight as in 7577. The continuous part of the sum of P(x/k) equals x I₀ Σ(−1)^(k−1)/k=x I₀ log 2. The infinite recurrence with that error results.

For each n, with f(t)=H(nt/x), one has Σ_{k>K}(−1)^k f(k)=−f(K)/2+O((n/x) Var(H′)) for even K. Proof: twice that tail plus f(K) is the alternating sum of consecutive increments f(k)−f(k+1) from K (up to global sign), bounded by the variation of the increments and its first modulus. Both cost O((n/x) Var H′) by integration over intervals of length one. Only n≤2U intervene, so Σ_{n≤2U} nΛ(n)/x≪U²/x by Chebyshev. For the continuum f(k)=xI₀/k, the variation and the first modulus of the increments from K cost O(x/K²). Subtracting finishes the proof. The cost of the boundary alone is not estimated by √x.

Another exact consequence of the same pairing is P(x)=∫₀^(x/2) 1_{⌊x/u⌋ even}P′(u)du+O(log(2x)/x), by continuity and summing the differences of each pair. If |√u P′(u)| is majorized by its supremum up to x/2, the cost normalized by √x is at most that supremum times 2Σ_{m≥1}[(2m)^(−1/2)−(2m+1)^(−1/2)]<1: each integral of t^(−3/2) over [2m,2m+1] is strictly smaller than the integral over [2m−1,2m], and the total integral from 1 equals 2. This coefficient transfers control of the derivative to the value; it does not give a contraction of P in one and the same norm. The cancellation of the retained terms remains pending.

### Two boundary values and cancellation at the vertices: the tail drops below root with only x^0.23 terms

Choose even K comparable to x^0.23, U=x/K, U'=x/(K+1). Without RH,
    P(x)=Σ_{k=2}^K (−1)^k P(x/k) − [P(U)+P(U')]/4 + O(x^0.495).
The regression on smaller scales only needs O(x^0.23) readings and the remainder is strictly below √x. The improvement over 7929 uses cancellation in the interior jumps that were estimated there by total variation.

Let w(t)=(−1)^⌊t⌋ and G its continuous primitive of period 2 and mean zero, G(K)=−1/2. For f(t)=H(nt/x), by two integrations by parts (the first with dw),
 Σ_{k>K}(−1)^k f(k)=−f(K)/2−f′(K+)/4+(1/2)∫_(K,∞) G(t)df′(t).
The absolutely continuous part of the integral is O((n/x)²): G has a bounded primitive and on the smooth segments H″ has finite variation and bounded modulus. The point masses are (n/x)[H′]_b G(bx/n) for b=1/2,1,2 with n<bU. Summing against Λ(n), the smooth remainders cost O(U³/x²) and the part n≤x^0.74 of the masses costs O(x^0.48). For larger n, G has an absolutely convergent Fourier series, without constant term and with coefficients O(h^(−2)) in exp(iπht). Truncating at h≤x^0.05 costs O((U²/x)x^(−0.05))=O(x^0.49).

For each non-constant mode and each N between x^0.74/2 and 2U, on any subinterval of [N,2N] one has
    |Σ Λ(n) exp(iπhbx/n)| ≪_ε N x^(−0.055+ε).
The type I/II proof of 7848 applies with parameters N^0.2 and phase scale F=hbx/N between constants times x^0.23 and x^0.31. In type I the second derivative in the inner variable gives the relative bounds N^(−0.6)√F+F^(−1/2). In type II, M≥L, ML≍N, L≫N^0.2, the relative bound is O_ε(x^ε (1/L+√F/M+1/√F)^(1/2)). Indeed the phase difference for two values of the short variable at distance l has second derivative in the long one comparable in modulus to Fl/(LM²), also for the reciprocal phase. The worst of the three savings is at least x^(−0.0575) up to constants. Partial summation incorporates n/x and the dyadic bands cost a logarithm; the error of the retained modes is O_ε(x^(0.54−0.055+ε)). For the continuum f(t)=I₀x/t the same integrations with the bounded primitive of G leave O(x/K³).

Finally replace f′(K+) by f(K+1)−f(K). Away from the crossed vertices the total Taylor cost is O(U³/x²). For each crossed vertex there are O(1+U/K) integers n and the slope discrepancy costs O((U/x)log x) per integer with its weight. The continuum also costs O(x/K³). All are below the announced exponent. Substituting in the infinite recurrence of 7929 gives the two boundary terms with the same sign. No root bound has been assumed for any of the retained P.

### Only j dilations for the averaged reading, uniformly down to widths 200/j

Put L_j(k)=E[exp(−S_j/2)P(exp(S_j)/k)], with the same distribution of S_j in all terms. There exist absolute c,C>0 such that, for large j and 200/j≤a≤.001, without RH,
    |Σ_{k=1}^j (−1)^(k−1) w_{j,k} L_j(k)| ≤ C exp(−cj),
    w_{j,k}=Σ_{r=k−1}^{j−1} binom(r,k−1)/2^(r+1).
The coefficient of the first term is 1−2^(−j); the others lie between zero and one. For the normalized reading of octave j therefore O(log x) dilations suffice, x=2^j, and the smallest central scale is x/j. It is not a pointwise improvement of the exponent of 7941 at width zero. The constants do not depend on a catalogue of verified zeros.

Proof. For Re s>0 the elementary acceleration of η(s) uses differences b_r(s)=Σ_{m=0}^r(−1)^m binom(r,m)(m+1)^(−s). By Laplace,
    Γ(s)b_r(s)=∫₀^∞ t^(s−1)e^(−t)(1−e^(−t))^r dt.
Summing with weights 2^(−r−1) gives Γ(s)η(s), first by Dirichlet for Re s>1 and then by continuation (the inner geometric sum gives 1/(1+e^(−t))). In 0<Re s<1, r≥1, the modulus of the integral is uniformly bounded: use (1−e^(−t))≤t on (0,1) and the exponential tail on (1,∞). The truncation η_j(s)=Σ_{k≤j}(−1)^(k−1)w_{j,k}k^(−s) thus has error ≤C2^(−j)/|Γ(s)|. Moreover |η_j(s)|≤j on the whole strip because Σ_{r≥m} binom(r,m)/2^(r+1)=1.

The formula of 7794 for L_j(k) has as component −M(ρ) λ_a(ρ−1/2)^j k^(−ρ); its remainder is O(exp(−j(log 2−.001)/2)) uniform in k≤j since exp(S_j)/k≥4 eventually. In |Imρ|≤j/10 use η(ρ)=0 and uniform Stirling for 1/Γ: |η_j(ρ)|≪2^(−j)(1+j)^2 exp(πj/20). Also |λ_a|≤exp((log 2+.001)/2), hence the total exponent is negative, with margin log 2−(log 2+.001)/2−π/20>0. At higher heights, |λ_a|≤√2 cosh(.001/2)/(a j/10)<0.08, by ja≥200, and |η_j|≤j suffices. The sum of |M(ρ)| is finite by 7794. These two ceilings and the trivial remainder give the inequality. The acceleration uses the factorial cancellation already recorded in 35708; here the error of its finite truncation is estimated for the averages of 7810. The identity also preserves the modes of exterior zeros: by itself it gives neither a contraction nor the sign of the readings.

### What the Euler error preserves: asymptotic per zero and linear cost of truncation

If ρ=β+iγ is any fixed non-trivial zero, the finite defect of 7957 has the complex equivalent
    η_N(ρ)=−2^(−N)(log N)^(ρ−1)/[(N+1)Γ(ρ)] · (1+o_ρ(1)).
In particular the modulus of the quotient of defects for ρ and 1−conj(ρ) is asymptotic to |Γ(1−conj(ρ))/Γ(ρ)| (log N)^(2β−1). The exponential rate 2^(−N) is the same on both sides; the difference between real parts appears in a power of log N.

Proof. In the integral of b_r of 7957 sum the geometric tail from r=N and put v=exp(−t). One obtains exactly
    η(s)−η_N(s)=2^(−N)/Γ(s) ∫₀¹ (−log v)^(s−1)(1−v)^N/(1+v) dv.
Scale u=(N+1)v. On u∈[N^(−1/2),√N] the quotient (−log v)/log N is bounded by positive constants and tends to 1 for fixed u, and (1−v)^N≤exp(−u/2). In the omitted lower part the normalized modulus is bounded because β<1. On v≥√N/(N+1) use (1−v)^(N/2)≤exp(−c√N) and (−log v)^(β−1)≤(1−v)^(β−1); the contribution is negligible even after multiplying by N and powers of log N. Dominated convergence and η(ρ)=0 give the equivalent.

Consequence for the readings: if there is an exterior zero, take a fixed width of 7810 with isolated maximum R>1 and pair ρ,conj(ρ). For N=⌊αj⌋ with fixed 0<α≤1, the Euler balance of the L_j(k), k≤N, has
    limsup |balance|^(1/j)=R·2^(−α).
Indeed, the unnormalized trivial term in P(exp S_j/k) is O((k exp(−S_j))²) by the support, so the total contribution is O(N³ exp(−(5/2)j(log 2−a))). Choose a<.001 as in 7957. This error is smaller than (R/2^α)^j. Truncate the series of zeros at a fixed height so large that the remaining bases have modulus <R/2^α with margin, using |η_N|≤N and the summability of |M|. On the finite list apply the previous equivalent; the bases of modulus smaller than R remain exponentially below the maximal pair. The dominant term is a cosine of phase j arg λ+γ log log N+constant, plus o(1) after removing its positive amplitude. Since arg λ is not a multiple of π and the increment of γ log log N tends to zero, the cosine has modulus bounded away from zero at at least one of every two sufficiently large indices. This proves the rate for 0<α≤1. In particular if α<log₂ R the truncated recurrence has no subexponential normalized error at that width. Another choice of weights is not excluded, nor is the existence of an exterior zero claimed.

### Positive physical remainder of the acceleration and threshold without octave averaging for the exponential weight

Change here the tent to P_e(x)=Σ_n Λ(n)exp(−n/x)−x. With the weights of 7957 and N≥1 one has the identity
 Σ_{k≤N}(−1)^(k−1)w_{N,k}P_e(x/k)
 = F(x)−x log 2 −2^(−N)[Σ_n Λ(n)g_N(n/x)−x∫₀^∞g_N(u)du],
    g_N(u)=(1−e^(−u))^N/(e^u+1),   F(x)=Σ_{m≥1}log m [e^(−m/x)−2e^(−2m/x)].
Neither RH nor a position of the zeros is presupposed. The accelerated geometric sum in z=e^(−u) is z/(1+z) times [1−((1−z)/2)^N]; integrating in u gives the continuous corrector and grouping by product gives F by the factorial identity of 7929. In particular the arithmetic error to be compared after multiplying by 2^N is a prime discrepancy with non-negative weight. With v=e^(−u), its integral mass is ∫₀¹(1−v)^N/(1+v)dv=1/(N+1)+O(1/N²). At u=log N+t one has N g_N(u)→exp(−t−e^(−t)); this identifies the physical scale around x log N, with width of order x.

There is c>0 such that, for N comparable to log x, the bracket is bounded unconditionally in modulus by O((x/N)exp(−c√log x)). Indeed PNT and Abel replace dψ by dt. For t≥√x use |ψ(t)−t|≪t exp(−c₁√log x) and ∫u|g_N′(u)|du≪log(2N)/N. For this last bound g_N is unimodal: the sign of the derivative with respect to v of v(1−v)^N/(1+v) is given by 1−(N+1)v−Nv². The maximum is O(1/N) and is attained at u=log N+O(1). Integrating by parts on the two branches gives the ceiling. For t<√x Chebyshev and g_N(t/x)≤(t/x)^N suffice, or integration by parts on its increasing branch. The extra logarithm is absorbed by reducing c. By first-order quadrature in the two sums of F one has F(x)−x log 2=O(log(2x)): before 1 the logarithmic singularity is integrable and from 1 on the variation of log t exp(−t/x) is O(log(2x)).

Thus, even for the pointwise reading without compact averaging, N=⌊(log x)/(2 log 2)−b√log x⌋ with sufficiently small b>0 gives a balance o(√x) for this weight. It is a bound on the acceleration mechanism and not on the sign of P_e. Lowering the leading coefficient of the cut by a fixed constant via this identity would require an additional power saving in the bracket. The comparison does not automatically transfer this bound to the tent without averaging.

### Minimax acceleration of the exponential factorial balance with weights between zero and one

For P_e of 7984 there exist explicit weights 0≤w_k≤1 with which the balance Σ_{k=1}^N(−1)^(k−1)w_k P_e(x/k) is o(√x) without averaging octaves, already at
    N=2⌊[(log x)/(2 log(3+2√2))−b√log x]/2⌋
for sufficiently small b>0. The leading coefficient is 0.28365… in natural logarithm, against 0.72135… for the Euler weights. The approximation is changed, keeping the factorial identity and a non-negative physical remainder before discounting the integral.

Indeed, z=e^(−u) and N=2m. Take R(z)=[T_m(2z−1)/T_m(−3)]², T_m the Chebyshev polynomial. R(−1)=1, R≥0 on [0,1] and ||R||∞≤4(3+2√2)^(−N). The polynomial z(1−R(z))/(1+z) has degree ≤N. Its coefficients are (−1)^(k−1)w_k: write R(−z)=Σ r_i z^i, with r_i≥0 by the double positive roots and Σ r_i=1. Then w_k=Σ_{i≥k}r_i. The leading coefficient of the recurrence w₁=1−R(0) tends to one. The identity of 7984 now holds with remainder g(u)=R(e^(−u))/(e^u+1), without the external factor 2^(−N). The error of the balance is O(log(2x)) plus the discrepancy of g against dψ−dt.

The weighted variation satisfies ∫u|g′(u)|du≪(1+N²)||R||∞, by Markov's inequality on [0,1] (or by |T_m′|≤m²) and the exponential decay of 1/(e^u+1). Abel on t≥√x gives O(x(1+N²)||R||∞ exp(−c√log x)) by the PNT; on t≤√x use |ψ(t)−t|≪t and ||g′||∞≪(1+N²)||R||∞ in the global Abel integral, with cost O((1+N²)||R||∞). The announced choice gives the result after absorbing N² and taking b small.

The rate 3+2√2 cannot be improved exponentially through only a uniform pointwise ceiling on the relative remainder: for any R of degree ≤N with R(−1)=1, ||R||∞ on [0,1] is ≥1/|T_N(−3)|. If it were smaller, the difference with T_N(2z−1)/T_N(−3) would alternate at the N+1 extremal points of the Chebyshev polynomial, with N roots inside and another at −1. This barrier is for that class of estimate and not for the signed arithmetic balance. No bound for P_e(x) in isolation is derived from it.

### Inversion of the factorial datum: an exact resonance and what the second base recovers

For b=2,3 let F_b(u)=1/(exp u−1)−b/(exp(bu)−1), with F₂(u)=1/(exp u+1). Each reading Σ Λ(n)F_b(n/x) is known in terms of Σ log m [exp(−m/x)−b exp(−bm/x)] by grouping divisors. Inverse question to 7996: approximate exp(−u) by combinations of these readings to eliminate the P_e of smaller scales. In L¹(du), with only base two, every approximant A(u)=Σ c_j F₂(t_j u), even with arbitrary real dilations, satisfies
    ∫₀^∞ |exp(−u)−A(u)|du ≥ |Γ(1+2πi/log 2)|>0.
In particular separating the target function between two combinations of that class requires an integral width at least twice that constant. The obstruction exists even if the weights are allowed to change sign.

Proof. With s=1+2πi/log 2, the functional h↦∫h(u)u^(s−1)du has norm one. The Mellin transform of F_b is Γ(s)ζ(s)(1−b^(1−s)), continued from Re s>1 to Re s>0 since F_b is bounded at zero. The base-two factor vanishes at s, also after any dilation; the exponential gives Γ(s). Concrete example: the positive density 1+ε cos((2π/log 2)log t+φ), 0<ε≤1, reproduces exactly all the F₂ readings of the measure dt. Its exponential reading at scale x differs by εx Re[exp(iφ)x^(2πi/log 2)Γ(s)]. It is only used as a proof of indistinguishability of those continuous readings; it is not a model satisfying the PNT.

With bases two and three this L¹ barrier disappears and the joint real dilations have dense span in L¹(du). Indeed the isometry h↦e^v h(e^v) converts dilations into translations up to constants. On the line Re s=1 the two multipliers have no common zero: at s=1 they equal log b, and away from that point one uses the classical non-vanishing of ζ on the line and the irrationality of log 2/log 3. By Wiener's Tauberian theorem for the ideal generated by two functions this gives density. More precisely in L¹(u^(σ−1)du), 1/2<σ<1, the same proof characterizes density by the absence of zeros of ζ exactly on that line; there not even the base-two factor vanishes. Hence the second base corrects an artificial loss at σ=1 and does not remove an obstruction coming from ζ in the interior. Qualitative density does not control the cost of coefficients, the number of dilations or the sampling error against the primes; it does not justify the root bound.

### Explicit continuous inverse with finite cost even when sampling over prime powers

Let K(u)=1/(e^u−1), J(u)=−(uK(u))′ and m(v)=Σ_{n≤v}μ(n)/n (here m is the Möbius sum). The factorial identity of 8008 also holds for real bases b>1. Dividing by b−1 and letting b↓1 gives the positive kernel J, bounded at zero and exponentially decreasing at infinity up to a linear factor. Its mass is one and its Mellin transform is (s−1)Γ(s)ζ(s), without the artificial zeros of a fixed base on Re s=1. Its reading is explicitly
    A(y)=Σ_n Λ(n)J(n/y)=Σ_{k≥1}log k (k/y−1)e^(−k/y).
This follows by differentiating the absolutely convergent series of K and grouping divisors. Positivity comes from the strict monotonicity of u/(e^u−1).

For every u>0 one has the pointwise inverse
    exp(−u)=∫₁^∞ m(v) J(vu)dv.
Indeed integrating each summand from v=n gives ∫_n^∞J(vu)dv=nK(nu); then Σ μ(n)K(nu)=exp(−u) by grouping into multiples. At fixed u the expansion is absolutely convergent. Moreover ∫₁^∞|m(v)|dv/v<∞ by PNT with remainder for Mertens and Abel, which give |m(v)|≪exp(−c√log v). Hence the same inverse can be applied to the primes without losing control of the tail:
    P_e(x)=∫₁^∞ m(v)[A(x/v)−x/v]dv.
Here ∫m(v)dv/v=1, integrating the first identity in u by Fubini. By Chebyshev and the finite weighted variation of J one has 0≤A(y)≪y for all y>0 (Abel, or dyadic partition); this justifies Fubini even for the prime reading. Truncating the last integral at v≤D≥2 costs in modulus O(x exp(−c′√log D)), with some c′>0. One thus obtains quantitative inversion for the infinitesimal-base datum, different from the combinations of only two bases of 8008.

The limit of using absolute norms in this construction is located exactly. For every small ε>0, finiteness of ∫₁^∞|m(v)|v^(−1/2−ε)dv, when required for all such ε, is equivalent to RH. Under RH it follows from Mertens with margin and Abel. Conversely, the Mellin transform ∫m(v)v^(−s)dv would be holomorphic on Re s>1/2 and coincides for Re s>1 with 1/[(s−1)ζ(s)]; the point 1 is removable and an exterior zero would produce a pole. The cost at mass scale is therefore proved, while the absolute cost at root scale contains the original difficulty. The identity does not exclude a better estimate for the signed integral.

### Fixed-sign factorial deficit and absolute cost in the physical variable itself

For reading A of the previous entry, D(y)=y−A(y) satisfies at all scales
    (1/10) min(y,1) ≤ D(y) ≤ 2 min(y,1).
Proof. Put t=1/y. For t≥1, use log n≤(n−1)log 2 and nt−1≤nt. Summing the differentiated geometric series,
    t A(1/t) ≤ 2(log 2)t² exp(−2t)/(1−exp(−t))³ < 0.8.
The maximum of the bound is at t=1. The upper bound for D uses A≥0.

For 0<t≤1 use the classical convergent expansion of the polylogarithm in exp(−t), differentiated in the order at zero:
    Σ log n exp(−nt)=(−γ−log t)/t−Σ_{k≥0}ζ′(−k)(−t)^k/k!.
Apply −(t∂t+1), allowed by radius 2π for the regular series. The result is
    A(1/t)−1/t=ζ′(0)+Σ_{k≥1}(k+1)ζ′(−k)(−t)^k/k!.
Here ζ′(0)=−log(2π)/2. To make the margin explicit, |ζ′(−1)|<0.22 by the functional equation: the numerator in modulus is at most ζ(2)|log(2π)−ψ(2)|+|ζ′(2)| and the denominator is 2π². Use ζ(2)<1.65, |log(2π)−ψ(2)|<1.5 and |ζ′(2)|<1.3 (series from 2 and integral comparison). Moreover |ζ′(−2)|/2!=ζ(3)/(2(2π)²)<0.025. For k≥3, the same differentiated functional equation gives
    |ζ′(−k)|/k! ≤ [ζ(k+1)(|log(2π)−ψ(k+1)|+π/2)+|ζ′(k+1)|]/[π(2π)^k] ≤ (k+6)/6^k.
It suffices to use ψ(k+1)=H_k−γ, ζ(k+1)<2 and |ζ′(k+1)|<1.3. The sum of (k+1)(k+6)/6^k from 3 equals 0.216. The total remainder in modulus is <0.731 and the claim follows.

In particular P_e(x)=−∫m(v)D(x/v)dv. For x≥1, replacing m by |m| costs, up to absolute factors in both directions, exactly
    ∫₁ˣ |m(v)|dv + x∫ₓ^∞ |m(v)|dv/v.
Even a bound O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) for every ε>0 for the first term alone would imply RH: summing over dyadic blocks gives ∫|m(v)|v^(−1/2−2ε)dv finite, and the previous Mellin identity applies. Under RH, Abel and the Mertens bound with margin give the converse for both terms. This excludes gaining the exponent through smallness of the positive deficit in certain bands. The signed estimate remains open.

### Positive decomposition of the deficit and obstruction to transferring the sign through Laplace

Write B(h)=D(1/h), F(u)=1/(exp u−1), E(u)=1/u−F(u). The integral formula for log n, applied also to the continuous reading with density exp(−hu), gives
    h Σ log n exp(−nh)+log h+γ = h∫₀^∞ [E(h+t)−exp(−t)E(h)]dt/t.
Differentiating with respect to h one obtains B(h) as an integral in dt/t of
    G_h(h+t)−exp(−t)G_h(h),    G_h(u)=E(u)+hE′(u).
The differentiation is locally dominated for h>0 by cancellation of order t at zero and by E(u)=O(1/u), E′(u)=O(1/u²) at infinity.

Each integrand is strictly positive. Indeed G_h+G_h′ is affine in h for fixed u. At h=0 it equals (u−1)/u²+F²>0: for 0<u<1 compare the coefficients of (exp u−1)/u with those of (1−u)^(−1/2), strictly larger from degree two on (by the ratio of successive terms). At h=u it equals 1/u²−F²[2u(1+F)−1]>0: with M=(exp u−1)/u this is equivalent to M³+M>2exp u, which follows from M>exp(u/2) by sinh(u/2)>u/2 and from the arithmetic-geometric mean. Hence exp(u)G_h(u) increases for u≥h. This allows truncating the Frullani integral to any band in t with positive remainder.

Another form of transfer can be falsified. There is no positive measure ν such that B(h)=∫exp(−hr)dν(r) on r≥0 for all h>0. The convergent expansion of the previous entry gives B'''(0+)=4ζ′(−3)>0. Indeed ζ(−3)=1/120 and its logarithmic derivative there is log(2π)−ψ(4)−ζ′(4)/ζ(4)>0. By continuity B'''(h)>0 also for small positive h. Any positive superposition of exponentials would have non-positive third derivative there (dominated differentiation using the reading at h/2). The band decomposition does preserve the sign of the weight; when integrated against m(v) the comparison by truncation is lost, since m changes sign (for example m(1)=1, m(5)=−1/30).

### Two-sided localization of the Möbius balance with reconstruction at root exponent

Let S f(x)=f(x/2). For each fixed integer r≥1 use
    H_r=(1−2S)∏_{k=0}^{r−1}(1−2^(−k)S),   W_r=H_r D.
The first factor kills the line and the others kill, one by one, the terms y^(−k) of the convergent expansion of D at infinity. Thus W_r(y)=O_r(y^(−r)) for y≥1. On 0<y≤1 one has W_r(y)=O_r(y^(−1)exp(−2/y)): the line has disappeared and the geometric series of 8032 bounds A at each scale. By linearity H_r P_e(x)=−∫m(v)W_r(x/v)dv.

Take x≥e and α_r=1−1/[2(r+1)]. The integral over v<x^α_r costs O_r(√x) in modulus, by bounded m and x^(−r)∫₀^(x^α_r)v^r dv. The part v>x log x costs O_r(x(1+log x)exp(−2log x)). Consequently for each fixed r and each 1/2≤σ<1 the following are equivalent:
- P_e(x)=O(x^σ).
- The signed integral of m(v)W_r(x/v) over x^α_r≤v≤x log x is O(x^σ).

For the reverse implication let U=∏(1−2^(−k)S)P_e. By smoothed PNT P_e=o(x), hence U=o(x). If V=(1−2S)U=O(x^σ), telescoping towards infinity gives U(x)=−Σ_{j≥1}2^(−j)V(2^j x)=O(x^σ). Now invert each factor 1−cS with 0<c≤1 towards smaller scales, down to [1,2]; the cost is geometric with ratio c2^(−σ)<1 and the boundary terms are bounded. The direct implication follows by linearity and the two tails. For any fixed δ>0 one can choose r so that v≥x^(1−δ) suffices (the tail bound also holds with any smaller lower endpoint, for 0<δ<1). The factors and the constants depend on r; this proof does not authorize taking r growing with x to reach a band of fixed ratio. The compensation in the indicated interval remains.

### A single reversible filter of infinite order and a subpower band

With S from the previous entry define Q(z)=∏_{k≥0}(1−2^(−k)z), H(z)=(1−2z)Q(z)=Σh_j z^j and W=H(S)D. They are entire functions in z and for R≥0 one has Σ|h_j|R^j=(1+2R)∏(1+2^(−k)R), by alternation. In particular in the identity H(S)P_e=−∫m(v)W(x/v)dv sum and integral can be interchanged by D(y)≪y and ∫|m(v)|dv/v finite.

For every integer r≥1, the remainder after degree r−1 of B(h)=D(1/h) at zero costs ≤C h^r for all h>0 with C independent of r. For h≤1 use the absolute sum of the Taylor coefficients (radius 2π); for h≥1 use that same sum for the polynomial and B bounded. Since H(2^k)=0 for k≥0, the polynomial can be subtracted inside the dilation series. Thus |W(y)|≤C y^(−r) Σ|h_j|2^(jr). Separating the factors with k≤r one obtains Σ|h_j|2^(jr)≪2^(r(r+1)/2+r), with constant independent of r (the residual factors are dominated by two copies of ∏_{l≥0}(1+2^(−l))). With r=⌊log₂ y⌋ one gets, for y≥2,
    |W(y)| ≤ exp(−(log y)²/(2 log 2)+O(log y)).
For y≤1 the cancellation H(1/2)=0 allows replacing D by −A in the series. Since Σ|h_j|2^j<∞ one keeps |W(y)|≪y^(−1)exp(−2/y).

Therefore for any fixed c>√(log 2), in the filtered reading the band
    x exp(−c√log x) ≤ v ≤ x log x
suffices. In the left tail the supremum of the weight is ≤x^(−c²/(2 log 2)+o(1)); multiplying by O(x) using bounded m gives o(√x). The right tail is o(√x) by the previous exponential estimate.

The reconstruction preserves each exponent 1/2≤σ<1. In the space with norm sup_{x>0}|f(x)|/x^σ, S has norm 2^(−σ), and Q(S) has inverse bounded by ∏_{k≥0}(1−2^(−k−σ))^(−1). To justify its application without assuming the conclusion, P_e=O(x) globally and o(x) at infinity. By dominated convergence Q(S)P_e=o(x) there. From the filtered datum O(x^σ) at infinity one recovers U=Q(S)P_e through the telescoping towards infinity of the previous entry; at zero it is already O(x). The sums for Q(S) inverse applied to U give the same function in the norms of exponents 1 and σ (same truncations, continuous pointwise evaluation). In exponent 1 they recover P_e. Thus a bound O(x^σ) for the restricted integral is equivalent to P_e=O(x^σ). A single weight and a single band serve simultaneously for all those exponents. The interior cancellation is missing.

### Exact elimination of the memory prior to the band

With W and H from 8076 put w(t)=W(1/t) and apply the factor 1−2S a second time to the datum. The weight in dv becomes g(t)=w(t)−2w(2t). Since w is integrable at both ends by the bounds already proved, g has zero mass and its tail primitive is exactly
    ∫_z^∞ g(t)dt=∫_z^(2z) w(t)dt=z L(z),    L(z)=∫₁² w(uz)du.
In particular the reading is written directly with the individual jumps, with bounded coefficients and without the factor x/n:
    (1−2S)H(S)P_e(x)=−Σ_{n≥1} μ(n)L(n/x).
Indeed each jump μ(n)/n contributes the integral from v=n, equal to n L(n/x). The interchange is absolute for each x by the exponential decay at infinity of g and the harmonic bound for the sum of the moduli of the jumps.

For any c>√(log 2), the previous sum is restricted to integers in [x exp(−c√log x), x log x] with absolute error o(√x). On the left the log-Gaussian bound of 8076 is applied uniformly to w(un/x), 1≤u≤2; the shift by log 2 alters only the O(√log x) term of the exponent at the endpoint. At most x integers are counted. On the right |L(z)|≪z exp(−2z) for z≥1, and integral comparison gives O((1+log x)/x). In the reconstruction, H(S)P_e=o(x) by PNT and dominated convergence, so the same telescoping towards infinity inverts the additional factor for σ<1. Thus the signed bound O(x^σ) on the finite sum is equivalent to P_e(x)=O(x^σ) for 1/2≤σ<1. Unlike the reading of m(v), modifying individual values μ(n) prior to the cutoff in this finite sum does not alter any summand. The equivalence uses the properties of the original arithmetic datum. No saving has been obtained in the interior sum.

### Mass of the localized weight and mandatory cancellation between different numbers of factors

The weight of 8090 has strictly negative mass. Indeed put b(t)=[Q(S)D](1/t). It is bounded near zero and t b(t)→Q(1/2)>0 at infinity: D(1/t)=1/t+O(t exp(−2t)) there and the dilation series converges absolutely. Since w(t)=b(t)−2b(2t), integrating up to R gives −∫_R^(2R)b(t)dt. By the definition of L and Fubini one gets
    I=∫₀^∞ L(t)dt=−(log 2)² Q(1/2)<0.
The second difference that eliminated the memory therefore does not eliminate the main term of the primes in the discrete reading.

For each fixed k≥1 let S_k be the contribution of μ(n)L(n/x) in the band of 8090 with exactly k distinct prime factors and n squarefree. One has
    S_k ~ (−1)^k I x (log log x)^(k−1)/[(k−1)! log x].
Indeed Landau's classical theorem for products of k distinct primes gives the asymptotic of the counter with constant 1/(k−1)!. By differences, the counting measure rescaled by that asymptotic converges on compact intervals of (0,∞) to length. To justify the passage to the full weight, on n≤ax, 0<a<1 fixed, use L bounded and the counter at ax: the normalized contribution has limsup O_k(a). For n>Bx, B≥2, split into [2^jBx,2^(j+1)Bx]; the bound of the normalized counter is O_k(2^j B (1+log(2^j B))^k) uniformly for large x, and |L(t)|≪t exp(−2t). Send a↓0 and B↑∞. Restricting to the band costs o(√x) absolutely by 8090.

In particular for every fixed K the sum of layers 1 to K is asymptotic to the last one, since their successive moduli grow in ratio (log log x)/(k−1) for k≥2. Keeping any fixed number of layers produces a contribution larger in modulus than x^(1/2+ε) for ε<1/2. Nor can the target be proved by bounding each layer in modulus and summing: already the prime layer exceeds that budget. The required estimate must respect cancellations between distinct values of k, with k without fixed bound. The asymptotic used is of fixed order and does not by itself quantify the growing threshold needed.

### Exact threshold in exponent for discarding the high layers in modulus
This is an application of the threshold of 5514 to the reversible weight L of 8090. The critical scale and the counting mechanism were already in the corpus.

Fix 0<a<1 and K=⌊a log x/log log x⌋. In the band of 8090, the sum of |μ(n)L(n/x)| with ω(n)≥K equals x^(1−a+o(1)). The same law holds imposing ω(n)=K. Here ω counts distinct prime factors; this is the cost of absolute discard.

For the upper bound take X=x log x. Summing over the divisors of n that are products of K distinct primes, the number of n≤X with ω(n)≥K is at most X(Σ_{p≤X}1/p)^K/K!. The reciprocal sum is O(log log X) by the Chebyshev bound and partial integration. Since log(K!)=(a+o(1))log x and K log log log X=o(log x), it suffices to use L bounded.

For the lower bound choose a fixed interval [u,v]⊂(0,∞) where |L|≥η>0, possible by continuity and nonzero mass. Choose 1<b<1/a and Y=(log x)^b. Form d with K−1 distinct primes from [Y,2Y]. For every d one has d≤x^(ab+o(1)). By PNT, there are ≫x/(d log x) primes q in [ux/d,vx/d], uniformly because x/d grows at least like a positive power of x. They are larger than 2Y, hence n=dq is squarefree and each representation is unique. All those n fall in the band for large x. If N is the number of primes in [Y,2Y], N≫Y/log Y and K=o(N). Therefore
    Σ_d 1/d ≥ binom(N,K−1)(2Y)^(−K+1) ≥ [N/(2Y(K−1))]^(K−1) = x^(−a+o(1))
on logarithmic scale, using also N≤2Y. This proves the lower bound even within a single fixed-sign interval of the weight and in the exact layer K.

For a>1/2 an absolute tail o(√x) is thus proved; for a<1/2 not even a single layer at that threshold can be discarded in modulus at root cost. At a=1/2 one obtains x^(1/2+o(1)), sufficient for every fixed margin ε. The signed summation up to that growing order is still pending.

### Limit of redesigning a fixed weight to compensate the prime layer internally

Let V be nonzero of class C¹ on (0,∞), with |V(t)|+|tV′(t)|≪min(t^η,t^(−1−η)) for some η>0. Its Mellin M(s)=∫V(t)t^(s−1)dt is holomorphic in an open strip around 1. There is a first integer r≥0 with M^(r)(1)≠0: otherwise by analytic identity and Fourier uniqueness for exp(u)V(exp u) we would have V=0. Then
    Σ_p V(p/x) ~ (−1)^r M^(r)(1) x/(log x)^(r+1).
Proof: outside √x≤p≤x^(3/2) the absolute sums are O(x^(1−κ)) for some κ>0 by the two tails, even counting integers. Inside, PNT with remainder O_N(z/log^N z) and Abel replace the sum by ∫V(z/x)dz/log z with error O_N(x/log^N x), since ∫t|V′(t)|dt is finite and the boundaries satisfy the same bounds. With z=xt, expand 1/(log x+log t) up to degree r, with remainder ≤2|log t|^(r+1)/(log x)^(r+2). Extending each moment to all t costs a power error up to logarithms. This proves the formula and excludes root scale for any fixed nontrivial weight of that class applied only to the primes.

For L of 8090, the derivative is controlled directly by tL′(t)=2w(2t)−w(t)−L(t), with the two tails already proved. If the difference V(t)↦V(t)−2V(2t) is repeated h times starting at L, the Mellin is multiplied by (1−2^(1−s))^h. Consequently the first nonzero moment is exactly the one of order h and the main prime term is (−1)^h h!(log 2)^h I x/(log x)^(h+1), with I from 8100. For fixed h the difference is reversible at the target exponents by the previous telescoping and PNT. No fixed repetition, nor any fixed redesign within the indicated class, allows treating the prime layer separately at root cost. No obstruction is deduced for weights varying with x.

### First signed compensation in the reading L when grouping by the largest prime

Fix 0<δ<1/2. In the band of 8090 select all n=dp with p prime, d≤x^δ and p>d. The representation is unique. Its contribution to Σμ(n)L(n/x) is
    I x/(log x)² + O_δ(x/(log x)³),    I=∫L<0.
The prime layer alone contributed −I x/log x: incorporating all these cofactors makes exactly that first order disappear and determines the sign of the residue. Grouping by cofactor has antecedents in the index (packets of the product with coefficient −Λ); here the sum is evaluated with coefficient μ(d) and the reversible weight L.

Indeed one can evaluate −Σ_{d≤D}μ(d)Σ_p L(dp/x), D=x^δ. The pairs with p≤d have dp≤x^(2δ) and are negligible to every inverse power by the log-Gaussian tail of L. For p>d each integer appears at most once, so imposing the band costs o(√x) by the absolute proof of 8090 (also counting all integers). Let l=log x. The PNT expansion of 8125 to three terms, at scale x/d, has coefficients I, −∫L(t)log t dt and ∫L(t)log²t dt, and error O((x/d)/log⁴(x/d)). It is uniform because x/d≥x^(1−δ); summing the errors in modulus gives O_δ(x/l³).

For j=1,2,3 sum by parts with m(v)=Σ_{d≤v}μ(d)/d:
    Σ_{d≤D} μ(d)/[d(l−log d)^j] = m(D)/(l−log D)^j − j∫₁ᴰ m(v)dv/[v(l−log v)^(j+1)].
The boundary is negligible to every inverse power of l by the unconditional bound of 8018. In the integral replacing the inverse denominator by l^(−j−1) costs O_δ(l^(−j−2)) using ∫|m(v)|log(v)dv/v finite by that same bound. Since ∫m(v)dv/v=1 and the tail from D is negligible, the sum equals −j/l^(j+1)+O_δ(l^(−j−2)). Substituting gives the equivalent with the indicated error. The same constant for each fixed δ implies that any strip x^α<d≤x^δ with 0<α<δ<1/2 costs O_{α,δ}(x/log³x) after summing with sign. The remaining sector must still compensate the term of order x/log²x.

### Signed comparison up to the moving cutoff p=√n

In the band of 8090, let B(x) be the reading of the n whose largest prime p satisfies p>√n, and C(x) that of the others. Let B_δ(x) be the subreading of 8133. For each fixed 0<δ<1/2 there is b_δ>0 such that
    |B−B_δ| + |B+C| ≪_δ x exp(−b_δ√log x).
In particular B∼Ix/log²x and C∼−Ix/log²x. The boundary p≈√n is included in the first estimate. Although the resemblance between the two balances has precision better than any inverse power of the logarithm, the second estimate is an application of the Möbius PNT and does not improve its power exponent.

Proof of the first estimate. For each p sum first over d=n/p. With p>√n one has d<p and μ(dp)=−μ(d), with no exceptions from divisibility. The band condition together with x^δ<d<p cuts out a single interval. On it, M(t)=Σ_{d≤t}μ(d) satisfies |M(t)|≪t exp(−b_δ√log x) by the classical Mertens remainder for t≥x^δ (adjust the constant at open endpoints). Abel gives a uniform bound O((x/p)exp(−b_δ√log x)) for that interval. Indeed the endpoints are controlled by sup_z z|L(z)| and the integral term by ∫z|L′(z)|dz, both finite by 8125. Sum over p≤x log x and absorb the factor O(log log x) by reducing b_δ. For the second estimate apply the same argument directly to n and L(n/x) over the whole band, whose left endpoint exceeds √x for large x. Substituting 8133 yields the equivalents with opposite signs.

The strongest local conclusion is that any additional subinterval of cofactors for each prime, even chosen depending on p, within d≥x^δ and d<p has the same total budget after summing first in d. No regularity of the endpoint as p varies is required. The root-scale bound on the total B+C remains pending.

### Disjoint pairing at root cost between products of opposite parity

In the reading L of 8090 one can construct, for all large x, a subfamily of ≫√x exp(b√log x) integers of [x,4x] whose balance is bounded by O(√x) summing in modulus the errors of the pairs. Put B=4√x. In [B,2B] take disjoint intervals with endpoints p and 2q, with p,q odd primes. For each interval and each odd squarefree k between x/B and 2x/B form pk, 2qk. The joint contribution is ±[L(pk/x)−L(2qk/x)], since p,q>k. There are no duplicates: parity separates both sides, and on the odd side the prime p is the largest, while on the even side q is the largest prime of n/2.

For each k, the absolute value of the summed errors is bounded by sup_{[1,4]}|L′| (k/x) B, since the lengths of the disjoint intervals sum to at most B. Summing over k costs O(x/B)=O(√x) regardless of how many intervals are occupied. To verify the claimed count divide [B,2B] into cells of length B exp(−b₀√log B), discarding the last incomplete one. By PNT with classical remainder, for b₀ small enough each cell contains both a prime and twice a prime (apply also to the cell divided by two). Choose one interior pair per cell. There are ≫x/B admissible values of k by the positive density of odd squarefree integers, or by subtracting among the odd integers the multiples of odd squares by union. Adjusting b gives the count. If one wants the sum of individual moduli to exceed the root cost, use a fixed subinterval of ratios n/x where |L|≥η>0, which exists by 8100: restrict [B,2B] and the range of k to sufficiently narrow proportional intervals, translating the latter by a constant factor. Increase the constant in B if needed to keep q>k. The same proof thus gives ≫√x exp(b√log x) of absolute mass with signed cost O(√x) in the band of 8090.

This mechanism uses the variation of the weight and the disjointness of intervals; the PNT only ensures that pairs exist. Neither a sufficient covering of the remaining integers nor a cancellation between the two sectors of 8145 is obtained: both members of a pair may have largest prime greater than √n.

### Oriented pairs crossing the largest-prime cutoff

The compensation of 8155 can be realized with prescribed sign on each side of the cutoff of 8145. There exist disjoint subfamilies of semiprimes pk and of products of three primes 2qk, paired one to one, such that the first side lies in P⁺(n)>√n with total contribution ≤−√x exp(b√log x), the second in P⁺(n)<√n with contribution ≥√x exp(b√log x), and the sum of the moduli of the errors per pair is O(√x) for some constant b>0 and all large x.

Since I<0, there is z₀>0 with L(z₀)<0. Fix B=√(3z₀x). Take p and 2q in [B,(1+η)B], and k prime in [B/3,(1+η)B/3], with fixed η>0 small enough that L≤−c<0 on [z₀,(1+η)²z₀] and η<1/4. Then k<q<2k and k<p. The largest prime of pk is p and exceeds √(pk); that of 2qk is q and is smaller than √(2qk). The three corresponding primes are distinct for large x. The parity of the number of primes gives the indicated signs. Build disjoint intervals with endpoints p,2q as in 8155. There are ≫exp(b₀√log x) intervals and ≫B/log B options for k. The logarithmic loss is absorbed by reducing b. Unique factorization and separation of ranges exclude duplicates. The same length budget bounds the sum of errors by O(B)=O(√x).

Covering limit for these fixed strips: even allowing geometric overlap and keeping only injectivity of the pairs, there are (1+o(1))ηB/log B choices for p for each k and only (1/2+o(1))ηB/log B for q. Thus ≫B/log B semiprimes remain unpaired for each k in this design, all with the same sign. Their joint mass is ≫x/log²x. This last bound is internal to the strips and to the indicated type of pair: it is not a global deficit, and other types of products could absorb it.

### Complete covering of a semiprime strip by four multipliers

Take A={2,3,7,42}. Each a is squarefree with μ(a)=−1 and Σ1/a=1. In the geometry of 8163 move the center of k to 2B/5, choosing B=√(5z₀x/2) to keep pk/x near z₀. Use strips [B,(1+η)B] for p,aq and [2B/5,(1+η)2B/5] for k prime, with η fixed small enough to separate the strip of k from all the strips of q and keep L≤−c<0. Then all the pk can be paired injectively with products aqk of opposite sign satisfying P⁺(aqk)<√(aqk): both k<aq and q<ak. The value of a is recognized by the small factors, and k by its strip. Therefore there are no collisions as k or a vary.

To prove covering, divide the strip of p into cells of equal length h comparable to B exp(−b√log B), with b fixed small enough. In each cell J the excess of the number of candidates aq over that of primes p is
    ∫_J [Σ_{a∈A} 1/(a log(t/a))−1/log t]dt + O(B exp(−c₁√log B))
by PNT with classical remainder at the endpoints, with c₁>b. The integrand is (Σ(log a)/a)/(log B)²+O(1/log³B), uniformly. The excess is strictly positive for large B. The aq are distinct. Choose an injection within each cell, and reuse it for every k. There are ≍x/log²x pairs, each of individual mass bounded below in modulus. Since |p−aq|≤h, the aggregate cost in absolute value of the weight differences is O((x/log²x) exp(−b′√log x)) with b′>0. The unused candidates have cardinality ≍x/log³x counting k, by the same integrated excess. This covering proof loses the disjoint-length budget of 8155: a finer transport estimate or cancellation with the remainder is missing to reach root scale.

### Semiprime covering with signed balance o(1) by ordered choice of partners

In a fixed strip of the geometry of 8171 one can select distinct integer partners for ALL the pk of the strip, with total signed error O(exp(−b√log x)). The selection depends on x and on L. Choose z₀ in an interval where L<0 and L′ has constant strict sign: such an interval exists by continuity of L′, negative mass and zero limit at infinity (on a component of L<0 the function cannot be constant). Reduce η so that all arguments, even after widening the endpoints by one cell, remain in that interval.

Use the cells of length h of 8171 and add one exterior cell at each end for candidates. For each cell J of primes there are enough candidates both in the immediately preceding cell and in the following one. Indeed shifting the integral of the main density 1/log t by ±h costs O(h²/(B log² B)), while the excess of 8171 is ≍h/log² B; the PNT error is also of lower order. For each direction build an increasing injection by ordering primes and candidates in each target cell. One obtains two strictly increasing lists u_i<p_i<v_i, both at distance ≤2h from p_i. All their entries are of the form aq of 8171.

Start from the list of partners u_i for each k. For each k in turn, change the partners to v_i running through the p_i from largest to smallest. At every moment the partners are distinct: at the boundary between left prefix and right suffix one has u_i<p_i<p_{i+1}<v_{i+1}. Between distinct k the uniqueness of factorization of 8171 still holds. The initial balance Σ[L(p_i k/x)−L(u_i k/x)] and the final one with v_i have opposite signs by monotonicity. Each change alters the balance by at most 4h(k/x)sup|L′|≪h/B. Stopping at the first zero crossing gives the claimed error. The individual contributions of both sectors have mass ≍x/log²x.

The improvement over 8171 is for the modulus of the joint balance, not for the sum of moduli of errors per pair. The leftover candidates depend on the crossing point; the selection does not reduce the balance of the total reading except insofar as it allows removing this family with error o(1). It does not prove a bound for the complementary family.

### Simultaneous pairing of linear mass in the localized reading

For all large x there is a subfamily in a fixed interval [u x,v x], 0<u<v, of absolute mass ≍x and signed balance O(exp(−b√log x)). The partners are chosen by the same prime replacement p ↦ aq of 8179, now at many scales; the cofactors may have any parity. The covering criterion is arithmetic on the origin side, while the choice of the target side depends on the weight.

Indeed choose z₀,η as in 8179 and the B=2^j between x^(3/5) and x^(4/5). For each B use p in [B,(1+η)B] and all squarefree k coprime to 42 in [z₀ x/B,(1+η)z₀ x/B]. There are ≍B/log B primes and ≍x/B cofactors uniformly. For the latter, by inclusion-exclusion of squares and of the primes of 42, the counter up to Y is Y φ(42)/42 ∏_{p∤42}(1−p^(−2))+O(√Y) (expand μ² and impose coprimality in the quotient). Both p and all q are larger than k for large x. In the origins pk p is recovered as the largest prime; in the targets aqk a is recovered as gcd(aqk,42), then q as the largest prime of the quotient. The product aq identifies the block because the strips widened by one cell are disjoint. Origins and targets are separated by coprimality with 42. Thus there are ≍x/log x pairs per block, ≍log x blocks, without duplicates; all individual weights have modulus ≥c>0.

Use the two injections of 8179 in each block. In each fiber (B,k) the additional sign μ(k) is constant. Choose the initial injection so that the balance of that fiber is non-positive and the final one so that it is non-negative. Change one fiber at a time; if the direction reverses, run backwards through the sequence of injections already tested. Each global jump costs O(exp(−b√log x)) uniformly by log B≥(3/5)log x and k/x≪1/B. The first zero crossing proves the claim. All the products satisfy P⁺(n)>√n for x large enough, also in the target, by q≫x^(3/5) and n≍x. Therefore the balance of this complete sector of 8145, of order x/log²x, persists in its complement even though linear absolute mass has been removed. The construction cancels a positive proportion of integers and at the same time exhibits why covering by cardinality is not enough to improve the global estimate.

### Crossing capacity exceeding the main term and calibrated extraction

In the geometry of 8179 there is a reserve of pairs crossing the cutoff P⁺=√n, with prescribed signs and capacity ≫x/log x on each side. For any target 0≤Y≤c₀x/log x with c₀ fixed small enough one can remove mass Y+O(1) from the negative side and the same from the positive one with difference O(exp(−b√log x)). This allows removing the common main term of 8145 with an explicit target independent of the exact sectoral balances.

Keep the strips of 8171, but use cofactors k=53m in the strip of k, with (m,42·53)=1 and μ(m)=+1. There are ≍B such k: the density of squarefree integers coprime to the fixed modulus is positive, and the sum of μ restricted to those coprimes is o(B). This last claim is obtained by convolving μ with the indicator of integers supported on the primes of the modulus, by Mertens o(B) and convergence of the reciprocal sum of those integers. Thus μ(k)=−1 and P⁺(k)≤max(53,k/53)<q even for a=42 and large B. The target aqk is decoded by gcd with 42 and the largest prime of its quotient. No factor of k or a exceeds √(aqk) and q<ak because a≥2 and k≥2B/5, q≤(1+2η)B/2. At the origin p>k. Therefore all origins have negative weight and all targets positive weight, and they cross the cutoff. There are ≍B²/log B pairs and |L| lies between two positive constants.

Order the origins, for example by k and then by p, and take them until Y is exceeded in sum of moduli. The excess is O(1). On that subset restrict the two injections of 8179: monotonicity and the collision-free traversal still hold when omitting origins. Stop the changes upon crossing zero balance as there. For Y=−I x/log²x, the main term disappears in the two residual sectors and each is left at O(x/log³x) by 8133–8145. The pairing error is o(1). This calibration uses a known sectoral term: the global error of the complement coincides with the original up to o(1), and no root-scale bound is obtained from it.

### Origin of the sectoral term and geometric limit of calibrated extraction

Let D=exp((log log x)^3). Within the sector B(x) of 8145, the natural subfamily n=dp with d≤D by itself has the term Ix/log²x+O(x/log³x). More precisely, for each fixed N the signed balance of ALL the rest of the sector is O_N(x/log^N x). Indeed, in the proof of 8145 sum first over the interval D<d<p. The supremum of |M(t)|/t there is ≪exp(−c√log D); the variation of L and the reciprocal sum over p cost in total O(x log log x). Since √log D=(log log x)^(3/2), the claim follows for all N. The equivalent for the core follows from 8133 and 8145.

To cross from this core to the opposite sector by the replacement p↦aq with q prime, keeping d and the scale (aq/p between two fixed positive constants), one needs uniformly a≥x^(1/2−o(1)). Indeed q≤√(daq) implies q≤da. Then aq≤da² and, since aq≥c p, one gets a≥√(c p/d)=√(c n)/d. In the band n≥x exp(−√log x), d≤D, this gives a≥√(cx)exp(−√log x/2−(log log x)^3). In particular, no catalog of multipliers ≤x^(1/2−ε) with fixed ε reaches even a single origin of this core by such a crossing.

Consequence for the reading of 8197: its negative extraction lies entirely in the natural remainder, whose complete balance before extraction was smaller than x/log^N x for every fixed N. After extracting the calibrated mass, that remainder by itself carries the term opposite to that of the intact core. It is a verifiable redistribution of the coefficient within B. To intervene directly on the core by pairing at comparable scale one must also change d, decompose p with multipliers of size at least √x corrected subpolynomially, or abandon that form of pairing. Other mechanisms to control the global sum are not excluded.

### Direct crossing of the whole core by substituting one prime by four

For D=exp((log log x)^3) and the band of 8090, each squarefree origin dp with d≤D simultaneously admits a target d r s t q of opposite sign, in P⁺≤√n, with all targets distinct and |rstq/p−1|≪exp(−b√log x). In particular d=1 is included. No subset of origins is chosen by its balance.

Fix a very small constant ε>0. Use primes r,s,t in the exponent intervals log(r)/log(x)∈[ε,.01], log(s)/log(x)∈[.27,.28], log(t)/log(x)∈[.32,.33]. All the p of the original band with d≤D satisfy p=x^(1+o(1)) uniformly. Split their range into geometric cells J=[P,P(1+θ)) with θ=exp(−b√log x), extending the extreme cells. For each triple count primes q with rstq in J. Its exponent belongs to [.37,.42] for x large enough. By PNT with classical remainder at the endpoints, if b is small enough there are at least θP/(2rst log x) options, uniformly. The products of quadruples are distinct by separation of exponents. By PNT and Abel, the product of the three sums of prime reciprocals tends to
    log(.01/ε) log(.28/.27) log(.33/.32).
Choose ε fixed so that this constant exceeds 10. In each cell there are thus surplus targets relative to the ≤2θP/log x origin primes. The same holds using the neighboring cell on each side, since the lengths differ by 1+o(1). The claim is asymptotic and ε may be extremely small.

Choose ordered injections in the cells. Among distinct d, d is recovered as the product of all factors smaller than x^ε (D<x^ε eventually); the four remaining ones are identified by their ranges. All are smaller than the root of the target x^(1+o(1)), and the parity of four versus one inverts Möbius. Over the whole band the sum of absolute errors per pair is O(x exp(−b′√log x)): by 8125 sup_z|zL′(z)|<∞, each error costs O(θ) and there are ≤x log x origins. Boundary targets may fall in the band widened by 1+O(θ); one works with the untruncated reading of 8090.

Moreover, on any compact [u,v] interior to an interval of monotonicity of L, ALL origins of the core with dp/x∈[u,v] can be paired with joint balance O(θ). For each d restrict the left and right lists to the corresponding subset, orient the initial one according to μ(d) and traverse as in 8179. The slightly exterior targets remain in the monotonicity interval. The bound per jump is uniform. The claim about the balance O(θ) refers to that compact; the bound over the whole band is the previous absolute one. It remains to control the remaining integers of the sector without dominant prime: the constructed oversupply does not estimate their balance.

### Compensation of the signed error of the whole core with a reserve at a second scale

For all origins of 8213 simultaneously one can choose distinct four-prime targets for the original cofactor, with total signed error O(exp(−b√log x)) and multiplicative distance to the origin 1+O(exp(−b√log x)). Monotonicity of L on the full band is not required. The datum left unestimated is the balance of the integers outside this selection.

Reserve only the prime origins (d=1) with p/x∈[u,v], a compact of positive length where |L′|≥c>0 and L′ keeps its sign, with margin at both ends. To separate targets subdivide the range of exponents of r of 8213 into two disjoint intervals, each with limiting reciprocal mass large enough that the product of the three masses exceeds 10. This can be done by first fixing a very small intermediate endpoint and then an even smaller ε. All ranges remain fixed and D<x^ε eventually. Assign one interval of r to the reserve and the other to the remaining origins. Decoding by factors guarantees disjointness.

Pair the non-reserved origins as in 8213, in fine cells of relative width θ=exp(−b₀√log x). Their signed error E satisfies |E|≪x log x θ by the elementary per-jump bound. For the reserved primes take geometric cells of relative width τ=√θ. Build an increasing injection towards the cells located TWO positions to the left, and another towards those located TWO positions to the right. The count of 8213 works in those cells: the reserve has density excess by a fixed factor and the relative lengths of origin and target tend to one. In particular each displacement has modulus between c₁τx and C₁τx, even at the edges of the original cells. By the mean value theorem each weight error in the reserve has modulus between c₂τ and C₂τ; the sign is constant in each injection and changes between them. There are ≍x/log x reserved origins. The available amplitude in each direction is therefore ≫xτ/log x, which dominates |E| since θ=τ². Adding E, the two extremes remain on different sides of zero. Traversing the injections from right to left as in 8179 preserves uniqueness and alters the balance by at most O(τ) per change. The first crossing gives the claim with b=b₀/2.

The selection can be carried out using only the data of the origins and their possible targets, without consulting the balance of the complement. In the untruncated reading its removal changes the total by o(1); consequently the complement must still satisfy the root-scale bound. The bound o(1) is for a single signed balance and does not control the sum of absolute errors.

### Complete catalog with calibrated constant without selection of partners

Let R be the fixed rectangle of exponents of r,s,t of 8213 (the lower endpoint of the first interval is allowed to vary). With d≤D from 8205 and q of exponent between .37 and .42, sum ALL the integers drstq of the band, without injection or selection by the weight. Its signed reading is
    −I C₂(R) x/log²x + o(x/log²x),   C_j(R)=∫_R du dv dw/[uvw(1−u−v−w)^j].
The different density for pairing primes at scale p≈x is C₁(R): for example the number of products rstq in [x,2x] is (C₁(R)+o(1))x/log x by the uniform PNT applied to q and reciprocal sum over the triple. Since 1−u−v−w<.42, C₂>C₁/.42. Supplying enough partners for all the primes by density (C₁≥1) necessarily leaves overcompensation of the main term if the whole catalog is kept.

Proof of the balance. For fixed m=rst, l_m=log(x/m)≍log x. Apply the expansion of 8133 to Σ_q L(q/(x/(md))) up to three terms and sum with μ(d) over d≤D. Its proof by Abel with l_m instead of log x is uniform: log D=o(l_m), m(v) of 8018 has absolutely integrable first logarithmic moment and ∫m(v)dv/v=1 (in this sentence m(v) denotes the Möbius sum, not the product rst). One gets −I(x/m)/l_m²+O((x/m)/log³x), with sign opposite to 8133 because there are four primes. Imposing the band in this expansion costs o(x/log³x) after summing the triples and cofactors. Indeed, with Y=x/(md)≫x^.36, for q<Y exp(−√log x) it suffices to count integers with L bounded, and for q>Y log x sum the exponential tail of 8090. The cost is O(Y exp(−√log x)+Y(1+log x)/x) per pair m,d. Use Σ_m1/m=O_R(1), Σ_{d≤D}1/d≪log D. In the band q automatically has the prescribed exponent for large x; all large factors are distinct and are decoded unambiguously. Finally PNT and Abel give weak convergence of the reciprocal measure in each fixed exponent range to du/u. Applied to the product and to the continuous integrand (1−u−v−w)^(−2), it gives C₂.

In particular there is a fixed lower endpoint ε_*∈(0,.01) with C₂=1, by continuity and strict monotonicity from zero to infinity when widening the range of r. For that natural catalog, the core of 8205 and ALL the targets together have balance o(x/log²x) without calibration on data or pairing. But C₁<.42: the first-order sectoral cancellation is achieved with insufficient candidates for a bijection of primes.
