Conversely, for an oversupply catalog of 8225, the unchosen ones by themselves keep the main contribution −I(C₂−1)x/log²x (widening the band by the boundary margin of 8213 costs o(x/log³x) by the same tails). The remainder and root-scale precision are pending.

### Homogeneous catalog matching the continuous prime density at all orders

Change the denominator of the three exponents of 8235 to log h, where h=rstq is the product itself. This leaves a single arithmetic list H independent of x and d. Choose the rectangle R with C₁(R)=1 (existence by the same continuity and divergence as ε↓0). For all large Y and every subinterval J⊂[Y,2Y],
    # {h∈H∩J} − # {p prime in J} = O_R(Y exp(−b_R√log Y)).
The constant is uniform in the endpoints of J. The order of the four factors is unambiguous by their separated exponents.

In the continuous measure ∏ dz_i/log z_i put y=log h=Σlog z_i and (u,v,w)=(log z_i/y) for the first three. The Jacobian in the four logarithmic variables is y³, the exponential numerator is exp y and the product of denominators y⁴uvw(1−u−v−w). Thus the image on h IS exactly C₁(R) dh/log h, even for a finite interval in h high enough that the factors exceed 2. There is no truncated expansion in inverse powers of the logarithm.

To justify the discretization replace successively each prime measure by dz/log z. With the other three coordinates fixed, the domain in the remaining one is an interval, since all constraints are linear in the logarithms. Its upper endpoint is ≤2Y/m for m the product of the other three, and in every nonempty fiber the factors are ≥Y^ε. PNT at both endpoints costs O_R((Y/m) exp(−c_R√log Y)). Integrating or summing 1/m in the other coordinates costs O_R(1) by the reciprocal sums or integrals between Y^ε and 2Y. This proves the uniform control and also allows comparison with the prime count in J.

In the band of 8090 gather the origins dp of 8205 and ALL the dh, h∈H, with the same limit d≤D and μ(d)≠0. The factors of h exceed D and are smaller than √(dh) eventually; d is decoded by the small factors (for example using x^(ε/2) as cutoff). Each cofactor contributes μ(d) times the difference between the two readings with weight L. By Abel on dyadic cells of the product h or p, the difference per cell costs O_R(Y exp(−b_R√log Y)) given that L is bounded and ∫|L′| finite. Here Y=x^(1+o(1)) uniformly in the core; the sum of Y over d is O(x log x/d). Absorbing these logarithms one obtains joint balance O_R(x exp(−b′_R√log x)). The bound holds even summing the moduli of the differences per cofactor: it requires no Möbius cancellation between them. This fixed rule cancels the core at all logarithmic orders. The arithmetic replacement error and the exterior of the catalog remain without root-scale estimate.

### Exact cost in exponent of passing the homogeneous catalog to prime powers

In [Y,2Y] substitute, in each of the four coordinates of H, the prime measure by the one assigning weight 1/j to p^j for j≥1, keeping the same logarithmic domain. Count tuples with their product weights. The excess over the catalog of simple primes is positive, of size Y^(1−ε/2+o(1)), where ε is the fixed lower endpoint of the first exponent in R. Even subtracting the analogous change in the prime count of a single factor, the excess has that same exponent.

Upper bound: in each additional tuple there is some coordinate n=p^j≥Y^ε with j≥2. For a given value n there are O((Y/n)log²(2Y)) possible integer triples in the other coordinates by harmonic summation, even without imposing ranges. For Z=Y^ε, the proper powers up to U are O(√U log(2U)) by summing over j≤log₂ U, hence Σ_{n≥Z,proper power}1/n≪Z^(−1/2)log(2Z) by dyadic blocks. The four positions and the weights ≤1 give the upper bound.

Lower bound: fix ε<u<.01, v=.275, w=.325 and take r=p² with p∈[Y^(u/2),2Y^(u/2)], primes s,t in [Y^v,2Y^v], [Y^w,2Y^w]. For each triple use all primes q in [Y/(rst),2Y/(rst)]. For large Y the three coordinates relative to log(rstq) lie in the interior of R. The PNT on intervals of ratio two gives ≫Y^(1−u/2)/log⁴Y tuples, of weight 1/2. Send u↓ε after taking the lower limit of the exponent. For the scalar count the proper powers in [Y,2Y] contribute only O(√Y log Y). This proves the statement. It is a non-negative discrepancy between two distinct arithmetic counts; it does not give a lower bound for the original discrepancy between H and the primes. It does exclude transferring to the catalog a root bound by discarding in modulus the proper-power terms of the explicit formula.

### Four proper powers: exact quadratic term and separation of the mixed captures

Let R be the homogeneous catalog with C₁=1 of 8245. In its version weighted by 1/j, the contribution T of the tuples with proper powers in ALL positions, over Y≤h≤2Y, satisfies
    T=(1/16) ∫_{√Y}^{√(2Y)} dz/log z + O_R(√Y exp(−b√log Y)).
Indeed the case of four squares is exactly 1/16 times the count of H on the interval of roots: dividing all logarithms by two preserves the four proportions. Apply 8245. For the remainder there is at least one power of order ≥3. Divide each position into dyadic ranges [U_i,2U_i), O(log⁴ Y) boxes. In an occupied box ∏U_i≤2Y and U_i≥Y^ε/2. Powers of order ≥2 cost O(U_i^(1/2)log Y) per coordinate and those of order ≥3 cost O(U_i^(1/3)log Y). Thus the total of the remainder is O_R(Y^(1/2−ε/6)log⁸Y). This bound includes unbounded exponents and does not require the bases to be distinct.

The scalar correction of all proper powers equals (1/2) times the same integral term, with error O(√Y exp(−b√log Y)) by PNT for squares and O(Y^(1/3)log Y) for higher orders. Hence T minus the scalar correction is −(7/16) times the previous integral, with the same subexponential error at root scale. This whole block already fits within the root budget.

In contrast, for a nonempty proper subset S of positions occupied by proper powers and the rest by simple primes, the exponent of the absolute mass is exactly 1−m_S/2, where m_S is the minimum of Σ_{i∈S}u_i on the closure of R, with u₄=1−u₁−u₂−u₃. In the dyadic bound use U_i^(1/2) for S and U_i outside S; in an occupied box ∏_{i∈S} U_i ≫ Y^(m_S). For the lower bound choose an interior vector close to the minimum and use squares in S and primes outside. Choose the bases in intervals [Y^(u_i/j_i), (1+c)Y^(u_i/j_i)] with j_i=2 in S and 1 outside, and c fixed with (1+c)^8<2. By PNT there are Y^(1−Σ_{i∈S}u_i/2+o(1)) tuples and for large Y they remain inside the domain. Approximating the minimum from the interior gives equality of exponents. All coordinates have positive fraction, hence m_S<1 for the 14 nonempty proper subsets. These are precisely the mixed strata that exceed root scale in this change of measure. This does not estimate the balance against the original prime reading.

### Global optimization of the correction by squares among four-factor catalogs

Consider homogeneous catalogs without multiplicity, given by open regions of exponents in the ordered chamber u₁<u₂<u₃<u₄, Σu_i=1, with mass ∫du₁du₂du₃/∏u_i=1 to match the prime density. There is an exact optimum for the exponent of the positive excess of proper powers. Define a_* as the unique solution of F(a)=1, where F(a) is the mass of the chamber with u₁>a. The best possible exponent is 1−a_*/2 and it is strictly greater than 47/50. Therefore moving the ranges to the center of the simplex does not bring the absolute correction to root scale.

Indeed F is continuous and strictly decreasing on (0,1/4), tends to zero at 1/4 and diverges at zero (for example fix the two intermediate coordinates in separated interior intervals). Every region of mass one has infimum m of its smallest coordinate ≤a_*. Squares in the smallest position force a lower exponent ≥1−m/2 by the construction in interior boxes of 8265; if m=0 it is approximated by fixed interior points. The full region u₁>a_* realizes m=a_* and has matching upper bound by dyadic counting or by the argument of 8257. Its equality boundaries are omitted, which does not affect the continuous measure; the ordered ranges distinguish the factors. The continuous normalization still gives the prime density by the change of variables of 8245 and the fibers are intervals once the order is imposed.

For the explicit bound F(a)≤(1−4a)^3/[144 a³(1−3a)]. The projected volume of the translated simplex is (1−4a)^3/6, the 24 chambers have equal measure and the product of coordinates is ≥a³(1−3a) (its logarithm is concave and the minimum is attained at a vertex). At a=3/25 the quotient is <1, hence a_*<3/25 and 1−a_*/2>47/50. This optimum concerns geometric catalogs of products counted once and the correction in modulus, not signed combinations nor the original discrepancy H minus primes.

### The mixed corrections preserve exactly the root scale when summing fiber errors

In the fixed domain of 8245, freeze ALL the proper coordinates of a mixed stratum S of 8265. For an admissible value v=(p_i^{j_i})_{i∈S} put m=∏v_i, λ(v)=∏1/j_i, j_i≥2. The remaining fibers are counts of one, two or three simple primes with product in [Y/m,2Y/m] and the original constraints with v fixed. The stratum is exactly Σ_v λ(v)N_v. For any approximants A_v and 1/2≤σ≤1 one has
    |Σ_v λ(v)(N_v−A_v)| ≤ C_R Y^σ sup_v |N_v−A_v|/(Y/m)^σ.
C_R is independent of Y, even at σ=1/2, where no logarithmic loss appears. The inequality still holds summing the errors in modulus. Therefore this step allows keeping the large corrections as explicit terms and concentrating the obligation on the discrepancies of lower dimension. It does not presuppose the validity of any approximant.

Proof. Each admissible coordinate lies between Y^ε and 2Y. For σ=1/2 the squares contribute to the weighted reciprocal sum at most (1/2) Σ_{Y^(ε/2)≤p≤√(2Y)}1/p=O_ε(1), by Chebyshev and Abel on that interval of fixed exponents. The orders j≥3 contribute O(1) even extending to all primes and exponents, by convergence of Σ_{n≥2} n^(−3/2)/(1−n^(−1/2)). Multiplying these bounds over the frozen positions gives Σ_v λ(v)m^(−1/2)≤C_R. The same proof without the weights 1/j gives the same bound for Σ_v m^(−1/2). For σ≥1/2 the factor m^(−σ) only decreases.

There are moreover O_R(Y^((1−ε)/2)) nonempty fibers per mixed stratum, since at least one prime ≥Y^ε remains, whence m≤2Y^(1−ε); use the unweighted reciprocal just bounded. As an unconditional application, in the four strata that leave only ONE free prime, the logarithmic conditions cut out an interval per fiber. Using differences of π at the two endpoints (with the appropriate convention for open endpoints) computes their exact contribution; even rounding each scalar reading with error O(1) would cost o(√Y) altogether. This count measures the number of queries to π, not the cost of evaluating π nor a bound for π−Li. The inequality resolves neither the fiber discrepancies nor the global complement.

### A single class of scalar fibers already realizes all dyadic intervals

Audit of the possible use of 8283 with A_v=∫_fiber dt/log t. In any of the four free positions, allowing only prime squares in the three frozen ones already makes the uniform bound O_δ((Y/m)^(1/2+δ)) for all δ>0 equivalent to RH. It suffices to consider variable Y and the single product interval (Y,2Y]. The sign of the endpoints does not affect the criterion.

Fix an interior vector (u₁,u₂,u₃,u₄) of the catalog of 8245 and free position i. Given any large real z, for j≠i choose a prime in [z^(u_j/(2u_i)),2z^(u_j/(2u_i))] and freeze v_j at its square. Put m=∏v_j, Y=mz. For all t∈(z,2z], the logarithmic proportions of the product mt differ from u_j by O_R(1/log z), uniformly. This follows from log m=((1−u_i)/u_i)log z+O(1). By interiority all constraints hold, and the product cutoff prevents any other t. The fiber is exactly (z,2z]. The argument uses only the existence of primes in intervals of ratio two.

Hence the postulated bound implies for E(z)=π(z)−Li(z) that E(2z)−E(z)=O_δ(z^(1/2+δ)) for all large z. Telescoping from a bounded scale by doublings gives the same bound for E(z), by geometric summation. Abel then gives θ(z)=z+O_δ(z^(1/2+δ)log z) and the proper powers only add O(√z log²z) to pass to ψ(z). The Mellin of ψ(z)−z would exclude zeros in Re s>1/2 via −ζ′/ζ; use every δ and the functional symmetry. Conversely, the classical bound under RH for π−Li at the endpoints of any fiber contained in [Y/m,2Y/m] gives the uniform bound with margin. The equivalence is for the indicated continuous approximant. It does not imply equivalence for an estimate averaged over v nor for a direct comparison between two arithmetic counts. The sup norm of 8283 preserves the scale but already contains RH; that is why this sufficiency must not be promoted to an independent closing route.

### Response of the arithmetic average over three squares to a mode in the smallest coordinate

In the rectangle of 8245 leave the first coordinate free (fraction u between ε and b=.01), with complex measure t^(ρ−1)dt/log t, and keep the other three as squares of real primes, with weight 1/2 each. Let Jρ(Y) be the result of imposing product h in [Y,2Y]. For fixed ρ with 1/2<Re ρ<1, put λ=ρ−1/2, s=1/2+bλ. One has
    Jρ(Y) ~ [g(b)(2^s−1)/(8λs)] Y^s/(log Y)^2,
    g(u)=∫∫ dv dw/[uvw(1−u−v−w)]
over the other two fixed intervals of the rectangle. The coefficient does not vanish and the real exponent exceeds 1/2. It is an algebraic experiment with a single mode imposed on the free coordinate.

Justification of the continuous substitution of the three squares. Split their three prime bases and the variable t into dyadic intervals (O(log⁴Y) boxes). Replace one by one the three prime base measures by dz/log z. With the other variables fixed, the domain of the substituted base is an interval by the linear logarithmic inequalities. In an occupied box with bases of sizes Z₁,Z₂,Z₃ and free variable of size T, the PNT error is O_ρ(exp(−c_R√log Y) Z₁Z₂Z₃ T^(Re ρ)), also in the mixed steps of discrete and continuous measures. Indeed the bases grow like fixed positive powers of Y, the free complex variable is not the substituted one and is integrated in modulus. The product of sizes is bounded by O(Y^(1/2+b Re λ)) because t∏z_i²≍Y and t≤(2Y)^b. Summing boxes, the error is o(Y^(Re s)/log²Y).

The continuous image of each base under z↦z² with weight 1/2 has density h_i^(−1/2)dh_i/(2log h_i). The Jacobian of 8245 therefore gives
    (1/8)∫_Y^(2Y) h^(−1/2) [∫_ε^b g(u) exp(λu log h)du] dh/log h.
Integration by parts in u, using Re λ>0 and g smooth, gives at the upper endpoint g(b)h^(bλ)/(λ log h) with error O_ρ(h^(b Re λ)/log²h). Integrating in h proves the complex equivalent. For a real cosine perturbation one obtains the real part and, if Im ρ≠0, the same exponent along a sequence of scales. The average reduces the exponent excess from Re ρ−1/2 to b(Re ρ−1/2), but does not cancel it. The behavior of the true prime discrepancy is not deduced, nor is compensation between modes or between strata excluded.

### A factor of subpower size and a complete mixed stratum at root scale

Define a single arithmetic catalog by dyadic bands of the product h itself. In 2^j=Y≤h<2Y keep the ranges of v,w of 8245 and use u∈[a_j,b_j], with b_j=(log log Y)^4/log Y for Y large enough. Choose a_j so that the mass C₁ of the rectangle is exactly 1. It exists by continuity and divergence at zero; moreover c b_j≤a_j≤c′ b_j with 0<c<c′<1 fixed because the product u g(u), with g defined in 8301, extends continuously to zero with strictly positive value. In this way the smallest factor lies between exp(c(log log Y)^4) and exp(2(log log Y)^4). It still exceeds D of 8205 in the band of the core for x large enough. The initial bands can be omitted for this asymptotic claim.

The change of variables of 8245 still gives exactly dh/log h in each band. The discretization by PNT on intervals keeps error O(Y exp(−c₁(log log Y)^2)) uniformly for subintervals of [Y,2Y] within the band: each factor is at least exp(c(log log Y)^4); in the fiber proof the reciprocal sums of the other factors are O(1) on their effective ranges, also in the first by the comparability a_j≍b_j. Polylogarithmic bounds are admitted without changing the conclusion. In particular the reading of the core with this catalog still cancels at all logarithmic orders by Abel as in 8245, although the previous quantitative bound was stronger.

Now the stratum where the only simple prime is the smallest factor and the other three positions are proper powers has absolute mass O(√Y exp(C(log log Y)^4))=Y^(1/2+o(1)). It suffices to fix the smallest factor r and count the other positions in dyadic boxes using O(√U log Y) options per coordinate and product of their sizes ≤2Y/r. Sum r^(−1/2) up to exp(2(log log Y)^4), absorbing the polylogarithmic factors. The proof covers real primes and all proper powers in the other positions, without assuming RH or uniformity in prime counts in short intervals.

The price is checkable: for the inverse stratum with only the first position a square and the other three primes, the exponent of the absolute mass is 1. Choose for the prime base of the square a band of ratio two strictly inside the interval of exponents of r (with growing logarithmic margin); s,t in interior bands of ratio two as in 8257 and q so that Y≤rstq<2Y. The variation of log h relative to log Y alters the proportions by O(1/log Y), below the margin. PNT gives at least Y exp(−C(log log Y)^4)/log⁴Y tuples, and the upper bound Y^(1+o(1)) is the elementary count of quadruples. The improvement of one stratum is not a bound for the complete error of the moving catalog.

### Normalized hybrid comparison over the exact small primes

In each dyadic band [Y,2Y) fix P=exp((log log Y)^4), and use as first factor exclusively the primes r∈[P,P^K] for a constant K large enough. In the three large factors take v=log s/log h∈[.32,.323], w=log t/log h∈[.33,.332] and q=h/(rst). The three large strips are disjoint, with q of exponent >.34 and <.36 eventually. Do not substitute r by a continuous measure nor by prime powers.

For h in the band define
    G(h)=Σ_r (1/r)∫∫ dv dw/[vw(1−v−w−log r/log h)].
With the three large factors continuous of measure dz/log z and the small one exact discrete, the image on h is G(h)dh/log h. Indeed for fixed r the Jacobian in the three logarithms of s,t,q with variables v,w,log h is (log h)^2, and stq=h/r. By Mertens for primes Σ_r1/r→log K. Since the integral lies between two uniform positive constants, K can be fixed with 1≤G(h)≤C_K eventually. Weighting each product by 1/G(h) gives hybrid density EXACTLY dh/log h with positive weights ≤1. This step is a weighted partition of the arithmetic datum: the remaining fraction of each term stays in the complement. The normalizer uses only primes ≤P^K=Y^o(1).

The discretization of the three large coordinates costs O_K(Y exp(−c√log Y)) on each subinterval. Without weight the proof by substitutions on fibers of 8245 applies, with r fixed and cost O_K((Y/r)exp(−c√log Y)); the other reciprocal sums are bounded. Sum 1/r and apply Abel to the weight 1/G (monotone within the band and bounded). The PNT error at the subpower scale of r no longer appears. The reconstruction by small cofactors of 8245 remains applicable since P>D eventually in the band of the core.

When substituting only the three large coordinates by prime powers, the total weighted excess has exponent exactly 1−.32/2=.84. The upper bound is obtained as in 8257 because every new proper power exceeds Y^.32, counting the other factors even among ordinary integers. For the lower bound choose a prime r in [P,2P], a square s in an interior strip of exponent v>.32, t prime near Y^.331 and q prime to complete [Y,2Y). The count of 8257 loses only Y^o(1) by fixing r and the weight is bounded below by 1/C_K. Approximate v↓.32. This avoids the exponent-one stratum of 8314 without attributing to it an unproved cancellation. The bound .84 describes the hybrid change of measure, not the error of the original reading. The large mixed terms and the weighted complement remain pending.

### Hybrid with a single free factor and three-quarters threshold

Fix dyadic band [Y,2Y), l=log Y, δ=1/√log l. Form a list M_Y of products of three primes m=rst with
    exp((log l)^4)≤r≤exp(l/log l),   Y^.20≤s≤Y^.21,   2√Y≤rst≤Y^(.5+δ).
For large Y, t has exponent between .27 and .32. The only free factor q=h/m has exponent 1/2+o(1), and q≤√h on the whole band. The ranges distinguish the four factors and separate them from the small cofactors of 8205.

Let H=Σ_m 1/m. One has H≍δ log l: the reciprocal sum over r is ≍log l, that of s is ≍1, and for each rs that of t between 2√Y/(rs) and Y^(.5+δ)/(rs) is ≍δ uniformly. For the last claim apply Abel and PNT with classical remainder at the two endpoints, both of exponent between .27 and .32; the logarithm of the quotient of their logarithms is ≍δ. Thus H→∞. The exact normalizer is
    G(h)=Σ_m (1/m) log h/log(h/m) ≍ H.
Weighting by 1/G(h), the sum of the images of dq/log q is exactly dh/log h. The weight lies between constants times 1/H and is ≤1 eventually. Since G is decreasing, Abel and the PNT for the single free factor give an error O(Y exp(−c√log Y)) on each subinterval: per m the unnormalized error costs O((Y/m)exp(−c√log Y)), and the normalizer absorbs H.

The absolute excess when allowing q=p^j with weight 1/j, j≥2, has size Y^(3/4+o(1)). In each fiber of scale Q=Y/m in the complete band, already the squares contribute ≫√Q/log Q and all proper powers cost O(√Q log Q). Here Q=Y^(1/2+o(1)) uniformly, so comparing with Q and summing using Σ_m Q=YH and G≍H gives the two exponents. The completion by powers in the scalar reading adds only O(√Y log Y).

Moreover, 3/4 is a floor for this class of normalization: for any fixed list in the band, with a single free factor, 2√Y≤m≤Y^(1−η) (η>0 fixed) and the same normalizer, G≍_η H. Since Q≤√Y, one has √Q≥Q Y^(−1/4); and Q≥Y^η allows counting the squares by PNT uniformly. Summing one obtains excess ≥c_η Y^(3/4)/log Y. The claim uses complete fibers in [Y,2Y] and does not exclude weights distinguishing squares nor signed compensations. The construction attains the floor in exponent while keeping all targets in the sector without dominant prime. It does not estimate the balance of the complement nor the global signed correction.

### Common correction by roots with absolute error budget per cofactor

For the hybrid of 8336, the whole positive correction by proper powers can be kept to precision Y^(1/2+o(1)) by ONE common scalar function, using only prime bases ≤Y^(1/4+o(1)). For t≤√(2Y) put B_J(t)=Σ_{2≤j≤J}π(t^(1/j))/j, with for example J=⌈log log Y⌉. In the band (Y,2Y] and any subinterval, the truncated correction is obtained by summing over m the Stieltjes integral of 1/G(mt) with respect to B_J(t) over the corresponding interval in t. The correction includes values of prime powers even if their bases coincide with one of the frozen factors, as required by the tuple count of the change of measure.

For fixed j, the exact stratum contributes Y^(1/2+1/(2j)+o(1)): by PNT the number of bases in (Q^(1/j),(2Q)^(1/j)] is ≍_j Q^(1/j)/log Q, with Q=Y/m=Y^(1/2+o(1)) uniformly; multiply by 1/(jG) and use Σ_m Q=YH and G≍H. Therefore no fixed J allows neglecting the tail in modulus with full margin over root. On the other hand, for any J→∞ the number of powers of higher order up to 2Q is ≤O(log Y)(2Q)^(1/(J+1)), which is Y^o(1). Moreover #M_Y/H≤Y^(.5+δ) by definition of H. The aggregate error of the tail is Y^(1/2+o(1)) unconditionally. This bound is uniform for partial intervals and does not need PNT in narrow intervals for variable j.

One can even round the cumulative function B_J(t) with uniform error ≤1 before using it in ALL the fibers. By Abel and monotonicity of 1/G the change per cofactor is O(1/H), including the two boundaries. The total is again Y^(1/2+o(1)). The same estimate holds with an additional weight of bounded variation and supremum on the band. Thus the term of size Y^(3/4+o(1)) is isolated as an explicit common arithmetic corrector plus an admissible remainder; the root bound refers to the representation error, not to the size of the corrector. It remains to compare with sign that corrector against the discrepancy of the count weighted by prime powers and to control the integers of the complement.

### Counterexample to deducing the compensation of the corrector from precision in the power count alone

Keep exactly M_Y and G of 8336. For the free coordinate construct a fixed set of integers with counter A and weighted power count J_A(t)=Σ_{k≥1} A(t^(1/k))/k, counting representations. One can have J_A(t)=Li₂(t)+O(log log(3t)) at every scale and, nevertheless, the hybrid count of the simple elements of A in (Y,2Y] minus its reference ∫dh/log h is NEGATIVE of magnitude Y^(3/4+o(1)). Here Li₂ is the integral from 2, extended by zero below 2. This counterexample concerns inferences based only on the error of the counter J; the free coordinate of the example is not the sequence of primes.

Construction. Define R(t)=Σ_{j≤log₂t} μ(j)Li₂(t^(1/j))/j. Divisor inversion gives Σ_k R(t^(1/k))/k=Li₂(t) exactly. R is continuous and for large t and away from the endpoints its derivative is (1/log t)Σ_{j≤log₂t} (μ(j)/j)t^(1/j−1); this lies between 0 and 1 eventually by the term j=1 and the bound O(t^(−1/2)log log t) for the remaining sum. Thus, from a large fixed integer on, the increments of ⌊R(n)⌋ are 0 or 1 and define a set of integers (omit the initial ones). Its counter A(t)=R(t)+O(1) for all t≥2 and it is zero below 2. The sum of the errors with weights 1/k proves the estimate for J_A. Moreover A(t)~t/log t by the expression of R, and the squares of this sequence in (Q,2Q] have cardinality ≍√Q/log Q by the same asymptotic at the endpoints.

Apply Abel to the error of J_A in each fiber, with the monotone normalizer 1/G of 8336: the hybrid power count of A minus its reference has modulus O((#M_Y/H)log log Y)=Y^(1/2+o(1)) as upper bound. Use here and below the tuple count over the fixed list of m, without requiring unique factorization for the test sequence. When removing the proper powers of A the correction is positive of size Y^(3/4+o(1)) by the squares and the same elementary upper bound of 8336. This proves sign and magnitude of the counterexample. In particular improving by itself an absolute bound for J−Li, even up to polylogarithmic precision, does not force the required compensation. Signed, prime-specific information or a mechanism involving the complement would be needed.

### Normalization by the density of simple primes obtained by inversion

Keep M_Y,H of 8336. Let R be the inverse of Li₂ from 8358 and f=R′ (take right-hand values at the thresholds). On (Y,2Y] define
    W(h)=f(h)/Σ_{m∈M_Y} f(h/m)/m.
For large Y, W is positive, ≍1/H and ≤1. The continuous reference of the simple primes is transported exactly to itself: Σ_m W(h) f(h/m)dh/m=f(h)dh. This corrects the bias of the counterexample without adding a selection of partners or querying π in the free variable. The chosen reference is dR on both sides. If E=π−R, the discrepancy of the real catalog with respect to the scalar prime count on an interval K of the band is exactly
    Σ_m ∫_{K/m} W(mt)dE(t) − ∫_K dE(h).
This is only the catalog-minus-primes difference; the complement of the Möbius reading is still present.

Variation control for the transfer. On each [T,2T] with T large, write f(t)=g(t)/log t; the constant term of g is 1 and the others are (μ(j)/j)t^(1/j−1) activated at t≥2^j. The sum of variations of these on the band, including jumps, is O(T^(−1/2)log log T): each term is monotone after its activation and at most O(T^(−1/2)/j). Thus sup|g−1| satisfies the same bound. The function f is ≍1/log T and has variation O(1/log T). Since log(h/m)≍log Y uniformly, the denominator of W has infimum ≫H/log Y and variation O(H/log Y). The quotient rule for functions of bounded variation gives Var W=O(1/H), also counting jumps. In the integrals against atoms a fixed representative of W is used; Abel with sup norm and variation controls both boundaries and the coinciding jumps (equivalently, by approximation with step functions).

In particular for the counter A of 8358, E_A=A−R=O(1). The difference between catalog and scalar counter of A is now O(1+#M_Y/H)=Y^(1/2+o(1)) as upper bound, uniformly in K. In general the same computation gives O((1+#M_Y/H) times the uniform bound of |E| on the intervals involved). The weight really changes: the relative magnitude of the perturbation with respect to 1/G is Y^(−1/4+o(1)), and its sign is positive. Indeed g(t)=1−t^(−1/2)/2+O(t^(−2/3)log log t), uniformly; the average of g(h/m) with positive weights 1/[m log(h/m)] has a deficit Y^(−1/4+o(1)) while that of g(h) is O(Y^(−1/2)). This explains how a small perturbation of the weight modifies the previous three-quarter-order term. For the real π the identity requires comparing the oscillations of π−R between scales; the variation of the weight and the cancellation of the references do not prove that comparison.

### The corrected hybrid amplifies even a fixed critical frequency

Test the operator of 8366 on the complex mode dE(t)=t^(ρ−1)dt, ρ=1/2+iγ with fixed real γ. Its response (catalog minus scalar reading) on [Y,2Y] has modulus Y^(3/4+o(1)), although the scalar increment has modulus ≍_γ√Y. The same holds in exponent for the mode with divisor log t in the density. The linear response to an isolated mode is measured, without identifying it with the behavior of the true primes.

Indeed U=Y^(.5+δ), V=2√Y as in 8336. For each admissible rs, Abel and PNT on the interval of the prime t give uniformly
    Σ_{V/(rs)≤t≤U/(rs)} t^(−ρ) = (U/(rs))^(1−ρ)/[(1−ρ)log(U/(rs))] (1+o_γ(1)).
The lower endpoint is negligible because (V/U)^(1/2)→0, the two endpoints are fixed positive powers of Y or uniformly bounded between them, and the continuous primitive has relative remainder O_γ(1/log Y) by integration by parts. The PNT remainder in Abel is also o_γ(1) relative. Multiplying by (rs)^(−ρ) leaves the SAME main phase for all rs. Therefore
    Σ_m m^(−ρ) ~ U^(1−ρ)/(1−ρ) Σ_{r,s} 1/[rs log(U/(rs))].
In particular its modulus is comparable, with constants depending only on γ, to Σ_m m^(−1/2). The common upper boundary of the product m prevents the average from suppressing the frequency.

Moreover W(h)=(1+o(1))/(2H) uniformly, by log(h/m)/log h=1/2+o(1) and 8366. The catalog reading factorizes exactly as (Σ_m m^(−ρ))∫_Y^(2Y) W(h)h^(ρ−1)dh. The integral is asymptotic to Y^ρ(2^ρ−1)/(2Hρ); the coefficient does not vanish. Given that Σ_m m^(−1/2)/H=Y^(1/4+o(1)), the announced exponent follows. For the divisor log t replace 1/log(h/m) by (2+o(1))/log Y: the absolute error is o of the main term by the comparison with Σ_m m^(−1/2) already proved. The scalar subtraction in both versions is of lower order.

There is also an example of a real integer counter with fluctuation O(√t) that exhibits the stability failure along a subsequence: at least one of the real and imaginary parts of the complex mode gives ≥1/√2 of its modulus in infinitely many bands. Add to R the primitive of that part and round as in 8358: its added derivative is O(t^(−1/2)), so the final increments are still 0 or 1. The aggregate rounding error is Y^(1/2+o(1)) by 8366. Thus, even scalar control at root scale is insufficient by itself to impose that scale on the auxiliary discrepancy. The construction does not decide whether modes of the real primes are compensated by other terms of the problem.

### Exact suppression of a nonzero frequency with arithmetic cofactors and positive weights

For any fixed γ≠0, ρ=1/2+iγ, there are coefficients 0≤a_m≤1 on the list of 8336 with Σ a_m/m∼H and Σ a_m m^(−ρ)=0 exactly. This repairs the amplification of 8378 for the mode with the natural density t^(ρ−1)dt/log t.

Proof. Write U=Y^(.5+δ) and F=Σ_{r,s}1/[rs log(U/(rs))]. For any fixed interval [A,B]⊂(0,1] the vector of the cofactors m in [AU,BU], divided by U^(1−ρ)F, converges to ∫_A^B z^(−ρ)dz. This is obtained by the same uniform Abel on the last prime of 8378, now keeping both endpoints. Choose three narrow disjoint intervals whose centers in log z have phases −γ log z separated by 2π/3. Their three limit vectors strictly surround the origin. Therefore the combinations with coefficients in [0,1] contain a disk of fixed positive radius around zero: there is a null combination with all coefficients strictly interior and the map has rank two. This inclusion persists, reducing the radius, for the discrete normalized vectors and all large Y.

Keep with weight one the m≤cU, with c>0 fixed below the three intervals. Their normalized vector has modulus O(√c), by the bound of 8378 with real exponent 1/2 and ceiling cU (in the limit Y→∞ the ratio of the logarithms of the ceiling tends to one for each c). Choose c small enough to absorb the opposite vector in the disk. Use a common fraction in each of the three intervals and weight zero for the other m>cU. The loss of reciprocal mass is O_c(F) by PNT and Abel on the last prime, while H/F≍δ log Y→∞ according to 8336. This proves the two properties simultaneously.

To apply to the density with logarithmic divisor use g(t)=f(t)log t of 8366 and Z(h)=Σ a_m g(h/m)/m. Assign to the term of cofactor m the weight
    w_m(h)=a_m g(h) log(h/m)/[Z(h) log h].
Since Z∼H→∞, these are weights between zero and one. The image of dR is exactly dR, by direct substitution. The catalog density induced by the mode is
    [g(h) h^(ρ−1)/(Z(h)log h)] Σ a_m m^(−ρ) = 0
on the whole band (also for the conjugate). The scalar reading being subtracted keeps size O_γ(√Y/log Y). The selection uses only the cofactors and γ; it does not use the errors of π in the free coordinate. It provides neither simultaneous suppression of the whole spectrum nor an estimate of the complement, and the real mode γ=0 does not admit such a cancellation with positive mass.

### Finite simultaneous cancellation in real cofactors and density limit

For any fixed list of distinct points ρ_j=β_j+iγ_j with 0<β_j<1 and γ_j>0 one can simultaneously impose Σ_m a_m m^(−ρ_j)=0 with the same 0≤a_m≤1 and Σa_m/m∼H. Rational independence of the frequencies is not required and distinct real parts are admitted. The conclusion concerns the response of the catalog; when subtracting the scalar count its own response survives, which for an exterior exponent may exceed root.

Proof of the needed convex interior. In real dimension 2k consider the vectors v(t)=(exp(ρ_j t))_j, t>0. Every nonzero real linear form takes values of both signs. Group its terms by the largest β with active coefficient and divide by exp(βt): what remains is a real trigonometric polynomial P(t) without zero frequency plus o(1). The frequencies of the group are distinct; the means on [0,T] of P and P² tend respectively to zero and to a positive constant by integration of exponentials. Since P is bounded, it follows that there are values bounded away from zero in both directions at arbitrarily large times (use P²≤‖P‖∞|P| and the positive and negative parts). By compactness of the dual sphere, a finite number of vectors v(t) has convex hull with zero strictly interior. Replacing each point z=exp(−t) by a narrow disjoint interval in (0,1), integrating (z^(−ρ_j))_j, preserves that property: dividing by its length gives an approximation of the pointwise vector and rescaling each vector by a positive number preserves the sign criterion. Their combinations with coefficients between zero and one contain a ball around the origin (they contain the convex hull).

For each interval [A,B] the coordinate j of its cofactor vector, divided by U^(1−ρ_j)F, converges to the corresponding integral, by the same Abel of 8392 with β_j instead of 1/2. The vector of the prefix m≤cU, with identical normalization, has upper limit of norm O_list(Σ c^(1−β_j)). Choose c fixed small enough below the intervals. The ball persists under discretization and allows absorbing the prefix simultaneously in all coordinates. The loss of reciprocal mass is still O_c(F)=o(H). Use the weights w_m(h) of 8392 to turn the cancellations into pointwise density identities, one for each mode and its conjugate.

A quantitative limitation in each band: let V=2√Y and D=log(U/V). For fixed β, the multiplier in frequency, centered at the midpoint of [log V,log U] and normalized to one at zero, is the transform of a probability supported in [−D/2,D/2]. By Jensen on the disk of radius 2T its number of zeros in |z|≤T, with multiplicities, is ≤TD/log 2 (use log|f|≤TD on the larger disk, or pass to the limit if a zero falls on its boundary). Thus this proof for fixed lists does not give a single choice cancelling an infinite list of superlinear density in frequency in a fixed band. No sufficient rate has been obtained for a list growing with Y nor a bound for the omitted frequencies.

### Interpolation of the complete scalar reading in a finite spectral space

For every fixed list as in 8406 one can choose measurable weights 0≤w_m(h)≤1 that reproduce at the same time dR and each density h^(ρ_j−1)dh/log h. Thus the catalog-minus-scalar difference is identically zero on the whole linear space generated by these densities and their conjugates, on any subinterval of the band. This includes prescribed exterior modes. The weights vary with h, without using data of π in the free coordinate.

With g=f log of 8366 impose the real and complex linear equations (separating parts)
    Σ_m a_m(h)[m^(−ρ_j)−g(h/m)/(m g(h))]=0.
Use the blocks and the prefix of 8406. When dividing coordinate j by U^(1−ρ_j)F, the change with respect to the vectors of that argument is o(1) uniformly in h and in each block, including the prefix: g(h/m)/g(h) is uniformly bounded and H/[U^(1−β_j)F]→0. The last convergence uses H/F≍δ log Y and the fixed list with maximum β_j<1. Hence the interior ball of the block combinations persists; the prefix fits in its interior by choosing c with margin as in 8406. One keeps a_m=1 on the prefix and Σa_m/m∼H uniformly.

Selection detail: the normalized matrix of the blocks has a fixed limit of real rank 2k. Choose a combination with all coefficients interior that gives zero in the limit (the hull contains zero in the interior, so positive mass can be given to each column and the masses reduced jointly). Fix 2k independent columns. Keep the initial coefficients and correct only those of these columns by solving a linear system to compensate the prefix and the discretization residue. The inverses are uniformly bounded; reduce c if needed before taking Y large. Thus the coefficients remain in [0,1] and are measurable functions of h by the matrix formulas. This construction avoids any regularity assumption on an arbitrary selection.

Put Z(h)=Σa_m(h)g(h/m)/m and w_m(h)=a_m(h)g(h)log(h/m)/[Z(h)log h]. Z∼H and these weights satisfy the required bounds. The identity for dR is direct. For density j, the image is h^(ρ_j−1)dh/log h multiplied by g(h)Σa_m(h)m^(−ρ_j)/Z(h)=1 exactly, and likewise for the conjugate. Uniformity of these interpolations as the space grows has not been proved, nor a bound for the real reading outside it. It is a result of reproduction of prescribed continuous densities; it does not identify a pointwise decomposition of the atomic prime measure.

### A list growing with the scale: first harmonics of a fixed frequency

Fix γ>0. In 8416 one can simultaneously reproduce the modes ρ_j=1/2+ijγ, 1≤j≤N=⌊(log Y)^(1/4)⌋, and their conjugates. The kept reciprocal mass is (1−o(1))H. This is a prescribed progression; it is not assumed that the heights of the zeros have that structure.

Quantitative details. Write z=m/U, t=−log z. Divide a period [0,2π/γ] into n=2N+1 equal cells with centers t_k. In each cell keep its central half; this allows assigning a constant coefficient in [0,1] to each block. Normalize row j by dividing by U^(1−ρ_j)F as in 8406. The vector of block k has entry
    n^(−1) d_k b_j exp(ijγ t_k) + O_γ(n^(−1)(n^(−1)+(log Y)^(−1)))
where d_k=exp(−t_k/2). To avoid losing margin when inverting, use the exact integral: integrating exp((−1/2+ijγ)t) over that half cell gives EXACTLY the written term with b_j independent of k, including the real exponential factor in the centered integrand. Thus the real approximation error is only O_γ(1/(n log Y)). The |b_j| lie between positive constants independent of n: on the centered half cell the phase oscillates at most π/4 from the center for j≤N, and the modulus of the integrand is comparable to one. Conjugate rows and an auxiliary row j=0 are added, the latter using only the normalized sum of m^(−1/2) over blocks (its final value is chosen freely).

For the error bound, replace the count of the final prime by its integral via Abel. The endpoints of that prime are fixed powers of Y and |j|=O(n); a relative cost polynomial in n from differentiation and inverse cell length is absorbed by the remainder exp(−c√log Y). In the integral replacing 1/log(Uz/(rs)) by 1/log(U/(rs)) costs a relative error O_γ(1/log Y) in modulus with respect to the absolute mass, since t varies over a fixed period. The normalized mass per cell is O_γ(1/n). The additional term g(h/m)/(m g(h)) of 8416 is uniformly negligible even summed over all blocks: it is O(H/(√U F)) after normalizing. The auxiliary row does not use that subtraction.

The main matrix is the discrete Fourier one with diagonal factors b_j,d_k and prefactor 1/n. Its inverse has row norm (ℓ∞→ℓ∞) O_γ(n), by the inversion formula. The perturbation has row norm O_γ(1/log Y), hence the discrete matrix has inverse of norm O_γ(n) by the geometric series. Start from coefficients κ/d_k with κ fixed so that all lie strictly between 0 and 1 with uniform margin. The discrete Fourier transform exactly cancels the nonconstant rows on that vector. Keep with weight one the prefix m≤U n^(−8); its normalized moment in each nonconstant row is O(n^(−4)) in absolute value, by summing the majorant m^(−1/2) up to that ceiling and PNT-Abel as in 8392 (log n=O(log log Y)). The normalization term of the prefix is also O(H/(√U F)). Cancel the residues by correcting through the discrete inverse and fixing the residue of the auxiliary row at zero, that is, leaving its initial reading unchanged. The correction in sup norm is O_γ(n/log Y+n^(−3))=o(1); it is real by conjugation and measurable in h. The rest of the cofactors is omitted. The lost reciprocal mass is O(F log n)=o(H) by PNT and Abel, since H/F≍δ log Y. The final weights and the exact reproduction of catalog and scalar follow from 8416. This supplies an explicit rate for one spectral geometry, without estimate of the exterior of that progression.

### Irregular frequencies with decreasing separation, in a single positive choice

Write l=log Y, L=log l. For large Y one can simultaneously reproduce all the densities of 8416 on Reρ=1/2 of any list whose positive heights are ≤l^(1/4) and such that the symmetric list Λ of heights including zero has minimal separation ≥100/L. Proximity to a grid is not required. The following constants are uniform in the lists. The kept reciprocal mass is (1−o(1))H.

Put t=log(U/m), φ(t)=max(0,1−|2t/L−1|). On 0≤t≤L use the initial weight b(t)=φ(t)exp((t−L)/2)/2 and allow multiplying it by 1+Σ_{ν∈Λ}c_ν exp(−iνt). For the rows of the system of 8416 normalize first by U^(1−ρ)F as in 8406 and then by D=L exp(−L/2)/4. In the auxiliary row zero use only the moment m^(−1/2), without subtraction, keeping the initial value of the adjustment zone. The correction matrix, up to errors described below, is
    K_{ων}=(2/L)∫₀ᴸ φ(t)exp(i(ω−ν)t)dt.
Its diagonal is 1. The transform of the triangle has modulus sinc²((ω−ν)L/4). In any column the off-diagonal sum is ≤32ζ(2)/100²<.006, by separation and ordering of Λ. The same bound in column zero measures the sum of moduli of initial residues of all nonconstant rows.

Justification of the uniform discrete approximation. When substituting the last prime by dz/log z in the sum for each rs, the interval of that prime lies between U exp(−L)/(rs) and U/(rs), with exponents bounded between .27 and .32 for large Y. Abel costs a normalized error O(l^C exp(−c√l)) per entry: the frequencies are O(l^(1/4)), the weight is piecewise smooth, and along that range the ratios of endpoints and D^(−1) are at most powers of l. More explicitly, the PNT remainder at each point is O((U/rs)exp(−c√l)); the supremum plus variation of the weight of the prime, including m^(−1/2) and the phase, is O(U^(−1/2)l^C); summing 1/(rs) costs O(lF). After the change to t, replacing 1/log(U exp(−t)/(rs)) by 1/log(U/(rs)) costs O(L/l) per normalized entry, since the remaining envelope is normalized φ. The subtractions of 8416 cost O(H/(√U F D)) per entry. Therefore the perturbation in column norm is o(1), since |Λ|=O(1+L l^(1/4)). The discrete inverse has ℓ¹→ℓ¹ norm less than 2.

Keep weight one on m≤U exp(−L)l^(−4) and zero between that prefix and the adjustment zone. The normalized moment of the prefix per row is O(l^(−2)/L)+O(H/(√U F D)), by the absolute bound of 8392 at the indicated ceiling, valid uniformly there by Abel and PNT. Its ℓ¹ norm is o(1); in the auxiliary row compensating the prefix is not imposed. Solving to erase the nonconstant residues costs Σ|c_ν|<1/4 for large Y by the bound of column zero and the inverse. Conjugation gives a real correction and b(t)≤1/2 guarantees admissibility. The lost reciprocal mass is O(F log l)=o(H). Applying the pointwise normalization of 8416, with coefficients depending measurably on h, gives exact reproduction. That separation has not been verified for all zeros, nor have closer clusters or the spectral tail been controlled.

### Uniformity against complex collisions, with bounded cardinality and height

Fix N and a compact rectangle K interior to 0<Re s<1, Im s>0. There is a threshold Y₀(N,K) common to ALL lists of up to N points of K, without minimal separation and with multiplicities. For Y≥Y₀ each mode is reproduced exactly in the difference of 8416 and, at a point of multiplicity d, also its first d−1 derivatives with respect to s (logarithmic factors). The relative loss of reciprocal mass tends to zero uniformly in the lists. No explicit rate in N or in K is obtained here.

Proof. Work on the normalized analytic rows of 8416 as functions of s: for a block the row is the sum of [m^(−s)−g(h/m)/(m g(h))] divided by U^(1−s)F. On each fixed block of ratios m/U in [A,B] it converges uniformly on compacts of the strip to ∫_A^B z^(−s)dz, by uniform Abel and the bound on the subtracted term of 8416. For the prefix m≤cU the upper limit of the supremum on a compact with Re s≤b<1 is O_K(c^(1−b)): majorize in modulus by (m/U)^(−b)/(UF), and apply Abel as in 8392. The subtracted term is o(1). Both claims are uniform in h.

Around a limit configuration with distinct centers s_i and multiplicities d_i, take small disjoint disks in the strip. In each disk replace the rows of the d_i positions by their successive divided differences of orders 0,...,d_i−1. For repeated nodes the confluent value is used. The Cauchy integral formula for a divided difference has denominator ∏(ζ−s_j) over a circle enclosing the nodes. Therefore the transformation of the analytic functions has a uniform bound as long as the nodes remain in a smaller concentric disk, even if their distance tends to zero. At the limit center the continuous columns become integrals of z^(−s_i)(−log z)^k/k!. For any real combination of those rows, in t=−log z the group of largest active real part dominates and, within it, the largest active degree in t. After dividing by exp(βt)t^k, what remains is a nonzero real trigonometric polynomial without zero frequency plus o(1). The sign argument of 8406 gives a convex interior also for these confluent columns.

Choose the blocks and the full-rank correction as in 8416 in the limit configuration. Reduce c to absorb the prefix even with the Cauchy bound. Continuity of the transformed columns, stability of the inverse and uniform arithmetic convergence keep the solution interior on a whole neighborhood and for all Y large enough. The system of vanishing divided differences is equivalent to vanishing at the nodes with their multiplicities, by Newton-Hermite interpolation; the analytic normalization does not vanish and does not change the order of the zero. By compactness of K^N a finite subcover suffices (also treat smaller cardinalities). The cost O(F) of lost mass for each design is uniform after that step. The pointwise identity of 8416 and its derivatives follow with the same weights, which once constructed are independent of the spectral variable s.

The novelty compared with applying the fixed list to the zeros known up to a height is the uniformity for lists that depend on Y and may approach each other at arbitrary speed. Compactness does not quantify the threshold nor does it cover an infinite tail by itself. It gives no bound on the global sign.

### Simultaneous rate without separation via polynomial remainders on a logarithmic mesh

Let L=log log Y. For Y large enough, 8416 holds uniformly with multiplicities for any list of N≤L^(1/4) points, with 1/4≤Re s≤3/4 and 1≤Im s≤T≤L^(1/4). Without minimal separation. The following argument gives a conservative rate in both dimensions.

Use Δ=1/(10T), x_s=exp(Δs), and P(X) monic with roots x_s and their conjugates, counting multiplicity, degree d=2N. The map is injective on the rectangle. For an analytic function A of X compute its interpolation remainder of degree <d at those roots by the Cauchy integral with kernel [P(z)−P(X)]/[(z−X)P(z)]. On the boundary of the convex hull of the nodes thickened by Δ/32, the distance to every node is ≥Δ/32, the length is O(1) and |z|≤exp(3Δ/4)+Δ/32. Thus the ℓ¹ coefficient norm of the remainder is ≤(CT)^(Cd) sup|A| on that boundary: for the divided numerator use the difference of monomials and that the coefficients of P have norm ≤3^d. The principal logarithm gives s=log(z)/Δ with Re s<.9 and |s|=O(T) on and inside the contour. This interpolation bound admits repeated nodes.

Construct a real polynomial positive in the sense of non-negative coefficients, divisible by P. For each upper node of argument θ=Δ Im s, the angles kθ and (k+1)θ, k=⌊π/θ⌋, enclose π. There are non-negative coefficients A,B such that 1+A x_s^k+B x_s^(k+1)=0 and A+B≤2: combine the two rays to obtain −1, using cos θ>.99 and |x_s|≥1. In case of angular coincidence one ray suffices. Multiply these factors, one for each repetition, and by 1+X+...+X^(d−1). The result Q has coefficients q_k≥0, q_k≥1 for k<d, sum ≤d3^N and degree K with KΔ=O(N). Its remainder is zero.

In the coordinate t=log(U/m) take blocks [kΔ,kΔ+η], 0≤k≤K, η=exp(−√L). Use on block k the coefficient a_m=e^(kΔ)b_k, starting with b_k=λq_k with λ=e^(−KΔ)/(4d3^N). There is margin ≥λ in the first d variables b_k for small perturbations and all initial weights are ≤1/4. After normalizing the analytic row of 8416 by U^(1−s)Fη, the column of the variable b_k is X^k+E_k(X). Uniformly on the contour and in h one has sup|E_k|≤exp(−√L+O(N+log(T+2)))+exp(−L+O(N+log(T+2))). Indeed the continuous model is the mean of e^(st) e^(kΔ−t) over the block. Freezing it at kΔ costs O(η(1+T) exp(O(N))); replacing 1/log(Ue^(−t)/(rs)) by 1/log(U/(rs)) costs O((1+N)exp(O(N))/log Y). In the fiber PNT of 8392 the prime endpoints are Y^(.3+o(1)) up to the fixed exponent range of the prime s (all between .27 and .32); the variation in modulus of the included phase is controlled by exp(O(N))(1+T) in the variable t. After dividing by η the PNT remainder is still exp(−c√log Y) with reduced c. The subtraction of 8416 costs ≤exp(O(N))H/[U^.1 Fη]. These estimates use Re s≤.9, including the complex values on the contour.

Keep in addition with weight one m≤U exp(−L^(3/4)). Its analytic row, in the same normalization, has supremum O(exp(√L−.1 L^(3/4)))+O(H/[U^.1 Fη]): majorize (m/U)^(−Re s) by (m/U)^(−.9) and apply Abel on the last prime, whose range is still in fixed exponents. Cancel the interpolation remainder of the prefix plus the blocks. The first d columns of remainders form the identity plus a perturbation of norm o(1) in ℓ¹, by the Cauchy bound and d log(CT)=o(√L). The norm of the initial remainder is o(λ): Q has zero remainder, Σb_k≤1 and λ≥exp(−O(N+log(d+1))). Correcting the first d variables with the inverse, of norm ≤2, preserves all margins. The coefficients are real by conjugation and measurable in h. The prefix only loses reciprocal mass O(F L^(3/4))=o(H) by Abel. The vanishing remainder imposes the equations of 8416 with the requested multiplicities and gives the final weights through their positive normalization.

By the classical count N(T)=O(T log(T+2)) this includes at once all zeros of height between 1 and L^(1/8) and real part in [1/4,3/4], without using spacings or RH. Their prescribed densities are reproduced; no interchange of an infinite explicit formula has been justified, nor have the other zeros or the complement been controlled.

### Interpolation of the complete low block after inversion of prime powers

With L=log log Y, T=K=⌊L^(1/16)⌋, one can reproduce with the same weights ALL modes ρ/k for 1≤Imρ≤T and 1≤k≤K, where ρ runs over the nontrivial zeros, without cutting the real part. The contribution of orders k>K in the exact arithmetic inversion of π−R costs Y^(1/2+o(1)) in the hybrid, even in total variation after weighting. The contribution of heights >T in the low orders and the arithmetic complement remain; the statement about modes is an identity for the finite block of densities.

Uniformity details in 8464. The classical zero-free region gives Reρ≤1−b with b=c/log(T+2), c fixed small enough. Use N=O(KT log(T+2)) nodes by zero counting. Their minimal height is ≥1/K; the powers of the positive trinomials of 8464 require total logarithmic length O(NK), because kθ≈π for each factor and the height is ≥1/K (here kθ denotes the auxiliary degree of that trinomial by its angle). Take the contour thickened by bΔ/8 instead of Δ/32; there Re s≤1−b/2 by the modulus bound and |s|=O(T). The norm of the remainder is ≤(CT/b)^(Cd) sup|A|, d=2N. Since NK+d log(CT/b)=o(√L), the margin λ≥exp(−O(NK+log(d+1))) and the perturbation o(λ) on the mesh of width exp(−√L) are preserved. The subtracted term is now O(exp(O(NK))H/[U^(b/2)Fη]), still negligible. The prefix row costs O(b^(−1) exp(√L−b L^(3/4)/2)) plus that subtraction: in Abel for the real exponent 1−b/2 the cost of integrating z^(−1+b/2) up to the ceiling of the prefix is ≤(2/b)exp(−b L^(3/4)/2); the PNT remainder is negligible since all prime endpoints remain between fixed powers of Y. These changes preserve the inverse and the positivity of the argument of 8464. The final weights are uniformly O(1/H).

To identify the block that matters, let J be the cumulative measure counting prime powers with weight 1/j. Exactly π(t)−R(t)=Σ_{k≤log₂t}(μ(k)/k)(J(t^(1/k))−Li₂(t^(1/k))). A density z^(ρ−1)dz/log z in the variable z=t^(1/k) becomes t^(ρ/k−1)dt/log t. Therefore the described finite block cancels in the hybrid−scalar difference, including the signs of the inversion, without making the weights independent across orders. For k>K no spectral expansion is used: in each fiber t≤2Y/m the absolute cost of the positive measures J and Li₂ evaluated up to t^(1/k) is O(t^(1/K)log²(2Y)) after summing the orders (J(z)≪z log(2z) suffices). Summing over m with the weights O(1/H), the bound of 8350 gives Y^(1/2+o(1)). On the scalar side it gives Y^o(1). This avoids interchanging an infinite series of zeros for the high orders. It does not supply an analogous estimate of the height tail for k≤K.

### Flattening the density of the last prime: cutoff at a power of log Y

In 8478 one can take simultaneously T=K=⌊(log Y)^(1/32)⌋ for heights and orders. The decisive modification is not to freeze the logarithm of the last prime. Write l=log Y, v=log(U/m) and
    F_v=Σ_{r,s}1/[rs log(U exp(−v)/(rs))],   F=F₀
with the same two fixed strips per band as in 8336. In the block zone modify each coefficient of 8464 by the factor common to that m, F/F_v. It is positive and ≤1 for v≥0. In the zone used v=O(NK)=o(l) its inverse is bounded and |(log F_v)′|≪1/l by direct differentiation. The continuous contribution after the PNT on the last prime had exactly the factor F_v/F in the integrand; its cancellation removes the error O((1+NK)/log Y), which was excessive for the new dimension. The correction is not applied to the prefix.

Budget verification. In the notation of 8478, N≪l^(1/16)log l, NK≪l^(3/32)log l, d log(CT/b)≪l^(1/16)(log l)^2, b=c/log(T+2). Keep the trinomials and the contour, with block width η=exp(−l^(1/4)) and prefix v≥l^(1/3). After flattening, the continuous error per column with respect to the monomial is O(η(1+T)exp(O(NK))) on the contour. The PNT error after Abel, normalization and division by η is exp(−c₁√l+l^(1/4)+O(NK+log l)); the derivative of the new factor does not change this bound. Indeed, for each rs, the endpoints of the last prime remain between Y^.27 and Y^.32 and its supremum in the box is ≤U/(rs). The variation of the integrand with respect to v over the block, before normalizing in U, costs at most exp(O(NK))(1+T) by the upper limit of Re s on the contour. The subtracted term of the moment, including the flattening, is still ≪exp(O(NK))H/(U^(b/2)Fη). When applying the remainder operator all these errors remain o(λ), since log(1/λ)=O(NK+log N) and d log(CT/b)=o(l^(1/4)).

The contribution of the prefix after normalizing is O(b^(−1) exp(l^(1/4)−b l^(1/3)/2)) plus the previous subtraction. For the bound of its weighted positive sum Chebyshev on blocks of ratio two in the last prime suffices, whose logarithm is comparable to l: summing the geometric series of ratio 2^(−b/2) costs O(1/b). Also after applying the remainder that contribution is o(λ). The reciprocal cost of omitting everything not in the prefix is O(F(l^(1/3)+1))=o(H), by Abel or Chebyshev on blocks, using H/F≍δl. With this the perturbed inverse and the margins of 8464 give admissible coefficients and exact reproduction of the same spectral block of the inversion. The higher orders are controlled as in 8478. The tail of heights >T for k≤K and the balance outside the catalog have not been estimated. The power 1/32 is a conservative choice, with no claim of optimality.

### Explicit formula of the real catalog on smooth tests within a band

There is a smooth variant of the weights of 8486 with the following identity. For φ∈C_c^∞((Y,2Y)), ||φ||∞≤1, write Δ(φ) for the reading of simple primes of the catalog minus the scalar one, and
    D_s(φ)=∫ φ(h) h^(s−1) [Σ_m w_m(h)m^(−s)/log(h/m)−1/log h] dh.
With K=T=⌊(log Y)^(1/32)⌋ one has unconditionally
    Δ(φ)=−Σ_{k≤K} μ(k)/k Σ_{ρ: |Imρ|>T} D_{ρ/k}(φ) + O(Y^(1/2+o(1))).
The series is absolutely convergent for each fixed Y and φ. The claim of uniformity in ||φ||∞ concerns the arithmetic remainder, not the sum in modulus of the series. Zeros are counted with multiplicities.

Construction: use the truncated reference R_K(t)=Σ_{k≤K}(μ(k)/k)Li₂(t^(1/k)) and g_K(t)=R_K′(t)log t in all the equations of 8486. In the arguments used, both h and h/m exceed 2^K, hence g_K is a finite sum of real powers, smooth, positive and 1+O(t^(−1/2)log K). The uniform estimates supporting the matrix inversion use here only the upper and lower bounds of g_K. The remainder matrix and its right-hand side depend smoothly on h: the nodes, the inverted columns and the lists of cofactors are fixed in the band. The solution by the inverse, and its normalization, are therefore smooth in the interior. Thus Δ(dR_K) is zero as a difference of densities, D_{ρ/k}(φ)=0 for the low modes, and sup w_m≪1/H. The classical fact that there are no nontrivial zeros with |Imρ|<1 is used.

Spectral justification: for the power counter J, the explicit formula of von Mangoldt applied in distributions on z>1 expresses dJ−dz/log z as the sum of −z^(ρ−1)dz/log z over the zeros and the trivial density −dz/[z(z²−1)log z]. It is obtained by dividing by log z the derivative of the formula for ψ; the constants disappear. Against a smooth test of compact support in z>2, integrating by parts in log z gives decay faster than any power of |Imρ|, uniformly in 0≤Reρ≤1 for fixed test. The zero count ensures absolute convergence. Apply to the orders k≤K via z=t^(1/k) and to the tests φ(mt)w_m(mt), all smooth of compact support. For fixed Y the sums over m,k are finite. The change of variable produces exactly the indicated D_{ρ/k}. The trivial term has bounded absolute mass on [2,∞); summed over m,k it costs O((1+#M_Y/H)log(2K)). The orders k>K of the inversion of π are bounded directly in total variation by 8478, even weighted by φ. These two remainders fit in Y^(1/2+o(1)). The Li₂ part in k≤K cancels by the exact normalization of dR_K.

The equality incorporates the low list into the formula of the genuine prime measure. Convergence separately for each band does not produce the uniform saving required in the tail; nor does it extend the identity at no cost to a sharp cutoff or control the integers outside the catalog.

### Absolute upper tail to root precision for a fixed Gevrey test

In 8496 take φ(h)=Φ(log(h/Y)), with Φ fixed of compact support interior to (0,log 2), ||Φ^(n)||∞≤A B^n(n!)² (Gevrey class of order 2). Let l=log Y. For a constant C_Φ large enough, the contribution of all |γ|>C_Φ l²/k at each order 1≤k≤K, summed even in modulus over zeros and orders, costs Y^(1/2+o(1)). Therefore for this class only a FINITE sum of intermediate heights T<|γ|≤C_Φ l²/k plus the admissible remainder is left. This claim is for the auxiliary balance of the band.

Necessary analytic uniformity. In 8496 continue h=Y exp(v) to a small fixed complex distance from the segment 0≤v≤log 2. Use g_K as a finite sum without cutoff in this continuation, with the branches log(h/m)=log(Y/m)+v. It is still 1+o(1) uniformly in the tube, since the real parts of the logarithms are ≍l. In the system of 8486 all dependence of the equations on h lies in the subtraction g_K(h/m)/(m g_K(h)); its estimate on the interpolation contour is uniform in that same tube. By the same perturbation of the identity the corrected coefficients are holomorphic, with correction o(λ) uniform in the first d variables b_k; the rest of the blocks is fixed. After multiplying by their factors e^(kΔ), bounded by e^(KΔ) (K the degree) as in the definition of λ in 8464, the a_m remain bounded in modulus. The prefix stays equal to one and the reciprocal mass of all blocks outside the prefix is o(H); hence Z(h)=(1+o(1))H in the tube and |w_m(h)|≪1/H. This justifies Cauchy with constant radius for all the weights at once, without differentiating the equations over the zeros.

For s=β/k+iγ/k, integrate by parts in v. The amplitude apart from exp(iγv/k) is Φ times a function holomorphic in the tube (the constant complex factor Y^(iγ/k)m^(−iγ/k) is taken out before continuing). Its envelope is ≪Y^(β/k)[1+Σ_m m^(−β/k)/H], even discarding the saving of the logarithmic denominators. By Leibniz and Cauchy the derivatives of order n cost at most that envelope times A′(B′)^n(n!)². Optimizing n of order √(|γ|/k) with a small constant gives
    |D_{ρ/k}(φ)| ≪_Φ Y^(.5+δ+1/(2k)) exp(−c_Φ √(|γ|/k)).
Here #M_Y/H≤Y^(.5+δ), Y/m≤√Y and β<1 were used; the scalar term Y^(1/k) satisfies the same ceiling. For the indicated cutoff half of the exponential absorbs Y^(1/(2k)). The other half is summed over all zeros at cost O_Φ(k log(2k)) by N(t)≪t log(2+t) and partial integration. Summing over k≤K, δ→0 gives the result.

The dependence on the regularity of the test is essential. If only ||φ||∞≤1 is fixed, in each band one can choose a smooth function equal to one at the primes of an interior strip and zero outside small neighborhoods of those primes that avoid all composite integers. The catalog contributes zero and the scalar ≫Y/log Y by PNT. Such a test may vary with Y and does not satisfy the uniform derivative bound. This observation does not obstruct the estimate for a fixed test.

### Transport of the high tail to the original weight L and to the sum over cofactors

The test of 8510 can be taken from a uniform family that exactly recomposes L(n/x) on the core of 8205, up to absolute tails o(√x). In particular the high tail of the catalog-minus-core formula costs x^(1/2+o(1)) AFTER summing all cofactors and bands. This does not presuppose a bound for the intermediate heights.

Regularity: B(z)=D(1/z) of 8032 is holomorphic and bounded in |arg z|<π/4. For |z|<1 use the convergent regular series of 8032; for |z|≥1 use 1/z and the series Σ log n(nz−1)exp(−nz) with Re z≥|z|/√2. By 8076, w(z)=Σ h_j B(2^j z) converges normally and stays bounded in the same sector, and so does L(z)=∫₁²w(uz)du. Hence v↦L(dY exp(v)/x) is uniformly bounded in |Im v|<π/4 for all positive d,Y,x. Cauchy gives analytic constants independent of the three scales.

Put a=(log 2)/2. Take a function χ of Gevrey-2 class, non-negative, of compact support interior to (0,2a), with Σ_{j∈ℤ}χ(v−ja)=1. For example normalize a positive Gevrey-2 bump on [a/4,7a/4] by dividing by the periodic sum of its translates, bounded below (the class is stable under reciprocals in that case). At Y=exp(ja), use the constructions of 8486–8510 with test Φ_{d,Y,x}(v)=χ(v)L(dY exp(v)/x). Its Gevrey constants are uniform by Leibniz and the previous Cauchy bound. The arguments for an individual dyadic band use only the endpoint ratio 2 and hold for these real Y; catalogs specific to each band are used.

For each d≤D=exp((log log x)^3) keep the bands [Y,2Y] intersecting [x exp(−√log x)/d, x log x/d]. The partition is complete for the origins dp in the interval of 8090. The additional scalar terms outside it cost o(√x) in modulus: every kept origin satisfies dp=x^(1+o(1)), hence p>d, it is unique and the fractions χ sum to at most one. Apply the two absolute tails of 8090 counting all integers. For the targets the result defines a subweight of the global reading: if h=mq lies in a kept band, the cofactor d is identifiable by all factors of size <x^(o(1)) with a concrete cutoff exp(2(log log x)^3), since r≥exp((log log Y)^4) and the other primes are larger. The exponent ranges of the four factors are disjoint also between neighboring bands. Thus each target integer has a single decomposition up to its band and the sum of coefficients χ w_m is ≤1. Its Möbius sign is μ(d), opposite to that of the origin dp. The values of L are evaluated at the effective product on both sides.

Multiply the identity of 8496 by μ(d), sum and apply 8510 with the same high-cutoff constant for all tests. The remainders are uniform by the proof of 8510. There are x^o(1) terms (at most O(D log x)), with Y=x^(1+o(1)), so their absolute sum costs x^(1/2+o(1)). The result is a reduction for the weight of 8090 itself: core and weighted targets together are represented by zeros in the intermediate bands plus an admissible remainder. The intermediate balance and the arithmetic remainder of the form remain; this operation does not bound them.

### Unconditional bound of the intermediate balance and cost by real part

For the core and the weighted targets of 8522, the modulus of the joint balance is
    O(x exp(−c log x/log log x))
for some constant c>0. Concretely this bound holds even summing in modulus all the intermediate zero terms of the reduction after integrating each mode. For modes with Reρ/k≤α fixed, 0≤α≤1, that sum costs at most x^((1+α)/2+o(1)). No phase cancellation is used for these estimates.

The distinction with respect to the crude majorant of 8510 is essential near Reρ=1. For σ=Reρ/k, start from the envelope before bounding the number of cofactors: Σ_m m^(−σ)/H≤U^(1−σ), exactly by H=Σ_m1/m. In a band, for the tests of 8522 this gives
    |D_{ρ/k}| ≪ Y^σ(1+U^(1−σ)) ≪ Y exp(−(1−σ)(1/2−δ)log Y).
The constants are uniform, since sup |w_m|≪1/H and the tests are uniformly bounded. The intermediate zeros have T<|γ|≤C(log Y)^2/k. By the classical zero-free region, 1−σ≥1−Reρ≫1/log log Y. The count N(t)≪t log(t+2) and K≤(log Y)^(1/32) allow summing with a polylogarithmic factor. For σ≤α, the same initial inequality gives Y^((1+α)/2+δ(1−α)). When passing to x it is not enough to invoke x^o(1) for the first claim: in 8522 there are O(exp((log log x)^3)log x) bands with cofactor, each Y≤x log x, and log Y≥log x−O(√log x+(log log x)^3). Those losses are absorbable by reducing c. The upper tail and the remainders already cost x^(1/2+o(1)).

In particular all orders k≥2 of the intermediate band together cost at most x^(3/4+o(1)), even without RH. The same ceiling holds for the modes of k=1 with Reρ≤1/2. Exceeding the exponent 3/4 in this estimate is only possible at k=1 and Reρ>1/2. Reaching 1/2 still requires also improving the treatment of the critical modes or compensating them with the complement. The argument uses smoothness and the zero-free region; it does not prove a widening of that region.

### Recombination audit: where the zeros removed from the catalog reappear

Let S_total=Σ μ(n)L(n/x) untruncated and A the balance of core plus targets with the partitions of 8522 (use the origins extended with χ for exact equality). Define C=S_total−A by the remaining arithmetic weights. Write M(s)=(1−2·2^(−s))² Q(2^(−s)), with Q from 8076. In the joint representation one has
    C = −A + Σ_{Reρ>1/2, |Imρ|≤(log x)/π} Γ(ρ)M(ρ)x^ρ + O(√x)
for large x. The error of this equality does not need RH. When the formula for A from 8522 is inserted into it, its arithmetic error becomes x^(1/2+o(1)). It is a recombination identity, not an independent arithmetic estimate of C.

Proof: by 8095, S_total=−(1−2S)²Q(S)P_e. The Mellin of the exponential gives P_e(y)=−Σ_ρ Γ(ρ)y^ρ+c₀+O(y^(−1/2)) by shifting to Re s=−1/2 the integral of −Γζ′/ζ (pole at 1 removed, constant residue at 0). The series converges absolutely by Stirling and the zero count. The shift uses heights avoiding zeros; on the final line the functional equation and Stirling give absolute convergence with constant independent of y>0. Apply the filter term by term, allowed because its coefficients have finite absolute sum even weighted by 2^(j/2). It kills c₀ and multiplies each term by M(ρ), uniformly bounded in the strip. The zeros with Reρ≤1/2 contribute O(√x) even in modulus. For the exterior tail use |Γ(ρ)|≪(1+|γ|)^(1/2)exp(−π|γ|/2) and counting by unit intervals O(log(2+|γ|)). With cutoff exactly (log x)/π this gives O(√x polylog x); to obtain the O(√x) shown in the equality, use in addition the zero-free region 1−Reρ≫1/log(2+|γ|) on the stretch from the cutoff to twice it, which absorbs that polylogarithm; from twice on Stirling suffices. Subtracting A concludes.

Consequences for the route. In the total, the critical modes cost √x although the sectoral majorant of 8534 reaches x^(3/4+o(1)); the auxiliary contributions indexed by k≥2 appear with opposite sign when writing the complement by subtraction. But a fixed exterior zero that 8486 reproduces in A for x large enough keeps its coefficient Γ(ρ)M(ρ) intact in this representation of C: M has no zeros in 0<Re s<1, by its factors and normal convergence of the product. Cancelling more modes in the catalog does not by that fact alone reduce the response of the total. To deduce the sign through this decomposition one would need information on C obtained from its own arithmetic or an independent joint estimate; substituting C by this equality returns the starting criterion. It has not been proved that an exterior zero exists.

### Arithmetic audit of the freedom of weights: identical interpolation and empty catalog on its atoms

In a fixed band high enough of 8496 one can impose ALL the same pointwise reproduction equations and the same positivity, with real C∞ weights on (Y,2Y), and make the prime count of the catalog exactly zero. Thus the interpolation of densities, even together with smoothness without uniform constants, leaves an arithmetic freedom of order Y/log Y. This result uses the catalog of real cofactors of 8336; the LP antecedent of 6576 referred to a semiprime catalog and different moment constraints.

For each integer h₀=mq in the band with m eligible and q prime, the separation of the four ranges makes m unique. Choose a C∞ bump of height 1 at h₀, supported in (h₀−1/3,h₀+1/3). Multiply the coefficient of that m by one minus the bump BEFORE solving the moments, grouping all bumps of the same m. Thus at every real h at most one cofactor has been attenuated, and at each atom the multiplier of its unique cofactor is zero. Use these multipliers both in the columns and in the prefix and in the final normalization of 8486–8496.

Verification that there is still a positive solution. In the normalization of the rows in 8464–8486 an individual term of m^(−s) is bounded on the contour by
    (UFη)^(−1) max(1,(U/V)) ≤ Y^(−1/2+o(1)),
since Re s≤1, m≥V, V=2√Y, F=Y^o(1) with 1/F=Y^o(1), η=exp(−(log Y)^(1/4)). The subtracted term of the same row costs O(1/[V U^(b/2)Fη]), with b from 8478. The block factors e^(kΔ) cost exp(O(NK))=Y^o(1); multiplying by the norm of the remainder operator, the number of columns or the inverse of the margin λ costs Y^o(1) in each case. All margins and invertibility persist uniformly for real h, also when removing a term of the prefix. One solves with the same columns; the masking is external to the unknowns and the individual coefficient remains zero at the atom. At most 1/V additional reciprocal mass is lost at each h. The inverse on the real axis gives smooth weights and reproduces dR_K and the prescribed modes. No uniform holomorphic extension bounds are claimed for these new weights.

For a fixed non-negative Gevrey bump positive on an interior strip, the original catalog of 8496 has mass ≍Y/log Y by PNT and the per-band estimate of 8534. The masked one has mass zero and the same readings of the reproduced densities. The discrepancy between the two is therefore ≍Y/log Y on that same fixed test. This does not contradict 8510: the uniform regularity of the weights in log h, used for the high tail, is an effective hypothesis that is lost. To control the complement by variation of weights one must control their resolution at the scale of the integers or their effect on the spectral tail.

### Common discrete quadrature for the regular weights on genuine primes

In each band of 8510 one can replace the prime catalog by a positive quadrature on ≤Y^(1/2+o(1)) real products mq, with total error o(1), simultaneously for all families of weights satisfying the same holomorphic bound O(1/H) in the logarithmic tube and all tests with the same Gevrey-2 constants. The quadrature nodes and weights depend on the actual primes of each fiber and on Y, but not on the choice of the spectral interpolator nor on the test. A reduction of arithmetic data is obtained; the quadrature coefficients may exceed one and do not represent a subcatalog that can be removed without accounting for their masses.

In each fiber of m fix the points v=log(mq/Y)∈[0,log 2] of the primes q, P_m in number. Choose P_m=0 as empty fiber. For the others use the Fourier moments of the counting measure on that interval seen as a period of length log 2. For J=⌈C(log Y)^2⌉ there is a measure of the same mass on at most 2J+1 of the original points with identical moments up to |j|≤J: divide by P_m and apply the elementary Carathéodory theorem to the vectors of cosines and sines of dimension 2J. The construction is independent of the function to be integrated.

For the integrand Φ(v) w_m(Y exp v) the periodic extension is smooth because Φ is supported in the interior. By 8510 the Fourier coefficients have modulus ≤(C₁/H)exp(−c√|j|) uniformly. The uniform tail is O(H^(−1) exp(−c′√J)), c′>0. By positivity and coincidence of masses, the error in the fiber costs at most twice P_m times that tail. Since ΣP_m≤2YH for large Y (by integer counting, using Y/m≫1), the global error is O(Y exp(−c′√J)), o(1) taking C large enough. ≤(2J+1)#M_Y nodes are used, and #M_Y≤H Y^(.5+δ)=Y^(.5+o(1)) by 8336. If each quadrature weight is rounded to the nearest integer, the additional error is O(J #M_Y/H)=Y^(.5+o(1)); this does keep root precision with margin. By the uniformity of 8522 it also holds for the family of tests of the original weight L, summing bands and cofactors with total rounding error x^(.5+o(1)).

Arithmetic scope: the moments are the exact sums over primes of each fiber. The theorem does not obtain them from the continuous density, nor does it claim to compute the nodes in time proportional to their number. In particular it does not contradict the falsifier of 8556, whose weights lose uniform regularity. Estimating with sign the value of this quadrature against the scalar datum and the complement remains pending.

### Common table of root-scale primes for the moments of all fibers

The arithmetic data of 8568 are obtained without enumerating the products mq of the band. Put τ_j=2πj/log 2 and store B_j(n)=Σ_{p≤n}exp(iτ_j log p). For the band convention (Y,2Y] the exact moment at m is
    exp(iτ_j log(m/Y)) [B_j(⌊2Y/m⌋)−B_j(⌊Y/m⌋)].
All indices are ≤√Y, since m≥2√Y. The endpoints carry no weight in the interior tests. The frequencies are the same in all overlapping bands of 8522; only the exterior phase changes.

It suffices to store each real and imaginary component of the prefix with error ≤1. The difference of two prefixes gives error of modulus ≤2√2 per moment. If c_{m,j} are the Fourier coefficients of the test with its weight, Σ_j|c_{m,j}|≪1/H uniformly by 8568. Therefore the error, even summed in modulus AFTER evaluating each fiber, is O(#M_Y/H)=Y^(1/2+o(1)), without needing to construct the Carathéodory nodes. The tail |j|>C(log Y)² costs o(1). The formula keeps the phases and signs in the unrounded datum; it does not assume independence between prefix errors.

For one band, sieving the integers up to √Y and forming the prefixes by accumulating over primes costs O(√Y polylog Y) arithmetic operations, counting elementary evaluations at sufficient precision. It suffices to approximate each phase with error O(Y^(−2)) and use fixed-point accumulators with O(log Y) bits before storing the prefix with unit precision; rounding the accumulator to units after each prime does not have that guarantee. Enumerating M_Y does not require going through the mq either: sieve up to U=Y^(.5+δ), list the pairs rs (≤Y^(.21+o(1)) candidates) and for each pair look up the endpoints of t in the list of primes; afterwards only the #M_Y triples are traversed. Computing the data and their queries up to J thus costs Y^(1/2+o(1)) operations per band. The claim only prices the arithmetic part of the moments, not obtaining zeros, the coefficients of the test, nor the precision of the spectral construction. Summing as in 8522 keeps x^(1/2+o(1)).

Implementation check of the index and the phase, separate from the proof: Y=16384, m∈{130,137,145,180,213}, j=0,...,12, direct comparison with the list of primes in (Y/m,2Y/m]. Maximum observed error 4.2·10^(−13) before rounding prefixes, 1.057 as bound of the observed maximum after rounding both components to integers. These m test the prefix identity, not the asymptotic geometry of the catalog.

### Balanced bilinear form for the complete balance, without catalog or prime reference

Application of the classical hyperbola identity (higher-order antecedent in 5463) to the specific weight of 8090. Write S_total(x)=Σμ(n)L(n/x) and V(t)=L(t)−2L(2t). For large x take X=10x log x, M=⌊√X⌋. For any fixed 0<δ<1/2 one obtains
    S_total(x)−2S_total(x/2)=−Σ_{a,b≤M, ab>x^(1−δ), a≠b} μ(a)μ(b) K(ab/x)+O_δ(√x log x),
    K(t)=Σ_{j≥1}V(jt).
