Both factors of the sum lie between x^(1/2−δ)/√(10log x) and √(10x log x). The required estimate O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) for all ε>0 is equivalent to that estimate for the off-diagonal sum alone. The indicated error fits within any margin ε.

Proof. Let u=μ restricted to n≤M, 1 the constant function and e the convolution unit. On n≤X the identity μ=2u−u*u*1 follows from μ*(e−u*1)², supported above X since e−u*1 is supported on n≥M+1. The reading of this identity can be extended to all n at cost O(1) by the tail V(t)≪t exp(−2t) for t≥1 and the elementary majorant O(n²) of the coefficients. The term 2u costs O(M) by boundedness of V. The remaining double sum gives K exactly.

The step that balances the divisors is ∫V=0 together with the flatness of L at the origin. The extension of V by zero on the negative half-line is Schwartz: in a strict complex wedge the bounds of 8076 are proved by the same Taylor remainder (for |z|≥1, B(z)=O(1) uniformly in that wedge, by 8522). They give decay faster than every power at the flat end and exponential at the other; Cauchy on disks of radius proportional to |z| gives the bounds for all derivatives. Poisson for the lattice of step t gives K(t)=t^(−1)Σ_{h≠0} V̂(h/t), whence K(t)=O_r(t^r) on t≤1 for every fixed r. On t≥1 it is bounded by the original series. Therefore the part ab≤x^(1−δ) costs O_r(M² x^(−rδ)); choose r>1/(2δ). The diagonal costs O(M). Finally S_total=o(x) by 8546 and dominated convergence (all β<1). Telescoping the difference towards infinity with weights 2^(−j) recovers S_total at any exponent 1/2+ε<1, without loss. The bound for the pairs with a≠b has not been proved.

### Growing inertia within the balanced zone

The real symmetric matrix K(ab/x) of 8590 admits, for all large x, a principal submatrix with at least c log log x positive eigenvalues and as many negative ones, all separated from zero by a fixed constant. It can be taken with all indices squarefree, in the retained product region, and it also holds after setting the diagonal to zero. This rules out a proof by semidefiniteness of this auxiliary matrix.

Indeed K is not identically zero. By inversion over multiples, V(t)=Σμ(j)K(jt), absolutely at fixed t by the exponential tails. If V were zero, L(t)=2^n L(2^n t) would give L=0, contrary to 8100. Choose t₀ with κ=K(t₀)≠0. On the ideal mesh of indices √(t₀x)R^j with j=±1,...,±n, the entry at (i,j) is K(t₀R^(i+j)). The ideal matrix differs from κ times the permutation j↦−j in operator norm by ≤Σ_{l≠0}|K(t₀R^l)|, by the row-sum bound. The two tails of 8590 allow fixing R large so that this sum is <|κ|/4. The permutation has n eigenvalues of each sign. When removing the diagonal the same perturbation bound still holds because that permutation has no fixed points.

Take n=⌊log log x/(4 log R)⌋. Each ideal index A can be replaced by a squarefree integer in [A,A+A^(2/3)], since the squarefree counter is t/ζ(2)+O(√t) by elementary inversion. The indices are distinct, fit under M and all their products exceed x^(1−δ) for any fixed δ>0 eventually. The variation of an entry is O((min A)^(−1/3)): sup_{t>0}|tK′(t)| is finite by the series on t≥1 and by the differentiated Poisson formula with Schwartz transform on t≤1. Multiplying by 2n still gives o(1) in operator norm. The spectral comparison proves the statement with gap |κ|/2. Conjugating the matrix by the diagonal of the μ(a) of those indices preserves the eigenvalues exactly.

A second arithmetic restriction: all surviving representations of the same product n have identical sign μ(a)μ(b)=(−1)^Ω(n), since both factors are squarefree. Although the multiplicities change, grouping only within each product produces no cancellation. Inertia does not decide the balance evaluated at the specific Möbius vector over ALL indices; the compensation between distinct products remains pending.

### Sufficient spatial resolution of the Möbius vector in the complete form

For the bilinear form BEFORE removing the diagonal and the product cutoff of 8590, a single integer vector of O(x^(1/4)log x) rounded local sums suffices. The error in the form is O(√(x log x)). The transfer uses only |μ|≤1; the arithmetic difficulty lies in the collective values of that vector.

Let M be from 8590 and choose integer step h=max(1,⌊x^(1/4)/√log x⌋). On the mesh y_j=jh, j=0,...,J=⌈M/h⌉, distribute μ(a) between the two neighbors with the linear interpolation weights: b_j=Σ_{a≤M}μ(a)(1−|a−y_j|/h)_+. Extend K by K(0)=0. Sup |K″| is finite and so is ∫₀^∞|K′(t)|dt, by the two representations of 8590 differentiated at the ends. For each a,b interpolate K(ab/x) successively in the two coordinates. The linear error bound in one dimension and the positivity of the weights give uniform error O(h²(M+h)²/x²) per pair, without requiring a sign for the kernel. Thus the difference between the original bilinear form and Σ b_i b_j K(y_i y_j/x) is O(h² M²(M+h)²/x²)=O(√x log x) with that h. To obtain the finer announced budget take instead h=max(1,⌊x^(1/4)/log x⌋): it gives O(√x), with J=O(x^(1/4)(log x)^(3/2)). Alternatively keep the first h and improve the sum of curvatures as follows.

With the first h, for fixed b use on each cell the local supremum of |K″(ab/x)|. Its sum over a≤M is O(x/b+h), uniformly: on blocks of length h the step in the argument is hb/x=o(1), and the upper sum is O(1) after multiplying by the step, by integrability of K″ and K‴. The same bound holds on the mesh with mass ≤2h per node. Hence the error when interpolating the first direction is O(h² Σ_{b≤M}(b/x)²(x/b+h))=O(h² M²/x)=O(√x); for the second, the nodes y_i>0 carry mass ≤2h, and hΣ_{i≤J}y_i=O(M²), with zero contribution at y_i=0. This gives the same ceiling O(√x), keeping J=O(x^(1/4)log x).

Finally round C_j=Σ_{i≤j} b_i to the nearest integer and use d_j=round(C_j)−round(C_{j−1}), C_{−1}=0. Each prefix sum of d−b has modulus ≤1/2; by Abel, in each row the variation of K(y_i y_j/x) plus its supremum is O(1) uniformly, also at i=0. Since Σ|b_j|≤M and Σ|d_j|≤M+J+1, the substitution in both directions costs O(M). One obtains
    S_total(x)−2S_total(x/2)=−Σ d_i d_j K(y_i y_j/x)+O(√(x log x)).
Here the complete identity of 8590 is used, keeping the small and diagonal entries in the compressed sum; the term 2u costs O(M). This reduces the required signed datum to root scale with margin without introducing a split into catalog and complement. It does not yet provide the estimate of the form in d.

### O(log²x) complex integer samples for the complete bilinear form

Let P=4log x, τ_j=2πj/P, A_j=Σ_{a≤M}μ(a)a^(−iτ_j), and F(z)=(1−2z)²Q(z) as in 8546. Define the fixed coefficient
    B(s)=ζ(s)(1−2^(1−s))Γ(s)ζ′(s)F(2^(−s)).
The removable values are taken by continuity. For large x, with Z_j obtained by rounding separately the two components of A_j to the nearest integer, one has
    S_total(x)−2S_total(x/2)=−(1/P)Σ_{|τ_j|≤4log x} B(iτ_j)x^(iτ_j) Z_j² + O(√(x log x)).
The sum is real by conjugation. In particular it suffices to prove the root bound with margin for this signed combination of O(log²x) complex squares. The size of the list does not bound the moduli of its elements.

Proof of the symbol: for Re s>1 apply the Mellin in x with measure x^(−s−1)dx to 8095. In the prime reading the filter kills the line and allows integrating the exponential without subtracting x; in the Möbius one the Mellin of L divided by ζ(s) is obtained. The interchanges are absolute, by Σ|μ(n)|n^(−Re s)<∞ and the weighted absolute sum of the filter coefficients. The result is ∫L(t)t^(s−1)dt=Γ(s)ζ′(s)F(2^(−s)). By 8590 multiplying by (1−2^(1−s))ζ(s) gives the Mellin of K. This is entire by its two tails; continue up to the imaginary line. There B is bounded near zero and ≪(1+|τ|)^C exp(−π|τ|/2) by Stirling and polynomial growth of ζ and ζ′ in a fixed strip.

Periodize K(exp v) with period P. Its Fourier series, written with exponentials exp(−iτ_j v), has coefficients B(iτ_j)/P by direct integration and converges absolutely. For v=log(ab/x), with a,b≤M, the positive aliases have argument ≥x³ and exponential tail. The negative ones have argument ≤(M²/x)x^(−4) and sum to O(x^(−4)log x) by K(t)=O(t) at zero. Truncating at 4log x costs O(x^(−5)) uniformly for large x, by the decay of the symbol. Both errors even multiplied by M² are o(1). When summing with μ(a)μ(b) the Fourier term factorizes into A_j². By |A_j|≤M, rounding changes each square by O(M), and (1/P)Σ_j |B(iτ_j)|=O(1) uniformly. With the previous error of 8590 the claim follows. This transformation preserves the phase; an estimate through |A_j|² is a different and stronger obligation. Controlling the indicated combination remains pending.

### The first sample of any shifted mesh already detects the Mertens wall

In 8623 shift the mesh to τ_j=2π(j+θ_x)/P, with any θ_x∈[−1/2,1/2], even data-dependent. The complex representation still holds with the same error (take the real part if desired). It suffices to periodize exp(iτ₀v)K(exp v) and then demodulate; the aliases only acquire factors of modulus one. The coefficients are still B(iτ_j)/P in the demodulated series. Rounding keeps the same bound.

The absolute obligation
    (1/P) Σ_{|τ_j|≤4log x} |B(iτ_j)| |A_j|² = O_ε(x^(1/2+ε)) for all ε>0
is equivalent to RH, for ANY choice of those shifts. The same holds for the rounded samples. Indeed B(0)≠0: the factor (1−2^(−s)) inside Q(2^(−s)) exactly cancels the pole of Γ at zero, while ζ(0), ζ′(0), 1−2^(1−s) and the other factors have nonzero limits. Already the sample j=0 forces |Σ_{a≤M}μ(a)a^(−iτ₀)|≪_η M^(1/2+η) for all η>0, absorbing logarithms and adjusting ε, since |τ₀|≤π/P and M=⌊√(10x log x)⌋ runs through all large integers as x varies.

Justification of the step from a twisted sample of VARIABLE frequency. For each integer n choose the corresponding x and call t_n that frequency. If H(v)=Σ_{a≤v}μ(a), Abel gives
    |H(n)| ≤ |Σ_{a≤n}μ(a)a^(−it_n)| + |t_n| ∫₁ⁿ |H(v)|dv/v.
For α=1/2+η, take n large enough with |t_n|/α<1/2. Dividing by n^α the integral is dominated by (1/α) sup_{v≤n}|H(v)|/v^α. Taking the maximum up to any N and absorbing the half, with bounded initial values, one deduces H(n)=O_η(n^α). For all η this is the Mertens bound equivalent to RH. Conversely under RH, Abel gives |A_j|≪_η(1+|τ_j|) M^(1/2+η), and the mean of |B(iτ_j)|(1+|τ_j|)² is uniformly bounded by its exponential tail. Hence the absolute obligation with full margin. Rounding alters an individual modulus by O(1).

This audit does not rule out an arithmetic argument for that bound if it brought an independent idea of the same caliber. It does prevent presenting the polylogarithmic number of samples, or shifting the mesh to lose the exact term H(M), as a simplification of the pointwise obligation. The estimate that keeps the complex squares and their phases remains open.

### Cancellation between two modes of distinct poles and diagonal residue with multiplicity

In the COMPLETE bilinear form of 8590 evaluate the model vectors a^(s−1), b^(t−1), with s,t fixed interior to the strip. Write Z=M²/x and B as in 8623. For the integral over [0,M]² the substitution u=ab/x gives, if s≠t,
    [M^(s−t)x^t B_Z(t)−M^(t−s)x^s B_Z(s)]/(s−t),   B_Z(v)=∫₀^Z K(u)u^(v−1)du.
On confluence, the value is x^s[B_Z(s)log Z−B_Z′(s)]. Replacing B_Z by B costs o(1) for s,t fixed in compacts, also with derivatives of fixed order, by Z∼10log x and the exponential decay of K. The quotient is continued on the diagonal by differentiation.

The passage to sums over integers introduces O_{s,t}((1+log x)^C x^((Re s+Re t−1)/2)). Indeed when fixing b the sum-versus-integral error in a is controlled by the variation of a^(s−1)K(ab/x), at most C_s(x/b)^(Re s−1) on scaling the variable, using flatness at zero and decay at infinity. Summing with b^(Re t−1) up to M and repeating with the variables interchanged in the other direction gives the indicated ceiling. Derivatives of fixed order cost only additional powers of log x. In particular the error is o(√x) for two fixed points of real part <1.

For a zero ρ of ζ, let u_ρ(a)=Res_{s=ρ} a^(s−1)/ζ(s). It is a well-defined model vector without requiring μ to be a sum of those vectors. In the bilinear value for u_ρ,u_σ with distinct zeros, the main term is ZERO: take both residues in the previous quotient with B instead of B_Z and divide by ζ(s)ζ(t). Each summand is holomorphic in at least one of the two variables in the pair, since B/ζ is holomorphic there. For the same zero ρ, of multiplicity m, put ζ(ρ+v)=c v^m+O(v^(m+1)) and D(s)=(1−2^(1−s))Γ(s)F(2^(−s)). Then B(ρ+v)=D(ρ)m c² v^(2m−1)+O(v^(2m)). In the difference quotient, the first nonzero homogeneous part is
    −x^ρ D(ρ)m c² Σ_{j=0}^{2m−2}(s−ρ)^j(t−ρ)^(2m−2−j).
The exponential factors of M,x only modify higher orders. When dividing by ζ(s)ζ(t) and taking the two residues only j=m−1 enters; the result is −m x^ρ D(ρ). Thus, up to o(√x) for each fixed pair, the interactions between distinct poles disappear, while each self-interaction reproduces exactly the coefficient of the zero in the global formula of the difference of 8590, with the exterior sign of that identity. This includes multiple zeros without dividing by ζ′(ρ). The computation does not authorize expanding the Möbius vector in modes nor summing the errors over infinitely many pairs: an arithmetic estimate for the real vector is missing.

### Mixed interaction of the real arithmetic vector with a residual mode

Denote by Q_x(f,g)=Σ_{a,b≤M} f(a)g(b)K(ab/x) the symmetric form without conjugation of 8590. For each fixed nontrivial zero ρ of multiplicity m,
    Q_x(μ,u_ρ)=−m D(ρ)x^ρ + o_ρ(√x),
with D and u_ρ from 8649. In particular Q_x(μ−u_ρ,u_ρ)=o_ρ(√x). This uses the genuine function μ without postulating a spectral expansion of the vector.

To see it first replace Σ_{b≤M} b^(s−1)K(ab/x) by the integral from 0 to M. On a small fixed circle around ρ contained in the strip, with Re s≤β₁<1, the sum of errors in a, even in modulus, is O_ρ(x^(β₁/2)log^C x)=o(√x) by the scaled variation of 8649 and |μ(a)|≤1. The same bound holds when taking the residue after dividing by ζ(s) using that circle free of other zeros. Completing each integral in b up to infinity gives (x/a)^s B(s); its residue after dividing by ζ(s) is zero because B/ζ=Dζ′ is regular. What remains is therefore the NEGATIVE of the integral over b≥M. In this tail integral one can extend to a>M at cost o(1) on the circle: by K(t)≪t exp(−2t) for t≥1, ab/x≥M²/x∼10log x, and the geometric sums and integrals give a negative power of x even after the polynomial factors. For example reserve exp(−M²/x) and bound the sum/integral with exp(−ab/x) by O(x³) for 0<Re s<1.

Now use the pointwise inversion Σ_{a≥1} μ(a)K(ab/x)=V(b/x) of 8601, absolutely convergent also under the integral over b≥M. Thus the pending residue is that of −∫_M^∞ b^(s−1)V(b/x)db/ζ(s). Restoring 0≤b≤M costs o(1) by flatness of V at zero. The Mellin of V is B(s)/ζ(s)=D(s)ζ′(s) by 8623; the result is exactly the residue of −x^sD(s)ζ′(s)/ζ(s), as claimed.

For any fixed FINITE set E of distinct zeros, taking each residual mode only once (its definition incorporates the multiplicity), let r_E=μ−Σ_{ρ∈E}u_ρ. By 8649 and the mixed identity, Q_x(r_E,u_ρ)=o_E(√x) for each ρ∈E and
    Q_x(μ,μ)=Q_x(r_E,r_E)−Σ_{ρ∈E} mult(ρ)D(ρ)x^ρ+o_E(√x).
Choose E stable under conjugation to obtain a real identity. It is a direct finite extraction within the arithmetic form. No uniform control of the errors as E grows was obtained, nor a bound for the form of the remaining vector.

### Joint extraction up to logarithmic height with uniform error at root scale with margin

For each large x one can choose T∈[log x,log x+1] and form U_T(a)=Σ_{|Imρ|<T} Res_{s=ρ} a^(s−1)/ζ(s), summing once per distinct zero. For Q_x of 8661 and R_T=μ−U_T,
    Q_x(R_T,U_T)=O(x^(1/2+o(1))),    Q_x(R_T,R_T)=O(x^(1/2+o(1))).
The second bound uses the spectral formula of the total; it provides no independent estimate of the extracted part. Neither simplicity of the zeros nor a bound for the individual residues is assumed.

Use the rectangle with verticals −1/2 and 1+1/log x and horizontals ±T. On its boundary |1/ζ(s)|≤x^o(1). On the right the absolute series suffices and on the left the functional equation and the absolute series at 3/2. To detail the height, in [log x,log x+1] avoid intervals of radius c/log²(2+log x) around the nearby ordinates, possible by the unit count O(log(2+log x)). On that horizontal the classical local formula ζ′/ζ(s)=Σ_{|T−Imρ|≤1}1/(s−ρ)+O(log T) in a bounded strip (by the logarithmic derivative of the completed function, subtracting its value at 2+iT) gives O(log³ T). Integrating from 2+iT along the horizontal gives |1/ζ|≤exp(O(log³ T))=x^o(1). The boundaries have length O(log x). The pole of ζ at 1 is not a singularity of 1/ζ.

Uniform control of the quadratures of 8649 and 8661 on the boundary. For 1≤a≤M the error of replacing the sum over b by an integral is O((1+T)(x/a)^(Re s−1))=O(1+T), by variation after the change b↦ab/x, with constants uniform in −1/2≤Re s≤1+1/log x thanks to both tails of K. The arithmetic multipliers μ(a) are bounded, and so is |a^(t−1)|≤O(1) on the boundary. For the second direction of the double integral quadrature, first restrict the already integrated variable to [1,M], where its weight is O(1); what is omitted in (0,1) costs O(x^(−2)) by flatness of K, with a fixed sufficiently large power and the other variable ≤M. One obtains O(M polylog x) before the contour integrations. The extensions in the tails ab≥M² of 8661 and of B_Z in 8649 remain negligible: the truncated double integral can be estimated using the bound for the difference quotient near the diagonal by differentiation (or its integral along the segment), with powers of log x; the moduli of the factors depend only on the real parts. Equivalently, for B_Z in 8649 the numerator is written as M^(s+t) times the difference of Z^(−v)(B_Z(v)−B(v)) at v=s,t, whose derivative is exponentially small. The extension in (0,M) of V in 8661 again uses its flatness. When integrating each error with one or two factors 1/ζ over the boundary, it remains x^(1/2+o(1)).

For the main terms, at fixed x there are finitely many residues and the exact computation of each is that of 8649–8661; the errors were integrated jointly, without summing them over individual circles. For Q_x(μ,U_T) and Q_x(U_T,U_T) one obtains the same value −Σ_{|Imρ|<T} mult(ρ)D(ρ)x^ρ with error x^(1/2+o(1)). This proves the first bound. Moreover, 8546 applied to the difference (1−2S) and 8590 give for Q_x(μ,μ) that same value with error O(M+√x): by Stirling all zeros above T≥log x cost O(√x) even in modulus. Expanding Q_x(R_T,R_T) gives the second bound. The dangerous contribution remains entirely in Q_x(U_T,U_T); to exclude it independent arithmetic information is still missing.

### Smooth cutoff: direct estimate of the samples of the residual vector

Take w real, 0≤w≤1, equal to 1 up to 1 and zero from 2 on, with Gevrey-2 derivative in logarithmic coordinate. Use u(a)=μ(a)w(a/M) in the identity of 8590: e−u*1 is still supported from M+1 and 2u costs O(M). The complete form now carries w(a/M)w(b/M) and a,b≤2M. The periodization of 8623 keeps the same period and the cutoff 4log x, since the maximal product only changes by a factor four.

There is a good height T∈[(log x)^4,(log x)^4+1] such that, uniformly for |τ|≤4log x,
    |Σ_{a≤2M} w(a/M)(μ(a)−U_T(a)) a^(−iτ)| ≤ x^o(1).
This is obtained before forming the bilinear form. In particular, for the form with the two smooth cutoffs, the remainder against itself costs x^o(1), and its cross term with μ costs x^(1/2+o(1)), without using the explicit formula of P_e or subtracting the total balance.

Proof. Let W(z) be the Mellin of w, continued by −(1/z)∫w′(t)t^z dt. It has a unique simple pole at 0 and on −1≤Re z≤2, |Im z|≥1, it costs O(exp(−c√|Im z|)) by Gevrey in log t. In the rectangle of 8675 with the new good height sup|1/ζ|≤exp(O((log log x)^3)) still holds. Inverse Mellin gives the real twisted sum of μ as the integral on the right vertical of M^(s−iτ) W(s−iτ)/ζ(s), with measure ds/(2πi). It coincides with its integral over the whole oriented boundary of the rectangle up to O(x^o(1)): the horizontals and the right tails cost o(1) because √T≍(log x)^2 and the left vertical costs O(M^(−1/2) x^o(1)). The pole s=iτ is kept inside the rectangle, without estimating its residue separately.

On the other hand, the twisted sum of the vector U_T is exactly the integral over the same boundary with numerator Σ_{a≥1} w(a/M)a^(s−1−iτ). The difference between this numerator and ∫₁^∞ w(t/M)t^(s−1−iτ)dt is O((1+T)log(2M)) on the boundary, by the variation on [1,2M], using Re s≤1+1/log x. This ordinary integral is M^(s−iτ)W(s−iτ)−1/(s−iτ) by continuation, since w is one on [0,1/M] after scaling. On the boundary |s−iτ|≥1/2. Multiplying by 1/ζ and integrating, with length O(T), proves the uniform ceiling for the difference of samples. Also sup_{1≤a≤2M}|U_T(a)|≤x^o(1) by the contour representation and a^(Re s−1)≪1. Therefore the aliasing and truncation errors of 8623 remain o(1) even for the residual products. The absolute sum of normalized Fourier coefficients is O(1); the sample-by-sample bound just proved and the trivial ceiling O(M) for the sample of μ give the two bilinear claims.

The increase of the contour height is deliberate and the result requires the smooth cutoff. The ceiling x^o(1) is for the samples of the vector after removing its modes, not for the samples of μ. The form on U_T still carries the sign obligation and its root bound has not been obtained.

### Cancellation of the cross term by Mellin inversion in the continuous moment

With M,w,W from 8687, write A(τ)=Σ μ(a)w(a/M)a^(−iτ). Define J(τ) as the sum of residues of M^(s−iτ)W(s−iτ)/ζ(s) at the nontrivial zeros with |Im s|<H, for the good height H of 8687. These are moments of the continuous modes. B is the Mellin of K. For x→∞ one obtains

    S_total(x)−2S_total(x/2)
      = −(1/2π)∫_{|τ|≤4log x} B(iτ)x^(iτ) J(τ)^2 dτ + O(x^(−1/4+o(1))).

Proof. Shift the Mellin of A to Re s=−3/2. The first trivial zero is at −2. The pole of W gives h(τ)=1/ζ(iτ). Thus A=J+h+E, with E≪M^(−3/2)x^o(1) uniformly in the band. Indeed, on the new vertical the inverse of ζ has polynomial growth by the functional equation. W decays like exp(−c√|Im z|) outside a neighborhood of the real axis, uniformly in this fixed strip by Gevrey integration by parts. The left integral costs M^(−3/2)(1+|τ|)^C. On the horizontals the bound of the good height of 8687 is kept, extended down to −3/2 by the functional equation on the added stretch. The decay exp(−c√H) absorbs any fixed power of x.

The form Q with the two smooth cutoffs is the integral of B(iτ)x^(iτ)A(τ)^2 over the line with measure dτ/(2π). Replacing A²−J² by 2Ah−h² in the band costs O(M^(−1/2)x^o(1)) by |A|≤2M and the integrability of B. To extend A², Ah and h² to the whole line the tails cost O(x^(1−2π+o(1))) by 8623 and the polynomial growth of h (functional equation and classical bound of 1/ζ on Re s=1 at large heights). In the mixed integral, B/ζ is the Mellin of V. By inversion one is left with Σ μ(a)w(a/M)V(a/x), which costs O_N(x^(−N)) for every fixed N by flatness at zero. In the pure integral B/ζ² is shifted to −3/2, at cost O(x^(−3/2)): in the closed strip there are no zeros of ζ and B is rapidly decreasing on verticals, by the Schwartz property and flatness of K in 8590. The inverse of ζ grows at most polynomially in the strip by the functional equation and the classical zero-free region near Re s=1. This proves the approximation of Q. Finally the linear term of the hyperbola identity is the same flat reading of V, and the tail from 10x log x costs O(x^(−15)) by the majorant of 8590. The formula with its minus sign follows.

The absolute precision tends to zero. The pending global estimate is that of the integral of J² at scale x^(1/2+ε) for all ε>0. J² is a complex square with oscillating weight. The computation identifies a cancellation of the representation error and does not give that estimate.

### Arithmetic obstruction to taking moduli in the long variable of the hyperbola

Take A=⌈exp(2√log x)⌉, Y=⌊10x log x/A⌋ and R_A(t)=Σ_{a≤A}μ(a)K(at)−V(t). One has simultaneously
    S_total(x)−2S_total(x/2)=−Σ_{b≤Y} μ(b)R_A(b/x)+o(1),
    Σ_{b≤Y}|μ(b)R_A(b/x)| = x^(1+o(1)).
The second claim is unconditional and refers to the effective arithmetic weights, even when omitting the non-squarefree ones.

For the first identity use u=μ up to A, v=μ up to Y, both zero afterwards. The difference between μ and u+v−u*v*1 is μ*(e−u*1)*(e−v*1), with support from (A+1)(Y+1)>10x log x. The tail costs o(1) as in 8590. The term u read against V(n/x) is o(1) by flatness. Grouping the other two terms gives the indicated sign.

Fix a nontrivial zero ρ of multiplicity m, β=Reρ. The Mellin of R_A is B(s)Σ_{a≤A}μ(a)a^(−s)−B(s)/ζ(s). At ρ, B has order 2m−1 and B/ζ order m−1, with nonzero coefficient by 8546 and 8657. The derivative of order m−1 of the Mellin of R_A at ρ is therefore a nonzero constant independent of A. It is the integral of R_A(t)t^(ρ−1)(log t)^(m−1) over t>0. Simplicity is not needed.

The part t<A^(−2) costs o(1): by flatness of K,V one has |R_A(t)|≪_k A^(k+1)t^k and k=3 suffices. For t>Y/x use inversion over multiples of 8590, R_A(t)=−Σ_{a>A}μ(a)K(at). There At≥(10−o(1))log x. The bound |K(u)|≪exp(−u) for u≥1 gives |R_A(t)|≪(1+1/t)exp(−At). Integrating with the previous weight costs o(1), by A=x^o(1) and the change u=At. On the remaining interval the modulus of the weight costs at most A^2(1+2log A)^(m−1) for large x. One deduces ∫₀^(Y/x)|R_A(t)|dt ≫_ρ A^(−2)(1+2log A)^(1−m).

The total variation of |R_A| is O(A) by invariance of the variation of K(at) under dilation and the integrability of K′,V′ (Poisson and the tails of 8590). Its supremum is also O(A). The squarefree count up to y is y/ζ(2)+O(√y+1) by inversion over squares. Partial summation gives for the total modulus x/ζ(2) times the unweighted integral, with error O(A(1+√Y)). The main term dominates this error and is ≥x^(1−o(1)); the trivial ceiling AY is x^(1+o(1)). The obstruction is proved. For this choice of factors any root-scale proof must recover cancellation in b, even after carrying out exactly the short sum and the hyperbola corrector term.

### The moduli barrier reaches the balanced hyperbola and all fixed-power splittings

Let A be an integer, A=x^(α+o(1)), 0<α<1 fixed, and Y,R_A as in 8714. For any fixed zero of real part β and each ε>0,
    Σ_{b≤Y}|μ(b)R_A(b/x)| ≫ x^(1−α(1−β)−ε).
In particular A=⌊√(10x log x)⌋ gives a floor x^(3/4−ε) using a zero with β≥1/2 (symmetry). The signed identity of 8714 keeps error o(1) because A/x tends to zero like a power. The novelty with respect to 8714 is the transfer of the continuous moment even when the global variation loses the main term.

Fix small η>0 with 1−α(1+η)>0. In the invariant moment of 8714 the tail up to A^(−1−η) costs O(A^{1−ηk−(1+η)β}(1+log A)^(m−1)) by flatness of order k; take k large. On t>Y/x the bound of 8714 still gives o(1): with u=At the majorized integrand is O(A^(1−β)(1+u)^C(1+log A)^C exp(−u)) for u≥(10−o(1))log x. Therefore on b∈[b₀,Y], b₀=x A^(−1−η), the integral of |R_A(b/x)| in db is ≫ x A^{−(1+η)(1−β)}(1+log A)^(1−m). It comes from dividing the nonzero moment by the supremum of the weight and changing t=b/x.

To transfer this mass to the squarefree integers divide [Y/2,Y], [Y/4,Y/2], etc., until b₀ is included (the last lower endpoint lies between b₀/2 and b₀). In each block [B,2B] form cells of equal length h comparable to B^(3/4). Repeated boundaries are counted at most twice. There is a fixed κ>0 such that always B≥x^κ. For each fixed j, b^j |(d/db)^j R_A(b/x)|≪_j A, since u^j K^(j)(u) and u^j V^(j)(u) are bounded by 8590 (differentiate Poisson near zero). In each cell the Taylor polynomial up to degree d has uniform error O_d(A B^{−(d+1)/4})=O(x^(−2)) by choosing d fixed large enough depending on κ.

Divide a cell into 2d+2 equal subintervals. Each contains ≫_d h squarefree integers, by the count with error O(√B). In every other subinterval choose a squarefree integer where the modulus of R_A is minimal. Each value is ≤C_d/h times the sum of moduli over the squarefree integers of the cell. The d+1 points are separated by at least h/(2d+2), so the Lagrange interpolation bases cost O_d(1) on the whole cell. Interpolating the Taylor polynomial at those points bounds the integral of the modulus of the function by C_d times the sum over squarefree integers plus O_d(h x^(−2)). The total error is o(1). This transfers the continuous floor without the term A√Y of the global estimate by variation. Taking η small enough for the given ε concludes.

The result quantifies the loss when discarding the signs of the last variable, even after summing the first one exactly. Nothing in the argument forces the signed sum to have that size.

### Signed cancellation relative to the effective mass of rows

For each fixed splitting of 8729 and some c_α>0, unconditionally,
    |Σ_{b≤Y} μ(b) R_A(b/x)| ≤ exp(−c_α √log x) Σ_{b≤Y} |μ(b) R_A(b/x)|
for x large enough. The denominator keeps the exact signed sum of the short variable inside each modulus. Thus the positive contributions and the magnitudes of the negative ones each represent (1/2+O(exp(−c_α√log x))) of the effective mass. The relative saving is still subpower.

Proof. Choose 0<κ<(1−α)/2. Split from Y downwards into dyadic blocks (D,2D] until the smallest D lies between x^κ/2 and x^κ. The absolute sum over the remaining b costs O(x^(−3)) by |R_A(b/x)|≪_k A(Ab/x)^k, choosing k fixed large enough. In a block, f(z)=R_A(z/x) is holomorphic and O(A) on the disk |z−3D/2|≤D: there |arg z|≤arcsin(2/3)<π/2 and the inverse Mellins of K,V on Re s=0 are absolutely convergent with exponential margin, uniformly in the modulus of the argument (8623, and the same symbol without ζ for V). Taylor of degree d=⌈C log x⌉ at the center gives a real polynomial p with uniform error O(x^(−4)) on the segment, because the ratio of radii is 1/2.

Put I=∫_D^(2D)|p(u)|du. Markov's inequality on the interval gives sup|p′|≤2d² sup|p|/D. A stretch of length ≫D/d² next to a point of maximum has |p|≥sup|p|/2, even if the maximum is at an endpoint. Thus sup|p|+Var(p)≪d⁴ I/D. Also Var(|p|)≤Var(p). Abel and the classical unconditional Mertens bound |Σ_{n≤u}μ(n)|≪u exp(−c√log u) give
    |Σ_{D<b≤2D} μ(b)p(b)| ≪ d⁴ exp(−c√log D) I.
Abel with the squarefree count gives Σ μ²(b)|p(b)|=I/ζ(2)+O(d⁴ I/√D) on that same block. The key is that the variation cost is controlled by I, even if the polynomial has small amplitude. Replacing p by f in the two sums costs O(D x^(−4)) per block. Summing, absorbing the logarithmic powers into the exponential using D≥x^κ/2 and absorbing the additive error by the floor of 8729 proves the claim.

Comparison with 8436: there Abel controls the error of replacing a prime count by continuous density. Here the Möbius signs are compared directly with the modulus of the same row after carrying out all cancellations of the short factor. The use of the classical Mertens bound leaves open the gain of a fixed power.

### Exact exponent of the relative cancellation in the rows

Fix 0<α<1 and A=x^(α+o(1)) integer. Put Θ=sup Reρ over the nontrivial zeros, D_x=Σ_{b≤Y}|μ(b)R_A(b/x)| and N_x=|Σ_{b≤Y}μ(b)R_A(b/x)|. Then
    lim log D_x/log x = 1−α(1−Θ),
    limsup log(N_x/D_x)/log x = −(1−α)(1−Θ),
taking log 0=−∞. The first formula holds at all large scales. The second is an upper limit exponent, so it allows stronger cancellations at particular scales.

Indeed, the classical Mertens theorem in a zero-free half-plane (used in 6270) gives sup_{u≤A}|Σ_{n≤u}μ(n)|≪_ε A^(Θ+ε); for Θ=1 the trivial ceiling suffices. Abel against K(at) in the variable a costs a constant uniform in t by boundedness and finite total variation of K. Hence sup_t |R_A(t)|≪_ε A^(Θ+ε) and D_x≪_ε YA^(Θ+ε). The floor of 8729 is applied first to a fixed zero with β arbitrarily close to Θ and then the lower limit is taken. It does not require the existence of a zero attaining the supremum.

For the numerator, 8714 identifies the signed sum, up to sign and o(1), with G(x)=Σ μ(n)V(n/x). Abel against V(n/x) and the same Mertens theorem give G(x)≪_ε x^(Θ+ε) by ∫₀^∞ t^(Θ+ε)|V′(t)|dt<∞. For the converse direction, the Mellin ∫₀^∞ G(x)x^(−s−1)dx is V̂_M(s)/ζ(s) on Re s>1, with V̂_M(s)=∫V(t)t^(s−1)dt. By 8623 this quotient is (1−2^(1−s))Γ(s)F(2^(−s))ζ′(s)/ζ(s). It has a simple pole at each nontrivial zero, even if multiple: the prefactor is nonzero there by 8546. The part x<1 of the integral is entire by exponential decay. A bound G(x)=O(x^σ) with σ<Θ would continue the integral holomorphically to Re s>σ, contradicting a pole. Thus limsup log N_x/log x=Θ. Subtracting the ordinary limit of the denominator gives the second equality.

Verifiable consequence for the balanced cutoff: the global sign is equivalent to N_x/D_x≪_ε x^(−1/4+ε) for all ε>0. More generally, any fixed saving δ>0 with losses ε in the quotient forces Θ≤1−δ/(1−α). The subpower saving of 8743 is compatible even with Θ=1. These identities fix the threshold of the route; they do not supply the arithmetic inequality that would reach it.

### Proof at sparse scales and limit of optimizing real dilations

Let A≥2. Approximate V(t) by ∫_[1,A] K(ut)dν(u), where ν is any real signed measure of total variation ≤A^C, for a fixed C≥1. Let d_C(A) be the infimum of the L¹(dt) norm of the error E(t). Then
    lim_{A→∞} log d_C(A)/log A = Θ−1.
The same limit holds when requiring ν=Σ_{a≤A} c_a δ_a with |c_a|≤1. The result allows choosing real scales, weights and signs adaptively. In particular it would suffice to construct, for ONE sequence A_j→∞, admissible measures with error ≤A_j^(−1/2+o(1)). The allowed growth A^C must have a fixed exponent.

For the lower bound the Mellin of the approximant is B(s)∫u^(−s)dν(u). The second factor is entire by compactness of the support, so the derivative of order m−1 of the Mellin of the error at each zero ρ is still the same nonzero constant of 8714. Fix η>0. By flatness, on t<A^(−1−η) one has |E(t)|≪_k (1+A^(C+k))t^k. The error in that moment up to that endpoint costs O(A^{C−kη−(1+η)β}(1+log A)^(m−1)), which tends to zero by choosing k large. From there to infinity the modulus of t^(ρ−1)(log t)^(m−1) costs O_ρ(A^((1+η)(1−β))(1+log A)^(m−1)), since β<1. Dividing the moment by this bound gives the floor uniform over all admissible measures. Pass first to the liminf, then η→0 and β→Θ.

For the upper bound ν=Σ_{a≤A} μ(a)δ_a suffices. By Abel as in 8757, sup|E|≪_ε A^(Θ+ε). Integrate up to 10log A/A. From that endpoint the inversion over multiples of 8590 gives |E|≪(1+1/t)exp(−At), integrable at cost O(A^(−9)). Thus bounded integer weights already attain the upper exponent, which coincides with the lower one also in the continuous class. By symmetry Θ≥1/2. The existence of the indicated sequence forces Θ=1/2, and conversely if Θ=1/2 any sequence can be taken.

Index antecedents: P33-8 and L18 already record approximation by dilations and the entry on factorial readings controls an L¹ distance with another kernel. The specific conclusion here is the stability of the exponent for this pair K,V even when passing from Möbius coefficients to real signed measures of polynomial mass. The added freedom allows choosing the construction without reproducing μ; the sequence with unconditional root rate has not been exhibited.

Precise bibliographic identification: K is literally the Müntz transform P[V] of Báez-Duarte because ∫V=0. His article deals with approximation by dilations in L². The kinship is in the operator itself. Reference: Luis Báez-Duarte, A general strong Nyman–Beurling criterion for the Riemann hypothesis, https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0505453.

### The Euler product of the primorial admits no repair with a fixed number of dilations

Take A=∏_{p≤y}p, ν_y=Σ_{d|A} μ(d)δ_d in the L¹ problem of 8770. For each fixed integer k≥0 and all y large enough, adding to ν_y up to k real masses of arbitrary weights and positions u>0 leaves L¹ error at least c_k/log y. This holds even if the parameters depend on y without size bound. In particular calibrating exactly the total mass with one dilation does not remove the obstruction at neighboring frequencies. Since log A∼y, the floor is of order 1/loglog A for fixed k.

Let P_y(s)=∏_{p≤y}(1−p^(−s)) and ℓ=log y. At s=1+iz/ℓ for fixed real z,
    ℓ(1/ζ(s)−P_y(s)) → g(iz),
    g(w)=w−exp(−γ) exp(∫₀¹ (1−exp(−wu))du/u).
Indeed, ℓ/ζ(1+w/ℓ)→w and ℓP_y(1)→exp(−γ) by the Mertens product. In the logarithm of the quotient P_y(s)/P_y(1), the prime-power terms of order ≥2 tend to zero by dominated convergence. The prime term is Σ_{p≤y}(1−exp(−iz log p/ℓ))/p. On δ≤log p/ℓ≤1 one passes to the integral by partial summation and PNT. The remaining stretch costs O_z(δ+1/ℓ) by Σ_{p≤v}(log p)/p≪log(2v). This gives the limit also at z=0 by continuity.

The function h(z)=g(iz) has real translations of infinite rank. Indeed, if its space of translations had finite dimension, it would be closed under uniform convergence on compacts and stable under differentiation (difference quotients). The characteristic polynomial of differentiation would give a linear differential equation with constant coefficients. Therefore h and g would be exponential polynomials, of growth at most exponential in a power of the modulus. But at w=−r+iπ the real part of the integral in g is ≳exp(r)/r for large r: on [3/4,1] the cosine is negative, the last stretch of length 1/r contributes ≫exp(r)/r, and on [0,3/4] the modulus of the integrand is ≤|w| exp(3r/4) using (1−exp(−wu))/u=w∫₀¹exp(−wuv)dv. The outer exponential contradicts the ceiling. Thus for each k there are k+1 independent translations h(z+v_j) and k+1 real points z_i where the evaluation matrix is invertible (the row vectors span the whole space by independence).

Each added atom contributes at those frequencies z_i+v_j a separable matrix, since u^(−1−i(z_i+v_j)/ℓ) is a product of two phases times 1/u. The matrix of all correctors, even multiplied by ℓ, has rank ≤k. The limit matrix [g(i(z_i+v_j))] has positive distance to the closed set of such matrices. Therefore at at least one of the fixed frequencies the discrepancy between 1/ζ and the corrected multiplier is ≥c_k/ℓ. To turn it into an L¹ floor multiply by B(s), continuous and nonzero at 1: B(1)=(log 2)∫L≠0 by 8100 and 8623. Since |t^(s−1)|=1, the modulus of the Mellin error costs at most the L¹ norm of the error in t. This proves the claim. The argument only treats the primorial with a bounded number of correctors, without deciding the case of corrections whose number grows.

### Constructive repair of the primorial with sparse integer dilations

With A=∏_{p≤y}p as in 8784, there is an explicitly constructible correction on O((log A)^(3/2)) integer positions giving L¹ error ≤exp(−c√log A) for some unconditional c>0. With O((log A)²) positions the optimal exponent Θ−1+o(1) of 8770 is reproduced. In both cases each added position is a squarefree integer ≤A missing from the primorial (it does not divide A), the weight has the sign of μ there, and the total variation of the corrected measure is ≤A. The number of positions counts only those added to the initial product.

Indeed, the difference between ν_y and the target measure Σ_{a≤A}μ(a)δ_a is corrected by adding the squarefree integers not dividing A with their weights μ. Compress that addition in each block D≤a<2D, D a power of 2, separately for positive and negative μ. For each nonempty group, the mean of the vectors (a,a²,…,a^d) is a convex combination of at most d+1 of those same vectors. Constructively, start with unit weights; while more than d+1 nodes remain, take a dependence among their columns (1,a,…,a^d) and add a multiple until one weight vanishes while keeping non-negativity. Keep the external signs. The mass of the group and its moments up to order d remain exact, also in the last incomplete block. These operations can be carried out over the rationals. This is a use of the method of moments of 8568 for the dilations themselves; it does not presuppose cancellation of the signs within each group.

For simultaneous control of all t, the function u↦K(ut) is analytic on the disk |u−3D/2|≤D. On that disk |K(ut)|≪min(1,(Dt)^(−2)), by inversion on the verticals 0 and 2: the angle is bounded by arcsin(2/3), the symbol B of 8623 has Stirling decay on both verticals and the removable singularities are taken by continuity. Taylor up to degree d at 3D/2 gives pointwise error ≪2^(−d)min(1,(Dt)^(−2)) for real u in the block. The integral of the majorant is O(2^(−d)/D). In the difference between the original group and the compressed one only the remainder intervenes, with total mass of the two measures O(D). Summing the blocks, the L¹ cost of the compression is O(2^(−d)log A) with O((d+1)log A) nodes.

For the uncompressed Möbius target, Abel and the classical Mertens bound give sup_t|Σ_{a≤A}μ(a)K(at)−V(t)|≪ A exp(−c₀√log A), using uniform variation and the maximum of the prefix up to A. Integrate up to 10log A/A and from there use the exponential tail of 8770. Choosing d=⌈√log A⌉ and reducing c gives the first claim. Choosing d=⌈4log A⌉ makes the compression cost O(A^(−2)); the upper bound for Möbius and the uniform lower bound of 8770 give the indicated exponent for this construction. The compressed weights at each node may exceed one, but the total absolute mass is preserved exactly. The procedure uses the Möbius signs up to A and only compresses their representation; it does not by itself obtain the root rate.

### Choice of the weights without Möbius data via two fixed meshes

For A large enough there is a real linear program whose coefficient block has O(log² A) columns of predetermined dilations and O(log⁵ A) observation rows. Its optimal value q_A satisfies log q_A/log A→Θ−1. It uses exclusively values of K,V and geometric weights. A feasible set of weights with value A^(−1/2+o(1)) along an unbounded sequence would certify the rate in the complete integral. This is the size of the matrix, without an estimate of the cost of evaluating its entries.

Construction. On each octave of [1,A] (trimming the last one and omitting degenerate intervals) use d+1 Chebyshev nodes of the first kind, d=⌈100 log A⌉. To justify that good weights exist on this fixed mesh, interpolate u↦K(ut) on each block. The Taylor estimate in 8797 and the reproduction of polynomials give integrated error O((1+Λ_d)2^(−d)/D) on [D,2D], also on the last interval by restriction. Here Λ_d is the Lebesgue constant, O(log(d+2)) for these nodes. Replace the Möbius measure of 8770 by the weights obtained by integrating each Lagrange basis function against that measure. Their total variation is ≤AΛ_d≤A² and the L¹ cost of the replacement is O((1+Λ_d)2^(−d)log A). The Möbius measure enters only in the proof of existence of a competitor.

To choose weights c_i, impose Σ|c_i|≤A² and set E(t)=V(t)−Σc_i K(u_i t). Split [A^(−2),10log A] into octaves, trimming the last one, and each block J into n=⌈1000(d+1)^4⌉ equal parts with centers t_j and length h_j. Minimize Σ h_j |E(t_j)|, which is linearizable with auxiliary variables. For any feasible c one has, with absolute constants,
    ∥E∥₁ ≪ Σ h_j |E(t_j)| + O(A^(−3)),
    Σ h_j |E(t_j)| ≪ ∥E∥₁ + O(A^(−3)).
At the lower end use |E(t)|≪_k(1+A^(2+k))t^k with k=4; from 10log A on use |K(u_i t)|+|V(t)|≪exp(−t). On each octave J⊂[D,2D] the angular analyticity of 8797 for K,V gives a Taylor polynomial p of degree d with pointwise error O((1+A²)2^(−d)). It is applied in the variable t, uniformly in all the u_i. By Markov, sup|p′|≤2d²sup|p|/|J| and sup|p|≤8d² ∫_J|p|/|J| (stretch next to a maximum). The error of the midpoint rule for |p| costs at most (|J|/n)Var_J(p)≤(16d⁴/n)∫_J|p|. The constant is less than 1/2 even on the short final block. Summing the Taylor errors costs O((1+A²)2^(−d)log A). This proves both inequalities. The interpolated competitor and the uniform floor for measures with C=2 in 8770 fix the exponent of the optimum. Perturbing all entries K,V in absolute value by A^(−8) changes each feasible objective by O((1+A²) A^(−8)log A), so finite absolute precision suffices for this comparison.

Linear duality also gives the exact formula
    q_A=max_{|λ_j|≤h_j} [Σ_j λ_j V(t_j)− A² max_i |Σ_j λ_j K(u_i t_j)|].
It follows by dualizing the discrete norm and using that the support function of the ℓ¹ ball is A² times the sup norm. The variational object is the same as in 8770, of Nyman–Beurling ancestry. The operational difference with respect to 8797 is that neither the nodes nor the selection by the program require a list of μ up to A, and that the proof controls what can happen between rows. The square-root bound for the optima along an unbounded sequence remains open.

### Necessary variation even with dilations of unbounded range

Reproducible exploratory test in probe_dilation_lp.py, distinct from the theoretical certificate of 8807. Five Chebyshev nodes per octave, 350 centers uniform in log t on [10^(−5)/A,30], quadrature with measure dt and 3501 centers for checking with a second period and Mellin cutoff. With budget A², for A=4,8,16,32,64,128 the approximate errors on the checking mesh were respectively 1.7161e−3, 9.5215e−5, 8.7988e−6, 1.0174e−6, 1.9998e−7, 1.0425e−7. The six returned solutions exhausted the budget within numerical precision. This depends on the nodes: at A=128, with budget 128 and adding 1,2,3 to the list (3 was already there), the checking error went from 6.7853e−7 to 1.2432e−8. With those nodes and budget 128² the optimizer returned a training value slightly worse than with 128, impossible for exact optima by inclusion. These are approximate solutions in double precision; the second sampling certifies neither an integral nor an asymptotic law.

Analytic result motivated by the cost of the weights. Let D(M) be the smallest distance, in the infimum sense, between V and ∫K(ut)dν(u) in L¹(dt), over all signed real measures on [1,∞) with total variation ≤M. No upper support endpoint is imposed. Then
    lim_{M→∞} log D(M)/log M = −(1−Θ)/Θ.
Thus error M^(−1+o(1)) with variation ≤M along an unbounded sequence would suffice, even with arbitrarily distant nodes.

Lower. Removing u>U costs at most M∥K∥₁/U by change of variable and Tonelli. Fix 0<ε<Θ/3 and take U=M^(1/(Θ−2ε)), so that M≤U. For the retained part the uniform floor of 8770 with C=1 gives error ≥U^(Θ−1−ε) eventually. The cost of the tail is O(U^(Θ−1−2ε)). Subtract, take logarithms and then ε→0. This holds even if the dilations beyond U form a continuum.

Upper. On the dilation mesh of 8807 the weight of node i of block J⊂[D,2D] in the interpolated competitor is Σ_{a∈J}μ(a)ℓ_i(a), with ℓ_i the cardinal polynomial. Assign each boundary integer to a single block. On every J its modulus is ≤Λ_d and its variation ≤2d²Λ_d by Markov, also on a trimmed final block. By Abel each weight costs O_ε(D^(Θ+ε)(1+d²)Λ_d). Summing over the d+1 nodes and the octaves gives variation ≤A^(Θ+ε+o(1)). The error estimate of 8770 and 8807 is still ≤A^(Θ−1+ε+o(1)). For Θ<1 choose ε<1−Θ and A=M^(1/(Θ+2ε)), so that the competitor fits for large M. Letting ε→0 gives the ceiling. For Θ=1 the zero measure suffices for the ceiling with exponent zero; the distance does tend to zero by 8797 using the Möbius cutoff up to ⌊M⌋. The result calibrates both original restrictions: increasing the largest node without controlling the total price of its weights does not provide a sign rate. Producing the reciprocal rate without assuming Θ=1/2 remains pending.

Lossless floor for each fixed zero, by a direct argument. For the error E of any admissible ν, the Mellin transform of the approximant factors in Re s>0 by Fubini (∫u^(−σ)d|ν|≤M); the derivatives also exist locally by domination. At a zero ρ of multiplicity m the moments with logarithms of order <m−1 vanish and the one of order m−1 is a nonzero constant. Therefore replacing log t by log(t/t₀) in this last moment preserves its value exactly. Since ∥E∥∞≪1+M, the part t<t₀ costs O_ρ((1+M)t₀^β) after scaling t=t₀v. Choose t₀=c_ρ(1+M)^(−1/β) with c_ρ small. For t≥t₀ the weight costs O_ρ(t₀^(β−1)), since v^(β−1)(log v)^(m−1) is bounded on v≥1. One obtains D(M)≳_ρ(1+M)^(−(1−β)/β) even for multiple zeros, with a constant depending on the zero. In particular any zero on the critical line already imposes a floor c/(1+M).

### Elementary reciprocal rate for tests with linear oscillation at the origin

With the budget M of 8822 one can construct a single error E with integral exactly zero satisfying
    |∫ f(t)E(t)dt| ≤ C/M
simultaneously for all measurable tests with |f(t)−f(0)|≤t. They may change sign arbitrarily away from the origin. The construction does not require a zero-free region.

Take N=⌊M/3⌋ and start from Σ_{a≤N} μ(a)δ_a. Set S=Σ_{a≤N}μ(a)/a and add at u=N a mass −NS. Since ∫V=0 and ∫K(at)dt=B(1)/a, this makes the integral of the error vanish exactly. One has |S|≤1+1/N≤2 by 1=Σ_{a≤N}μ(a)⌊N/a⌋. The total variation fits in 3N. Before correcting, E(t)=Σ_{a>N}μ(a)K(at) by inversion over multiples. Its norm with weight t is ≤∥tK(t)∥₁ Σ_{a>N}a^(−2) ≤∥tK(t)∥₁/N. The correction adds to this norm at most |NS|∥tK(t)∥₁/N². Subtracting f(0) proves the statement for large M, independently of f.

More precisely, for fixed 0≤κ≤1, define D_κ(M) as the infimum of ∫t^κ|E(t)|dt with variation ≤M, support in [1,∞) and ∫E=0. This norm is exactly the supremum of the readings over |f(t)−f(0)|≤t^κ (choose the phase of the error). Then
    lim log D_κ(M)/log M = −(1+κ−Θ)/Θ.
In particular the reciprocal rate with arbitrarily small losses is attainable along an unbounded sequence if and only if Θ≤(1+κ)/2. At κ=0 the full problem is recovered even when requiring zero mass.

Lower: in the last argument of 8822, divide the Mellin weight on t≥t₀ by t^κ and use that v^(β−1−κ)(log v)^(m−1) is bounded on v≥1. With the same t₀ this gives D_κ(M)≳_ρ(1+M)^(−(1+κ−β)/β) for each zero, even a multiple one. It does not require the additional mass condition.

Upper: the Möbius cutoff up to A has error norm with weight t^κ ≤A^(Θ−1−κ+ε+o(1)) upon integrating its uniform ceiling O_ε(A^(Θ+ε)) up to 10log A/A. From there on the tail of 8770 is negligible also with the weight. The signed interpolation of 8807 and 8822 preserves that precision: in 8797 take the vertical line 3 instead of 2, so that the integral of the Taylor remainder with weight t^κ costs O(2^(−d)D^(−1−κ)) per unit of mass in the octave. The same Lebesgue factor holds for the fixed nodes. With d=⌈100log A⌉ this cost is negligible. The variation of the interpolated weights is ≤A^(Θ+ε+o(1)) as in 8822. For the interpolated error E₀ add at A the weight A∫E₀/B(1); the estimate with κ=0 gives an additional variation cost ≤A^(Θ+ε+o(1)). The change in weighted norm is O(A^(−κ)∥E₀∥₁), of admissible order. Choose A=M^(1/(Θ+2ε)) and let ε→0. For Θ=1,κ=0 a constant ceiling with the zero approximant suffices. This yields the exponent with the simultaneous conditions. The elementary construction at κ=1 explains exactly which weakening of the dual class already allows a reciprocal rate; at κ=0 the reciprocal upper bound remains open.

### Simultaneous inversion for all measurable tests of a growing logarithmic period

Fix 0<δ<1 and D>0. With P=(1−δ)log M and λ=exp P, there is a real measure on O_{δ,D}(log² M) dilations in [1,λ], of variation o(M), such that
    sup_{|f|≤1, f(λt)=f(t)} |∫ f(t)E(t)dt| ≤ M^(−D)
for all sufficiently large M. Arbitrarily discontinuous tests with oscillations of amplitude one down to zero are allowed. The measure is common to all tests of the chosen period. Explicit construction without evaluating μ.

Write τ_k=2πk/P, n=⌈C_D P log M⌉ and L=2n+1. For |k|≤n take a_k=1/ζ(1+iτ_k) with a₀=0 by continuation. At r_j=jP/L, 0≤j<L, form
    w_j=L^(−1) Σ_{k=−n}^n a_k exp(2πijk/L),   c_j=exp(r_j)w_j.
The weights are real by conjugation. For ν=Σ c_j δ_{exp(r_j)} the Mellin transform of the measure at 1+iτ_k equals a_{[k]}, where [k] denotes k modulo L in [−n,n]. By the classical polynomial bound for 1/ζ on the line 1 (used in 8701), max|a_k|≪(1+log M)^C. Thus Σ|c_j|≤λ L max|a_k|=M^(1−δ)(log M)^O(1)=o(M). In particular the mass of E is exactly zero. Its Mellin moments for |k|≤n all vanish because B(s)/ζ(s) is the Mellin transform of V.

To generalize from characters to measurable tests, periodize in r=log t the density e^r E(e^r). The series of translates converges in L¹ of one period by integrability. Its Fourier coefficients are, up to the sign of the index, [V̂_M(1+iτ_k)−B(1+iτ_k)a_{[k]}]/P. The symbols cost O((1+|τ|)^C exp(−π|τ|/2)) by 8623 and Stirling on the vertical line 1, with a removable value at τ=0. The sum over |k|>n of the moduli of the moments costs O(P (1+log M)^C exp(−c n/P)) and by the choice of C_D is ≤M^(−D). The absolutely convergent Fourier series represents the periodization by uniqueness in L¹. Integrating its modulus over one period costs at most that sum, which dominates all the indicated readings.

To check what is lost when identifying scales, the perturbation δ₁−λδ_λ is invisible to every test of this period, by change of variable. Its variation 1+λ still fits within the budget margin for large M; its response K(t)−λK(λt) has L¹ norm tending to 2∥K∥₁>0. Indeed, separate t<λ^(−1/2) from the complement: on the first the mass of |K(t)| tends to zero, on the second the same happens with λ|K(λt)|. This gives an exact example, within the dilation family itself, of order-one errors undetectable by the whole periodic battery. Antecedent 8623 uses periodization to evaluate a bilinear form. Here the weights are designed by discrete inversion to resolve the periodic class simultaneously; control of the discrepancy between replicas remains open.

### Exact cost in order of magnitude when unfolding the periodic scales

Let E(t)=V(t)−∫K(ut)dν(u) with support u≥1 and variation ≤M. Write F_λ(E) for the supremum of 8852 over measurable tests that are λ-periodic on the multiplicative scale, of modulus ≤1. Uniformly for M≥10 and λ sufficiently large,
    sup_ν [∥E∥₁−F_λ(E)] ≍ M log(λ)/λ.
The supremum is over the whole ball, with no smallness condition on F_λ of the extremal example. In particular λ=M² allows recovering the full norm to precision M^(−1+o(1)) without hypotheses on the largest node.

Upper. On any fundamental interval [R/λ,R) extend periodically the real phase of the error on that interval. The loss with respect to ∥E∥₁ is at most twice the exterior mass. With R=4log λ, the lower tail costs O((1+M)R/λ) by uniform boundedness of K,V. The upper one costs O((1+M)exp(−R)) by exponential decay and u≥1.

Lower. By 8623, inverting in Re s>1, V is the application of the filter (1−2z)^3 Q(z) of dyadic dilations to −Σ_{n≥2}(log n)exp(−nt). The constant coefficient of the filter is one, and its coefficients are absolutely summable. Thus V(t)=−(log 2)exp(−2t)+O(exp(−3t)) on t≥1 and K has the same expansion by summation over multiples. Choose a fixed [a,b] where K(z)≤−c<0, with a large, and h>0 such that 2hb<1/2. Take u=λ/(h log λ) and ν=(M/2)(δ₁−δ_u). For t=h z log λ, a≤z≤b, E(t)≥c₁ M exp(−2t) by the expansion and ut=λz. On the replica t/λ one has E(t/λ)≤−c₂ M because u t/λ=z and K,V tend to zero at the origin. The constants can be chosen uniform in M≥10. Upon folding, both contributions appear with opposite signs and densities E(t), E(t/λ)/λ in dt. Each pair loses at least 2 min(|E(t)|,|E(t/λ)|/λ)≥c₃M/λ in the triangle inequality; other replicas cannot undo that loss. The interval of t injects into the period since b/a<λ, and has length h(b−a)log λ. Integrating gives the floor. This calibration does not claim that the constructed error has small folded optimum.

Consequence for building the bridge. For P=2log M, τ_k=2πk/P, it suffices to find, along a sequence M→∞, measures of variation ≤M such that, for all |τ_k|≤C log M,
    |V̂_M(1+iτ_k)−B(1+iτ_k) ∫u^(−1−iτ_k)dν(u)| ≤ M^(−1+o(1))
with the o(1) uniform. Indeed there are O(log² M) readings; the remaining ones cost in total O(M^(−2)) by Stirling, |∫u^(−1−iτ)dν|≤M and C an absolute constant large enough. The Fourier inequality of 8852 gives the folded ceiling and the upper bound just proved gives the full ceiling. Conversely the full ceiling implies each of the reading inequalities. Support [1,M²] can be imposed: write u=v λ^j with 1≤v<λ and replace each weight by λ^(−j) times that weight at v. This preserves exactly all the sampled moments and only reduces the variation. The method of 8852 synthesizes the values with budget M for periods (1−δ)log M; applying it directly at 2log M only guarantees budget M² up to a polylogarithmic factor. The construction that fits these readings at cost M remains open.

### Effective saving in the synthesis cost for the critical period

For each fixed D≥2 and large λ, on O_D(log² λ) predetermined nodes of [1,λ] one achieves F_λ(E)≤λ^(−D) with total variation
    ≤ λ exp(−c√log λ)
for some c>0 and λ sufficiently large depending on D. In particular the cost improvement over the direct inversion of 8852 operates at the same period and keeps arbitrary power precision. To obtain the weights, the construction uses a long Möbius prefix.

Take H=⌈exp(C_D(log λ)²)⌉. The truncation with weights μ(n) up to H gives ∥E∥₁≤λ^(−D)/3 by the unconditional estimate of the last paragraph of 8797 before compressing, increasing C_D. Refold n=v λ^j with v∈[1,λ), j≥0, to a weight λ^(−j)μ(n) at v. Against each λ-periodic test the reading of K(nt) is λ^(−j) times that of K(vt), by change of variable. Hence the refolding preserves exactly the reading of the truncation. There are only O_D(log λ) replicas.

Use the octaves of [1,λ] of 8807 with their fixed Chebyshev nodes and d=⌈C'_D log λ⌉. In each replica j and virtual block J⊂[B,2B] interpolate K(vt) and integrate the cardinals ℓ_i(v) with the refolded weights. Allow, in the last replica, the data to occupy only part of J, without changing the nodes. The absolute sum of the raw weights in that piece is ≤λ^(−j)(2Bλ^j+1)≤3B. By 8797 and 8807, the integrated interpolation error is O((1+Λ_d)2^(−d)) per piece. There are O_D(log² λ) pieces; choose C'_D large enough for total error ≤λ^(−D)/3. The nodes are the same in all replicas, so the corresponding weights are added.

The cost is estimated AFTER the interpolation. Each weight in a piece is λ^(−j)Σ μ(n)ℓ_i(n/λ^j) over an interval of integers ≤2Bλ^j. By Abel and the variation O(d²Λ_d) of 8822, its modulus costs
    O((1+d²)Λ_d B exp(−c₀√log(2Bλ^j))).
Here the maximum of the Mertens prefixes up to the endpoint is used, adjusting constants for small endpoints. If B≤√λ the ceiling O(√λ polylog λ) suffices; if B>√λ the exponential saves exp(−c₁√log λ). Summing the polylogarithmic number of terms and reducing c concludes. This is equivalent to being able to pay with budget M for periods with log λ=log M+c₂√log M for c₂>0 sufficiently small. The period needed for the uniform argument of 8866 has log λ=2log M.

Threshold check. If C_D(λ) denotes the infimum of variation for F_λ(E)≤λ^(−D), then log C_D(λ)/log λ→Θ. For the ceiling use in the same Abel step the prefix bound O_ε((2Bλ^j)^(Θ+ε)). If Θ<1 choose ε<1−Θ; this leaves O_ε(polylog(λ) B^(Θ+ε)) per piece, uniformly in j. For Θ=1 use the previous unconditional ceiling. For the lower bound, the per-zero floor of 8822 and the unfolding of 8866 give, for variation m,
    c_ρ(1+m)^(−(1−β)/β) ≤ λ^(−D)+C(1+m)log(λ)/λ.
Since D≥2, the first term on the right is absorbed into the second and one obtains 1+m ≳_ρ (λ/log λ)^β. Take β arbitrarily close to Θ. The subexponential improvement is unconditional; the cost λ^(1/2+o(1)) at unbounded scales remains unproved.
